title: [bug] Fix lazy-source-unavailable tool registry error (write_clipboard capability table mismatch + on-device tools) and Side Panel page summarization
description:
## Problem
When using the Chrome Extension Side Panel (and in background agent runs), asking to summarize the current page or calling any tool fails with:
`lazy-source-unavailable` on `search_tools`, `list_tools`, and `run_pipeline` (`agent-do:tool:search_tools in 87.0ms (error)`).

## Root Causes (verified in source)
1. **`capability_table_inventory_mismatch` thrown inside `liveChromeLazyRecords` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:2253, 2725` & `extension/lib/chrome-tool-capabilities.js:640`)**:
   - `service-worker.js:2725` attaches `liveManagementTools.write_clipboard = tool({...})` onto `liveManagementTools`.
   - `liveChromeLazyRecords` calls `canonicalChromeCapabilitiesByTool(managementTools, 'management')` (`capabilitiesByTool(toolMap, 'management')` in `chrome-tool-capabilities.js:640`), which checks `MANAGEMENT_CAPABILITY_TOOL_NAMES` (51 tools, missing `write_clipboard`) and throws `Error('capability_table_inventory_mismatch')`!
   - `LazyToolProtocol` (`extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js:889, 916, 990`) catches any throw from `readSources()` and returns `fixedError('lazy-source-unavailable')`!
2. **`bookedOnDeviceTools` (`summarize_text`, `translate_text`, `detect_language`) omitted from `liveChromeLazyRecords`**:
   - `service-worker.js:2779` creates `bookedOnDeviceTools` and passes it in `extraTools`, but `readMasterLazySources` (`service-worker.js:2815`) does not pass `onDeviceTools: bookedOnDeviceTools` into `liveChromeLazyRecords`, so the lazy tool catalog never exposes `summarize_text`, `translate_text`, or `detect_language`!
3. **Side Panel active-tab context in `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js`**:
   - When running a turn from the Side Panel's Page view (`runPageTurn` in `sidepanel.js:463`), the sidepanel knows `currentTabId`, `currentTabOrigin`, and the tab's title/URL, and `read_page` / `capture_page` must be immediately discoverable and usable via `search_tools` / `execute_tool` without ever throwing `lazy-source-unavailable`.

## Required Fix
1. Move/register `write_clipboard` cleanly in `extension/lib/management-tools.js` (`managementToolset`) AND add its canonical capability row to `extension/lib/chrome-tool-capabilities.js` (`MANAGEMENT_CAPABILITY_TOOL_NAMES`, `CHROME_TOOL_CAPABILITY_BOUNDS.managementTools = 52`, `totalTools = 191`, and `rows` entry: `record('write_clipboard', 'management', ['management.clipboard.write'], [], 'none', 'mutating', false, 'mutating', 'management.clipboard')`). Update any test that pins the management tool count (51 -> 52, total 190 -> 191).
2. Wire `bookedOnDeviceTools` into `liveChromeLazyRecords` (or `executableBuiltinToolRecords` / `executableManagementToolRecords`) so `search_tools({ query: 'summarize' })` and `search_tools({ query: 'read_page' })` both succeed with `ok: true` and return executable `selectionRef`s.
3. Also log diagnostic details when `liveSnapshot(this.#readSources)` catches an error in `LazyToolProtocol` (or in `service-worker.js` `readMasterLazySources`) so a source error is never silently swallowed without a diagnostic message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Falsification unit test calling `liveChromeLazyRecords` / `createLazyProviderToolset` with the real `browserToolset()` + `managementToolset()` + `onDeviceTextToolset()` and asserting `search_tools({ query: 'read_page' })`, `search_tools({ query: 'summarize' })`, ` search_tools({ query: 'clipboard' })`, and `list_tools({}) ` all return `ok: true` (never `lazy-source-unavailable`).
- Real headless Chrome verification opening `sidepanel.html` and verifying tool search and page companion state.
close_reason: Closed

title: [perf] Eliminate 30-45s task-open stall (thread.get:view OPFS store.keys scans, write-lock contention, and delayed showThreadView)
description:
## Problem
Clicking a task in the NTP sidebar takes 30–45 seconds to load (measured in owner console logs: `ntp:open_thread in 24407.4ms`, `thread.get:view in 43532.9ms`, `thread-view:logs:exec:<uuid> in 14307.1ms` and `7158.0ms`).

## Root Causes (verified in source)
1. **O(N) full-OPFS `store.keys()` directory walks inside `migrateExecutionLog` (`extension/lib/durable-runs.js:753-820`)**:
   - `listLogs(executionId)` (line 819) does NOT check `migratedExecutions.has(executionId)` before calling `await store.has(MIGRATED_PREFIX + executionId)`.
   - Worse, when `start()` creates a brand-new execution or when `migrateExecutionLog(executionId)` runs for an execution without a `run-log-wal:<id>` marker, `migrateExecutionLog` calls `await store.keys()` (line 766) while holding the global exclusive `locked()` mutex! In OPFS with hundreds of run records/chunks, each `store.keys()` walks the entire OPFS directory tree (~1–3s per call), blocking all readers and writers.
2. **Global exclusive `locked()` in `listThreadExecutions` (`extension/lib/durable-runs.js:895`) + duplicate call in `service-worker.js:7413`**:
   - `listThreadExecutions(threadId)` takes the exclusive `locked()` write lock even when `stored != null || scannedThreads.has(threadId)`, queueing behind background scheduler writes.
   - `service-worker.js:7401` and `7413` call `durableRuns.listThreadExecutions(m.id)` twice per `thread.get`.
3. **No memoization of terminal execution logs in `thread-run-view.js`**:
   - Once an execution reaches a terminal phase (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`), its WAL log is immutable, yet `readExecutionLogs` re-reads and re-hydrates all 50 executions from OPFS on every `thread.get`.
4. **Delayed `showThreadView()` & duplicate `thread.get` calls in `extension/ntp/ntp.js:2787-2866`**:
   - `openThread(id)` awaits `send('thread.get', { id })` BEFORE calling `showThreadView()` or highlighting the clicked sidebar row, so the UI appears frozen and repeated clicks spawn overlapping `thread.get` calls that multiply OPFS load.
   - At boot, overdue `scheduler:task_fire` tasks fire simultaneously at the exact same millisecond, contending with interactive `thread.get` reads.

## Required Fix
1. In `extension/lib/durable-runs.js`:
   - In `start()`, immediately mark new executions in `migratedExecutions.add(executionId)` (and write/queue the WAL marker without calling `store.keys()`, since a brand-new execution has no legacy KV rows).
   - In `listLogs(executionId)`, check `migratedExecutions.has(executionId)` FIRST before touching `store.has()`.
   - In `migrateExecutionLog(executionId)`, cache a single one-time scan of legacy `run-log:` keys per worker lifetime (`legacyLogKeysByExecPromise`) so `store.keys()` is called at most ONCE per worker lifetime instead of once per execution!
   - In `listThreadExecutions(threadId)`, use `lockedRead` when the thread index already exists (`stored != null || scannedThreads.has(threadId)`), only escalating to `locked` if the one-time legacy thread migration scan is needed.
2. In `extension/lib/thread-run-view.js` & `extension/background/service-worker.js`:
   - Cache settled/terminal execution log arrays in a bounded LRU map (`settledLogsCache`, e.g. max 256 entries keyed by `${executionId}:${record.revision ?? record.updatedAt ?? ''}`, invalidated on `forgetCachedState` / purge) so re-reading settled executions in `buildThreadRunView` is O(1) in-memory.
   - In `service-worker.js` `thread.get`, reuse the executions list from `buildThreadRunView` (or deduplicate in-flight `thread.get` calls for the same `id` + pagination key) instead of calling `listThreadExecutions` twice.
3. In `extension/ntp/ntp.js` (`openThread(id)`):
   - Switch to the thread surface immediately on click (`showThreadView()`, highlight the sidebar row via `highlightTaskSidebarRow(id)`, set initial title from the clicked row/cached thread if available) before awaiting `send('thread.get', { id })` so task clicks respond visually in <16ms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit test in `tests/thread-open-perf.test.ts` proving `listLogs` and `buildThreadRunView` across 30 executions make at most 1 `store.keys()` call total (0 for new executions) and complete in <50ms.
- Headless Chrome verification clicking tasks in NTP and measuring `ntp:open_thread` and `thread.get:view` latency.

title: Eliminate NTP thread-list heartbeat hydration storm, deduplicate terminal thread.get refreshes, show thread surface immediately on click, and lazy-load offscreen artifact previews
description:
WHY / MEASURED TRACE:
Owner trace showed:
1. `ntp:thread-list-hydrated` firing ~70 times in 4 minutes on a 5-second cadence (`+505ms`, `+5209ms`, `+9289ms`, `+499ms`, `+5192ms`), and every single hydration unconditionally calling `refreshFailedRuns()` (`run.list`, `run.dismissedFailed`, `named-agent.list`) and `refreshBoard()` (`board.list`, `board.messages`).
2. Multiple overlapping `thread.get` requests fired for the same open thread, with `ntp:open_thread` waiting for `thread.get` before calling `showThreadView()`, leaving the UI appearing frozen on click.
3. 24 sequential `route asset.get` RPCs fired synchronously on thread mount when rendering `<artifact-card>` / `<screenshot-strip>` items across historical turns.

ROOT CAUSES PROVEN IN CODE:
1. `extension/lib/task-sidebar-lifecycle.js:5-20`:
   - `threadRunRevisions(runs)` keys on `run.revision` for every thread-bound run.
   - Because `durableRuns.heartbeat()` and `preToolUse()` bump `run.revision` every 5s while `run.phase` stays `'running'` (without mutating thread storage), `onRunSnapshot` triggers `loadThreads()` (`thread.list`) and `commitThreads` (`renderTaskRows`) on EVERY heartbeat and tool call!
   - Instead, `taskSidebarLifecycle` should key on the thread-relevant state of each thread-bound run (`phase`, `threadId`, `taskPreview`, `terminal?.ok`, `terminal?.cancelled`, `terminal?.summary`), so heartbeats/tool-progress bumps within `'running'` do not re-fetch `thread.list` once the running state has been rendered, while preserving retry semantics when a read fails.
2. `extension/ntp/ntp.js:2219-2233` (`renderTaskRows`):
   - `renderTaskRows` unconditionally calls `refreshFailedRuns()` and `refreshBoard()` on every sidebar render, even when triggered by `openThread(id)` (which only changes `activeId` highlight!) or when failed runs / board have not changed.
   - `renderTaskRows` also wipes and rebuilds all `#thread-sidebar` DOM nodes (`el.replaceChildren()`) even when only `activeId` (`aria-current`) changed on an identical thread list.
3. `extension/lib/terminal-thread-projection-lifecycle.js:27-42`:
   - `onRunSnapshot(snapshot)` loops over `snapshot.runs` and pushes a separate `refresh(run, openThreadId)` (`loadThread(openThreadId)` = `send('thread.get', { id })`) for EVERY newly-observed terminal run on `openThreadId` in the snapshot, instead of coalescing to at most ONE `refresh(latestRun, openThreadId)` per `openThreadId` per snapshot!
4. `extension/ntp/ntp.js:2571-2650` (`openThread`):
   - `openThread(id)` waits until AFTER `await send('thread.get', { id })` before calling `showThreadView()` and setting the known thread title from the sidebar/cached list, so clicking a slow thread leaves the user staring at the old view with no feedback.
5. `extension/shared/components.js:6606` (`_loadArtifactPreview`):
   - Every `<artifact-card>` in a reopened thread calls `RUNTIME_SEND('asset.get', { origin, id })` immediately in `appendArtifact`, firing 24+ RPCs at once on long threads. Deferring offscreen cards via `IntersectionObserver` (when available, with immediate fallback in unit tests or when `IntersectionObserver` is absent) avoids flooding the SW with offscreen `asset.get` calls on thread open.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Update `extension/lib/task-sidebar-lifecycle.js` so mid-run `revision` bumps that do not change a run's thread-visible state (`phase`, `threadId`, `taskPreview`, `terminal` state) do NOT re-trigger `loadThreads()` after the run's initial running state has been rendered, while preserving all existing recovery/retry guarantees when `loadThreads()` fails or returns a new thread.
2. In `extension/ntp/ntp.js`:
   - Avoid full `#thread-sidebar` DOM replacement and skip redundant `refreshFailedRuns()` / `refreshBoard()` when `renderTaskRows(threads, activeId)` is called with an unchanged thread list digest and only `activeId` changed (updating `aria-current` in place).
   - In `openThread(id)`, immediately transition to the thread view (`showThreadView()`) with the known thread title (if available from the sidebar) and a loading indicator while `thread.get` resolves, fencing commits with `runSurfaceOwner` as before.
3. In `extension/lib/terminal-thread-projection-lifecycle.js`:
   - Coalesce per-snapshot terminal refreshes for `openThreadId` so a snapshot with N newly-observed terminal runs for `openThreadId` performs at most ONE `loadThread(openThreadId)` call.
4. Pin with unit + falsification tests in `tests/task-sidebar-lifecycle.test.ts` and `tests/terminal-thread-projection-lifecycle.test.ts`.

F1 — P1: extension/lib/thread-rows-digest.js IS BINARY TO GIT, AND THAT FILE DECIDES WHETHER A RENDER IS SKIPPED. Line 26 is a join whose string literal is ONE RAW NUL (U+0000) — the only NUL in 1288 bytes — a deliberate collision-avoidance separator (line 28 uses "|"). Consequences: git diff/show/log -p report "Binary files differ" (numstat "- -"), git blame and git grep skip it unless -a, GitHub renders "Binary file not shown" — SO THE FILE THAT DEFINES THE RENDER-SKIP DECISION IS THE ONE FILE NORMAL TOOLING CANNOT REVIEW, WHICH DIRECTLY UNDERMINES THE INDEPENDENT-REVIEW MANDATE. Content-classifying CI/lint/coverage gates misclassify it too. It should still parse (a raw U+0000 in a string literal is valid ECMAScript). SMALLEST FIX: write that separator as the SIX-CHARACTER ESCAPE backslash-u-0000 instead of the raw byte — THE RUNTIME STRING STAYS BYTE-IDENTICAL AND TEXT-DIFF REVIEWABILITY IS RESTORED.
  INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: this is the same defect chrome-agent-platform-merger found and filed as chrome-agent-platform-tb3v, with the artefact-level measurement that esbuild emits the escape (so the built bundle carries no raw NUL) and the digest never leaves the module. Two lanes, independently. Land-then-escape is the endorsed path.

F2 — P2: TWO TESTS WOULD PASS WITH A BROKEN IMPLEMENTATION. tests/task-sidebar-lifecycle.test.ts compares threadRowsDigest(...) TO ITSELF with the same inputs — always true for a deterministic function and asserting nothing about the output (only its null/undefined-to-empty-string cases are meaningful). The two "ntp wiring" tests read ntp.js AS TEXT and assert substrings and ordering; they never execute renderTaskRows, so they would still pass if lastThreadRowsDigest were initialised wrongly (ntp.js:2463 is never asserted) or if the digest were computed from the wrong fields at the call site. It does not bite today because commitThread IGNORES the selected run (ntp.js:2851) and re-reads the authoritative thread with force:true. Latent footgun the moment _run renders a specific status; the tests never assert WHICH run wins a coalesce. FIX: document that _run is ignored, or select by heartbeatAt/at, or assert the chosen run.

F4 — P2 LATENT: the removed RUNTIME_SEND guard in _previewNow IS SAFE, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the only two callers (components.js:7051 fallback, :7065 observer callback) are both behind "if (!RUNTIME_SEND) return;" at :7049, and RUNTIME_SEND is a module const (:669). Leak check: a disconnected card's job is cleared by the not-connected branch; per-conversation observer holds only pending targets; a card cannot be double-observed today, but the new code silently DROPS the first job if called twice on one card. FIX (optional): re-add the guard for self-containment.

F5 — P2 PRE-EXISTING, FLAGGED SO THE COALESCING CHANGE IS NOT BLAMED FOR IT: terminal-thread-projection-lifecycle.js:39-40 sets observedTerminalRevisions unconditionally, so a terminal run seen while another thread is open is marked consumed; byte-identical to the pre-diff code, compensated by openThread.

Omitted but accounted: aria-current (re-applied by highlightTaskSidebarRow, ntp.js:2480); the "(N)" badge (updated BEFORE the gate, ntp.js:2468); failed-runs/board sections (run-driven changes force meta.runsChanged === true; board changes have their own board-* event path, ntp.js:1916). title: Fix 27s thread.get stall: register run-log-wal: in DURABLE_KEY_RE, avoid full-OPFS store.keys() in migrateExecutionLog, use lockedRead on read paths, and cache settled execution logs
description:
WHY / MEASURED TRACE:
Owner reported opening a task from the UI takes 11-27 seconds (`thread.get:view in 27328.9ms`, `thread-view:logs:exec:<id>` staircase from 630ms to 11343ms, and a 27192ms Service Worker route stall across `thread.list`, `run.list`, `actions.list`).

ROOT CAUSES PROVEN IN CODE:
1. `run-log-wal:` missing from `DURABLE_PREFIXES` and `DURABLE_KEY_RE` in `extension/lib/memory.js:283-285`:
   - `extension/lib/durable-runs.js:751` uses `MIGRATED_PREFIX = 'run-log-wal:'` to mark that an execution's log has been migrated to WAL.
   - `memory.js` omitted `run-log-wal` from `DURABLE_PREFIXES` and `DURABLE_KEY_RE` (even though `archive-target-registry.js:273` included it).
   - Every `store.has('run-log-wal:<execId>')` and `store.setTrusted('run-log-wal:<execId>', ...)` threw `Error: invalid durable-run key: run-log-wal:<execId>`, which `.catch(() => false)` / `.catch(() => {})` swallowed!
   - The migration marker was NEVER persisted to OPFS.
2. Full-OPFS `store.keys()` walk inside exclusive `locked()` on every execution read after SW boot (`extension/lib/durable-runs.js:766, 819-820`):
   - `listLogs(executionId)` did not check `migratedExecutions.has(executionId)` before calling `store.has(...)`. Because `store.has` always threw/returned `false`, EVERY `listLogs` call queued `await locked(() => migrateExecutionLog(executionId))` on the exclusive write lock!
   - On the first read of each execution in a SW lifetime, `migrateExecutionLog` called `await store.keys()`, which in `durableRunMemory()` walks EVERY execution dir, payload dir, thread dir, registry dir, and master memory across OPFS (~630ms per execution), serializing 28+ executions for 18-27 seconds under `locked()`!
   - Brand-new executions created via `start()` also did not record `migratedExecutions.add(executionId)` or persist the `run-log-wal:` marker, so they too paid the migration walk on next boot.
3. Exclusive `locked()` used on read-only paths (`durable-runs.js`):
   - `list()` (line 2058), `dismissedFailedRuns()` (line 2086), and the `listThreadExecutions(threadId)` fast path when `stored != null` or `scannedThreads.has(threadId)` (line 895) all acquire the exclusive `locked()` mutex instead of `lockedRead()`, serializing against concurrent `listLogs` readers.
   - `service-worker.js:7181-7193` calls `durableRuns.listThreadExecutions(m.id)` twice during a single `thread.get` (once inside `buildThreadRunView` and a second time for `pendingApprovalRequirementsForExecutions`).
4. Settled (`terminal` / `cancelled`) execution logs re-read from OPFS on every `thread.get` & uncoalesced concurrent `thread.get` RPCs:
   - Opening or refreshing a thread re-reads up to 50 settled executions' WAL + payload files from OPFS every time, and overlapping `thread.get` calls for the same thread multiply the OPFS reads.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Add `'run-log-wal:'` to `DURABLE_PREFIXES` and `run-log-wal` to `DURABLE_KEY_RE` in `extension/lib/memory.js`.
2. Add `keysForExecution(executionId)` on `durableRunMemory()` in `extension/lib/memory.js` (reading only that execution's store + legacy master keys for that executionId) and use it (with fallback to `store.keys()` for custom stores) in `migrateExecutionLog` and per-execution cleanup paths in `durable-runs.js` so `migrateExecutionLog` NEVER walks all other executions/payloads/threads.
3. In `durable-runs.js`:
   - In `start()`, mark the new execution as WAL-native (`migratedExecutions.add(executionId)` and persist the `run-log-wal:<executionId>` marker).
   - In `listLogs(executionId)`, check `migratedExecutions.has(executionId)` FIRST before calling `store.has(...)`; if `store.has(...)` returns true, add to `migratedExecutions` and skip `locked(() => migrateExecutionLog(executionId))`.
   - Use `lockedRead` for `list()`, `dismissedFailedRuns()`, and the `listThreadExecutions(threadId)` fast path when `scannedThreads.has(threadId)` or `stored != null`.
   - Cache hydrated logs for settled (`terminal` / `cancelled`) executions in a bounded LRU map (invalidated in `appendLog`, `appendRegistryRow`, `compactExecution`, `purgeForTarget`, `purgeFailedForAgent`, `forgetCachedState`, and when `before`/`limit` pagination is non-default).
4. In `extension/lib/thread-run-view.js` & `extension/background/service-worker.js`:
   - Return `executionIds` (or reuse the executions list) from `buildThreadRunView` so `thread.get` does not call `listThreadExecutions` a second time.
   - Coalesce concurrent in-flight `thread.get` calls for the same `(id, limit, offset, all)` in `service-worker.js`.
5. Pin with unit + falsification tests proving `store.has('run-log-wal:<execId>')` succeeds on `durableRunMemory()`, `listLogs` does zero `store.keys()` walks and zero exclusive lock acquisitions for WAL executions, and settled execution logs are served from cache on repeated `buildThreadRunView` calls.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-UI-CONTRAST-A11Y-01] Fix dark-mode contrast token drift, Shadow DOM menu keyboard traps, .aex-agent collision, and CSS anchor-scope/field-sizing
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **Severe Dark-Mode Contrast Failures (1.15:1 to 2.35:1) from Undefined CSS Token Names**:
   - `var(--surface-2, #f5f2ec)` in `<jobs-board>` (`components.js:11767, 11796`), `options.css:1480`, and `artifacts/index.html:28` uses `--surface-2` (undefined in `theme.css`; canonical token is `--panel-2`), painting light cream `#f5f2ec` behind light text `#eae6de` in dark mode (1.15:1 contrast).
   - `var(--accent-fg, #fff)` in `options.css:419` (`.usage-range[aria-selected="true"]`) uses undefined `--accent-fg` instead of `--btn-fg` (2.35:1 contrast in dark mode).
   - `var(--text-muted, #6b675f)` and `var(--border-subtle, #e3e1dc)` in `components.js:6279-6283` and `folder-browser.js:195` use undefined tokens instead of `--muted` and `--border` (2.28:1 contrast in dark mode).
   - `var(--secondary, #b45309)` in `components.js:9999` (`<model-picker>`), `var(--accent-2)` in `options.css:478`, and `var(--ok, #1c7c33)` in `sidepanel.html:100` / `ntp.js:3763` use drifted names instead of `--accent2` and `--success`.
   - Hardcoded `background: #fff` in `artifact/artifact.html:36` and `artifacts/index.js:261` ignores dark mode (should use `var(--bg-elevated)`).
2. **Broken Shadow DOM `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` Navigation in `<mic-button>` & `<attach-button>`**:
   - `MicButton` (`components.js:1231-1235`) and `AttachButton` (`components.js:1720-1726`) compute `options.indexOf(document.activeElement)` inside Shadow DOM, which always returns `-1` because `document.activeElement` is the shadow host—permanently trapping keyboard focus on item `0`.
3. **Broken Cross-Shadow `#ap-list` Lookup in `<agent-composer>`**:
   - `AgentComposer._presentAgentPopover` (`components.js:7436-7448`) calls `this._agentPick?.querySelector?.("#ap-list")`, which always returns `null` because `<agent-picker>` renders in Shadow DOM (`this._root`).
4. **`<activity-explorer>` `.aex-agent` Class Collision & Missing `.tt-*` Styles**:
   - `components.js:11090-11150, 11166, 11353, 11411`: Both `<select class="aex-agent">` and row badges `<span class="aex-agent">` share `.aex-agent`, and `ActivityExplorer` omits `.tt-block-controls` / `.tt-raw` CSS rules needed by `buildToolTreeBlock()`.
5. **Accessibility, Constitution & Modern CSS Gaps**:
   - Dangling `aria-describedby` in `<durable-run-registry>` (`components.js:12708-12713`) when `reason` is empty.
   - Invalid `<summary>` outside `<details>` in `MessageBubble` (`components.js:5963`) and missing `aria-expanded` on `.long-toggle` (`components.js:5611, 6008`).
   - Missing `role="tablist"` + arrow-key navigation in `<agent-nav>` (`components.js:10201`) and missing `<main>` + `<h1>` in `extension/artifacts/index.html`.
   - Raw emoji `⚠️` in `<table-preview>` (`components.js:3917`), missing `aria-hidden="true"` on `▾` in `agent-template-select.js:282`, and raw permission names in `renderAgentPermissionsPanel` (`components.js:13861`).
   - Duplicate `anchor-name: --composer-anchor` across multiple `<agent-composer>` instances without `anchor-scope` (`components.js:7058`), and synchronous JS textarea height measurement instead of CSS `field-sizing: content` (`components.js:7110, 9016`).
   - Ghost card `box-shadow: var(--shadow-1)` on bordered inline cards (`<artifact-card>`, `<conversation-run-status>`, `<plan-strip>`, `<permission-approval-card>`).

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `extension/shared/components.js`
- `extension/shared/theme.css`
- `extension/options/options.css`
- `extension/artifact/artifact.html`
- `extension/artifacts/index.html` & `extension/artifacts/index.js`
- `extension/lib/folder-browser.js`
- `extension/lib/agent-template-select.js`

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification tests verifying:
  1. `MicButton` and `AttachButton` `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` keydown advances focus across menu items `0 -> 1 -> 2` inside Shadow DOM.
  2. `<activity-explorer>` scopes select vs badge styles distinctly and includes `.tt-block-controls` and `.tt-raw` CSS rules.
  3. `<durable-run-registry>` omits `aria-describedby` when `reason` is empty.
  4. Canonical tokens (`--panel-2`, `--btn-fg`, `--muted`, `--border`, `--accent2`, `--success`) replace all drifted `--surface-2`, `--accent-fg`, `--text-muted`, and `--border-subtle` occurrences, and `npm run check:gallery` passes after syncing.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-STREAMING-DOM-PERF-01] Fix O(N^2) token streaming in conversation/MessageBubble and lazy-render collapsed tool-card DOM trees
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **Quadratic $O(N^2)$ Full-Markdown & Shadow DOM Rebuild on Every Streamed Token**:
   - In `extension/shared/conversation.js:2063-2096`, every `text` and `text-delta` event mutates `streamBubble.setAttribute("content", streamedText)`.
   - In `MessageBubble.attributeChangedCallback` (`extension/shared/components.js:430-433, 5635-6076`), every `content` change synchronously runs `renderMarkdown(body)` over the entire accumulated response and overwrites `shadowRoot.innerHTML = "<style>...140 lines...</style>..."`, destroying and recreating the Shadow DOM and re-parsing the stylesheet on every token.
2. **Synchronous Layout Thrashing on Scroll & Thinking Deltas**:
   - `AgentConversation._scrollToBottom()` (`components.js:6295-6306`) and `thinkingDelta()` (`components.js:6750-6762`) synchronously read `scrollHeight`/`scrollTop`/`clientHeight` immediately after DOM mutations on every token.
3. **Eager 200-Row DOM Construction Inside Collapsed `<details class="tool">` Cards**:
   - `buildToolCardDom` (`components.js:5177-5352`) eagerly calls `buildToolTree(detail)` and builds up to 200 interactive DOM rows (~1,400-2,000 DOM nodes) even when the `<details class="tool">` card is closed (`card.open === false`). A 50-run thread with 10 tool calls/run builds 500,000+ hidden DOM nodes on thread switch.

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `extension/shared/components.js:5177-5352` (`buildToolCardDom`)
- `extension/shared/components.js:5635-6076` (`MessageBubble`)
- `extension/shared/components.js:6295-6306, 6750-6762` (`AgentConversation`)
- `extension/shared/conversation.js:2063-2096`

## Implementation & Invariants
1. **Lazy Tool-Card Body Construction**: In `buildToolCardDom` (`components.js:5309-5352`), when `!card.open`, defer calling `buildToolTree(detail)` until the `<details>` `toggle` event fires with `card.open === true` (or a test/caller opens `card.open = true` and dispatches `toggle` / accesses the tree). Ensure error cards (`status === "error"`, which set `card.open = true`) still build their tree immediately, and ensure the leakage probe / shadow-root inspection tests that open cards via `card.open = true` + `toggle` (or a getter/MutationObserver fallback) see the exact same unwrapped tree and raw JSON view.
2. **Reuse Stylesheet & Optimize Streaming Updates in `MessageBubble`**: Keep the `<style>` node persistent in `MessageBubble`s shadow root (or use `adoptedStyleSheets`) so `_render()` only updates a content wrapper instead of destroying and re-parsing the 140-line `<style>` sheet on every update.
3. **Add `content-visibility: auto`**: Add `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 64px;` to `.run-group` in `AgentConversation`.

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification tests verifying:
  1. `MessageBubble` preserves the same `<style>` element identity across repeated `setAttribute("content", ...)` updates during streaming.
  2. A closed `<details class="tool">` card produced by `buildToolCardDom` does not eagerly mount `.tt-row` children while closed, and populates the full `.tt-tree` and `.tt-raw` immediately when opened.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-BUNDLE-FOOTPRINT-01] Fix zod/v4 CJS+ESM double-bundling (-311KB SW) and strip AI SDK & SW stores from UI bundles
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **CJS + ESM `zod/v4` Double-Bundling in `service-worker.js` and `agent-worker.js` (Solves Risk R18)**:
   - In `build.mjs:407`, `const CANON_ZOD_V4 = requireFromRoot.resolve("zod/v4")` uses Node CommonJS resolution (`createRequire`), resolving to `node_modules/.deno/zod@3.25.76/node_modules/zod/v4/index.cjs`.
   - Meanwhile, `ai`, `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`, and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` import `zod/v4` via ESM, resolving to `.../zod/v4/index.js` and `.../zod/v4/core/index.js`.
   - Because `.cjs` files cannot be tree-shaken by esbuild and `zod/v4/index.cjs` eagerly `require()`s `./locales/index.cjs`, esbuild bundles **both the CJS and ESM copies of Zod v4 plus 78 locale files** (190 files, 1,168,661 B raw) into `service-worker.js`.
   - `duplicateAiSdkInputs` in `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:49-78` missed this because both CJS and ESM copies live inside the same `.deno/zod@3.25.76` store directory.
2. **Accidental Bundling of the Full AI SDK (~1.73 MB raw / ~620 KB minified) into `options.bundle.js`**:
   - `extension/lib/provider.js:37` explicitly states that `provider-catalog.js` exists for "the Settings page (which must NOT import the heavy model layer)".
   - However, `extension/options/options.js:30` imports `../lib/provider-gate.js`, and `extension/lib/provider-gate.js:23` has `import { effectiveBaseURL, PROVIDER_CHOICES } from "./provider.js";`. Both symbols are already defined in and exported by `extension/lib/provider-catalog.js:43-195`. Importing from `./provider.js` pulls `ai`, `@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `zod`, and `demo-model.js` into `options.bundle.js`.
3. **Accidental Bundling of SW-Only Backend Stores (~401 KB raw) into `ntp.bundle.js` and `options.bundle.js`**:
   - `extension/ntp/ntp.js:12` and `extension/options/options.js:16` import the pure helper `projectUnifiedAgents` from `../lib/named-agents.js:1123`. Because `named-agents.js` also contains SW storage mutations that import `memory.js`, `durable-runs.js`, `system-prompts.js`, `scheduler.js`, `skill-registry.js`, and `threads.js`, ~401 KB of SW-only backend code is bundled into both UI bundles.

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `build.mjs:407-425` (`CANON_ZOD_V4`)
- `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:49-78` (`duplicateAiSdkInputs` / CJS+ESM duplication check)
- `extension/lib/provider-gate.js:23`
- `extension/lib/agent-projection.js` (new pure module extracted from `extension/lib/named-agents.js:1123-1182`)
- `extension/lib/named-agents.js:1123-1182` (re-export `projectUnifiedAgents` from `./agent-projection.js`)
- `extension/ntp/ntp.js:12` and `extension/options/options.js:16`
- `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts`

## Implementation & Invariants
1. In `build.mjs:407`, resolve `CANON_ZOD_V4` to the ESM entrypoint (`.replace(/\.cjs$/, ".js")`).
2. In `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs`, add a check ensuring no bundle contains both `.cjs` and `.js` inputs from `zod` (or any `SINGLETON_PACKAGES` package), and ensure `options.bundle.js` does not pull in `provider.js` / `@ai-sdk/*`.
3. In `extension/lib/provider-gate.js:23`, import `{ effectiveBaseURL, PROVIDER_CHOICES }` from `"./provider-catalog.js"`.
4. Extract `projectUnifiedAgents` into `extension/lib/agent-projection.js`, re-export it from `extension/lib/named-agents.js`, and update `ntp.js:12` and `options.js:16` to import from `../lib/agent-projection.js`.

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification tests in `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts` asserting:
  1. Zero `.cjs` inputs from `zod` in `service-worker.js` and `agent-worker.js` metafile inputs.
  2. `options.bundle.js` metafile inputs do NOT include `extension/lib/provider.js` or `extension/lib/durable-runs.js`.
  3. `ntp.bundle.js` metafile inputs do NOT include `extension/lib/durable-runs.js`.
- Verify tests go RED against the unfixed build and GREEN after the fix.
- Run `npm run build:production` and confirm `service-worker.js` drops by ~310 KB minified (~2.57 MB vs 3.00 MB budget).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — candidate cap-wfo5-browser-tools @ 4bad1f6d557592cda63d75734fea732911282c05, base 13c530ce. Claimed by cap-k3. Not landed; author does not close.

MEASURED STATE BEFORE: browserToolset() contains 135 tools (138 with developerFeatures:true — get_cookie/set_cookie/remove_cookie are developer-only). Exactly THREE were callable by a harness: list_tabs, group_tabs, ungroup_tabs. open_tab, read_page, capture_screenshot, click_element, type_text, scroll_page, search_history, create_bookmark, create_window, get_system_memory and 122 others were implemented, permission-checked and grant-gated, and refused by a hand-kept allow-list.

THE DIRECTIVE AS WRITTEN WOULD HAVE OPENED A HOLE. The bead asks for HARNESS_PERMITTED_BROWSER_TOOLS = new Set(Object.keys(browserToolset())). That alone is unsafe, measured not inferred: runBrowserToolCall called browserToolset() with NO gate arguments, and requireDestructiveApproval returns { ok: true } when destructiveActionGate is null. So widening the set alone makes close_tab, close_window, remove_bookmark, wipe_browsing_data, set_cookie and remove_cookie mutate the user's browser with no owner card at all. (get_cookie's value read, write_file and schedule_task already fail closed on their own; those six did not.)

THE FIX takes the house pattern from executeWorkerTool, which had already solved this for the worker caller:
  extension/lib/browser-tools.js — harnessPermittedBrowserTools() derives the permitted set from the toolset's own keys rather than retyping it (a hand-kept copy is a list that drifts: the old one silently excluded 132 tools). LAZY and cached, because computing it at module scope throws ReferenceError: Cannot access PRIVACY_SETTING_NAMES before initialization — the eager version failed on import, measured. Adds HARNESS_GATED_BROWSER_TOOLS (nine names, mirroring GATED_WORKER_TOOLS) and runBrowserToolCall(name, args, gates), which FAILS CLOSED for a gated name when no approval channel is supplied.
  extension/background/service-worker.js — the browser.callTool route binds all four gates to dispatchRoute(..., context), exactly as executeWorkerTool does. The route already had context and simply dropped it.
  scripts/acp-bridge.ts — BROWSER_TOOL_DECLARATIONS is now all 135, GENERATED from browserToolset()'s own descriptions and zod schemas. Committed as data rather than derived at runtime because the bridge CANNOT import that module: it runs under a plain 'deno run -A' with no node_modules resolution and import zod fails (measured). Block costs ~19 KB / ~4.7k tokens, injected once per session.

THE HONEST LIMIT, asserted in its own test rather than glossed: for the six destructive actions a harness gets a bounded REFUSAL today, not an approval card. Two measured reasons — those action names are NOT in OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS, and a harness call arrives with principal 'extension' not 'model', so requireOwnerApproval skips the owner-direct shortcut AND the in-conversation card branch (model-only) and returns its tail 'This operation requires owner approval in Settings.' That is the correct end state for this change (the alternative was an unapproved close/wipe), but it means close/wipe/cookie-mutate are not yet usable from Claude Code. Raising a real card for the harness principal is FOLLOW-ON WORK and is not claimed here. The test exists so nobody reads the headline as 'all 135 work' and nobody later deletes the refusal to make it look finished.

FALSIFICATION — four mutants, sequential, restored and verified clean between each, every guard asserting its target text occurred exactly once:
  M1 permitted set reverted to the old three names -> exit 1, kills the derivation test + the per-name fail-closed test
  M2 fail-closed branch removed (the gate hole)    -> exit 1, kills the per-name fail-closed test
  M3 the ROUTE stops passing gates                 -> exit 1, kills the route-binding test
  M4 close_window dropped so the two gated lists drift -> exit 1, kills the fail-closed test + the mirror test
M3 is the one I would previously have missed: cap-astra has twice caught me testing a helper while nothing bound the call site, so the route handler is SOURCE-EXTRACTED AND EXECUTED with its collaborators injected and the recorded gate arguments + dispatch routes asserted, not regex-matched.

GATES on 4bad1f6d: tests/browser-tool-proxy.test.ts 12 passed / 0 failed · build:production 0 · check:dist 0 · npm run test:changed exit 0 and it FAILED CLOSED to the full suite, so that run IS npm test — 4504 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, 499 files, wall 307s. Bridge verified standalone under plain deno run -A: 135 rows, block 19980 chars, no mcpServers / http:// / https:// strings, the directive-named tools declared.

NOT VERIFIED, stated rather than allowed to pass as done: scripts/kat-browser-tool-proxy.ts drives the real path (real harness -> real bridge -> real Chrome -> chrome.tabGroups) but only calls list_tabs and group_tabs — the two tools that ALREADY worked. There is NO browser-driven evidence yet for any newly-permitted tool. Extending that KAT to drive open_tab/read_page/capture_screenshot end to end is the functional verification this change still owes; it needs the heavy-gate slot and a quiet box. Per the repo mandate, treat the unit evidence as necessary and not sufficient.

Needs an independent verdict from a different model family. Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/cap-wfo5/REPORT.md, mutant-M{1,2,3,4}*.log, test-changed-2.log.

  the harness is TOLD the whole toolset (declared count > 100; was 3)
  open_tab            not refused by the allow-list, and chrome.tabs.query FINDS the opened tab
  read_page           not refused, and returned the REAL page (untrusted:true, url matches, real text)
  capture_screenshot  not refused, and returned real PNG bytes with real width/height

Run 2 on b6f9b457: 22 passed / 0 failed, exit 0, measured window load 11.46 on 32 cores.

RUN 1 WAS 19/21 AND BOTH REDS WERE MINE, recorded rather than quietly re-run. read_page and capture_screenshot failed with 'cannot read the page: the tab's address could not be read' and 'only available on http(s) pages'. UNCHANGED BY THE DRIVE, and now confirmed in a real browser rather than only in unit tests: the six destructive tools (close_tab on a foreign tab, close_window, wipe_browsing_data, remove_bookmark, set_cookie, remove_cookie) return a bounded REFUSAL to a harness caller, not an approval card — their action names are not in OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS and a harness call arrives with principal 'extension', not 'model'. Whether a harness call should be able to raise an approval card at all is a PRODUCT DECISION for the owner and was deliberately not made here.

title: Main red at c34a548e: the skills-panel substring pin dies under b9uh's send→sendFn rename — re-anchor the pin to the contract, and note that a substring pin is invisible to test:changed
description:
OBSERVED. `npm test` at pristine origin/main c34a548e fails one test in the parallel phase: tests/skills-in-settings.test.ts "renderSkillList groups by intent and hands use to onUse" — AssertionError "the list renders from the live recipe.list record" at :68. Proven not environmental: it fails deterministically solo (9 ms, no browser), and it fails at PRISTINE main with no local diff (stash proof).

MECHANISM. The assertion is the substring pin `panel.includes('send("recipe.list")')` over extension/skills/skills-panel.js. 0b7f98ec (b9uh) renamed the panel's send binding to `sendFn`, so the live code at skills-panel.js:75 is now `sendFn("recipe.list").catch(...)` — the literal `send("recipe.list")` no longer occurs anywhere in the file. THE PROPERTY IS INTACT: the list still renders from the live recipe.list record. The pin watched a SPELLING, not the contract — AGENTS.md Test-honesty mode 2/3, and the exact shape of the 1fd1a980 incident (a pin's token re-anchored away by an otherwise-clean lane).

WHY EVERY GATE BEFORE THE FULL SUITE MISSED IT: a substring pin has no import link to the file it watches, so `npm run test:changed` — which selects tests that transitively IMPORT what changed — is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to it. The b9uh/kozg.4 lanes never ran this guard; only the full suite sees it. This is a new, general lesson for the canon: substring pins over a file the test does not import are full-suite-only watchers, so a lane that retires or renames a token owes the grep, because no cheap gate will catch it for them.

FIX (small, mechanical — the d7af497f precedent): re-anchor the pin to the CONTRACT it always guarded — the panel fetches the live recipe.list record regardless of what the send binding is named: `assertMatch(panel, /\bsend\w*\(\s*["'`]recipe\.list["'`]/)`. Falsification: GREEN against the current sendFn spelling; RED when the recipe.list fetch is deleted from the panel entirely (the property the pin exists for), not merely when the binding is renamed again.

ACCEPTANCE: `npm run test:file -- tests/skills-in-settings.test.ts` green solo; full `npm test` green at the tip carrying the fix; the re-anchored pin observed RED under the deleted-fetch mutant and GREEN under both spellings; commit subject carries this bead id; independent review per lifecycle.

title: [P0 EMERGENCY] Multi-task concurrency, in-context approval surface, and orphan-pause resolution
description:
Architectural fix for multi-task concurrency and approval routing:
1. Concurrency: withRunLock must serialize per-thread (threadId || id) rather than globally, so tasks on different threads run in parallel while turns on the same thread stay sequential.
2. Approvals: requireOwnerApproval must fail closed immediately if no UI is open, timeout after 60s, and thread.get must surface pending approvals for reopened threads so approval cards are always reachable.
3. Pause recovery: boot sweep resumes paused-side-effect-uncertain runs with ownerConfirmed: true.
4. Transcript: renderRunTranscript handles approval-request events.

title: Settings boot lands on a blank 'provider server tools' view instead of the providers list — first-click UX broken
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-04 (urgent — about to distribute to first users): clicking the Settings button for the first time lands on a view that just says 'provider server tools' instead of showing the list of providers. The user can't configure their provider because they're stuck on the wrong view.

ROOT CAUSE (likely): the multi-section navigation change (0181699e) introduced lazy section rendering. The first Settings click may land on a section hash that maps to the server-tools sub-panel rather than the main providers list. Combined with the wuvg fix (initProviderServerTools called from ensureSectionRendered('providers')), the server-tools sub-panel may be rendering as the only visible content when the full providers section (with the provider list, API key entry, model picker) should be showing.

FIX: the first Settings click should ALWAYS land on the main providers list (the provider entries with API key fields and model pickers), NOT a sub-panel. The default section hash should be #providers pointing to the full provider management view.

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): fresh install → click Settings → see the providers list (not server tools); enter an API key; press Use; the model is configured. A first user can go from zero to a working agent in under 60 seconds.
notes: 2026-09-05 pi lane: the blank-boot P0 was already fixed on main by 7ff2f479 (09-05 05:59). Verified empirically: parent d898d687 boots to provider-panels with 0 children (the reported blank 'provider server tools' view); HEAD renders tabs+panels+API-key fields through plain tab, #providers hash, and the embedded hub Settings view. Root cause: empty hash normalized to falsy so boot never called ensureSectionRendered('providers') while the panel was statically active. Harness blind spot closed on branch cap-beads-hy91 @ 3748b196 (content assertion, falsification-proven).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED in a real loaded extension (not the multi-section change, not the wuvg server-tools fix).

The hub's Settings button opens options/options.html with NO fragment (extension/ntp/ntp.js:3666); Chrome's own extension Options entry does the same. navigationController.syncCurrent() routed that through handleHashChange, which fails closed when normalizeSettingsSectionId() returns null — correct for a mid-session navigation, fatal on boot: ensureSectionRendered() never ran for ANY section. options.html marks #providers class='panel active' statically, so the panel was visible but completely unbuilt. With developer features on, the only thing still painting inside it is the static 'Provider server tools' card — which is why the owner read it as a provider-server-tools view.

Measured (fresh profile, headless):
  options.html            -> tabs 0, panels 0, provider cards 0
  options.html#providers  -> tabs 1, panels 4, provider cards 7

FIX (branch cap-hy91-settings-boot, off origin/main@d6019129):
- extension/lib/navigation-controller.js: opt-in defaultHash; syncCurrent() falls back to it when the current hash is absent or unresolvable. Mid-session navigate() to an unknown hash still fails closed.
- extension/options/options.js: defaultHash: '#providers'.
- extension/options/options.js: ensureSectionRendered() took its one-shot claim BEFORE awaiting the renderer, so a renderer that threw left that section blank for the life of the page with no retry. The claim is released on failure and the error rethrown.

It now asserts rendered provider cards + key fields + tab strip, and adds a stale-deep-link fallback check. 3/3 RED on the pre-fix bundle; re-running on the rebuilt one.

title: Remove ALL self-imposed size caps across tools, storage, transport, and rendering (owner directive: unlimited)
description:
OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-03 (Telegram, emphatic): 'Don't discard anything, don't limit... Unlimited. I hate all these weird constraints for output and tools and tool call message... there's no real rational argument for why the limits have been chosen. There's been no evidence gathered about what limits should be... This is my extension doing the things I need it to do... No limits please.'

SCOPE: every SELF-IMPOSED size bound in our code. Known inventory (audit to complete this list):
- Tool-argument contract caps (extension/lib/tool-argument-contract.js — per-call byte caps on tool args)
- fs read transport caps (MAX_FS_READ_BYTES 10MiB window cap; MAX_FS_TEXT_DECODE_BYTES 2MiB diff-card decode)
- artifact bounds: 64KiB per-call append cap, 256KiB/4MiB artifact ceilings, serialized-value bound routing
- sandbox preview host 300,000-char discard (p45y finding; removal steered into the p45y r5 revise)
- memory-store per-value/per-store bounds (MAX_VALUE_BYTES 256KiB family; MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES/MAX_THREAD_BYTES threads caps; memory.js:221 8MiB store cap — kmpq started this: payloads by reference; finish removing the rest)
- journalEntry.id 200-char bound, name/description length caps in workflows save
- any MAX_* / maxBytes / char-slice bounds in extension/lib + extension/shared

RULES:
1. REMOVE self-imposed caps outright. Where a REAL platform constraint exists (browser message size, OPFS quota, storage quota), do NOT fake a smaller cap: route around it (chunking, by-reference payloads — the kmpq pattern) and surface the PLATFORM's honest error when the platform itself refuses.
2. The default becomes: store/return/attach COMPLETE data. No 'bounded limit' language anywhere in tool errors.
3. Each removal ships with a falsification test proving the formerly-capped operation succeeds at sizes past the old bound (use the owner's real repro shapes: 9KB reads, 10MiB responses, append-grown artifacts).
4. Keep SECURITY bounds that are not size-related (path traversal, origin-keying, approval gates) — this directive is about SIZE limits only.
5. Audit deliverable: a bead comment listing every constant found, its classification (removed / platform-routed / security-non-size), and the test proving it.

Related already-landed steps: jb0a (read_file), kmpq (journal complete-storage), p45y in-flight (append + preview cap removal). This bead is the umbrella for finishing the sweep everywhere else.

title: [P0] Saving an API key fails in embedded Settings: credential route treats the embedded surface as non-Settings; inline script CSP-blocked; error string passed as the API key
description:
Owner-reported P0, 2026-09-02 (repro + console evidence):

Repro: open the hub (NTP), open Settings via the embedded view (options.html?embedded=1), Providers section, paste a Gemini API key, save. Result: 'Failed — provider credential routes are restricted to the Settings surface — Check the API key in Settings → Providers — it is missing, invalid, or revoked.' EVEN THOUGH the user IS in Settings → Providers.

Console evidence:
1. CSP violations: "Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'" for options.html?embedded=1:9 — an inline script in the embedded Settings page is BLOCKED. The embedded boot path likely never runs, so the page cannot prove it is the Settings surface.
2. The smoking gun: the subsequent fetch is generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models?key=Failed%20%E2%80%94%20provider%20credential%20routes... — the ERROR STRING was passed as the API key. The page-side code caught the route refusal and used the refusal text as the credential value.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis to verify): the credential-route surface check (provider credential routes 'restricted to the Settings surface') inspects the requesting document/surface — the embedded Settings iframe (options.html?embedded=1) fails that check, probably because its boot script (inline, CSP-blocked) never stamped the surface attestation, or because the embedded=1 boot path is classified as non-Settings. Fix BOTH layers:
(a) Remove the inline script from options.html (move to the external boot bundle) so CSP never blocks it;
(b) Fix the surface classifier so options.html?embedded=1 — the REAL Settings surface — passes the credential-route check (the check should accept the settings document by URL/origin regardless of embedding, or consume the boot-stamped attestation).

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): adding a Gemini (and OpenAI-class) key from the EMBEDDED Settings surface succeeds end-to-end (key stored, models list fetch uses the real key); the CSP console violation is gone; the surface check still REFUSES credential routes from genuinely non-Settings surfaces (that regression test must exist and stay green); no inline scripts in any html page (vocabulary/CSP lint). Tests: provider surface-check route tests with an embedded=1 document double; CSP lint over html files.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (upgraded analysis; the inline-CSP theory was secondary): this is a regression from the one-shell merge (2cc00604) — openView now appends ?embedded=1 to every embedded view frame URL (options.html?embedded=1). The owner-surface authorization isExactOptionsSender (extension/lib/pure.js:830) accepts ONLY the bare options.html URL or options.html#<closed-set fragment> — a QUERY STRING never matches (the second branch requires the URL suffix to be exactly a #fragment from OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES). So the embedded Settings page's principal never becomes owner-options and EVERY owner route fails: provider credentials (routes/auth.js:12), tool-catalog diagnostics (SW:5013 — the second symptom the owner reported), tool preview (SW:5033), factory reset (SW:5999,6022). The inline-script CSP violation in the owner's console is a real but SEPARATE pre-existing issue; the auth break is the query-param equality. FIX DIRECTION: normalize the embedded document's URL at boot (history.replaceState to pathname + hash, dropping ?embedded=1) so the sender URL returns to the exact authorized form, OR extend the closed-set check to accept exactly '?embedded=1' (and '?embedded=1#<fragment>') as a product-owned query — the boot-normalize approach is preferred because it keeps sender-URL equality strict regardless of future params. Same acceptance: embedded Settings saves keys, lists tools, previews tools; non-Settings surfaces still refused (regression test).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: MERGED to origin/main @ 2afd3910 (lane cap-csp-inline-fix, commits a19f9796 + 7ba15959 + ce7b32c8). Root cause fixed at the boot layer: embedded-boot.js (shared, external — CSP-safe) sets data-embedded then strips ?embedded=1 via history.replaceState inside iframes, so the document URL returns to the exact form isExactOptionsSender authorizes. Embedded Settings regains owner-options: saving API keys, tool-catalog diagnostics, tool preview all work from the hub again. Non-Settings surfaces are still refused (the exact-document + closed-set-fragment checks are unchanged). Gates on the merged tree: build PASS, full suite 3119/0. Also landed: the CSP lint (no shipped page may carry an inline script — data-src smuggle case covered) and the shared boot file.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: Owner-confirmed: fails on a FRESH Settings panel too (not panel reuse). Narrows to the live request path: identity binding, the provider.test route itself, or the network call it makes. Browser-driven instrumented repro in flight.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (final, confirmed by browser-driven repro + landed fix): Chrome reports an iframe's COMMITTED url (query included) as sender.url on runtime messages — so the earlier boot-time history.replaceState strip could never change what the service worker saw, and isExactOptionsSender kept rejecting the embedded Settings document. THE FIX (cap-p0-provider @ 98134e38, merged to origin/main @ d4265234): embedded views now boot at their EXACT canonical URL with no query at all (openView no longer appends ?embedded=1; embeddedness self-detects via window.self !== top; legacy stored routes with the marker are normalized), and the route error classifier names surface refusals honestly (SettingsSurfaceRequiredError → surface/permission recovery copy) — a surface refusal NEVER reads as provider key blame again. Gates on the merged tree: build PASS, full suite green. Owner instructions: pull, npm run build, reload the unpacked extension, reopen Settings from the hub, Test connection. If the test still fails it will now say the REAL reason (e.g. network/host permission) instead of key blame.

title: [CAP-FB-20260901-READ-PAGE-HOST-GRANT-01] read_page on a site without host access returns a raw Chrome error instead of the Allow card
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260901-READ-PAGE-HOST-GRANT-01] read_page on a site without host access returns a raw Chrome error instead of the Allow card
- Feedback: 2026-09-01 — owner's run log: `execute_tool:2` → `read_page` on tab 1840671856 returned `{"error":"Cannot access contents of the page. Extension manifest must request permission to access the respective host."}`; no permission card appeared, the model moved on, and the digest silently omitted that site. "I can't see the error in the UI".
- Updated: 2026-09-01 22:23 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: model worker (Fable 5 subagent) under the reanalysis coordinator session — CLAIMED; do not start a parallel attempt
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/read-page-host-grant` (pushed to origin as the candidate branch; merged by the coordinator)
- Base: `ffaac6af`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: `read_page` (and every tool that injects into a page: the page-action family, `capture_screenshot`) on an origin the extension has no host access for returns the structured permission denial (`permissionDenial(..., {grantOrigins:[origin]})`) so ONE Allow card renders in the conversation naming the site; Allow grants that origin via `chrome.permissions.request` on the owner's click and the run resumes and reads the page; Deny leaves a readable error line ("Not allowed to read example.com — you declined") on the card. Privileged URLs (`chrome://`, the Web Store) still fail closed with the existing message. The raw Chrome string never reaches the model or the owner.
  - Context: `CAP-FB-20260830-HOST-ACCESS-STORY-01` (DONE) made host access optional, so a fresh profile has NO host permissions. `extension/lib/browser-tools.js:923` `readPage` checks only `hasScriptingPermission()` (`:925`) then calls `chrome.scripting.executeScript` (`:932`); the host-permission failure is caught at `:946` and returned as `{error: String(e.message)}` — a plain error, not the `permissionDenial` shape that `CAP-FB-20260830-DENIAL-TO-GRANT-CARD-01` (DONE) turns into the in-conversation Allow card (compare `close_tab` at `browser-tools.js:2248-2252`, which returns `permissionDenial(..., {grantOrigins:[origin]})`). `agent.js:1052` `onPermissionRequest` blocks the run on that shape until the owner decides, and the SW persists `permissionRequirement` on the row (`service-worker.js:2678-2688`) so a reopened thread re-renders the card. What must NOT change: the privileged-URL block (PRIVILEGED-URL-BLOCK-01); the browser-control grant semantics (host access ≠ browser control — reading a page needs host access + `scripting`; acting needs browser control too); one card per distinct origin per run (the card dedupes on `requirement.key`).
  - Reproduce today: fresh profile, real provider, open `https://example.com`, run "Read the page in the example.com tab and summarise it" → the tool card (if visible) says "Cannot access contents of the page…", no Allow card, the model apologises.
  - Files: `extension/lib/browser-tools.js` (`readPage` 923: resolve the target tab, derive `canonicalOrigin(tab.url)`, `chrome.permissions.contains({origins:[origin + "/*"]})` → if false return `permissionDenial("host access not granted for <origin>", {reason: "read the page on <host>", grantOrigins:[origin], permissions:["scripting"]})`; the same pre-check in the page-action family's shared injector and in `captureTabScreenshot`; keep the catch at `:946` as a backstop that maps the "Cannot access contents" message to the same denial shape); `extension/lib/permission-approval*.js` / the grant path behind the card (the Allow handler must call `chrome.permissions.request({origins})` on the click — verify it already does for `grantOrigins` and add it if it only handles `permissions`); `extension/ntp/ntp.js` (nothing if the card path is shared); tests.
  - Steps: (1) unit RED-first: `tests/browser-tools-read-page.test.ts` (new or nearest) with a fake `chrome.permissions.contains` returning false → `readPage` returns the denial shape with `grantOrigins:["https://example.com"]`; with the raw executeScript rejection → the same shape (backstop). (2) Implement. (3) Journey: seeded profile WITHOUT host access for the fixture origin; scripted provider calls `read_page` → the Allow card names the site; click Allow (the harness pre-grants via `test-manifest-pregranted` the way `scripts/webmcp-acceptance.ts:54` documents, since headless cannot show the native prompt) → the run resumes and the transcript contains the page text; click Deny in a second run → the card shows the declined line and the model's final text mentions the site could not be read. (4) Screenshot `read-page-allow-card.png`, `read-page-denied.png`.
  - Out of scope: `list_tabs` (needs only `tabs`); WebMCP tool calls (their own consent path); making host access install-time again (rejected by HOST-ACCESS-STORY-01).
- Review: pending
- Gates: the falsification gates apply
  - Unit: as Steps (1). Falsification: revert the `permissions.contains` pre-check → "returns the denial shape" RED → restore → GREEN.
  - Browser: the two journey checks in Steps (3) in `EXPECTED`; the named screenshots.
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test -A tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green.
  - Constraints: one Allow card per origin per run; the grant is requested on the owner's click only (a user gesture — never pre-emptively); the card copy names the site and the reason; no emoji; fail closed on privileged URLs.
- Blockers: —
- Next: the `readPage` pre-check + unit test, then confirm the card's Allow handler requests origins.
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep=CAP-FB-20260901-READ-PAGE-HOST-GRANT-01`
- History:
  - 2026-09-01 20:30 UTC — opened from the owner's run log. Verified at `origin/main@ffaac6af`: `browser-tools.js:923-948` checks `scripting` only and returns the caught message as `{error}`.
  - 2026-09-01 22:23 UTC — CLAIMED by the reanalysis coordinator; worker started in its own worktree on `cap/read-page-host-grant` off `origin/main@ffaac6af`. Other agents: pick a different entry.

title: [CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01] A run stops after four to six tool actions — the lazy protocol charges two steps per action, selection refs are single-use, and the budget is invisible
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01] A run stops after four to six tool actions — the lazy protocol charges two steps per action, selection refs are single-use, and the budget is invisible
- Feedback: 2026-09-01 — owner, same 30-tab research run: "it certainly doesn't go through all of them", "whatever is happening ends too early, it should go through every tab", "I get a lot of selection-replayed errors and I've no idea what it means", "list_tabs, I'm not sure it gets all the tabs". The run log shows 8 `execute_tool` calls (two of them `selection-replayed`), 6 `search_tools` calls, and a digest written after reading two pages.
- Updated: 2026-09-01 22:23 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: model worker (Fable 5 subagent) under the reanalysis coordinator session — CLAIMED; do not start a parallel attempt
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/run-budget-every-item` (pushed to origin as the candidate branch; merged by the coordinator)
- Base: `ffaac6af`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: With 30 open tabs and "read every tab and produce a sourced digest", a run on gemini-3.7-flash reads every readable tab (one `read_page` per tab, no `selection-replayed`, no repeated `search_tools` for a tool it already holds) and the digest cites every readable tab; the conversation shows a step counter ("Step 34 of 80") while working and, if the budget is exhausted, a "Budget reached — Continue" card that resumes the same thread with the same context rather than a silent finish. Protocol errors the model or owner can see are sentences with a next action, never a bare token like `selection-replayed`.
  - Context: three compounding causes. (1) Budget: `extension/lib/agent.js:536` `maxIterations = 12` (the hub default — `service-worker.js:2457` passes 12 when unset; named agents `routes/agent-worker.js:196` same default, capped 64) and `agent.js:947` `innerStepLimit: Math.max(2, Math.min(maxIterations, 8))` — one inner turn is at most 8 model steps, and the lazy protocol costs TWO model steps per logical tool action (`search_tools` then `execute_tool`; the comment at 944-946 says so), so a turn fits ~4 tool actions. (2) Single-use refs: `extension/lib/tool-selection.js:271-290` `claim` deletes the record on first use and any reuse is `selection-replayed` (`:243`); `release` (`:298`) hands it back ONLY on argument-validation failure (`lazy-tool-protocol.js:852-857`), not on a tool-level failure (the owner's log: `execute_tool:5` failed with "No tab with id", the model retried the same ref at `:7` → replayed). A ref authorizes nothing (`authorizes:false, requiresLiveAuthorization:true` at `:198-200`, and `authorizeRecord` runs live per call at `lazy-tool-protocol.js:863`), so single-use buys no security — it only forces a `search_tools` round-trip before EVERY call and doubles the step cost. `TOOL_SELECTION_BOUNDS.maxSelectionsPerRun: 32` (`tool-selection.js:13`) is a further hard ceiling of 32 tool actions per run. (3) Opaque errors: `selection-replayed`, `selection-missing-or-expired`, `selection-scope-mismatch`, `selection-catalog-stale`, `selection-source-stale` (`tool-selection.js:239-260`) reach the model and the card as bare tokens. What must NOT change: live authorization per call; the run-bound scope check (`sameContext`); the catalog-generation staleness check; the per-run ceilings stay bounded (raise, do not remove); the fence on untrusted results.
  - Reproduce today: open 30 tabs (any), run "Read every open tab and produce a sourced digest" on a real provider; count `execute_tool` rows in the run log (≤ 8) and `selection-replayed` rows (≥ 1 whenever a tool call fails and the model retries); observe the run finishes with a digest that cites 2-3 tabs and no UI element says why it stopped.
  - Files: `extension/lib/tool-selection.js` (a ref is REUSABLE for the same tool within its run until `expiresAt`: replace the delete-on-claim with a per-ref `uses` counter bounded by a new `maxUsesPerSelection: 64`; keep `#consumed` for refs that hit the bound so the error stays honest; `defaultTtlMs` 60 s → 10 min (a 30-tab loop takes longer than a minute), `maxTtlMs` 15 min; `maxSelectionsPerRun` 32 → 128; every error token gains a `message` sibling in plain English with the next action, e.g. `selection-replayed` → "This selection reference has been used 64 times; call search_tools once more for a fresh one"); `extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js` (release the claim on a tool-level failure as well as on validation failure, so a failed call never burns the ref; surface `message` in the error result the model sees); `extension/lib/agent.js` (`maxIterations` default 12 → 48 for interactive hub runs, `innerStepLimit` → `Math.max(2, Math.min(maxIterations, 24))`; emit `{type:"budget", step, total}` progress so the UI can count); `extension/background/service-worker.js` (the run's step budget as a run-log field; when exhausted, the terminal carries `errorCategory:"budget"` with `errorAction:"Continue"` — the thread's existing terminal/action wiring renders it; a `run.continue` route resumes the thread with the same executionId lineage (the durable resume path already exists — reuse it)); `extension/lib/master-skill.js` (the operating manual: "A selection reference works for every call of that tool for the rest of the run — do not search again for a tool you already hold"; "When asked for every item, iterate every item; say which items you could not read and why"); `extension/shared/components.js` (`<conversation-run-status>` shows "Step N of M"; the budget card reuses the approval-card chrome with one Continue button); `extension/lib/browser-tools.js` (`list_tabs` 2202: add `windowId`, `groupId`, `active`, `index`, and a `count` field so the model and the owner can verify completeness; verify `chrome.tabs.query({})` spans every window — record the count in the History line); tests.
  - Steps: (1) unit RED-first: `tests/tool-selection.test.ts` — "a ref resolves for a second execute of the same tool", "the 65th use is selection-replayed with a message", "a tool-level failure releases the ref"; `tests/lazy-tool-protocol*.test.ts` — the error result carries `message`. (2) Implement the reusable ref + release-on-failure + messages. (3) Budget: raise defaults, emit the budget event, terminal `errorCategory:"budget"` + Continue. (4) Manual text. (5) `list_tabs` completeness fields. (6) Journey (scripted provider): a 12-tab fixture, the demo model iterates 12 `read_page` calls with ONE `search_tools` → 12 `execute_tool` rows, 0 replayed; a run whose budget is 4 → the Continue card renders and clicking it produces a second execution on the same thread. (7) Live check on gemini-3.7-flash with 30 real tabs (keys in ~/.env; never log them): every readable tab read; record counts.
  - Out of scope: the host-permission denial on `read_page` (CAP-FB-20260901-READ-PAGE-HOST-GRANT-01); provider-side context limits (a 30-page context on a small model may need summarisation — record it as a finding, do not solve it here); the pipeline lane (TOOL-PIPELINES-01) which is the structural fix for loops.
- Review: pending

  - Browser: the two journey checks in Steps (6) added to `EXPECTED`; screenshots `run-budget-step-counter.png`, `run-budget-continue-card.png`, `every-tab-digest.png` (the live 30-tab run's transcript, tabs count visible).
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test -A tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green; `deno run -A scripts/security-injection*.ts` (the fence probe) still green since results stay fenced.
  - Constraints: every bound stays finite and named in `TOOL_SELECTION_BOUNDS` / `LAZY_TOOL_PROTOCOL_BOUNDS`; no authorization is cached across calls; the manual stays under its byte budget (MODEL-CALL-ECONOMY-01 measures it — add no more than 300 bytes); no eval.

title: [CAP-FB-20260901-APPROVAL-RESUME-REEXECUTES-01] After the owner clicks Allow, the paused tool call is not re-run — the model is told to "retry with a fresh search_tools selection" and the string leaks into the transcript
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260901-APPROVAL-RESUME-REEXECUTES-01] After the owner clicks Allow, the paused tool call is not re-run — the model is told to "retry with a fresh search_tools selection" and the string leaks into the transcript
- Feedback: 2026-09-01 — found by the EXEC-DEMO-01 rehearsal (worker, headed and headless): after Allow on the in-chat browser-control card, the resumed run's `group_tabs` card reads "Error: Owner approved the requested capability, but this attempt did not run. Retry group_tabs now with a fresh search_tools selection." The `demo-path: step 1` journey check is red on exactly this (forbidden string `search_tools` in the thread); the sibling `create_asset` call issued alongside the paused call fails on resume with a raw `selection-scope-mismatch` card and the artifact is dropped.
- Updated: 2026-09-01 23:00 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: model worker (Fable 5 subagent) under the reanalysis coordinator session — CLAIMED; do not start a parallel attempt
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/approval-resume-reexecutes` (pushed to origin as the candidate branch; merged by the coordinator)
- Base: `a52315fa`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: When the owner approves a permission card, the paused tool call is executed by the runtime with its ORIGINAL arguments and the model receives that tool's real result as if the call had succeeded first time — no "retry" instruction, no second `search_tools`, no `search_tools`/`selection-*` string anywhere in the transcript. Sibling tool calls issued in the same model step are not invalidated by the pause (they run, or are re-run, under the same run scope). Deny and expiry keep their current terminal sentences. The card shows the tool's real outcome (e.g. "Grouped 3 tabs into Web Development"). `demo-path: step 1` goes green.
  - Context: `extension/lib/agent.js:1051-1071` — `onPostToolUse` awaits `onPermissionRequest(permissionDenial)`; on `approved` it rewrites `modelContent` to the retry sentence (`:1061`) and `userSummary` to "BLOCKED — approved; retry required" (`:1066`) instead of re-dispatching. The comment at `:1055-1057` explains why: the lazy protocol's grant digest changed while the call was paused, so the OLD selectionRef no longer resolves (`extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js` `authorizeRecord` "before-validation"/"after-validation" and the catalog-generation check in `extension/lib/tool-selection.js:250`). The fix is to re-execute inside the runtime: after `approved`, call the same executor the loop uses (`executeWorkerTool` in `extension/background/service-worker.js` for hub runs, or the lazy protocol's `execute` with a runtime-issued fresh selection for the SAME stableId + the ORIGINAL validated args) and put THAT result into `e.result` — the model never learns a pause happened. The sibling failure: a second tool call in the same step resolves its ref after the generation bump → `selection-scope-mismatch`; with the re-execution path the runtime must re-issue refs for in-flight calls of the same step (or CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01's reusable refs must survive a generation bump when the descriptor's stableId is unchanged — coordinate: land whichever comes first, keep both). What must NOT change: the approval binds the digest of the exact requested capability; a denied/expired call is never executed; the re-execution runs under the SAME run fence, grant lock and untrusted fence as any tool call; one card per distinct requirement.
  - Reproduce today: `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` at `origin/cap/exec-demo@b6898cba` → `demo-path: step 1 groups tabs and renders sentences` prints `forbidden=["search_tools"]` and FAILS; headed: fresh profile, real model, "Group my open tabs by topic…", click Allow → the `group_tabs` card shows the retry sentence, the model calls `search_tools` again, and the artifact from the parallel `create_asset` is lost.
  - Files: `extension/lib/agent.js` (`onPostToolUse` ~1051: on `approved`, re-execute and replace `e.result` with the real result; keep `permissionRequirement`/`permissionDecision` on the progress event so the card still records the grant; add a `reexecuted:true` marker on the event for the card's "approved, then ran" line); `extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js` (a runtime-only `reexecute({stableId, args, context})` that issues its own selection, bypassing the model-facing search; scoped so a page/model principal can never call it); `extension/background/service-worker.js` (thread the re-execute dispatcher into `createAgent` like `onPermissionRequest`); `extension/shared/components.js` (the tool card: status `done` with a small "approved by you, then ran" caption — no new component); `tests/agent-permission-resume.test.ts` (new); the `demo-path` group already on `cap/exec-demo` is the browser gate.
  - Steps: (1) unit RED-first with a fake tool that returns `permissionDenial` once then succeeds: "approved → the event's result is the tool's real result and modelContent contains neither `search_tools` nor `Retry`", "denied → unchanged terminal sentence", "a sibling call in the same step still completes". (2) implement the re-execution. (3) merge `cap/exec-demo`'s journey group (or rebase onto it) and show `demo-path: step 1` green. (4) headed re-check of script step 1 with gemini-3.7-flash: one card, Allow, grouped, no retry text — screenshot `approval-resume-reexecuted.png`.
  - Out of scope: the number of cards per step (CAP-FB-20260901-ONE-CARD-PER-STEP-01); WebMCP call consent (CAP-FB-20260901-WEBMCP-CALL-CONSENT-01).
- Review: pending
- Gates: the falsification gates apply
  - Unit: as Steps (1). Falsification: revert the re-execution (restore the retry sentence) → "result is the tool's real result" RED → restore → GREEN.
  - Browser: `demo-path: step 1 groups tabs and renders sentences` (from `cap/exec-demo`) PASS; screenshot `approval-resume-reexecuted.png`.
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test -A tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green at the tip INCLUDING the three demo-path checks.
  - Constraints: never execute a denied/expired call; re-execution only from the runtime (no model-callable route); the run fence/grant lock/untrusted fence apply; no new strings from the protocol vocabulary reach the model or the owner.
- Blockers: —
- Next: the unit test + re-execution in `agent.js`, then land together with the `cap/exec-demo` journey group.
