comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-arch-0eq00
comments.text:
ARCHITECT DESIGN for chrome-agent-platform-0eq00 (arch-0eq00, read-only audit at worktree HEAD 73ea41ba; origin/main 612a25b2 fetched 2026-10-14; NO build/gate/Chrome run by architect). Cross-refs: hub fleet-1ojy.2 authoritative measurements in coord comments 2026-10-13; cached-gate coverage measurement via coord 2026-10-14.

== EVIDENCE (source-audited) ==
Gate config (authoritative, env-scoped): ~/.fleet/check-chrome-agent-platform.conf (read via FLEET_CHECK_CONF; machine-global ~/.fleet/check.conf currently holds agents-factory tools/{full,fast}-gate.sh and is NOT the CAP gate):
  FULL: npm run build:production && npm test && npm run test:build
  FAST: npm run build:production && npm run test:changed
Local cache ~/.fleet/checks (289 records): FULL n=99 PASS-median 437s; FAST n=190 PASS-median 153s (hub: latest 139s). 146 PASS records have coverage ABSENT; 94 records carry coverage{suites,unmapped,omitted,changed,indeterminate}; sampled PASS coverage shows suites:[] with unmapped non-empty — producer schema is not yet truthful (see LEDGER).
Where the duplicate ~95s build is: NOT twice inside one command. It is paid once per tier per change: FAST prefix build:production, then merger FULL prefix build:production again (~95s each, ~190s/change lifecycle). Inside FULL, npm test does NOT rebuild a third time when the record is valid: tests/build-smoke.test.ts via storeBuildOnce runs-or-REUSES the build-once record build.mjs writes only on exit 0 (keyed commit+source-authority, marker re-validated). test:build (scripts/build-gate.ts: build-bootstrap/build-debug-mode/build-tool-bundling) runs its own in-place builds BY DESIGN — that is build-behaviour coverage, not duplication; do not touch.
Freshness authority already exists: scripts/dist-complete.mjs validateDistCompleteMarker binds EXACT commit (line 536: marker.commit !== gitCommit(root) throws stale), every indexed source byte, outputs, target=store. Any commit (incl. version-bump hook) invalidates. Serial phase of npm test already fails on stale marker.

== DECISION (a) — remove/reuse, FAST saving first ==
1. FAST tier: replace unconditional `build:production &&` prefix with BUILD-IF-NEEDED:
   - Step 1: run selector in plan mode (scripts/select-tests.mjs selection without executing) to get selected set + changed set + unmapped set.
   - Build REQUIRED iff: selection intersects dist-consumers (READ_ONLY_DIST in scripts/test-partition.mjs, tests/build-smoke.test.ts, any SERIAL dist reader) OR changed set intersects build inputs (build.mjs, scripts/dist-complete.mjs, scripts/lib/build-*, extension/** shipped sources, package.json non-version fields, deno*.jsonc) OR unmapped non-empty (fail-closed path runs full suite, which requires build).
   - Build NOT required: record omission in ledger (below) with reason `no selected test consumes dist and no build input changed`.
   - If build required: VALIDATE-OR-BUILD — validate dist.complete for exact HEAD; reuse if valid (same commit+source bytes ⇒ identical artifact authority), build only if absent/stale/invalid. Never re-stamp a marker without building.
   Expected FAST saving: ~95s on non-dist changes (FAST PASS median 153s → ~55-60s target; hub latest-PASS basis 139s → ~45s). FALSIFIER: if implementer measurement on 3+ real non-dist changes shows <60s saved, or any selected dist-consumer ran against stale dist, design is wrong — revert to unconditional build.
2. FULL tier: keep build, but same VALIDATE-OR-BUILD seam. Honest limit: marker binds exact commit, so merger union commit ≠ branch commit ⇒ reuse almost never hits across tiers; FULL saving expected near zero on union trees. Do NOT weaken commit binding to tree-only: version-bump hook mutates package.json/manifest source bytes per commit, so tree-only reuse would need a separate determinism proof (unknown, out of scope). FULL win comes from FAST no longer pre-paying + fewer full re-runs, not from union reuse. If coord wants union reuse, that is a NEW bead requiring byte-determinism evidence of build.mjs outputs for identical source bytes under different commit ids.
3. test:build's internal builds: necessary, measured reason = they ARE the subject under test (mode alternation, symlink bootstrap, regen idempotence). Exempt from reuse.

== DECISION (b) — coverage/omission ledger, fail closed ==
Every gate record (fast and full) MUST carry producer-written coverage{suites:[{name,files,executed}], omitted:[{file,reason}], unmapped:[], changed:[], build:{ran|reused|omitted, reason, markerCommit}, indeterminate:bool}. Tier ledger:
  test:file — executes: named file only. Omits: everything else, reason `inner-loop single file`. Never a gate.
  test:changed (FAST) — executes: ALWAYS_ON core + tests transitively importing merge-base..HEAD changes (+tree-walking guards for unimported scripts/*.ts harnesses; version-only JSON diff maps to data-readers — existing nco2 behaviour). Omits: unselected tests, each reason `no import path from changed set`. FAIL CLOSED to full suite when: unmapped executable/config non-empty, selector machinery itself changed, git comparison fails, or build required but marker invalid after build. A missing/unreadable ledger = NOT PASS.
  npm test (FULL unit) — executes: every tests/*.test.ts exactly once via test-partition (serial → read-only-dist → parallel), minus BUILD_GATE and HEAVY_GATE partitions. Omits: build-gate 3 files (reason: `dedicated test:build tier, same FULL command`), heavy files (reason: `test:heavy NOT in FULL command — see risk`).

title: Double-iframe HTML artifact embeds: proxy user-gesture external window.open/link navigation and clipboard writes safely through sandbox host
description:
Owner report (2026-10-12): HTML artifact / generate_ui embeds rendered in the double-iframe sandbox (about:srcdoc inside sandbox/artifact-preview.html) break on two essential user-gesture actions needed by interactive agent-generated pages (such as a social media agent page built from Chrome History that copies drafts and posts to X):
1) Opening a new window/tab via window.open(...) or clicking external <a href> links fails silently because navigationGuardScript() stubs window.open to return null and calls stopPropagation() on anchor clicks in capture phase, and the inner/outer iframes use sandbox="allow-scripts" without allow-popups.
2) Calling navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) fails with:
   [Violation] Permissions policy violation: The Clipboard API has been blocked because of a permissions policy applied to the current document (crbug.com/414348233)
   NotAllowedError: Failed to execute 'writeText' on 'Clipboard'

Architecture & Acceptance Criteria:
1. Inner srcdoc bridge (components-core.js navigationGuardScript + preferenceBootstrapScript):
   - Track genuine user activation (navigator.userActivation.isActive or recent trusted pointer/keyboard gesture) inside the closure alongside the frame's one-time nonce.
   - Proxy navigator.clipboard.writeText(text) and document.execCommand('copy') over postMessage (type: 'cap:artifact-action', action: 'clipboard-write', nonce, requestId, text, userGesture: true) and resolve/reject the returned Promise from 'cap:artifact-action-result', eliminating the Permissions Policy violation. Reject without user gesture.
   - Proxy window.open(url, target, features) and user-activated external <a href>/<area href> clicks over postMessage (type: 'cap:artifact-action', action: 'open-external', nonce, requestId, url, userGesture: true) after validating URL scheme (https:, http:, mailto: only; no credentials; no javascript:/data:/blob:/file:/chrome:/chrome-extension:), returning a non-null window stub from window.open when allowed and null when blocked/unactivated.
   - Stop calling stopPropagation() on capture-phase anchor clicks in navigationGuardScript so page-level onclick handlers on <a href> can execute while default frame navigation remains prevented.
2. Middle sandbox host (extension/sandbox/artifact-preview.js):
   - Validate 'cap:artifact-action' from active.frame.contentWindow (matching nonce, non-thumbnail frame, userGesture === true, bounded requestId, strict URL/text validation) before relaying to window.parent, and relay 'cap:artifact-action-result' back down to active.frame.contentWindow.
3. Privileged extension host (extension/shared/components-core.js wireHtmlFrameContent + components-artifacts.js ArtifactInspector):
   - Verify source === iframe.contentWindow, matching nonce, non-thumbnail frame, rate limits, and payload safety (validateSafeExternalUrl / bounded clipboard text).
   - Execute clipboard write via writeHostClipboard(text) (navigator.clipboard.writeText with focused offscreen textarea execCommand('copy') fallback) and external URL open via openSafeExternalUrl(url) (chrome.tabs.create with window.open(..., '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer') fallback), then post 'cap:artifact-action-result' back to the frame.
   - Fix ArtifactInspector.startPreview() in extension/shared/components-artifacts.js to wire HTML frame content properly.
4. Verification:
   - Unit falsification tests in tests/frame-guards.test.ts, tests/security.test.ts, tests/components.test.ts, and updated wildcard inventory in tests/postmessage-wildcard-guard.test.ts.
   - Real headless Chromium CDP test proving a double-iframe embed can copy draft text via navigator.clipboard.writeText and open an external https://x.com/intent/tweet?... URL on user click while blocking javascript:/chrome-extension: and unactivated calls.
close_reason: Closed

title: 0om0o review-finding (deepseek): parked-daemon suppression is unreachable in the production boot-staging path
description:
REVIEWER(deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro) independent review of chrome-agent-platform-0om0o @ c88806f97 (merge-base 01fa6ab3f).

P1: The fix's parked-daemon suppression is UNREACHABLE in the sole production path, so the reported live bug is not fixed by this diff.

Evidence:
- The only real-browser caller of attributeBootRun is tests/ntp-boot-staging.test.ts (git grep: no scripts/ harness; only tests/ntp-boot-staging.test.ts + tests/ntp-boot-attribution.test.ts).
- That caller establishes a baseline BEFORE the boot interval: `const baselineSample = await readLoadSample(); ... let currentSample = await readLoadSample(baselineSample.cpu ?? null)` (lines 172-174). `readLoadSample(prev)` sets `unbaselined: prev == null`. currentSample is read against baselineSample.cpu (a non-null Map), so `currentSample.unbaselined === false`.
- The new suppression branch requires `const isInitialSample = ... sample === allSamples[0]` AND `const isUnbaselined = sample.unbaselined !== false` (scripts/lib/ntp-boot-attribution.ts ~404-405). For the production first sample, `unbaselined !== false` is `false !== false` === false, so the branch is skipped.
- If baselineSample is instead unmeasurable, it is unshifted to intervalSamples[0], and attributeBootRun fails closed as "unmeasurable host load" before hasActiveBuilder is consulted — still never reaching the suppression.

Consequence: the live failure log the bead cites (`heavy-builders=2 active=0[esbuild]` excluded) came from an INTERMEDIATE sample with activeCompilers>0, which this diff's isInitialSample guard explicitly excludes from suppression. The author's premise ("initial samples taken without a prior CPU map (prev == null)") does not match the production code, which DOES establish a prior CPU map. The diff therefore changes only unit-test-level behavior for a hypothetical unbaselined-initial path the production gate never takes.

Suggested fix: determine whether the intermediate active>0 was (a) genuine tick advance (then exclusion was correct and the bead is a false alarm) or (b) a baseline-reset artifact from a transient /proc read failure mid-loop. If (b), suppress/re-baseline mid-interval unbaselined samples (or make failedSample carry forward the prior cpu map), rather than only the initial sample. Re-run the real-browser gate with instrumentation to confirm the actual mechanism before closing.
close_reason: Resolved in fleet/qazo-0om0o @ 0e4bc7619: Re-rooted suppression across the entire boot interval so intermediate samples in samplingLoop seeing parked daemons (0 CPU ticks advanced from boot start to settling) are admitted as valid, while retaining contention detection on baselined initial samples with real activity. Added intermediate parked daemon unit test and verified against live real-browser tests/ntp-boot-staging.test.ts (all 5 runs validMeasurement=true).

title: z4tzw review-finding: APP_READY_EXPRESSION providersHydrated is vacuous vs real provider-select
description:
REVIEW-FINDING (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, independent) against chrome-agent-platform-z4tzw @ 6dcbcf0a5.

The board-permissions providersHydrated signal in scripts/lib/app-readiness.ts is VACUOUS against the real <provider-select> component.

Evidence:
- scripts/lib/app-readiness.ts (new code): `providersHydrated = !!agentSelect && (Array.isArray(agentSelect.providers) || !!agentSelect.getAttribute?.("providers"))`.
- extension/shared/components-settings.js:791: `get providers() { return parseJSONAttr(this.getAttribute("providers"), []); }`.
- extension/shared/components-core.js:121-126: `parseJSONAttr(null, [])` returns the `[]` fallback.

So once the custom element is upgraded (which happens during options.js module eval, before readyState==="complete"), `agentSelect.providers` is ALWAYS an array — `[]` when populateBoardDenyAgents has not yet set the attribute. `Array.isArray([]) === true`, so providersHydrated is true BEFORE the providers list is populated. The probe certifies ready as soon as the section is active + element upgraded, NOT once the providers array is populated (contradicting the LAND-SUMMARY claim and the code comment).

Reproduction (standalone, in /tmp extraction): evaluating APP_READY_EXPRESSION against a mock where agentSelect.providers getter returns `[]` and getAttribute("providers") is null (upgraded-but-unpopulated), with section active + addBtn present, returns `{ready:true, signal:"options-hydrated"}`.

The regression test's "unpopulated" mock is `{ tagName:"PROVIDER-SELECT", id:"board-deny-agent" }` with NO `providers` property, so it models "unpopulated" as `providers === undefined`, not the real `providers === []`. The test passes against a probe that is vacuous against reality (green-by-wrong-mechanism).

Smallest fix: `providersHydrated = !!agentSelect && (Array.isArray(agentSelect.providers) ? agentSelect.providers.length > 0 : !!agentSelect.getAttribute?.("providers"))` (populateBoardDenyAgents always appends at least the "hub" entry, so length >= 1 post-populate). Also update the test's unpopulated mock to model the real getter (providers getter returning []) so the falsification test actually discriminates.

Severity: P1.

title: site-docs-fallback extractMarkdownLinks is still O(N^2) via lastIndexOf rescan — e7gwq linear-scan fix incomplete
description:
What: extension/lib/site-docs-fallback.js extractMarkdownLinks (commit 0e54d122f, bead e7gwq) is NOT linear — it is O(N^2). lastIndexOf("[", closeBracket) rescans backward to a stale "[" on every "openBracket < i" step, so a crafted llms.txt drives quadratic rescanning. The fix is a lateral move: the OLD regex was also quadratic (on "[x](" + "a".repeat(N), confirmed ~4x time per doubling), and the NEW scanner is quadratic on a different input.

Repro (measured, exact committed file):
parseLlmsTxt("[x](y)" + "](".repeat(N)) — N=128000 (256KB) => 5.6s; N=250000 (500KB, inside the 512KiB MAX_DISCOVERY_DOC_BYTES ceiling) => 21.3s. Time ~4x per doubling of N. This stalls the extension service worker — the exact MEDIUM DoS this bead exists to fix.

Why the ceilings don't save it: maxLinks=256 does not bound the loop (the openBracket<i path pushes no URLs, so urls.length stays 0), and the break-on-missing-")" is skipped on that path. The byte ceiling only caps input length; the quadratic blow-up is within the 512KiB budget.

Acceptance: replace with a genuinely O(N) single forward pass (scan chars once; look up the opening bracket in a bounded window or track the last "[" as you advance — never a full backward lastIndexOf per candidate). Add a falsification input of the "[x](y)" + "](".repeat(N) form that times out (or violates a time bound) under the current code and passes under the fixed scanner.
close_reason: Closed

title: beads-landing-link SOURCE-BOUND test is wedged by merge boundaries + landingLinks --no-merges
description: The SOURCE-BOUND case runs landingLinks over origin/main~30..origin/main and requires >=15 unique beads. landingLinks uses `git log --no-merges`, but the LANDING commit is usually the MERGE whose subject names the bead, so merges are excluded and bead-less bookkeeping commits (release bumps, integration fixes, changelog retitles) advance the first-parent window and drop bead-naming side commits out of it. On 2026-10-09 the merger's r65i bookkeeping commits dropped the count to 14 (<15), wedging EVERY landing (it had passed on the previous gate at origin/main 0e8324e41). The first-parent window is also topology-sensitive: ~30 gives 14 unique beads (no merges), ~32 gives 45, a cliff at a merge boundary. FIX (bounded one-off, authorized by coord, non-weakening): evaluate the same window over BOTH merge and non-merge commits (extractBeadRefs + groupByBead on a plain git log), threshold UNCHANGED at 15. Counts: ~30 window with merges = 23 beads; neighbourhood 25..31 = 19,20,20,21,23,23, so margin >15. landingLinks itself is unchanged (its --no-merges is right for its report). PROCESS RULE adopted: merger bookkeeping commits SHOULD name the bead they serve.

title: WebMCP fixtures/polyfills defensive shadowing on Chrome 154: document.modelContext getter shadows bare assignment
description: Chrome for Testing 154.0.8037.92 ships a NATIVE getter-only document.modelContext on Document.prototype (registerTool/getTools/executeTool/ontoolchange; navigator.modelContext undefined). The repo's three fixtures install their polyfill with a bare assignment (fixtures/webmcp-fixture.html:23, fixtures/webmcp-errors.html:84, fixtures/showcase-shop.html:187) which sloppy-mode discards against an accessor with no setter, so document.modelContext.getTools() returns [] on 154. Measured: registerTool natively works with NO launch flag; --disable-features=WebMCP restores all 11 polyfill tools. Consequence: scripts/webmcp-acceptance.ts (npm run test:webmcp, harness-registry.ts:110 claims 82/0) launches with NO WebMCP flag, so its declared-tool assertions should now be RED (recorded on a pre-154 browser). Fix: switch the fixtures to native registerTool (or Object.defineProperty to shadow the getter) and confirm npm run test:webmcp. Do NOT rely on --enable-features=WebMCP (no-op on 154). Found by coord scout while unblocking ckebt (j5yz ckebt browser probe: getTools() returned [] despite inline happy_echo).
close_reason: Closed

title: Make the full test gate fast: parallel phase regressed 390s -> 685-1063s, flaky real-browser tests fail gates (owner directive)
description:
Owner directive (Paul, 2026-10-08): the test infrastructure is not optimised; make the full gate fast. jjsz LANDED (0d3e309c0, all its commits are in main; the serial build-once cache works: serial phase 90-180 s), but the gate is still slow, and it is now the merge bottleneck.

MEASURED on this VM (fleet-check logs, ~/.fleet/checks, 2 vCPU):
| sha | result | waited for slot | gate ran | serial phase | parallel phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 401004284 | PASS | 11 min | 11 min | 89 s | 390 s (624 files) |
| 36ffb6b8f | PASS | 9 min | 11 min | 94 s | 395 s |
| 0d3e309c0 (jjsz) | PASS | 32 min | 12 min | 116 s | 422 s |
| 151562931 | PASS | 10 min | 18 min | 125 s | 662 s |
| 1f79854c8 | PASS | 15 min | 16 min | 122 s | 685 s (640 files) |
| b0b285579 | FAIL | 28 min | 16 min | 152 s | 760 s |
| 051b972d5 | FAIL | 0 | 22 min | 182 s | 1063 s (641 files) |

Three findings, in order of cost:
1. THE PARALLEL PHASE IS THE GATE, and it got 2-2.7x SLOWER today (390 s -> 685-1063 s) with only ~16 more files. Find out why (per-file timings from the run-tests output; which files grew; real-browser files serialised on the chrome slot semaphore; concurrency picked for 2 CPUs under load). Target: back under 400 s, then lower.
2. REAL-BROWSER TESTS FAIL GATES INTERMITTENTLY: agent-header-rename-reload (7zf0, q0yg), agent-share-import (pu7n), conversation-run-sequence, durable-task-restore. A flaky failure costs a whole re-gate (~15 min + queue). Make them deterministic, or run them in a separate browser stage that the merge gate retries once and reports separately.
3. Test selection: give the merger a way to run the FULL gate only for what the batch can affect (select-tests already computes this for test:changed) plus a scheduled full run on main, instead of 640 files per landing.

Fleet side already done (fleet tooling, not this repo): implementers run fleet-check --fast (build:production + test:changed); only the merger runs the full gate, and its slot request goes first; fleet-check now reports run time separately from queue wait.
Done when: the full gate on this VM runs in <= 8 min end to end with no flaky browser failure in 10 consecutive runs, measured with fleet-check run_s.

comments.text:
2026-10-08 17:00Z - HUB, for the owner of this bead (chunk of evidence about the experiment this bead is running, found while answering c-a-p's saturation report):

THE HUB-SIDE GATE-SPEED RUNS DO NOT ENTER THE HEAVY QUEUE. At 16:38Z the hub was at load 3.39 on 2 CPUs, and the job doing it was ~/work/gs-par.sh par-j2 running a deno test against ~/worktrees/cap-gate-speed - a `nice -n 10` command with a 1800s bound. It is properly bounded and nicely behaved; the problem is that ~/.fleet/heavy was EMPTY, so those runs never enter the queue and cannot yield to anything. A heavy job that bypasses fleet-heavy is invisible to the merger-first priority by construction, which is the whole reason the queue exists.

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH IT IS ON THE HUB: the hub is not an idle machine - it serves the inbox, the dashboard and the VMs' status surfaces - so saturating it degrades the thing every lane and the owner read. And a gate-speed experiment is exactly the kind of job whose whole PURPOSE is to run under load, which makes it the last thing that should be exempt from the load schedule.

SUGGESTED FIX, and it is a launch-line change rather than an engineering one: launch gs-par runs through fleet-heavy like every other heavy job, so they queue and yield. The runner already re-queues on preemption, so the experiment should survive the wait.

RELATED, FILED SEPARATELY AS fleet-ifqz: chrome-agent-platform's own heavy queue was running THREE gates at once on 2 vCPUs (its merger's full gate plus two implementer fast gates), all correctly inside fleet-heavy with the preempt wrapper. So the priority mechanism works as written and the box is still oversubscribed - a concurrency property of the queue, not a priority failure. c-a-p has applied a local lever (implementer lanes hold fast gates while a merger full gate is queued or running). The general fix is in fleet-ifqz; this comment is only the hub-side half.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-imp-0eq00
comments.text:
OVERLAP EXPERIMENT: STOPPED at coord's constraint 1 (write-set check). Result is a measured reason NOT to do it, which coord pre-declared a complete outcome. Read-only analysis; no gate run, no code change.

First, the record coord asked for is already above in this bead's scout comment: this VM measures 8 vCPU / 15 GB; parallel phase 164 s in the newest complete gate (run_s 398 s) and 664 s in the slow window; half the gate serial (198 s); 685-1063 s era = ambient CPU starvation with 28 following gates at 370-461 s (median 409) and wait_s median 1 s; flake census top red = STALE DIST MARKER, 13 fast runs (the class 0eq00 closes); merger STALE waste 351 s on 2026-10-14.

THE WRITE SET: npm run test:build is NOT read-only with respect to extension/dist. It is
  test:build = deno run -A scripts/build-gate.ts   (package.json)
  -> runSerialFiles(BUILD_GATE_FILES) over 3 files, and the files themselves do the writing:
  - tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts:22   execFileSync("node", ["build.mjs", "--target=store"]) - a REAL in-place production build
    tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts:84,115,124  reads extension/dist/dist.complete before and after the builds ("dist.complete bytes drifted")
    tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts:145,167     PLANTS a dangling symlink under extension/dist-versions/v-* and asserts the next build GC's it
    tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts:66          asserts extension/dist IS the pointer symlink (steady-state v-boot)
  - tests/build-debug-mode.test.ts:38   spawnSync("node", ["build.mjs", ...]) - developer + store builds (mode alternation)
    tests/build-debug-mode.test.ts:56   reads extension/dist/dist.complete after each build
  - tests/build-tool-bundling.test.ts:301,306,319  build.mjs runs (bogus flag, enterprise, default)
    tests/build-tool-bundling.test.ts:242          writes a stray file into the generated output and asserts GC
  - scripts/test-partition.mjs BUILD_GATE_REASONS states it outright: "runs node build.mjs in-place (dist/dist-versions rewrite; 3 production builds)" / "(debug+store bundles; mode alternation)" / "(verify-mode drift check and regen)".
So the write set is: extension/dist/** (bundle bytes), extension/dist/dist.complete (the marker 0eq00 teaches gates to validate), extension/dist-versions/** (v-boot pointers, created and GC'd), the bundled-tool generated output, and stray/residue files.

THE CONFLICT (why overlap is unsafe, not just untidy)
1. The parallel phase CONTAINS dist readers with a documented guard: scripts/test-partition.mjs READ_ONLY_DIST (diff-core, wasm-tree-shaking, bundle-budget, bundled-tool-packages, tool-exec-preview, owner-approval-security). A concurrent rewrite of dist + dist.complete makes them read a dist that no commit describes. That is not hypothetical: bundled-tool-packages.test.ts:405 already reds gate runs with "Error: dist.complete validation failed: marker indexed source authority is stale" in 13 stored fast-run logs - the #1 recurring red in the fleet's own records. Overlapping would convert a rare stale-marker red into the expected case.
2. extension/dist is itself a SYMLINK into the generated dist-versions dir (measured: extension/dist -> dist-versions/v-2078063-1792018493063; both gitignored, 0 tracked files). The build-behaviour tests repoint/GC that target, so "the tree's dist" changes identity mid-run, not just content.
3. A concurrent rebuild can change a TRACKED file mid-run: extension/dist/shared/diff-core.bundle.js is copied by the gate's own suites into the tracked docs/diff-core.bundle.js (70 "synced docs/..." lines in the passing full gate log, scripts/sync-gallery.mjs). A tracked-file content change during the run is exactly what fleet-check's witness reports as STALE - the 351 s loss of 2026-10-14 was the same failure mode. Overlapping makes that race likely rather than accidental.
4. No ordering fix is available for (3): the sync happens inside the parallel phase, so "run test:build after the sync" is not expressible; and (1) would require moving the 6 dist readers to run after test:build, which buys back only part of the saving while leaving the tracked-file race in place.

DECISION: do not overlap test:build with the parallel phase. The 118 s build-behaviour block is genuine coverage (3+ real production builds asserting marker stability, v-boot GC, developer/store alternation, generator drift) and it MUTATES the artifact the rest of the gate reads, so it must stay ordered last. It is irreducible without one of: (a) build.mjs gaining a private/out-of-tree output that those tests can point at while still asserting the tree's steady-state semantics - hard, because their assertions are ABOUT the in-tree steady state; (b) the gallery sync no longer copying generated dist bundles into tracked docs/ (removes the tracked-file race but not the read race); (c) fleet-check witnessing tracked content at phase boundaries rather than continuously (fleet-side, and it weakens the witness - not recommended).

WHAT I RECOMMEND INSTEAD (measured, none of it needs the overlap)
1. The bead's headline criterion looks MET, so it should be judged rather than chased: the newest complete gate is 398 s and the 28 consecutive complete gates after the starvation window were 370-461 s (median 409 s) with wait_s median 1 s - inside the "<= 8 min end to end" done-criterion, on a VM the bead still describes as 2 vCPU. The "back under 400 s parallel phase" target is already exceeded (164 s).
2. Remaining safe, bounded lever if the owner wants more: the #1 cost file is wasm-sync-workspace at 48.1 s case time (29 percent of the phase's case time, 10 MiB byte matrices) - moving it into the existing test:heavy tier saves up to 48 s, and its cost is that the landing gate stops covering the 10 MiB byte validator. That is a coverage decision for the owner, not a mechanical optimisation.
3. The 351 s STALE is the cheapest thing to reclaim, and it is fleet-side: capture git status --porcelain at verdict time when a gate goes STALE; the observed tracked-file writers (gallery sync) then name the cause in one run instead of leaving it undetermined.
4. Re-slice batch items stay worth doing as CPU-seconds, not wall: inventory-once ~10-15 s CPU, wasm fill ~6 CPU-s, evaluator-scan 2-5 s, fake-runner probes 1.5-3 s each.

title: ACP: CAP cannot connect to a healthy local ACP bridge - 'Failed to connect to ACP harness at ws://127.0.0.1:3210/acp?harness=claude-code' with no actionable cause
description: Reported by Paul directly 2026-10-07 19:49Z. The bridge is demonstrably UP and healthy: scripts/acp-service.mjs listening on http://127.0.0.1:3210/, ws://127.0.0.1:3210/acp (token required), /health returns ok:true harness=claude-code adapterPresent=true harnessCliPath=/Users/paulkinlan/.local/bin/claude, supportsHarnessSelection=true, knownHarnesses pi/claude-code/codex. The ACP service banner itself says: 'auth: token required - the bridge generated one; it is persisted in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cap-acp/bridge-token (paste it into acp.token)'. The extension then throws: 'Uncaught (in promise) Error: Failed to connect to ACP harness at ws://127.0.0.1:3210/acp?harness=claude-code' (stack points at incremental-sha256.js:7) with NO mention of auth/token/origin - so the user cannot tell whether this is a token problem, an origin/CORS rejection, a path query problem, or a real outage. Also note the bridge prints the endpoint WITHOUT the ?harness= query while the extension requests it with ?harness=claude-code. Next action: run the bridge locally, drive the WS handshake with (a) no token, (b) wrong token, (c) correct token, (d) each Origin style the extension uses, and capture what each returns; then make the extension surface the REAL reason (auth required / token invalid / origin rejected) instead of a generic connect failure, and fix any genuine handshake bug. Immediate workaround for Paul: paste the token from ~/.config/cap-acp/bridge-token into the CAP acp.token setting (or start the bridge with --token).

comments.text: coord — FIX IMPLEMENTED, in review: branch fleet/acp-connect @8008e8c0 (deepseek-v4-pro worker). Root cause PROVEN by a locally reproduced handshake matrix: the bridge takes the token ONLY as a ?token= query param (constant-time compare), guards run harness(400) -> upgrade(426) -> Origin(403) -> token(403); Paul connection carried NO token (acp.token empty) so the bridge 403d "missing or wrong token" - and the browser WebSocket API hides the status/body (opaque error + close 1006), so the client could only say "Failed to connect". The advertised-vs-requested ?harness= difference is NOT a bug (legitimate per-connection harness selection; upgrade succeeds either way). Fix: bridge exports acpConnectionRefusal() and adds GET /acp/preflight running the same guards, returning {ok:false, reason: token-missing|token-invalid|origin-rejected, detail}; the live 403 body carries the same detail (statuses/order unchanged). Client adds acpPreflightUrl/acpProbeConnectionFailure (2s timeout)/acpConnectionErrorMessage so connect() rejects with actionable text ("Paste the token from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cap-acp/bridge-token into acp.token (Settings -> ACP)") on both the runner and acp-model paths, falling back to the generic message if the bridge is unreachable. Tests: new tests/acp-connect-error.test.ts 4 passed, plus acp-client 17, acp-bridge-security 6, acp-runner 23, acp-harness-selection 5, acp-end-to-end 2/1 ignored, acp-model 5 and others - all focused, no full suite. comments.text: coord — LOOPBACK OPT-OUT IMPLEMENTED (deepseek-v4-pro worker): branch fleet/acp-loopback-optout @047071b9, built on a merge of the two reviewed ACP branches. Flag: --allow-anonymous-loopback, default unchanged (token required everywhere). title: Local beads Dolt DB diverged from remote: bd dolt push fails silently (60 never-pushed beads, 148 remote beads missing); tracker-reading gates go red
description:
## Observed (2026-10-07, found while landing chrome-agent-platform-jjsz)

The local tracker (the shared Dolt DB at `<primary checkout>/.beads/embeddeddolt`, `sync.remote: git+https://github.com/PaulKinlan/chrome-agent-platform.git`) has DIVERGED from the remote and nothing says so.

- `bd dolt push` is rejected (non-fast-forward). `bd dolt pull` aborts: "merge conflicts in issues require operator resolution".
- The post-commit hook runs `bd dolt push 2>/dev/null &`. The failure is swallowed, so every commit "succeeds" while the push silently fails. The tracker has probably been diverging for a while.
- `bd diff main origin/main`: 275 issues affected = 148 added on the remote and MISSING locally, 67 modified, 60 local-only and NEVER PUSHED (incl. jjsz, 716s.*, 9epn.*, 3p3e*, kr97, mxra, qvve, rtzf, djft). None of the 60 is in `origin/main:.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- Consequence for gates: `tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts` "SOURCE-BOUND" asks the live tracker (`bd show`) whether any bead referenced by the last 30 origin/main commits is CLOSED. 25 are referenced; the diverged DB knows ~1 of them. The test is RED here (~10 s) and it is RED on a pristine origin/main worktree too (proven 2026-10-07), so it is the tracker's state, not any branch's code. It is not one of the three named environmental signatures in docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md §2, so it reads as a product red and blocks every landing from this host.
- The installed pre-commit hook in the shared `.git/hooks` is stale against `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` (the stale one exports the DIVERGED local DB over `.beads/issues.jsonl`); syncing the tracked hook before the DB is reconciled would block every commit. Order matters.

## Rehearsal (on a scratch COPY of the DB, remote removed from the copy so it cannot push)

- `bd dolt pull --strategy theirs` and `--strategy ours` both complete: 943 -> 1116 issues (+173, none removed). All 60 never-pushed local beads survive unaltered.
- The two strategies differ on EXACTLY ONE row, so the true conflict set is one bead: `chrome-agent-platform-vyhl`. Local: closed 2026-10-05T16:40:10Z "Landed on origin/main at 58ce2e33 (v0.3.577)". Remote: in_progress (updated 16:09:22Z, older). `git merge-base --is-ancestor 58ce2e33 origin/main` = yes, so CLOSED is the truthful state: the right resolution is `--strategy ours` (it keeps the local closure; every non-conflicting remote change, including 59 status flips mostly to closed and 300 rows of new comments, merges in either way).
- With the reconciled copy supplied through `BEADS_DIR`, `tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts` SOURCE-BOUND passes in 0.4 s (was RED in 10 s on the diverged tracker).

## Work (needs the OWNER'S go-ahead: it modifies the shared tracker and publishes 60 beads)

1. Back up `.beads/embeddeddolt`, then `bd dolt pull --strategy ours`, check `vyhl` is still closed, `bd dolt push`.
2. Make the post-commit hook surface a push failure (one stderr line + a non-zero marker file) instead of `2>/dev/null &`; a diverged tracker must be loud.
3. Add a divergence check to the doctor/gate preflight (`bd dolt status` or a fetch+compare) so a diverged tracker is named BEFORE a landing gate reds on it.
4. After 1: install the tracked pre-commit/post-commit hooks from `scripts/git-hooks/` into the shared `.git/hooks` (the playbook's install line).
5. Decide whether `beads-landing-link` SOURCE-BOUND should skip with an ENVIRONMENT verdict (like the hlgr browser refusal) when the tracker cannot resolve most referenced beads, instead of failing as a product red. Do NOT weaken it to read the passive jsonl snapshot.

## Acceptance
- `bd dolt push` succeeds from the shared checkout; `bd diff main origin/main` is empty; the 60 beads are on the remote.
- A deliberately diverged scratch DB makes the hook/doctor say so in one line.
- `npm run test:file -- tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts` is green on the shared tracker without BEADS_DIR.

Evidence: /tmp/jjsz-probe/rehearsal-theirs, /tmp/jjsz-probe/rehearsal-ours, /tmp/jjsz-probe/conflict-ids.json (copied to the landing evidence bundle).

title: Massively improve build, unit test, validation gate, and merge queue speed
description:
Owner directive (2026-10-06): Unit test time, agent validation gates (npm run test:changed, npm test, npm run test:build), and build.mjs take far too long, stalling merge queues and agent validation loops.

Root causes & seams identified across the build and test pipeline:
1. Redundant full production rebuilds in serial test phase (tests/fixtures/build-once.mjs + build.mjs):
   - Every agent and merger runs `npm run build:production` (`node build.mjs --target=store`) after committing, before `npm test`.
   - However, `build.mjs` does NOT write the `serial-build-once` record (`$HOME/cap-evidence/serial-build-once/<commit>-<digest>.json`).
   - Consequently, `tests/build-smoke.test.ts` (the first serial test in `npm test`) misses the cache and triggers an entire SECOND `node build.mjs --target=store` from scratch on an already-fresh Store tree!
   - Having `build.mjs --target=store` populate the validated `serial-build-once` record (or having `storeBuildOnce` recognize a valid Store `dist.complete` when its stdout summary is recorded by `build.mjs`) eliminates a redundant full production build on every `npm test` run.

2. `build.mjs` internal bottlenecks (executed in every build, and 6x in `npm run test:build`):
   - `computeIndexedSourceAuthority` reads and SHA-256 hashes all ~2,226 git-indexed files sequentially (`for (const row of rows) { await lstat(); await readFile(); }`) and is called 4 TIMES per build (`sourceBefore`, `sourceAfter`, inside `writeDistCompleteMarker`, and inside `validateDistCompleteMarker`). Parallelizing batched file reads in `computeIndexedSourceAuthority` and passing pre-computed/verified authority cuts ~2.2s per build.
   - `esbuild.build()` is invoked 12 times sequentially instead of `Promise.all()` across independent entrypoints, and `esbuild.transform()` minification is invoked 12 times sequentially instead of in parallel (or minifying in the esbuild pass / parallelizing transforms).
   - `denyZodDocCompiles` and `assertNoDynamicEvaluators` each parse all 12 bundles (~25 MB unminified + ~12 MB minified) sequentially with single-threaded Acorn and walk the full AST twice per bundle. Fast pre-filtering / parallelizing / avoiding redundant AST walks on bundles without `Doc` class bodies or dynamic evaluator tokens cuts seconds per build.
   - `scanShippedJs` parses all 298 `extension/**/*.js` files sequentially; concurrent reading/scanning speeds up the pre-build AST check.
   - Unconditional `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2_000))` 2-second sleep in `build.mjs` before `dist-versions` GC even when `dist-versions` has no prior version to collect, or waiting 2000ms unconditionally on every build.

3. Serial test phase overhead in `npm test` and `npm run test:changed` (`scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs`, `scripts/test-partition.mjs`):
   - `runSerialFiles` spawns a separate `deno test` OS process for every serial file sequentially (16 files in `npm test`, 3 files in every `npm run test:changed` via `ALWAYS_ON`).
   - Read-only dist consumers (`tests/diff-core.test.ts`, `tests/wasm-tree-shaking.test.ts`, `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts`, `tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts`, `tests/tool-exec-preview.test.ts`, `tests/owner-approval-security.test.ts`) were placed in `SERIAL` ONLY because they read `extension/dist` while in-place rebuild tests (`build-smoke.test.ts`, `store-doc-denial.test.ts`) could rewrite `extension/dist`. Once the build step in phase 1 completes (or within a read-only post-build batch), read-only `dist` tests do not mutate `extension/dist` or process-global locks and never race each other!
   - In `npm run test:changed`, `ALWAYS_ON` includes 3 `SERIAL` files (`owner-approval-security.test.ts`, `real-browser-teardown.test.ts`, `requires-owner-gesture-column-allowlist.test.ts`) that each pay sequential `deno test` process startup before the parallel phase even starts.
   - `tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts` sleeps for 2s + 4s + 5s = 11s of pure `setTimeout` wait in every `npm test` run; tightening the fixture delays while preserving the exact structural kill/survive margin cuts ~7s of dead wait.

4. `ALWAYS_ON` / `test:changed` and parallel phase stragglers:
   - `tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts` runs in every `npm run test:changed` and `npm test`, taking ~4s to walk and scan all test files sequentially.
   - `scripts/select-tests.mjs` `buildReverseGraph()` reads every file in `extension`, `scripts`, `lib`, `packages`, `tests`, `cap-evidence` (including huge evidence/artifact directories if present).

5. Merge queue & `npm run test:build` (`scripts/build-gate.ts`, `tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts`, `tests/build-debug-mode.test.ts`):
   - `npm run test:build` runs 6 full `build.mjs` invocations sequentially across `build-bootstrap.test.ts` (3 store builds + 2 full zip packagings) and `build-debug-mode.test.ts` (1 dev build + 2 store builds).
   - Every improvement to `build.mjs` and `packageExtensionArchive` directly multiplies by 6x in `npm run test:build` and across every merge queue landing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Measure before/after wall-clock times for: (a) `npm run build:production` / `npm run build`, (b) `npm run test:changed`, (c) `npm test` (serial phase + parallel phase), and (d) `npm run test:build`.
2. Eliminate the redundant full production build when `npm test` runs after `npm run build:production` on a clean built tree, while preserving all falsification teeth (tampered source or stale marker still triggers rebuild/failure).
3. Massively speed up `build.mjs` and `scripts/dist-complete.mjs` while keeping every security gate, AST check, bundle budget check, and deterministic `dist.complete` marker contract intact.
4. Reduce serial phase and `test:changed` wall-clock time without weakening any test or partition guard invariant.
5. Full unit test suite (`npm test`) and build gate (`npm run test:build`) pass 100% green.
notes:
Root causes identified and measured on feat/jjsz-build-test-speed:
1. Build time (8.54s baseline):
   - build.mjs runs an unconditional 2,000ms setTimeout before dist-versions GC even when 0 stale versions exist.
   - computeIndexedSourceAuthority (scripts/dist-complete.mjs) sequentially lstats+reads 2,226 files (~600ms/call) and is called 4x per build.mjs run and 2x per collectPackageInventory (scripts/package-archive.mjs).
   - 12 esbuild.build() calls (855ms) and 12 esbuild.transform() calls (437ms) run sequentially instead of Promise.all.
   - denyZodDocCompiles parses all 12 bundles with acorn + 2x full AST walks (1,423ms) even when 10/12 bundles contain no 'class Doc'.
   - build.mjs does not write the serial-build-once memoization record, causing tests/build-smoke.test.ts to immediately run a second full store build (+8.70s).
2. Orphaned Chrome processes & process-group cleanup:
   - launchChrome() isolates Chrome in its own session/PGID (PGID_CHROME !== PGID_DENO). When a test process group is killed on timeout (kill -PGID_DENO) or deno crashes/exits before teardownChrome(), Chrome's PGID is never signaled and Chrome + helpers survive as orphans (PPID=1). Fix: attach a kernel-pipe parent-lifeline watchdog in launchChrome() that watches a pipe held only by parent deno and kills -PGID_CHROME + pkill user-data-dir on EOF.
   - On macOS (Darwin), /usr/bin/setsid and /proc do not exist: launchChrome(), runLockAware(), process-tree.ts, build-lock.mjs, bounded-child.mjs, and quiet-window.ts all failed or silently misbehaved. Worse, build-lock.mjs treated ENOENT on /proc/<pid>/stat as 'gone', stealing live build locks on macOS.
3. Parallel/Serial test stragglers:
   - tests/cdp-client.test.ts takes 33.03s because it rsyncs the entire repo including node_modules/.deno/ and .git/, compiles the identical esbuild wrapper 11 times, and leaks 9 fakeChild() processes.
close_reason: DELIVERED. Landed 0d3e309c0 (0.3.602): jjsz speed work in main — the big items via jjsz-paul 0582999a (serial-build-once cache write + parallel esbuild) plus the speed slice 8bbeb209 (build.mjs 2s GC grace now conditional on a prior version; select-tests skips cap-evidence). Residual tracked separately: o49qg (move read-only dist consumers out of the serial phase — safety-critical) and the b7ny0 journey epic. Paul's P1 directive satisfied.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Implemented and verified on branch feat/jjsz-build-test-speed (commit 17412440 in /Users/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-beads-jjsz).

### 1. Build Pipeline & Gate Speedups
- build.mjs: Parallelized all 12 esbuild.build() bundle compilations, 12 bundle report writes, 12 scrub passes, 12 esbuild.transform() minification passes, 12 assertNoDynamicEvaluators() checks, and Pyodide runtime staging; reused precomputed sourceAfter in writeDistCompleteMarker; lowered version-GC grace sleep default from 2000ms to 50ms (configurable via CAP_BUILD_GC_GRACE_MS); seeded the serial-build-once cache record on store builds so tests/build-smoke.test.ts and tests/store-doc-denial.test.ts reuse a fresh production build without rebuilding.
- scripts/dist-complete.mjs: Parallelized computeIndexedSourceAuthority reads (concurrency 64) and outputAuthority hashing.
- scripts/lib/scrub-zod-doc.mjs: Fast-path skip when !/\bDoc\d*\b/u.test(source) and lazy findDynamicEvaluators(ast).
- scripts/scan-shipped.mjs: Parallelized readText (concurrency 32), combined the two setup AST walks into one, and parallelized scanBundledWasmFiles.
- scripts/package-archive.mjs: Batched collectPackageInventory and copyInventoryToStage (concurrency 64).
- tests/cdp-client.test.ts: In-memory esbuild.transform compilation once per module, /bin/sleep + activeFakeChildren tracking in fakeChild(), and minimal scripts/ copy + symlinks in startup-fail test (33.03s -> 1.3s, 25x faster).
- tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts: Replaced whole-tree cp -a (which copied 956 MB node_modules + .git) with rsync excluding node_modules/.git/evidence/dist-versions (21s -> 4s, cutting parallel phase disk contention in half).
- tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts: Batched bd show IDs into a single invocation (8.0s -> 32ms, 250x faster).

### 2. Zero Orphaned Chrome Processes & Portable Process/Lock Liveness
- scripts/lib/process-tree.ts & scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts & scripts/lib/lock-aware-command.ts: Added setsidSpawnSpec() (Linux /usr/bin/setsid, macOS /usr/bin/perl POSIX::setsid), /bin/ps process-group introspection fallback when /proc is absent, and attachProcessLifeline(proc, { profileDir }) — a detached kernel-pipe parent-lifeline watchdog that receives EOF immediately if the parent test runner dies (even via SIGKILL) and reaps -pgid, proc.pid, and user-data-dir=<profile>. Verified with new falsification test in tests/process-tree-cleanup.test.ts.
- scripts/lib/chrome-for-testing.ts: Added macOS Chrome for Testing cache resolution (mac_arm-*, mac-*).
- scripts/lib/build-lock.mjs, scripts/lib/bounded-child.mjs, scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts, scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs: Added macOS /bin/ps, Deno.loadavg(), and fstatSync+flock fallbacks when /proc is absent so live locks are never stolen as gone and quiet-window/custody gates pass on Darwin and Linux.

### 3. Measured Timings (Before -> After)
- npm run build:production: 8.54s -> 4.27s (2.0x faster)
- tests/build-smoke.test.ts + tests/store-doc-denial.test.ts (warm dist.complete): 10.0s -> 1.1s (9x faster)
- tests/cdp-client.test.ts: 33.03s -> 1.3s (25x faster)
- tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts: 21.0s -> 4.0s (5.2x faster)
- tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts: 8.0s -> 0.032s (250x faster)
- npm run test:build (all 3 heavy build-behaviour files): ~460s historical -> 31s (ALL 3 GREEN)
- npm test (all 605 files: 19 serial, 586 parallel, 5,274 tests): 64 failures on baseline -> 100% GREEN (0 failed) in 95s wall (44s parallel phase)
- Orphaned Chrome for Testing processes after full suite + build gate: 0

family match discriminates. Note V8 background threads always sit in
futex_wait_queue even for an idle main thread, so the thread-table pin's

INDEPENDENT REVIEW (adversarial; different family from the glm-5.3 author). Target: fleet/review-glm-reds @ db06c094, base origin/main 40a1ad18 (merge-base confirmed = 40a1ad18).

VERDICT: PASS-with-notes. The regex fix is CORRECT, minimal and necessary; it loses NO real strength. One P2 finding, on the in-code comment only — not on the fix.

CLAIM VERIFIED (all measured on this box, kernel 6.12.93, node v24.21.0, git 2.43.0):
1. Kernel premise TRUE. `grep -c futex_do_wait /proc/kallsyms` = 0 (absent); `futex_wait_queue` = 1 (present, T). So `/:futex_do_wait/` is deterministically unsatisfiable here.
2. Failure text MATCHES the claim. Ran the parent (40a1ad18) version of tests/bounded-child.test.ts: FAILED at test :80 / assert :102, 6 passed | 1 failed, `AssertionError: the thread table must show the futex wait, got 1804400:futex_wait_queue,1804401:do_epoll_wait,1804402:futex_wait_queue,1804403:futex_wait_queue,(+3 more)`. Tree restored byte-identical afterwards (`git diff HEAD` empty).
3. Post-fix tests/bounded-child.test.ts = 7 passed | 0 failed.
4. MUTANT CLAIM INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, and correctly attributed. I applied the drill myself (test-1 child FUTEX_WAIT -> IDLE_SURVIVOR, new regex in place): 6 passed | 1 failed, killed by `AssertionError: wchan must show the futex wait, got do_epoll_wait` — i.e. the SIBLING pin at line 92, exactly as the bead predicted. Not killed by line 106. Mutant reverted, tree clean.
5. MAIN-THREAD DISCRIMINATOR UNCHANGED — verified against the pre-image (`git show 40a1ad18:tests/bounded-child.test.ts`): line 92 `assert(/futex/.test(wchan))` on the process-wide `/proc/<pid>/wchan` is byte-identical. That assert is what carries the futex-vs-epoll discrimination.

DOES THE LOOSENING LOSE REAL STRENGTH? NO — and your bd comment already says so correctly ("V8 background threads always sit in futex_wait_queue even for an idle main thread, so the thread-table pin's strength equals the original's exactly ... the main-thread discriminator is and remains the process-wide wchan assertion"). I measured the mechanism independently: driving an epoll-idle child through runBoundedChild gives thread table `1804818:do_epoll_wait,1804819:do_epoll_wait,1804820:futex_wait_queue,1804821:futex_wait_queue,(+3 more)`. scripts/lib/bounded-child.mjs:29 does `tasks.slice(0, 4)` over TID-sorted tasks, so ambient V8/libuv workers land inside the table for ANY node child. On the same table: line 92 `/futex/` FAILS (real discriminator), line 106 `/:futex/` PASSES, old `/:futex_do_wait/` FAILS (only because the symbol is gone on 6.12). Net: the old pin was worth zero on this box and the discrimination was never in the table.

P2 FINDING (comment accuracy; does not block landing the red fix).
tests/bounded-child.test.ts:104-105 — the new comment asserts: "Either way an epoll-idle thread reads do_epoll_wait, which never matches, so the pin stays falsifiable."
That sentence is MEASURABLY FALSE and it CONTRADICTS your own (correct) bd note. The table is not "an epoll-idle thread"; it is the first four TIDs of a 7-thread node process, 5 of which are ambient workers parked in futex_wait_queue regardless of what the main thread does. Proven above: for an epoll-idle child `/:futex/` on m[5] returns TRUE. So line 106 does not discriminate the child's behaviour at all, and the comment is the only thing telling a future maintainer whether it has teeth. This is the repo's test-honesty mode 2/3 shape (a pin satisfied by an occurrence unrelated to the guarded construct) plus a false falsifiability claim — worth fixing before it misleads someone into trusting line 106.
SMALLEST FIX: replace that third sentence with the true reason, e.g. "The table also carries node's ambient V8/libuv workers, which sit in futex_wait_queue for ANY child (measured: an epoll-idle child's table matches too), so this assert proves the table carries real futex-family wchans; the futex-vs-epoll discrimination is the process-wide wchan assert above, unchanged."
OPTIONAL STRICTER PIN (measured, if you want line 106 to actually discriminate): `/^\d+:futex/`. The table is TID-sorted ascending and the main thread is the lowest TID, so entry 0 IS the main thread. Measured: futex-parked child -> true; epoll-idle child -> false. Kernel-spelling-agnostic like the landed regex, but with real teeth.

UNVERIFIED ATTRIBUTION (note, not a finding): the precise "<=6.6 / >=6.7" rename boundary in the comment and in docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md:43 cannot be checked on this box (no kernel source tree). What I verified is only the 6.12.93 fact (futex_do_wait absent, futex_wait_queue present). The fix does not depend on the boundary being exactly 6.7 — the family regex is correct either way — so this is cosmetic.

OTHER GATES I RAN (focused only, per instruction; no full gate): deno check on bounded-child + worktree-audit + options-providers = exit 0. Cross-cutting guards, since the diff touches tests/ and a doc (AGENTS.md coupling rule 4): substring-pin-honesty 14/14, test-partition-guard 11/11, docs-process-truth 10/10, beads-precommit-hook 5/5. comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW (claude family, not the gpt-6-sol author) of fleet/coord-jixr-t3 @ 5208a482 (base 2e48a70c). Adversarial, measurement-based. 4 changed files only.

VERDICT: PASS-with-notes. 2 x P1, 2 x P2. Nothing in the diff is unsafe or wrong AS CODE; both P1s are about the recorded CAUSE and about paths that silently opt out of the new mechanism. No redesign needed.

=== VERIFIED CORRECT (with measurement) ===

1. ISOLATED GROUP + PGID CAPTURE - CONFIRMED, driven against a REAL headless Chrome.
   - Spawn: scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:635-641 -> new Deno.Command("/usr/bin/setsid", { args: [binary, ...args, "--remote-debugging-port=0"] }). /usr/bin/setsid exists (util-linux 2.39.3). setsid(2) then execvp; a Deno-spawned child is never a pgrp leader, so setsid does NOT fork and proc.pid stays the browser pid and becomes the new pgid/sid.
   - Capture: scripts/lib/process-tree.ts:26-34 isolatedProcessGroup() polls /proc/<pid>/stat and returns proc.pid ONLY when pgrp === proc.pid. Field indexing is right (post-")" split: [0]=state [1]=ppid [2]=pgrp) and lastIndexOf(")") makes a comm with spaces/parens safe. Fail-closed: 20x25ms then THROW "did not enter its own process group"; zombie/exited -> undefined.
   - MEASURED (reviewer probe, 1 browser, closed in finally, field verified clean after): group=1703410 === proc.pid; runner pgid differs; ppid === Deno.pid (direct child, setsid exec'd, no fork); 11 live group members (zygote/renderer/GPU); after teardownChrome(launched) -> 0 group members AND pgrep -f exit 1. Zero chrome/chromium left, zero leftover profiles.
   - CANNOT KILL UNRELATED PROCESSES: scripts/lib/process-tree.ts:66-70 refuses group unless isSafeInteger && >1 && !== Deno.pid && !== runner's own pgid && (proc ? group === proc.pid : true). Because group MUST equal proc.pid, Deno.kill(-group) can only reach the group the launcher created. I proved all six refusals fire (Deno.pid, 1, 0, -5, 1.5, runner pgid): reviewer probe 2/2 GREEN.

2. SHARED TEARDOWN + N1 FALSE-GREEN - CONFIRMED FIXED.
   - scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:769 extracts processGroup; :773 (profile path) and :778 (no-profile path) both forward it.
   - N1 IS FIXED. Base 2e48a70c had `await runOut(PKILL, ...).catch(() => {})` - it swallowed pkill's exit status ENTIRELY. HEAD scripts/lib/process-tree.ts:81 now throws on pkill exit != 0/1.
   - scripts/lib/process-tree.ts:89-92: return requires out.code === 1 AND (no group OR liveGroupMembers(group).length === 0); out.code !== 0 && !== 1 THROWS. REVIEWER PROOF: killProcessTree(null, "[") - an unbalanced ERE, so BOTH pkill and pgrep exit 2 - rejects with "cannot confirm cleanup" instead of returning clean. The `return code !== 1` false-green is NOT present.
   - Bounded retry 20x250ms then throw naming the surviving pids (:93) - I observed that exact message under mutant M1.
   - liveGroupMembers I/O is fail-closed (only NotFound swallowed, :20-21); a D-state survivor is counted and hard-fails rather than passing.

3. MUTANT FIXTURE NON-VACUOUS - CONFIRMED WITH TWO INDEPENDENT MUTANTS.
   - GREEN at HEAD: 5/5 tests/process-tree-cleanup.test.ts.
   - M1 (delete ONLY `Deno.kill(-group,"SIGKILL")`, keep verification) -> RED: "Error: process tree survived cleanup (group 1701625: 1701626)". The VERIFICATION has teeth.
   - M2 (delete the group kill AND revert the return to base `if (out.code === 1) return;`) -> RED: "AssertionError: ... the unmarked child must be gone as well as the parent". The FIXTURE detects an unmarked surviving descendant.
   - Restored (git diff --exit-code clean) -> GREEN 5/5. Fixture finally (tests/process-tree-cleanup.test.ts:78-82) kills -proc.pid + leader + awaits status; neither mutant left an orphan (post-run sweep empty).

4. KNOWN LIMITS - PRESENT AND HONEST about not reproducing. Commit body: "the composer leak did not reproduce standalone after a production build; profiles were unique, Chrome was a direct child, and no post-teardown births were observed. The full gate plus user-data-dir monitor is the deciding evidence." It does NOT claim to have proved the leak. BUT it DOES overclaim the MECHANISM - see Finding 1.

5. SCOPE / TYPECHECK / TESTS - no overreach.
   - Diff is exactly the 4 declared files, no unrelated edits.
   - deno check CLEAN: scripts/lib/process-tree.ts, scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts, tests/process-tree-cleanup.test.ts, scripts/live-every-tab.ts, scripts/kat-site-delegation-attachments.ts, scripts/kat-bgagent-delete.ts.
   - Focused GREEN (63 tests): process-tree-cleanup 5/5, harness-debug-port 5/5, real-browser-teardown 2/2, chrome-launch-lock 5/5, chrome-launch-lock-scope 6/6, chrome-slot-semaphore 17/17, chrome-profile-isolation 3/3, substring-pin-honesty 14/14, machine-path-honesty 7/7, harness-registry 11/11, scripts-exit-codes 3/3, chrome-test-contract 5/5, chrome-profile-static 2/2, select-tests-always-on 7/7, quiet-window-static 3/3.
   - Only RED: tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts - PROVEN pre-existing/stale-base, NOT diff-caused (see merger notes).

=== FINDINGS ===

FINDING 1 (P1) - THE RECORDED CAUSE IS FALSIFIED BY THE BRANCH'S OWN EVIDENCE AND BY LIVE MEASUREMENT.
scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:750-753 says:
  "On this VM Chromium's zygote/renderer/GPU processes encode the full command (including --user-data-dir) inside argv[0], not separate argv entries. Since argv text is not a reliable tree identity, setsid isolates their process group..."
Sentence 1 is TRUE. Sentence 2's causal premise is FALSE: pkill/pgrep -f match the JOINED /proc/<pid>/cmdline as an ERE substring; whether the text sits in argv[0] or argv[n] is irrelevant.
Three independent proofs:
  (a) The branch's OWN sampler, ~/cap-evidence/jixr-t3/baseline-descendants.jsonl: 17 descendants, 16 with nargv=1/exact=False - and 17/17 contain the literal `user-data-dir=<profile>` in the joined cmdline, so pgrep -f matches EVERY one.
  (b) Reviewer synthetic probe: one 884-char argv[0] with the marker buried inside -> /usr/bin/pgrep -f <marker> exit 0, pid printed. (Same probe re-confirms the startsWith("-") guard: a leading -- gives exit 2.)
  (c) Reviewer live-Chrome probe at HEAD: "group=1703410 members=11 pgrep-f matches=11 members-not-matched-by-pgrep=0".
The diff also REPLACED a CORRECT base rationale. Base 2e48a70c read "Chromium child processes inherit --user-data-dir=... in their command line, so matching user-data-dir=${profile} eliminates orphaned children" - which my measurement confirms was accurate.
docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md:57 carries the weaker echo ("... so profile-text matching alone does not establish that every descendant was reaped") - the "so" is a non-sequitur.
Why P1: this is the authoritative contract doc + the permanent code rationale for a defect that was NEVER reproduced. AGENTS.md canon names exactly this ("A verified observation does not license an unverified cause"), and the wrong mechanism points future lanes at argv encoding while the real open question from the merger's note - a teardown-CONFIRMATION race where pgrep reported no match while the tree was alive - stays uninvestigated. The setsid group kill remains a genuine, safe defence-in-depth improvement; only the stated reason is wrong.
SMALLEST FIX (2 comment lines, zero behaviour change):
  - chrome-launch.ts:751-752 -> "argv[0] encoding does NOT defeat pkill -f (measured: 17/17 sampled descendants and 11/11 live group members matched the profile text). The isolated group is defence-in-depth for a descendant that leaves the profile match or is born after it; the cause of the original confirmation miss is still OPEN."
  - docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md:57 -> replace the "so ..." clause with "profile-text matching measured complete on this VM (11/11 group members matched), so the group is a second, argv-independent identity rather than a correction to a broken match; the original confirmation miss is unexplained and the full gate plus the user-data-dir monitor is the deciding evidence."

FINDING 2 (P1) - THREE REAL-CHROMIUM TEARDOWN PATHS SILENTLY SKIP THE GROUP KILL; ONE IS INSIDE `npm test`.
scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:769 derives the group ONLY from `target`: `const group = target && "processGroup" in target ? target.processGroup : undefined;`. A raw Deno.ChildProcess has no such property, so the group is dropped with NO error and NO log. So the answer to "no path can skip it" is: three paths can, silently.
  - tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:131 `proc = launched.proc;` -> :167 `await teardownChrome(proc, profile);`. THIS TEST IS IN THE npm test GATE and unconditionally launches a real Chromium (AGENTS.md / CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT). It gets no group kill.
  - scripts/kat-site-delegation-attachments.ts:14 `const { proc, wsUrl } = await launchChrome({...})` -> :28 and :154 `await teardownChrome(proc, profile);`. A real-Chromium KAT harness (scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:197, class "kat") that jixr-t2 explicitly claimed to have fixed.
  - scripts/live-every-tab.ts:104 `proc = l.proc;` -> :141 `await killProcessTree(proc, \`user-data-dir=${profile}\`);` with no group. Worse, tests/process-tree-cleanup.test.ts:106 PINS that exact call text, so the pin now actively blocks adding the group.
REVIEWER PROOF (executable, no browser): spawning the same setsid+bash fixture and calling teardownChrome(proc, marker) with a RAW Deno.ChildProcess left survivor pid 1705413 alive in the group; teardownChrome({ proc, profile, processGroup }) leaves none.
SMALLEST FIX (one place, covers every current and future raw-proc call site):
  module scope in chrome-launch.ts: `const procGroups = new WeakMap<Deno.ChildProcess, number>();`
  after `group = await isolatedProcessGroup(proc)`: `if (group !== undefined) procGroups.set(proc, group);`
  chrome-launch.ts:769 -> `const group = (target && "processGroup" in target ? target.processGroup : undefined) ?? (proc ? procGroups.get(proc) : undefined);`
  plus live-every-tab.ts:141 -> `killProcessTree(proc, \`user-data-dir=${profile}\`, { group: launched.processGroup })` with the :106 pin updated in the same commit. Minimal variant if you prefer: at least change tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:167 to `teardownChrome(launched, profile)` (keep `launched` in scope), since that one is in the gate.

FINDING 3 (P2) - GROUP GUARD BYPASSABLE WHEN proc IS NULL; NO PID-REUSE PROTECTION.
scripts/lib/process-tree.ts:67-69: the `(proc && group !== proc.pid)` conjunct short-circuits when proc is null, so killProcessTree(null, m, { group: N }) will SIGKILL ANY group id N > 1 that is not the runner's own. Reachable via the exported teardownChrome({ profile, processGroup: N }). Not reachable from launchChrome today.
Related: by teardown time the leader may already be reaped, so a recycled pid that became a session leader would take an unrelated group down - a cross-lane kill, which AGENTS.md treats as severe.
SMALLEST FIX: have isolatedProcessGroup also return the leader's start_ticks (fields[19]), carry it on LaunchedChrome, and in killProcessTree re-read /proc/<group>/stat and skip the group signal unless field 19 still matches; also require `proc` whenever `group` is supplied.

FINDING 4 (P2) - DOCS / FORMAT.
  - docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md:58-60: the new paragraph is followed by THREE consecutive blank lines before the ASCII diagram (verified with cat -A). Delete two.
  - docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md:57 says "On Linux it starts Chrome through setsid", but chrome-launch.ts:635 hardcodes /usr/bin/setsid with NO OS conditional - on a non-Linux host every launch now throws NotFound at spawn. Practically unchanged (process-tree.ts:18-19 already hardcoded /usr/bin/pgrep|pkill at base), but the doc implies a conditional that does not exist. Either drop "On Linux" or state the hard dependency.
  - process-tree.ts:53-55 and :62: edited JSDoc lines run to 144 columns mid-sentence while the rest of the file wraps at ~80. Cosmetic only - deno.jsonc has no lint/fmt section, so no gate enforces it.

=== NOTES FOR THE MERGER (not findings against the diff) ===
  - BASE IS 9 COMMITS BEHIND origin/main (203666c6). tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts is RED at this tip: "tests/requires-owner-gesture-column-allowlist.test.ts - writes under extension/ or packages/". PROVEN NOT diff-caused: that test file and scripts/test-partition.mjs are byte-identical between base and HEAD, the guard reads neither changed file, and origin/main already carries the missing SERIAL_REASONS entry (scripts/test-partition.mjs:41, added by aeaede9c / 9c1e895a, both AFTER base). REBASE ONTO origin/main BEFORE GATING or the serial phase reds on an unrelated file. git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 5208a482 exits 0 -> clean merge, no conflicts.
  - scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:9368 killChromiumTree is the journeys harness's OWN copy of the tree kill and does NOT group-kill, while the same file launches through launchChrome (:48, :131) - so the 370-check journeys browser is now in an isolated group its own teardown never signals. File is byte-identical base vs HEAD, so NOT a regression, but the journeys gate does not benefit from this fix. Its pgrep exit-2 handling (:9392-9394) is correct.
  - deno check scripts/chrome-journeys.ts: 1 pre-existing error (TS2345 at :215, `fatalEvents = []` inferring never[]); file identical at base. Differential only, per AGENTS.md.

=== BOTTOM LINE ===
The mechanism WORKS and is SAFE: real Chrome provably lands in its own group with pgid === proc.pid, the guards make a cross-lane kill unreachable via the launcher, the verification cannot false-green on pgrep/pkill exit 2, and the mutant fixture dies to two independent mutants by the right assertion. I recommend landing after (a) correcting the argv[0] rationale in chrome-launch.ts:750-753 and CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md:57 - a wrong root cause in the contract doc is exactly the drift AGENTS.md forbids, and it would leave the real confirmation-race question uninvestigated - and (b) making the group unreachable-to-skip (WeakMap) or at minimum fixing tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:167, the one gate-test path that drops it. Finding 1 alone is enough to withhold an unqualified PASS: the fix is right, the stated reason is not.
Reviewer environment: worktree pi-worktree-0b707e1a...s0-0, HEAD verified 5208a482, tree restored clean (git diff --exit-code), no browser or fixture process left running, no repo file modified by this review.

Root cause analysis & fix for npm test rc=124 post-totals:
1. Root Cause 1 (Timeout false-red): scripts/run-tests.mjs and scripts/select-tests.mjs hardcoded PARALLEL_PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS default to 600,000ms (10 minutes). As the test suite expanded to 578 parallel files, running on 2 vCPUs under typical VM load requires 650-1100s. At 600s, spawnSync timed out with ETIMEDOUT, returning exit 124. run-tests.mjs printed summary totals ('wall 1173s' = 572s serial + 601s parallel) and called process.exit(124). Outer wrappers perceived this as a post-totals hang killed by timeout.
2. Root Cause 2 (Orphan process leakage): runParallel in run-tests.mjs and runPhase in select-tests.mjs did not spawn detached and did not kill the process group (-r.pid). When timeouts or crashes occurred, child processes survived in the background. Furthermore, tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts (the sole real-browser test in tests/) previously used parent-only proc.kill('SIGKILL'), leaving Chromium renderer/zygote children alive for 45+ minutes, which triggered reaper attribution false-positives.

- Sized DEFAULT_PARALLEL_TIMEOUT_MS to 1,800,000ms (30m) across run-tests.mjs and select-tests.mjs.
- Added detached: true and process.kill(-r.pid, 'SIGKILL') on timeout AND exit in runParallel and runPhase.
- Updated tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts to use killProcessTree() with its user-data-dir marker.
- Added CLI file argument support to run-tests.mjs and pathToFileURL entrypoint guard.
- Added tests/parallel-phase-resilience.test.ts proving clean rc=0 exit, 30m default timeout, and process group orphan elimination on both timeout and normal completion.

title: [security] hooks.subscribe FIRST-TIME create path skips the owner-approval gate that three authorities declare, and persists a model-authored promptTemplate that is executed verbatim as a privileged recurring run
description: Source: software-factory nightly project-audit 2026-10-06 (vuln-triage finding 2 of 25, CRITICAL; the highest-value NEW work in that audit). VERIFIED UNCHANGED ON CURRENT MAIN 303b37e6 at extension/lib/hooks.js:516. DEFECT: hooks.subscribe is declared owner-approval-required in three places — extension/lib/owner-approval.js:32 (DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS), docs/SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS.md:198 (OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED), and the route's own call to requireOwnerApproval at service-worker.js:10862-10867 — but that call is passed only as gateOnReplace, and subscribeHook (hooks.js:481-528) invokes it ONLY when a row for the exact (hookId, skillId) pair already exists. The CREATE path, which is the common case for a new pair, calls writeSubscriptions(list) with no owner-facing decision; its only check is checkHookAllowed (deny-list plus the hook's optional permission, neither of which inspects the template). REACHABILITY: the path is directly model-callable — management-tools.js:456-469 exposes subscribe_hook with hookId, skillId and promptTemplate, and lib/chrome-tool-capabilities.js:525 classifies it idempotent so no destructive-class card fires elsewhere. The persisted template is then executed verbatim as the task at service-worker.js:12081-12082 (task = sub.promptTemplate.replaceAll with the payload, handed to runTask with agentRole hook:<hookId>) — a privileged recurring run — and the untrusted-event-data fence applies to the payload, NOT to the template, so attacker-influenced text sits in the INSTRUCTION position. Two amplifiers: the gate is keyed on (hookId, skillId) so varying either dodges it; and the sibling paths (replace, and unsubscribe's gateBeforeDelete at service-worker.js:10877) DO gate, so this is a specific omission rather than a policy choice. Reachability is conditional (a model tool call must be steered by the R4 prompt-injection class), which is why this is P1 rather than P0. ACCEPTANCE: (1) make the approval unconditional and content-bound — call the seam for EVERY subscribe, not only the replace case, with the digest of hookId+skillId+promptTemplate for non-owner principals; (2) collapse promptTemplate out of the model-callable schema so only the owner Settings surface can author a template, with the model path falling back to the skill prompt plus the fenced payload; (3) reconcile owner-approval.js:32, census 4.4 and chrome-tool-capabilities.js:525 with the enforced gate; (4) FALSIFY: drive a first-time subscribe_hook through the model tool path with principal model, assert a pending approval row is created and the subscription list is unchanged, then delete the existing && short-circuit and show the test RED. FOLDED IN (audit finding 7, same route, different class): bound promptTemplate length in subscribeHook and mirror .max() in the subscribe_hook tool schema — the repo currently PINS the absence of a bound (tests/hooks.test.ts:198-202 asserts the template is stored whole, and tests/security.test.ts:248 drives a 70,000-character template), so the accepted consequence today is storage-quota exhaustion and token-cost amplification on every matching event up to the 50-run fan-out cap at service-worker.js:12056. NOT A DUPLICATE: the scout searched all 966 beads (title, description, notes, design, acceptance, external_ref); the nearest are closed owner-approval CENSUS beads (18ug, dari, ygvt) which classify routes rather than fix this create path, and the one subscribe_hook hit (e5oe) is an unrelated recipe-to-skill migration.

MEASURED FIRST - THE DEFECT IS REAL ON THIS TREE, and here is the exact code:
  extension/lib/hooks.js:481-528 subscribeHook({hookId, skillId, recipeId, promptTemplate}, {gateOnReplace=null}):
    checkHookAllowed(hookId) is the ONLY check on the create path; then, inside withHookLock, the entry is
    built and the gate runs ONLY here:
      `if (existing && typeof gateOnReplace === "function") { const gate = await gateOnReplace(...) }`
    so for a FIRST-TIME (hookId, skillId) pair - `!existing` - the entry is pushed by `list.push(entry)` and
    written by `writeSubscriptions(list)` with NO owner-facing decision.
  extension/background/service-worker.js:10848-10876 `hooks.subscribe` passes ONLY `gateOnReplace`, and its
    payload is a digest of hookId + skillId + promptTemplate (content-bound) - but that whole gate is dead for
    the create case. (The 7975 gateOnReplace I first found belongs to named-agent.create, not this route.)
  extension/lib/management-tools.js:456-469 `subscribe_hook` exposes `promptTemplate: z.string().optional()`
    with NO max, and `execute` forwards it straight into `call("hooks.subscribe", {..., promptTemplate})` - so
    the model path can author an unbounded template on a first-time subscribe.
  Also verified: `promptTemplate` is stored verbatim and is later the INSTRUCTION (hooks.js comment "default:
    the skill's own prompt + the payload appended" applies only when the template is empty).
PLAN, coord's acceptance in order, plus reporting the length bound as an accepted consequence change:
  1. Make approval UNCONDITIONAL and content-bound: replace the replace-only seam with one gate called for
     EVERY subscribe (create and replace), passed {existing, candidate}, and keep the route's digest payload
     (hookId+skillId+promptTemplate). Owners must still pass through without a prompt - I will verify
     requireOwnerApproval's owner short-circuit at service-worker.js:5229 before relying on it.
  2. Collapse promptTemplate out of the model-callable schema (management-tools.js subscribe_hook): the model
     path authors no template and falls back to the skill prompt + the fenced payload; the owner Settings
     surface stays the only author.
  3. Reconcile owner-approval.js:32 (DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS), docs/SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS.md:198 + 4.4, and
     chrome-tool-capabilities.js:525 (the idempotent classification) with the now-enforced gate.
  4. FALSIFY: first-time subscribe_hook through the model path with principal model -> a pending approval row
     is created AND the subscription list is unchanged; then bypass the gate and show the test RED.
  5. Folded-in finding 7: bound promptTemplate length in subscribeHook. I accept that this CHANGES two pinned
