51cd IMPLEMENTED (code + pinned-test changes), falsification test in flight.

CODE (all four acceptance items begun):
 1. UNCONDITIONAL, CONTENT-BOUND GATE - extension/lib/hooks.js: the seam was `gateOnReplace` invoked only
    `if (existing && typeof gateOnReplace === "function")`; it is now a single `gate` invoked for EVERY
    subscribe with `{ existing: existing ? {...existing} : null, candidate: {...entry} }`. The seam stays
    OPTIONAL at the lib level on purpose: agent-seeds.js:164 and the skill enable/disable callers pass no gate
    and must keep working; the ROUTE is where it is mandatory.
    extension/background/service-worker.js `hooks.subscribe`: renamed the seam, and - the hazard the scout
    caught - the payload builder no longer dereferences `existing` (on CREATE it is null), so a create cannot
    fall into the catch and be REFUSED. The absent-row form is an explicit stable marker
    `canonicalField("existing", payloadFields([["present","false"]]))`, because the digest is the retry
    identity: an unstable create payload would make an approved retry unmatchable. Error text no longer says
    "replacement".
 2. NO MODEL-AUTHORED TEMPLATE - extension/lib/management-tools.js: `promptTemplate` is GONE from the
    subscribe_hook inputSchema and is no longer forwarded; the description says template authorship belongs to
    the owner and the run uses the skill prompt + fenced payload (the dispatch fallback at SW 12083-12084
    already implements that, so no dispatch change was needed). Belt-and-braces in the ROUTE: a model
    principal's `promptTemplate` is forced to "" before the digest, so even a future route that forgets its
    gate cannot put model text in the instruction position.
 3. AUTHORITIES RECONCILED - chrome-tool-capabilities.js: subscribe_hook AND unsubscribe_hook move from
    idempotent to MUTATING (matching the set_agent_provider row), and tool-replay-safety.js removes both from
    IDEMPOTENT_TOOLS (they stay in BUILT_IN_TOOLS, so they classify "mutating"), with the same rationale the
    schedule controls already carry: a replay re-runs the owner-gated route, so the gate re-arms. Without both
    files the consistency pin tests/chrome-tool-capabilities.test.ts:136-143 stays RED - that coupling is
    exactly why the scout flagged it.
 4. FALSIFICATION TEST delegated to a worker (tests/hook-subscribe-approval.test.ts): first-time subscribe
    through the MODEL path -> a pending approval row is created AND the list is unchanged, AND after the owner
    approves the SAME call LANDS (the anti-silent-denial assertion, because a payload bug that refuses every
    create would otherwise read as "fixed"), AND the stored template is "". Then the worker restores the old
    `existing &&` short-circuit and requires the test RED, then reverts.

PINNED TESTS CHANGED (the accepted consequence, recorded rather than quietly edited):
 - tests/hooks.test.ts "a prompt template past the old 64 KiB cap subscribes whole (dptw)" -> now asserts the
   64 KiB bound REFUSES and writes nothing, AND that a template AT the bound is still stored whole. Old
   behaviour: 256 KiB stored whole. Why wrong: the template is model-authorable, runs verbatim in the
   INSTRUCTION position, and re-runs per matching event up to the 50-run fan-out cap, so it is a storage-quota
   and token-cost amplifier. Bound basis: 64 KiB is the cap this repo enforced before dptw and already ~16k
   tokens of instruction.
 - tests/hooks.test.ts "concurrent same-key first subscriptions cannot produce an ungated replacement" -> the
   numbers invert: gates 2 (was 1), nothing lands (was 1), list empty. Its INTENT is preserved and
   strengthened: the ungated-create path no longer exists.
 - tests/security.test.ts dptw hook-fan-out test -> a template past the bound is refused even on a KNOWN
   recipe, with the known-recipe guard still asserted intact.
 - tests/tools-management.test.ts -> asserts the schema has no promptTemplate AND that one invented by a caller
   is not forwarded.
 (The scout also found the concurrent test, which the bead description did not list - worth recording.)
COORD'S OPTIONAL ITEM 5 (make the census test gate declaration-vs-enforcement): RECORDED AS A FOLLOW-ON, not
folded in. It is not cheap in the honest form - it needs a per-route enforcement proof for the 16 routes the
census classifies, which is the same AST/route harness work this bead's falsification test needed for ONE route.
Folding it in would widen a P1 security fix into a test-infrastructure project; I will file it as its own bead
unless coord prefers otherwise.
DOCS still to update after the code settles: SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS 4.4, HOOKS.md:53,
ARCHITECTURE.md:166, inline-approval-audit.md:19, plus CHANGELOG/PLAN per the docs-never-drift rule.
PLAN NOTE: hooks.subscribe is NOT owner-direct (pinned by tests/owner-approval-security.test.ts:75), so an
owner-options caller would take the pending+retry path rather than passing free, and in practice there is NO
owner subscribe UI today - so acceptance (2) is satisfied as "the model cannot author a template" and template
authorship is currently unreachable rather than owner-reachable. That is stated rather than implied.

WHAT CHANGED, file by file

  `gateOnReplace`, invoked only `if (existing && ...)`), receiving `{ existing: null }` on create; the seam stays
  OPTIONAL at the lib level so agent-seeds.js:164 and the skill enable/disable callers keep working - the ROUTE is
  where it is mandatory. New export `MAX_PROMPT_TEMPLATE_CHARS = 64 * 1024`, checked before the lock and the gate.
  `migrateHookSubscriptions` now PURGES a non-empty template on every migrated row and reports `clearedTemplates`.
- extension/background/service-worker.js hooks.subscribe: the payload builder no longer dereferences `existing`
  (on CREATE it is null - the naive change would have REFUSED every create via the catch, reading as "fixed" in a
  test that only checked nothing was written), the absent-row digest form is the stable marker
  `canonicalField("existing", payloadFields([["present","false"]]))` because the digest is the retry identity, and
  a model principal's promptTemplate is forced to "" before the digest.
- extension/lib/management-tools.js: promptTemplate gone from the model-callable schema and not forwarded.
- extension/lib/chrome-tool-capabilities.js + tool-replay-safety.js: subscribe/unsubscribe move from idempotent to
  MUTATING (a replay re-runs the owner-gated route, so the gate re-arms) - both files, because the consistency pin
  tests/chrome-tool-capabilities.test.ts:136-143 reds on a partial move.
- tests/hook-subscribe-approval.test.ts (new): drives the REAL route through the MODEL path with the real approval
  store - first-time subscribe publishes exactly ONE approval card, leaves exactly ONE pending row, persists
  NOTHING, then LANDS after owner approval with an empty template. Falsification: restoring `existing &&` makes it
  RED - no card, no row, and the subscription lands ungated (log ~/cap-evidence/j5yz-51cd/hook-subscribe-approval-MUTANT-RED.log).

  ARCHITECTURE.md, PLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md, and tool-platform-architecture.md's now-false "hook idempotents" class.

THE PINNED-TEST CHANGE, stated as coord required (old behaviour -> why wrong -> bound and basis)
- tests/hooks.test.ts "a prompt template past the old 64 KiB cap subscribes whole (dptw)" and
  tests/security.test.ts's dptw fan-out test asserted an UNBOUNDED template was accepted. OLD BEHAVIOUR: a 256 KiB
  (and 70 KB) template was stored whole on the premise that size/count are not the guard. WHY IT WAS WRONG: the
  template is model-authorable, it is executed VERBATIM in the INSTRUCTION position of a privileged recurring run,
  and it re-executes on every matching event up to the 50-run fan-out cap, so an unbounded one is a storage-quota
  and token-cost amplifier. THE BOUND: 64 KiB (`MAX_PROMPT_TEMPLATE_CHARS`) - the cap this repo enforced before
  dptw and already ~16k tokens of instruction; the tests now assert the boundary from BOTH sides (bound+1 refused
  writing nothing; exactly the bound accepted and stored whole), and the known-recipe guard is asserted intact.
- tests/hooks.test.ts "concurrent same-key first subscriptions cannot produce an ungated replacement": the numbers
  invert (gates 1->2, landed 1->0, list empty). Its INTENT is preserved and strengthened - the ungated create path
  no longer exists.
- tests/tools-management.test.ts: asserts the schema has no promptTemplate AND that a caller-invented one is not
  forwarded.

VERIFICATION
- 159 passed | 0 failed across 13 files: the new falsification test, hooks, security, tools-management,
  chrome-tool-capabilities, owner-approval-security, owner-approval-classification,
  sw-dispatch-authority-census, sw-route-modularization, skill-identity-migration, docs-process-truth, changelog,
  vocabulary. check:reachability OK (297/297). Factory stations running now.
- INDEPENDENT REVIEW (different family, run 8937c355): APPROVE "OK with notes", no P1. It independently verified
  every attack vector: no ungated persisting path reachable by a model (the two ungated callers are internal and
  not model/page-reachable), the digest is stable and content-bound, no remaining way for a model to author a
  template, the bound is unbypassable and evaluated before the gate, the reclassification is clean across both
  files and the durable-runs consequence is understood, and the changed pins are STRONGER not weaker.
  ITS ONE P2 (fixed in de857eae): pre-fix legacy rows kept their template. Migration now purges it.
- NOT MINE: tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts is RED on pristine main (bead chrome-agent-platform-ygxk),
  reproduced in a SECOND worktree with none of this branch. Recorded in the commit body so the merger does not
  attribute it here.

HONESTY / SCOPE NOTES
- There is NO owner subscribe UI: acceptance (2) is satisfied as "the model cannot author a template" and template
  authorship is currently UNREACHABLE, not owner-reachable. Stated in the code comments and the docs.
- hooks.subscribe is NOT owner-direct (pinned by tests/owner-approval-security.test.ts:75), so an owner-options
  caller would take the pending+retry path; in practice there is no such caller.
- The reachable attacker for the fixed defect is the HUB/MASTER agent steered by prompt injection: subscribe_hook
  is only mounted for unscoped runs (service-worker.js:2808 `scoped ? {} : ...`), so hook and site sub-agents
  never had the tool.
- COORD'S OPTIONAL ITEM 5 (make the census test gate declaration-vs-enforcement rather than completeness alone) is
  NOT folded in: the honest form needs a per-route enforcement proof for the 16 routes the census classifies, which
  is the same harness work this bead needed for ONE route. Filed as a follow-on recommendation, not silently
  dropped.

title: [ui/security] Surface environment secret storage, origin-pinned proxy rules, live service-tool auth, and request ledger in Settings → Web services
description:
Complete and surface the CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE (jao1) environment secrets storage, configuration, and proxy flow so the owner can see and configure how secrets are stored, bound to origins/headers, and proxied:

1. Fix live service-tool proxy principal mismatch (extension/background/service-worker.js, extension/lib/service-tools.js):
   - synthesizeServiceTools calls proxyCall(..., { principal: 'model' }), which enclaveProxyRoutes currently rejects because isAllowedCaller checks isOwnerPrincipal(context) ('extension' | 'owner-options' only).
   - Authorize in-worker synthesized service tool executions (and origin-pinned python.fetch / enclave.proxy calls) while keeping external runtime message callers fenced to owner principals.

2. Surface Preset Services + Custom Environment Secret Proxy Rules (extension/lib/service-tools.js, extension/background/routes/enclave-proxy.js, extension/background/routes/vault.js):
   - Expand built-in SERVICE_DESCRIPTORS / DEFAULT_SERVICES with Brave Search (BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY -> https://api.search.brave.com, header X-Subscription-Token) and GitHub (GITHUB_TOKEN -> https://api.github.com, Bearer token).
   - Support owner-configured custom secret proxy rules (cap:vault:custom-services) binding keyId (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE) -> allowed origin (https://...), auth injection mode ('bearer' | 'header' | 'query'), header/query name, and optional testPath.
   - Enforce origin-pinned secret resolution in enclave.proxy and python.fetch: a secret KEY_ID (via service auth or $VAULT{KEY_ID} template) may ONLY be injected into requests targeting that secret's configured origin(s), preventing cross-origin secret exfiltration.

3. Redesign Settings -> Web services (#web-services in extension/options/options.html & extension/options/options.js) & Request Ledger (extension/lib/enclave-ledger.js):
   - Show the storage & proxy architecture summary (AES-GCM-256 at-rest encryption in chrome.storage.local, SW-only token decryption, $VAULT{KEY_ID} origin-pinned header/query injection).
   - RenderVAULT_SERVICES preset cards (Brave Search, GitHub) even before a key is saved so the user immediately sees supported services, their target origins, auth header mappings, and configure/rotate/test/remove controls.
   - Allow configuring Allowed Origin + Auth Injection (Bearer / Header / Query) when adding a custom secret key in #vault-add, and display the bound origin and injection rule on every row in #vault-services.
   - Record proxied calls (timestamp, service/keyId, method, origin, status, durationMs — never secret values) in extension/lib/enclave-ledger.js and render the live audit ledger in #web-services.

title: [bug] main red: ACP client keeps a rejected session active (Pi refusal leaks ses_fake_1)
description:
MEASURED ON origin/main 2260ab3a (and on cap-beads-6yfm/cap-beads-fwf6, i.e. nothing to do with either branch): tests/acp-end-to-end.test.ts:151 is RED.

  ACP tool servers: Pi refuses new/load before the adapter; empty Pi and other adapters still work
  AssertionError: Values are not equal: rejected requests must not activate a session
  Actual: "ses_fake_1"   Expected: null
  at tests/acp-end-to-end.test.ts:151:15

MECHANISM (read, not guessed): extension/lib/acp-client.js loadSession() — JSDoc at 203, body at 207 — does

    this._resetCommands();
    this.activeSessionId = params.sessionId;                       // line 213
    await this.request("session/load", { sessionId, cwd, mcpServers });
    this.activeSessionId = params.sessionId;                       // line 215 (redundant)

The id is assigned BEFORE the request. When the request REJECTS — the Pi adapter's refusal ("Pi's ACP adapter does not mount supplied MCP servers … Claude Code or Codex … local tools only") — nothing rolls the assignment back, so the client is left pointing at a session that was never activated while the caller only sees a thrown error. Line 213 looks deliberate (in-flight session/update notifications are filtered against activeSessionId at acp-client.js:541/545), so the fix is most likely try/catch with rollback on rejection (or restoring the previous value) rather than deleting the line — owner's call.

CONTROL (why this is not the branch's fault): with the fwf6 product change reverted (tree = origin/main + a version bump) the same file fails identically at the same line; the test imports neither extension/shared/components.js nor composer-commands.js. npm test on i76t's base (7c94c0d6, 563 files) was GREEN, so this red arrived with the newer landings (vl6c/wp7y/vmja) on 2260ab3a.

IMPACT: npm test on main = 5037 passed / 6 failed / 3 ignored (5 of the 6 are the i76t set). This one is not in i76t's scope and no bead existed for it.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main @ 742fb208 (v0.3.568). Restores activeSessionId on rejected session/load. Focused tests 13/0 green, acp-end-to-end:151 green.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: Claimed by bak-ds-flash (deepseek-v4-flash) to implement activeSessionId rollback on rejected session/load.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED — cap-beads-tliw @ 3c07161e (origin/main 2260ab3a + this bead, v0.3.568). Worktree ~/worktrees/cap-tliw.

FIX (extension/lib/acp-client.js loadSession): the optimistic id assignment is KEPT, because in-flight session/update frames are filtered against activeSessionId (_handleSessionUpdate), so the session being loaded must be the one they attribute to. What changed is that the previous value is captured and restored on rejection, with the error re-thrown unchanged; the redundant post-success re-assignment is gone. A refused load no longer leaves the client pointing at a session the agent never opened.

PINS (both RED before restore; tests/acp-client.test.ts drives the real client over the mock transport and answers session/load with a real JSON-RPC error frame — no stub of request()):
- a refused load with a live prior session restores that session ('ses_live'), and the SAME test pins the in-flight attribution ('ses_refused' while the request is outstanding) so a future cleanup that removes the pre-assignment breaks a test instead of silently misrouting notifications;
- a refused load with no prior session leaves the client unattached (null) — the exact shape of the end-to-end assertion.
Mutant (rollback removed, original three lines restored): RED 11 passed / 2 failed. Restored: 13 passed / 0 failed.

ACCEPTANCE: tests/acp-end-to-end.test.ts — 2 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (LIVE pi stays ignored; it was 1 failed before). The 'rejected requests must not activate a session' line is green.

FULL GATE (npm run test:changed failed closed to the full suite because the release-note bump rewrites manifest/package files): 549 parallel + 18 serial files, 5037 passed / 5 failed / 3 ignored, wall 4m12s. Five failures = EXACTLY the i76t set (durable-root, heavy-gate-slot, machine-path-honesty, quiet-window, task-view-simplify) — one fewer than the 6 this branch started from, so the delta is this bead and nothing else. Both new tests appear green in the full-suite run.

FILED WHILE HERE: chrome-agent-platform-1gf1 (P3) — a rejected session/new still clears activeSessionId and wipes the command list (_resetCommands), which is the same class but a different contract question (rollback vs detach), so it is deliberately NOT in this commit; the bead states both options and what to pin.

title: feat(tools): declarative service descriptor & tool synthesis engine with Brave Search preset (CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE Stage 3)
description:
Stage 3 of CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE:
Implement extension/lib/service-tools.js:
- Declarative API service schema (JSON):
  * Service metadata: id, name, origin, description.
  * Auth declaration: type ('header' | 'bearer' | 'query'), secretId (pointer to vault key).
  * Tool definitions: semantic tool name (e.g. brave_search), input parameters schema, and request template mapping.
- Model isolation: The generated AI SDK tool definition exposes ONLY the clean semantic parameters (query, count, country) to the model. Auth fields and raw API keys are NEVER included in the tool parameter schema.
- Built-in Brave Search Preset:
  * Tool brave_search({ query: string, count?: number }): routes to GET https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search via the enclave proxy with X-Subscription-Token injected from vault.
  * Transforms and simplifies the raw Brave response into clean, concise web search result objects.

title: feat(proxy): secure enclave outbound proxy with template secret injection (CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE Stage 2)
description:
Stage 2 of CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE:
Implement extension/background/routes/enclave-proxy.js in the Service Worker:
- Template-driven secret injection: substitutes $VAULT{SECRET_KEY} placeholders into request headers (e.g. 'Authorization: Bearer $VAULT{KEY}', 'X-Subscription-Token: $VAULT{KEY}') or query parameters.
- Strict security & SSRF defense:
  * Destination origin must match the service's approved origin whitelist (e.g. api.search.brave.com).
  * Private IP and loopback blocking via shared checkFetchTarget.
  * Credentials always omitted (credentials: 'omit').
  * Redirects set to manual (redirect: 'manual') to prevent token leakage via redirect laundering.
- Response handling: strip echoed auth headers, bound body size (1MB max), and wrap response in tagUntrusted().
- Output sanitization: ensure injected secrets are never echoed in error messages or response bodies.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Stage 1 candidate pushed: branch jao1-secret-vault @ 3c167cfc0 (off origin/main e362fd80).

DELIVERABLE: extension/lib/secret-vault.js — createSecretVault({storageArea, extensionId, installSaltB64}):
- AT REST: AES-GCM-256 with a key derived via PBKDF2-SHA-256 (210k iterations, non-extractable) from the extension id + a per-install random salt (chrome.storage.local, reserved key cap:vault:install-salt). Records live under the reserved cap:vault:secret:<KEY_ID> namespace: {scheme, iv, ct, configuredAt, lastUsed, rotations} — the at-rest payload carries NO plaintext (pinned by test: the storage serialization contains neither the secret nor a prefix).
- AUTHORITY: raw reads are service-worker-ONLY — every other caller (ui/content/model/options) is refused with a named error (the negative-permission test sweeps five callers). Mutations are SW authority. The UI surface is a MASKED projection ({keyId, configured, lastUsed, rotations, masked: '…wxyz'}) whose JSON serialization provably carries no plaintext (pinned).
- INTEGRITY: a flipped ciphertext byte fails closed with an error naming the KEY ID, never a decrypted fragment; error messages never carry values (pinned).
- KEY IDS: strict UPPER_SNAKE_CASE credential ids (BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY shape) — a TypeError names the id, never the value; rotation refuses unknown ids so a typo cannot mint records.
- EXTENSION-BOUND: a different extensionId derivation cannot decrypt the record (pinned).
- HONEST THREAT MODEL in the module header: the at-rest encryption is defense-in-depth for storage snapshots; the structural boundary is SW-only authority + MV3 storage privacy + the masked-only UI surface — not a defense against extension-context code execution.

TESTS: tests/secret-vault.test.ts, RED-first (all 10 failed on the missing module — /tmp/jao1-red.log), 10/10 green after implementation.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
STAGE 1 REVIEW VERDICT: PASS (with three recorded findings; none blocks Stage 1, two worth fixing before Stage 2).
Reviewer: voicebox-dsflash1 (independent, cross-family; author cap-glm-flash).

REVIEWED: jao1-secret-vault @ 3c167cfc0 in a clean worktree over origin/main e362fd80 (diff: secret-vault.js 219 lines, tests 200, check-reachability +2). Ran the file suite: 10 passed / 0 failed.

WHAT THE DIFF PROVES (verified by reading the mechanism, not the claims):
- At rest: AES-GCM-256, PBKDF2-SHA-256 210k iterations over `${extensionId}:${installSaltB64}` with a 32-byte random per-install salt; the derived AES key is imported with extractable=false (secret-vault.js:80) and a FRESH 12-byte IV per encryption (secret-vault.js:99-101) — no IV reuse, the classic GCM failure, is possible.
- Serialization carries no plaintext: the record is {scheme, v, iv, ct(base64), configuredAt, lastUsed, rotations} under cap:vault:secret:<KEY_ID>; the test that reads the whole storage area for a plaintext substring passes.
- Masked projection: maskValue returns "…"+last4 for length>=8 and "…" otherwise (never a prefix) (secret-vault.js:42-45); listMasked refuses callers other than ui/sw and returns {keyId, configured, lastUsed, configuredAt, rotations, masked}.
- Integrity fail-closed: GCM decrypt rejects a tampered ct and getSecretRaw converts that into a named refusal whose message carries the key id only (secret-vault.js:120-137); the tamper test passes.
- Strict ids (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE), refuse-unknown semantics on rotate/delete, rotation counter semantics (setSecret keeps rotations, rotateSecret increments). Suite 10/10.

FINDINGS (severity + file/line):
1. MEDIUM — the "SW-only" boundary is a CALLER-SUPPLIED LABEL, not verified provenance. assertSwCaller compares `caller`/`by` to the string "sw" (secret-vault.js:86-90), so any extension-context code that passes {caller:"sw"} gets raw reads; the header calls the boundary "structural". The stated threat model (key material reconstructible inside extension contexts) already concedes privilege-equivalent code can bypass — so the mechanism is acceptable, but the claim should be corrected to "an API boundary enforced by label; privilege-equivalent code is out of scope (see threat model)", or the boundary made real (a module-private token held only by the SW entry, or a provenance check in the SW module). Tests pin the label check, not provenance.
2. MEDIUM (Stage 2 hardening) — the ciphertext is not bound to its storage key: AES-GCM is called with no additionalData (secret-vault.js:102, 120), so moving record A's {iv, ct} into the cap:vault:secret:B slot decrypts cleanly and is served as B's credential (mask and raw). Authenticating the keyId as AAD closes the swap class and costs one line each in encrypt/decrypt.
3. LOW — install-salt creation is not atomic (secret-vault.js:47-54): two concurrent opens can each generate a salt and set it; the loser derives from a salt that is then overwritten, so its records fail integrity later (fail-closed, but silent data loss). Re-read after set (or compare-and-set) and adopt the stored salt.
4. NOTE — listMasked decrypts every record to compute masks, i.e. the UI projection needs the derived key in the calling context. That is coherent with this design (same extension, same derivation), but it means the mask path's cost scales with the number of secrets and the projection is not "metadata only". Worth a sentence in the docstring.
5. NOTE — `v: 1` is recorded but no migration path exists yet; fine for Stage 1, name it in Stage 2 before the first format change.

CLEARED for Stage 1: the four properties in the request are implemented and tested (at-rest encryption, no plaintext serialization, non-SW refusal by label, fail-closed integrity), with the honest threat model stated at the top of the file. Findings 1 and 2 are worth a follow-up bead before Stage 2 builds on this store; 3 is a two-line hardening.

title: [epic] Secure Enclave Proxy & Credential-Vault Tool Gateway (CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE)
description:
Architectural overhaul per Paul Kinlan's directive (2026-10-03):
Enable Chrome Agent Platform to expose authenticated web APIs and external services (e.g. Brave Search, GitHub, SaaS REST APIs) as first-class tools without requiring dedicated MCP servers and without EVER leaking API keys, bearer tokens, or environment secrets to the LLM or agent context.

Architecture:
1. Secret Vault & Key Storage (extension/lib/secret-vault.js): isolated storage for service tokens, never serialized into logs, prompt context, or agent messages.
2. Secure Enclave Outbound Proxy (extension/background/routes/enclave-proxy.js): Service Worker proxy intercepting service calls, injecting stored credentials into headers/query params, enforcing strict origin allowlists, SSRF protection, manual redirects, and response redaction/fencing.
3. Declarative Tool Synthesizer (extension/lib/service-tools.js): declarative JSON descriptors mapping semantic tool parameters to HTTP request templates without exposing auth fields to the model.
4. Sandboxed Code Mode (extension/lib/code-mode-sandbox.js): chaining multiple tool and enclave calls in sandbox without credential disclosure.
5. Settings UI & Credential Management (extension/options/): Secure Enclave Vault UI for managing API keys, presets (Brave Search, etc.), with masked status and test verification.
6. Enclave Audit Ledger & Quota Limiter: per-service request ledger, rate limits, and fail-closed quotas.

REVIEW VERDICT: FAIL — one blocking finding (content-based refusal is defeated by a CD/local-header mismatch), two notes. Reviewer: cap-ds-flash (deepseek), author voicebox-gemini (gemini) — cross-family. Candidate 27f43e69, detached worktree ~/worktrees/review-4p7j4.

BLOCKING — THE "REFUSES BINARY WHEELS BY CONTENT" PROPERTY IS DEFEATED BY A CD/LOCAL-HEADER MISMATCH. validatePurePythonWheel reads the CENTRAL DIRECTORY and returns those names (`if (names.length > 0) return names;` in extractZipFilenames), so an archive whose CD lists only pure entries while its LOCAL headers carry a native binary is accepted. Reproduced with a hand-built fixture (my own, not the author's): a zip with local headers `pkg/__init__.py`, `pkg-1.0.dist-info/WHEEL`, `pkg/payload.so` and a CD rewritten to list ONLY the WHEEL entry -> validatePurePythonWheel returns `{ok:true}` while the bytes physically contain `pkg/payload.so`. Repro: ~/cap-evidence/review-4p7j4/{rev4p7j4-probe.mjs,rev4p7j4-fixtures,result.txt} (`{"name":"cd-mismatch-py3-none-any.whl","ok":true,...}`). Today the store does not extract, so this is not yet exploitable end-to-end — but the validator's contract is content-based admission and the future extractor is exactly the consumer that could read local headers. CHEAPEST FIX: in extractZipFilenames, when the CD path yields names, ALSO walk the local headers and either validate those names too or reject when the two name sets differ (a well-formed wheel always agrees); add this fixture as a test. Secondary: the local-header fallback trusts `compressedSize` without handling ZIP64 (0xFFFFFFFF)/data descriptors, so it can desync and truncate the name list — fail closed there once both sets are validated.

VERIFIED TRUE (my own probes, not the author's tests): my valid wheel `pkg-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` -> ok:true; my disguised binary wheel (pure name, `pkg/native.so` inside) -> binary-wheel-rejected; my traversal binary (`../../evil.so`) -> binary-wheel-rejected. Routes: wheel.list extension|owner-options, wheel.put/wheel.delete owner-options only, delete digest-regex validated, content validated BEFORE storage. Focused suites: 19 passed / 0 failed (wheel-store-routes + sw-route-modularization + sw-dispatch-authority-census); the census's AST derivation asserts 275 and passes.

NOTES: (1) a traversal-shaped PURE name (`../../pkg/__init__.py`) passes the validator — harmless today, zip-slip for a naive extractor; reject `..`/absolute names. title: [ui] Anchor NTP sidebar footer (Directory, Artifacts, Settings) to bottom and flex open collapsible sections to fill remaining height
description:
Owner feedback:
'Can we get directory, artifacts and settings section anchored to the bottom then space the other sections out to fill the rest (keeping the collapsable nature)'

### Root Cause
1. In extension/ntp/ntp.html, .side-foot lacked margin-block-start: auto and flex: 0 0 auto, so when #tasks-section was collapsed (or short), the footer floated up into the middle of the sidebar.
2. Only #tasks-section[open] had flex-grow > 0 (flex: 1 1 280px), while #agents-section[open], #board-strip[open], #activity-section[open], and #failed-runs[open] had flex: 0 0 auto and hard-coded max-height caps (120px/140px/160px on .bs-list, .agents-list, #side-agents, .activity-list, .fr-list), preventing open sections from expanding and spacing out to fill the available vertical height above .side-foot.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. Anchor .side-foot to the bottom of .side via margin-block-start: auto; flex: 0 0 auto; in both expanded and collapsed sidebar states.
2. Give open collapsible sections proportional flex growth (#tasks-section[open] flex: 1.6 1 160px; #agents-section[open] flex: 1.2 1 130px; #activity-section[open], #board-strip[open], #failed-runs[open] flex: 1 1 96px; with min-height and overflow: clip) and remove the hard-coded 120px/140px/160px max-height caps on .fr-list, .bs-list, .agents-list, #side-agents, and .activity-list (setting flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; max-height: none; overflow-y: auto) so open sections distribute and fill the vertical space down to .side-foot while closed sections (:not([open])) collapse to flex: 0 0 auto.
3. Add falsification tests in tests/ntp-sidebar-collapsible.test.ts and verify in headless Chrome (1280x900) across multiple disclosure states (all open, Tasks closed + Agents/Board open, all closed) that .side-foot stays anchored to the bottom of .side (sideRect.bottom - footRect.bottom <= 20) and open sections fill the available height.

title: [ui] Rethink NTP left sidebar: collapsible disclosure sections, Tasks primary flex height, human cadence, and clean collapsed rail
description:
## Problem
Owner feedback with screenshots (`Screenshot 2026-10-02 at 13.25.37.png` expanded and `Screenshot 2026-10-02 at 13.29.04.png` collapsed):
1. **Expanded sidebar (`13.25.37.png`)**:
   - All sections (`Tasks`, `Failed runs (2)`, `Harness agents`, `Board (0 open)`, `Agents`, `Activity (8)`) are permanently stacked in the 240px sidebar. `Harness agents` and `Board (0 open)` eat the middle of the sidebar, starving `Tasks` and `Agents` into tiny 2-item scroll areas.
   - Owner: *'These should all be collapsible like the Activity one'* and *'We need to massively rethink how the sidebar in the NTP works... I think it is fundamentally terrible UI, the collapse and hide doesn't work well, it's hard to use'*.
   - Also in `Agents`, scheduled agents still display raw `Scheduled · every 1440 min` instead of human cadence (`Scheduled · daily`).
2. **Collapsed sidebar (`13.29.04.png`)**:
   - Owner: *'the collapsed state looks terrible'*.
   - In `.side.collapsed` (56px rail):
     - `#board-strip` (`Board (0 open) Social Media Planner finished...`) is NOT hidden in `.side.collapsed`, so its bordered card and text literally overflow and get clipped underneath the `#side-toggle` (`>`) button!
     - `#side-toggle` sits mid-rail overlapping `#board-strip` with a persistent circular focus outline.
     - `Tasks` collapses into 4 unlabelled grey dots (`.t-dot`) floating in empty space, and two identical `+` buttons (`#new-task` and `#new-agent`) stack as mystery-meat squares.
     - Agent avatars at the bottom clip through the section divider, and the footer stacks `Artifacts` + `>` awkwardly.

## Required Fix
1. **Collapsible disclosure sections across the expanded NTP sidebar (`extension/ntp/ntp.html`, `extension/ntp/ntp.js`)**:
   - Make `Tasks` the primary flex-growing section (`flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 180px`) at the top of the sidebar so the user's task history has generous vertical room.
   - Make `Failed runs` (`#failed-runs`), `Harness agents` (`#harness-section` / `#harness-presence`), `Board` (`#board-strip`), `Agents` (`#agents-section`), and `Activity` (`#activity-section`) clean collapsible `<details class="side-disclosure">` sections with a consistent summary header (chevron + title + count badge, matching `Activity (8)`, plus the `+` action button on `Agents`), persisting open/closed state in `localStorage` (`cap:ntp:side-sections`), with `Tasks` and `Agents` open by default and `Harness agents`, `Board (0 open)` (when 0 open), and `Activity` compact/collapsible so `Tasks` is never starved!
   - Compact the `Harness agents` chips inside its disclosure so `pi`, `Claude Code`, `Codex` fit cleanly as compact pills without giant 44px full-width rows.
   - In `extension/ntp/ntp.js` (`renderAgentsPanel`), format `periodInMinutes` using `formatCadenceMinutes` so `1440` renders as `Scheduled · daily` instead of `Scheduled · every 1440 min`.
2. **Rethink and fix the collapsed sidebar state (`.side.collapsed` in `extension/ntp/ntp.html`, `ntp.js`)**:
   - Move/anchor the sidebar collapse/expand toggle cleanly into the sidebar header row (next to the brand logo when expanded, and centered at the top of the rail when collapsed, with `:focus-visible` outline only — never a persistent floating circle overlapping content mid-rail, while keeping `#side-toggle` id and aria-label/aria-expanded contract intact!).
   - When `.side.collapsed` is active (56px rail):
     - Strictly hide ALL section bodies, cards, and text bleed: `#board-strip`, `#failed-runs`, `#harness-presence`, `#activity-section`, `.side-disclosure`, `#tasks-list`, `#agents-list`, and `#new-agent` must be cleanly hidden (`display: none !important`) in `.side.collapsed` so there are ZERO mystery dots, ZERO clipped agent avatars, ZERO duplicate `+` buttons, and ZERO `Board (0 open)` text bleed!
     - In the collapsed 56px rail, show a clean, intentional vertical icon bar:
       1. Top: Expand sidebar button (`#side-toggle`)
       2. Primary action: New task icon button (`#new-task`, with tooltip `New task`)
       3. Quick section jump buttons (or clean icon triggers for Tasks & Agents that expand the sidebar and focus that section when clicked)
       4. Spacer (`flex: 1`)
       5. Bottom rail icons: Directory (`#open-directory`), Artifacts (`#open-gallery`, with `#drawer-toggle` hidden in collapsed mode), and Settings (`#open-settings`) — all cleanly aligned 40x40 icon buttons with tooltips!

## Acceptance Criteria
- Falsification unit/DOM tests in `tests/ntp-sidebar-collapsible.test.ts` verifying:
  - Collapsible disclosure sections in the sidebar and persisted state.
  - `formatCadenceMinutes(1440)` used in sidebar agent subtitle (`Scheduled · daily`).
  - In `.side.collapsed`, `#board-strip`, `#failed-runs`, `#harness-presence`, and `#tasks-list` have `display: none` and zero horizontal overflow (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth`).
- Headless Chrome before/after screenshots of both the expanded sidebar (with 20+ seeded tasks, failed runs, harness agents, board, and 6 named/scheduled agents) and the collapsed sidebar rail.

title: [bug] Anchor @ agent mention picker and /agent popup directly to the composer input box in Side Panel and Hub
description:
## Problem
When using the Side Panel in the extension and typing `@` to reference an agent (or `/agent`), the agent picker popup is detached from the composer input box instead of being anchored directly to it.

## Root Causes (verified in source)
1. **`#page-view` and `#agents-view` in `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.html:26, 83` set `container-type: inline-size`**:
   - In CSS, `container-type: inline-size` creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants!
   - `placeFloating` (`extension/shared/components.js:152-183`) computes `anchor.getBoundingClientRect()` (relative to the viewport, which includes the 53px top tab bar in `sidepanel.html`), and then sets `floatEl.style.position = 'fixed'; floatEl.style.top = top + 'px'`. Because `#page-view` is the fixed-position containing block, `top` is offset by `#page-view`'s top offset (~53px), detaching the popup from the input box!
2. **Clamping & height mismatch in `placeFloating` when filtering `@` mentions**:
   - When `placeFloating` places the popup above the composer using `top = a.top - h - 4` and clamps `top = Math.max(margin, Math.min(top, window.innerHeight - h - margin))`, if `h` (up to 320px) is larger than `a.top` (e.g. when `#page-empty-state` is shown and `.page-composer` sits mid-viewport because `#page-history:empty` is `display:none`), `fitsAbove` is false AND `fitsBelow` is false, so `placeFloating` clamps `top` to the middle/bottom of the viewport right on top of or detached from the input box!
3. **Conflicting invalid CSS anchor positioning on `.popup, .slash-menu` (`extension/shared/components.js:7660`) and `.agent-pop` (`line 7726`)**:
   - Line 7660 uses `position-area: bottom span-x-start` (invalid CSS keyword in Chrome) while line 8818 unconditionally overrides with `placeFloating` (`position: fixed`).
   - Line 8074 skips `placeFloating` when `supportsAnchorPositioning()` is true, leaving `.agent-pop` (`/agent` and `+` -> Choose agent) relying on `anchor-scope` across light-DOM custom elements which fails to anchor in the sidepanel popover top-layer.
4. **In `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.html:56-59`**:
   - When `#page-history` is empty (`#page-history:empty { display: none }`), `.page-empty-state` does not have `flex: 1`, so `.page-composer` floats in the middle of the sidepanel instead of staying pinned at the bottom of the panel!

## Required Fix
1. In `extension/shared/components.js`:
   - Anchor `agent-composer .popup, agent-composer .slash-menu` directly to `.composer` (`position: relative`) using `position: absolute` (or subtract the offsetParent/fixed-containing-block rect in `placeFloating`):
     Specifically, since `.popup` is a direct child of `.composer` (`position: relative`), positioning it with `position: absolute; left: 12px; right: 12px; width: auto; max-width: 440px;` and choosing `bottom: calc(100% + 6px); top: auto;` (when opening above) vs `top: calc(100% + 6px); bottom: auto;` (when opening below), with `max-height` dynamically clamped to the available space above/below (`Math.max(120, Math.min(300, availableSpace - 12))px`), guarantees the popup is **physically attached** `6px` from the composer border in BOTH Side Panel and Hub, never drifts when `container-type: inline-size` is used, and stays attached as the list height shrinks/grows while typing `@...`.
   - Fix `placeFloating` so that for any `position: fixed` element (like `.agent-pop` in the top layer or `.tab-picker`), it accounts for any transformed/container containing block (or top-layer viewport coordinates) AND always call `placeFloating(this._input || this._attach, this._agentPop, { minWidth: 280, maxWidth: 380 })` in `_presentAgentPopover()` and on query changes in `_openSlashAgentPicker()` so `/agent` and `+` -> Choose agent are ALSO tightly anchored to the composer in the Side Panel!
2. In `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.html`:
   - Give `.page-empty-state` `flex: 1; justify-content: center;` when visible so `.page-composer` stays consistently docked at the bottom of the Side Panel whether the conversation is empty or populated, giving the `@` picker full room above the input box.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Falsification unit test + headless Chrome verification in `sidepanel.html` (at 360x640) typing `@`, `@s`, and `/agent` in `#page-composer` and `#agent-composer`, asserting via `getBoundingClientRect()` that the gap between the popup and the composer input box is `<= 8px` (attached directly above or below the composer, never detached or overlapping).
- Save before/after screenshots of `@` mention picker in `sidepanel.html`.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Hub Timeline filter segmented-control white active selector stays stuck on All when clicking Runs/Waiting/Made/Scheduled
description:
Observed by owner (2026-10-02): Clicking Timeline filter tabs (All / Runs / Waiting / Made / Scheduled) in the Hub does not move the white background active selector off 'All'.

Root cause (cross-branch interaction between 9epn.2 and 716s.6):
1. 'segmented-control' was placed in NON_HUB_ELEMENTS in extension/shared/components.js:908 (9epn.2), deferring customElements.define('segmented-control', SegmentedControl) on ntp.html until after Stage 2 (renderTimeline).
2. In extension/ntp/ntp.js:1485, renderTimeline() assigns timelineFilterEl.value = savedFilter BEFORE <segmented-control id='timeline-filters'> is upgraded. That assignment creates an OWN data property (Object.hasOwn(timelineFilterEl, 'value') === true, value: 'All') on the HTMLElement instance.
3. When registerDeferredComponents() later defines 'segmented-control', the instance's own 'value' property SHADOWS SegmentedControl.prototype.value (the getter/setter).
4. When the user clicks 'Runs', 'Waiting', 'Made', or 'Scheduled', SegmentedControl._select() sets this._value = 'Runs' and calls this._sync(), which reads 'const value = this.value' — returning the shadowing own property 'All' instead of this._value! Thus aria-selected='true' (and the white background selector) remains permanently stuck on 'All', and _select()'s 'changed = value !== this.value' check is also corrupted.

Fix & Acceptance:
1. Remove 'segmented-control' from NON_HUB_ELEMENTS in extension/shared/components.js (it is a primary Hub element in ntp.html).
2. In Component / SegmentedControl (and AgentTimeline), upgrade pre-upgrade own properties in connectedCallback (_upgradeProperty('value'), _upgradeProperty('entries'), _upgradeProperty('filter')) by deleting the own property and re-assigning through the prototype setter so pre-upgrade property assignment can never shadow prototype accessors.
3. Also ensure SegmentedControl._select() / _sync() works when an overflow filter (Hooks/Pages/Spent) is selected and then a primary tab (including 'All') is clicked again.
4. Falsification unit test + real headless Chrome for Testing verification clicking All -> Runs -> Waiting -> Made -> Scheduled and asserting aria-selected='true' and computed backgroundColor move to the clicked tab.

title: [bug] A paused run reopened in a new tab shows “Working — run in progress…” with NO Allow card; sidebar dot (amber), timeline (“Running…”) and status row disagree (UI #1)
description:
Observed: start a task on a keyless profile → the run pauses on the list_tabs approval card (shot thread-waiting-card-1440-light.png; sidebar dot amber). Open the hub in a NEW tab and click the same thread: body shows "Working — run in progress…" and no permission-approval-card / tool card after 2 s, 5 s and 12 s (measurements-followup.json → pausedReopen; shot thread-paused-reopened-after-12s-1440-light.png). The sidebar dot is still amber (paused) while the body says Working; the hub timeline row reads "Running…" (hub-timeline-1440-light.png). Live view title says "New task" while paused; the reopened view shows the task text (two title sources).
Cause: extension/ntp/ntp.js:2702-2705 renders ANY actionable run on reopen as { state: "running", activity: "run in progress" } regardless of paused/waiting; the approval card is mounted only by the live projection path, not by projectSurfaceRunTranscript() replay.

Build: on reopen derive the status row from the run's actual state (paused → "Waiting for you" + re-mount the pending approval card from the run registry / journal; running → Working; done/failed as today). Make the sidebar dot, the timeline row and the status row read from ONE projection (extension/shared/thread-projection-authority.js) so three surfaces cannot disagree. One title source for live and reopened views. Answering the re-mounted card must route through the same durable approval path as the live card (no second approval identity).

Acceptance (falsifiable):
- Pure projection unit test: a run in paused-permission with a pending approval projects {state:"waiting", card:{...}}; running → working; the same projection feeds the dot/timeline/status (one function, three consumers) — RED on origin/main.
- Journey (CfT): start keyless task, wait for the approval card, open the thread in a second tab → within 2 s the second tab shows the Allow/Not now card and status text "Waiting…" (not "Working"); clicking Allow there resolves the SAME approval id; measurements pausedReopen.cardText non-null. Screenshots before/after.
- Sidebar dot colour, timeline row text and status row state agree for paused, running, done, failed (table-driven test over the projection).
- Live and reopened titles are identical for the same thread (test).
Seams: extension/ntp/ntp.js openThread (~2690-2715), projectSurfaceRunTranscript, extension/shared/thread-projection-authority.js, AgentTimeline row text (extension/shared/components.js ~12138-12222), renderRunStatus. Effort M.

title: Split shared/components.js into a core + lazily registered feature modules with esbuild splitting (sidepanel 635 → ≤250 KB, ntp 833 → ≤500 KB, options 843 → ≤450 KB) (perf #2 part 2)
description:
Observed: shared/components.js (768 KB source, 58 elements, ≈480 KB minified) is statically compiled into ntp (52 % of its 1.23 MB pre-minify), options (53.5 %) and sidepanel (≈83 % of 635 KB). Per-surface usage (audit's components-usage.json): ntp 31/58, sidepanel 20/58, options 17/58. No splitting/dynamic import() exists in UI source (only options/user-wasm-panel.js:6). AGENTS.md requires components to remain the single source consumed by the gallery (scripts/sync-gallery.mjs; check:gallery).

Build: (1) split into shared/components-core.js (Component base, mountTemplate, the ≤ 15 elements shared by all three main surfaces) and feature modules (components-conversation.js, components-settings.js, components-artifacts.js, components-directory.js …) with shared/components.js kept as the aggregating barrel so the gallery and existing imports keep working; (2) esbuild splitting:true + outdir for the UI entries (build.mjs:495-497) so feature modules become shared chunks; await import() them at first use (openThread, openView('options…'), drawer open, Settings section mount) through one small lazy-define registry (customElements.whenDefined + a placeholder that preserves layout — no CLS); (3) keep tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:326-391 isolation assertions and the eval scrub over every emitted chunk; (4) ratchet the per-surface budgets down to the new ceilings.
Acceptance (falsifiable): store sizes sidepanel initial ≤ 250 KB, ntp initial ≤ 500 KB, options initial ≤ 450 KB (budgets pinned; shown failing before); customElements.get('tool-library') is undefined on ntp until the directory/settings view opens (journey); every surface's chrome-journeys checks stay green; check:gallery passes; assertNoDynamicEvaluators runs over every chunk; no CLS on lazy mount (CLS 0 budget in perf harness).
Seams: build.mjs:450-519, 536-595; extension/shared/components.js (all customElements.define sites, :792 mountTemplate); scripts/sync-gallery.mjs; docs/components.html; scripts/bundle-budget.mjs; tests/bundle-budget.test.ts. Effort L — consider landing core/barrel + splitting flag first, then moving element groups in follow-up commits on the same branch.

title: Site tools follow the tab into the hub run: /tabs attach ⇒ WebMCP tools available with in-moment Allow, no Settings enrollment (#1)
description:
User job: "On this flight-booking tab, use the site's own tools to change my seat" typed in the hub composer with the tab attached via /tabs — with zero visits to Settings. PRODUCT.md rule 3 + lines 188-196 name this as "the biggest gap between what the product IS and how it presents itself".

Observed: a run's WebMCP workers are built from listOrigins() = ENROLLED origins only (extension/background/service-worker.js:2424-2429 "// Workers = enrolled site origins"), filtered by the agent allow-list. A /tabs attachment reaches the model as the text line "[tab: name — url]" only (extension/lib/attachments.js:51-52). The side panel already proves the on-tab pattern: "Enable site tools" requests scripting + the exact origin, calls agent.enroll-origin and reloads (extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js:143-172). agent.discoverable-tabs (service-worker.js:7692) backs a picker, not the composer. Owner history: xv1n was ABANDONED because it drifted into inferring page JS functions — this bead is strictly DECLARED WebMCP (navigator.modelContext / the detection registry), no inference.

Build:
1. Attachments carry tabId + documentId (not just url). When a composer turn carries a tab attachment (or the side-panel page thread), the SW consults lib/webmcp-detection-registry.js for that tab's document; if a positive capability report exists and the origin is NOT enrolled, the run builds a worker for that origin in EPHEMERAL mode: origin memory read-only, no persistent Site Agent record, torn down with the run. The JIT grant is the same request sidepanel.js:153 makes (scripting; host access is install-granted so no origin prompt).
2. First model use of a tool on that origin raises the EXISTING per-tool consent card (lib/site-tool-consent.js — Q23 semantics unchanged: ask once, Allow persists, Deny sticky).
3. Composer: an "Offers N tools" chip next to the tab attachment (count only — CONSTITUTION §1: the passive detector transports a COUNT, descriptions reach the model only after Allow), with an "Add as Site Agent" affordance for standing access. Enrollment remains the explicit persistent choice; Settings → Site agents is the management view.
4. Side panel reuses the same route rather than enrolling as its first step (keep its Enable button as the standing-access path).
Security: the origin MUST come from the detection registry's browser-attested tab/document, never the attachment payload. Ephemeral worker uses siteMemory(origin) read-only and never the master sentinel. No cross-origin OPFS access.

title: Product-owned context menu + keyboard command: “Ask agent about this page / selection / link / image” (#2)
description:
User job: select a paragraph on any page → right-click → "Ask agent about selection" → the side panel opens on that tab with the quote attached (fenced as untrusted) and the page as context. Same for a link ("summarise what this links to"), an image (vision attachment), and the page itself. A keyboard chord does the page variant.

Observed: no chrome.contextMenus.create is owned by the product — the only creators are the model tool create_context_menu (extension/lib/browser-tools.js:3364) and skills that ask the model to register one (extension/lib/skill-registry.js:148-167). The SW only binds contextMenus.onClicked as a hook event (service-worker.js:11348). The three manifest commands all open a surface and carry no selection/page context (service-worker.js:11541-11595); omnibox carries text only (:11597-11665). Probe: contextMenus is optional and ungranted on a fresh profile, so the menu must be registered after grant.

Build:
1. registerProductContextMenus(): one parent "Agent" with four children — Ask about this page (contexts ["page"]), Ask about selection (["selection"]), Ask about this link (["link"]), Ask about this image (["image"]). Register on runtime.onInstalled AND on permissions.onAdded containing "contextMenus"; remove on permissions.onRemoved. Idempotent (removeAll then create) so SW restarts never duplicate.
2. Click handler (user gesture): build a composer prefill — selectionText as a text/plain attachment tagged untrusted:true; pageUrl/linkUrl as a tab/url attachment; srcUrl via the existing image attachment path. Open the side panel on that tab (chrome.sidePanel.open is legal on the gesture) with fallback to the hub via the existing hash-prefill route the omnibox uses. Prefill hand-off must be origin-safe (session storage keyed by tabId or the existing SW→surface port), never a URL query carrying page text.
3. Fourth manifest command ask-about-page (suggested Alt+Shift+A) doing the page variant.
4. Grant moment: Settings → Permissions already has a generic row for contextMenus ("Right-click menu") — confirm its copy; add a one-time dismissible hub banner "Add 'Ask agent' to your right-click menu" with ONE action that calls chrome.permissions.request on the click. Never request from the SW without a gesture.
Constitution: selection/link text is page-controlled → untrusted:true so the fence applies; render in cards with textContent; no SW-initiated sidePanel.open outside the gesture.

Acceptance (falsifiable):
- Unit (fake chrome): after permissions.onAdded(["contextMenus"]) exactly 1 parent + 4 items exist with the expected contexts; after onRemoved none; calling register twice yields the same 5 ids (idempotent). RED without the change.
- Unit: the onClicked projection for {selectionText:"hello", pageUrl} produces an attachment {kind:"text", untrusted:true, bytes:5} plus the url attachment; link/image variants produce their attachment kinds.
- Journey (CfT): dispatch the click handler on a fixture tab → side panel shows the composer with a "Selection (5 chars)" attachment chip; the next model request's attestation contains the fenced block. Screenshot.
- Without the permission: no items, Settings row reads Off, no console error.
- Manifest test pins the fourth command.
Seams: extension/background/service-worker.js (new registerProductContextMenus + command handler), extension/lib/notification-action-routing.js (click→surface pattern), extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js (prefill), extension/manifest.json commands, extension/lib/permission-language.js, components.js banner (reuse the existing onboarding banner component — no hand-rolled markup). Effort S/M.

title: [bug] list_recently_closed / restore_closed / list_synced_devices can never run: `sessions` is not an optional permission and the capability table says none is needed (#3)
description:
Observed: extension/lib/chrome-tool-capabilities.js:432-440 catalogues the three sessions tools with optionalPermissions: [] and the comment "sessions (no manifest permission)". That is wrong: chrome.sessions requires the "sessions" permission, and "sessions" is absent from both permissions and optional_permissions in extension/manifest.json:7-45. Live probe in the loaded SW: typeof chrome.sessions === "undefined"; the tool returns "sessions API not available in this browser context" unconditionally (extension/lib/browser-tools.js:4812-4813). Three catalogued tools are a promise that always fails — the open_side_panel precedent (OPEN-QUESTIONS Q17) says such tools are either made real or removed with a guard.

Decision (recommended, implement this): option (a) — make them real. "Reopen the tab I closed an hour ago" is a genuine coworker ask and the implementation is already written.
1. Add "sessions" to optional_permissions in manifest.json.
2. Set optionalPermissions: ["sessions"] on the three rows in chrome-tool-capabilities.js; route through the standard in-context Allow card with plain-language copy in lib/permission-language.js ("see and restore recently closed tabs"). The restore_closed grant model (browser-control covering every restored origin) stays as is.
3. On a profile without the grant the call must return the standard permissionDeniedResult("sessions") (the one that drives the Allow card), never the "not available" string.
4. Update scripts/permission-matrix-acceptance.ts row + docs/PERMISSION-MATRIX.md + the Settings → Permissions row (it is generic; confirm it renders).
If the owner prefers (b) cut: remove the three tools + rows + browser.sessions purpose group with a removal guard like tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts (138→135). Do NOT do both; default to (a).

Acceptance (falsifiable):

- Unit test with a fake chrome: without the grant, list_recently_closed returns the permission-denied shape (not the "not available" string); with chrome.sessions present it returns entries.
- Journey (CfT, seeded permissions): close a fixture tab → list_recently_closed returns it → restore_closed restores it (tab count +1). Record screenshot/evidence path.
- Manifest test pins "sessions" in optional_permissions and NOT in permissions.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-SETTINGS-SKILLS-BACKUP-01] Fix LM Studio connection test, expose required local provider fields, fix Skills onUse ReferenceError, and wire .tar backup restore
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **LM Studio "Test Connection" Hard-Fails with `Unknown provider "lm-studio"`**:
   - `"lm-studio"` is registered in `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_IDS` in `provider.js:164-172` and `options.js:219-227`, but omitted from `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_IDS` in `extension/lib/provider-test.js:23-30`. Clicking **Test connection** on the LM Studio card always fails at `provider-test.js:141`.
2. **Required `Model` & `Base URL` Fields Hidden Under Collapsed `<details>Advanced</details>` for Local/Custom Providers**:
   - In `buildProviderCard` (`extension/options/options.js:768-776`), `Model` and `Base URL` are hidden inside a collapsed `<details class="provider-advanced">` even for `ollama`, `lm-studio`, and `openai-compatible` where `models: []` / `defaultModel: ""` require user input. And `returnToHubComposer()` (`options.js:830`) only triggers when `p.needsKey` is true.
3. **Clicking "Use" on Any Imported Command in Settings → Skills Throws `ReferenceError: onUse is not defined`**:
   - In `extension/skills/skills-panel.js:308`, inside `mountSkillsSection`, imported command rows wire `row.addEventListener("use", () => onUse?.(view))`, where `onUse` is not in scope (it is only a parameter of `renderSkillList` at line 73). Additionally, `useSkill` (`L116-136`) hardcodes `/skill:${skill.name}` instead of respecting `view.ref` (`/${cmd.name}`) for commands.
4. **Backup Export (`.tar`) vs. Import (`.json`-only) Format Mismatch**:
   - `#export-all-btn` (`options.js:3276-3299`) exports a `.tar` archive via `streamExportArchive`, but `#import-all-file` (`extension/options/options.html:465`) sets `accept=".json,application/json"` and `options.js:3337-3351` parses the selected file as JSON via `owner.import.all`, rejecting `.tar` backups.

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `extension/lib/provider-test.js:23-30`
- `extension/options/options.html:398-401, 447, 465`
- `extension/options/options.js:768-835, 3331-3360`
- `extension/skills/skills-panel.js:116-136, 305-315`

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification tests verifying:
  1. `testProviderConnection({ provider: "lm-studio", baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1", model: "local-model" })` succeeds against a mock OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint instead of returning `Unknown provider "lm-studio"`.
  2. Clicking `use` on an imported command row in `mountSkillsSection` (`skills-panel.js`) does not throw `ReferenceError` and copies/routes `/<command-name>`.
  3. `#import-all-file` accepts `.tar` and `.json` files, and selecting a `.tar` backup invokes `streamRestoreArchive` while `.json` continues to use `owner.import.all`.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-SIDEPANEL-UX-01] Preserve tool cards/artifacts/approvals on Side Panel tab switches, add 1-click site tool enrollment, and fix narrow-width overflow
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **Side Panel Tab Switching Drops All Tool Cards, Artifacts, Screenshots & Approval Cards**:
   - In `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js:252-262`, `loadTabThread(tabId)` calls `send("thread.get", { id: pageThreadId })` and passes `res.thread` directly to `projectThreadMessages(res.thread)` without fetching `run.thread-logs` or calling `projectThreadWithRunLogs(thread, executions)`.
   - Because tool calls, artifacts, screenshots, and permission approval cards live in durable run logs, switching tabs and returning wipes them all from the Side Panel conversation.
   - In addition, `PAGE_THREADS_KEY` is stored only in `sessionStorage` (`sidepanel.js:205-217`), which clears when the Side Panel is closed, and `#page-history` / `#agent-history` lack event listeners for `open-tab`, `reuse`, `open-image`, and `approval-decision`.
2. **Dead-End "No site tools added" Status & Non-Interactive Tool Chips**:
   - In `sidepanel.js:116-154`, unenrolled sites show `"No site tools added"` with no button to enable site tools in-place, and discovered tools render as inert `<span class="tool-chip">` elements without descriptions or click actions.
3. **360px Header Overflow & Typography Drift**:
   - In `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.html:35-156`, `.agent-bar-title` has `white-space: nowrap` without `min-width: 0; flex: 1`, causing long agent names to collide with action buttons at 360px width; fractional font sizes (`11.5px`, `12.5px`) and uppercase tracked `.agent-section-h` violate `docs/DESIGN.md`.

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js:116-154, 205-262`
- `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.html:35-156`

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification tests verifying:
  1. `loadTabThread` in `sidepanel.js` fetches `run.thread-logs` and projects via `projectThreadWithRunLogs` so tool cards, artifacts, and approval cards survive tab switches.
  2. Unenrolled `http(s):` origins in the Side Panel render an actionable enable-site-tools control that requests `scripting` + origin access and calls `agent.enroll-origin`, and discovered tool chips render as interactive `<button class="tool-chip">` controls with descriptions.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-HUB-RUN-UX-01] Fix Hub starter chips on keyless/NTP profiles, mid-run Queue/Steer with attachments, slide-over Settings routing, boot RPC deduplication, and private workspace file list
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **Starter Example Chips Dead-End on Keyless Profiles & Privileged NTP URL**:
   - `extension/ntp/ntp.html:1064` and `extension/ntp/ntp.js:4381` set `<example-chips items="Group my tabs by topic|Summarise this page|Watch this price">`.
   - On a fresh keyless profile, `local-assistant.js` only supports tab intents (`group`, `summarise`, `dedupe`, `list`), so 2 of the 3 starter chips immediately fail. Even with a cloud model, clicking `"Summarise this page"` on the Hub tries to run `read_page` on `chrome-extension://.../ntp.html` and fails.
2. **Local Providers (Ollama / LM Studio) Leave First-Run Banner Stuck**:
   - `extension/lib/first-run-onboarding.js:68-90` (`providerReadyForFirstTask`) rejects `ollama` and requires `hasApiKey === true`, so configuring keyless `ollama` or `lm-studio` leaves `<first-run-guide>` ("Connect a model") stuck on the Hub.
3. **`#provider-status` & Error "Fix in Settings" Open Separate Tabs Instead of the Hub Slide-Over**:
   - `ntp.js:4426-4428` calls `chrome.runtime.openOptionsPage()` instead of `openView("options/options.html#providers", "Provider settings", trigger)`, and `ntp.js` does not refresh `renderProviderStatus()` or `refreshFirstRunGuide()` on `visibilitychange` or `chrome.storage.onChanged`.
4. **Mid-Run `While running` Bar Silently Bypassed When Sending with Attachments or `@agent`**:
   - `ntp.js:4166, 4212` gates `runControlSend` with `&& !attachments?.length && !agent?.ref`. Sending with an attachment or `@agent` while `Queue` or `Send now + stop` is selected bypasses the queue bar, starts a parallel `runThreadTurn()`, and overwrites `runSurfaceOwner.claim()`, orphaning the active run stream.
5. **NTP Cold-Boot RPC Stampede & `panelFrames` Spawning 4 Duplicate `options.html` Iframes**:
   - `ntp.js:4365-4366` calls both `renderNamedAgents()` and `renderBackgroundAgents()` (which immediately calls `renderNamedAgents()` again), `subscribeAmbientProgress` (`L1648`) calls `scheduleRunLogRefresh()` on every `ev.type === "text"` token, and `panelFrameFor(path)` (`L4677-4688`) keys `panelFrames` by full `path#hash`, creating up to 4 separate `options.html` iframes.
6. **Agent Private Workspaces Cannot Be Inspected Before Clearing**:
   - `ntp.js:4948-4982` shows only byte/file counts for `agent-workspaces/<key>/` without listing the files stored inside.

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `extension/ntp/ntp.html:171-216, 1064`
- `extension/ntp/ntp.js:343-398, 509-566, 1234-1239, 1648, 4166, 4212, 4362-4385, 4426-4428, 4677-4688, 4948-4982`
- `extension/lib/first-run-onboarding.js:68-90`

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification tests verifying:
  1. `providerReadyForFirstTask` returns `true` when `ollama` or `lm-studio` is explicitly selected and configured with a model or verified connection.
  2. Hub starter chips use tab-safe intents (`"Group my tabs by topic|Summarise my open tabs|Find duplicate tabs"`).
  3. `panelFrameFor` keys by base path (`options/options.html`) and updates hash navigation instead of spawning duplicate iframes.
  4. Mid-run `Queue` and `Send now + stop` preserve `attachments` and `agent` in `queuedTurns`.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-COMPOSER-TURN-QOL-01] Add composer clipboard paste & drag-drop attachments, in-place slash permission grants, ArrowUp history, 1-click expired approval retry, and turn copy/retry actions
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **No Clipboard Paste (`Cmd/Ctrl+V`) or Drag-and-Drop File/Image Support in `<agent-composer>`**:
   - `AgentComposer._wire()` (`extension/shared/components.js:7223-7274`) only accepts attachments via the `+` menu. Pasting a screenshot or dragging a file onto `.composer` does nothing.
2. **Ungranted `/bookmarks`, `/history`, `/files`, and `/folder` Slash Commands Redirect to Settings Instead of Granting In-Place**:
   - Selecting an ungranted `kind === "capability"` item in `AgentComposer._select` (`components.js:8114-8120`) leaves `/bookmarks` stranded in the input and calls `chrome.runtime.openOptionsPage()`, even though the selection is a user gesture that can call `chrome.permissions.request({ permissions: [this._activeToken.ns] })` directly in-place and immediately refresh the autocomplete list.
   - Similarly, `kind === "files-action"` (`components.js:8068-8074`) opens Settings instead of invoking `regrantFsGrantAccess` / `createNewFsGrant` in-place when available.
3. **No Prompt History (`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`) or `.tab-picker` Keyboard Navigation in `<agent-composer>`**:
   - Pressing `ArrowUp` in an empty composer does not recall previous sent prompts, and the floating `.tab-picker` (`components.js:7515-7554`) has no `Escape` or `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` handlers.
4. **Expired Permission Approval Cards (`state="expired"`) Lose Their `Allow` Button Permanently**:
   - `PermissionApprovalCard._render()` (`components.js:8571-8573`) only renders `.btn.allow` when `state === "pending"`. Once the 60s timer expires, the button disappears—even though `handleConversationApprovalDecision` in `ntp.js:3846-3879` already implements post-timeout grant + automatic task re-run!
5. **Missing Copy Action on Normal Agent Replies (< 4,000 Chars) & Inline Retry on Error Bubbles**:
   - `MessageBubble` (`components.js:5591-5634, 6008-6040`) only shows a copy button on responses > 4,000 chars (with no "Copied" confirmation), has no inline Retry button on `role="error"` bubbles, and calls `chrome.runtime.openOptionsPage()` directly from `.err-fix` instead of emitting a composed `fix-settings` event first.

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `extension/shared/components.js:5591-5634, 6008-6040` (`MessageBubble`)
- `extension/shared/components.js:7223-7274, 7515-7554, 8068-8125, 8242-8248` (`AgentComposer`)
- `extension/shared/components.js:8571-8573` (`PermissionApprovalCard`)

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification tests verifying:
  1. Pasting or dropping an image/file onto `<agent-composer>` adds an attachment chip via `addAttachment`.
  2. Selecting a `kind === "capability"` item in `<agent-composer>` calls `chrome.permissions.request` in-place and re-queries the slash command on grant.
  3. Pressing `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` in an empty `<agent-composer>` cycles through previously sent prompts.
  4. `<permission-approval-card state="expired">` renders an enabled `.btn.allow` (`"Allow & retry"`) that dispatches `approval-decision` with `{ decision: "allow" }`.
  5. `<message-bubble role="agent">` renders a copy button with `"Copied"` confirmation, and `<message-bubble role="error">` dispatches `retry-turn` and `fix-settings` events.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-OPFS-FS-PERF-01] Shard OPFS writeMutex per directory, cache gen/tombs metadata, skip .git/node_modules in fs-grants, and lazy-lock backup-export streams
description:
## Observed Problem & Why It Matters
1. **Process-Wide Global `writeMutex` & OPFS Write Amplification (`extension/lib/memory.js`)**:
   - `let writeMutex = Promise.resolve()` (`memory.js:717`) is a single module-wide lock that serializes all OPFS writes across `master`, `durable-runs`, `threads`, and every origin/agent store.
   - Inside each write (`setValueInner`, `compareAndRestore`), `currentVersion(dir, key)` (`L141-155`) and `issueVersion(dir)` (`L81-99`) re-read `__tombs.json` and `__gen.json` from disk on every key write (4-6 sequential OPFS file ops per write; 20-25 OPFS file ops per tool call).
2. **Cold-Wake OPFS Root Open in `recoverPendingImport` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:11199`)**:
   - Every SW wake calls `navigator.storage.getDirectory()` inside `recoverPendingImport` even when no `cap:importBackup` key exists in `chrome.storage.local`.
3. **Unbounded Local FS Traversal Over `.git` & `node_modules` (`extension/lib/fs-grants.js`)**:
   - `searchFsGrantFiles` (`L435`), `grepFsGrant` (`L756`), and `scanFsGrantManifest` (`L1001`) walk `.git`, `node_modules`, and `.deno` directories by default with `Infinity` depth/entry bounds, and `grepFsGrant` scans the entire file buffer for binary control bytes (`bytes.some(...)` at `L816`) instead of the first 8 KiB.
4. **Upfront Stream Reader Locking in `streamExportArchive` (`extension/lib/backup-export.js:30-72, 149-174`)**:
   - `rechunk(handle.stream, chunkSize)` (`L31`) calls `stream.getReader()` immediately inside the setup loop over `paths` (`L151-174`), locking $N$ concurrent `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` instances across all OPFS files before the first TAR header is emitted.

## Seams & Exact File Locations
- `extension/lib/memory.js:79-155, 717-790`
- `extension/background/service-worker.js:11199-11206`
- `extension/lib/fs-grants.js:435-534, 756-891, 1001-1095`
- `extension/lib/backup-export.js:30-72, 149-174`

## Implementation & Invariants
1. In `extension/lib/memory.js`, shard `writeMutex` by directory key (while preserving a barrier for global `resetAllStores`), and maintain a per-directory in-memory cache of `__gen.json` and `__tombs.json` that is invalidated whenever a directory is cleared/reset or external state is restored. All CAS/version/tombstone invariants tested by `tests/memory*.test.ts` must remain 100% intact.
2. In `extension/lib/fs-grants.js`, skip `".git"`, `"node_modules"`, and `".deno"` directory entries by default in `searchFsGrantFiles`, `grepFsGrant`, and `scanFsGrantManifest` unless `options.includeIgnored === true` is passed (or the query/path explicitly targets them), and check binary control bytes on the first 8192 bytes (`bytes.subarray(0, 8192)`) in `grepFsGrant`.
3. In `extension/lib/backup-export.js:30-72`, acquire `reader = stream.getReader()` lazily inside `ReadableStream.pull()` (and release/cancel cleanly on `cancel()`) so streams are not locked until TAR encoding pulls that entry.

## Falsification & Acceptance Criteria
- Add falsification unit tests proving:
  1. `rechunk` in `backup-export.js` does NOT lock `stream.locked` until the returned `ReadableStream` is pulled.
  2. `searchFsGrantFiles` and `grepFsGrant` skip `.git` and `node_modules` directories by default and include them when `includeIgnored: true`.
  3. Concurrent writes to two distinct origin/agent stores in `memory.js` preserve exact version monotonicity and tombstone semantics while avoiding redundant `__gen.json`/`__tombs.json` reads.

title: [CAP-FB-20260928-AUDIT-QOL-PERF-UI-01] UI, Performance, and UX Quality-of-Life Audit Remediation
description:
Umbrella epic tracking the comprehensive UI, Performance, Memory Resilience, and UX Quality-of-Life (QoL) improvements identified in the 2026-09-28 full-repository audit.

## Pillars
1. **Build & Bundle Footprint (P0/P1)**: Eliminate CJS+ESM double-bundling of zod/v4 in service-worker.js (-311 KB minified, solving Risk R18), strip the AI SDK (-1.73 MB raw) from options.bundle.js, and decouple SW-only backend stores (-401 KB raw) from ntp.bundle.js and options.bundle.js.
2. **Storage, OPFS & Local FS Performance (P0/P1)**: Shard global writeMutex per OPFS directory, cache __gen.json and __tombs.json per directory, skip .git/node_modules/.deno in fs-grants traversal, and lazily lock OPFS file streams in backup-export.js.
3. **Streaming & DOM Rendering Performance (P0/P1)**: Replace quadratic O(N^2) per-token full Markdown + Shadow DOM rebuilds during streaming with rAF-coalesced updates and persistent stylesheets, and lazily build collapsed <details class="tool"> trees on toggle.
4. **UI Contrast, Shadow DOM Keyboard A11y & CSS Polish (P0/P1)**: Fix dark-mode contrast failures from drifted token names (--surface-2, --accent-fg, --text-muted, --secondary, --ok), fix Shadow DOM activeElement keyboard traps in <mic-button> and <attach-button>, fix cross-Shadow #ap-list lookup in <agent-composer>, fix .aex-agent CSS collision and missing .tt-* styles in <activity-explorer>, add anchor-scope and field-sizing: content.
5. **Composer & Turn UX QoL (P1)**: Add clipboard paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V) and drag-and-drop file/image attachments, in-place permission grants for /bookmarks, /history, /files, and /folder slash commands, ArrowUp/ArrowDown prompt history, 1-click "Allow & retry" on expired permission approval cards, and Copy/Retry actions on conversation turns.
6. **Hub Onboarding, Mid-Run Queueing & Slide-Over Routing (P1)**: Fix Hub starter chips for keyless/NTP profiles, recognize configured Ollama/LM Studio in first-run readiness, route #provider-status and Fix in Settings to the in-context slide-over, preserve attachments/@agent in mid-run Queue/Send-now modes, deduplicate boot RPCs and panelFrames iframes, and list private workspace files in the Agent Editor.
7. **Side Panel Companion & Site Tools UX (P1)**: Project full run logs (tool cards, artifacts, screenshots, approvals) on Side Panel tab switches, persist PAGE_THREADS_KEY in chrome.storage.session, add 1-click "Enable site tools" in the Side Panel header, make tool chips interactive, and fix 360px header overflow.
8. **Settings, Skills & Backup Restore Parity (P1)**: Fix LM Studio Test Connection ("lm-studio" in OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_IDS), expose required Model/Base URL fields for local/custom providers, fix ReferenceError: onUse is not defined in skills-panel.js, and wire .tar backup files to streamRestoreArchive in options.js.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Implemented & pushed feat/0u8n-streaming-restore-driver @ a1f30413:
- extension/lib/backup-restore.js: Implemented 3-phase transactional streaming restore pipeline over decodeTarStream per docs/STREAMED-BACKUP-RESTORE-ARCHITECTURE.md:
  1. Staging directory extraction (.staging-restore-<timestamp>/): extracts, validates manifest, and holds staged files with clean rollback if stream fails.
  2. Owner confirmation: prompts confirm({ manifest, summary }) before mutation; aborts and cleans up staging if cancelled.
  3. Quiescence & Atomic Swap: clears/suspends alarms, writes cap:importBackup sidecar journal with full undo ops, atomically swaps staged files to destination, prunes unreferenced files if overwrite, applies KV/alarms, invalidates agent caches, and purges journal on success.
  4. Automatic fallback for legacy JSON cap-export bundles via existing importArchive.
- tests/backup-restore.test.ts: Added tests for staging/cancellation, rollback journal recovery on swap error, and legacy JSON fallback routing. 6/6 pass.
- npm run check:reachability: clean.
- npm run test:changed: 348 passed / 0 failed in 9s.
Ready for independent cross-family review.
