INDEPENDENT REVIEW: FAIL — three blockers (bak-k3, kimi family; author voicebox-resolver / Gemini — cross-family). Reviewed origin/feat/0u8n-streaming-restore-driver @ a1f30413 in a detached worktree (~/worktrees/bak-k3-review-0u8n), base origin/main 7c94c0d6. tests/backup-restore.test.ts 6/6 on my run; everything below is reproduced on my machine.

BLOCKER 1 — the production build FAILS at the tip. 'build:production clean' does not reproduce: options.bundle.js is 903,744 bytes against the 900,000 store budget (Error: bundle budget exceeded). Main on the same machine measures 899,231 — 769 bytes of headroom, and this branch adds ~4.5 KB bundled (the restore driver lands in the options bundle). The branch cannot land over a red build; the error's own guidance applies (lazy-load the driver / cut a contributor / an owner decision in docs/CONSTITUTION.md to raise the budget).

BLOCKER 2 — O(profile) memory retention, against the architecture's hard O(1) contract. docs/STREAMED-BACKUP-RESTORE-ARCHITECTURE.md is explicit: 'It must support arbitrarily large user profiles with O(1) constant memory overhead' (line 74; line 117: bounded by the 64 KiB chunk buffer) and the restore design says files MOVE from staging to live. The candidate's stagedEntries retains every file's BYTES across all three phases (push({ relPath, stagedPath, bytes }), then commit writes from the held bytes) — a 500 MB profile is held in JS memory for the whole restore. The staging directory already persists the bytes; the commit phase should re-read each stagedPath (or move) and never retain them. This reintroduces the exact property the 11rm epic exists to eliminate.

BLOCKER 3 — the rollback test cannot fail (mutant proven). I deleted the sidecar journal write entirely (the kvSet of cap:importBackup before the swap) and the suite stayed 6/6 GREEN. The 'swap failure triggers automatic rollback' test injects its disk error on the FIRST live write — before any mutation lands — so the asserted 'original data' was never overwritten; the journal is never exercised. Re-anchor per the canon: fail the SECOND live write and assert the FIRST file was restored to its original bytes by recoverPendingImport FROM THE JOURNAL. That test dies under my mutant and lives under the fix.

SHOULD-FIX: the legacy-JSON confirm path wraps confirm in try/catch{} — a JSON.parse or confirm-throw falls through and proceeds to importArchive UNCONFIRMED (fail-open), while the TAR path treats a confirm error as cancel (fail-closed). One rule, both paths.

VERDICT: FAIL — not cleared to land. The extraction shape (three phases, journal format matching recoverPendingImport's contract, alarm quiescence) is right; the three blockers are all fixable in one pass.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
webai-opus, INTERIM, 2026-09-28. This is NOT A VERDICT and nothing here has been PROBED. I was assigned the independent review of e630e2226 on 2026-09-26 and it stalled. I'm posting what my source read found so this candidate does not land on the author review alone. Every item is a hypothesis from reading the code, and each one needs a repro before it counts as a finding.

H1. Skipping an entry after a partial read over-drains. When onEntry returns false, the code does `body.cancel(); remaining = size;` and then drains `remaining` bytes. If the consumer already read k bytes, pull() had already taken them, so the drain eats k bytes of the NEXT header(s). A realistic path: pipeTo(staging) fails mid-entry, the dest error cancels the source and releases the lock, and the driver skips the file. The result is a desync, or, when the over-read lands in trailing zero padding, a "successful" decode that silently drops later entries. The only skip test covers skipping without reading.
H2. The "O(1) memory" claim is false. TarByteReader.readExact advances queueOffset but never clears or compacts the consumed queue[] slots, and pull() pushes forever. Every source chunk stays referenced until the decode ends, so the whole archive is retained. The 1 MiB test cannot show this.
M3. Decoded names (ustar name, PAX path, GNU 'L') are returned unvalidated. The encoder calls validateTarMemberName; the decoder does not, so "../x" and "/abs" reach the Stage-4 restore driver.
M4. The ustar prefix field (bytes 345..500) is ignored, so prefix-split long names decode silently truncated. That affects GNU --format=ustar, and bsdtar whenever the path fits in prefix+name. Neither case is tested.
M5. PAX 'x' and GNU 'L' payloads are read with an unbounded readExact(header.size).
M6. TarByteReader.pull() silently drops chunks that are not a Uint8Array, which shifts the stream. The encoder throws a TypeError for the same input.
M7. A body read after onEntry resolves gets a clean empty EOF, not an error.

Full notes, suggested fixes and the probe list are in ~/cap-evidence/opus-vv8c-review/NOTES.md on this machine. Recommendation: HOLD landing until at least H1 and H2 are probed. A verdict will follow the probes.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
REVIEW VERDICT — CHANGES REQUESTED (the hold was justified). Reviewer glm-5.3-flash; source hypotheses by webai-opus (NOTES.md), probes executed by me in ~/worktrees/cap-opus-vv8c-review @ e630e222. Probe script + full log: ~/cap-evidence/opus-vv8c-review/glm-probes.mjs / glm-probes.log.

BLOCKING M3 — PATH TRAVERSAL CONFIRMED, ALL FOUR VECTORS. The decoder validates nothing: names reach onEntry verbatim from the ustar name field, PAX 'path' records and GNU 'L' entries.
- ustar name "../evil.txt" → delivered verbatim, payload "pwned" intact.
- ustar name "/etc/evil.txt" → delivered verbatim (absolute path).
- PAX 'path' record "../../etc/shadow" → overlay delivered verbatim (crafted record "0027 path=../../etc/shadow\\n").
- GNU 'L' long name "../../evil/long" → delivered verbatim.
A Stage-4 restore driver consuming these names writes outside the restore root. Fix as opus proposed: validate the EFFECTIVE name after the overlay is applied (normalize "./" prefix and trailing "/"), fail closed with a named error. Confirmed by live probe, not just source read.

BLOCKING H1 — SKIP-AFTER-PARTIAL-READ OVER-DRAIN CONFIRMED. Entry of 200,000 bytes (larger than the 64 KiB pull granularity), consumer reads 131,072 bytes, releaseLock(), returns false: the decoder's `remaining = size` reset makes the drain consume 200,000 bytes from the stream — the next entry's header is consumed as payload and the decode THROWS "tar header checksum mismatch for 'AAAA…'" (stored 40,744,665). Desync confirmed; the archive is unrecoverable from that point. (The lock-held variant also confirmed: body.cancel() rejects with "Invalid state: ReadableStream is locked" and that error escapes the decode.) The existing skip test only covers skip-without-reading, which passes.

SHOULD-FIX M4 — USTAR PREFIX FIELD IGNORED, CONFIRMED. A real `tar --format=ustar` archive of a 154-char member name decodes to only the LAST name-field component ("eee…txt", 30 chars) while `tar -tf` lists the full path — silent name truncation that breaks the "GNU-tar interop both directions" claim for ustar-format archives.

NOT PROBED / UNPROVEN (stays as source-read hypotheses, no verdict from me): H2 (retained-chunks memory), M5 (unbounded PAX/L buffering — note readExact DOES fail closed with a named truncation error when the source ends, so the OOM case needs a source that actually has the bytes), M6-M13, L8-L13. opus's probes 1, 3, 7, 8 from NOTES.md remain outstanding for whoever continues.

GOOD (unchanged): round-trip matrix, real GNU archives decode, checksum/truncation mutants red — none of my probes contradicted the passing behavior.

VERDICT: changes requested — M3 + H1 block landing; M4 should ride along. Author (cap-glm-flash) has the probes to fix against. Routed to the webai merger with this comment.

PAUL'S DIRECTIVE (verbatim): "Harness: I need tools in the browser to be available to the harness (like claude) and then have it called and messaged back to Chrome over a protocol inside this app (not via MCP). One example: group my tabs - should be able to get the tabs from chrome an then move them into grouos... theis means we need to proxy the tool calls from harness to chrome client"

ARCHITECTURE (coord's brief): declare browser tools to the harness session (signatures in prompt/protocol); when the harness calls one it sends `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"…","method":"browser/call_tool","params":{"name":"…","args":{…}}}` over the EXISTING WebSocket/native connection; `extension/lib/acp-runner.js` receives it, dispatches to `browserToolset()` (list_tabs, group_tabs, …), and returns the JSON result on the same channel. **NO MCP**: no MCP SDK, no external HTTP server.

CANONICAL DRIVE: "group my tabs" — harness calls list_tabs, computes the grouping, calls group_tabs({tabIds, title, color}), Chrome executes chrome.tabs.group; verified in a browser.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests for the dispatch + an end-to-end drive that really groups tabs.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
chrome-agent-platform-2amt: the harness can call CAP's browser tools over the app's own protocol

PAUL'S DIRECTIVE: "I need tools in the browser to be available to the harness (like claude) and then
have it called and messaged back to Chrome over a protocol inside this app (not via MCP). One example:
group my tabs … this means we need to proxy the tool calls from harness to chrome client."

WHAT EXISTS NOW, and none of it is MCP (no MCP SDK, no HTTP endpoint, no mcpServers):
  * scripts/acp-bridge.ts declares the catalogue to the harness ONCE per session — prepended to the
    session's first prompt — with the exact envelope to emit:
      {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"…","method":"browser/call_tool","params":{"name":…,"args":{…}}}
    and the relay is unchanged: the bridge already forwards adapter lines to the browser socket
    verbatim, so an agent→client request arrives where it should with no new transport.
  * extension/lib/acp-client.js handles that method in _handleAgentRequest (where permission requests
    already land), reports it to the turn listener as a tool event, and answers on the SAME id.
  * extension/lib/browser-tools.js gains runBrowserToolCall(name, args): the catalogue, the zod
    validation and the tool bodies are the EXISTING browserToolset() — list_tabs, group_tabs,
    ungroup_tabs and the rest. The GRANTS STAY INSIDE THE TOOLS, so this adds reach, not authority: a
    harness call is refused exactly where a model call would be.
  * unknown tool / invalid arguments / a throwing tool come back as a JSON {error,…} a harness can
    correct rather than a protocol error or an unhandled throw.

THE ANTI-DRIFT GUARD: tests/browser-tool-proxy.test.ts compares BROWSER_TOOL_DECLARATIONS with
Object.keys(browserToolset()) in BOTH directions, so a tool cannot be declared without existing and
cannot exist without being declared — and asserts the declaration block introduces no mcpServers and
no http(s) URL, which is Paul's "not via MCP" as a test rather than a comment.

TESTS (6/6): the both-directions declaration guard; the once-per-session injection (second prompt
untouched, a different session decorated, non-prompt frames verbatim); the dispatcher's three error
paths; the GRANT property (an ungranted call is refused by the tool itself and no tab count leaks);
the happy path (list_tabs complete, chrome.tabs.group called once with the harness's tabIds); and the
ACP client turning a real browser/call_tool FRAME into a JSON-RPC result on the same id, with
unknown methods still -32601 so the client is not a black hole.

GATES: npm run test:changed GREEN; npm test GREEN — 4486 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (14 steps),
serial phase 17 files.

NOT DONE, AND NOT CLAIMED: the in-browser end-to-end drive has NOT been run, so by this repository's
standard the feature is UNVERIFIED. The blocker is diagnosed: extension/lib/browser-tools.js imports
bare specifiers ("ai", "zod") and the extension ships no import map, so the module is only reachable
through its BUNDLES — a harness-visible drive therefore needs either the full ACP path (a fake
harness script + acp-bridge + the extension's real acp-client: all real, only the harness stubbed) or
a bundle-exposed hook in the style of the existing randomized test hooks. The two facts the browser
drive must assert, once either route exists: chrome.tabs.group really ran, and chrome.tabGroups.query
shows a group with the title and colour the harness asked for.

title: The collapsed sidebar cuts its own chips off: the rail re-styles every row type except the harness rows (117px chips in a 40px rail, 90px cut)
description:
OWNER REPORT (Paul, 2026-09-23, verbatim): "icons are there however when that sidebar they are in is closed, they get cut off."

FILED AS ITS OWN BEAD, not on l3ts. l3ts was "the one-click agent buttons had no marks, a collapsed side panel squashed them" and it landed the MARKS (they are there — the owner says so) plus the side-panel geometry. This is a different defect in a different surface: the NTP's own collapsible task sidebar, whose rail re-styles every row type when it collapses EXCEPT the harness rows, so the chips stay full-width pills inside a 40px content box. l3ts is closed and its subject (marks exist) is satisfied; re-opening it for a rule that was never written would blur what it fixed. discovered-from l3ts; same family as qzae (a collapsed-panel rule that was pinned but never fired).

MEASURED IN THE BUILT EXTENSION (real browser, CDP, geometry not appearance) — collapsed rail = 60px, content 40px:
- BEFORE: each harness chip 117x29, visible 27x29, ratio 0.231, cutRight 90px, outside the rail by 89px. Clippers: div#side-harness (overflow hidden auto, 10..49) <- section.side-section.side-harness (overflow clip, 10..49) <- aside#side.side.collapsed (overflow clip, 0..60).
- WHAT IS CUT: the CHIP (mark + label pill), truncated mid-pill; the mark itself was intact at ratio 1.0 (16x16 fully visible). So the owner's "icons cut off" is the chip being chopped right after its icon — the identity survived only by luck of the 8px padding.
- AFTER: chip 34x34, ratio 1.0, cutRight 0, outsideRailBy 0, mark 16x16 ratio 1.0, label display:none (hidden by rule, not clipped), title + aria-label carry the full name, glyphs still distinct (pi / C / X).

CAUSE: `.side.collapsed` re-styles .thread-item, .agent-item, .foot-btn, .new-task, .side-label-row — and had no rule for the harness rows at all, leaving `.harness-list`'s 12px inline padding and the chips' full-width mark+label layout inside the 40px rail.

FIX (branch fix/panel-collapse-clipped-mark @ 1f64a7b3, version bump c0b8a92e = 0.3.475): collapsed harness rows become icon-only like the rest of the rail — `.side.collapsed .harness-list { flex-direction: column; flex-wrap: nowrap; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 0 8px; }`, `.side.collapsed .harness-list button { inline-size: 34px; block-size: 34px; padding: 0; justify-content: center; gap: 0; }`, `.side.collapsed .harness-list .hq-label { display: none; }`, plus `btn.title = name` so the full name stays reachable on hover once the label is hidden (the convention the rail's task rows already use).

WHY THE WIDTH HARNESS DID NOT CATCH IT, which is the instrument part of this bead: a clipped element still has a bounding box, so the existing checks ("every harness button carries a mark", markW >= 12) pass on a chip that is 90px cut off. scripts/constrained-width-layout.ts now measures the missing observable — every icon's box intersected with ALL its clipping ancestors (visible ratio, side cut) — for the collapsed rail at 1400px and 900px, plus an identity check (the marks must not collapse to one repeated glyph) and a per-width non-vacuity guard. 16 new checks: 49 -> 65.

MUTANTS (all run; the two surprises are statements about the checks and are recorded, not hidden):
1. collapsed rules removed -> RED: 117x29 / ratio 0.231 / cutRight 90 / outsideRailBy 89. The reported defect is caught.
2. label hidden but the 34x34 chip rule removed -> GREEN. Hiding the label is what ends the cut (the chip then sizes to the mark); the 34x34 rule is uniformity with the rail's other icon rows, NOT the load-bearing part. Stated plainly rather than claimed as necessary.
3. harness section hidden when collapsed -> RED at the non-vacuity guard (chips 0x0), so an absent rail cannot pass.
4. the three named marks given one glyph -> RED at "the marks distinguish the harnesses" ({"glyphs":["Z","Z","Z"]}). Two earlier attempts at this mutant were wrong and are recorded: mutating the fallback glyph changed nothing (pi/claude-code/codex are in the named map), and one mutant produced invalid code — a broken mutant proves nothing.

GATES: npm run test:width 65 passed / 0 failed; npm run test:changed 5 passed / 0 failed; npm test GREEN (serial phase 17 files, parallel phase 478 files in 50s). Heavy-gate slot taken for every browser run (the probe announced its holder; test:width is registry class "named", so it does not take the turn itself). No --no-verify.

EVIDENCE: the harness's own geometry.json (rail section) per run, /tmp/pc-*.log for the matrix, and the before/after tables in this comment.

title: MAIN IS RED at cc2711fa: muc's components.js refactor regressed diay's segmented-control scroll-into-view (scrollIntoView called 0 times, test expects exactly once) — npm test exits 1 for every lane
description:
FOUND while gating an unrelated change (chrome-agent-platform-qdjn). npm test exits 1 on unmodified origin/main @ cc2711fa with three failures, none of them in the gating lane's files. This bead is the one with a decisive attribution; the other two failures are listed at the end.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A LANE PROBLEM: npm test is the pre-push gate for every lane. Right now every lane that runs it gets these three reds and has to decide whether they caused them. I nearly had to; I verified at a pristine checkout instead. A red main makes every lane's gate verdict ambiguous, which is how a real regression gets waved through as "someone else's".

THE REGRESSION, MEASURED.
  At cc2711fa (muc, current main tip):
    npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts
    segmented-control scrolls the activated tab into view (chrome-agent-platform-diay) ... FAILED (1ms)
    segmented-control scrolls the attribute-selected tab into view on render (chrome-agent-platform-diay) ... FAILED (934µs)
    FAILED | 54 passed | 2 failed (2s)
    Assertion, verbatim from tests/components.test.ts:1147:
      error: Error: click: the activated tab must be scrolled into view exactly once, got 0

  At 61e4fdab (the commit immediately before muc), same worktree, only extension/shared/components.js + docs/components.js + tests/components.test.ts checked out at that revision:
    npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts -> exit 0, GREEN.

So the break is localized to muc's edit of those files, and muc did NOT touch tests/components.test.ts. Its changed-file list is docs/components.html (+9), docs/components.js (+130), extension/ntp/ntp.js (+175), extension/shared/components.js (+130), plus release/tracker bookkeeping. The test asserts on components.js, which muc refactored for the agent-picker row unification.

WHAT REGRESSED, IN PRODUCT TERMS: bead chrome-agent-platform-diay was "Providers tabs at 360px: active tab can scroll out of view", and it landed at c80b8abc — TWO COMMITS BEFORE muc. Its fix made the segmented control scroll the activated tab into view. That behavior is now gone: scrollIntoView is called zero times where the fix required exactly once. So this is not a stale test asserting an old shape; it is a shipped accessibility/usability fix at a narrow width being silently undone by an unrelated component refactor. The test is correctly red and the product is wrong.

THIS IS THE COUPLING RULE, TEXTBOOK: AGENTS.md — "File-disjointness is not suite-greenness. Two lanes whose diffs touch disjoint files can still break each other through a watcher... Neither lane alone can see the break; only the union gated together can." muc and diay share no file. muc changed a component; diay's test watches that component. Only a full-suite run at the union sees it.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts green at the tip, with both diay checks passing because the behavior is restored — NOT by editing or deleting the assertions. The test is right; weakening it would re-break the owner-visible fix at narrow widths.
2. The restored behavior driven in a real browser at the narrow width diay cared about (360px / the segmented control's container), not only in the unit test, since the unit test observes a scrollIntoView call count rather than the rendered result.
3. Determine whether the agent-picker row unification and the segmented-control scroll behavior can both hold, or whether muc's refactor needs to carry diay's scroll wiring forward. The likely shape: the refactor replaced or re-parented the element that owned the scroll-into-view call.

comments.text:
SUPPLEMENT to my classification, after two corrections from cap-astra. Artifact: ~/cap-evidence/mo2f-astra-20260923/acp-classification-supplement.json. Same read-only contract: no edits, no build, no gate, no merge, no push. Snapshot still 9811e07c, still verified equal to the live origin/main tip.

TWO CLAIMS IN MY PRIMARY ARTIFACT ARE SUPERSEDED, and both corrections were cap-astra's, not mine.

1. I bound cap/mcp-harness-tools' intended_delta to SIX COMMIT SUBJECTS. Subjects are history; the net diff is content. Two of those subjects describe work the branch later removed, so my delta read as if a client-hosted MCP server and a gated provider still ship. They do not — they were added by 44cb7f2d and dropped by 441f900c, and they do not appear in the net diff at all, because added-then-removed inside a branch nets to zero. Verified independently rather than accepted: git diff --stat d0f01545..9d40cfec is 9 files, 241 insertions, 16 deletions, of which the functional content is scripts/acp-bridge.ts +40 (PI_MCP_CONFIG_MODE=exclusive and the spawn env carrying it), tests/acp-bridge-mcp-isolation.test.ts +96 (rule and wiring pinned as two separate layers), docs/MCP-SUPPORT-DESIGN.md +83 (what was measured as NOT built). The rest is release/tracker bookkeeping. Corrected content verdict: the net new symbols are harnessMcpIsolationEnv and PI_MCP_EXCLUSIVE_ENV, both ABSENT from main; createAcpServer is already on main (2 occurrences in scripts/acp-bridge.ts), so the test imports a pre-existing export and the branch extends an existing seam rather than introducing a server. This is the same error class as trusting a test's NAME for its coverage — item 1 in this repo's own test-honesty canon.

2. I overstated the shim hazard. I wrote that a naive merge "could re-introduce files main removed". For an ordinary three-way merge that is WRONG: base has the file, main deletes it, the branch does not modify it, so the merge preserves the deletion — no conflict, no resurrection. MEASURED: git diff --name-status 38e3418d <tip> -- browser-shim-node.js browser-shim-process.js returns EMPTY for all three branches; zero shim files modified anywhere.

The residual hazard is real but narrower, differently shaped, and only on two of the four branches: a MODIFY/MODIFY CONFLICT ON build.mjs. Base 38e3418d's build.mjs has 3 shim references; main's has 0, because e3c55a25 (azlc) deleted both files AND their wiring in one commit (-66, -22, and build.mjs -23/+5). feat/harness-tools and feat/wp7y-picker-on-430b76fa each still carry all 3 references — build.mjs:459 (shimNode), :468 (swInject) and :518 (inject) — and BOTH modified build.mjs for an unrelated reason (bundle-budget enforcement: assertBundleBudget gained an enforce flag). So build.mjs conflicts, the branch side points at three files that no longer exist, and resolving it by taking the branch side or union-restoring yields a build that imports missing modules. That is a LOUD build failure, not a silent resurrection — materially smaller than what I first wrote. Desk action: take main's side for the shim wiring and the branch's side for the bundle-budget change; they are in different regions, so it is a line-level resolution, not a choice between versions. feat/harness-ui is EXEMPT: 10 files changed, no build consumer among them, so it carries the inert shim files and nothing that references them. cap/mcp-harness-tools is exempt by base.

PROVENANCE FOR 9d40cfec — the search is now exhausted rather than merely not-done, which is a stronger negative than my primary artifact gave. cap-astra is right that a missing DB row is not proof no review occurred, so I looked everywhere a review could be: bd show mcp1 (no issue); bd list across every status for mcp1 / "MCP server FOR a harness" / "mcp harness" (no match); bd list --desc-contains CAP-FB-20260912-ACP-INTEGRATION-01 across every status (No issues found — so the external id the test header cites has no bead row either); bd show qlho (CLOSED epic, 5/5 children, and its four independent ACP audit rounds vp3r/vn6b/3iyj/iadt are all CLOSED and all predate this work — qlho last updated 2026-09-12, the branch is 2026-09-22); qlho's comments grepped for isolation / MCP config / inherit / review / verdict / 9d40cfec (nothing); grep -rlI across ~/cap-evidence for the exact tip sha and its full form (only my own artifact, worktree-audit logs that enumerate every remote head, and one cdp manifest — no review artifact); grep -rlI for harnessMcpIsolationEnv / PI_MCP_CONFIG_MODE / mcp-isolation / MCP-SUPPORT-DESIGN (only built-extension snapshots under scratch/cap-emscripten-loaded-ext-*/ from unrelated emscripten work); and all six commit bodies (author self-report throughout — the tip is titled "review fixes" but names no reviewer and no reviewed sha).

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: requirement provenance is the OWNER and it is dated — the test header states the rejected behaviour is "owner-reported 2026-09-22" and quotes the owner's architecture (tools live in the client, the harness asks, the request routes back to the client, which acts on the tab the owner is looking at; "a local process asking to run Google Chrome" is the rejected behaviour). Author fixture evidence exists at ~/cap-evidence/acp-mcp-isolation-fixture/ (mock-adapter.mjs, env-pi.json {"harness":"pi","isolation":"exclusive"}, env-claude-code.json {"harness":"claude-code","isolation":null}, dated 2026-09-22 21:53/22:21), corroborating the test's two claims — but author-produced, not review-produced. WHICH LANE AUTHORED IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: all six commits are under the repo's shared identity (Paul Kinlan <paul.kinlan@gmail.com>), which every lane commits under, so git author identifies nothing here.

WHAT REMAINS UNESTABLISHED: reviewer lane, reviewer model, reviewed SHA, review verdict. The word "review" in the tip's subject is the only trace, and a subject line is not provenance. What would settle it is outside read-only reach from here: ask the authoring lane, or check the fleet board / intercom logs for 2026-09-22 around the mcp1 commits.

For orphan recovery, the tracker gap is now precisely two ids that resolve to nothing — bead mcp1 and CAP-FB-20260912-ACP-INTEGRATION-01 — under a closed epic whose audit rounds predate the work by ten days. Filing the orphan should carry the owner-reported requirement and the fixture evidence above, so the new bead is not thinner than what the test header already knows.

FINAL BOUNDED PROVENANCE CHECK, and it CORRECTS MY OWN PRIMARY ARTIFACT. Addendum: ~/cap-evidence/mo2f-astra-20260923/provenance-addendum.json. Read-only, bounded to vl6c's comment thread, the two evidence files the author cites, and one targeted cap-evidence grep — no broad search, no gates.

QUESTION (cap-astra): does the vl6c review actually BIND its verdict to 430b76fa, or is that SHA merely the baseline used to reproduce four inherited failures?

ANSWER: IT DOES NOT BIND. THE EXACT REVIEWED SHA IS UNKNOWN — the verdict cites no SHA at all.

My primary artifact recorded reviewed_sha = 430b76fa and justified it by quoting the FULL-SUITE CONFIRMATION comment. That conflates two things, and cap-astra named the conflation exactly: that citation proves which tree the reviewer's REPRODUCTION RUN used, not which tree the REVIEW VERDICT judged. I reported a reproduction baseline as a reviewed SHA.

WHAT THE RECORD ACTUALLY SAYS, in order:
- 20:13 AUTHOR: "Published incomplete candidate origin/feat/harness-tools @ 3cf1d93d579f710f2ba14af5f1112f6e40300229, backend commit be1d7a68; exact commit focused tests 46 passed/0 failed, production build EXIT 1: SW 3,003,397 > unchanged 3,000,000... Full suite, real existing tool call, native denial UI, supersession browser drive remain unverified; branch is NOT mergeable." Cites cap-evidence/cap-harness-build-3cf1d93d.log and cap-harness-tests-3cf1d93d.log — BOTH VERIFIED PRESENT ON DISK.
- 21:57 REVIEWER (vb-extensions): the INDEPENDENT REVIEW verdict — mechanism REAL and driven, codex roundtrip re-established, deny path driven, one gate finding. It says "Focused suites 55 green on the exact commit after building the fresh worktree dist". "THE EXACT COMMIT" IS NEVER NAMED.
- 21:57 REVIEWER: "independent review complete, one gate finding (changelog language) owed by the author; landing blocked on that rewrite + the findings 1-6 custody fixes already reviewed on the custody side."
- 22:00 REVIEWER: "FULL-SUITE CONFIRMATION... all four inherited failures REPRODUCE on 430b76fa in my own full-suite run (exit 1)". A REPRODUCTION BASELINE, three minutes after the verdict.

SO: the only SHA bound to a reviewer run is 430b76fa and the binding is to a reproduction, not a verdict. The only SHA bound to evidence ARTIFACTS is 3cf1d93d. No receipt, log or artifact bound to a review of 430b76fa exists — one targeted grep for vl6c|430b76fa across cap-evidence returned only unrelated hits (a j95l-recovery frames file, harness-finish CHANGELOG copies, cap-harness-finish-dev.log).

WHY 430b76fa IS PLAUSIBLE WITHOUT BEING ESTABLISHED: 3cf1d93d's build FAILED the SW budget at 20:13 (3,003,397 > 3,000,000), and 430b76fa's own subject is "scope the store budget, persist harness selection, drive the permission" — so 430b76fa is the commit that fixed that overrun and was the tip by 21:57. Plausible by adjacency and by content. NOT CITED, and inferring a reviewed SHA from a three-minute adjacency between two comments by the same lane is the same move the task forbids when it forbids inferring readiness from ancestry. Adjacency is not a citation. Recorded as UNKNOWN.

FINDINGS 1-6 CUSTODY — the distinction cap-astra asked for:
- WHAT IT IS: a blocker ASSERTED BY THE REVIEWER AT 21:57 ON 2026-09-21. A statement about that moment inside a comment, not a tracked dependency: no bead id, no link, no artifact, no SHA attached to "findings 1-6".
- WHAT IT IS NOT: an established CURRENT blocker. Establishing that needs to know whether those custody fixes have since landed, and nothing in vl6c's record says. Within the bounded search I could not locate the custody review the phrase refers to at all.
- THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME SENTENCE IS DISCHARGED ON THE EVIDENCE: the changelog rewrite the reviewer owed the author demonstrably happened (x1zq's f396f880 then ab1f111b), and I verified by diffing ab1f111b's CHANGELOG hunk that the named jargon is gone. So one of the two named blockers is discharged and the other is unlocatable.
- NOTE ON THE WORDING: "already reviewed on the custody side" says the REVIEW of those fixes happened elsewhere; it does not say they were applied or landed.

UNCHANGED BY THIS CHECK: reviewer LANE is vb-extensions (named in the verdict comment itself); reviewer MODEL is still not stated in the record; and the tip ab1f111b is two commits after 430b76fa, so WHICHEVER sha was reviewed the tip is not it — that gap stands however the reviewed-SHA question resolves. All three other branches' findings and both corrections in the supplement are unaffected.

NET FOR THE DESK: feat/harness-tools has a recorded independent review by a named lane with a named verdict and a named finding that was subsequently discharged — but the verdict is NOT bound to any SHA, and the branch tip is two commits past the only SHA a reviewer is recorded as having run anything on. If the desk needs review coverage of the tip, that is a re-review of f396f880 + ab1f111b, not a lookup.

title: The post-commit hook carried a second copy of the changelog filter that did not know the internal: marker, so it published three internal notes as release entries and burned a version on one
description:
FILED AFTER THE FIX because no bead existed for it: the branch cap/whatsnew-449 and its review findings were tracked only in a branch name and an intercom thread. The fix is on cap/whatsnew-hook-sync @ e247cf3832d9b94aa0e6aa2801bd292fc2f5d6ae, branched off a1365f60.

DEFECT. scripts/bump-version.mjs carried its own copy of the six filter regexes plus isUserFacingEntry, justified in a comment as "so the standalone script functions in scratch temporary test mirrors without relying on outside module resolution". The two copies agreed until extension/options/changelog-filter.js gained the `internal:` marker (INTERNAL_MARKER_RE :33, isInternalEntry :42, returning false at :48). The duplicate had no isInternalEntry, so it scored a marked note USER-FACING. scripts/git-hooks/post-commit:19 calls `node scripts/bump-version.mjs patch --skip-if-no-note --message "$MSG"` on EVERY commit, and :111's bail is `if (cleanNote && !isUserFacingEntry(cleanNote))` — so for a marked note the bail did not fire and the hook took the PUBLISH path.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, not a drift table. On that branch, CHANGELOG.md line 4 read:
    ## [0.3.452] — 2026-09-22
    - internal: the changelog gate now allows a stated-internal note instead of forcing a user-facing sentence
The hook published the marker's OWN commit as a release entry and consumed 0.3.452 for it — six version strings across package.json, package-lock.json, extension/manifest.json and extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js moved 0.3.451 -> 0.3.452 for a note the marker exists to suppress. A second and third `internal:` line sat at 0.3.448 and 0.3.446, but those are NOT this defect — see the distinction below, which is the part a reviewer or a future lane is most likely to get wrong.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS. Only 0.3.452 was hook output. A post-commit hook can only PREPEND an entry for the commit it runs on; it cannot rewrite entries four versions back. The `internal:` markers on 0.3.448 and 0.3.446 were hand-applied by the copy-rewrite commits 2b321a77 and 51346e12 and are THE FEATURE WORKING: they hide a rationale correction and a measurements commit from the readable five while keeping them under Show all, and changelog-filter.js names both as its motivating cases. Deleting them would re-expose "correct the F1 rationale to what was actually measured" and "the measurements behind the constrained-width fix" to readers. I was instructed to remove all three, checked the diff first, and removed one.

FIX. bump-version.mjs imports isUserFacingEntry from extension/options/changelog-filter.js, exactly as scripts/check-changelog.mjs:9 already did; the duplicate and its six regexes are deleted. A second copy of a rule is how two gates drift apart.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT HAD TO BE PRESERVED. The standalone rationale was real: FOUR scratch mirrors spawn this script from a temp dir (tests/bump-version-sanitize.test.ts 1, tests/named-agents-provider.test.ts 3) and none copied the filter, so a bare import would have made the script die on module resolution in all four and read as a bump failure. All four mirrors now carry extension/options/changelog-filter.js. Verified only two copies of the filter existed repo-wide (grep for the regex names across scripts/, extension/, tests/), so the sync is complete.

UNDO. Six version strings reverted 0.3.452 -> 0.3.451 (the faithful undo — the bump should never have happened) and the 0.3.452 block removed from CHANGELOG.md; extension/CHANGELOG.md is gitignored and regenerates. check:changelog-order reports 871 entries, unique + descending, latest 0.3.451 — exactly one fewer than the 872 measured before the fix. LANDING NOTE: this branch's commits consumed 0.3.449-0.3.452 while main independently consumed through 0.3.456, so landing must take main's side on the version surfaces and let the hook assign the next free number. Do not renumber by hand; the hook owns version assignment.

FALSIFICATION, three ways.
1. THROUGH THE REAL HOOK ON A REAL COMMIT: the fix commit's own subject starts with `internal:`, and the hook printed "[bump-version] commit note ... does not pass user-facing filter — NOT bumping version", consuming nothing. Version stayed 0.3.451, no entry written.
2. UNIT, BOTH HALVES: an `internal:` note with --skip-if-no-note must exit 0, consume no version (stays 1.2.3), write no entry, and print the same loud notice bookkeeping gets; a user-facing note must still bump to 1.2.4 and still publish, so syncing the filter is not the same as disabling the hook. 6 passed / 0 failed.

And the marker's comment said "deliberate and explicit, never inferred" without naming the cost, so both residual risks are now in the code: a bullet that should be marked and is not still passes if it reads as user-facing (the marker suppresses, its absence never accuses), and the marker can hide real user-facing copy with nothing objecting (silent by construction, since the point of the marker is that nobody has to justify it).

title: journey abort at 132/370 is an unanswered service-worker round trip reported as fleet load — assert the probe's expectations and measure the box on an evaluate timeout
description:
Found measuring chrome-agent-platform-muc on the union tree (muc + dnop + 0lj3). Full evidence in the chrome-agent-platform-qk7p comment of 2026-09-23; this bead is the fix.

WHAT IS BROKEN (precise, source-referenced):
1. scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:512-530, runScriptedToolProbe: the wait loop 'while (provider.requests.length < expectRequests && Date.now() - t0 < 120000)' exits SILENTLY on timeout — it never asserts that the provider received the requests it expected. The probe then returns a partial result, the caller's check fails on a confusing payload, and the failure surfaces one step later as a timeout about something else. (Same class as the seed-nothing fixtures: a probe that found nothing, letting the failure land elsewhere.)
2. scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:334-345, evalIn: 'Runtime.evaluate' with awaitPromise: true. When the awaited page promise is an in-page chrome.runtime.sendMessage round trip (msgValue, line 1345) and the SERVICE WORKER never answers — queued behind a run that never settled — the promise never settles and Cdp.send's 15 s timer rejects with the generic 'cdp timeout: Runtime.evaluate (requestId=…, targetId=unavailable, sessionId=…)'.
3. The timeout is then classified environmental WITHOUT any measurement of the machine at that moment, so the verdict reads 'under fleet load' on an idle box. On the measured run: load/core 0.11, three parked (idle) esbuild daemons, zero active compilers, the fleet-wide gate slot held. The classification rule is right; applying it with no reading is what made it wrong as a conclusion, and it has been masking this defect from every lane.

ACCEPTANCE:
- the probe asserts its own expectation (fail with 'the scripted provider received N of M requests and the run reached phase X' rather than silently proceeding), so a never-settling run is named where it happens;
- an evaluate timeout carries a MACHINE READING at the moment of the timeout (the quiet-window sampler already exists: readLoadSample/environmentLine), and the environmental verdict says which of 'the box was loaded' or 'the box was idle and something never settled' it is — an idle box must NOT be reported as fleet load;
- a canary/assertion for the keyless + cookie-probe block that fails with the real reason (SW unanswered / run not terminal) instead of a CDP timeout.
REPRO (no full 370 needed): run the keyless/cookie-probe section (or the suite until it reaches it) and observe, in order: the 120 s silent loop, the 'Cookies: …' assertion failing, then 'journey failure: cdp timeout: Runtime.evaluate (… targetId=unavailable …)' — the last of which is a rendering artefact, not a dead target. Evidence log: /tmp/union-journeys.log (lane copy), retained line numbers above.
NOT OWNED BY THE MEASURING LANE: the fix belongs with whoever owns the keyless/cookie-tools block; handed over with this repro rather than patched from the outside.

title: Serialise load-sensitive gates through one declared fleet-wide slot, announced, and report INCONCLUSIVE naming the holder
description:
Coord 2026-09-22, option (a). The measurement that made this a design question: with chrome-agent-platform-dnop fixed, chrome-journeys STARTED and reached 132/370 before aborting on 'cdp evaluate exceeded the budget under fleet load' at load/core 0.13 — a box quiet by every measure the quiet-window gate has could not complete 370 round-trips. More threshold tuning cannot fix that; there is no threshold left to loosen.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES (source, verified):
- chrome-slots.ts is a bounded SEMAPHORE (CAP_CHROME_MAX_CONCURRENT, default 4) and it is a MEMORY bound, not a correctness one.
- launchChrome's acquireLaunchScope treats the two scopes as mutually exclusive: with canonicalLock (or lockPath) it acquires the flock and takes NO slot (slot: -1); otherwise it takes one of 4 slots and NO flock.
- So a journey holding the canonical lock does NOT exclude a KAT batch's up-to-4 browsers: journeys and KATs can run concurrently by construction. The canonical lock only excludes other canonical-lock users (journeys, the security custody supervisor).
- The KAT runner is serial WITHIN a run, but several lanes each run their own KAT batch, and each KAT browser takes a slot.

DESIGN OF RECORD (the shape coord asked for):
1. ONE declared fleet-wide slot for load-sensitive gates: a flock on /tmp/cap-heavy-gate.lock, held for the gate's lifetime, release = close the holder's stdin (the crash-safe pattern the canonical lock already uses, so a killed lane leaves no held slot — the kernel drops it).
2. ANNOUNCED: the holder writes an atomic sidecar (/tmp/cap-heavy-gate.holder.json) with gate name, harness/npm script, pid, started-at, cwd. A refusing lane reads it and NAMES the holder, so 'who has the machine' is answerable without asking a human.
3. BOUNDED + INCONCLUSIVE: the wait is bounded (CAP_HEAVY_GATE_BOUND_MS, default 20 min, the canonical lock's contract). A lane that cannot get the slot reports the ENVIRONMENTAL verdict — exit 75 with the existing CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL marker carrying {"reason":"heavy-gate-slot-busy","holder":{...}} — never a product red, never a silent skip, never a green.
4. NO INTERFERENCE: measure and wait, or refuse. The module never kills, renames, re nices or otherwise touches another lane's processes (the same DO-NOT as quiet-window.ts, with the same source-scan guard).
5. ORDERING: acquire the slot FIRST, then wait for the quiet window. Holding the slot means no other heavy gate can start while we measure, so the quiet predicate then measures only non-gate load.
6. WIRED (this change): chrome-journeys.ts (the 370-check gate) and scripts/kat-runner.ts (one slot for the whole serial batch). FOLLOW-UP, listed not hidden: the other gate-class entries in scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts (a11y, components, width, security injection, the security custody supervisor's own lock on fd 9) — the custody chain's exclusivity already exists and must not be double-locked without reading its protocol.

ACCEPTANCE / MUTANTS:
- two concurrent heavy gates: exactly ONE holds; the other's bounded wait expires and its refusal NAMES the first (gate + pid from the sidecar). Falsification, mandatory: with the slot disabled/pointed at a private path, BOTH hold — the test must be able to fail, otherwise it pins nothing.
- crash safety: a holder SIGKILLed mid-hold leaves no held slot; the next acquirer gets it within the bound.
- announcement: the sidecar is written only by the holder and is removed/refreshed on release; a refusal never invents a holder.
- the DO-NOT source scan passes over the new module.
- end to end: with the slot held by another process, chrome-journeys exits 75 with the holder named and does NOT start a browser.

HONEST LIMITS, stated: the slot serialises GATES against each other. It does not stop another lane's compiler from spiking mid-run — that remains the quiet-window predicate's job (and the qk7p classification's), and a transient spike can still kill a journey mid-run. This closes gate-vs-gate competition, which is the part that is ours to fix.

Evidence: /tmp/muc-journeys3.log (the 132/370 abort at load/core 0.13, with the gate's own 'box quiet after 10068 ms' line above it).

CANDIDATE PUSHED — branch cap/nweh-cookie-redaction @ 6525c3ce, STACKED on 835bff08 (the selector repair, bead im52). Ordering is NOT symmetric: this fix is only measurable on top of that one, because without the selector repair the suite times out before reaching the cookie section. 835bff08 can land alone; this cannot land first. Worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-security-suite, 1 file changed (scripts/security-suite.ts), no product code.

I built on the reviewer's reproduction rather than re-deriving it, and both halves are confirmed by reading the code. They are worse together than separately: the fixture returned zero rows on a fresh profile and Array.isArray([]) is true, so the check passed with nothing to redact; and cookieModelContent was JSON.stringify of already-serialized content strings, so every inner quote came back escaped and /"value"/ could never match the text it inspected. Either alone weakens the check; together they made it structurally incapable of failing. The production mapper is correct — metadata only — so this was purely an instrument that could not see a leak.

FIX, following this bead's acceptance item by item:
- seed and assert a NONEMPTY matching synthetic-cookie metadata row: chrome.cookies.set (the same API the tool reads) for a non-httpOnly nweh_probe cookie on 127.0.0.1 with a per-run sentinel, seeded before the run; new check (a) asserts the seeded row reached list_cookies as metadata.
- inspect the DECODED executeEnvelope result for own value keys: a bounded recursive walk (ownKeyPaths) over cookiesEnv.result, not a grep over a stringified blob, plus both spellings (bare and escaped) in the raw model text as a backstop.
- assert the synthetic value is absent from the model transcript: check (c) scans EVERY message of EVERY provider request in the probe run, not just the last tool message — a leak in message four of nine would have passed the narrower version.
- pristine passes and the real browser-tools value:c.value mutation fails SPECIFICALLY on redaction: measured, below.
- the provider capability / terminal-run check is kept unchanged.
- the sentinel never enters evidence: if (c) fires the detail carries an occurrence count, not the transcript. A redaction check that prints the value it was watching for has moved the leak rather than closed it.
No real user secret was used at any point; the value is a per-run synthetic sentinel.

  MUTANT — extension/lib/browser-tools.js mapper returns value: c.value, rebuilt:
    RESULT: 19 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are exactly the redaction checks:
      FAIL: cookies: list_cookies returns no value field (metadata only) — in the model's own context — {"decodedValueKeys":...}
      FAIL: cookies: the seeded synthetic value reaches NO message the provider received — {"sentinel":"nweh_synthetic_..."}
    The two that stayed GREEN: "the redaction probe run executed list_cookies for real (capability granted, envelope settled, run terminal)" and "the probe fixture was NON-EMPTY". So the redaction assertions are the ones doing the work; the plumbing is not what reddened. That is the differential this bead's acceptance asked for.

title: The security gate reported a section it never ran: providerRequests [] and both cookie-redaction checks absent from the transcript, on a gate whose subject is credential leakage — masked by an exit-124 timeout
description:
Distinct from the selector migration (chrome-agent-platform-4vfj), which is the CAUSE. This bead is the DEFECT CLASS and the classification rule that let it hide, and it is filed separately because the sentence that matters is not about selectors.

THE SENTENCE: a gate inside test:all reported a section it never ran. providerRequests:[] proves no model turn started, so this was not a check that ran and passed quietly — it was a check that did not exist. And the checks that did not exist were the COOKIE-REDACTION ones, on a gate whose whole subject is credential and cookie leakage. That is not a neutral gap.

MEASURED BEFORE, on unmodified origin/main @ c80b8abc (fresh detached worktree; npm ci + deno install + npm run build:production all rc=0; canonical lock verified free with flock -n before launch and released cleanly — receipt residue [], cleaned true, groupSurvived false, killSent false):

  npm run test:security
  CAP_SECURITY_RESULT {"result":"FAIL","scenario":"production","exit":124,"timedOut":true,"termSent":true,"killSent":false,"cleaned":true}
  wall 23:36:46 -> 23:38:46 BST = 120 s = PRODUCTION_TIMEOUT_MS (scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:31)
  runner.log: 16 PASS, then
  FAIL: script.run: a model-initiated run_script (real provider path) pauses on the approval card with the source shown and the script un-run
        — {"setProvider":"openai-compatible","composer":false,"card":null,"lastRunAt":null,"providerRequests":[],"overflow":0,"threadText":""}
  Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/.local/state/chrome-agent-platform/security-suite/ab2a08c3ee28a5c5/

The suite reached 17 of its 19 checks. The two it never reached:
  cookies: the redaction probe run executed list_cookies for real (capability granted, envelope settled, run terminal)
  cookies: list_cookies returns no value field (metadata only) — in the model's own context

WHY IT HID — THE CLASSIFICATION RULE THAT MASKED IT. The receipt's headline was exit 124 / timedOut:true. This repo's own canon (AGENTS.md, "Test honesty", observer rule 5) says a timeout is INCONCLUSIVE and an environmental verdict is never a product red. That rule is correct in general, and here it completed the masking: the FAIL was printed to runner.log roughly 100 seconds BEFORE the supervisor sent TERM, but anyone reading the receipt saw a timeout and moved on. One failure mode hiding another, with our own discipline doing the hiding.

THE RULE THIS BEAD ASKS THE PLAYBOOK TO ADOPT (coord's wording, confirmed by these timestamps rather than by argument): **a timeout is environmental only if nothing failed before it. A timeout that follows a failed assertion is a failure, and the assertion is what you report.** Operationally: on any receipt with timedOut:true, read runner.log for FAIL lines before classifying the run as environmental.

WHY IT ALSO HUNG (arithmetic, not a second defect). The suite spent its whole 120 s budget in polling loops waiting on a run that could never start: the 20-try composer loop at 250 ms, then the 60-try approval-card loop at 500 ms, then section 7's own waits. A hang that is retries multiplied by waits against a precondition that can never become true is worth recognising by shape — it is not a slow machine.

MEASURED AFTER the four-selector repair (chrome-agent-platform-4vfj, stacked candidate cap/4vfj-security-suite @ 835bff08):
  CAP_SECURITY_RESULT {"result":"PASS","exit":0,"timedOut":false,"termSent":false,"killSent":false,"residue":[],"cleaned":true}
  wall 23:48:19 -> 23:48:34 BST = 15 s (was 120 s + TERM)
  runner.log: RESULT: 19 passed, 0 failed — including the run_script approval-card check and BOTH cookie-redaction checks
  Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/.local/state/chrome-agent-platform/security-suite/490692ad190a9a68/
exit 0 was not accepted as proof on either side; both transcripts were read and the PASS/FAIL lines counted (17-of-19 before, 19-of-19 after).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. npm run test:security reaches all 19 checks and reports 19/0 with exit 0 and timedOut:false. DONE on the candidate, awaiting landing.
2. The classification rule above is written into the playbook / AGENTS.md observer rules, so the next exit-124 is read for a preceding FAIL before it is called environmental. NOT DONE — this is the durable half and it is the reason this bead exists separately from 4vfj.
3. A gate that cannot reach a section says so. The suite printed its FAIL and then hung; nothing in the receipt distinguished "ran 19, failed 1" from "ran 17, timed out". Consider carrying a reached/total count in CAP_SECURITY_RESULT so a truncated run is legible from the receipt alone. NOT DONE, and it is a judgement call for the owner — the cheapest version is a checkedCount/expectedCount pair in the result JSON.

RELATED: chrome-agent-platform-4vfj (the migration and its guard — the cause), chrome-agent-platform-cwy2 (the same class in sidebar-parity: a harness that ran zero of its checks while its registry row still asserted a verdict), chrome-agent-platform-nco2 (subset gates that cannot see cross-cutting guards).

CORRECTION TO MY FIRST REPORT, then the sweep and the fix shape (coord asked for both verbatim). I told coord three files. The real number on origin/main tip d0f01545 is 35 files, ~150 sites. I under-reported because I only listed what I had personally hit; the grep is below and is reproducible in one command.

THIS IS AN ANNOUNCED MIGRATION THAT WAS NEVER COMPLETED, not a set of independent stale selectors. Bead chrome-agent-platform-sndb deliberately removed the fixed ids and pinned the removal in tests/agent-composer-unique-ids.test.ts, which asserts (1) AgentComposer must NOT hardcode <textarea id="task-input"> or <button id="run-task">, (2) it MUST expose [data-composer-input] and [data-composer-send], (3) focusInput() resolves via [data-composer-input], (4) NTP and sidepanel declare distinct composer host ids. The reason was real: #composer and #thread-composer share one document, so getElementById('task-input') silently resolved to the hub composer while the user was in the thread view and input went to a hidden element. The product half landed and is unit-pinned. The harness half did not: only 9 files in the whole repo mention the stable hooks (git grep -ln 'data-composer-input|data-composer-send' -- scripts cap-evidence tests): chrome-journeys.ts, sidebar-parity.ts (as of cwy2), lib/harness-registry.ts, 4 cap-evidence one-offs, and 2 tests. b5q4 told the fleet to use the stable hooks on 2026-09-18 and named the drift; nothing swept.

REPRO: git grep -n 'task-input|run-task' -- scripts cap-evidence tests | grep -v data-composer

GATES INSIDE test:all (highest severity, in this order):
- scripts/a11y-audit.ts:399,406,442 — 'agent-composer textarea#task-input'. MEASURED RED TODAY: 4 combobox checks fail, exit 1 (/tmp/cap-a11y-baseline.log on unmodified a3e35928). Silent mechanism: :406 reads t?.getAttribute(...) so a null element yields null for role/haspopup/expanded/activedescendant and attrs comes back {} — the checks cannot pass, and the failure reads as a product ARIA defect. The guard that should name it, 'if (!t) throw new Error("no composer textarea")' at :399, never surfaces (the run continued to the checks), so cdp.evl is swallowing the page exception — that swallow is its own defect.
- scripts/security-suite.ts:339,347,417,426 — centerOf('#task-input') / '#run-task', and centerOf at :201 is a plain document.querySelector with NO fallback. STATIC FINDING, NOT RUN (running it takes the canonical Chrome lock and would queue every other lane's browser gate behind me, so I did not). Mechanism, each link verified by reading plus the live probe: #task-input is absent -> clickAt returns false -> the 20-try loop leaves composer=false -> the typing and Run click inside 'if (composer)' never happen -> the check at :361 'script.run: a model-initiated run_script pauses on the approval card' includes composer in its condition, so it FAILS LOUDLY. Worth saying twice: this one is loud because composer is in the assertion. That is the pattern the other 34 files should copy, and it is why I am not claiming a silent pass here.
- scripts/component-gallery-smoke.ts:200,216,217 — c.querySelector('#task-input'), and :217 also probes '#run-task, .run'. Not run; classify before fixing.
- scripts/chrome-journeys.ts — 38 sites, most routed through boxOf() at :367-380 which DOES carry the compat mapping (#task-input -> [data-composer-input], #run-task -> [data-composer-send]). Two read it directly with no fallback: :2688 comp?.querySelector('#task-input') and :2721 document.querySelector('agent-composer #task-input')?.value ?? ''. Both use ?. / ?? so they read null or empty string and the checks around them can pass on nothing. That is the silent shape inside the suite's strongest gate.

FIX SHAPE — the composer is addressed by a stable hook or it is not addressed at all:
1. ONE resolver, not 35 patches. scripts/lib/composer-target.ts exporting the scoped selectors and a helper that takes the composer HOST id (ntp.html has two: #composer and #thread-composer, so a bare document-wide [data-composer-input] is wrong for the same reason the fixed ids were). 2. A STATIC GUARD that pins the RULE, not today's instances: fail if 'task-input' or 'run-task' appears as a selector anywhere in scripts/, cap-evidence/ or tests/ outside the resolver and the sndb pin. Per this repo's own canon a rule-pin owes a second mutant that ADDS a fresh instance, so the guard is proven to cover the rule rather than the current 150 sites. Delete the ?. / ?? reads that turn a missing element into null, an empty string or {}: they are what made a11y-audit's red look like a product ARIA defect and what lets chrome-journeys:2688/2721 pass on nothing. Fix the cdp.evl swallow so a page-side throw surfaces. security-suite.ts:361 including composer in its assertion is the model.

title: Nothing runs cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts automatically: the repaired checks are a runbook, not a gate
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/l3ts-check-strength (ac0a62d4).

MEASURED - NOTHING RUNS THIS DRIVER AUTOMATICALLY.
  git grep -n "constrained-width-layout" -- tests/ scripts/ package.json
  -> NO MATCHES.
It is absent from scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts, and no test, script or npm
script refers to it. It runs when a human runs it, and at no other time.

WHY THIS IS THE FINDING WITH THE LONGEST TAIL: q264 and qzae were repaired IN THIS
FILE, on the strength of measurement, and landed. Because nothing runs it, the
checks repaired to catch a regression cannot catch one. The repair is a runbook,
not a gate. The next change to the grid track rule (minmax(0, 1fr)) or to the
@container rule in sidepanel.html can restore the exact defect and every automatic
gate stays green - which is the state that produced q264/qzae in the first place.

THE DRIVER IS GATE-READY, which is why this is cheap: it asserts on geometry
(never appearance), it launches Chrome through launchChrome() so it takes a
browser slot rather than a fixed port, and it already carries a clean exit-code
contract - `Deno.exit(fail ? 1 : 0)` on the last line.

PRECEDENT IN THIS REPO - 5 of the 17 cap-evidence drivers are referenced, this one
is not. The mechanism used by tests/tar-stream.test.ts:15-16 is a STATIC URL
reference, with the reason in a comment:
  // Static references so buildReverseGraph in scripts/select-tests.mjs links
  // evidence instruments to this test
  const _CHROME_ACCEPTANCE = new URL("../cap-evidence/11rm1-tar-stream-acceptance.ts", import.meta.url);
That reference is what makes scripts/select-tests.mjs' buildReverseGraph link the
instrument to the test, so a change to the instrument selects the test.

PROPOSAL - two levels, and they are not the same thing. Doing (1) alone is cheap
and closes the "a change nobody notices" half; (2) is what makes it a gate.
  (1) SELECTION LINKAGE (cheap, proven pattern, no new browser budget): add the
      static `new URL("../cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts",
      import.meta.url)` reference into a test that owns this surface, so a change
      to the driver selects that test under `npm run test:changed`.
  (2) EXECUTION AS A GATE (what the finding actually asks for): register the driver
      in scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts with its class and exit-code contract, so
      its assertions run without a human. Cost: one headless Chrome launch taking a
      browser slot via launchChrome(); tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts and
      the journey harness already do this, so the budget exists.
  (3) OR the two load-bearing assertions - deep min-content containment, and the
      collapsed rule firing in BOTH directions - folded into an existing registered
      harness that already drives the built extension, spending no new browser.

WHAT MAKES IT UNSAFE TO WIRE IN AS-IS, and must be decided rather than ignored:
  - the driver READS A BASE BUILD via CAP_ACCEPTANCE_EXT. A gate must run it
    against the tree under test, not a base build, or it asserts on the wrong tree.
  - it MUTATES the loaded page (renames elements, forces widths, rewrites label
    text). That must be inside the harness's own browser instance, never against
    anything another process measures.
  - it must not depend on ambient state it does not create (fleet convention,
    chrome-agent-platform-p15i): the base build it reads is a path a human supplies.
  - it writes evidence to cap-evidence/l3ts-constrained-width/. Confirm that path
    is not inside the tracked tree at gate time (a gate that dirties the tree it
    is testing fails the next run - the same shape as p15i).

ACCEPTANCE: the driver either runs in an automatic gate with a recorded red/green
run at HEAD, or this bead is closed with the stated reason it cannot be and a
pointer to where its two load-bearing assertions ARE enforced automatically.

title: A layout check that cannot fail: the padding check compares 0 to 0 when both elements are absent (third instance of the class)
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/l3ts-check-strength (ac0a62d4), in cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts:283. NOT fixed by that branch.

OBSERVED (DRIVEN, not read): the check
  check("hub: the Jobs board's content is inset like its own panel header",
        Math.abs(bodyLeft - headLeft) <= 1, ...)
PASSES when BOTH elements it reads are absent.

MECHANISM: lines 281-282 compute each side with a default:
  const bodyLeft = parseFloat(String(pad1440.panelBodyPadding || "0").split(" ")[1] ?? "0");
  const headLeft = parseFloat(String(pad1440.panelHeadPadding || "0").split(" ")[1] ?? "0");
Absence becomes "0" on both sides, and |0 - 0| <= 1 holds. The check cannot tell
"both insets agree" from "neither element exists".

REPRO (the reviewer's, by measurement): in a copy of the built extension, rename
#jobs-board-host and the jobs-section .panel-head away, then run the driver with
CAP_ACCEPTANCE_EXT=<that copy>. The driver prints
  boardPad="undefined" headPad="undefined"
and THIS CHECK PASSES while 8 other checks fail - including its own sibling
"hub: the board's content sits on the same inset as its own panel header"
(line 318), which reads real rects through padAlign and so does go red.

SAME CLASS AS q264/qzae: a check that cannot fail reads as safety. This is the
third shape of it in one file - an empty list, a statically-satisfied predicate,
and now a zero-vs-zero comparison.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE: require PRESENCE before the comparison is meaningful.
  const ok = typeof pad1440.panelBodyPadding === "string" && pad1440.panelBodyPadding.length > 0
          && typeof pad1440.panelHeadPadding === "string" && pad1440.panelHeadPadding.length > 0;
  check("hub: the Jobs board's content is inset like its own panel header",
    ok && Math.abs(bodyLeft - headLeft) <= 1,
    { ok, bodyPadding: pad1440.panelBodyPadding, headPadding: pad1440.panelHeadPadding });
Then prove it can fail by renaming the two elements away and watching it go RED.

ACCEPTANCE: RED when either element is absent; RED when the insets genuinely
differ by more than 1px; green on the fixed tree - all three recorded.

comments.text: FIXED on fix/harness-marks-live @ d0f01545ae00a7675366e249d7d1db0f476fa159. The check read each side with a default of "0", so a missing element gave parseFloat("0") on BOTH sides and |0-0| <= 1 held while the measured thing did not exist. Now an unparseable side yields null and null fails. DRIVEN PROOF: a copy of the canonical extension with #jobs-board-host renamed away gives exit 1 and this check RED, where it PASSED before the fix; the unmutated tree gives exit 0 and 46/0, so the check is conditional rather than unconditionally red. comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Independent review of fix/harness-marks-live @ d0f01545 (PASS).

THE FIX WORKS — re-derived, not accepted. The same mutant, both drivers:
- PRE-fix driver (origin/main cap-evidence/): `PASS hub: the Jobs board's content is inset like its own panel header` while 8 others failed -> 38 passed / 8 failed, exit 1. The check passed on a tree where BOTH elements it measures are absent.
- NEW driver: `FAIL ... {"bodyLeft":null,"headLeft":null}` -> 37 passed / 9 failed, exit 1.
Mutant: rename `#jobs-board-host` (ntp.html:1103) and the jobs-section `.panel-head` (ntp.html:1099) away, in a copy of the canonical extension. So absence now fails, and the check has teeth. Baseline unmutated = 46/0 with the check passing, which is the positive control.

ONE NEW DEFECT, MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — the fix introduces a false-red on a legitimate layout.
`padLeft` splits the padding string on whitespace and takes index [1]. For a UNIFORM (single-value) padding there is no [1], so it returns null and the check fails — even though both elements are present, their padding is read, and the property being asserted HOLDS.

Control: both elements present, both `style="padding:14px"` (left insets equal, so the check should PASS).
- PRE-fix driver: PASS, 46/0, exit 0.
- NEW driver: FAIL, 45/1, exit 1 -> `{"bodyPadding":"14px","headPadding":"14px","bodyLeft":null,"headLeft":null}`.
The failure detail contradicts its own verdict: it shows the two padding strings and still reports failure, because only the *token count* differed.

So the fix swapped one conflation for its mirror image: before, absent and zero were indistinguishable; now, "no second token" is treated as "no element".

Suggested predicate (keeps absence failing, accepts a uniform shorthand):
    const padLeft = (value) => {
      const t = String(value ?? "").trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
      if (!t.length) return null;                      // element absent -> FAIL, as intended
      const part = t.length >= 2 ? t[1] : t[0];        // 1 value == all four sides
      const n = parseFloat(part);
      return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null;
    };

Severity, stated plainly: NOT a blocker. It is fail-CLOSED (red on a good state) rather than fail-open, the shipped tree uses `12px 14px` for both so it is unreachable today, and the driver is `named` so no gate runs it. But it is a check that can fail for the wrong reason, which is the class this commit set out to remove. Worth fixing immediately as a follow-up, with the control above as its regression test.

title: A collapsed-panel rule pinned statically but never observed firing (every chip check passed with the rule dead)
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/harness-logos (e72ca133), in cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts.

OBSERVED: every side-panel chip check used the form `b.labelClipped || !b.wrapped`, which `white-space: nowrap` alone satisfies — with nowrap nothing ever wraps, so `!wrapped` is always true. Removing `container-type: inline-size` from `#agents-view` leaves the driver GREEN while the collapsed chip grows 34px -> 54px; the rule is dead and nothing notices.

WHY it goes dead rather than falling back: `#page-view` also carries `container-type`, but it is a SIBLING of `#agents-view`, not an ancestor of the chips. Removing it from `#agents-view` therefore leaves the chips with no container context at all, so `@container (max-width: 320px)` can never match.

Removal IS caught statically — tests/harness-marks.test.ts asserts `container-type: inline-size` on `#agents-view` — so what was missing is evidence that the rule TAKES EFFECT.

REPRO: `cp -a extension /tmp/m4 && sed -i 's| container-type: inline-size;||' /tmp/m4/sidepanel/sidepanel.html`, then run the driver with CAP_ACCEPTANCE_EXT=/tmp/m4. Pre-existing chip checks: 6/6 PASS. New collapsed-rule check: RED at 260px and 300px.

ACCEPTANCE: the behavioural check observes the collapsed state in BOTH directions — the label is clipped at 260/300px and not clipped at 400px — and goes RED when `container-type` is removed while the pre-existing checks stay green (recorded, to show what it adds).

STATUS: fixed and measured in the same session; see Evidence.md 'What the two new checks assert' and 'Mutations'.

title: A layout check that cannot fail: the shadow-root walk found nothing, and .every() on [] is true
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/harness-logos (e72ca133), in cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts.

OBSERVED: the check 'hub: nothing inside the Jobs column holds the grid track open' was written on `shrinkHolders`, which is a plain `jobs.querySelectorAll('*')` walk. <jobs-board> renders its rows into a SHADOW ROOT, so that walk never saw them. The reviewer measured 0 entries in both the baseline and the mutant, so `.every(o => o.minContent <= 320)` was evaluated on an EMPTY array and returned true. The check passed on the base tree, where the defect is real and reproduced by twelve other checks.

The instrument that DOES cross the shadow root was already in the file: `deepMinContent` walks `node.shadowRoot.children` and correctly names `span.jb-excerpt` at 684px min-content. It was computed, printed and returned, and asserted on by nothing.

REPRO: put the check back in its vacuous form and run the driver against a base build: `CAP_ACCEPTANCE_EXT=<base extension> deno run -A cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts` — it reports PASS while twelve checks fail.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) the containment property is asserted through the shadow-crossing instrument, not a light-DOM walk; (2) a non-vacuity guard fails loudly when the probe finds nothing, so no future check of this shape can pass by finding nothing; (3) the check goes RED on the base and on a reverted-`minmax` mutant, and green on the fixed tree — all three recorded.

STATUS: fixed and measured in the same session; see cap-evidence/l3ts-constrained-width/EVIDENCE.md sections 'What the two new checks assert' and 'Mutations'.

- old check vs BASE ext: PASS, while 9 other checks FAIL. It could not fail on the tree it was meant to protect.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE, measured. "the shadow-root walk found nothing, and .every() on [] is true" is true on the FIXED tree and on the previous reviewer's box — but NOT on the base tree on this box. At 1440px `shrinkHolders` held TWO entries, both 178px (`div.panel-body.jobs-board-body` and the `jobs-board` host). comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW — cap/harness-logos @ e72ca133. Reviewer: separate session, own worktree
(/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/review-harness-logos), author's checkout untouched, canonical
checkout still on main@3091eaba.

VERDICT: PASS. The fix is correct, load-bearing and green. Findings below are about CHECK
STRENGTH and REPORTED NUMBERS; none of them changes the verdict.

=== WHAT I DROVE (not read)
Driver: cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts, run 9 times on a built extension in
headless Chrome. 42 browser checks per run. Full suite once: EXIT CODE 0, 487 files,
4402 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 177s (verified with an explicit `; echo $?`,
not through a pipe).

  state                              browser checks
  branch (fix)                        42 passed /  0 failed
  TRUE BASE (origin/main, rebuilt-ish) 29 passed / 13 failed
  M1 grid minmax reverted             37 passed /  5 failed
  M2 padding removed                  39 passed /  3 failed
  M3 nowrap removed from .hq          41 passed /  1 failed
  M4 container-type removed           42 passed /  0 failed   <-- see F2
  M5 overflow:hidden removed          42 passed /  0 failed
  M6 min-width:0 added back           42 passed /  0 failed

=== CLAIM-BY-CLAIM
1. Jobs board grid — CONFIRMED, load-bearing. Base 1440px grid=[202.156px 685.844px]
   agents.w=202; 1100px grid=[116.359px 685.844px] agents.w=116. Branch [444 444] / [389 389].
   Mechanisms confirmed: the base rule at ntp.html:582 does use minmax(0,1fr) and the
   @media (min-width:1100px) override did regress it to bare `1fr`; and the track floor is
   content-driven — the shadow-crossing instrument names span.jb-excerpt at 684px min-content,
   matching the 685.844px track. M1 turns 5 checks red.
2. Padding — CONFIRMED. Base boardPad="4px 0px" vs headPad="12px 14px" exactly as reported;
   #jobs-board-host really does carry .jobs-board-body, so the check measures the fixed
   element. M2 turns 3 checks red.
3. Chip nowrap — CONFIRMED. M3 (nowrap off the .hq rule only) reddens the long-name check.
4. min-width:0 dropped as redundant — CONFIRMED, AND THE REASONING IS SOUND. M6 (adding it
   back) is byte-identical to baseline at every width: it was genuinely redundant, not
   "the check was too weak". M5 shows overflow:hidden on .hq is equally redundant.
5. Marks / provenance — CONFIRMED. Inline <svg viewBox> wrapper, currentColor, aria-hidden,
   no emoji, no hard-coded colour; asserted by tests/harness-marks.test.ts (19 passed), which
   extracts rule bodies rather than substrings. docs/HARNESS-MARKS-PROVENANCE.md is accurate.
6. Gate complaint — CONFIRMED: my npm test also ran 487 files, the same selection
   test:changed reported.

=== FINDINGS
F1 (should fix before landing) — A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL. The check "hub: nothing inside
   the Jobs column holds the grid track open" is `shrinkHolders.every(o => o.minContent <= 320)`.
   shrinkHolders uses jobs.querySelectorAll('*'), which does NOT cross the shadow root, so it
   is EMPTY in every state I drove — and .every() on [] is true. Proven empty (0 entries) in
   both baseline and M1. Meanwhile deepMinContent, the instrument that DOES cross the shadow
   root and correctly names span.jb-excerpt at 684px, is computed, printed, returned — and
   asserted on by nothing. The right instrument was built and then not used.
F2 (should fix before landing) — THE CONTAINER QUERY IS PINNED STATICALLY, NOT VERIFIED
   BEHAVIOURALLY. M4 removing `container-type: inline-size` from #agents-view leaves the
   browser driver 42/0 GREEN while the collapsed chip changes from 34px (label clipped) to
   54px (label visible) at 260/300px. The check that looks like it covers this —
   `labelClipped || !wrapped` — is satisfied by nowrap alone and cannot fail for this reason.
   It IS caught by the unit test (M4 -> 18 passed / 1 failed at harness-marks.test.ts:162,
   via ruleBody extraction), so removal is guarded; what is unverified is that the rule FIRES.
F3 (report accuracy) — THE BEFORE/AFTER TABLE IS NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE. EVIDENCE.md says "same
   harness, same seeded content", but the totals are 24/11 (35 checks) before vs 42/0 (42
   checks) after — a different driver revision. Re-measured on the current driver the base is
   29 passed / 13 failed over 42 checks.
F4 (report accuracy) — PIXEL DRIFT. Author's base 1440px grid [198.156px 689.844px] vs my
   measured [202.156px 685.844px]: same 888px total, 4px redistributed. Author's "`.main-wrap`
   overflow at 1100px = 4px"; I measure 0px on the true base at 1100px (and the author's own
   two track figures sum to 806.2px against 826px available, which is not an overflow).
   Author's M7 [116.359px 717.844px]/32px vs my M1 [116.359px 713.844px]/28px. The agents
   track (116.359) and the padding (4px 0px) match exactly, so the fixture is right and
   something else shifts the Jobs track by 4px. Direction and mechanism confirmed; treat the
   exact figures as approximate.
F5 (minor) — The console summary prints `wrapped=${b.wrappedToMultipleLines}`, but the probe
   field is `wrapped`. Every printed line reads `wrapped=undefined`. The verdict is unaffected
   (the check reads b.wrapped correctly), but the printed evidence misleads.
F6 (minor) — EVIDENCE.md's fourth instrument note says conflating scrollWidth-at-width-0 with
   min-content "named the wrong culprit (.jb-excerpt)". That is not supported by the driver's
   own shadow-crossing instrument, which reports .jb-excerpt at 684px in BOTH base and fixed
   states, matching the track floor. The FIX is still right (a nowrap one-line excerpt is the
   intended design; the TRACK was the defect) — but the note reads as a measurement claim it
   cannot support.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY
- More than three registered agents (only pi / Claude Code / Codex exist here); the author
  lists this under "Not covered" honestly.
- The true side-panel width is a user drag; 260/300/400px emulation is a proxy.
- My TRUE BASE run could not complete a rebuild: `npm run build:production` fails with
  "dist.complete validation failed: indexed source is missing: extension/shared/harness-marks.js"
  when the branch's new module is removed under a dist.complete marker written by the branch
  build. Not a product defect (the marker binds indexed sources by design); it means my base
  run used base HTML/CSS with the stale branch bundle. The hub (ntp.html, loaded directly) is
  therefore a fully valid base; the sidepanel base is base-CSS-with-branch-JS, which is exactly
  the CSS-only isolation the claimed fix needs, and the wrap defect reproduces there (ws=normal).

=== WHY THE VERDICT IS PASS DESPITE F1/F2
The fix is proven the hard way: both defects reproduce on the base (29/13), every claimed line
is load-bearing under mutation except the ones the author correctly dropped, the mechanism
matches the diagnosis exactly, and the full suite is exit-0 green. F1 and F2 are weaknesses in
the TESTS, in the one direction this repo's canon is explicit about — a check that cannot fail
is the defect, not the reassurance — and they should be closed, but they do not make the fix
wrong, and the browser checks that DO have teeth (overflow, 60% share, padding inset, body
scroll, wrap) are all sensitive to mutation.

Landing on this verdict is the coordinator's call; the author fixes their own work.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW of cap/l3ts-check-strength @ ac0a62d4 — VERDICT: PASS. Safe to fast-forward.
