title: Default-tier bundled tools are memory-rejected in the offscreen WASI-job lane: buildPreviewJob hardcodes tier tiny, so the shipped compressops and zxing (and oxipng) cannot execute in live runs
description:
Found by the m3vb ladder's step-5 dispatch check (the ten9 KAT, scripts/kat-bundled-execute.ts, extended with an oxipng pair): oxipng dispatched end-to-end — search_tools ranked it #1, execute_tool → SW dispatchBundledWasmStream → offscreen WASI_JOB_RUN_TYPE → the job worker — and the worker refused it: phase "memory-rejected", error "worker fail-closed: audit:memory_exceeds_ceiling" (cap-evidence/kat-bundled-execute/2026-09-06T20-43-00.795Z/result.json). A no-Chrome reproduction over the REAL CAS bytes of every admitted non-stream, non-callexport tool through the REAL job-worker entry (runWorkerJob) with the job built exactly as the service worker builds it (buildPreviewJob) — cap-evidence/cap-oxipng/job-lane-tier-gap-probe.log — shows the class: REJECTED (declared tier default, maxPages 2048): zxing, compressops, oxipng. Dispatched fine (declared tiny): the other 21. So TWO ALREADY-SHIPPED "admitted" tools (compressops from y75s, zxing from 2htn) cannot execute in a live agent run since ten9 (e5a6673c) opened the lane — a regression of ten9's own directive ("no tool may be preview-gated; all bundled tools fully agent-available"). Nobody saw it because (a) ten9's KAT drives only tiny-tier tools (gzip/sha256sum/uuid) through the job lane, (b) the compressops/zxing/imageops admission tests run the STREAM worker, and (c) tests/bundled-tools-live-execution.test.ts "ten9 GUARD: live dispatch … reaches the executor" only asserts the result is not preview_only_tool — a memory-rejected result passes it.

MECHANISM (pinned): extension/lib/tool-exec-preview.js:443 — buildPreviewJob calls createWasiJob({ tier: "tiny", … }) for EVERY tool. extension/lib/wasm-execution-worker.js:150-158 — runWorkerJob audits the binary against WASM_PACKAGE_LIMITS.TIERS[job.tier].maxPages (512 for tiny) via auditWasmBinary; a binary declaring max 2048 pages fails memory_exceeds_ceiling (wasm-package-authority.js:507). The worker already ACCEPTS tier "default" (wasm-execution-worker.js:99 — ["tiny","default"]; large stays refused), so the lane supports it — the job builder just never passes the tool's declared tier. PREVIEW_SPECS (tool-exec-preview.js ~70-127) does not carry the tier, though the generated row has it: row.binary.tier / row.binary.maxPages (never request-borne). Both callers build the same job: executeBundledWasiJob (tool-exec-preview.js:748, the ten9 run path) and the tool.preview.run Settings route (service-worker.js:6566) — so the Settings preview of compressops/zxing is very likely broken the same way; CONFIRM in a loaded extension at pickup (the options-page host: check whether it runs wasm-execution-worker).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) PREVIEW_SPECS carries each tool's declared tier + maxPages from the generated row, and buildPreviewJob passes spec.tier (default "tiny" only when the row lacks one) — the tier is spec authority, never from the request; (2) a no-Chrome test (the probe above, made a test: tests/bundled-tools-job-lane-tier.test.ts) drives runWorkerJob over the real CAS bytes of every admitted non-stream, non-callexport tool with buildPreviewJob's job and asserts no result has phase memory-rejected — RED today naming exactly zxing, compressops, oxipng; GREEN after; (3) tests/bundled-tools-live-execution.test.ts's GUARD additionally asserts the phase is not memory-rejected / import-rejected (the executor's OWN refusals, not only the former preview gate); (4) scripts/kat-bundled-execute.ts gains one default-tier job-lane pair (compressops: search "zstd compress" → execute {args:["zstd"], stdin:"…"}; assert the zstd magic 28b52ffd / KLUv in stdoutBase64) so the Chrome gate covers the class (EXPECTED_CALLS +2) — with m3vb's oxipng pair landing separately; (5) compressops and zxing Settings previews verified in a loaded extension (screenshots). FALSIFICATION: revert the tier plumbing in buildPreviewJob → test (2) RED; force spec.tier = "large" for one tool → tier_blocked (the large block must survive). MUST NOT CHANGE: the tier ceilings, auditWasmBinary, the large-tier refusal, the stream lane, any manifest/CAS. Gates: test:changed per change, npm test once, the KAT in a loaded extension, independent review; store SW budget headroom is 16,776 B after m3vb — this fix adds no data.

BLOCKS: chrome-agent-platform-m3vb step 5 (MODEL-VERIFIED) — its KAT pair is RED on this gap by design; it stays blocked until this lands. The next tranche beads (agpu, moim, ou4x) all target the same lane and inherit the fix.

title: user-wasm-store v2: generalize into the shared owner-blob store (neutral root, .bin, kind, tested migration)
description:
SPEC: cap-evidence/claude/4p7j-analysis.md — the Python-module epic's S1 is literally 'Shared owner-blob store (with 9ux7.1, not beside it)', because 'Wheels and Wasm modules are both owner-supplied binary blobs with owner-written metadata. They should share one store, or we will maintain two stores with one bug surface each. This is a coordination point, not a preference — worth settling before either lands.' Review that found the gap: cap-evidence/reviews/9ux7.1-design-intent-review.md (findings R1 + R3).

CURRENT STATE (already on main, byte-identical to candidate 55fd033d): extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js is BEHAVIORALLY the shared store — record {version:1, digest, name, description, size, addedAt} with no wasm-specific fields, verbs put/list/getFile/remove, and ZERO admission gates (no size/count cap, no \0asm magic check, no parse/compile at upload), so a wheel is as acceptable as a module. Digests are already comparable to the bundled CAS (sha256 hex over the bytes; extension/wasm/cas/<sha256>.wasm via scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs:52; cross-checked against crypto.subtle at tests/user-wasm-store.test.ts:84). It is NOMINALLY wasm-bound in exactly three places, and those are what a wheel cannot reuse:
1. USER_WASM_ROOT = 'cap-user-wasm-v1' — the OPFS directory name.
2. DATA = /^([0-9a-f]{64})\.wasm$/, temporary = upload-<uuid>.wasm, PENDING = /^upload-[0-9a-f-]+\.wasm$/ — a wheel would be stored as <digest>.wasm, anything sniffing by extension mis-handles a zip, and crash recovery only cleans .wasm temporaries.
3. createUserWasmStore + owner-facing copy ('Invalid user-wasm digest', 'Stored user-wasm bytes are missing', 'Uploaded file not found').

ACCEPTANCE
1. A neutral v2 store: neutral OPFS root (e.g. cap-owner-blobs-v1), neutral data extension (<digest>.bin), neutral temp/recovery patterns, a kind field in the record ('wasm' | 'wheel' | …, validated against a closed set), neutral API + error copy. The record keeps version/digest/name/description/size/addedAt and gains kind.
2. TESTED MIGRATION for existing v1 owner data: real owner bytes already live under cap-user-wasm-v1 on disk, so v2 must find them — migrate on first open (move or re-key) or read both roots, with the choice stated. Tests must cover: a v1 store with entries opens under v2 and lists them with kind 'wasm'; a partially-migrated store (crash mid-migration) recovers without losing or duplicating bytes; a v1 store whose bytes are missing still fails CLOSED the way v1 does today; migration never rewrites owner bytes (digest identity preserved bit-for-bit).
3. All five consumers on main updated: extension/lib/user-wasm-store-client.js, extension/lib/user-wasm-store-worker.js, extension/options/user-wasm-panel.js, scripts/kat-user-wasm-store.ts, tests/user-wasm-ui.test.ts (+ tests/user-wasm-store.test.ts). No consumer left importing the v1 names.
4. R3 folded in: put() returns an explicit replacement signal (e.g. replaced: true / previousName) so the S2 UI can say 'this replaced the name on an existing file' instead of the caller inferring it; keep getFile(digest) (returning a File reference, bytes never ride messaging JSON) but document the bead-vs-code naming (9ux7.1 asked for get) and accept a Blob OR bytes for put so a wheel installer holding bytes in memory need not wrap them.
5. Every durability property that exists today is preserved and still tested: publication last (bytes committed before metadata), empty-metadata = unpublished upload, durable delete intent completed on reopen, metadata-without-bytes fails closed, orphan bytes pruned, digest pinned to /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ against traversal, names are metadata never paths (Unicode), >64 MiB stored without a whole-file allocation, two store instances serialize put/remove without lost updates, identical bytes = one CAS entry with addedAt retained, same name + different bytes = two entries.
6. Falsification: break the migration (leave v1 entries unreadable) → migration test RED; break kind validation → RED; remove the replacement signal → RED; break the digest computation → round-trip RED. Each reverted, shown RED, restored.
7. Gates: npm run test:changed per change, npm test green before push, real-browser evidence for the Settings panel (drive it in headless Chrome via the existing KAT: upload a module, see it listed, remove it) since this touches an owner-visible surface.

BLOCKS: chrome-agent-platform-ovfm (installable JavaScript/Python modules in the sandbox) — 4p7j's S2 installs a pure-Python wheel 'from stored bytes', i.e. from THIS store. Two stores is the outcome this bead exists to prevent.
DO NOT: add admission bounds (no size/count/parse gates — owner decision on the epic); do not change the digest identity scheme (it must stay comparable to the bundled CAS); do not delete v1 owner data during migration.

title: S0.5 permissioned proxy bridge: model-authored Python gets network access that is visible, scoped and revocable
description:
Owner decision (Paul, 2026-09-06), design sketch in analysis §10.2b.

Paul: model-authored code should STILL be able to make network requests, but only under a permission grant, via a proxy. S0 strips the ambient globals; this stage gives back a narrower capability in their place. Ambient fetch is a capability the owner cannot see, scope or revoke; a proxied grant is all three.

SHAPE: Python 'await cap.fetch(url, ...)' shim -> JS callback in the worker (correlation id per request) -> postMessage to the offscreen python host -> chrome.runtime to the SERVICE WORKER, which is the ONLY network actor -> grant check -> fetch -> response envelope back. With S0 landed the worker holds no network globals, so the shim is the only route out and cannot be bypassed.

THE CONFUSED-DEPUTY RISK — the part most worth reviewing. The service worker holds host_permissions <all_urls> AND the owner's ambient cookies for every origin. A naive fetch(url) in the SW issues AUTHENTICATED requests to any granted origin, so a grant that merely says 'example.com is allowed' could read the owner's logged-in session there. Required defaults:
- credentials: 'omit' ALWAYS. A proxied request is anonymous; authenticated access is its own, louder grant.
- redirect: 'manual'. A granted origin redirecting to an ungranted one is re-checked against the allowlist — redirect chains are how an allowlist gets laundered.
- refuse non-http(s) schemes outright (chrome-extension://, file://, data:) — some of them read the extension's own package.
- strip caller-controlled Cookie/Authorization and the implied Origin/Referer.

AWAITABLE, NOT SYNCHRONOUS: the shim returns a promise the Python side awaits; runPythonAsync supports that, so no SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics. Consequence stated honestly in the shim's docstring: requests/urllib CANNOT be offered this way and stay unavailable — a module importing them fails with a readable message pointing at cap.fetch, in the teaching style script-sandbox.js already uses for storage APIs.

GRANTS: per-origin allowlist in Settings beside the existing permission surfaces, showing origin, when granted, by which gesture, with a Remove per row. First-use prompt optional (Paul); when off, an ungranted origin fails with an error naming the origin and how to grant it — never a silent empty response.

TRANSCRIPT: every request lands in the run's transcript the way a tool call does — method, URL, status, bytes, duration. REFUSED requests are logged too; a denied origin is exactly what an owner wants to see. Visibility is the stated point, so this is not a debug facility.

BOUNDS: the 30 s wall deadline still applies and network time counts against it (visible in the logged duration, never silently absorbed). No response size caps (analysis §5).

NOT IN SCOPE: sessions, streaming, websockets, a general HTTP stack. One awaitable function, one allowlist, one logging path.

ACCEPTANCE: in a real loaded extension, Python awaiting cap.fetch against a GRANTED origin returns a real response and the request appears in the transcript; against an UNGRANTED origin it fails with an error naming the origin, and that refusal also appears; a granted origin redirecting to an ungranted one does NOT complete; a request to an origin where the owner is logged in carries no cookies (assert the request was anonymous, not merely that it succeeded).
DEPENDS ON: S0.

comments.text:
S0.5 implemented and gated. Branch claude-4p7j-s05 @ dc5cac0d (v0.3.311), rebased on origin/main@7f903962, worktree ~/worktrees/claude-4p7j-s05, NOT pushed (held for the coordinator).

SHAPE AS BUILT: Python 'await cap.fetch(url)' -> JS shim in the Pyodide worker (correlation id per call) -> postMessage to the offscreen python host -> chrome.runtime to the SERVICE WORKER, the only network actor -> owner grant check -> fetch -> envelope back. The worker decides nothing: no allow-list, no credential policy, no logging there, so there is one place to read to know what Python may reach.

REUSE, NOT A SECOND COPY: four of the five confused-deputy defaults already existed in the script sandbox's cap:fetch route. The scheme + loopback/private-address (SSRF) predicate is now checkFetchTarget in lib/fetch-policy.js, called by BOTH bridges, so neither can drift into being the weaker one. That predicate was MISSING from the design sketch in analysis 10.2b - a real hole in the analysis, closed in the code.

WHAT IS NEW: (1) the AUTHORITY for the allow-list - per-origin owner grants, persisted, listed in Settings -> Permissions with when/by-which-gesture and a Remove that revokes immediately; (2) the RECORD - every request and refusal is written by the SERVICE WORKER, not the program, and travels back attached to the tool result, so catching the refusal and printing nothing cannot hide it.

EVIDENCE
- scripts/kat-python-permissioned-fetch.ts (new, registered): 28 passed / 0 failed in a loaded extension. The grant is made by CLICKING Allow in Settings; the request is made by Python through the real python.execute route.
- kat-python-no-ambient-network (S0): 14/0, unchanged.
- Full unit suite: 3996 passed / 0 failed, 422 files, 116s.
- Build: 7 pinned runtime files re-verified; 133 generated files byte-identical.

ACCEPTANCE, item by item: granted origin returns a real response and the request appears in the records (PASS); ungranted origin fails with an error naming the origin, and the refusal is recorded too (PASS); a granted origin redirecting to an ungranted one does NOT complete and the target is never reached (PASS); a request to an origin where the owner IS logged in carries no cookies - asserted as 'the server saw no cookie', not merely 'it succeeded' (PASS).

FALSIFICATION, single-variable, both in a real browser:
1. credentials omit -> include: red on the anonymity assertions, the owner's real session cookie arrived at the origin. Note the header sanitizer STILL refused the caller's own Cookie header - the cookie came from the ambient jar, which is exactly the confused deputy 'omit' exists for and is NOT covered by header sanitizing.
2. redirect manual -> follow: red on the laundering assertions, a grant for one host reached a host that was never granted.
Both restored; 28/28 again.

TEST SEAM WORTH KNOWING: the policy refuses loopback outright, so a 127.0.0.1 test server could never prove the ALLOWED path. Chrome is launched with --host-resolver-rules mapping public-looking hostnames to the local server. That is the DNS caveat lib/fetch-policy.js already documents, used deliberately as a seam and noted in the harness header.

TRAP FOR THE NEXT EDITOR: python-worker.js is hash-verified twice. Any edit must update its sha256 in BOTH wasm-tools/python/MANIFEST.json and PYTHON_RUNTIME_PIN, or Python fails closed at startup.

OPEN FOR THE OWNER: the first-use prompt is not built (the bead calls it optional) - today an ungranted origin fails with an error naming the origin and how to grant it, and Settings is the only way to grant. POST is allowed, PUT/PATCH/DELETE are not: a grant to read is not a grant to write; widening that is an owner decision.

title: S0 strip the ambient network globals from the Pyodide worker
description:
Owner decision (Paul, 2026-09-06), analysis §7.3/§10.2 in /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/claude/4p7j-analysis.md.

MEASURED TODAY, not theorised: through the real python.execute route in a loaded extension, 'import js' exposes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, importScripts, Worker, indexedDB and caches (all True); the worker holds the chrome-extension origin; and a real cross-origin request returned status 404 — it left the browser. The extension holds host_permissions <all_urls>, so model-authored Python can reach any origin with the extension's privileges, today, with nothing in the transcript.

WHAT: delete fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource and importScripts from the worker's global scope in wasm-tools/python/python-worker.js BEFORE loadPyodide runs, so 'import js' finds nothing to reach the network with.

THE BOUNDARY — this must be in the code comment, verbatim in spirit (Paul): IN SCOPE is the Pyodide worker's own scope only. OUT OF SCOPE and untouched: every other request the extension makes — the service worker's provider calls, the offscreen document's fetches, script-sandbox.js's host-bridged fetch for agent scripts, and python-host.js's own fetch of the pinned runtime bytes (that runs in the HOST, not the worker, and MUST keep working or the runtime cannot be hash-verified). If Python needs HTTP it returns as an explicit permissioned capability (S0.5), never as an ambient global.

This is not an admission bound (analysis §5): it removes a capability the tool never advertised. It refuses no payload and caps no size.

ACCEPTANCE: the probe that returned 'FETCH REACHED NETWORK, status: 404' returns an honest failure instead, and 'import js' reports the stripped names absent; python_execute still runs ordinary code (stdin -> stdout unchanged); the runtime still hash-verifies at host startup. Falsification: restore one global, watch the probe reach the network again, re-strip.

FILES: wasm-tools/python/python-worker.js (+ its sha256 in wasm-tools/python/MANIFEST.json and PYTHON_RUNTIME_PIN in extension/lib/python-runtime.js — the worker is a PINNED file, so changing it means re-pinning in both places or the host fails closed), tests/python-runtime.test.ts, a browser probe.
NOTE: the pin is deliberate friction, not an obstacle — python-host.js verifies every runtime byte before the interpreter loads.
close_reason: Stripped ambient network globals (fetch, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, importScripts, Worker, SharedWorker, WebTransport, sendBeacon) from Python worker scope; functionally verified via kat-python-no-ambient-network.ts 14/14 green, landed @ 9a93679f

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
S0 IMPLEMENTED AND GATED — branch claude-4p7j-s0 @ 2e7e6841 (v0.3.271) in ~/worktrees/claude-4p7j-s0. NOT pushed.

WHAT LANDED: wasm-tools/python/python-worker.js replaces the ambient network globals with throwing guards immediately after loadPyodide resolves, before any Python runs. List: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, importScripts, Worker, SharedWorker, WebTransport, navigator.sendBeacon — longer than the bead's, deliberately: importScripts loads remote script, Worker spawns a nested worker with its own untouched fetch, sendBeacon posts a body and needs no response. A strip that leaves one door open is theatre.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: Pyodide's own loader needs fetch to read pyodide.asm.wasm and python_stdlib.zip, so the strip cannot run first — it would break the interpreter before it exists. It runs in the .then() after init; runtime() is awaited before the per-run stdout/stdin wiring and before runPythonAsync, so there is no window where the globals are both present and reachable from Python.

TWO MISTAKES THE PROBE CAUGHT IN MY OWN WORK:
1. delete self.fetch was a SILENT NO-OP — these globals live on WorkerGlobalScope.prototype, not as own properties, so it deleted something that was never there and returned true. Only the '= undefined' fallback shadowed them.
2. The result was js.fetch resolving to None, so a caller saw "'NoneType' object is not callable" — capability gone, model taught nothing. Each name is now defineProperty'd to a function that throws a readable refusal naming the boundary and saying what to do instead, matching script-sandbox.js's teaching style for storage APIs.

RE-PINNED: python-worker.js is hash-verified twice (build, then python-host.js before the interpreter loads), so its sha256 was updated in MANIFEST.json AND PYTHON_RUNTIME_PIN. Build reports 'admitted Pyodide runtime staged (7 files, sha256-verified)'. NOTE FOR REVIEWERS/REBASERS: any future edit to that file must update both or Python fails closed at startup.

FALSIFICATION (single variable): removed exactly one name (fetch) from the guard list, re-pinned, rebuilt, re-probed -> 'fetch -> STILL CALLABLE  <-- FAIL' and 'STILL REACHED NETWORK, status: 404'. Restored -> green. The guard is what blocks, not the environment.

PERMANENT GATE: scripts/kat-python-no-ambient-network.ts (new), registered in harness-registry as class 'kat'. 14 passed / 0 failed. Its assertions CALL each name rather than checking existence — presence is not the test, power is — and it asserts the refusal teaches (/no ambient network access/, explicitly not /NoneType/), so the weak version of this guard cannot pass it either. Without it the property would rest on a scratchpad script that dies with the session.

GATES: unit 3771 passed / 0 failed (395 files, 91 s); kat 14/14; build clean; vocabulary/gallery/reachability/changelog/changelog-order all OK.

ADJACENT, FILED NOT FIXED: indexedDB and caches remain reachable from Python — storage, not network, so stripping them would have made this stage's scope untrue to the decision. Filed as chrome-agent-platform-4p7j.3.

acceptance_criteria:
# 6854 — proposed acceptance criterion after owner clarification

PROPOSED, NOT APPROVED. This follows Paul's direction against incidental invalidation and coordinator seq177. It replaces the proposed blanket pin of every non-version manifest field; it does not alter the sealed historical record.

1. **Preserve history.** The original manifest, probe/glue/Wasm hashes, browser/runtime identity and result remain immutable evidence of the build actually tested. A later change never rewrites or retroactively invalidates that observation.
2. **Compare the execution contract, not release metadata.** Reusing the compatibility conclusion for a changed implementation requires fresh relevant browser verification when the Emscripten runtime/ABI version or executable probe/glue/Wasm bytes change; when CSP or execution-relevant isolation changes; when worker/module loading, main/side dependency resolution or import/provider mechanics change; or when the host-to-native operation/interface surface changes (arguments/results, imports/exports, memory/thread policy or reachable authority). These changes do not erase the old result. Any changed expected contract or fixture pins require explicit reviewed replacement, retaining their predecessors.
3. **Incidental metadata is non-invalidating.** Extension release `version`/`version_name`, names/descriptions, icons, and evidence/copy locations or timestamps do not require rewriting the historical manifest/probe pins or fail the compatibility check when the execution contract is unchanged. Other runtime-irrelevant metadata is likewise non-invalidating. A field affecting loading or the execution realm's security/authority is not classified as incidental merely because it is in a manifest.
4. **Bind every actual run honestly.** Record the current full manifest digest, actual runtime/browser identity and current complete production build. Verify the loaded copy is byte-identical to that current source/build, plus the exact reviewed probe/glue/Wasm asset pins. A changed copy must fail even if the changed field would have been an acceptable metadata change in the source. Metadata tolerance never excuses a mismatched copy, changed CSP, unreviewed executable asset or widened authority.
5. **Prove the distinction.** Executed tests accept metadata-only source evolution without changing historical pins; refuse current-source/copy mismatches and unreviewed runtime-contract or probe-asset drift; and record the actual current manifest identity. Preserve original REDs and independently review the concrete projection and regression tests before landing. All normal build/unit/browser/security gates remain required; this criterion is not an exemption from them.

Paul's approval-or-edit is requested for this boundary, not approval of an arbitrary manifest-field allowlist or of the current overbroad implementation. No source edit, publication, or issue closure is authorized merely by writing this proposal.

title: De-serialize the Chrome test gates: per-instance isolation + bounded concurrency instead of the global lock
description: Paul directive 2026-09-05: 'work out how to get around this browser gate — you can run your own instance of Chrome.' Headless Chrome instances with distinct --user-data-dir profiles and --remote-debugging-port=0 are fully isolated; the global flock serializes everything unnecessarily. Fix: (1) default harness launches take NO canonical lock — profiles/ports already isolate; (2) replace exclusivity with a bounded-concurrency semaphore (e.g., max 3-4 concurrent chromes, env-tunable) to avoid OOM; (3) suites that genuinely need machine determinism (security custody) opt into the canonical lock explicitly; (4) retire the cap-chrome-slot-POISON cross-contamination mechanism that only exists because of shared-slot assumptions; (5) the eo4d.1/journey environmental-red class should vanish.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-WEBMCP-SITE-RESET-ASK-FENCE-01] Site reset must invalidate pending first-use ASK cards even with no stored decisions
description:
# eo4d independent exact-object review — REVISE

Reviewer: Astra (independent session/model from implementation). Date: 2026-09-05.

- Reviewed candidate: `25acd4671075f9a2291e3a9f953d2717e59587df`
- Base: `35ad5264f1c8b3d7c261fb358a2dbf89d27e5741`

- Landing authority remains coordinator `01a06e79`. This report does not authorize another SHA.

## Blocking finding R1 — P1: a site reset with only ASK tools leaves outstanding first-use cards authorized

Locations: `extension/lib/site-tool-consent.js:339–343`; `extension/background/service-worker.js:7782–7784,7799`.

Repro: enroll a site with a new tool; start its genuine first-use request and leave the Allow/Deny card pending; in Settings choose either site-wide **Reset decisions** or **Disable automatic use** while there are no stored matching decisions. The storage reset returns success without advancing the consent revision (`removed.length === 0`). The Settings route likewise computes no `affected` consent rows and skips `invalidateSiteToolWork`. Consequently the old card's exact ASK snapshot still matches, and a late Allow can save automatic-use authority and proceed after the reset.

This violates requirement 4 and the packet's explicit pending-card reset fence. Per-tool ASK reset correctly advances the revision even when no stored decision exists; the site-wide route does not.

Independent executable evidence (external probe, importing the candidate's real storage/tools modules with its in-memory OPFS fixture):

```sh
npm run test:file -- /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/eo4d-25acd467-review/reset-fence-probe.test.ts --filter 'review:'
```

- `all` reset: RED — expected `site_tool_consent_changed`, stale Allow instead succeeds; revision stays 0.
- `automatic` reset: RED — same failure and revision remains 0.
- Exact-tool ASK reset positive control: GREEN — the stale Allow is rejected.
- Result: **1 passed, 2 failed**, runner exit 1. These are assertion failures, not setup/tooling errors.
- Probe: `reset-fence-probe.test.ts`; output: `reset-fence-probe.log` in this report directory.

Required fix: make an explicit successful site reset establish a persisted invalidation boundary even if the materialized decision set is empty, and invalidate pending/in-flight work independent of the number of changed decision rows. Preserve sticky Deny for `automatic` mode. Add regression tests that observe these two stale-card cases fail before the fix and pass afterward, plus a loaded owner-action test showing the old card cannot dispatch/save consent after reset and a fresh use must ask again.

## Evidence checked and limitations

- Read-only diff/source review covered consent identity/revisions, sticky Deny, owner routes/resolver identity, audit store and production dispatch/publication seams, lazy authority, reset barriers, Settings/components, owner-local activity hydration, and associated tests.
- Exact candidate packet and current clean Git object verified. All **16** manifest-listed screenshot hashes and sizes match the supplied files.
- Personally inspected exact-candidate saved first-use/result and Settings light/dark/forced-colors/narrow/audit/final screenshots. The presentation and direct activity slice show substantial improvement over the historical r3 packet; this does not clear R1.
- Supplied logs checked: changed/full suite 3663/0; production build PASS; Chrome 369/370 with sole owned `dptw` expected-red; loaded WebMCP 137/0. These are implementer-run gates, not independent reruns here.
- Loaded acceptance manifest truthfully remains **OPEN / automated-variant**: the deep invocation branch uses pregranted permissions; fresh-profile picker/JIT uses shipped manifest. No claim of fully shipped-byte native-permission coverage.
- No Chrome launched under coordinator freeze. No source edits, commits, resets, amendments, or pushes performed in the candidate worktree.
- No second speculative concern is promoted to a finding. R1 alone requires REVISE.

## Disposition

**REVISE `25acd4671075f9a2291e3a9f953d2717e59587df`.** Preserve the immutable candidate; implement the correction in a new commit, refresh the relevant evidence, and request exact-object re-review through the coordinator.

Real storage regressions are RED on 25acd467 and GREEN on the fix. A loaded Settings reset while the first-use card is pending prevents the old card saving Allow or dispatching; fresh use asks again. Independent exact-object review and complete serial landing gates required.

# 11rm: reconcile the TAR carrier with the retained CAPX safety contract

**Scoping only — no implementation, runtime acceptance or closure.** Source anchor: fetched main `b590da1360328bf7a76e012a2aa813e4012dd047`. The [status inspection](/home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/11rm-status-20260918/REPORT.md) established that Settings still uses the capped JSON path. This report proposes the work boundary; it does not amend the old accepted artifacts or silently change the constitution.

## Recommendation

**Use one new user-facing format: streaming TAR with POSIX PAX extensions, driven outside the service worker. Carry forward the earlier target-admission, sanitization, integrity and recovery obligations, not CAPX's wire framing.** Keep v1 JSON import-only, but stream it into the same admitted/staged transaction path. Do not build both a new public TAR format and an unnecessary private CAPX intermediate merely to reuse an old parser.

The later 2g90 design governs the new carrier and Options-side data plane. It is not permission to drop the earlier security/transaction decisions. Conversely, the old r6 APIs/frame limits/frozen hashes are not requirements to recreate a retired orchestration or to emit CAPX forever. No released CAPX producer was found in the inspected product/checkpoints; supporting external CAPX backups would need a separate, evidenced requirement.

The smallest useful first implementation is **`chrome-agent-platform-11rm.1`: a backpressured TAR/PAX encoder**, without a decoder, profile access, sanitization, UI or live restore. The child is OPEN and unassigned; no build has started. It is a missing transport primitive with a stable contract independent of the unresolved transaction wiring. See [first sub-bead specification](/home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/11rm-scope-20260918/first-subbead.md). It unblocks creation of real TAR staging archives and independent reader fixtures; it does **not** by itself unblock shipping Export All, close 11rm, or satisfy dsnh.

## What changes, what survives

| Concern | Reconciliation |
|---|---|
| Carrier/context | Replace CAPX magic/frames/footer representation with a defined TAR/PAX backup profile. Bulk I/O and parsing stay in Options/a dedicated worker, not SW. Runtime messages carry bounded job metadata, never archive strings, base64 or whole target lists. |
| Large files and paths | Plain ustar has an 8,589,934,591-byte member limit and fixed name/prefix fields. Use standard per-file PAX `size`/`path` records, not another cap, truncation, or GNU-only numeric extension. Existing platform/owning-schema limits remain distinct from invented archive admission limits. |
| Integrity/completeness | Retain payload digests, ordered metadata/body integrity, exact counts/lengths, mandatory completion and trailing/truncation rejection. TAR's checksum covers its **header**, not payload. The later archive-profile stage must specify a bounded seal record and streaming/disk-backed per-entry verification; no giant manifest array. This is corruption/completeness evidence, not producer authentication. |
| Portable targets | Reuse current registry and owning validators. Re-census current writers rather than assume the Sep-6 census still covers main. Classify and obtain an awaited explicit successful duplicate claim before opening a destination sink. Unknown/authority/private targets fail closed; do not treat the doc's illustrative `opfs/` tree as an allowlist. Keep exact IDs, store integrity metadata and graph relationships. |
| Secrets/dsnh | The streamed path must execute classification plus exact sanitizer dispatch before bytes reach the sanitized destination spool/archive. Import revalidates/re-sanitizes; an archive's assertion that it is sanitized is not authority. Reuse the landed logical-site helper, recursive four-key policy and MCP/provider rules. Carry actual-local endpoint/agent-instance identity checks for any credential reattachment. Do not substitute the doc's obsolete object-valued MCP transport/headers example for the real schema. |
| Memory | State a bounded **working-buffer** contract, not a universal 64KiB total-RAM claim. Raw payloads/count/aggregate size have no new cap; source and sink obey backpressure. Disk-backed claims/indexes and one-entry metadata must be accounted for. Preserve the accepted r6 per-structured-value 10MiB and endpoint/native-parse compatibility limits, labelled accurately—not generalized to raw files. Do not assume a new PAX metadata policy from a CAPX framing limit. |
| Snapshot/export | Retain a verified cross-context writer barrier while producing a consistent, sanitized, immutable private snapshot; seal it, release the barrier, then copy the sealed archive to the owner's selected file. This adds a staged copy versus literal live-OPFS→slow-disk streaming, but avoids holding writers for the external download and avoids a mixed-time snapshot. Quota/I/O failures remain visible, never truncation or fallback to a whole Blob. |
| Restore | Validate/stage before live mutation; hold a verified all-writer barrier and seal exact rollback bytes **and prior absence**. Re-read intact live denials, compute/validate and durably retain the final multiset union **before any clear**. Apply through owning writers; retain protected local state, rederive/revoke use authority. Before commit, recover exact prior state; after durable commit, finish forward before writers resume. |
| v1 compatibility | Preserve streaming lexical/base64 decoding, strict Unicode/duplicate/accounting semantics and the accepted BOM rule. Route normalized entries into the same admission/seal/transaction engine. The doc's `file.text()`/legacy `parseArchive` fallback does not satisfy11rm and must not survive in the completed product. Detection must tolerate the admitted v1 whitespace/grammar, not just match a fixed16-byte literal. |
| Resume | Reuse proven journal **invariants and tests**, after adapting to the new carrier. CAPX frame-boundary cursor snapshots do not transfer verbatim. First safe implementation may replay an incomplete private attempt from its durable input; it must not invent a resumable TAR cursor or lose post-mutation recovery. A valid journal model alone is not a persistence adapter or barrier. |

## Corrections required before product integration

These belong to11rm's forward implementation plan, not to reopening closed helper beads:

1. **No claimed atomic multi-file swap.** File stream close/locks do not establish a transaction across OPFS, chrome.storage and alarms. Replace the three-phase sketch's blanket atomicity/error statement with the explicit recovery sequence above. A failure after the first live write cannot be described as “live profile untouched.”
2. **Cancel/invalidate is not an all-writer barrier.** The old census identified KV/direct-page writers, MemoryStore, workspaces, user-Wasm storage, grants and alarm/scheduler writes. Refresh that census on the implementation base, including pending writes and cross-context caches. A lock only works when every relevant writer participates; a durable gate is needed across context death. Source search found no implementation of the named archive/restore barriers on the inspected main.
3. **Budget is a gate, not a reason to omit coordination.** The 3,000,000-byte SW limit remains. The TAR doc simultaneously sketches new prepare/quiesce/commit messages and promises zero added SW bytes via route reuse. That exact-zero promise is not established. Keep payload code outside SW; measure any necessary authority integration, make a real budget-neutral refactor or escalate if it cannot fit. Do not weaken recovery or silently raise the budget. Old 106/350-byte headroom numbers are not current measurements.
4. **Seal/schema graph before trust.** Specify the TAR backup profile separately from the generic encoder: reserved member names, kind/target mapping, payload representation, per-entry digests and a final seal. Validate all metadata, duplicate targets and graph references before mutation. The reader accepts only that declared regular-file/PAX subset; it refuses link/device/sparse or other undefined extraction semantics. It is not a general filesystem extractor. A readable TAR, header checksum or size match is insufficient.
5. **Acceptance stays larger than the original limit.** The later doc's >100MiB KAT is insufficient for the original >512MiB requirement. The completed product needs real generated multi-file export→restore at ≥590MiB, including a binary member whose old base64 IPC representation exceeds the old message boundary; exact data/logical metadata, bounded buffers and no whole-message transport. Keep >100k entries as a separate streaming/count control rather than accidentally retaining that cap. Drive disk/quota errors, cancellation, late invalid input, interruption/recovery, deny races, credential mismatches and the dsnh planted-secret/unmanaged-target negatives.

## Work shape after the encoder

This is a dependency outline, not claims that these implementations already exist:

- **Encoder → sealed TAR staging/admission.** Define the backup profile, reuse SHA/classifier/sanitizer authorities, add disk-backed claims and normalized entry staging. This makes an inspectable archive, not a live restore. It supplies the streamed consumer for dsnh's redaction checks.
- **In parallel: current writer barrier + durable recovery engine.** Port only useful journal/state invariants from 776118f8, add real storage/boot adapters and writer coverage, and prove pre-clear safety. No dependence on TAR byte layout is needed to begin this authority work.
- **Profile/admission contract → strict TAR reader and streaming v1 adapter.** Both feed the same provisional staging/validation path. Raw decoder output never gets live write authority. No second, weaker legacy path.
- **Staging + barrier → owner export integration.** Genuine file-picking gesture, progress/cancel/error behavior, seal-before-copy, no IPC body. Only here does Settings leave the old export path.
- **Readers + barrier/recovery → owner restore integration.** Preview/confirm, exact rollback, safety merge, protected authority and postcommit recovery. Then execute the original large-profile acceptance and mutation controls.

`dsnh` can be checked against the same assembled candidate, but cannot close from the encoder/helper tests or from 8fuc's legacy walk. Do not reverse its existing dependency into a cycle: it currently waits on 11rm. The parent's own acceptance still requires credential exclusion before it is declared complete.

## Reuse and evidence limits

title: S4 call path: execute_tool runs an uploaded module from an agent run and returns its stdout
description:
Fourth stage of chrome-agent-platform-9ux7, and the stage that carries the epic. Today the WASI executor is reachable ONLY from the owner-only Settings preview (service-worker.js 'wasm.preview.run' + previewSpecFor's trusted spec map, executed in the options document). This stage gives it a route reachable from an agent run.

WHAT: dispatching a 'user-wasm-task' tool call fetches the module bytes from the S1 store by digest, builds the WASI job from the call arguments (stdin text + argv), runs it through the EXISTING extension/lib/wasm-executor.js (fresh Worker per call, no main-thread fallback, wall deadline) and returns stdout as the tool result. Reuse the executor and the offscreen/options host — do not write a second execution path; if the existing host cannot be reached from a background run, extend it rather than fork it, and say in the bead comments which one you extended.

NO ADMISSION BOUNDS: no size, imports or memory gate before the call. The wall deadline STAYS and is not an admission bound — it is what lets a runaway module be terminated and reported honestly rather than hanging the run forever. A module that traps, refuses to instantiate, or exceeds the deadline produces an honest tool error the model can read and retry against, never a silent empty result.

APPROVAL: an uploaded module runs under the normal tool-approval flow, unchanged. That is the standing consent model for tools, not a new bound introduced here.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW (k3, fresh qwen — a different model family from the
implementer, gemini) of dc90432a. VERDICT: **REVISE — do not land as-is.**

Not a quality judgement: the implementation is good, the gates reproduce exactly,
and the functional browser check passes 16/16. It cannot land because main moved
under it and the required resolution is a design decision with a security
consequence, not a merge chore.

━━ BLOCKING: does not rebase onto current main, and the conflict is SEMANTIC ━━
`git rebase origin/main` (c0a3e060) on dc90432a CONFLICTS in
extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js (and CHANGELOG.md). Cause: m6x8 landed a
+142/-29 GENERALIZATION of the very store this candidate extends, in the same
region — it replaced the `list()` area where this candidate inserts
`listUserWasmStore` and rewrites `list:` to delegate to it.

Main's store is now `createOwnerBlobStore` with:
  OWNER_BLOBS_ROOT = "cap-owner-blobs-v1" (neutral root), V1_ROOT =
  "cap-user-wasm-v1" (legacy + migration), OWNER_BLOB_KINDS =
  Object.freeze(["wasm","wheel"]) — a CLOSED set whose comment says ovfm (Python
  modules) extends it and it is the only sanctioned way to add a kind — every
  record carries `kind`, and `list()` returns ALL kinds.

This candidate's `listUserWasmStore` was written against the OLD wasm-only store:
it reads `USER_WASM_ROOT` (a constant that no longer exists on main) and returns
every record from `recover(root)` with NO KIND FILTER. So both naive resolutions
are wrong:
  • map USER_WASM_ROOT -> OWNER_BLOBS_ROOT and keep the body: EVERY owner blob is
    registered as an executable agent tool. Python wheels would appear in the
    tool catalog as sourceKind "user-wasm", carrying the WASI argv+stdin schema
    and dispatcherKind "user-wasm-task", surfaced through search_tools and
    selectable. A wheel is not a WASI command module; handing one to that
    dispatcher is at best a confusing failure and at worst an execution path
    nobody designed.
  • take main's side and drop listUserWasmStore: the SW's readUserWasmRows()
    import breaks, so S3 does not exist.
REQUIRED resolution: rebase `listUserWasmStore` onto the generalized store —
neutral root plus the v1 migration path main already implements — AND filter
`kind === "wasm"`. Preferred shape: make it kind-parameterized
(`listOwnerBlobs({ kind })`) so ovfm's Python modules get their own listing
instead of a second near-duplicate function, and the closed-kind-set invariant is
enforced in one place.

━━ gates, reproduced independently (not the implementer's numbers) ━━
Environment: real `npm ci`, then `deno install`, then `npm run build`. NOTE for
whoever maintains the onboarding docs: a fresh worktree now needs **npm ci AND
deno install AND npm run build** — build.mjs resolves the MCP SDK through
`node_modules/.deno` and refuses without it ("run deno install"). `npm ci` alone
crashes the build with ENOENT on node_modules/.deno.

━━ functional browser check, driven in REAL Chrome (the mandate) ━━

/home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/review-9ux7.3-browser-1788717572921 with four
screenshots (01-empty.png, 02-uploaded.png, 03a-confirm-dialog.png,

Real Chrome with the real built extension, real service worker registered, real

one is being relied on. Logs: cap-evidence/9ux7.3-review/mutation-*.log.

━━ other items, per coordinator rulings already issued ━━
  • Per-agent grants must be DIGEST-ONLY. `allowed.has(row.digest) ||
    allowed.has(row.name)` in liveChromeLazyRecords: the store's own documented
    semantics are "same name + different bytes = separate entries,
    disambiguated by full digest", so a name-based entry admits every same-name

    with the blocking item: on the generalized store, name matching is also how a

  • Digest binding boundary (accepted, to be recorded on the bead): the
    descriptor validation is FORMAT-only (`/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/`) and the store

  • Fail-silent layers: `listUserWasmStore` returns [] when OPFS or locks are
    unavailable and `readUserWasmRows` swallows every error to [], so a corrupted

    should surface owner-visibly, and unavailable-vs-empty should be
    distinguishable.
  • Positive note, verified: `buildToolCatalog` handles a throwing descriptor
    per-row (try/catch -> diagnostics.rejected), so ONE malformed user-wasm row

    that the rejection is silent to the owner.

# RE-REVIEW: 9ux7.3 @ 60a131b1 (rebased on c0a3e060)

**VERDICT: REVISE — not a PASS.** Merger should not land on this.

The rebase blocker is genuinely resolved and the RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR IS CORRECT —
verified in a real browser, 16/16, and both gates reproduce the implementer's
numbers exactly. But three of the four findings' fixes are NOT PINNED: each can
be reverted and the entire selected suite stays green. And the test added for
finding 3 is named "executes" while reading the service worker as text.

Code right, behaviour right, net still full of holes. The work left is small and
precisely specified below.

---

## Blocker from the first review: RESOLVED

`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main 60a131b1` → true. The revision contains
current main (c0a3e060) and is fast-forwardable; no conflict. The store is now
the generalized `createOwnerBlobStore`, `listOwnerBlobs({kind})` is the shared
listing, and `listUserWasmStore` is a one-line delegate to
`listOwnerBlobs({kind:"wasm"})` — the preferred shape I recommended, so ovfm's
Python modules get their own listing instead of a near-duplicate function.

## Finding 1 — kind filter: code CORRECT, **NOT PINNED**

Code level, verified:
- `store.list({kind})` validates `KINDS.has(kind)` (TypeError on an unknown kind)
  and filters `r.kind === kind` — so `kind:"wasm"` cannot return a wheel.
- `listOwnerBlobs({kind,storage,locks})` delegates to it; the SW calls
  `listOwnerBlobs({ kind: "wasm" })`.
- the adapter carries a second, defensive layer:
  `if (row?.kind && row.kind !== "wasm") continue;`

**Mutant M2** replaces the store's filter with `.filter(() => true)`, i.e. wheels
surface as executable wasm tools. Result: **SURVIVED** the whole selected suite,
0 failed. So the security guarantee coord and I both flagged as the reason this
candidate could not land has no test that fails when it is removed.

Minor note, not blocking: the adapter's defensive filter is `row?.kind && …`, so
a row with NO kind field passes through rather than being rejected. Directionally
that is the permissive choice. It is defensible for legacy v1 records, and the
store stamps `kind:"wasm"` on migration and validates kinds on read, so a kindless
row should not exist — but if the intent is "defensive", `row?.kind !== "wasm"`
is the fail-closed form.

## Finding 2 — digest-only grants: code CORRECT, **PINNED** (the one that held)

`allowed.has(row.digest)` only; the `|| allowed.has(row.name)` branch is gone, and
`userWasmRows` is now hoisted and computed once instead of twice.

**Mutant M3** re-adds `|| allowed.has(row.name)`. Result: **KILLED** —
"SW live records must enforce digest-only allowlisting (no row.name
allowlisting)". Finding 2 is closed.

Mechanism note for the record, not a objection: that pin is a source-text
assertion (`swCode.includes("allowed.has(row.digest)") &&
!swCode.includes("allowed.has(row.name)")`). It does kill the mutant, which is
what matters, but it is textual — it constrains the source, not the behaviour.

## Finding 3 — "EXECUTING test": **NOT FIXED**, and the name is the problem

The added test is `user-wasm catalog: service worker wiring executes and
imports correctly`. Its first line is:

    const swCode = await Deno.readTextFile(new URL("../extension/background/service-worker.js", import.meta.url));

Everything after that is `swCode.includes(...)` and windowed slices
(`indexOf("async function readShadowCatalogInputs")` + 4000 chars). **It executes
nothing.** The genuinely executing test in the revision — the
`ShadowToolCatalogController` one, which is good and does assert
`summary.toolsBySource["user-wasm"]` length 1 vs 0 with and without the adapter —
constructs the controller INSIDE THE TEST. It never touches the service worker,
so it cannot detect the service worker's wiring being dead.

**Proof, and it is the decisive result of this re-review.** Mutant **M1'** wraps
BOTH service-worker call sites in `false ? … : []`, leaving every pinned
substring byte-identical in place — `adaptUserWasmTools`,
`executableUserWasmToolRecords`, `listOwnerBlobs`, `allowed.has(row.digest)`, and
the windowed `adaptUserWasmTools(await readUserWasmRows()`. `node --check` exit
0, so it is valid JavaScript and a clean dead-code mutant, not a broken file.
Result: **SURVIVED — 692 passed / 0 failed across 58 selected files.** The
service worker can ship with user-wasm wiring that never runs, and S3 does not
exist, with the entire suite green.

I must also correct my own intermediate reading: an earlier, sloppier dead-code
mutant (M1) was KILLED, and I checked why before believing it. It was killed
*incidentally* — that mutant deleted the `allowed.has(row.digest)` text and so
tripped finding 2's source pin, not any execution check. Had I reported M1 as
"finding 3 fixed" I would have handed merger a false PASS. The mutant that
preserves the pinned text is the one that answers the question.

This is the third instance of the chartered theme, and the sharpest: a test whose
NAME asserts execution while its body reads text is worse than no test, because
it converts an open, known gap into a believed-closed one.

## Finding 4 — owner-visible diagnostics: code CORRECT, **NOT PINNED**

`readUserWasmRows` now catches and calls
`pushDiagnostic("error", "User Wasm catalog listing failed: …", "user-wasm",
"catalog")` before returning `[]`, so a storage failure is owner-visible and
distinguishable from an empty store. That is the right shape.

**Mutant M4** deletes the `pushDiagnostic` call (keeping `return []`). Result:
**SURVIVED**, 0 failed. The fail-silent layer can be restored without a test
noticing.

## Gates, reproduced independently on 60a131b1

Environment: fresh worktree, `npm ci` **and** `deno install` **and**
`npm run build` (the onboarding fact from the first review; skipping `deno
install` crashes the build with ENOENT on `node_modules/.deno`).

- `npm run build:production`: PASS — "store SW bundle **2980862** bytes <= 3000000
  budget" (19,138 bytes headroom). Matches the claimed 19 KB headroom; the built
  `extension/dist/background/service-worker.js` is 2,980,862 bytes on disk.
- `npm test`: PASS — serial phase (13 build/artifact files) GREEN 129/0, parallel
  phase (392 files) GREEN **3873 passed / 0 failed**, **405 files total**, wall
  111 s. Matches the claimed 3873/405 exactly.
- baseline `npm run test:changed` before any mutant: green, 22.1 s.
- every mutant applied from a pristine snapshot, restored and re-hashed after
  each, `git status --porcelain` empty at the end (verified: SW sha
  95faa4c6c010…, store sha 1e9c506579ce…).

## THE LANDING GATE — real browser re-run on 60a131b1: 16/16 GREEN

`cap-evidence/9ux7.3-r2/browser-check-r2.ts`, log `browser-check.log`, evidence
`/home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/review-9ux7.3-browser-1788718129923` with four
screenshots (01-empty, 02-uploaded, 03a-confirm-dialog, 03-deleted-no-reload).
My 16/16 on dc90432a was labelled pre-rebase and does not carry, so this was
re-run against the revision. Real Chrome, real built extension, real service
worker, real options UI, native file chooser
(`Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog` + `DOM.setFileInputFiles`) and REAL trusted
keyboard activation (`Input.dispatchKeyEvent` Enter) — a synthetic `.click()`
carries no user activation and Chrome never opens the chooser.

- committed save reported: "Saved “review module …” locally. Saving does not run
  it." (copy changed from "Uploading" to "Saving" in the revision)
- `listUserWasmStore()` returns exactly one row against REAL OPFS
- its digest is 64-hex **and equals the sha256 of the bytes actually written**,
  computed independently in Deno from the same 8-byte module
  (93a44bbb96c751218e4c00d479e4c14358122a389acca16205b1e4d0dc5f9476) — the
  write-time content hash is real and browser-verified
- owner name/description and the real size carried through; the Settings list
  shows the same digest
- the row's Remove control opens `dialog.cap-confirm-dialog`; removal asks for
  confirmation before destroying owner data
- after accepting: GONE from `listUserWasmStore()` with NO RELOAD, Settings list
  empty with NO RELOAD, navigation entries confirm no reload occurred

What the browser check still cannot prove, unchanged and stated rather than
hidden: `extension/lib/tool-catalog.js` imports the bare specifier `"ai"` and no
dist bundle re-exports the catalog functions, so
`adaptUserWasmTools → buildToolCatalog → buildToolSearchIndex` cannot be driven
from a browser context, and a model-issued `search_tools` needs a provider
credential. That is precisely the surface finding 3's executing test was supposed
to cover, and does not.

---

## REVISE list — small, precise, and all of it test work

1. **Rename or replace the misnamed test.** `service worker wiring executes and
   imports correctly` must not be named "executes" while it reads text. Either
   rename it honestly (e.g. "…is present in the service worker source") or make
   it actually execute.
2. **Close finding 3 for real.** The service worker is a bundle with side effects
   and cannot be imported by a unit test, so the practical shape is: extract the
   two wiring compositions into small exported functions in a lib module —
   e.g. `userWasmCatalogInputs(rows, {version, scope})` and
   `userWasmLazyRecords(rows, {agentTools, scope})` — have the SW call those, and
   execute THEM in a test (including the digest-only filter and the
   `false ?`-resistant assertion that the returned array is non-empty for a
   non-empty row list). That shrinks the dead-codeable surface in the SW to two
   one-line calls. If the SW call sites themselves still cannot be executed in a
   unit test, SAY SO on the bead and attach the browser evidence as the binding
   proof — do not let a text-reading test stand in for it.
   Acceptance: mutant M1' (both call sites dead-coded, all pinned substrings
   preserved, `node --check` clean) must be KILLED, or the bead must record that
   it is unkillable by unit test and why.
3. **Pin the kind filter (finding 1).** A test that puts a `kind:"wheel"` row in
   the store and asserts `listOwnerBlobs({kind:"wasm"})` excludes it, plus a
   direct adapter test that a wheel row handed to `adaptUserWasmTools` produces
   no descriptor. Acceptance: mutant M2 (`.filter(() => true)`) must be KILLED.
   This is the security surface — wheels surfacing as WASI command tools.
4. **Pin the diagnostic (finding 4).** A test that makes the listing throw and
   asserts the owner-visible diagnostic is pushed AND that the failure is
   distinguishable from an empty store. Acceptance: mutant M4 must be KILLED.
5. Consider making the adapter's defensive filter fail closed
   (`row?.kind !== "wasm"`) rather than permissive toward a missing kind.

Everything else in the revision is sound and should not be touched.

## Evidence

# THIRD-PASS REVIEW: 9ux7.3 @ b5cbef3a — **VERDICT: PASS**

Reviewer: k3 (fresh qwen), independent of the implementer (gemini/cap-arch-docs).
Merger may land on this PASS. Two non-blocking notes at the end; neither is a
condition of landing.

Ancestry verified first, per the rule this review earned:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main b5cbef3a` → **true**. The revision
contains current main (`eb86cb52`) and is fast-forwardable, so its gates describe
a tree that can actually land.

---

## All five r2 items are addressed, and I verified each by RE-BREAKING it

I did not accept the implementer's reproof table. The implementer ran MY r2
harness, which encodes `M1` — the sloppy dead-code mutant that was only ever
killed incidentally in r2 (it deleted the `allowed.has(row.digest)` text and so
tripped a different finding's pin). The mutant that answers the question is the
text-preserving one. So I rebuilt the mutants and ran them myself in a fresh
worktree (`npm ci` + `deno install` + `npm run build`), pristine snapshot per
file, restore + re-hash + empty `git status` after every one.

| mutant | what it restores | result |
|---|---|---|
| **M1'** `false ? … : []`, every pinned substring byte-identical, `node --check` exit 0 | the r2 finding: SW wiring present but never executed | **KILLED** |
| **M1''** `true ? [] : CALL` — call in the ELSE branch, so the blacklist regex for `false ?` cannot match | an idiom added *after* the pin was written | **KILLED** |
| **M2** store `.filter(() => true)` | wheels surface as executable wasm tools | **KILLED** |
| **M3** re-add `\|\| allowed.has(row.name)` in the extracted `userWasmLazyRecords` | name-based per-agent grants | **KILLED** (2 tests) |
| **M4** delete the `pushDiagnostic(…)` call, keep `return []` | the fail-silent layer | **KILLED** |
| **M1''''** `.slice(0, 0)` on the projection — spread literal intact, no `false ?`, no global oracle | adversarial projection-emptying | **SURVIVED** (full 406-file suite, 0 failed) — see note 1 |

Kill messages, so the pins are auditable rather than merely green:
- M1' → "shadow catalog inputs must spread userWasmCatalogInputs/adaptUserWasmTools"
- M2 → "list({ kind: 'wasm' }) must return only wasm blobs and exclude wheels"
  (in `tests/user-wasm-store.test.ts`, a real executing store test)
- M3 → "name-based grant must be rejected — grants are digest-only" (a new
  dedicated test) plus the source pin
- M4 → "service-worker must push error diagnostic on User Wasm catalog listing failure"

### Item-by-item

1. **Honest renaming — done.** The test no longer claims to execute. It is now
   `service worker calls are active and not dead-coded (M1/M1' guard)`. It is
   still a source-text pin and says so by its assertions. See note 1 on the
   residual overclaim in "not dead-coded".
2. **Extraction + executing tests — done properly, and this is the substantive
   fix.** `userWasmCatalogInputs(rows, context)` in `extension/lib/tool-catalog.js`
   and `userWasmLazyRecords(rows, {agentTools, scope})` in
   `extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js` are exported and IMPORTED AND EXECUTED
   by dedicated tests (`tests/tool-catalog-user-wasm.test.ts` lines 9, 18, 76,
   117). The service worker's surface is now two one-line spreads (lines 1912 and
   4435) — exactly the shrinkage I asked for, so the semantics are executed and
   only the two spreads remain text-pinned. `userWasmLazyRecords` verified
   digest-only at code level: `(rows || []).filter((row) => allowed.has(row.digest))`
   with no name branch anywhere.
3. **Kind filter pinned — done.** The store's `list({kind})` validates
   `KINDS.has(kind)` and filters `r.kind === kind`; `listOwnerBlobs({kind})`
   delegates; the SW calls `listOwnerBlobs({ kind: "wasm" })`; and M2 is now
   killed by a real executing store test that puts a wheel in the store.
4. **Diagnostic pinned — done.** `readUserWasmRows` catches and pushes an
   owner-visible `pushDiagnostic("error", "User Wasm catalog listing failed: …",
   "user-wasm", "catalog")`, and M4 is killed.
5. **Adapter fail-closed — done.** `extension/lib/tool-catalog.js:741` is now
   `if (row?.kind !== "wasm") continue;` so a kindless row is dropped rather than
   admitted.

### An unexpected extra defence, found by accident and worth recording

My first attempt at the ELSE-branch bypass used `globalThis.__cap_never_defined__`
as the falsy condition. It was killed — not by a user-wasm test but by the BUILD:

    Error: shipped-code scan failed (1 violation(s)):
      - extension/background/service-worker.js: accesses
        `globalThis["__cap_never_defined__"]` (test oracle)

`build.mjs` refuses to ship code containing test oracles. That is a real,
existing layer I did not know about, and it independently blocks a whole family
of adversarial mutants. Credit where due.

## Gates, reproduced independently on b5cbef3a

Unchanged limitation, stated not hidden: `tool-catalog.js` imports the bare

from a browser context, and a model-issued `search_tools` needs a provider

adapter→catalog→search chain is bound by the candidate's executing unit tests

## NOTE 1 (non-blocking) — the residual, stated precisely so nobody over-trusts the pin

`M1''''` SURVIVES the full 406-file suite: appending `.slice(0, 0)` to the
projection keeps the `...userWasmCatalogInputs(` spread literal intact (so the
includes-pin passes), contains no `false ?` (so the blacklist passes), and uses
no global oracle (so the shipped-code scanner passes) — while guaranteeing the
catalog gets nothing. Valid JS, `node --check` exit 0.

This is NOT a reason to hold the candidate, for three reasons: (a) no source-text
pin can establish execution — that is a property of the technique, not a defect
of this pin; (b) it is adversarial rather than realistic — the accidental
regression modes (deleting the call, constant-condition dead-coding in either
branch shape) are all killed, as proven above; (c) the semantics ARE executed via
the extracted functions, so what remains unexecuted is two one-line spreads.

Two small asks, both cheap, neither a landing condition:
- Scope the test name to what it establishes — e.g. "…are present as active
  spreads and not constant-condition dead-coded" — since "not dead-coded" reads
  as absolute and M1'''' is dead in effect while passing every assertion.
- Record the residual on the bead: the SW call sites are pinned against deletion
  and constant-condition bypass, the executable semantics live in
  `userWasmCatalogInputs`/`userWasmLazyRecords` unit tests, and the binding proof
  that the SW path runs end to end is the real-browser evidence

  r2 item 2 allowed for, and writing it down is what stops the next reader
  assuming the text pin proves execution.

## NOTE 2 (non-blocking, already ruled) — the digest boundary

Unchanged from r2 and already ruled by coord: the descriptor validation is
FORMAT-only (`/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/`) and the store verifies SIZE on read, not
content. The write-time content hash is real and browser-verified above. S3's
guarantee is write-time-hash + size-on-read; the content re-hash pre-instantiate
belongs to 9ux7.4's acceptance so S4 does not assume a binding it does not have.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-USER-WASM-UI-01] S2 add and remove uploaded WebAssembly files in Settings
description:
Second stage of chrome-agent-platform-9ux7. The owner-facing surface over the S1 store.

WHAT: a Settings section (Tool library is the natural home) that lets the owner pick a .wasm file, give it a NAME and a DESCRIPTION, and see what is installed with a Remove control per row. The description field must say plainly that this text is what the agent reads to decide when to call the tool — that is the single most important field on the form and users will not guess it.

NO ADMISSION BOUNDS: the picker accepts any .wasm the owner chooses. No size warning that blocks, no imports preview that refuses. If something about the module is worth SHOWING (its size, the imports it declares), show it as information, never as a gate.

DESIGN: every piece of UI is a reusable Web Component in extension/shared/components.js and appears in docs/components.html (check:gallery fails on drift). No emoji icons — inline SVG, currentColor. Untrusted text (the filename, anything read out of the module) renders with textContent, never innerHTML.

ACCEPTANCE: in a real loaded extension, pick a real .wasm, name it, describe it, see it listed; reload Settings and it is still listed; Remove takes it away and it stays gone after reload. Assert the CONTENT of the list (rows, the name the owner typed), never merely that a panel is visible — that blind spot is chrome-agent-platform-rfca and it is exactly how a P0 shipped green.

FILES: extension/options/options.html + options.js, extension/shared/components.js, docs/components.html, scripts/kat-* for the browser proof.
DEPENDS ON: S1 (the store).
OUT OF SCOPE: making the tool callable (S3/S4).

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-USER-WASM-STORE-01] S1 user-wasm store: digest-keyed unbounded OPFS with owner metadata
description:
First stage of chrome-agent-platform-9ux7. A pure-ish module plus its OPFS backing that holds user-supplied Wasm modules; no UI, no catalog, no execution.

WHAT: extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js — put(bytes, {name, description}), list(), get(digest), remove(digest). The key is the sha256 of the bytes (same identity scheme the bundled CAS uses, so digests are comparable across both tranches). Metadata: owner-written name, owner-written description (this is the text the MODEL sees, so it is product copy, not a filename), byte size, added-at, and the digest.

NO ADMISSION BOUNDS (owner decision on the epic): no size cap, no imports inspection, no memory tier, no refusal on a module that fails to parse — a module that will not instantiate is a call-time failure with an honest error, not an upload-time rejection. Storage failures (OPFS quota) surface the browser's own honest error; never a silent truncation and never a cap invented here.

WHY OPFS rather than chrome.storage: modules are megabytes; chrome.storage.local is the wrong shape and the repo already has OPFS helpers (extension/lib/opfs-tool-workspace.js) to follow for directory handling and error language.

ACCEPTANCE: round-trip a multi-megabyte module through put/get and get identical bytes back; two puts of the SAME bytes with different names do not duplicate the stored bytes (one CAS entry, and the second put is honest about which name won); list() returns metadata without reading the bytes; remove() deletes both the entry and its bytes. Falsification: break the digest computation, watch the round-trip test go red, restore.

FILES: extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js (new), tests/user-wasm-store.test.ts (new).
OUT OF SCOPE: the upload UI (S2), catalog registration (S3), execution (S4).
notes: TRANSFERRED to astra: S1 user-wasm store — digest-keyed OPFS, owner metadata (name/description), no admission gates, no size caps, duplicate-name semantics explicit, Web Locks for cross-context serialization, bytes never ride messaging JSON (64MiB limit) — stream/file-backed.

DESIGN INTENT vs cap-evidence/claude/4p7j-analysis.md (which asks for ONE shared owner-blob store, 'with 9ux7.1, not beside it'; S1 of that plan is literally 'Shared owner-blob store'):
- Behaviorally shared ALREADY: record {version,digest,name,description,size,addedAt} with no wasm-specific fields; verbs put/list/getFile/remove; ZERO admission gates (no size/count cap, no \0asm magic check, no parse/compile at upload) so a Python wheel is as acceptable as a module; digests comparable to the bundled CAS (both sha256 hex over the bytes; tests cross-check against crypto.subtle at :84).
- Nominally wasm-bound in three places: USER_WASM_ROOT='cap-user-wasm-v1'; DATA/temp/PENDING pin '<digest>.wasm' (a wheel would be stored as .wasm and anything sniffing by extension mis-handles a zip); createUserWasmStore + 'user-wasm' error copy.
- FINDING R1 (decision needed before ovfm starts): generalize now — neutral root, <digest>.bin, a kind field, neutral copy — plus an explicit TESTED migration for the v1 root, because owner data already exists on disk under it and the store already has five consumers on main (user-wasm-store-client.js, user-wasm-store-worker.js, options/user-wasm-panel.js, scripts/kat-user-wasm-store.ts, tests/user-wasm-ui.test.ts). The version:1 field and -v1 suffix make this a clean v2. Cost now: one file's constants + five consumers + a migration. Cost after ovfm/S4: two stores with one bug surface each — the outcome 4p7j calls 'the real mistake'. NOT a defect in the implementation: this bead specified a wasm store and that is what was built, correctly.
- FINDING R2 (scaling; will bite the SHARED store): run() calls recover(root) on EVERY operation under one origin-wide Web Lock — full directory enumeration plus JSON.parse of every metadata file. So getFile(digest), the read path S4 execution and 4p7j's per-run wheel materialization would use, pays a full scan per wheel; and put holds the lock for the entire byte stream (a 65 MiB upload blocks a concurrent Settings list()). Correct but coarse, and with the owner's no-bounds decision the cost grows with total entries. Direction: recover once per lock acquisition or only for list(); single-record reads for get/remove; shorter put critical section (stream bytes outside the lock, publish metadata under it — the design already publishes last, so the invariant survives).
- FINDING R3 (minor/API): the bead asked for get(digest), the store ships getFile(digest); the 'honest about which name won' signal is implicit (the caller infers replacement from the returned record) — an explicit replaced/previousName would let S2's UI say 'this replaced the name on an existing file'; put requires a Blob, so a wheel installer holding bytes in memory must wrap them.

QUALITY: no correctness defect found. Publication is last (bytes moved before metadata); empty metadata is treated as an unpublished upload (the getFileHandle(create:true) trap); delete intent is durable and completed on reopen; metadata-without-bytes fails closed; orphan bytes are pruned; digests are pinned to /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ with a traversal test; names are metadata never paths (Unicode covered); bytes never ride messaging JSON (>64 MiB tested without whole-file allocation, input streamed without arrayBuffer); two store instances serialize put/remove without lost updates; duplicate and same-name semantics match the bead. 18 tests cover the acceptance list and the crash-consistency matrix; the bead's falsification requirement is satisfied in substance by the native-SHA cross-check.
Tests I would add if R1/R2 are taken: a legacy-root migration test, a kind round-trip, and an assertion that get/remove do NOT enumerate the directory (that property would fail today, which is the point of pinning it).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ANALYSIS + DESIGN COMPLETE — /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/claude/4p7j-analysis.md (413 lines), marked FINAL: READY FOR REVIEW. Analysis stage only; no product code written.

Grounded in origin/main@5b128f12 and, where it mattered, in MEASUREMENT rather than code reading: six probe runs through the real python.execute route in a loaded extension (harness in the session scratchpad, analysis-only).

WHAT THE PROBE SETTLED:
- loadPackage FAILS SILENTLY — micropip before:False, 'returned without raising', after:False, ModuleNotFoundError. It neither installs nor throws. Any install path built on it must verify the import afterwards or it reports success over a no-op. This is the finding that shapes the design.
- The offline property HOLDS: loadPackage reaches no CDN (numpy never arrives; the local wheel URL 404s). My first reading of the micropip result was that it had silently used the network — that was WRONG and the doc records the corrected finding.
- The offline install spine is PROVEN by two independent mechanisms: a plain FS write into /lib/python3.12/site-packages, and unpackArchive from an in-memory zip. Both imported successfully in-run. S2 is wiring, not research.
- Ambient fetch is CONFIRMED: import js exposes fetch/XHR/WebSocket/EventSource/importScripts/Worker/indexedDB/caches, the worker holds the chrome-extension origin, and a real cross-origin request returned status 404 — i.e. it left the browser. Model-authored Python under python_execute can exfiltrate today, independent of this bead.
- Fresh-interpreter-per-run confirmed empirically (a global set in one run reads back None in the next), so the persistence question is real.

DESIGN POSITIONS:
- Pinning/provenance for the 310 official packages is ALREADY SOLVED in-repo: pyodide-lock.json ships with sha256 per package and is itself hash-pinned and re-verified at runtime. We ship the index and no wheels — the gap is payloads, not trust.
- QUOTAS: none, deliberately. EXECUTOR_BOUNDS already sets every byte ceiling to Infinity (dptw), Paul's 'no bounded admission' applies, xzp2 says don't cap, and the extension is not store-hosted. Time bounds stay and are named as time, not size.
- PERSISTENCE is the open decision (Option A re-install per run / B warm interpreter / C snapshot the installed FS). I recommend C and flag it as the least-verified claim in the doc.
- JS MODULES should be split into their own bead: sandbox/script-sandbox.html already gives them BETTER isolation than Python has (host-bridged fetch vs ambient), so it is a module-resolution problem, not a payload one.
- The wheel store should SHARE the digest-keyed OPFS store being built for 9ux7.1 rather than be a second store.

FOUR QUESTIONS FOR PAUL are in §10; §12 states what I am least sure of.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
OWNER DECISIONS RECORDED — analysis §10 rewritten from questions into answers, plus a new §10.2b for the proxy refinement. Doc now 559 lines, still FINAL: READY FOR REVIEW.

1. ISOLATION: Option C — fresh-per-run REQUIRED, persist installed FILES not the interpreter. This also RESOLVED the biggest uncertainty I had flagged in §12, in the owner's favour: I had worried Option C depended on Pyodide 0.26.4 FS-snapshot support I had not verified. It does not. Probe N2 already proved that writing files into /lib/python3.12/site-packages and importing them works, so 'persist installed files' is implementable today as materialize-the-stored-tree-into-each-fresh-interpreter. No snapshot API, no research stage. The residual unknown is per-run materialization COST against the 30 s budget — an S4 measurement, not a design risk.

2. FETCH: S0 strips the ambient globals at PYTHON WORKER SCOPE ONLY; extension-level requests untouched (explicitly including python-host.js's own fetch of the pinned runtime bytes, which runs in the host and must keep working or the runtime cannot be verified). Filed as 4p7j.1 with that boundary written into the bead for the code comment.

3. Then Paul refined it: model-authored code KEEPS network access, but only under a permission grant, via a proxy. Designed as §10.2b and filed as 4p7j.2 (S0.5): Python cap.fetch shim -> postMessage -> service worker as the ONLY network actor, per-origin allowlist grants in Settings, optional first-use prompt, every request AND every refusal logged to the transcript.

   FLAGGED FOR REVIEW on that stage: the SW holds <all_urls> AND the owner's ambient cookies, so a naive fetch(url) in the proxy would issue AUTHENTICATED requests — a grant saying 'example.com is allowed' could read the owner's logged-in session there. Required defaults are in the bead: credentials 'omit' always, redirect 'manual' with re-check against the allowlist (redirect chains are how an allowlist gets laundered), http(s) only, and caller-controlled Cookie/Authorization stripped. Also recorded honestly: the shim is awaitable-only, so requests/urllib cannot be offered this way and must fail with a message pointing at cap.fetch rather than pretending.

4. JS MODULES: split to chrome-agent-platform-ovfm, depending on the shared blob store.

5. OFFICIAL WHEELS: vendored and always preferred; resolution order vendored-official -> owner-supplied, so an upload never silently shadows an official package. Which packages to vendor is an S3 measurement, not a guess — 'all 310' is likely tens of MB and the honest first cut is what the owner asks for.

4p7j.1 blocks 4p7j.2. Analysis stage complete; no product code written.
