title: [CAP-FB-20260905-USER-WASM-UPLOAD-01] User-uploaded WebAssembly tools: upload + call path
description:
EPIC. Paul (2026-09-05): users upload their OWN .wasm modules and they become callable tools, like the bundled ones. Owner decisions ON RECORD for this epic: NO BOUNDED ADMISSION (no size cap, no imports allowlist gate, no memory-tier gate, no admission refusal) and NO WEB STORE (the extension is not store-hosted, so store-policy/remote-code compliance does not constrain this path). Where a bound is load-bearing for correctness rather than policy — a wall-clock deadline that lets a runaway module be terminated — keep it and say so honestly; never reintroduce an admission gate under another name.

WHERE THE CODE STANDS (read before implementing): there IS a real WASI execution path — extension/lib/wasm-executor.js (fresh Worker per call, no main-thread fallback, wall deadline, one-way transport), extension/lib/wasm-execution-worker.js, extension/lib/wasm-sync-workspace.js, extension/lib/wasm-offscreen-host.js. It is reachable ONLY from the owner-only Settings preview route: service-worker.js 'wasm.preview.run' resolves toolId through a TRUSTED SPEC MAP (previewSpecFor), fetches a pinned bundled manifest + CAS bytes from extension/wasm/, and executes in the options document. extension/lib/bundled-tool-packages.js ships every descriptor admitted:false/disabled:true with disabledReason 'no-execution-host' and states outright that nothing there registers a tool in the live catalog. tool-catalog.js already reserves sourceKind 'bundled-package' and dispatcherKind 'bundled-wasm-task' (adaptBundledTools), unused live.

So this epic is what makes Wasm tools LIVE — for user-supplied modules — and it necessarily builds the piece the bundled tranche is also waiting on: a real execution route reachable from an agent run rather than from Settings only.

ACCEPTANCE FOR THE EPIC: a user picks a .wasm file in Settings, gives it a name and a description, and an agent run can then find it via search_tools and call it via execute_tool, with its stdout coming back as the tool result — proven end to end in a real loaded extension with a genuinely user-supplied module (not a bundled one), at a size and with imports that no admission gate would have had to approve.

title: Show thinking tokens in the conversation when the provider streams them — collapsible trace under the thinking indicator
description:
Owner feature request 2026-09-03: when an agent is thinking, the user wants to see the actual thinking tokens streaming from the provider (available from Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, and other models that expose chain-of-thought). Currently these tokens are either hidden or discarded. The user wants a collapsible dropdown under the 'thinking...' indicator that shows the thinking trace in real time as tokens arrive.

DESIGN:
- The conversation's run-status surface (the existing 'thinking...' indicator) gains a expandable section when thinking tokens are available from the provider
- Tokens stream in real time (same streaming mechanism as the response text)
- The section is collapsed by default; the user clicks to expand and see the live trace
- When thinking finishes, the section collapses and the response begins
- If the provider doesn't send thinking tokens, the section doesn't appear at all

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. The provider layer (models/*.js) already receives thinking tokens in the stream (reasoning_content, thinking blocks, etc.) — currently these are discarded or logged. Capture them and emit them as a new event type (e.g. 'thinking-token') through the existing streaming pipeline.
2. The conversation component (shared/conversation.js) receives the thinking stream and renders it in a collapsible section under the thinking indicator.
3. The collapsible section: collapsed by default, click-to-expand, live-streaming text inside, auto-scroll to bottom while expanded.
4. Provider-specific handling: Gemini (thought parts), Claude (thinking blocks), DeepSeek (reasoning_content field), OpenAI (if available).
5. The thinking trace is NOT persisted in the thread after the run completes — it's a live-streaming view only (unless the owner wants it saved, which is a follow-up).

ACCEPTANCE: a Gemini/Claude task with extended thinking shows the thinking trace streaming in the collapsible section; a task without thinking tokens shows no section; the trace is live (tokens appear as they arrive, not all at once); the section collapses when thinking ends; falsification-gated.

title: Settings tool library shows 0 site tools (declared/inferred) — the shadow catalog reads hub scope and never includes per-origin WebMCP tools
description:
Owner report 2026-09-03: 'Site tools (declared)' in Settings shows 0 when browsing sites that have declared WebMCP endpoints (e.g. beads.gascity.com declares search_docs and open_skill). The content script discovers and reports them (tools-reported log confirms), but the Settings tool library never shows them.

ROOT CAUSE: readShadowCatalogInputs() (service-worker.js:3592) builds the shadow catalog from HUB-scope sources only: builtin tools, browser tools, management tools, and bundled packages. The per-origin WebMCP declared/inferred tools — which live in per-origin site toolsets built by siteToolset(origin, runGenCell) — are NEVER included because they exist only in per-origin contexts, not at the hub scope.

FIX: aggregate WebMCP declared/inferred tools across ALL enrolled origins and include them in the shadow catalog inputs under the 'webmcp-declared' and 'webmcp-inferred' source kinds. Each row should show the origin it belongs to (e.g. 'search_docs — beads.gascity.com') so the owner can see which sites have declared tools. The catalog already has the source kinds ('webmcp-declared', 'webmcp-inferred') in TOOL_SOURCE_KINDS — the data just never reaches it.

ACCEPTANCE: browse a site with declared WebMCP tools → Settings tool library shows them under 'Site tools (declared)' with the origin; browse a site with inferred tools → shows under 'Site tools (inferred)'; multiple origins' tools are aggregated; no tools → count is 0 (honest).
close_reason: Fixed on origin/cap-tool-library-sitetools-lmk2 @ b55f0380 (v0.3.66). TRUE root cause (different from the bead's description): the shadow catalog's origin loop existed since 08-22, but dptw removed TOOL_CATALOG_BOUNDS.maxDescriptors on 09-03 and the loop kept computing it — undefined*2 = NaN, slice(0, NaN) = [], so EVERY origin's declared/inferred tools were silently dropped and Settings showed 0. Fixed: removed the dead bound arithmetic (dptw: no size caps), added origin labels to summary rows (descriptor.scope.origin, bounded 2048), UI renders the site per row. Gates: new harness 5/0 (byte-faithful loop mirror proved RED=undefined counts before, GREEN after), related suites 33/0 + 17/0, full suite 342 files GREEN, build RC=0. Browser-journey residual (beads.gascity.com live browse) noted — unit chain is proven end-to-end.

title: Provider server tools toggle resets on reload — the init code is in renderAgents() but the toggle lives in the providers section (broken by multi-section navigation)
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-03: 'provider server tools' is not set on reload. The multi-section navigation change (0181699e) introduced ensureSectionRendered() which lazily mounts section renderers. The server-tools init code (state load + toggle listener + renderServerToolAgents) lives inside renderAgents() (line 1303) which is called by ensureSectionRendered('agents') — but the server-tools toggle HTML (#server-tools-enabled) is in the PROVIDERS section. On page reload, navigating to providers calls renderProviders() which doesn't touch server tools — the toggle stays unchecked even though the setting was persisted.

FIX: extract the server-tools init into its own function (initProviderServerTools) and call it from ensureSectionRendered('providers') alongside renderProviders(). Ensure renderAgents() no longer double-initializes it (guard with a flag or move the init entirely out of renderAgents()).

ACCEPTANCE: reload the page → navigate to Providers → the server tools toggle shows the persisted state; toggling saves and the state persists across reload; agents section still renders correctly.

title: Site-agent search_docs on beads.gascity.com still throws opaque 'DOMException: UnknownError' — and the agent needs a docs-fallback path when site tools fail
description:
Owner follow-up 2026-09-03 (after the ajcc fix landed @ 89f91ccb): invoking search_docs/open_skill on beads.gascity.com via @-mention STILL returns 'DOMException: UnknownError (an internal exception in the documentation site's client-side search/storage engine)' with no useful diagnostics. Two problems:

1. THE OPAQUE ERROR PERSISTS: ajcc fixed the redaction/classification layer, but the error the owner sees is still the raw DOMException from the PAGE-SIDE dispatcher — our extension is relaying the page's own error honestly, but the page's handler throws unhelpfully. Diagnose WHY the page-side handler throws: is it the site's localStorage/IndexedDB in a restricted context, a CORS/CSP issue on the beads.gascity.com side, the WebMCP dispatch layer unavailable in this Chromium, or our bridge mangling the call? Instrument the dispatch boundary (per ajcc's honest-errors work) and capture the actual page-side stack.

2. THE AGENT NEEDS A DOCS FALLBACK: when a site's declared tools fail, the agent should have a fallback — fetch the site's documentation directly (https://beads.gascity.com has a well-structured docs site: /core-concepts, /workflows, /getting-started/quickstart, /cli-reference) via the platform's fetch/read-page tools, and answer from that. The agent should TRY the site's tools first, and on failure FALL BACK to fetching the docs page — not just report failure.

3. THE REAL ROOT CAUSE: the site declares WebMCP tools (search_docs, open_skill) but Chrome's native WebMCP dispatch may be unavailable in this Chromium build (no document.modelContext even with flags — per ajcc's investigation). If that's confirmed, the error should say exactly that ('this site declares WebMCP tools but your browser does not currently expose the WebMCP dispatch layer — open the page directly or fetch its documentation instead').

ACCEPTANCE: (a) instrumented repro against beads.gascity.com capturing the real page-side error; (b) the honest error names the actual cause; (c) a fallback path: agent fetches https://beads.gascity.com docs pages and answers the owner's question even when search_docs fails; (d) falsification tests for the fallback trigger (search_docs fails → fetch fires) and the honest error content.

title: Task composer: steer (redirect/stop the running agent) and queue (enqueue follow-up messages like the pi framework)
description:
Owner feature request 2026-09-03: when a task is queued or the owner replies while an agent is RUNNING, the composer should offer the two interactions the pi framework does well:

1. STEER — reply to the RUNNING agent and redirect it live: the new message is injected into the in-flight run (the agent sees it as guidance and adjusts course). Optionally with force options: steer-gently (inject as context), steer-and-stop-current-step, or stop-the-run outright. The pi model: typing while running steers; nothing is lost.
2. QUEUE — enqueue follow-up messages that the agent processes AFTER the current turn/run completes (a real queue with visible pending items: '2 queued messages', reorderable/removable before they fire). Today a queued message either races the run or is lost.

REQUIREMENTS:
- The composer detects a running task and offers both affordances explicitly (Send-now-stop / Steer / Queue) with keyboard shortcuts.
- Steered messages appear in the transcript as owner interruptions with their own visual treatment; queued messages appear as pending chips above the composer.
- Steer plumbing exists at the run level (the agent-worker architecture has the message ports — extend the protocol with a steer control message the run loop honors between steps).
- Queue plumbing: per-thread FIFO drained at run end, persisted across reloads (the durable run journal already stores thread state — reuse it).
- Falsification tests: steer mid-tool-call changes the agent's next action (fixture agent asserts the steering message arrived between steps); queue-while-running fires messages in order after completion and survives reload; stop-the-run cancels cleanly (no orphaned durable run).
- Works for named agents, background agents, and site agents alike (one protocol, all surfaces).
notes: Landed on branch cap-beads-afiu @ a8a92b31 (not merged to main). Steer+queue implemented: lib/run-control.js control plane (live-run steer store + durable per-thread kv FIFO), between-step model-seam injection in lib/agent.js + lib/agent-loop.js (fixture-verified: steer mid-tool-call changes the agent's next action; stop-step ends the loop at the next step boundary; stop-run never injected as text), agent-worker:steer protocol route, run.control.* owner-gated SW routes, NTP composer Steer/Queue/Send-now bar + persisted reorderable/removable pending chips, steer bubbles rendered as owner interruptions, drain-one-item-per-settled-run queue firing. Gates: npm run build green; deno test tests/ = 3187 passed / 0 failed. Not yet browser-journey verified (that is the merge coordinator's gate).

title: Generated sandboxed UI artifacts use unavailable APIs (localStorage etc.) — the agent must KNOW the sandbox constraints, and runtime errors must teach rather than just throw
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-03: generated interactive artifacts (games/UI) run in a srcdoc sandbox WITHOUT allow-same-origin, so localStorage, sessionStorage, and other storage/permission-gated APIs are UNAVAILABLE — the agent keeps generating code that uses them, and the artifacts break at runtime ('guarded fallbacks' throw on restricted permissions). The agent has no way to know, so it makes the same mistake every time.

WORK:
1. TELL THE AGENT UP FRONT: the create_asset/append tool schema + the generating system prompt gain an explicit constraint block: 'the artifact runs in an origin-opaque sandbox: no localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies; no cross-origin fetches without CORS; no permission-gated APIs. Persist state IN-MEMORY in the artifact, or ask the platform to store data for you.' Keep it bounded (schema description, not a prompt essay).
2. RUNTIME ERRORS THAT TEACH: the sandbox error path currently surfaces raw DOMExceptions ('SecurityError: The document is sandboxed...'). Wrap/guard the known-broken API surfaces so the thrown error says WHAT to do instead: 'localStorage is unavailable inside sandboxed artifacts — keep state in a variable, or store it with the platform's asset/memory tools.' The error text is the teaching moment at exactly the moment of failure.
3. BLOB/PLATFORM ALTERNATIVES (evaluate, don't guess): where persistence is genuinely needed, evaluate (a) in-memory + export/import affordances, (b) the platform's asset tools as the persistence layer (agent writes state snapshots via append/asset tools), (c) OPFS-in-sandbox viability. Recommend one with evidence in the bead; do not build all three.
4. EVAL HARNESS: extend the artifact generation evals with a case asserting the composed guidance reaches the model and a fixture generation avoids localStorage (falsification: guidance removed → the fixture generation using localStorage must be flagged by the eval's checker).
Related: chrome-agent-platform-dptw (no-limits sweep), chrome-agent-platform-ajcc (site-tool honest errors).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED on origin/cap-beads-np64 @ 2cf8f5ec (pushed 2026-09-03). Three layers + eval:

(1) THE AGENT IS TOLD UP FRONT — constraint block added to BOTH carriers:
    - Tool schemas (extension/lib/management-tools.js): create_asset, generate_ui carry the full block ("origin-opaque sandbox: NO localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies, NO network, NO permission-gated APIs — keep state IN-MEMORY or store state with the platform (a saved-state artifact/memory key)"); update_asset + patch_asset repeat it for the edit path.
    - The generating system prompt: new PROTECTED runtime-policy rule id "sandboxed-artifacts" (lib/runtime-policy.js) — it composes into every scope's final prompt layer, so owner prompt overrides can never remove it. Prompt budget kept < 6144 B (composed hub now 6135) by trimming unpinned master-skill prose and tightening the policy header/footer wording; constraints layer version bumped 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 in the registry.

(2) RUNTIME ERRORS TEACH — sandboxApiGuardScript (shared/components.js) is injected into every generated-document frame via injectFrameGuards (after CSP/navguard/bootstrap, before generated code). Verified-in-Chrome surfaces are wrapped so the throw names the fix instead of the raw SecurityError: localStorage/sessionStorage, document.cookie writes, indexedDB, caches, OPFS navigator.storage.getDirectory, fetch. localStorage throw is near-verbatim from the issue: "localStorage is unavailable inside sandboxed artifacts - keep state in a variable, or store it with the platform's asset/memory tools". The script-sandbox host (extension/sandbox/script-sandbox.js) got the same teaching guards for storage surfaces (fetch stays the controlled host-bridged api there).

(3) PERSISTENCE ALTERNATIVES — RECOMMENDATION: in-memory as the artifact's only local state + the platform's asset/memory tools as the durable layer (agent stores snapshots on the owner's request). Evidence (real headless-Chrome CDP probe of an allow-scripts opaque frame, saved at worktree evidence-np64/sandbox-api-probe.log + red/green logs): localStorage/sessionStorage read -> SecurityError sandboxed; document.cookie write -> SecurityError; indexedDB.open -> SecurityError "access ... denied in this context"; caches -> SecurityError; OPFS navigator.storage.getDirectory() -> "Storage directory access is denied because the context is sandboxed and lacks the 'allow-same-origin' flag"; storage.estimate -> "not supported in this context"; fetch under the frame CSP -> opaque "Failed to fetch". So (c) OPFS-in-sandbox is NOT viable (opaque origin has no origin-keyed storage at all — Chrome refuses every storage API). In-memory + platform-store is the only stack that works today; an export affordance is the artifact rendering its state as copyable text that the agent then saves. NOT building all three: only the in-memory + platform-store guidance shipped (in the rule/schemas/guard), OPFS explicitly rejected with probe evidence.

(4) EVAL HARNESS — tests/artifact-sandbox-guidance-eval.test.ts (6 scenarios): composed prompt carries the constraint (hub + worker); create_asset/generate_ui + update_asset/patch_asset schemas carry it; the eval's fixture checker flags a localStorage-using generation and passes an in-memory one (this case is GREEN even with the guidance removed — the checker judges the generation text, the issue's falsification); the guarded frame carries the teaching guard before generated code; the shipped guard BEHAVES against shims (localStorage access throws the teaching sentence, cookie writes throw, OPFS/fetch reject with teaching text).

Falsification proven: product changes stashed -> 5/6 eval tests FAIL (1/6 = the checker backstop stays green, as designed) -> restored -> 6/6 GREEN (logs in worktree evidence-np64/red-prefix.log + green-eval.log). Gates: npm run build PASS; check:gallery PASS; deno test --allow-all tests/ PASS 3184 passed / 0 failed (full suite, retried after cross-lane Chrome-lock contention froze the first attempt inside security-suite-custody); focused suites for every touched surface 296/0.

Coordination note: p45y's append_asset tool (origin/cap-beads-p45y, not yet on main at this branch point) is the literal "append" schema the issue names — when it merges, add the same HTML_ARTIFACT_SANDBOX_NOTE to its description (create_asset's note is the template). r5 review P1 #3 — persistence recommendation, ONE with evidence: RECOMMEND (b) the platform's asset tools as the persistence layer, with (a) in-memory as the runtime default (the issue's export/import affordance is inherent: the artifact IS the stored document).

title: Site-agent tool calls to declared page tools (e.g. search_docs on beads.gascity.com) always fail: 'DOMException: UnknownError from the page-side dispatcher' — opaque, unloggable, unreproducible from the error alone
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-03: a task calling a site agent invokes the site's declared tool (e.g. search_docs({query:'installation'}) on https://beads.gascity.com) and ALWAYS errors: Status Failed, 'DOMException: UnknownError from the page-side dispatcher — The site's search handler threw an internal DOM exception during execution.' No console errors, no logs that explain the cause. Owner suspects content-script realm isolation (main world vs isolated world) or the page-side dispatch plumbing.

WHAT'S WRONG BEYOND THE BUG ITSELF: the error is opaque by construction — 'UnknownError' with no underlying cause surfaced, no page-console capture, no dispatch trace. Even if the fix were trivial, the diagnosis path is broken.

WORK:

title: Test suite runtime: massively optimise deno test (target selection, dependency-aware subsetting, parallelisation) — more tests must not mean proportionally slower gates
description:
Owner feedback 2026-09-02: the deno test command takes way too long (~5-10 min per full run and growing). Adding features adds tests (good), but the gate time grows linearly with them. Want options + implementation to massively optimise how tests run, and ways to TARGET tests:

Investigate and implement (evidence for each option: measured before/after on the full suite):
1. PARALLELISATION — does the suite run files in parallel? deno test runs test modules concurrently by default but per-file serialization/permissions/shares may serialize. Measure: --parallel flag behaviour, per-file timing histogram (top-10 slowest files), whether slow files dominate.
2. TARGETED RUNS — a dependency-aware subset picker: a script that maps changed files (git diff --name-only origin/main) -> the test files that import/exercise them (static import graph), running ONLY those + the always-on core (security, vocabulary). This becomes the per-commit gate; the full suite stays the pre-merge/land gate.
3. ACTIONABLE npm scripts — npm test:changed / npm test:file -- <path> / npm test:fast (core + changed) so agents and the owner can target without thinking.
4. SHARED FIXTURE COST — the suite spends large time in fake-indexeddb/extension-boot fixtures per file; consider a shared test server-mode (deno test --parallel + module-level singleton fixtures) or moving heavy integration journeys out of the unit gate entirely.
5. REPORT the histogram + the chosen architecture in the bead before implementing (a design comment), so the owner can steer.

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): full-suite wall time reduced measurably (record before/after); test:changed runs in <60s on a typical one-file change and catches a known regression injected into a changed seam (RED/GREEN proof); no test weakened or skipped — subsetting must be additive tooling, the full suite remains the merge gate.
close_reason: Closed

  wall 345s (5m45s), 3117 passed / 3 failed. In-suite per-file test-time histogram
  (top-10 slowest, summed per-file test durations):
    1. tests/durable-runs.test.ts          107.3s   <- 31% of suite test time; six tests >=4s each (37s/23s/20s/15s outbox byte-bound tests)
    2. tests/task-view-full-response.ts     49.0s
    3. tests/provider-gate.test.ts          32.3s
    4. tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts        22.0s
    5. tests/wasm-sync-workspace.test.ts    15.0s

    7. tests/bgagent-delete.test.ts          8.0s

   10. tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts   3.1s
  All files sum to 304.7s of test time; top-6 files = 238.3s = 78% of it. Slow files DOMINATE.

PARALLEL FINDING (probe on synthetic 8x4s files): default `deno test` runs test
  MODULES SERIALLY (33s wall). `--parallel` runs them concurrently (4s wall).
  DENO_JOBS alone is inert without --parallel. Per-file processes are already
  isolated; the repo serializes Chrome via its own cross-process lock, so file
  concurrency is safe by construction. --parallel is adopted for SUBSET runs only;
  the full-suite merge gate keeps its exact current invocation (deno test -A tests/).

ARCHITECTURE CHOSEN (additive only; nothing skipped or weakened):
  scripts/select-tests.mjs — dependency-aware subset picker:
    changed = `git diff --name-only origin/main` + untracked, filtered to the repo
    source/test trees; selection = tests that TRANSITIVELY import a changed file

    packages/, tests/) ∪ changed test files themselves ∪ ALWAYS-ON CORE
    (security/vocabulary family: security, secret-redaction, security-suite-custody,
    owner-approval-security, vocabulary = 76 tests, ~3s).
    Subset executes `deno test -A --parallel <selected>` to hold the <60s bar.
    Known limitation (by design, stated): file-reading/scanning tests that do not
    import the changed file are not selected; the full suite stays the merge gate.
  npm scripts:
    test:changed -> picker (dependency-aware subset + core)  [falsification target]
    test:file    -> `deno test -A` + explicit path (npm run test:file -- <path>)
    test:fast    -> always-on core only (~3s pulse). NOTE: issue item 3 reads

      one-line alias — steering point for the owner.

  from the AGENTS.md commit + 2 /tmp-inode-exhaustion env failures) — being filed as discovered.

title: read_file refuses files over a 2000-byte maxBytes bound (fs_file_too_large) — reading any file must work; LLM-transport is an attachment concern, not a refusal
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-02: read_file on a file from a granted directory handle fails with 'The file is too large to read within the bounded limit' (code fs_file_too_large, maxBytes 2000, path cairn-gateway/README.md, size 9080). A 9KB README is refused because the default bound is 2,000 BYTES — an absurd placeholder.

OWNER DIRECTIVE: read_file must work with ANY file size. The tool reads from the file handle locally — size is irrelevant to the read itself. If the content must reach the LLM's context, the system works out HOW to deliver it: attach as a file reference the model can read in chunks (offset/limit reads), summarize, or pass through to another tool — never a flat refusal at a tiny bound.

FIX:
1. Find the maxBytes=2000 default in the fs tool family (grep fs_file_too_large / maxBytes in extension/lib/ + the fs tools seam) and remove the refusal path for reads backed by a real handle.
2. read_file returns the complete content; the run-transport layer decides delivery: below the model-context budget -> inline; above -> attach via the existing file-attachment/retained-payload mechanism (retainedPayloadRef) so the model can request chunks (support offset/length params on read_file for chunked reads of huge files).
3. If a genuine transport budget exists, the error becomes actionable guidance ('file is 9KB; use offset/limit or ask for a summary') rather than fs_file_too_large at 2000 bytes.
4. Falsification tests: a 9KB file reads completely (the exact owner repro); a 10MB file reads via offset/limit chunking; no read is refused on size alone when a handle exists.

Related: chrome-agent-platform-kmpq (remove the 256KiB storage truncation regime), chrome-agent-platform-p45y (artifact size truncation). This is the same no-silly-caps family: tools must not refuse real work at placeholder bounds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Generated interactive artifacts: click events don't reach the artifact, and generated code appears truncated at size bounds
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-02 (Telegram, voice):

SYMPTOM A — interactivity: when an agent generates an interactive artifact (e.g. a little game), CLICK EVENTS don't get through in the artifact view. Owner suspects the double-iframe (artifact iframe nested inside the hub's view frame) or some layer above it swallowing pointer events. Investigate: (a) iframe nesting + any overlay from the view chrome (frame bar, [data-embedded] rules from the one-shell merge) capturing pointer events; (b) the artifact iframe's sandbox/allow attributes — do they permit scripts + pointer interaction; (c) z-index/stacking of .view-frame vs artifact canvas; (d) whether the wheel/click hit-testing added for the dialog scroll work (chrome-journeys probes) interacts. Repro: ask an agent to build a click-based game; open the artifact; click buttons. Falsification-gated journey: synthetic click lands on a button inside the artifact iframe and increments visible state.

SYMPTOM B — truncation: the generated code sometimes looks CUT OFF in the artifact source view, and generation itself may be truncated at a size bound (owner has seen artifacts 'cut at certain sizes'). Two suspects to verify and fix separately: (1) the artifact WRITE path caps content (write_file/artifact tool bounds — check the artifact-tx bounds and any 64KiB-class limits on tool args); (2) the SOURCE VIEW renders truncated text (source view reading the rendered DOM/text slice instead of the complete stored content — same family as the copy-reads-DOM bug). The generation model may also stop early if the tool-call args cap applies — check whether write_file tool-call arguments are byte-capped at the protocol layer (lazy-tool-protocol / agent-do) and whether that cap is honest to the model (the model should be told the cap BEFORE generating, or streaming/appending writes should be supported: write_file in chunks).

ACCEPTANCE: (A) a generated click-game is fully interactive in the artifact view (journey with a real synthetic click asserting state change, screenshot evidence); (B) an artifact larger than any legacy bound stores COMPLETE (size asserted end-to-end: what the model wrote == what the source view shows == what runs), the source view shows the COMPLETE stored content byte-for-byte, and if a protocol cap exists it is either removed (payloads by reference, see chrome-agent-platform-kmpq) or surfaced to the model with a chunked-append write path. Related: chrome-agent-platform-kmpq (storage truncation regime removal).

title: Remove the 256KiB memory-store truncation for agent responses and thread data — OPFS/journal becomes the complete store, no more silent-feeling caps
description:
Owner directive 2026-09-02 (high priority): the 240KiB/256KiB store and outbox bounds are wrong. 'I don't want limits. Agent responses, data that can be used in threads and a whole bunch of other stuff like the truncation — it's incredibly dumb. We need to get it fixed.' A recent bug: outbox records stall at the 256KiB memory-store limit.

REDESIGN: agent responses and thread payloads must be stored COMPLETE, without memory-store size caps dictating truncation.
- Primary storage for large payloads moves to OPFS / the durable run journal (the retainedPayloadRef mechanism ALREADY exists — threads.js comments say the complete text stays in the durable run journal via retainedPayloadRef). The memory-store row keeps only a bounded INDEX/summary + a reference to the complete payload.
- Threads must hydrate the COMPLETE response from the journal/OPFS on open (no truncation marker as the end-user experience; the marker/digest may remain only as a loading affordance, not a cap).
- The outbox serialized into memory stays small BY DESIGN (references, not payloads) — records no longer stall at 256KiB because payloads never live there.
- Remove/adjust the bounds constants (threads.js MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES 240KiB, MAX_THREAD_BYTES 248KiB) as PRODUCT bounds; they may remain only as per-ROW summaries, not content caps.
- Migration: existing truncated threads backfill from the journal where the complete text exists (retainedPayloadRef); where it does not, the marker stays honest about what is lost.

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): a 10MiB agent response is fully persisted (journal/OPFS) and rendered COMPLETE when the thread is opened; the memory-store row for that thread stays under the 256KiB store bound (index+ref only); no outbox record ever approaches 256KiB (payloads by reference); reload/cold-start hydrates complete; migration path tested; the current truncation-marker tests are re-worked to assert the NEW contract (complete storage, bounded index) rather than the old caps. NOTE: this supersedes the truncation-contract direction pinned by chrome-agent-platform-znx9 — coordinate: znx9's tests pin bounds the product no longer wants.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DESIGN (kmpq lane, 2026-09-02/03):

NEW CONTRACT: complete terminal text lives ONCE, in the durable retained
payload (run-payload:* chunked keys, unbounded total). Memory rows + outbox
records hold bounded summaries + retainedPayloadRef ONLY; the thread VIEW
hydrates the complete response from the journal on open.

S1 threads.js (row writer): commitThreadTerminal terminal rows gain an
optional retainedPayloadRef (persisted when the terminal carries one).
Content rule per terminal row: utf8Bytes <= MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (240KiB, stays a
per-ROW summary bound, byte-complete as today) -> store byte-complete;
larger WITH retainedPayloadRef -> row content = bounded digest (~16KiB,
never-silent) + ref on the row (index/summary + ref only, row stays light);
larger WITHOUT a durable ref (demo/board/direct) -> today's boundText marker
behaviour (nothing else holds it; marker honest).

S2 durable-runs.js settle()/outbox (stall fix): the outbox no longer embeds a
near-bound content copy. threadTerminal.content in the OUTBOX = bounded
digest only; retainedPayloadRef rides threadTerminal. Envelope fields
(toolCalls/skills/citations/serverToolEvents) are bounded at outbox build
(same caps threads.js commit applies). The serialized-size shrink loop +
fail-loud content machinery goes away: records never approach 256KiB because
payloads never live there (any result size fits).

S3 durable-runs.js processOutbox(): before commitThread, when
threadTerminal.retainedPayloadRef is present, resolve the FULL text from the
chunked payload (readJsonPayload) and pass payload.result as content, so the
memory thread row is byte-complete up to its own budget for normal answers
(and S1 digests only genuinely over-budget text). Crash-safe: payload is
written BEFORE the outbox; recovery re-resolves.

S4 thread view hydration (thread-run-view.js + thread.get): terminal
assistant/error body rows whose execution log terminal row carries a fuller
payload.result than the stored content get content replaced with the complete
payload text at view build (listLogs already hydrates terminal payloads for
viewed executions, so this adds no I/O). Missing-terminal reconciliation
prefers terminalRow.payload.result over the record preview. This is the
migration path: existing truncated rows (240KiB marker text) backfill from
the journal where the complete text exists; where it does not, the marker
stays honest.

CONTRACT FLIP (this lane supersedes the truncation contract pinned on main):
outbox tests now assert content-by-reference (small outbox at ANY result
size, full text in payload), thread-row tests assert byte-complete <= the
row summary bound + digest+ref above it, and the view tests assert the
reopened thread renders the COMPLETE 10MiB response from the journal.
Falsification: 10MiB response -> outbox << 256KiB, thread row < 256KiB with
summary+ref, listLogs terminal payload.result length == 10MiB, reopened view
messages carry the full text; migration row (legacy marker text) backfills.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DESIGN — task-level tab-tools bundle (one card per tab step)

Requirement shape: the bundle reuses the EXISTING permissionRequirement shape the conversation already renders — { reason, permissions, grantOrigins, grantGlobal } — so no new card component, no new requirement type on the conversation side. The bundle ask is: permissions = whichever of [tabs, tabGroups] are still missing; grantOrigins = the denial's own sites union the canonical origins of the owner's currently open web tabs, minus sites already browser-control-granted; grantGlobal passes through only when the denial is genuinely origin-less (a chrome:// tab). A bounded marker field bundle:tab-tools identifies the offer; the card key derives from the content as today.

Where the SW offers it (denial path): every model-run permission pause routes through waitForInlinePermissionDecision (service-worker.js). The offer fires there, gated to denials of the tab family (list_tabs, list_tab_groups, group_tabs, update_tab_group, ungroup_tabs, move_tab_to_group — passed as the selected tool name via the onPermissionRequest hook) whose requirement is permission-shaped (no approvals, no hostOrigins). The offer is MEMOIZED per executionId: the first tab-family denial in a run mints the bundle from live state; any later tab-family denial in the same run reuses the exact minted requirement. The offer stamps the denial's permissionRequirement object IN PLACE — agent.js and the retained tool result share that exact object, so the live approval-request card, the tool-result event, the journaled row, and the reopened thread stay byte-identical (one card everywhere, incl. the denied path).

Allow grants everything in ONE gesture: approvePermissionRequirement is unchanged — one chrome.permissions.request carrying the union permissions (plus any host patterns), then one browser-control.set for the grantOrigins. The bundle simply rides the existing owner-gesture path (trusted-click + user-activation gated), never a new grant route.

Second tab tool, no new card: after Allow, tabs+tabGroups+the sites' browser control are all in place, so the second tool's pre-check finds nothing missing and runs (no denial, no card). A second tab-tool denial BEFORE a decision (a re-run) reuses the memoized requirement -> same card key -> the conversation merges it into the existing card and shares the owner's one click across both paused calls.

Per-tool floor: the builder returns null for non-family tools, non-permission denials, a bundle that would ask nothing, or any failure reading tabs/permissions — the denial is left untouched and the per-tool card renders exactly as today.

Decline: the existing deny path — run.resolve-inline-approval approve:false, terminal '[tool] DENIED by owner', nothing granted. The card's sticky-denied state means a re-denial of the same bundle does not nag again.

Owner-gesture-only (source pin): the bundle exists only as a requirement shape rendered on the owner's card. No new model route, no new tool. A test asserts the model tool-registry files in extension/lib (browser-tools.js, management-tools.js, tool-catalog.js, lazy-tool-protocol.js, chrome-tool-capabilities.js, tool-selection.js, capabilities.js, bundled-tool-packages.js) never name the bundle id or builder.

- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the terminal-ordering test must be shown failing against the current build

Both execution-ownership predicates claim the migration marker, and purging removes the log FILE (which is not in `store.keys()`) via an injectable `removeLogFor`. Falsification: putting the terminal write back on the key-value path turns the new regression test RED; removing the marker from the rollback predicate turns the remnant test RED. Note that the FIRST falsification attempt on the remnant test passed — because there are two ownership predicates and I had weakened the wrong one; the test only proved its point once the rollback path's predicate was the one broken.
  - 2026-08-28 19:00 UTC — the injected-failure tests were RETARGETED, not deleted, because the data moved rather than the property changing: `failDeleteKey`/`failKey` pointed at `run-log:<exec>:accepted`, a key-value row that no longer exists. The partial-delete test now targets the migration marker, and the quota test injects the fault where the write actually happens — `createMemoryRunLogHandles({ failWriteFor })`, a log-write fault. Both still assert exactly what they did before: a partial auxiliary delete preserves authority and retries safely, and a quota failure while admitting a run leaves every old log intact and strands nothing.
  - 2026-08-28 19:00 UTC — also fixed the reason this was hard to see: SIX `createDurableRunRegistry` call sites across five suites passed a fake `store` but no `logHandleFor`, so they reached past their own fake straight to real OPFS. All now inject `createMemoryRunLogHandles()` bound to the store. Gates: unit **1894/0** (2 new), Chrome journeys **127/127**, `npm run test:opfs` **6/6**, security suite PASS, build clean.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — `start()` writes `run-log:<exec>:accepted` and the terminal path writes `run-log:<exec>:terminal` with `store.setTrusted`, bypassing `appendLog` entirely. That was harmless when reads came from the key-value store. Since `f6d0cf23` reads come from the WAL, and the KV→WAL migration is one-time and marker-guarded: **a row written to KV AFTER the marker is set is never read again.** In a real run `appendLog` is called during the run, so the marker is set before `settle()` — meaning the terminal log row is orphaned. Not currently user-visible, because `buildThreadRunView` takes run status from `e.record.terminal` rather than from the log row, which is why no shipped test caught it; it is still wrong, and it blocks any guarantee about ordering rows relative to the terminal.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — the fix has a tail: once these rows live in the log, the two execution-ownership predicates that purge `run-log:<exec>:*` must also claim `run-log-wal:<exec>` (the migration marker — otherwise a purged execution leaves a remnant, AND a recreated one would skip migration) and must delete the log FILE, which is not in `store.keys()`. Attempted in the same session; five terminal fault-matrix steps then failed because they inject failures around the old `store.setTrusted` write. Recorded rather than rushed.

title: [CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-WRITE-BUFFER-01] Buffer and flush the run-log WAL
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-WRITE-BUFFER-01] Buffer and flush the run-log WAL
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — product owner: "I think we need to buffer and flush the WAL", and then "if we do the buffer and flush, I'm presuming the read includes the buffer too, right?"
- Updated: 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P1
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `f6d0cf23`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: rows appended close together are coalesced into ONE file open, so writing 1,000 rows costs ~1 ms rather than ~14 s; `appendLog` still resolves only when the row is ON DISK, so an awaiting caller keeps today's durability guarantee; a reader can never miss a row that was already accepted; and no run reaches a terminal state with unflushed history behind it. Coalescing is asserted by COUNTING file opens, not inferred from a timing number
- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the coalescing test must be shown failing against the unbuffered build
- Gates: full unit suite; Chrome journeys; `npm run test:opfs`; the security suite; and the `scripts/thread-open-trace.ts` matrix showing the write column drop
- Blockers: —
- Next: closed pending review. Streaming the first page (design stage 4) is NOT needed — at 27 ms for 1,000 rows it would add moving parts for no measurable gain
- Recover: `git grep -n "queueAppend\|flushExecution" -- extension/lib/durable-runs.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 — DONE at `origin/main@dc04e4c7`. Merged and green.
  - 2026-08-28 21:00 UTC — **DONE. Task open 918 ms → 27 ms (~34x) and writing 1,000 rows 171,375 ms → 1,390 ms (~123x), against the pre-WAL baseline.** Full matrix: open 15/213/918 → 5/14/27 ms at 10/250/1,000 rows; write 140 ms/11.2 s/171 s → 30 ms/323 ms/1.4 s. Extrapolated to the product's own bound (6,250 rows), opening a task goes from ~6 s to ~170 ms. Gates: unit **1926/0**, Chrome journeys **127/127**, `npm run test:opfs` **6/6**, security suite PASS, build clean.
  - 2026-08-28 21:00 UTC — two changes carried the last order of magnitude. **(1) Coalescing:** the row is queued under the write lock and the flush awaited OUTSIDE it. Both halves matter — an earlier version awaited the flush while holding the lock, which serialised every append and produced **21 file writes for 20 concurrent appends**. The test asserts the write COUNT rather than a timing number, and was falsified: holding the lock across the flush takes it to 20 writes and the test RED. **(2) The preamble:** with file writes coalesced the remaining cost was per-append — a marker read and a directory/file open on every row, plus a SHA-256 computed whether or not it was needed. Marker and handle are stable for an execution's life and are memoised (cleared on purge); the digest is now computed only when a payload actually overflows, which is the only thing it names.
  - 2026-08-28 21:00 UTC — the owner's question is answered in the code and in a test: **a read FLUSHES, it does not merge the buffer.** One source of truth (the file), and byte cursors stay meaningful because a buffered row has no offset yet. The flush sits INSIDE the shared-lock callback, which has already awaited the write chain — placed before it, a read races an append that had been called but had not yet queued. Also asserted: an awaited append is genuinely on disk (a fresh registry over the same storage sees it), a run never settles with unflushed history behind it, and a failed flush REJECTS every caller whose row it carried rather than dropping rows silently.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — **attempted, working, and reverted to keep main green.** The design is settled and was proven in the attempt: queue the row UNDER the write lock, await the flush OUTSIDE it, flush on a macrotask. Both halves matter — an earlier version awaited the flush while still holding the lock, which serialised every append and produced **21 file writes for 20 concurrent appends**, i.e. no coalescing at all. Measured after the fix: 20 concurrent appends → far fewer writes, with every row present.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — **the owner's question answered: a read FLUSHES first, it does not merge the buffer.** Flushing keeps one source of truth (the file) and keeps byte cursors meaningful — a buffered row has no offset yet, so a merged view could not be paged back through. The flush must sit INSIDE the shared-lock callback, which has already awaited the write chain: placed before it, a read races an append that has been called but has not yet queued its row. Two tests for this are KEPT on main (`a read sees rows that were appended but not awaited`, `appendLog still resolves only once the row is durable`) because they hold for the current implementation too.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — reverted because the change kept widening: buffering forces terminal ordering, which exposed `CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-REGISTRY-ROWS-01`, which forces the purge/rollback paths to delete the log file and the migration marker, which broke five fault-matrix steps that inject failures around the old `store.setTrusted` terminal write. Each of those is legitimate work; none of it should be rushed into the durable run authority at the tail of a long session. Main stays at the shipped 6.3x/12x.

- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: detached candidate on `origin/main`
- Base: `2c25e82`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: this commit on `origin/main`
- Acceptance: clicking Clear on a site agent's row in Settings → Data & memory visibly empties that store without a reload — the memory explorer's key count for the origin drops to zero; the store really is empty; the agent stays enrolled, because clearing memory is not a revocation; and the owner is told what actually happened rather than being shown a success message the code never checked
- Review: author self-review 2026-08-25 (two further defects found and fixed, below); **no independent review** — the product owner asked the author to review directly
- Gates: `scripts/data-memory-clear.ts` **13/13** on a clean profile, with both regressions verified to FAIL against the unfixed code (`before=4 after=4` for the stale count, `after=[]` for the collapsed tree); unit 1591/0; Chrome journeys 127/127; security suite PASS
- Blockers: —
- Next: an independent pass if one becomes cheap; otherwise closed. `extension/memory/explorer.js` is a separate removal candidate, not a fix for this report
- Recover: `npm run test:data-clear && git grep -n "renderMemoryExplorer" -- extension/options/options.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-25 19:20 UTC — **author self-review, not independent.** Two further defects found in my own fix, both fixed here. **(1) I introduced a UX regression:** making the explorer refresh meant it rebuilt the whole tree with every node collapsed, so clearing snapped shut whatever the owner had expanded — on precisely the refresh where they are looking at that store. Expansion is now keyed by a stable `data-mem-id` and restored across the rebuild, and a restored store re-fetches its (now empty) keys. Individual key/value nodes are deliberately NOT restored: their content can be stale after a clear, and collapsing one is far less disruptive than losing the tree. **(2) A third Clear button exists** in `extension/memory/explorer.js` with the same ignore-the-result shape. It is NOT reachable — nothing in the extension, tests or scripts links `memory/explorer.html` — so it is not the button in this report and is recorded as a removal candidate rather than fixed in place, which would have meant maintaining a dead surface.
  - 2026-08-25 19:20 UTC — also checked and found clean: every other `memory.clear` caller tolerates the new result shape (`scripts/opfs-real-browser.ts`, `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` and the route-modularization test all ignore or destructure it safely).
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — reproduced exactly as reported and fixed. The data WAS being cleared; the UI just never showed it. The origin-row handler called `renderData()` (which redraws the enrolled-origins list, unchanged by a clear) but not `renderMemoryExplorer()` — and the explorer is the surface that displays keys and counts, so it kept showing the cleared store's old count until a reload. Both Clear handlers now refresh both surfaces.
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — second defect found while fixing the first: `memory.clear` resolved to `undefined`, so neither handler could tell success from failure and both flashed "Cleared…" unconditionally. The route now returns `{ok:true, origin}` or `{ok:false, error}`, and both handlers report the real outcome. A button that lies about having worked is the same class of bug as one that does nothing.
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — checked and ruled out a worse possibility: `clear()` does remove the site store's `enrolled` key, but enrollment authority does not live there, so a clear never silently disenrolls a Site Agent. Asserted in the new script so it stays true.
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — coverage lives in a dedicated `scripts/data-memory-clear.ts` on a clean profile rather than inside the 127-check journey suite. Adding it there first was tried and rejected: the fixture had to be created mid-suite, where accumulated global state (a revoked `storage` capability, several enrolled origins) made the explorer assertions unreliable, and the extra enrolled origin made a later step's first-match `.origin-row .disenroll-origin` click remove the wrong agent. A focused script tests the button instead of the suite's history.

## [CAP-FB-20260825-SITE-DISCOVERABILITY-01] Site-agent discoverability + content-script boot reconciliation

- Feedback: 2026-08-25 — product owner: "I can't work out how site agents get discovered and approved any more... I'm refreshing a site and it doesn't appear and I don't see any console logs."
- Updated: 2026-08-25 20:3x UTC

- Branch: —
- Base: `2c25e82`
- Candidate: `e152f7c0`
- Shipping: `origin/main@2bff0af` (0.2.267)
- Root cause: (a) chicken-and-egg — discovery required the content script to run, which only ran on ENROLLED origins (ensureOriginScriptsRegistered registers per-origin + host permission, transactional), so an un-enrolled site surfaced nothing; (b) enrolled origins' dynamic content scripts were not reconciled on SW startup/browser boot, so an enrolled site went silent after a restart ("no logs").
- Fix: proactive discovery — NTP + Settings surface open discoverable pages with one-click "Add Site Agent"/"Enroll" (explicit owner gesture, host-permission request, no typing origins) + discovered-but-not-enrolled listing; reconcileEnrolledOriginScriptsOnBoot() re-registers enrolled origins' scripts on boot. Security model verified hard (Pro e384c626): zero broad injection, host-permission grant stays owner-gesture, transactional enroll/rollback intact.
- Acceptance: an owner can see which open pages are discoverable and enroll one with a single explicit gesture, without typing an origin; discovery no longer requires the origin to be enrolled first; an already-enrolled origin's content scripts are re-registered on service-worker/browser boot so it does not go silent after a restart; no broad injection is introduced and the host-permission grant stays behind an owner gesture with transactional enroll/rollback intact
- Review: PASS (Pro e384c626), 1595/1595, manifest untouched.
- Gates: independent security review (Pro `e384c626`) confirming zero broad injection, owner-gesture host-permission grant and intact transactional enroll/rollback; 1595/1595 unit; manifest unchanged

Pro conclusively identified the emitter: the owner's installed Claude for Chrome extension (fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn v1.0.81) bundles the web-vitals library + OpenTelemetry; the exact crash is web-vitals INP longest-interaction attribution reading entries[0].startTime on an EMPTY entries array = known upstream defect GoogleChrome/web-vitals#758. - History:
  - 2026-08-29 — **all three hand-rolled dialogs converted; `createElement("dialog")` now appears exactly once in the extension, inside the shared component itself.** (1) `extension/artifacts/index.js` artifact delete → `confirmActionDialog`, gaining backdrop light-dismiss, an `aria-label` and a settled guard it did not have; its 13 lines of bespoke `.delete-dialog` CSS are deleted. (2) `confirmAgentProviderMutation` → the shared confirm. **This one carried a security property the shared confirm lacked** — approve only on a click that is `isTrusted` AND has active user activation — so rather than keep the duplicate for it, the property moved INTO the shared component as `requireGenuineGesture`, alongside `returnFocusTo` and `note`. Every future approval now gets it by construction instead of by remembering to re-implement it. (3) `editRecipePrompt` → `<agent-dialog>`, the content shell; it gains a close button and backdrop dismissal it never had, and its bespoke panel/backdrop CSS is replaced by the shell's. **Evidence, driven in a real loaded extension (`scripts/kat-dialog-consolidation.ts`, 18/18):** a destructive confirm focuses Cancel; a backdrop click resolves false and removes the node; a non-destructive confirm focuses the confirm control; **an untrusted scripted click cannot approve** and the refusal is explained in the dialog; Escape denies; the shell is announced by its title and its body scrolls on overflow. That last group is why this is a KAT and not only a unit test — a DOM shim cannot tell you whether `event.isTrusted` gating actually holds. **Falsification:** `tests/provider-options-approval.test.ts` pinned the OLD implementation's source lines and had to be rewritten; it now pins the property across BOTH halves (the call site must ASK for the check, the component must IMPLEMENT it and gate the true result on it), because asserting only one half would let the flag become a no-op or let the call site quietly stop passing it. Four deliberate regressions — call site drops the flag, component drops the trusted-click check, the guard warns without refusing, and the hand-rolled duplicate returns — each drove it red before being reverted. **Gates:** build clean; unit **2004 pass / 0 fail**; Chrome journeys **127/127**; gallery, vocabulary and tracker schema green.
  - 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC — captured by source audit. **Five dialog implementations ship.** Two are the intended shared ones in `extension/shared/components.js`: `<agent-dialog>` (the content-dialog shell) and `confirmActionDialog` (the promise-based confirm). Three are hand-rolled duplicates outside the component system: `extension/artifacts/index.js:83` (artifact delete), `extension/options/options.js:1236` (`confirmAgentProviderMutation`), and `extension/options/options.js:1555` (`editRecipePrompt`). This is precisely the failure mode the owner already named as a project rule — "never hand-roll a one-off version of an existing component (the blank-toggle + menu bugs came from hand-rolled duplicates)" — and it is the most likely explanation for dialogs behaving inconsistently: each of the five owns its own focus, dismiss, overflow and sizing behaviour, so a fix to one does not reach the others.
  - 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC — **good news worth recording:** `window.confirm` / `window.alert` / `window.prompt` are already fully eliminated from the extension; the only remaining occurrence is the explanatory comment above `confirmActionDialog`. `CAP-FB-20260823-DIALOG-CONFIRM-MODERNIZATION-01` is therefore substantially further along than its OPEN status suggests — what is left of that task is this consolidation.

- What it is: the async/broadcast complement to `delegate_to_agent`. A hub-level

  named agent or the hub posts work, and any capable agent claims it (atomic

  board_post_job / board_claim_job / board_complete_job / board_send_message /

  textContent-only). Guards are pure functions in `extension/lib/agent-board.js`
  mirroring `agent-delegation.js`; caller identity comes from the route context
  (never model args).
- Permission model (owner decision 2026-08-29; deny layer landed 2026-08-30):
  default-open among named agents + the hub, plus owner-controlled per-edge
  DENY rules (Settings → Board permissions; owner-options principal only;
  fail-closed on malformed rules and corrupt store; rules load fresh inside
  each locked post/claim).
- DEFERRED (planned extensions): automatic wake of idle agents on post
  (scheduler/alarm machinery — v1 wakes live surfaces via broadcastProgress);
  bidding/auctions; cross-device boards; A2A wire-protocol interop.

    superseded-heartbeat compaction + a fail-closed board-full post gate;
    stale model contexts denied (never hub-escalated); settlements commit

title: [CAP-FB-20260829-FIXED-DEBUG-PORTS-01] Nine harnesses hard-code a debug port, so a KAT can report green against the wrong browser
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260829-FIXED-DEBUG-PORTS-01] Nine harnesses hard-code a debug port, so a KAT can report green against the wrong browser
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — surfaced by the noun-discipline lane: "an early KAT run gave a full page of false failures because a fixed debug port silently attached to another lane's chromium"
- Updated: 2026-08-29 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P1
- Owner: implementation session (author review; falsification gates cleared)
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap-fb-20260829-fixed-debug-ports-01`
- Base: `84991bddd` (`origin/main` at the rebase)
- Candidate: `origin/main@ab454213`
- Shipping: `origin/main@ab454213`
- Acceptance: no browser-driving script hard-codes a debug port; every one launches with `--remote-debugging-port=0` and discovers the real port from the `DevTools listening` line (the pattern 28 scripts already use); each converted harness still passes on its own; and two harnesses that previously shared a port pass when run CONCURRENTLY, which is the case that produced false results
- Review: author review 2026-08-29 — falsification cleared in real browsers (a decoy browser holding the old fixed port; the pre-change harness reported the decoy tree's string, the converted harness reported its own). No independent review: no second model is available, per AGENTS.md "Review without a second model"
- Gates: each converted KAT green individually; a concurrent run of the previously-colliding pair green; `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:chrome`, `npm run check:gallery`, `node scripts/check-tasks.mjs`
- Blockers: —
- Next: owner merges the candidate to `origin/main`
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep CAP-FB-20260829-FIXED-DEBUG-PORTS-01`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — verified independently by the coordinator session and merged. Cherry-picked onto current `main` (the tracker row and CHANGELOG conflicted and were resolved keeping both lanes' content). **My own falsification, not the implementer's:** adding `--remote-debugging-port=9351` to `kat-usage-viz.ts` drove the gate RED (4 pass / 1 fail); removing it returned to green — so the gate fails for the right reason. A `grep` for a fixed port anywhere under `scripts/` now returns nothing outside the launcher. Gates at the merge tip: build clean, unit **2004 pass / 0 fail**, Chrome journeys **127/127**, gallery + tracker schema green. **One correction applied on merge:** the second test was named "only the shared launcher writes the debugging-port flag" but asserted merely that the launcher is *among* the writers — roughly thirty other scripts spawn Chrome themselves with the safe `=0` form. Renamed to "the shared launcher owns the debugging-port flag" and documented the scope in the test, because a test that claims more than it checks is the same defect class this entry exists to fix. The safety property (no script may name a port) is enforced by the first test and is unaffected. Migrating the remaining ~30 scripts onto `launchChrome()` is a separate cleanup, not a defect.
  - 2026-08-29 — **converted, falsified and gated.** Twelve harnesses now launch through one shared `scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts`; `launchChrome()` passes `--remote-debugging-port=0` and reads the DevTools endpoint out of its OWN child's stderr, so the endpoint provably belongs to this process and there is no probe to race. The port-0 form was used everywhere — no harness needed the weaker probe-then-bind fallback — and the two scripts that already carried private copies of that helper (`kat-noun-discipline`, `kat-bgagent-delete`) were folded onto the shared launcher too, leaving one spawn path instead of nine fixed ports and two copies. FALSIFICATION: a decoy browser was started holding 9351 (the port `kat-usage-viz` hard-coded) running a deliberately altered copy of the extension; the PRE-CHANGE harness, pointed at the real tree, reported `FAIL: cost card is labelled an estimate — "costs are DECOY approximations (this tree is NOT under test)"` — a string that exists only in the decoy — proving it drove a browser it did not launch; the converted harness, with that same decoy still holding the port, passed 13/13 against the real tree. CONCURRENCY: `kat-usage-viz` + `kat-ux-lows` (both 9351) run together — before, one lane hung to a 300 s timeout when the other killed the browser they were sharing; after, both finish with their solo results. Individually every harness matches its pre-change tally: back-stack 6/0, dark-scheme 32/3, narrow-toggle 20/0, usage-viz 13/0, ux-lows 9/1, axe-audit 7/0, providers-tabs 19/0, agent-templates 13/0, composer-grow 11/0, noun-discipline 14/0, bgagent-delete 11/0 (the 3 dark-scheme and 1 ux-lows failures are pre-existing contrast/landmark findings, unchanged by this work); `kat-failed-runs` went from hanging for the full 300 s timeout against a live zombie on 9357 to 7/0 in 10 s. TWO THINGS FOUND THAT THE REPORT DID NOT DESCRIBE: the slow port poll was also masking a startup race — reading the endpoint off stderr is fast enough that MV3 has not registered its service worker yet, so eight harnesses gained an explicit bounded `waitForServiceWorker()` instead of depending on how long a probe happened to take; and `kat-bgagent-delete`'s own helper called `Deno.listen` outside its `try`, so a taken port threw out of the function rather than moving on to the next. A new gate, `tests/harness-debug-port.test.ts`, fails on any fixed debugging port anywhere in `scripts/` and on a launcher that would accept a caller-chosen one; it was observed RED with a port reintroduced into `kat-usage-viz` and GREEN with it removed.
  - 2026-08-29 — measured, then corrected after the reporting lane pointed out the failure mode is worse than "a flake". **A fixed-port harness does not merely hang or error — it attaches to another lane's browser and reports confident PASS/FAIL results about an extension it is not testing.** The reporting run produced 7 such results. That means a fixed-port harness can go **green against the wrong tree**, which is worse than a red suite, because the output reads as evidence. Eleven scripts name a port; two of them (`kat-bgagent-delete` on `cbf89c33`, `kat-noun-discipline`) already probe for a free one, leaving **nine hard-coded**. Four ports are each claimed by two of those nine: 9347 (`kat-narrow-toggle`, `kat-dark-scheme`), 9351 (`kat-usage-viz`, `kat-ux-lows`), 9353 (`kat-providers-tabs`, `axe-audit`), 9359 (`kat-agent-templates`, `kat-composer-grow`); `kat-failed-runs` holds 9357, the port `kat-bgagent-delete` starts probing from. 28 other scripts already launch with `--remote-debugging-port=0` and read the real port off the `DevTools listening` line, and `scripts/kat-noun-discipline.ts` carries a reusable `freePort()` (probe `/json/version`, then bind-test) — so both the pattern and a helper are already in-repo.

Whatever the policy, a test proves an artifact cannot leave the library without either an explicit `asset.delete` or an owner-visible decision
- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the test must be shown failing against a build that still evicts silently
- Gates: unit suite; Chrome journeys green; `npm run test:opfs`
- Blockers: needs an owner decision — refusing a create fails a task mid-run, while evicting loses work silently. Both are bad in different ways and it is a product call, not an engineering one
- Next: put the two options to the owner with the real numbers (the bound is now ~15,000 rows) before building either
- Recover: `git grep -n "maxIndexBytes" -- extension/lib/artifacts.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 04:30 UTC — the index carries a byte bound and, when a create would exceed it, drops the OLDEST rows (`idx = idx.slice(1)`) and records eviction obligations to clean their bodies. For a library whose stated purpose is being "the central source of all the information that has been created by the worker", silently discarding the oldest thing the person made is the wrong terminal behaviour — it is the same class as the bug just fixed, reached by a different route. The durability fix raised the bound from 128 KiB to 2 MiB (~940 rows to ~15,000) because the bound had been PER ORIGIN and became shared, which would otherwise have been a capacity regression. That defers the problem by roughly an order of magnitude; it does not fix it, and it is recorded here rather than left implied.

## Design (2026-09-02, cap-beads-4dg increment): in-context provider host-access grant card

Scope: the last remaining Settings-redirect dead-end in the permission UX. Every
browser-tool denial already renders one in-context `<permission-approval-card>`
(Allow / Not now) — but when the configured NETWORK provider's exact origin is
not granted, the conversation preflight (extension/shared/conversation.js
runConversationTurn, "provider.permission-summary" check) appends a terminal
error reading "open Settings → Providers and approve that exact origin" and the
turn ends. The card UX directive: when an agent needs a permission, show an
in-context card, not a Settings redirect, with a clear grant/deny choice.

Change:
- On preflight ungranted-origin: do NOT return a dead-end error. Render ONE
  in-context permission card via the existing maybeRenderApproval machinery
  with requirement `{ reason: "connect to <host> (the provider that runs this
  task)", hostOrigins: [exact origin] }` (hostOrigins = the read-page-host-grant
  shape: Allow requests `<origin>/*` through chrome.permissions.request from
  the owner's genuine card click; the same request Settings' Use button makes).
- Allow (grant succeeds) → the run starts (executeTurn) — the SW run gate then
  passes; no Settings trip. Not now → honest terminal denial bubble: "Network
  access to <host> was not granted — you declined. The run did not start."
- Grant refused by Chrome → card shows the error and stays pending (Try again),
  matching the live-card contract; nothing is granted silently.
- Config problems (missing/invalid base URL, local-provider checks) are
  UNCHANGED — Settings remains the right surface for a configuration edit; this
  increment covers only the permission ask.

Mechanics (conversation.js only):
- runConversationTurn gains a pre-run pause state between the preflight and the
  first executeTurn: maybeRenderApproval is called with two new internal
  options (preRun: skips the legacy turn-retry flag, settle: an entry resolver)
  so the outer flow awaits the card decision deterministically — no polling,
  no double-run (the legacy approvalRetryRequested path would otherwise start a
  second attempt after a granted pre-run card).
- The user's own message bubble renders first (today the dead-end leaves the
  conversation without it).

Why hostOrigins: provider network access IS Chrome site access for one exact
origin (`<origin>/*`). The card already renders "Access this site: <origin>",
the exact-scope request, the "Chrome will ask you to confirm" note, and
granted/denied/error states. Reuse beats a new card type.

Not in scope (later increments of the bead): durable pending inbox for
background/scheduled runs with no open surface; multi-waiter ordering on one
browser-global permission; Settings decision history; in-run provider-access
revocation recovery (post-error) — the mid-run path still ends honestly and
points at Settings for the re-grant.

Tests: unit test driving runConversationTurn with a stubbed
provider.permission-summary (ungranted origin) + fake DOM container asserting:
(1) no Settings-redirect error is appended, one permission card entry is
created, status waiting-for-permission; (2) Allow → chrome.permissions.request
carries exactly the provider's `<origin>/*` and agent.run then executes exactly
once; (3) Not now → honest declined error, agent.run never dispatched, nothing
granted.

Today runs live only in SW memory: an MV3 restart orphans a paused-for-permission run and no owner-facing record survives. Plan: bounded chrome.storage.local inbox records {runRef, requirement (reason/patterns/permissions), createdAt, lease generation, state} — NO task args/secrets (doc's leakage rule); SW writes the record when a run pauses on permission; the conversation + a Settings surface render it owner-only; deny/cancel write terminal outcomes (doc's distinct DENIED vs CANCELLED); resume = deterministic same-run continuation after grant per the acceptance line and the 2026-08-22 settled policy ('auto-resume on restart, visible pause + resume for recoverable permission problems'). (2) MULTI-WAITER ORDERING — the primitive EXISTS: extension/lib/perm-lease.js + routes/perm-lease.js (SW single authority per canonical pattern, generation + owner token, 8s lease, backpressure, settle broadcast consumed by options.js + conversation.js). m6id's repro (get_cookie then list_cookies: second card never renders, then 'Approval expired') is the consumer side: the second same-pattern acquire hits the in-flight lease (busy) and the card flow drops it instead of queueing. comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DESIGN (cap-beads-lj7 lane) — Directory tool explorer + enrollment policy, posted before implementation.

RESEARCHED DECISION (enrollment vs per-tool/invocation approval; resolves the bead blocker):
- Enrollment (owner gesture that makes a site a Site Agent) remains the coarse ALLOW and the consent for that origin's tools as a class (WEBMCP-AUTOAPPROVE-01 stands — no per-tool approval UI dead-ends).
- Per-tool invocation consent exists ONLY as the per-site "ask" policy state, paid per call through the SAME in-run owner-approval card machinery the destructive/cookie classes use (requireOwnerApproval, CAP-FB-20260830-DESTRUCTIVE-ACTION-POLICY-01). Unattended/scoped runs without a conversation fail closed (never auto-run).
- Directory (owner surface) always shows truthful per-tool provenance for review; the AGENT toolset is where deny excludes tools.

POLICY MODEL — per-site, stored in the enrollment registry entry (cap:enrollment, atomic under the existing global enrollment lock, generation bumped on change so in-flight catalogs revoke):
1. allow (default) — tools flow today unchanged (enrollment = consent).
2. deny — the site's tools are EXCLUDED from every agent toolset (readSiteLazySources returns no records — the falsification gate) and every invocation path fails closed with a named reason (authorization-guard conjunct + invokeSiteTool early reject).
3. ask — tools stay discoverable; every invocation pays an in-conversation owner card (Allow once / Deny) via a new extension-only approval action webmcp.use-tool, gated by the run-bound model dispatcher threaded into the WebMCP dispatch closure; absent a card channel the call fails closed honestly.

EXPLORER UX (extension/directory):
- Per-site groups keep bounded tool cards (name, description, input-schema summary, source chip) and gain page provenance (declaring page URL) on the card + origin in the heading.
- Each site group header gains the enrollment-policy control: Allow / Ask before use / Blocked, exactly labelled to the site; Blocked sections state the site's tools are not available to agents; cards carry the policy state so a blocked/"ask" badge can never detach from the tool (containment + exact AX labels per the acceptance).

SEAMS: extension/lib/tools.js (registry policy column + get/set + snapshot carries policy); extension/lib/webmcp-authority.js (pure deny conjunct "site-policy-denied" + guard); extension/background/service-worker.js (readSiteLazySources exclusion + ask dispatch gate + invokeSiteToolCore deny + tools.policies/tools.policy.set routes + webmcp.use-tool approval route); extension/lib/owner-approval.js (approvable action webmcp.use-tool + canonical target kind); directory UI + tool-directory-card page row.

TESTS (falsification-gated): enroll + declare tools → set deny → build the agent toolset exactly as readSiteLazySources does → the blocked site's tool MUST NOT appear and its invocation MUST fail closed with the named reason; allow default regression (tool present + dispatches); ask gate: dispatch consults the owner gate (approved → runs, denied → refused); registry unit tests (default allow, set/get, generation bump).
