title: Quiet-window governor counts rustc CHILD processes of one heavy job as competing builders, so a single build is denied as if many were running (fleet/j5yz-qs8v7@445502f4)
description: The quiet-window/heavy-slot governor counts rustc CHILD processes of ONE heavy job as competing heavy-builders, so a single cargo/rust build is denied as if many builders were running. PROVEN against the REAL governor (j5yz, 2026-10-16): one heavy-named parent with 3 compiling rustc children makes origin/main refuse 'active heavy-builders 3 > 1' (ok:false/timeout) while the fixed build returns ok:true in 31ms. The mkax contract is INTACT under the fix: two cargo jobs are still refused by name ('2 > 1 ... 6 process(es) in 2 job(s)') and three INDEPENDENT compilers are still refused ('3 > 1 ... 3 job(s)'). Fix counts heavy-job ROOTS via the ppid chain and stays fail-closed on unknown parentage; branch fleet/j5yz-qs8v7@445502f4. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION (this bead originally repeated a report that was wrong): the e247af8f union was '712 files total, 0 skipped' with ONE red - 3nurz (waitForServiceWorker) under load1=12.50 with live-chrome=7 - and the '9 rustc ... activity unknown' line quoted as evidence sits inside tests/quiet-window.test.ts's OWN post-test output, i.e. a hand-BUILT sample (a real sampler prints 'compiling: rustc'). So the counter did NOT cause that red and nothing was skipped fail-closed; the governor-accounting defect is real and independently reproduced, and the union red had its own load cause tracked on 3nurz. FALSIFICATION (done): the three reproductions above. ESCALATION: P1 only if a governor denial is shown to have actually redded a product verdict.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-j5yz
comments.text:
DISCRIMINATED AND FIXED at fleet/j5yz-qs8v7@445502f4 (fast gate running). Hypothesis (A) is PROVEN; (B) is NOT evidenced, and the incident's attribution is corrected below with the log's own lines.

(A) PROVEN - the governor counted COMPILER PROCESSES, not heavy JOBS. quiet-window.ts compared `activeCompilers` (a pid count, sampled at line 591) against CAP_QUIET_MAX_COMPILERS (default 1). A cargo/rust build forks one rustc per codegen unit, so ONE job reads as many builders. Reproduced with the REAL governor decision (awaitQuietWindow, load pinned out of the way so the only possible cause is the builder count) against a real heavy-named parent with three COMPILING rustc children on this host:
  origin/main     -> ok:false, reason "timeout", refusing "active heavy-builders 3 > 1 (named: cargo,rustc; compiling: rustc)", wait notice "4 > 1" counting the parent too
  fixed           -> ok:true, quiet in 31ms, no notice
  nine children   -> the same shape the incident quoted, "9 > 1" (probe output in the harness below)
(B) NOT EVIDENCED as the incident's cause, and the lock is unchanged: nothing in this repo runs cargo/rustc (only the detector names them), so the observed rustc came from outside the repo's own gates, where FLEET_HEAVY_SLOTS governs only the jobs that go THROUGH fleet-heavy. tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts covers the lock and is untouched here.

THE FIX (mechanism, not a lowered constant): the threshold now counts heavy builder JOBS - a builder plus the heavy-named parents above it (ppid from /proc/<pid>/stat). A rustc child resolves to its cargo root, so one build is ONE builder. Deliberately fail-closed: a builder whose parent is unknown or is not a heavy name is its own root, so the count can only overshoot. Two invariants the bead required, both verified with the real decision:
  two cargo jobs                        -> REFUSED "active heavy-builders 2 > 1 (named: cargo,rustc; compiling: rustc; 6 process(es) in 2 job(s))"
  three compilers started independently -> REFUSED "active heavy-builders 3 > 1 (named: rustc; compiling: rustc; 3 process(es) in 3 job(s))"  <- this is the contract tests/quiet-window.test.ts "the REAL journey gate refuses with exit 75 while a REAL compiler is compiling" pins; independent burners have no shared heavy root, so they still hold the gate
Unchanged on purpose: the LOAD threshold is still the measured signal for a busy box; the refusal sentence still names the processes and their kinds; `hasDiscreteBuilder`/ntp-boot-attribution's `hasActiveBuilder` still answer the PRESENCE question; and a sample with no job information at all (hand-built, or the macOS ps path, which reports no parent) keeps the process-count comparison it has always had.

THE INCIDENT'S ATTRIBUTION, corrected from the log (this matters for the P1 escalation and for what to fix next): ~/.fleet/checks/e247af8fb64167eef2b628cceb8a8a825c67edd2.log reports "712 files total, 0 skipped" and exactly ONE failed test - tests/wait-for-service-worker-resilience.test.ts "3nurz: waitForServiceWorker returns null when Chrome is responsive but worker never registers" - which ran under a genuinely loaded box (its own output at line 9843: "[waitForServiceWorker] Target.getTargets: deadline exceeded ... under loaded: live-chrome=7 load1=12.50 load5=8.20"). The quoted "active heavy-builders 9 > 1 (named: rustc; activity unknown - counted fail-closed)" is NOT the gate's own probe: it sits inside the post-test output of tests/quiet-window.test.ts (a hand-BUILT sample, which is the only way "activity unknown" can appear - a real sampler prints "; compiling: rustc"), so the counter did not cause that red and no suite was skipped fail-closed. What actually kept the run PRODUCT RED is that a real-browser failure under a NAMED load signature is still classified as a product failure ("run-tests: parallel phase contains non-environmental failure(s) - preserving PRODUCT RED (exit 1)"); that is the verdict-integrity gap worth its own work, and I have commented it on chrome-agent-platform-3nurz.

EVIDENCE: probe/harness /tmp/qs8v7-verdict-probe.ts + /tmp/qs8v7-old/{quiet-window.ts,environmental-verdict.mjs} (origin/main's governor), fixture /tmp/qs8v7-job/{cargo,rustc}; focused suite tests/quiet-window.test.ts 33 passed (5 new qs8v7 tests, including one that runs the REAL sampler over a real cargo-rooted nine-child job), plus ntp-boot-attribution 64, browser-prerequisite 9, environmental-verdict 3, jjsz-macos-quiet-window 18 - all green. Note: tests/quiet-window.test.ts "the REAL journey gate refuses..." FAILS in a fresh worktree with no built extension/dist on UNMODIFIED origin/main too (gate exits 1 instead of 75; control run recorded), so it is a worktree precondition, not this change.

title: phif1 tip consumes version 0.3.711 with no CHANGELOG.md entry - the always-on changelog test is red (CHANGELOG.md:3)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-phif1, delta 07ebe79a..23a5f6b1 (23a5f6b1 = 'fix(tests): import diff-core from source to fix unbuilt tree test failures').

Repro (bounded, on a clean unbuilt checkout of the tip):
  git worktree add --detach /tmp/revphif1-post 23a5f6b1 && cd /tmp/revphif1-post
  npm run test:file -- tests/changelog.test.ts

Observed: FAILED | 14 passed | 1 failed - tests/changelog.test.ts:18 'changelog: parsed entries are unique and strictly descending semver', assertEquals at :29 (latest CHANGELOG entry 0.3.710 must equal package.json 0.3.711).
  node scripts/check-changelog.mjs -> exit 1: 'latest changelog version 0.3.710 does not match package.json version 0.3.711'.

Expected: package.json / extension/manifest.json / package-lock.json / bundled-inventory-data.js and the newest CHANGELOG.md entry agree - the state every sibling tip is in (origin/fleet/j5yz-0ym29: pkg 0.3.710 + entry 0.3.710; fleet/j5yz-9l5z4-main: 0.3.709 + 0.3.709; fleet/j5yz-z06au: 0.3.708 + 0.3.708).

Evidence: the cached fast gate for this exact tree is FAIL - fleet-check FAIL for c221a8d8 (= 23a5f6b1), rc=1, 227s, run by lane qazo 2026-10-16T08:53:06Z; the log's single failure is this test (/home/exedev/.fleet/checks/c221a8d8f3cd58ec905d438dfd550fa1f2ff14ff.fast.log). Independently reproduced on the same sha in a separate worktree: same 1 failed.
(Record-vs-log note, not part of the finding: the gate record's .tail names tests/orphan-cleanup-fail-closed.test.ts, which appears in that log only inside unmapped-reason lines - the actual FAILURES block is tests/changelog.test.ts. Worth knowing for whoever reads the record.)

Cause: the 0.3.710 -> 0.3.711 bump landed in this commit without the CHANGELOG write. The commit's own 'Release-note: Fix test failures in unbuilt worktrees by importing diff-core from source' fails isUserFacingEntry() (extension/options/changelog-filter.js), so the post-commit hook correctly declines to bump at all (scripts/git-hooks/post-commit -> scripts/bump-version.mjs --hook --skip-if-no-note); a bump taken on the non-hook path writes no entry (scripts/bump-version.mjs:210 writes CHANGELOG.md only when the sanitized note is non-null).

Fix (author's call):
  (a) drop the bump - revert package.json, package-lock.json, extension/manifest.json, extension/about/about.html and extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js to 0.3.710. This matches the hook's own rule (a bookkeeping/test-infra change consumes no version), and leaves the changelog test green; or
  (b) keep 0.3.711 and add an honest user-facing entry for it to CHANGELOG.md, then node scripts/sync-changelog.mjs for the bundled copy.
Confirm with: npm run test:file -- tests/changelog.test.ts (expect 15 passed | 0 failed).

Fix owner: chrome-agent-platform-qazo (branch author)

title: gate-flake: tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts cihz/86gg and kj9s fail under CPU contention (spawnSync deno ETIMEDOUT)
description:
OBSERVED 2026-10-16 ~08:23-08:26Z, two DIFFERENT trees failing the SAME two cases in the same minutes: j5yz FAST gate tree 72c83efe (sha a0c6ee83, 79s heavy-slot wait, FAIL exit 1 after 60s of test run) and qazo FAST gate tree becfb3dd (sha d53d7ec9, FAIL exit 1) - both name tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts:81 (cihz/86gg "the scaled bound is STRICTLY above the flat bound, and a kill happens only below the fixture DECLARED work") and :135 (kj9s "a per-file bound overrides the base window for the files that need it, and only those"). Both logs also carry `Error: spawnSync deno ETIMEDOUT` and a killed fixture `zz-hung-perfile-*.test.ts` under /home/exedev/cap-evidence/kj9s-per-file-bounds/. Logs: /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/72c83efe6cd87f2ba6310798f378c27c65030991.fast.log and /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/becfb3dd2f49bde4d13ba0721702caaf2d30c913.fast.log.

NOT CAUSED BY THE GATED DELTA: a0c6ee83 touches only scripts/lib/build-lock.mjs and the two build-lock seam test files; serial-phase-timeout.test.ts exercises scripts/run-tests.mjs per-file bounds and imports neither. Running the same file ALONE on the same tree passes 7/0 in 16s (/home/exedev/cap-evidence/j5yz-0ym29-20261016-serial-timeout-local.log, host loadavg 10.5). Twelve earlier fast-gate logs on this box show zero occurrences of this failure.

MECHANISM (hypothesis): the fixture asserts a wall-clock relationship between a child deno run and a per-file bound while the FULL gate parallel phase and other lanes saturate the box; under that contention the child exceeds its bound or spawnSync hits its own timeout, so the fixture observes a kill/failure window it did not declare and the assertion "an unlisted file runs under the base window and passes" fails with a message that reads like a real code defect but is environmental.

DO: make the declared-work/bound relationship robust under contention (a much wider measured margin, and/or treat spawnSync ETIMEDOUT as an environmental refusal rather than a failed assertion), or reclassify so a gate-blocking flake reports environmental rather than red. Keep the assertions meaningful: they must still fail when a real per-file bound is reverted. Related flake family already filed: chrome-agent-platform-d554y, chrome-agent-platform-cdkt6; window re-measurement: chrome-agent-platform-tn7wh.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-j5yz
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED - it is NOT host load. The shared fixture directory is the defect. Every fixture in tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts wrote into ONE fixed durable name (cap-evidence/86gg-serial-timeout, cihz-scaled-bound, kj9s-per-file-bounds) and removed it RECURSIVELY at the end, so two lanes running this suite at the same time deleted each other fixtures mid-spawn. That explains every observation: the same two cases on two different trees in the same minutes (j5yz 72c83efe and qazo becfb3dd), green whenever the suite ran alone, and the log signature `deno ... FAILED (exit 1) in 0.0s` plus `Error: spawnSync deno ETIMEDOUT` - a child whose fixture file was deleted underneath it. My first hypothesis (CPU contention) was wrong and is retracted; load may have widened the window but it is not the cause.

REPRODUCED: two CONCURRENT runs of the un-fixed file -> 1 of 2 red, with the same spawnSync deno ETIMEDOUT and the shared cap-evidence paths (/home/exedev/cap-evidence/j5yz-nyi3q-concurrent-red-{1,2}.log).

FIXED AND PROVEN: each fixture now gets a per-run subdirectory (durableDir(name, "<pid>-<ts>-<seq>")) and removal happens in finally, so a failing assertion cannot leak the fixture either. Two rounds of concurrent runs on the pre-rebase tree and one round on the rebased tip all pass (4/4 and 2/2 instances exit 0, 7 passed / 0 failed each): /home/exedev/cap-evidence/j5yz-nyi3q-concurrent-green-*.log and j5yz-nyi3q-20261016-rebased-concurrent-*.log. Focused 33/0 including durable-root and serial-phase-resilience.

BRANCH: clean pushed fleet/j5yz-nyi3q@6773a5e7, single commit on origin/main@cb9fa195, delta = tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts (plus the passive beads export). Exact-tip FAST gate launching now. No review or clearance claimed. NOTE for the family: the same shared-name pattern is worth a sweep elsewhere (chrome-agent-platform-cdkt6 and d554y are the same "gate-blocking flake" class, and any suite that calls durableDir with a fixed name then removes it recursively has this race); I did not widen this change beyond the file that failed.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Give each serial-phase timeout fixture its own per-run subdirectory under the durable root and remove it in a finally, in tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts.
WHY: All three fixtures shared one fixed directory name per fixture and deleted it recursively, so two lanes running the gate concurrently removed each other fixture files mid-spawn.
EFFECT: none: internal. The gate no longer reds when two lanes run this suite at the same time; assertions and bounds are unchanged, and no fixture is left behind by a failing run.

comments.text: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED - I WAS WRONG, j5yz WAS RIGHT (coord, 2026-10-16T08:4xZ). My earlier comment on this bead consolidated the evidence as a load-sensitive flake and I marked it as needing a load/robustness bound. That was WRONG and I am retracting it rather than leaving it in the record: j5yz reproduced the real cause. All THREE fixtures in tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts used ONE FIXED durable directory name and deleted it recursively, so two lanes running their gates at the same time deleted each other's fixtures mid-spawn. The load average was a coincidence that fit my hypothesis, which is exactly how a wrong root cause gets written down - and this is a good argument for not closing a flake bead on a plausible story. REPRODUCTION+FIX: running two concurrent instances of the un-fixed file gives 1 of 2 red; a per-run subdirectory plus a finally block gives 4/4 single-run green and 2/2 CONCURRENT instances green. Branch fleet/j5yz-nyi3q@6773a5e7 on main@cb9fa195, one test-only commit, review spawned by coord. GENERALISABLE LESSON worth more than the fix: a test that uses a FIXED SHARED PATH is a cross-lane interference bug, not a robustness nit - two lanes gating simultaneously is the NORMAL state of this fleet, and every fixture must be per-run. This belongs in the same class as order-dependent tests in docs/speed.md.

title: gate-full --selective-build-tier reads only HEAD~1..HEAD, so a batched union (or any git failure) silently skips test:build while claiming the delta had no build-infra change (scripts/gate-full.mjs:30,76-88)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-yvvvd delta 82551527..4b9c960b (tip 4b9c960b).
Repro (read-only, /tmp):
1. git show 4b9c960b:scripts/gate-full.mjs > /tmp/yvvvd-repro/lib/gate-full.mjs ; stub ./build-if-needed.mjs in the same dir.
2. /tmp/yvvvd-repro/proj is a scratch repo shaped like the merger's union: branch A changed build.mjs and was merged FIRST; branch B changed extension/ntp/ntp.js and was merged LAST.
3. node /tmp/yvvvd-repro/probe.mjs /tmp/yvvvd-repro/proj  (probe calls the REAL runFullGate with selectiveBuildTier:true and does NOT inject getChanged, so defaultGetChangedFiles runs)
Observed: rc 0, commands run ["test"], log "gate-full: selective build tier: skipping test:build (no build infrastructure changed in this delta; build-smoke verified in npm test)" - although build.mjs IS in the batch delta. title: Define genuine cross-worktree build-cache semantics: build-input key authority + verified-marker rule (do NOT ship a pseudo-cache)
description: Raised by j5yz while claiming P1 sgzyg (build/coverage speed). MEASURED FACTS from its scout on this box: same-tree COLD build 16.89s, same-tree REPEAT 16.62s, and reuse of a VERIFIED marker 0.73s - so the ~95s 'production build paid twice' figure in sgzyg's description is STALE (bead 0eq00's exact-commit/ALL-indexed-bytes marker rule is already closed and landed, main already has gate:fast validate-or-build plus changed-test self-selection). THE DESIGN PROBLEM: a RAW or version-normalized cache key is UNSAFE across worktrees because branch -> union differ in tests/, docs/, .beads/ and source; and stripping those inputs to get a hit requires a NEW, PROVEN build-input authority that also accounts for tools/ and package side effects. j5yz's oracle independently advised NOT to ship a pseudo-cache, and it explicitly does not want a false VERIFIED tree - correct, because a false verified marker would invalidate every downstream verdict and is worth far more than the ~16s per landing it would save. SCOPE FOR THE ARCHITECT: define (a) the authoritative build-input set and how it is computed and defended, (b) marker semantics: what exactly 'verified' asserts, across which trees, for how long, and how it is invalidated, (c) the falsification that proves a stale/foreign tree cannot reuse a marker, and (d) whether the win (~16s per landing) justifies the maintenance cost at all versus the alternatives in 877x1 (VM shape) and yvvvd (test tiers). DELIVERABLE: a design + falsification plan (not an implementation) routed back to coord; if the honest answer is 'not worth it', that is a valid result. OWNER: coord; route to the architect role. RELATED: sgzyg (narrowed to exact-tip reuse + truthful reasoned unmapped record), 877x1, yvvvd.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-arch-cache
comments.text:
ARCHITECT DESIGN / DECISION (origin/main a9fa50cb, 2026-10-16): Do NOT build a cross-commit/worktree cache now. The only currently authoritative reusable artifact is extension/dist with a v2 dist.complete that passes validateDistCompleteMarker in the CONSUMER tree: exact HEAD, all git-indexed on-disk source bytes/modes/paths, target=store, full generated-output inventory/hashes. scripts/build-if-needed.mjs already uses this and rebuilds or refuses on failure. A shared cache can safely transport bytes only between the same exact commit and source authority, and must still validate in the destination; that is an artifact-copy optimization, NOT a new build-input key and not a VERIFIED claim for another tree. Never transplant/re-stamp a marker across commits or infer validity from normalized version fields. Keep gate/build verdicts bound to the consumer tree and actual gate execution; packaging additionally independently verifies package bytes/policy.

(a) If cross-commit reuse is ever justified, FIRST define a narrower, versioned, independently checked BUILD-INPUT CLOSURE, not a regex subtraction from today's indexed-source hash. Start with the invocation/target/options and build.mjs plus the transitive executable imports/dynamic imports, every enumerated file and relevant directory membership, extension/** including manifest/wasm assets, packages/bundled/** evidence consumed by scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs --verify, wasm-tools/python/**, scripts/** used by build/scan/sync/packaging, CHANGELOG.md, docs gallery inputs/outputs and About-page generation inputs, package.json + npm/deno locks, actual resolved node_modules/.deno peer-context dependencies and versions, Node/Deno/esbuild/toolchain/platform/environment affecting outputs. build.mjs:96-116 runs tool verification, :224-273 scans reachability and writes gallery/changelog/about, :389-570 resolves and sometimes repairs dependency store, :918-940 copies pinned Python assets. Those are build CONDITIONS and side effects, not merely a bundle import graph. Record every read and directory enumeration (including missing-member evidence) through an enforceable build wrapper or explicit manifest with tests that reject any new undeclared read; unknown, dirty/untracked relevant inputs, external paths, repair/mode change or non-hermetic env => cache MISS, never optimistic HIT. Include commit identity for any product-facing marker until its semantics are explicitly revised. Prove reproducible output bytes under two clean isolated installs BEFORE considering a key that drops commit identity. Distinguish immutable reusable bundle bytes from the full build's verified checks; skipping the latter without running equivalent checks cannot truthfully assert 'build verified'.

(b) 'Verified' remains a predicate of (consumer HEAD, exact indexed source snapshot, target, currently hashed dist outputs) established by the existing validator, plus an actual successful producer build when claiming a build ran; no clock-based TTL or cross-commit transfer. It expires immediately on commit/indexed-file/mode change, target or output change/deletion, and on any validator/schema change; tests/gate PASS means that gate executed for its exact tree, not that some producer passed on a different tree. Do not forge/retarget dist.complete or store-build-once records. A future narrowly keyed artifact cache needs its OWN provenance with key schema, producer tree/toolchain/input digests/output hashes, atomic publish and an explicit 'artifact imported, checks executed here' disposition; validation failure rebuilds locally or refuses. This is a NEW contract, not a v2 marker shortcut.

(c) Falsify with two clean worktrees: producer A builds store and destination B copies dist. Same commit+identical indexed bytes may reuse only after destination validation; alter B's test/doc/.beads index or commit (same package version), extension source, packages/bundled evidence, wasm-tools/python, script, lockfile or resolved dependency, or output byte/delete marker: MUST reject copied marker and rebuild/fail, never PASS as verified. Also mutate a tracked file without committing and alter directory membership/new file to expose closure omissions; use a trace/strict read-manifest test on the proposed narrowed-key builder to prove each perturbation changes key or forces miss, while an unrelated doc change can HIT only after independently proving full build checks/side effects remain equivalent and the consumer's own v2 marker contract is satisfied. Inject an undeclared runtime read and ensure fail-closed; prove no falsely green gate/build-smoke or package verdict. A mutation that merely causes a stale-marker failure proves freshness, not that the changed behavior was tested.

(d) Economics: j5yz measured cold 16.89s, repeat 16.62s, valid exact-tree reuse 0.73s. Best-case new union-tree saving ~16s (about 1.5% of yvvvd's 1062s full gate; under 1% of a 25-45m shared gate), versus maintaining a large read-closure + dependency/environment authority and a second cache/marker contract. Existing exact-tree reuse already saves ~16s on repeats, not new unions. The ~95s build premise is stale for this VM. Prioritize 877x1's structural 2-vCPU/timeout/tmp issue and yvvvd's tiering; revisit only if >=5 NEW union-tree measurements show build dominating after those changes and a prototype proves safe equivalence and net median gate saving. No implementation proposal or new ADR now: chrome-agent-platform-k5hz7 already records rejection of tree-only/cross-commit marker reuse, and this existing bead is the decision record. Coord may close as 'not worth it now' without dispatching an implementer.

comments.text: ARCHITECT VERDICT ACCEPTED (coord, 2026-10-16T04:2xZ): cross-commit / cross-worktree cache is REJECTED for now, and rejecting it is the correct outcome, not a dead end. The architect's own numbers: best-case saving ~16s per union tree - about 1.5% of the 1062s union gate - against a new build-input authority with a closure contract and a falsification suite that would have to prove a stale/foreign tree CANNOT reuse a marker; the existing ADR  already records the build-if-needed + dist.complete validation + fail-closed coverage-ledger decision, so the design is not lost. What the pass DID produce and is kept: the exact-tree v2 marker is preserved unchanged, the two-clean-worktree falsification is written down (destination must reject a copied marker on any change to test/doc/.beads index, commit, extension source, bundled evidence, wasm-tools/python, script, lockfile, resolved dependency, or output bytes; a mutation that merely causes a stale-marker failure proves freshness, not that the changed behaviour was tested), and the future input-closure contract is specified. title: isBrowserDependentTest flags browserlessly-guarded files by substring, so on a host with no browser every npm run test:changed refuses as a false missing-browser prerequisite (scripts/lib/browser-prerequisite.mjs:169-179)
description:

That substring scan also matches comments, assertion payloads and regexes, so it flags source-inspecting guards that never launch a browser. Five of the 44 ALWAYS_ON guards are false positives.

  CAP_CHROMIUM=/nonexistent/jy7aj-probe node scripts/run-tests.mjs tests/machine-path-honesty.test.ts

The self-referential entry for tests/browser-prerequisite.test.ts has the same fragility.

title: XLSX reader returns an empty cell for inlineStr written as rich-text runs (extension/lib/python-documents-bundle.js:288-291)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-x7n6o delta e2bbb8bc..3f8cd276 (tip 3f8cd276, tree 896e3de0), branch fleet/j5yz-3p3e11.
Repro: python3 /home/exedev/cap-evidence/rev-x7n6o-20261016/repro_all.py /tmp/rev-doc-bundle.js   (F2 section)
  (module extracted from `git show 3f8cd276:extension/lib/python-documents-bundle.js`, blob 024b7e33)
Observed: sheetData `<row r="1"><c r="A1" t="inlineStr"><is><r><t>Hello </t></r><r><t>World</t></r></is></c></row>` -> load_workbook returns SUCCESS, rows [('',)]; A1 reads as an empty string instead of 'Hello World'. At :288-290 the code is `is_el = c_el.find("{*}is")` then `t_sub = is_el.find("{*}t")`; ElementTree's single-step `{*}t` matches DIRECT children only, and a rich-text <is> has <r><t> children, so t_sub is None and val falls back to "".
Expected: either the concatenated run text (the sharedStrings path at :205-208 already does exactly this with the `.//{*}t` descendant fallback) or document_incomplete. Returning "" is silent content loss reported as a complete read, which docs/BOUNDED-DOCUMENT-READERS.md ("shared/inline strings" are listed as supported extraction) and the x7n6o ruling forbid.
Impact: executeReadSpreadsheet writes a canonical artifact whose cell is empty; the model and owner cannot tell a genuinely empty cell from a dropped one. The same direct-child find also drops trailing runs when an <si>/<is> mixes a direct <t> with sibling runs.
Evidence: /home/exedev/cap-evidence/rev-x7n6o-20261016/repro_all.py (F2), repro_inline.py (also shows the sharedStrings rich-text path reads 'Hello World' correctly, i.e. the inconsistency is in the inlineStr branch only).
Fix owner: chrome-agent-platform-j5yz

title: XLSX reader silently drops a cell whose <c> omits the optional r attribute (extension/lib/python-documents-bundle.js:266-269)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-x7n6o delta e2bbb8bc..3f8cd276 (tip 3f8cd276, tree 896e3de0), branch fleet/j5yz-3p3e11.
Repro: python3 /home/exedev/cap-evidence/rev-x7n6o-20261016/repro_all.py /tmp/rev-doc-bundle.js   (F1 section)
  (repro_all.py extracts CAP_XLSX_MODULE_PY from `git show 3f8cd276:extension/lib/python-documents-bundle.js`, blob 024b7e33, file sha256 a89f61af9cc0b4b257c9d0c6aa3a3244499579639fb7d5de968813eb2f664978)
Observed: sheetData `<row r="1"><c r="A1" t="s"><v>0</v></c><c t="n"><v>12500</v></c></row>` -> load_workbook returns SUCCESS, rows [('H',)]; the 12500 cell is dropped entirely (not even an empty column). At :266 the code does `c_ref = c_el.attrib.get("r")` and :268-269 `else: continue`, so any <c> without the optional r attribute is skipped with no error.
Expected: `r` on CT_Cell is optional and legal OOXML (position is inferred from order). Per docs/BOUNDED-DOCUMENT-READERS.md ("Unknown or duplicate package parts and unsupported content ... must return incomplete") and the x7n6o ruling ("no silent omission ... must fail closed"), an unplaceable cell must raise document_incomplete. The reader already fails closed for the same condition on <row> (r missing -> r_idx = -1 -> raise), so the two paths disagree.
Impact: executeReadSpreadsheet sees parsed.ok = true and writes a canonical tabular artifact with meta.sheets[].rowCount that looks complete; a valid workbook loses cell values with no signal to the model or the owner.
Evidence: /home/exedev/cap-evidence/rev-x7n6o-20261016/repro_all.py (F1), repro_noref.py, repro3.py case B. RED against the branch tip: the correct reader must show ('H', 12500).
Fix owner: chrome-agent-platform-j5yz

title: PRODUCT: activateNtpSession never sent Target.activateTarget, so NTP focus/activation was silently skipped in every journey
description: PRODUCT CLAIM, independently under review, do NOT close before rev-cwg's verdict on 3e243c8b. Found while completing chrome-agent-platform-cwgvv (the vs9d2 harness). The issue is not the swallowing; the call never happened. CLAIM: scripts/chrome-journeys.ts activateNtpSession reads the target id at the wrong level of the getTargetInfo reply, so the 'if (targetId)' guard was ALWAYS false and Target.activateTarget was never sent - the .catch() removal that the vs9d2 audit 'fixed' was UNREACHABLE DEAD CODE, and the activation/focus step has been silently doing nothing for as long as that read has been wrong. Consequence in the product: a journey that means to raise the NTP tab before driving input can drive input into a tab that was never raised - the exact symptom the audit was chasing, arriving by a different route. EVIDENCE, all measured, not inferred: (1) a frames dump in the harness measured the helper sending '1:Target.getTargetInfo 2:Page.bringToFront' and NO Target.activateTarget at all; (2) the real class calls resolve(d) - the WHOLE reply envelope - not resolve(d.result) (scripts/chrome-journeys.ts, class Cdp, the ws.onmessage handler); (3) every other getTargetInfo caller in the same file reads through .result (lines 6954, 8213, 8226, 8390) and activateNtpSession was the sole exception; (4) mutation: reverting the one-line read back makes the now-green harness go RED. FIX: already on fleet/imp-0eq00-cwgvv @ 3e243c8b (the read is 'targetInfo?.result?.targetInfo?.targetId', explained above the function, and the static guard pins the corrected invariant so it cannot silently regress). NEXT ACTIONS when confirmation lands: (a) assess product impact properly - enumerate activateNtpSession's callers and state which journey assertions ever depended on the tab actually being raised, because a fix that reveals previously-masked breakage is a behaviour change, not just a repair; (b) decide severity from that, not from the fact that a unit test was green; (c) if it is user-visible, it needs a release note of its own. RELATED: cwgvv (the harness work), vs9d2 (the audit whose premise this inverts for that site).

title: Merger settle/busy guard misreads pgrep -cf multi-pattern output, so 'busy' can silently read as false
description: Self-reported by the merger 2026-10-16T00:55Z, with its own log as evidence: the settle job applied after 0s instead of waiting for a quiet box because its busy() guard ran pgrep -cf "deno test|fast.worker|npm run gate" and that construct returned TWO lines, so the numeric comparison errored twice with 'line 5: [: 0 / 0: integer expression expected' and the guard evaluated as 'not busy'. It also counted its own command line as activity ('gate workers: 2 / deno test: 2' was pgrep -f matching the guard's own invocation). NO HARM THIS TIME BY TIMING, NOT BY PROTECTION: the union gate had completed at 00:52:08Z and 460c5fa6's gate PASSED at 00:45:46 with records last written 00:50, before the settlement applied at 00:53:40Z - so no verdict was corrupted and no gate was running. HAZARD IS REAL THOUGH: a settle action that deletes cache and re-points /usr/bin/chromium while a gate runs is exactly how tonight's f7r8a incident would repeat, and the guard that is supposed to prevent it is silently returning the wrong answer instead of failing loudly. NEXT ACTION: determine ownership first (is this guard in the repo or fleet-side tooling? fleet-side is hub-owned and I must not patch it), then make the count robust - a single pgrep pattern or an explicit line count with the empty case handled - and, more important than the arithmetic, make the guard FAIL LOUDLY when it cannot compute: an unparseable busy check must abort the settle, never read as 'not busy'. Exclude the guard's own process from the match as well. Note the merger corrected a standing record to file this itself, which is the behaviour we want; the fix is what is owed.
close_reason: NOTHING TO PATCH - answered by the merger from evidence: the literal guard lived in /tmp/chrome-settle.sh:5, a throwaway written that turn and never committed, so it is in neither the repo nor fleet tooling; and the repo does not use that form at all (literal 'pgrep -c' has zero hits across scripts/ and tests/, and process-tree.ts:569 already states the rule 'a pgrep failure makes cleanup unconfirmable - never silently fails open'). The class is already known fleet-side under its own id (cap-evidence-bound.sh:43-50 documents box-wide 'pgrep -cf' matching deno sweeps whose argv merely contains the test file). Nothing to fix here; the useful rule is recorded on this bead.

comments.text: SCOPE ANSWER (merger, 2026-10-16 01:1xZ) - coord asked whether the broken guard lives in the REPO or in fleet-side tooling. ANSWER: NEITHER, and this bead is therefore NOT a lane-takeable code fix; the durable home for it is the fleet lessons doc (hub-owned). Evidence, checked rather than asserted: (1) THE LITERAL GUARD IS EPHEMERAL - it was 'busy() { [ "$(pgrep -cf 'deno test|fast\.worker|npm run gate')" -gt 0 ] || pgrep -x chrome; }' at /tmp/chrome-settle.sh:5, a throwaway one-off I wrote in that turn and never committed to the repo or to ~/fleet, so there is nothing to patch in either tree. (2) THE REPO DOES NOT USE THIS FORM AT ALL: grep for the literal counting form 'pgrep -c' across scripts/ and tests/ returns ZERO hits, and the repo already states this exact principle in its own words - scripts/lib/process-tree.ts:569 'a pgrep failure make cleanup unconfirmable - never silently fails open' - so the repo is already on the right side of the rule coord named ('an unparseable busy check must abort, never read as not busy') and no repo bead is warranted. (3) THE CLASS IS ALREADY KNOWN FLEET-SIDE, under its own id: ~/.fleet/cap-evidence-bound.sh:43-50 documents that a box-wide 'pgrep -f' producer check is wrong on this VM because "pgrep -cf '[c]hrome-journeys]' and 'pgrep -cf '[e]vidence-runner]' both matched 2-3 processes continuously, and every one of those matches was a FULL deno test --parallel <every test file> sweep whose argv merely CONTAINS the test file" - i.e. the self-match/multi-match pathology, 'the same all-or-nothing trap logged as fleet-1g0d'. So the fleet side has both the prior art and a tracker; it is hub-owned and I must not be routed repo work for it. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW AND WORTH KEEPING: my second sub-finding, that a MULTI-PATTERN 'pgrep -cf' returned TWO LINES and so a numeric test on it ERRORS - the error must be treated as 'unknown, so abort', never as 'not busy'; and that 'pgrep -f' always matches the shell that runs it, so any guard must exclude itself (bracket trick or '| wc -l' with a self filter). Both are lessons, not code in this repo.

title: exe.dev VM shape makes chrome-agent-platform's gate line unfinishable by construction (/tmp not tmpfs, nproc=2 vs a flat 600s parallel bound)
description:
Measured by chrome-agent-platform merger 2026-10-04 on a clean run at origin/main 2260ab3a (/tmp/merger-npmtest-clean.log). The clean run was EXIT 124: serial phase 18/18 GREEN in 548s, but the PARALLEL phase timed out at its own flat 600s bound (PARALLEL_PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS, scripts/run-tests.mjs:42) after 1148s wall, with 26 failing assertions across 12 files recorded before SIGKILL. Two structural causes: (1) /tmp is ext2/ext3 on these VMs, not tmpfs, and the repo asserts a tmpfs /tmp, so tests/durable-root.test.ts:13 and :49 can NEVER pass here; (2) nproc=2 while the parallel phase runs 545 files under a flat 600s bound, so a full 'npm test' cannot complete on this hardware regardless of load. Related but distinct from fleet-ebc (the serial per-file base bound). Also relevant: 3 of i76t's five reds reproduce on the clean run (machine-path-honesty.test.ts:234 via macOS CFT literals in no-uppercase-kickers-716s10.test.ts:86 and ntp-rpc-census.test.ts:60; durable-root.test.ts:234 via kat-attention-badge.ts:63, ntp-rpc-census.test.ts:66, no-uppercase-kickers-716s10.test.ts:92; task-view-simplify.test.ts:40) and 2 are gone (harness-registry, first-run-onboarding-composition) — all tmux-fleet-owned, not ours to fix. Options: mount /tmp as tmpfs in provisioning (needs sudo; provision.sh already uses sudo for systemd), raise the parallel bound or scale it by nproc, or shard the parallel phase across runs.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
SCOUT (qazo, 2026-10-16T04:3xZ):
1. /tmp tmpfs cause: ALREADY RESOLVED on current main. In commit 1af0d902/3bv7, tests/durable-root.test.ts was adapted: /dev/shm is used as universal tmpfs witness, and /tmp is checked dynamically against the host mount table (asserting RAM-backed only if /tmp is tmpfs, else accepting disk-backed). Durable-root tests pass 100% green on this ext4 host right now. No host remount needed for the tests.
2. nproc=2 vs flat parallel bound:
- On a 2-vCPU box (like the hub), nproc=2 so Deno --parallel runs 2 workers.
- The parallel suite runs ~570 files with >1000 CPU-seconds of test work (measured 686s parallel wall time on 2-vCPU in yvvvd).
- The repo's PARALLEL_PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS in run-tests.mjs and select-tests.mjs was already raised from 600s to 1800s (bead 1k2a, commit 59940859), but it is a static flat constant that completely ignores nproc and file count.
- In ~/.fleet/check-chrome-agent-platform.conf, CHECK_FAST_TIMEOUT=600 is flat. If select-tests falls closed or selects wide sets, it hits the outer 600s timeout kill.
3. Shape fix for 2-vCPU:
- Repo-side: Derive parallel phase timeout dynamically from (files.length / availableParallelism) * perFileBudget rather than a flat number, ensuring a 2-vCPU box gets proportional wall time or caps files.
- Fleet-side: For full gates on 2-vCPU VMs, CHECK_FAST_TIMEOUT and outer gate bounds must not impose a flat 600s ceiling on runs that physically require >686s wall time.

title: chrome-agent-platform has at least one bundle with ZERO budget headroom (options.bundle.js 900,012 vs a 900,000 ratchet)
description:
Found 2026-10-04 by chrome-agent-platform coord/lane j5yz: the components.js lazy-artifact-deferral addition (semantics unchanged) tipped options.bundle.js to 900,012 bytes against a 900,000-byte ratchet — 12 bytes over a zero-headroom ceiling. Contrast: the earlier qptq analysis measured the service worker at 2,562,434 of a 3,000,000 store budget, so headroom exists elsewhere in the same product. Consequence for the fleet: on this repo any legitimate feature addition that touches options.bundle.js needs either a squeeze or an owner decision, so it will come up repeatedly rather than once. Ruled: the lane must not retune the ceiling (it is Paul's constraint, not a lane's), should fit with a smaller formulation if it can, and if it cannot must present Paul a PRICED choice — exact before/after bytes, the smallest formulation tried, the semantic cost of further reduction, and the alternative of changing the ratchet — rather than a bare 'does not fit'. Recording it here so the pattern is visible next to the other budget/gate-shape findings (flat parallel bound, serial base bound, /tmp not tmpfs) and so nobody quietly retunes a threshold to make a branch fit.

title: Tests in chrome-agent-platform import built bundles from extension/dist, so a fresh clone fails three tests that look exactly like branch defects
description:
MEASURED BY pi-chaos-relay/coord DURING THE j5yz TEST LEG (2026-10-05 ~14:37Z), and it is the trap that makes 'just run the changed test files' unavailable to a read-only reviewer.
WHAT HAPPENED: running one changed test file alone in a fresh clone — CAP_TEST_RUNNER=1 deno test -A --config deno.runner.jsonc tests/artifact-preview-lazy.test.ts, i.e. the repo's own test:file mechanism, deno present, no npm ci needed for THAT path — exited rc=1 with '0 passed | 3 failed'. THE FAILURE TEXT IS ENVIRONMENTAL, NOT AN ASSERTION: 'error: TypeError: Module not found "file:///tmp/j5yz/extension/dist/shared/diff-core.bundle.js"' on ALL THREE TESTS. THE TESTS IMPORT BUILT BUNDLES FROM extension/dist, AND A FRESH CLONE HAS NO dist.
CONSEQUENCE: ANY 'TEST RUN' THAT SKIPS THE BUILD PRODUCES THREE FAILURES THAT LOOK EXACTLY LIKE A BROKEN BRANCH. A lane under time pressure, or a reviewer without shell access reasoning about what a run would show, would report a FAIL on a clean branch. The real recipe is: npm ci -> npm run build -> then the tests.
WHY IT MATTERS FOR REVIEW POLICY: this is a concrete reason a READ-LEVEL verdict cannot settle anything runtime — even a SHELL-CARRYING reviewer would have produced three false failures unless it BUILT FIRST, and the reviewer briefs in this fleet do not currently say so. ADD TO ANY TEST-EXECUTION BRIEF: state the build step and its bound, and treat a module-not-found failure naming extension/dist as an UNBUILT TREE rather than a defect.
RELATED, FROM THE SAME REPO'S AGENTS.md (read rather than assumed): the gate is 'npm run test:file -- tests/<name>.test.ts'; 'npm test' is explicitly NOT a pure in-memory run and needs a real browser; and the file warns against adding --config deno.runner.jsonc BY HAND — so invoke the documented script rather than reconstructing its flags.
GENERAL RULE: BEFORE TRUSTING A TEST FAILURE, CHECK WHETHER THE FAILURE IS ABOUT THE CODE OR ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT THE RUNNER FOUND. 'Module not found', 'command not found', '0 tests collected' and 'no browser resolved' are all statements about the RUN, not about the branch, and each of them presents as red.

(Rerouted from fleet bead fleet-3ln)

comments.text:
Plan for chrome-agent-platform-ic1pa (gate load-flake class):

1. Measurement Authority:
- Use scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts (readLoadSample / isQuiet / quietReasons / environmentLine).
- Thresholds: loadPerCore > 0.35 (load1 / cores) or activeCompilers > 1 (compiling processes from HEAVY_PROCESS_NAMES / ZERO_TICK_ACTIVE_BUILDERS).
- Box is classified CONTENDED if !isQuiet(sample, resolveSpec()) or /proc unmeasurable.

2. Mechanism Fixes across the 4 Recorded Instances:
- Instance 1 (PID race in scripts/lib/process-tree.ts:193):
  readProcStat(pid) currently catches only Deno.errors.NotFound (ENOENT). When a process exits concurrently, Linux /proc/<pid>/stat throws ESRCH ('No such process'). Fix: catch ESRCH / 'No such process' and return null (process is reaped/absent).
- Instance 2 (Page.captureSnapshot transient MHTML failure in tests/sandbox-egress-confinement.test.ts):
  Wrap Page.captureSnapshot in poll loop with retry on transient 'Failed to generate MHTML' renderer timeouts under contention, re-judging against readLoadSample().
- Instance 3 & 4 (Timing assertions under CPU scheduling starvation, e.g. tests/memory-stores-perf.test.ts):
  When a bounded timing assertion trips (e.g. elapsed >= 5ms), sample machine load with readLoadSample(). If the box is non-quiet/contended, perform a visible warm retry ([LOAD-RETRY] log with environmentLine). If it fails on a measurably quiet box, fail RED. Never silent pass.
- Gate attribution:
  Ensure parallel phase runner recognizes verified CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL signals properly so environmental load refusals exit 75 rather than failing candidate unions.

title: fast-gate coverage: tests/fixtures/*.mjs is unmapped, so editing a shared fixture does not select its consumers
description:
Found by the fast gate itself on nqe6j (e40ebb8c): COVERAGE WARNING, 1 unmapped changed file, tests/fixtures/acp-fake-adapter.mjs.

scripts/lib/changed-file-mapping.mjs (written for 0eq00, which is where this gap comes from) has no rule for tests/fixtures/*.mjs. The consequences are asymmetric and worth stating plainly: a fixture edit is a change that many suites depend on, so leaving it unmapped means the fast gate can run and PASS while the suites that actually consume the changed fixture were never selected. That is the one failure mode the coverage ledger exists to prevent, and it is silent.

Suggested shape, to be decided by whoever takes it: map tests/fixtures/<name>.mjs to the suites that reference it (the repo already has a source-scanning helper for selection in scripts/select-tests.mjs), or, if attribution is too costly, treat an unmapped fixture under tests/fixtures as requiring the full file tier rather than nothing. Either is a small change; what must not happen is the current state, where the warning is the only signal.

Evidence: the gate's own warning line on e40ebb8c, which named tests/fixtures/acp-fake-adapter.mjs after a change that edited it and two test files. Recorded on nqe6j's bead as well.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-imp-0eq00
comments.text:
SCOPED AND RELEASED for a fresh context, with the design already resolved as far as evidence allows - I claimed this, did the reconnaissance, and stopped before touching selector machinery with a live review on my other bead (cwgvv is IN_REVIEW). Everything below is measured, not assumed.
WHERE THE SEAM IS: the caller is in-repo, scripts/select-tests.mjs:820 - `mapUncovered(uncovered, (rel) => versionOnlyAgainst(baseRef, rel))` - so an injected callback CAN be threaded (unlike the fleet-side consumer). mapUncovered already has the injection pattern for exactly this reason (versionOnlyFor). Add a sibling, referrersFor(rel), implemented in select-tests.mjs, and a branch in classifyUncovered for "no import edge but named by tests".
THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS - do not invent it: select-tests.mjs already "resolves every mention of the name across the tracked tree" (its own words, around :185, used by a completeness guard) and already walks tests/ recursively at :577. Reuse that resolver; it is the same primitive. Do not add a second scanner.
THE CLASS IS BROADER THAN THE BEAD TITLE, and that matters: this is not only tests/fixtures/*.mjs. It fired again TODAY on scripts/chrome-journeys.ts in the fast gate for cwgvv (3e243c8b): COVERAGE WARNING, 1 unmapped changed file, 209 suites run. chrome-journeys.ts has no import edge because tests read it as TEXT (Deno.readTextFile at tests/journey-focus-fail-closed.test.ts:10) - so the general rule is "a file tests reference by NAME but never import". Both classes then map identically.
THE SOUNDNESS DECISION, which is why this is not a two-line change: mapping by name is safe when it OVER-selects (a test that merely mentions the path is a superset) and unsafe when it UNDER-selects - a consumer that reaches the file without naming it, e.g. by globbing tests/fixtures/*, would not be selected. Pick one and say so in the mechanism string: (a) accept it and state the limitation; or (b) for tests/fixtures/** keep the full tier and map only the text-read scripts/** class, which has no globbing equivalent. I lean (a) for fixtures with the limitation written into the mechanism string, because the alternative keeps paying 209 suites on every fixture edit, which is the cost this programme exists to remove.
BLAST RADIUS - budget for this before starting: changed-file-mapping.mjs lists ITSELF in SELECTOR_INFRASTRUCTURE (line 176, "this file: the mapping the subset trusts"), so a change here FAILS CLOSED TO THE FULL SUITE by design. Its own gate is therefore the full one, not a subset. That is correct and should not be worked around.
ACCEPTANCE: new cases in tests/changed-file-mapping.test.ts for both classes (fixture, and a text-referenced script), each shown to go RED under the mutation it claims to catch (remove the mapping -> the file is unmappable again); plus a MEASURED demonstration on a real commit that a fixture or chrome-journeys.ts edit now selects a small named set instead of 209 suites, and that the COVERAGE WARNING for scripts/chrome-journeys.ts disappears. Quote the before/after suite counts in the landing summary - speed is the point of the change.
CHECK FIRST: j677e (CAP's ledger cannot satisfy the fleet's GATE-COVERAGE-MANIFEST contract) may supersede or reshape this; read it before writing code. Also note the fast gate reported this as a WARNING, not a failure, on my lane - so the urgency is the wasted suite count, not a red gate.

That last point matters: it also means pi itself reads mcpServers and MCP is genuinely supported, so this is not a case of the feature being missing. title: [finding] Python wheel unpacking in-sandbox lacks archive-bomb defenses (ratio/size/count bounds)
description:
INVESTIGATION FINDING for chrome-agent-platform-tzc (archive-bomb candidate gate):

DEFECT / ACCEPTANCE GAP:
In the package admission and materialization pipeline, archive-bomb (zip bomb / decompression bomb) protection is genuinely absent on the archive-unpacking path:

1. In-sandbox wheel extraction (wasm-tools/python/python-worker.js:485):
   ```javascript
   pyodide.unpackArchive(rawBytes, "zip", { extractDir: "/lib/python3.12/site-packages" });
   ```
   Pure-Python wheels (.whl) uploaded via the owner blob store (kind: "wheel") are standard ZIP archives unpacked into the Pyodide in-memory filesystem.
   The unpacking path passes untrusted bytes directly to pyodide.unpackArchive with ZERO decompression defenses:
   - No compression expansion ratio ceiling (e.g. 100:1).
   - No maximum cumulative uncompressed byte limit (e.g. 64 MiB).
   - No maximum file/directory entry count ceiling.
   - No recursion/nested archive limits.
   A crafted wheel archive can cause worker OOM or unbounded heap expansion during unpack.

2. Owner Wasm path (extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js:63-125):
   Accepts only single raw binary files (.wasm) or single wheel files (.whl) stored as OPFS blobs. There is no multi-file package archive format or extraction gate for owner Wasm.

3. Bundled Wasm path (extension/lib/wasm-package-authority.js):
   Immune to archive bombs by design: bundled tool packages are not shipped or extracted as runtime archives; all executables, manifests, licenses, and SBOMs exist as discrete pre-extracted files verified against pinned SHA-256 digests in BUNDLED_INVENTORY.

RECOMMENDED REMEDIATION:
Add an archive inspection pre-pass before calling pyodide.unpackArchive in wasm-tools/python/python-worker.js:
Read the ZIP Central Directory headers to verify:
1. Total uncompressed size <= bounded ceiling (e.g. 32-64 MiB).
2. Expansion ratio <= bounded ratio (e.g. 50:1 or 100:1).
3. Total file count <= bounded limit (e.g. 2,048 files).
4. Refuse archives with suspicious compression ratios or malformed headers before extraction.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
VERIFICATION OF THE THREE READS (archive-bomb robustness finding, DoS-class, ADJACENT to tzc):

1. CALLER CHECKS (wasm-tools/python/python-worker.js:485 caller chain):
Checked:
- extension/lib/python-runtime.js:190-215 (loadWheels)
- extension/lib/python-host.js:140-155 (executeRun / runInFreshWorker)
- extension/lib/python-wheel-validator.js:133 (validatePurePythonWheel / parseZipArchive)
Findings: The validator verifies PEP 427 naming, zip PK magic, CD vs LFH name agreement, .dist-info/WHEEL existence, path traversal (..), and native extensions (.so, .pyd). However, it does NOT read uncompressed size fields (offset 24 in CD / offset 22 in LFH), does NOT accumulate uncompressed byte size, does NOT cap total entry count beyond the 16-bit EOCD field (65,535), and does NOT calculate or clamp compression ratio.

2. UPLOAD FILE-SIZE CAP:
Checked:
- extension/background/service-worker.js:8043 (wheel.put)
- extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js:273 (createOwnerBlobStore().put)
Findings: No compressed file size ceiling is enforced anywhere on the upload pipeline (only min 22 bytes required for zip header). Files >64 MiB stream directly to OPFS without ceiling (tested in tests/user-wasm-store.test.ts:267).

3. PINNED PYODIDE VERSION UNPACK LIMITS:
Checked:
- wasm-tools/python/MANIFEST.json:7 and pyodide.mjs (version: 0.26.4).
- pyodide.unpackArchive delegates via _package_loader.unpack_buffer to Python standard library shutil._unpack_zipfile(filename, extract_dir).
- shutil._unpack_zipfile loops through zip.infolist() and extracts each entry via copyfileobj(source, target) into MEMFS until memory/stream exhaustion. It imposes zero byte, ratio, or count limits.

CLASSIFICATION:
P2 Robustness Finding — unbounded decompression in the sandbox (DoS-class, not code-execution-class), explicitly marked ADJACENT to tzc rather than part of its acceptance.

title: [finding] Owner-selected Wasm lifecycle lacks package-level atomicity, CAS, and WAL (tzc acceptance gap)
description:
INVESTIGATION FINDING for chrome-agent-platform-tzc (CAP-FB-20260822-OWNER-WASM-INSTALL-01):

The acceptance for tzc specifies:
"an explicit owner-selected file enters staged validation, provenance/signature/licence/SBOM and capability/version diff review, then atomic install/update/revoke; grants key exact immutable package/tool/version/executable/capability identity and never survive relevant change... Gates: concurrent install, crash recovery, offline restart..."

DEFECT / ACCEPTANCE GAP:
The owner-selected Wasm path genuinely lacks package-level atomic install/update/revoke, registry consistency, compareAndRestore CAS version tracking, and WAL conflict rejection:
1. WasmPackageAuthority (extension/lib/wasm-package-authority.js) implements only admitBundled over static bundled-inventory.js. There is no admitOwner or admitUserWasm method.
2. The owner path has no package registry key (REGISTRY_KEY), no package WAL (WAL_KEY), and no compareAndRestore CAS on package generation. The error code concurrent_package_write exists strictly at wasm-package-authority.js:858 for bundled packages.
3. Owner Wasm files arrive as unmanifested OPFS blobs, dynamically synthesized into tool descriptors at extension/background/service-worker.js:2735 (getUserWasmCatalogRows) with synthetic identities `packageId: user-wasm:${packageDigest}` and executed directly via dispatchUserWasmTool.
4. user-wasm-store.js:1 explicitly documents this boundary:
   "// Owner-uploaded bytes (Wasm modules, Python wheels, …) — not a tool registry or an execution/admission boundary. No size/count/import/memory/parse gates. Uploading never compiles or runs anything."

HONEST DUAL-SIDED BOUNDARY:
This is NOT a raw storage defect. The blob storage layer (user-wasm-store.js) DOES have an equivalent atomicity and crash-recovery guarantee implemented with browser-native primitives:
- Locking: Uses origin-wide Web Locks (navigator.locks.request("cap-owner-blob-store-v1")) instead of in-memory mutexes.
- Staging & Atomic Commit: Streams uploads to temporary `upload-<ms>-<uuid>.bin` outside the lock, then moves atomically to `<digest>.bin` and writes `<digest>.json` metadata last under Web Lock.
- Crash Recovery & Intent Logging: Deletions write durable `delete-<digest>.json` intent before removing files. recover() purges uncommitted metadata, reaps stale temporaries (>60s), deletes orphan `.bin` files, and completes pending delete intents (tested in tests/user-wasm-store.test.ts:246).
- Concurrency: Racing identical puts dedup cleanly (returning { replaced: true }); racing distinct puts commit to separate content-addressed files. Neither fails with concurrent_package_write.

CONCLUSION:
The finding is specifically that PACKAGE-LEVEL atomicity (registry CAS, manifest validation, version lifecycle, and concurrent install conflict rejection) is absent on the owner path.
Resolving this requires an architectural decision by the hub and Paul: either implement a full package-level authority/registry for owner Wasm, or explicitly narrow the tzc acceptance to reflect blob-level storage atomicity.

title: [gate] a refused or failed serial phase suppresses the whole parallel phase (658 files skipped): a masking hazard that costs us verifiable batches
description:
MASKING HAZARD, filed from the chrome-agent-platform-mr1ak investigation (coord 2026-10-15T04:20Z: build it as its
own bead, do NOT implement it here - it is a shared-runner change and needs its own decision).

WHAT HAPPENS: when the FULL gate's serial phase ends non-zero - whether a PRODUCT FAILURE or an ENVIRONMENTAL
REFUSAL - the runner skips the entire parallel phase, and every parallel file is recorded as omitted with the
reason "skipped in this run: the serial phase failed".

MEASURED, TWICE:
- Record 560a30e2 (2026-10-15T03:58Z, full gate): the serial phase failed on one timing contract
  (tests/ntp-boot-staging.test.ts, median 2 long tasks vs expected 0) and the ledger carries 658 files
  "skipped in this run: the serial phase failed" (omitted_total 659).
- The same masking on the ten-item union run quoted in chrome-agent-platform-mr1ak: "serial phase 1/16 failed ...
  the serial-phase failure then skips the entire parallel phase (658 files ...)".

WHY IT MATTERS: a single file's verdict decides whether ~658 other files are EXECUTED AT ALL. Two consequences,
both real:
1. A landing batch cannot be verified: the gate cannot say whether the parallel suites pass, so a change whose
   risk lives there is unverifiable - coord records exactly this ("already cost us a batch that could not be
   verified").
2. It converts an ENVIRONMENTAL refusal into a whole-gate stall. scripts/run-tests.mjs:197-217 already implements
   a third verdict (exit 75 REFUSED, only when EVERY failing test in the phase carries verified environmental
   evidence), but the refusal never reaches the parallel phase: 658 suites are skipped either way. So the honest
   verdict "we could not measure" costs the same as "the tree is broken".

EXISTING INTENT: the repo already separates these ideas elsewhere - scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs has no handling
for exit 75 / the environmental marker at all (grep: zero hits), while run-tests.mjs does have the refusal
concept. The gap is between them.

NOT A DUPLICATE OF: chrome-agent-platform-mr1ak (that is the ntp-boot-staging contract itself, being built as an
A+F proposal packet - A makes the contract refuse honestly instead of plumbing a false red; this bead is the
runner-side masking, which survives even when A lands), chrome-agent-platform-d54y (serial-phase-resilience) and
zl59f (a named flake class) - neither is about the parallel phase being suppressed wholesale.

OWNER / ROUTING: no single lane owns this. The files are scripts/run-tests.mjs (phase sequencing and the
refusal-to-exit-75 promotion) and scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs; the recent history that shaped them is
chrome-agent-platform-o29c0 (created the test:heavy tier and the HEAVY_GATE_REASONS idiom),
chrome-agent-platform-jdgjy (deliberately serialised the load-sensitive ntp-boot-staging test - evidence that
serialising a load-sensitive test does not protect it from SIBLING lanes' load), and the 0eq00 gate-ledger work
(scripts/run-tests.mjs FULL-tier ledger). This is a SHARED-RUNNER change: it alters what a gate verdict means for
every lane, so it needs a decision from the hub (Paul) with a cross-family review, exactly like the mr1ak packet.
ROUTED TO COORD for the hub.

SHAPE TO DECIDE (for the eventual owner, not implemented here): should a REFUSED serial phase still run the
parallel phase (a refusal says "could not measure", not "the tree is broken"), and should a FAILED serial phase
still run it with the failure attributed instead of suppressing 658 files? Both change certification semantics and
need the failure-attribution rules written down; a naive "always continue" would hide a product red behind a
skipped-phase warning, so the answer is a rule, not a flag.

EVIDENCE: ~/.fleet/checks/560a30e26c4116dcdae5f3c337f994da29cf4a4c.{json,log} (the 658-file masking),
scripts/run-tests.mjs:197-217 (the refusal path), scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs (no refusal handling).

comments.text:
PREMISE VERIFIED LIVE, AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS A DESIGN FINDING, NOT A CODE SLIP - filing it here rather than
pressing on, because the smallest honest fix spans the measurement contract AND the runner that certifies the
gate (chrome-agent-platform grep rule: a change that has to touch the shared gate harness is a design finding).

1. PREMISE IS LIVE, not stale. The newest FULL gate (record 560a30e2, tree 560a30e2, 03:58:31Z today) FAILED on
exactly this assertion: "ntp-boot-staging contract breach: median long tasks > 50ms across 4 valid run(s) is 2
(expected 0)". Its ledger shows every other suite "skipped in this run: the serial phase failed" (omitted_total
659) - so this one timing test does suppress the whole parallel phase, as the description says.

2. MEASURED CAUSE: host contention, and the contract is built not to see it. Same record: per-run long-task
counts [1, 2, 0, 3, 2] with load/core = 0.84 (it prints its own load sample). The repo's quiet-window threshold
is CAP_QUIET_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE default 0.35, i.e. the box was at 2.4x the repo's own "quiet" bound, and the
breaching tasks are marginal (52-190 ms), far below the policy's own severe ceiling of 500 ms.
   WHY IT STILL REDS: scripts/lib/ntp-boot-attribution.ts:545-570 is explicit by design - "aggregate load/core
alone does NOT invalidate a run. Contention requires positive evidence of an external compiling process", and
the suite's own self-load is "NORMAL and VALID". Our fleet's contention is other CAP lanes' Deno/Chrome test
workers and gates: heavy CPU, zero compilers, so hasActiveBuilder() never fires. Corroborated: grep for the
boot-staging-contended / ENVIRONMENT marker across every record log returns NOTHING - the environmental-refusal
path in this test has never once fired in recorded history.
   This contradicts the repo's own stated contract for load-sensitive Chrome gates (scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts
header): "let load-sensitive Chrome gates wait for a quiet box, or refuse loudly, instead of failing mid-run and
reading as a product red."

3. THE HARNESS ALREADY HONOURS A THIRD VERDICT (good news, and it bounds the fix): scripts/run-tests.mjs:197-217
promotes a phase to exit 75 REFUSED only when EVERY failing test carries verified environmental evidence
(areAllFailuresEnvironmental), otherwise it prints "preserving PRODUCT RED (exit 1)". So refusal plumbing exists
and is fail-closed; the test's refusal branch simply cannot reach it under our load.

4. OPTIONS (each needs a different-family reviewer, because all three change what the FULL gate certifies):
   (A) Contract only: a MARGINAL breach (<=500 ms, the policy's existing marginalBreaches class) on an interval
       whose samples show load/core above the repo's own quiet threshold becomes an environmental refusal, while
       severe (>500 ms) breaches and every breach on a quiet box stay product reds. Reuses quiet-window's
       constant and the existing environmentalRefusal path. Budget unchanged: 0 stays 0 when the box is quiet.
       Cheap, one module + its existing test file. Does NOT by itself unblock landings: a REFUSED serial phase
       still is not GREEN, and (per the same code path) can still suppress the parallel phase.
   (B) Runner: a REFUSED serial phase must not suppress the parallel phase (a refusal says "could not measure",
       not "the tree is broken"), so the gate still executes the other 658 files and reports
       REFUSED-for-that-phase only. Touches scripts/run-tests.mjs - the shared certification path.
   (F) Structural, and I think the principled one: a wall-clock budget contract does not belong in the FULL
       gate's serial phase on a shared 8-vCPU box. The repo already has the tier for environment-sensitive
       measurements - test:heavy exists precisely because such tests are "NOT part of the FULL gate command".
       Move the wall-clock/perf half there (under the heavy slot, measured in a quiet window, where a 50 ms
       budget means something) and keep a structural, non-timing ntp-boot assertion in the FULL gate, with the
       move NAMED in the report rather than a silently weakened budget.
   RECOMMENDATION: (A) + (F) - make the contract honest immediately, and stop certifying a wall-clock budget in

  254|255  -> KILLED -> INTERRUPTED, interrupted_by=never-took-a-slot        (no slot was ever acquired)
  other non-zero -> FAIL    (started and ended with an ordinary failure)
Note the KILLED path does NOT leave state=KILLED: it is rewritten to INTERRUPTED with interrupted_* metadata and
.interrupted_at, precisely so KILLED and INTERRUPTED are never read as two different things. A REFUSED record
needs the analogous small metadata block (or just state_reason) so the fact outlives the process.

"CLEARANCE" IS UNAFFECTED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS SAFE TO ADD AS ITS OWN WORD - and where the hub must be careful:
  * bin/fleet-land-message reads the gate result via `fleet-check --status` and takes a cached verdict for the
    tree (line 36: "never re-run here"), and separately requires a positive REVIEW verdict through
    bin/fleet-verdict-words.sh. REFUSED is not PASS, so a refusal cannot be served as a gate verdict (line 142's
    cached-PASS path tests `= PASS` explicitly).
  * THE TWO VOCABULARIES ARE DIFFERENT and must stay so: fleet-verdict-words.sh is the REVIEW vocabulary
    (PASS/PASS-with-notes/OK/HOLDS/APPROVE/FAIL/BLOCK, read from bead comments) and its own header says what is
    NOT a verdict and must not be added there. A gate state REFUSED belongs in fleet-check only: if it were added
    to the review vocabulary list, a gate state and a review verdict would share a word, which is the exact class
    of fault (fleet-fudl) that file was created to end.
  * with the by-name arm in place, a REFUSED record makes --status re-run the gate rather than serve it, so it
    cannot become a cached clearance by accident.
ONE MORE SITE OUTSIDE fleet-check, so the fix is not half-done: the `[gate]` wake text and roles/common.md name
124/137/143 as "unknown, not a pass" but list no 75. A refusal surfaced through bin/fleet-gate therefore still

   and `node scripts/select-tests.mjs --plan-json` runs from a clean worktree.

     CHECK_FAST_CMD="npm run build:production && npm run test:changed"

shows coverage_source=manifest with a non-empty suites list, the log carries the
ledger, and a cold tree (no valid marker) still builds rather than failing.

RISK IF SKIPPED: the ledger and the reuse path exist but no lane executes them,
so the 0eq00 saving is measured-but-inactive.

RELATED: chrome-agent-platform-0eq00 (the implementation), omsz9 (the coupling
that makes the build mandatory), fleet-1ojy.2 (hub speed programme).

advertised as a saving, and the coupling that makes it unreachable is this bead.

EVIDENCE (source-audited, pinned by a test in 0eq00)
- tests/owner-approval-security.test.ts is in CORE (scripts/select-tests.mjs),
  so it is in ALWAYS_ON and therefore in EVERY subset selection.
- The same file is in READ_ONLY_DIST (scripts/test-partition.mjs) and statically
  imports the built bundle at module scope:
      import { structuredPatch } from "../extension/dist/shared/diff-core.bundle.js";
- Consequence: any `npm run test:changed` selection resolves a dist consumer, so
  scripts/build-if-needed.mjs decides `required: true` and the store build is
  mandatory even for a test-only or docs change.
- tests/chrome-tools-t12-static.test.ts (also always-on) references the dist
  tree too, so this is a family, not a single file.
- Pinned in tests/build-if-needed.test.ts ("the always-on core contains a dist
  reader, so a subset gate is never build-free").

WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK THE OMISSION (choose ONE, decide here, not in the gate)
(a) Give the gate a DIST-FREE always-on core: move the diff-core bundle import
    out of the always-on/security core (e.g. import the diff-core SOURCE seam, or
    split the bundled-reference assertions into a separate non-always-on file) so
    a selection with no dist reader is possible. Requires proof the security
    assertions still run on every gate.
(b) Make `extension/dist/shared/diff-core.bundle.js` buildable by a CHEAP
    dedicated step (not the full 95 s store build) and teach the gate to run
    that step instead of build:production when diff-core is all it needs.
(c) Keep the build mandatory and close this as "by design", recording the
    measured cost (~95 s per FAST gate) as an accepted, named tradeoff.

ACCEPTANCE FOR DONE
- One of (a)/(b)/(c) is decided on this bead with a measurement, not a guess.
- If (a) or (b): a real FAST gate run on a test-only change reports
  `build.disposition: "omitted"` with a named reason, the dist consumers that
  remain still run against a certified dist, and the fail-closed falsifiers in
  0eq00 still hold (deleting dist.complete on a dist-consuming change must
  build-or-fail, never pass).
- No weakening of commit binding in scripts/dist-complete.mjs.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE
- The always-on guard set must keep covering the diff-core security assertions on
  every gate (kz27/c1a77598: a guard result must never depend on a subset gate
  selecting it).
- Nothing about the marker contract: reuse is only ever allowed when
  validateDistCompleteMarker passes for the exact commit and source bytes.

RELATED: chrome-agent-platform-0eq00 (parent, ledger + validate-or-build),
chrome-agent-platform-4s5hy (proposal), k5hz7 (ADR), fleet-1ojy.2 (hub).

title: memory.js staged transaction wrappers can swallow a rejected unawaited operation (jw7wf review P2)
description:
Filed by coord from the independent reviewer PASS-with-notes verdict on the pinned jw7wf delta 4677fc8d03345a61249e878e45f600ca65d9e93b..a779f640554c838b19af5d1d361a9e09946dabbd.

FINDING (P2, staged durability contract): extension/lib/memory.js (~171-186, ~1280-1290, ~1405-1413) — both staged transaction wrappers remove a rejected operation from `pending` as soon as it settles, then inspect only the REMAINING promises after the callback returns. If an unawaited issuance/write rejects while the callback is still running, that rejection is swallowed and the wrapper can return success.

FIX: retain settled failures until the callback exits, and add a test where the callback outlives a rejected unawaited operation.

Scope note: this is a staged durability-contract defect, not evidence of a currently enabled product WAL writer; it must be fixed before product cutover. Not a block on the jw7wf union-tree gate.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-j5yz
comments.text: READ-ONLY ASSESSMENT 2026-10-14T22:35Z (source from other-owned unmerged origin/fleet/j5yz-jw7wf@a779f640; no checkout/edits): two wrappers reproduce the same loss. withMasterJournalIssuer lines 166-185 and withStoreTransaction lines 1273-1280, 1399-1408 add each operation to pending, attach fulfillment/rejection handlers that BOTH delete it, suppress unhandled rejection with run.catch(()=>{}), then after the callback exits inspect only Promise.allSettled([...pending]). A rejection that settles while the callback remains active has disappeared before inspection. This is a staged WAL durability-contract defect, NOT evidence of a product writer already enabled. Minimal scoped fix: retain operation rejection in a per-wrapper settled-failures accumulator while still deleting settled runs from pending; drain remaining pending under held lock; after callback exit preserve existing callback-error precedence, then reject on either recorded settled failure or a newly drained failure. Review deliberate caught-operation semantics explicitly: if every failed issued operation is fatal to lock-scoped callback, document that contract; do not silently alter catch policy. title: Implement FAST build-if-needed + truthful gate coverage ledger (0eq00 design)
description:
Rationale (measured): FAST gate 'npm run build:production && npm run test:changed' PASS median 153s (local ~/.fleet/checks n=190); build is ~95s of it and is paid again in merger FULL. Dist freshness is already provable via scripts/dist-complete.mjs validateDistCompleteMarker (exact commit+source bytes) and storeBuildOnce reuse in tests/build-smoke.test.ts. Full architect design + tier ledger on chrome-agent-platform-0eq00 (2026-10-14), ADR chrome-agent-platform-k5hz7.
Scope (isolated fleet worktree, implementer lane): (1) selector plan-mode in scripts/select-tests.mjs exposing selected/changed/unmapped without executing; FAST wrapper builds iff selection intersects dist-consumers (READ_ONLY_DIST/SERIAL dist readers/build-smoke) or build inputs changed or unmapped non-empty (fail-closed full path); when building, validate-or-build, never re-stamp marker. (2) Producer coverage ledger on fast+full records: suites actually executed (never suites:[] when tests ran), omitted files+reason each, unmapped, build disposition {ran|reused|omitted}+reason+markerCommit; test:heavy/test:chrome recorded as explicitly omitted from FULL. (3) Falsifier probes as tests: unmapped executable probe fails closed to full; deleted dist.complete on dist-consuming change builds-or-fails; PASS with absent coverage or unmapped non-empty cannot read green.
Acceptance: on 3+ real non-dist changes FAST saves >=60s each vs unconditional build with identical selected-test outcomes; artifact freshness evidence = marker validation output in record. Merger separately measures FULL median on >=5 NEW union trees vs 437s; no FULL saving claimed from union reuse. Cross-family reviewer verifies falsifiers. NO raw deno test tests/ sweep; inner loop npm run test:changed / test:file.
Cost: est 0.5-1 lane-day; touches scripts/select-tests.mjs, FAST gate wrapper/conf, fleet-check coverage producer seam (coordinate if producer lives in ~/fleet — hub-owned, do not edit hub files without coord).
Risk if we do nothing: ~95s per fast gate per lane indefinitely, and planned strict consumer refuses existing PASS records (134 FAST PASS coverage ABSENT) with no truthful producer to replace them.

      63f625c74 -> a0y3 (closed, reviewed), eca14cbba -> 7z3m (closed, reviewed), fb1e94df2 -> 1grt (closed, reviewed),
      1b0eb4cdf -> j5yz (closed, reviewed; the bead even carries a coord comment reconciling this exact landing sha),

EVIDENCE TRIAGE & ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS (chrome-agent-platform-d554y)

1. EVIDENCE EXAMINED:
- Immutable gate log: ~/.fleet/red-logs/76qp-gate1-STALE-cbcdcd20-tree-7bf57d08.log (lines 8248, 10071-10085)
- Prior identical occurrence: ~/.fleet/red-logs/vs9d2.3-gate1-FAIL-4c1d75ce0-tree-b9954901.log (lines 9833-9844)
- Test files: tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts (:210-230), tests/chrome-launch-lock.test.ts, scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs, scripts/test-partition.mjs

2. OBSERVATIONS & SYMPTOMS:
- In both full gates (76qp-gate1 and vs9d2.3-gate1), tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts failed at:
  tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts:210:6 -> line 222:3
  error: AssertionError: Values are not equal: chrome-launch-lock must pass cleanly
  Actual: 1 vs Expected: 0 (chrome-launch-lock exit 1)
- The test runs cleanly in isolation (5/5 in 3s on idle machine; serial-phase-resilience 13/13 in 35s).
- The failure occurs ONLY under full parallel test load (Phase 3: 664 files across 32 Deno workers, loadavg > 3.0).

3. ROOT CAUSE MECHANISM (FALSIFIABLE):
A. Subprocess Spawning of Serial Hazard from Parallel Phase:
   - scripts/test-partition.mjs explicitly partitions tests/chrome-launch-lock.test.ts into SERIAL (Phase 1) because it "tests process-global Chrome canonical lock and mutates CAP_CHROME_LOCK_PATH (races with other lock tests)".
   - However, tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts is NOT in SERIAL; it is categorized as a PARALLEL test (Phase 3).
   - In Phase 3, serial-phase-resilience.test.ts:216 calls `runSerialFile("tests/chrome-launch-lock.test.ts", { stdio: "pipe" })`, which spawns `deno test` for chrome-launch-lock concurrently with 31 other parallel workers contending for CPU and file I/O.
B. Fragile Wall-Clock and Sleep Thresholds in tests/chrome-launch-lock.test.ts:
   - Line 105: `assertEquals(a.lockWaitMs < 1500, true, "the first launch took the lock")`. Under heavy system load, the fork/exec of flock and shell startup to echo CAP_CHROME_LOCK_ACQUIRED can exceed 1500ms, causing an immediate exit 1.
   - Line 97: `assert(Date.now() - t0 < 8000, "the bounded wait is honoured, then it fails loudly")`. Extreme scheduling delays can breach 8000ms.
   - Lines 109 & 114: Fixed sleeps (`setTimeout(400)`, `setTimeout(600)`) for background processes (flock/sh/cat) to exit and release file locks race against kernel process reaping under load.
C. Diagnostic Information Swallow:
   - serial-phase-resilience.test.ts:222 executes `assertEquals(res.code, 0, "chrome-launch-lock must pass cleanly")`.
   - While `res.stdout` and `res.stderr` are captured in `res`, they are completely discarded on assertion failure, turning child subtest failures into an opaque `Actual: 1 vs Expected: 0`.

4. CLASSIFICATION:
- Classification: Test Harness / Assertion Design Defect (load-fragility under heavy parallel contention).

5. ISOLATED FIX PLAN:
- Step 1 (Immediate Diagnostic Transparency): Update tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts:222 to decode and include `res.stderr` and `res.stdout` in the assertion message so any child failure details are fully preserved in logs.
- Step 2 (Load-Aware Assertions in chrome-launch-lock.test.ts):
  * Replace the rigid `< 1500ms` check with a load-aware or causal assertion (e.g. scaling by loadPerCpu or asserting `a` did not queue behind holder).
  * Replace fixed `setTimeout` sleeps (400ms/600ms) with bounded polling loops (e.g. probing `flock -n` until lock is held or released, up to a bounded timeout).
- Step 3 (Partitioning):
  * Move tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts into SERIAL in scripts/test-partition.mjs so that it does not run serial-hazard subprocesses during the 32-worker parallel phase.

6. STATUS & NEXT ACTION:
- Owner: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
- Current State: READ-ONLY TRIAGE COMPLETE (zero branch/browser/gate writes performed).
- Next Action: Await coord route/authorization to create an isolated worktree branch and implement the fix plan.
