comments.text:
REVISED PLAN & SPEED/GATE COST ESTIMATE (chrome-agent-platform-d554y)

1. SPEED CONTRACT ALIGNMENT (SERIAL PARTITION):
- tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts will NOT be moved to SERIAL.
- Measurement: serial-phase-resilience takes ~35s total. Moving it to Phase 1 (SERIAL) would add 35s directly to the sequential critical path of npm test. Keeping it in Phase 3 (parallel) respects the speed contract and adds 0s to the serial gate phase.

2. INVARIANT-BASED ASSERTION PLAN (NO ARBITRARY TIMEOUT INFLATION):
A. Immediate Diagnostic Transparency:
   - In tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts:222, decode res.stderr and res.stdout in the assertion failure message:
     assertEquals(res.code, 0, `chrome-launch-lock must pass cleanly (exit ${res.code}):\nSTDERR:\n${errOut}\nSTDOUT:\n${stdOut}`);
   - Eliminates diagnostic loss without touching any timing.
B. Invariant-Based Lock Assertions (tests/chrome-launch-lock.test.ts):
   - Replace rigid wall-clock check `assertEquals(a.lockWaitMs < 1500, true)`:
     * In this test, no lock holder exists. The invariant being tested is that `a` takes the lock without queuing behind an external holder, and `b` is reentrant (`b.lockWaitMs === 0`).
     * We should assert the structural outcome (reentrancy + non-queued acquisition) rather than a tight 1500ms wall-clock assumption that measures kernel fork/exec scheduler latency under 32-worker CPU pressure.
   - Replace fixed blind sleeps (setTimeout(400), setTimeout(600)):
     * In the multi-browser release test, after `await settled(a.proc)`, the test sleeps 400ms hoping background flock/cat is still alive, and after `await settled(b.proc)`, sleeps 600ms hoping background flock has exited.
     * Replace blind sleeps with bounded polling probes (flock -n with 25-50ms intervals up to a bounded timeout, matching the existing `holdConfirmed` pattern in the same file).
     * This makes the test causal and event-driven: passes as soon as state transitions, while gracefully tolerating scheduler jitter without arbitrary timeout expansion.

3. EXPECTED FAST / FULL GATE COST:
- Fast gate (npm run test:changed):
  * Untouched runs: 0s delta (neither file runs).
  * Touched runs: tests/chrome-launch-lock.test.ts runs in ~2.5s (down from 3s due to eliminating 1000ms of fixed setTimeout sleeps); serial-phase-resilience.test.ts runs in ~34s.
- Full gate (npm test):
  * Phase 1 (SERIAL): 0s added (file remains in parallel Phase 3).
  * Phase 3 (PARALLEL): Neutral or slightly faster (replacing fixed 400ms/600ms sleeps with immediate polling when processes settle).
  * Net full gate impact: 0s added; saves ~352s by eliminating gate-blocking flake reruns.

4. CURRENT STATUS:
- No edits made. Standing by for coordinator route and hook fix before initiating implementation.

## Root cause (`tests/ntp-boot-attribution.test.ts:808-812`)

The fixture spawned by the test writes `ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER` and immediately calls `Deno.kill(Deno.pid, "SIGKILL")` in the same tick:

```ts
Deno.test("fixture: abnormal exit after marker", () => {
  Deno.stderr.writeSync(new TextEncoder().encode(ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER + ' {"reason":"test-refusal"}\n'));
  Deno.kill(Deno.pid, "SIGKILL");
});
```

Under parallel CPU load, `Deno.kill(Deno.pid, "SIGKILL")` terminates the child `deno` process before the parent `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` process drains the `stderr` pipe (or before the worker isolate's output reaches the parent pipe), so `capturedOutput.includes("CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL")` in `scripts/run-tests.mjs:195` is false and line 211 (`missing test summary — preserving exit`) is not reached.

## Acceptance criteria

1. In `tests/ntp-boot-attribution.test.ts:808-812`, yield briefly (e.g. `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 50))` or synchronize on parent stderr receipt) after `Deno.stderr.writeSync(...)` before calling `Deno.kill(Deno.pid, "SIGKILL")` so the refusal marker is deterministically observed by `scripts/run-tests.mjs` before abrupt process death.
2. Verify 20 consecutive runs of `mujlt runner boundary: abnormal exit before test summary preserves exit code` under parallel load pass 100%.

title: [VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE-STAGE-3c] Hub-hosted Settings view: URL contract, a11y pass, leak gates, opener flip
description:
Related: Stage-3 umbrella chrome-agent-platform-8v5l (under the VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE feature chrome-agent-platform-lmq); siblings 8v5l.1 (3a modular panels), 8v5l.2 (3b SW settings session), 8v5l.3 (3c hub Settings view); owner decision chrome-agent-platform-l354r; bug candidate chrome-agent-platform-4pf8z.

## Intent

Stage 3c of VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE (lmq -> 8v5l -> 8v5l.3): the hub hosts Settings as a client-side view of the hub document, with the URL contract from review correction C5, the accessibility pass (C10), the leak gates, and, LAST, the flip of every opener. A panel renders in the hub only when `PANEL_REGISTRY` (8v5l.1) says `host: "hub-ok"` AND, for any route it needs from the Settings-only set, 8v5l.2's allowlist admits it. Every other panel keeps rendering from the exact options document through the existing iframe path, so no authority moves unless the owner said so. Skills is the first panel (it needs no Settings-only route).

START: owner (Paul), 2026-10-12 22:05 BST. Evidence snapshot: origin/main 73ea41ba (v0.3.678); re-verify every line at claim. Work in your OWN worktree off origin/main (AGENTS.md).

Size XL. Risk High. You may sub-split: file 3c-i (dark-launched view + URL contract + CSS scoping + gates, unreachable from any opener) and 3c-ii (the flip + journey rewrites) with `bd create --parent chrome-agent-platform-8v5l.3`. Different-model review required at every rung that changes behaviour.

## Blocked by (hard edges)

- 8v5l.1: panel modules + `PANEL_REGISTRY` (a panel cannot render in a second host before that).
- 8v5l.2: the SW settings-session mechanism (needed the first time a hub-hosted panel calls a Settings-only route; Skills/About/Usage should not need it).
- the owner-decision bead chrome-agent-platform-l354r (Stage 3 hosting policy) — **RESOLVED 2026-10-14 09:40 BST (Paul: "re: 1 - a-f defaults.", `l354r` closed)**:
  - (a) Credential/owner-flow panels (`providers`, `web-services`, `mcp-servers`, `data`) stay `exact-document` (`options/options.html#<section>`, no query string).
  - (b) Document-bound panels (`user-wasm`, `tool-library`) stay `exact-document`.
  - (c) Approval-bound panels (`agents`, `permissions`) stay `exact-document`; `mayResolveApproval` (`extension/lib/owner-approval.js:934`) is NOT relaxed.
  - (d) Hub markup source: lazy `fetch` + `DOMParser` of `options.html`, importing only the hosted sections (`options.html` stays the single source of markup).
  - (e) Bundle budget: build the Settings view as its OWN lazily-imported surface bundle (`SURFACE_BUNDLES` in `build.mjs:742-749`) with its own report-only reference in `STORE_BUNDLE_BUDGETS` (`scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:32`).
  - (f) Stage 4 (`p9it`) shrinks to retiring the iframe pool for `hub-ok` panels while keeping one exact-document iframe path for `exact-document` panels.

## Corrections to the 2026-10-04 Stage 3 text (all verified on 73ea41ba)

- 16 panels, not 13 (12 default-visible + 4 developer-only; `extension/lib/pure.js:830` and `:857`). Stale: docs/SETTINGS-CLEANLINESS.md:24, docs/UX-AUDIT-2026-08-28.md:12, docs/DESIGN.md:85 ("15"): fix the docs you touch.
- There is no `#view-settings` container. Follow the Stage 1/2 convention: a third `<section id="settings-view" class="settings-view" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="view-title" hidden>` inside `#view-client-host` (`extension/ntp/ntp.html:2233`, next to `#directory-view` and `#artifacts-view`).
- Skills and Providers are SECTIONS of Settings, not views. Skills needs no Settings-only route (`mountSkillsSection(sectionEl, { send })`, `extension/skills/skills-panel.js:156`). Providers owns the credential routes and is NOT hub-eligible without an owner decision: `provider.test` merges the stored key with a caller-supplied base URL (`extension/background/routes/provider.js:188`). `#section-providers` exists nowhere; the hash is `#providers`.
- The hub is `principal: "extension"` today. `isExactOptionsSender` (`extension/lib/pure.js:888`) has ONE call site (`extension/background/service-worker.js:13251`). `ui:`-bound approvals are resolvable only from "owner-options" (`extension/lib/owner-approval.js:934`).
- `user-wasm` and `tool-library` are bound to the options DOCUMENT (`extension/lib/user-wasm-store-client.js:3-8`, `extension/lib/wasm-package-admission.js:47`): they can never render in the hub.
- Stage 4 (p9it) cannot fully retire `panelFrameFor` while any panel is exact-document-only (recorded on p9it).
- Two goals in the original text have no measured baseline or no identifiable referent. (i) "Retires Settings document bootstrap latency (12,837px initial render)": that figure comes from the 2026-08-28 audit quoted in lmq's description and has NOT been re-measured on 73ea41ba; F10 below measures it. (ii) "provider-status overlay bypass": nothing on main carries that name. The nearest thing is the topbar pill `extension/ntp/ntp.html:2001` `id="provider-status"`, whose click opens `#providers` in the Settings view (`extension/ntp/ntp.js:5265`). Ask the plan author (GLM-5.2 review, 2026-10-05) what it meant, or drop it with an explicit comment on this bead; never drop an owner-stated goal silently.

## Verified hub routing seams (extension/ntp/ntp.js)

- `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5689` `const panelFrames = new Map();`; `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5692` `function panelFrameFor(path) {`; `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5726` `function embeddedViewRoute(path) {` whose LAST line `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5731` `return VIEW_ROUTE.SETTINGS;` makes EVERY unknown path Settings, so an explicit hub `settings` route must be recognized BEFORE that default or `panelFrameFor("settings")` would load a nonexistent URL.
- `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5734` `function openView(path, title, trigger) {`; the Skills redirect `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5740` `path = "options/options.html#skills";`; `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5756` `const [basePath, hash] = String(path ?? "").split("#");` (pinned verbatim by `tests/hub-run-ux.test.ts:127-131`); `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5758` `const isClientSide = targetRoute === VIEW_ROUTE.DIRECTORY || targetRoute === VIEW_ROUTE.ARTIFACTS;`; `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5759` `teardownArtifactsView();` (the teardown-on-route-change pattern, lessons 80dd2753 / 57c50b0d); the iframe branch `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5790` `const frame = panelFrameFor(path);` boots embedded frames at the exact canonical URL with NO query (`isExactOptionsSender` rejects queries; commit 98134e38).
- History write `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5819` `const hash = \`#view=${encodeURIComponent(path)}\`;`; `closeView` `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5842`; `goHome` `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5872`; `applyCurrentHashRoute` `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5885`.
- `isOpen` quirk: the traverse path looks frames up with `panelFrames.get(parsed.path)` (`extension/ntp/ntp.js:5956`) where `parsed.path` can carry a `#hash`, but frames are keyed by basePath (`:5756`); so a traverse to `settings#section` always falls through to `openView`. Fix with a test.
- iframe -> hub postMessage bridges are gated by `isPanelFrameSource` (`extension/ntp/ntp.js:5712`): `cap:go-home` `:6125`, `cap:edit-named-agent` `:6132`, `use-skill` `:6142`, `cap:attach-artifact` `:6154`, `cap:return-to-hub-composer` `:6171`. A hub-hosted panel must use CALLBACKS (8v5l.1's `ctx.callbacks`), never postMessage to itself.
- The exact pinned focus expression `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5839` `focusAfter: activePanelFrame ?? (isClientSide ? (document.getElementById("view-back") ?? (targetRoute === VIEW_ROUTE.DIRECTORY ? directoryViewEl : artifactsViewEl)) : null),` is asserted verbatim by BOTH `tests/directory-client-view.test.ts:56` and `tests/artifacts-client-view.test.ts:72`. A third client view edits the expression and BOTH pins in lockstep, keeping them exact (never loosen to a regex).
- Openers to flip LAST (all in ntp.js): `:639`, `:4590`, `:5265`, `:5274` (provider settings), `:5740` (skills redirect), `:5769` (Directory -> Settings, see bug bead chrome-agent-platform-4pf8z for the `#section-agents` alias), `:6027` (Settings button), `:6064` (`#background-agents`). Plus `extension/directory/directory.js:92`. NOT part of the flip (they open the standalone page in a tab, which must keep working): the `chrome.runtime.openOptionsPage()` fallbacks `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5267` and `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js:433`, the new-tab opener `extension/shared/components-conversation.js:4672` `options/options.html#local-folders`, and the static links in `extension/about/about.html:24` and `extension/privacy/privacy.html:65`.
- Routing helpers: `VIEW_ROUTE` `extension/ntp/route-focus.js:6`; `parseNtpHash` `extension/lib/navigation-controller.js:206` already tolerates `settings#section`; `navigateNtpRoute` `extension/lib/navigation-controller.js:268` REPLACES when already inside a view and pushes only from the hub.
- Stage 1/2 precedents: `d266aff3` (`renderDirectoryContent` in `extension/directory/directory.js`, `tests/directory-client-view.test.ts`) and `ffebac63` (`renderArtifactsView` `extension/artifacts/index.js:525` + `teardownArtifactsView`, `tests/artifacts-client-view.test.ts`). Pattern: the module exports `render*(container, callbacks)` + `teardown*`; the standalone page keeps its own esbuild entry (`build.mjs:717`, `:719`); the hub gets markup in ntp.html and an `isClientSide` branch. There is NO lazy-load precedent in the hub today.

## Design

1. URL contract (C5): the hub route is `#view=settings%23<section>`; the raw form `#view=settings#<section>` also parses; the legacy `#view=options%2Foptions.html%23<section>` resolves to the same view and section. Switching sections INSIDE the view goes through `navigateNtpRoute` so a visit leaves exactly ONE history entry (replace once inside a view); exactly ONE `navigate` listener exists in the hub window (a second one double-intercepts same-pathname navigations: options.js has its own at `extension/options/options.js:4656`, so options.js must never be imported into the hub). Legacy aliases (`section-<id>`, `section=<id>`, `provider`, `background`, `background-agents`) resolve to the canonical id BEFORE any frame is loaded or URL committed. Standalone `options.html#<section>` links and `OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES` (C6) are untouched.
2. Panel content: `hub-ok` panels mount in-DOM through the 8v5l.1 modules with a hub `ctx` (`byId` scoped to the section element, `send` = the hub's own sender, callbacks wired to hub functions, `embedded: false`). `exact-document` panels render through an iframe of `options/options.html#<section>` (closed hash set, NO query; to hide the standalone nav in single-panel mode use something the sender URL does not carry, e.g. the iframe `name`, never a query). The iframe pool (`panelFrames`) stays for them until Stage 4.
3. Markup: per the owner decision (d). Recommended: lazy `fetch` + `DOMParser` of options.html (trusted, shipped markup; import only the hosted sections). If the markup is duplicated into ntp.html instead, a drift pin against options.html is mandatory. Never `innerHTML` untrusted data.
4. CSS: `extension/options/options.css` (2,108 lines) is NOT namespaced and shares class names with ntp.html's inline CSS (researcher counted 14 collisions on 73ea41ba, e.g. `.side`, `.btn`; re-count). Scope it under `#settings-view` first (nesting or `@scope`), with standalone parity proven by screenshot/computed-style diff and the hub's own components unchanged.
5. Bundle: per decision (e). Recommended: a lazily imported surface bundle (`SURFACE_BUNDLES`, `build.mjs:742-749`) with its own reference in `STORE_BUNDLE_BUDGETS` (`scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:32`). ntp.js SOURCE must never mention `tool-library` or `components-settings.js` (`tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1087`), so keep the section list inside the lazy module. Measure with `npm run build:production`; the local `extension/dist` is a developer build.
6. Accessibility (C10, Constitution section 2): focus moves to the view on open (`tabindex="-1"` container or its heading), to the new panel's heading on a section switch (as `handleSettingsHashNavigation` does at `extension/options/options.js:4645-4649` `heading.focus({ preventScroll: true });`, with the heading made focusable by `tabindex="-1"` first), and back to the opener on close; `aria-current` on the nav; no duplicate `main`/banner landmarks inside the hub; keyboard: Esc/back parity with the other views; reduced motion respected; no emoji icons (inline SVG, currentColor). There is NO in-hub a11y probe today: `scripts/a11y-audit.ts:577` covers the standalone options page only, so add one.
7. Skills (first panel): its 7 routes are `skill.list`, `skill.discover`, `command.list` (read-only) and `skill.import`, `skill.importBatch`, `skill.delete`, `command.delete`, which the census files under Unclassified Mutations (`tests/sw-dispatch-authority-census.test.ts:116-117` `skill.importBatch`), so the hub's "extension" principal can already call all of them: moving Skills widens no authority. "Unclassified" is not "approved": do not describe them as classified. `useSkill` (`extension/skills/skills-panel.js:128-140`) copies to the clipboard when `window.parent === window`; the hub passes `onUseSkill` that does what the `use-skill` bridge does (`extension/ntp/ntp.js:6142`): close the view and prefill the composer. No postMessage inside one document.

## Commit ladder (each rung leaves main green and shippable; the product is unchanged until rung 6)

0. CSS scoping (independent of every decision).
1. `settings` route alias + `isOpen` fix + URL-contract parser tests (no UI).
2. Lazy bundle + `#settings-view` container, unreachable from any opener (needs decisions (d) and (e)).
3. Skills first (callbacks), then About, then Usage if 8v5l.1 audited it hub-ok.
4. Nav + exact-document panels through the iframe path inside the view.
5. In-hub a11y probe + leak gates + recorded production sizes.
6. Flip the openers, LAST; rewrite the journeys; evidence screenshots from a real browser.

## Acceptance and falsification

- F1: a hub-ok panel renders with NO iframe and NO `panelFrames` entry (mutant: still create a frame, RED).
- F2: credential/exact-document panels never mount in the hub DOM (mutant: flip Providers to hub-ok, RED in 8v5l.1's registry pin AND in a hub test).
- F3: URL contract round-trips for all 16 sections, the legacy envelope and the raw form; open + 5 section switches + ONE Back returns to the hub (mutant: `pushState` per section switch, RED).
- F4: focus on open / section switch / close, in a real browser (mutant: remove one move, RED).
- F5: leak gate: 20 open/close cycles; the slope of DOM nodes AND listeners AND documents <= threshold. `scripts/panel-leak-probe.ts` is vacuous for this today: it samples a stale `#view-frame` id (`scripts/panel-leak-probe.ts:70`) and its verdict (`scripts/panel-leak-probe.ts:126`) gates only retained targets, documents and frames, never nodes or listeners. Extend it (mutant: skip `unmount()`, RED).
- F6: authority unchanged: from the hub, a Settings-only route WITHOUT a session is still refused with `SettingsSurfaceRequiredError`; `owner-approval-security`, `provider-gate`, `configure-deeplink`, `internal-sender-contract-audit`, `onmessage-sender-guard` stay green UNCHANGED.
- F7: bundle: ntp <= 500_000 and aggregate chunks <= 750_000 on `npm run build:production` (`tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1064`, `:1079`), ntp.js names no `tool-library`, size report recorded.
- F8: standalone options.html and every other hub view are pixel/DOM-equivalent (screenshot diff).
- F9: every in-repo producer of a Settings URL satisfies `isExactOptionsSender` (drift test; subsumes bug bead chrome-agent-platform-4pf8z for `#section-agents`).
- F10: latency: record open-to-interactive for the hub Settings view (a hub-ok panel) against today's iframe path on the same machine (CDP trace, 5 runs, median) and compare with `docs/CONSTITUTION.md:161-162` `render fast`; re-measure the audit's 12,837px initial height instead of quoting it. Reported, not a hard threshold.

Tests/gates to update in this bead: `tests/hub-run-ux.test.ts:127-131`, `tests/directory-client-view.test.ts:56` + `tests/artifacts-client-view.test.ts:72` (lockstep), `tests/panel-frame-pool.test.ts` (stays valid while the iframe branch exists), `tests/one-shell-layout.test.ts`, `tests/postmessage-wildcard-guard.test.ts` (keep `cap:go-home`/`use-skill` allowlist counts), `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` iframe probes (grep `options/options.html`), `scripts/skills-in-settings-evidence.ts`, `scripts/kat-interactive-artifact-click.ts`, `scripts/kat-settings-cleanliness.ts`, `scripts/kat-settings-multi-section.ts`, `scripts/kat-providers-tabs.ts`, `scripts/kat-attention-badge.ts`, `tests/provider-gate.test.ts`, `tests/security.test.ts`, `tests/settings-focus-and-diag-badge-716s13.test.ts`.

## Must NOT change

`OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES`, standalone `options.html#<section>` deep links, `isExactOptionsSender`, `requireSettingsSender`, `mayResolveApproval`, the iframe pool for non-hub panels, the `cap:*` channel names and their `ALLOWED_WILDCARD_CHANNELS` entries, the exactness of the focus-expression pins, the single-`navigate`-listener rule, the factory-reset journey's selectors (bead rghlv), and the Constitution rules: no eval/new Function, no provider key in the bundle/logs/receipts, textContent for untrusted data, no emoji icons.

## Collisions

Open beads that edit options.js/options.html/ntp.js: jt83l, ie3x1, rghlv (in_progress), s06h, qq6or, urdr4, lrd8, ome8i, 3p3e.12, kw84a, hiuce, osi7q (related links added). Rebase onto whichever lands first.

## Review

A fresh different-model reviewer per behaviour-changing rung, falsification-focused, against docs/CONSTITUTION.md section 1 (credentials; sender-origin), section 2 (focus management, landmarks) and section 4 (leak probe `docs/CONSTITUTION.md:156`, budgets `:161`). "Serves" is not "works": every rung that changes what a user sees carries browser-driven (CDP) evidence with screenshots.
close_reason: Landed at eb7170c8e8e0bac2f726abf11ba008c12603c4a3 (v0.3.684): Hub-hosted Settings view for hub-ok panels (skills, usage, about) in #settings-view, C5 URL contract, C10 a11y focus pass, F1-F10 falsification suite; independent pro review PASS; full 707-file test suite green.

title: [VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE-STAGE-3b] Service-worker settings-session authorization (mechanism only, EMPTY allowlist, security review)
description:
Related: Stage-3 umbrella chrome-agent-platform-8v5l (under the VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE feature chrome-agent-platform-lmq); siblings 8v5l.1 (3a modular panels), 8v5l.2 (3b SW settings session), 8v5l.3 (3c hub Settings view); owner decision chrome-agent-platform-l354r; bug candidate chrome-agent-platform-4pf8z.

## Intent

Stage 3b of VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE (lmq -> 8v5l -> 8v5l.2): the service-worker half of "admit in-hub Settings calls with session security tokens". It implements review correction C4 (GLM-5.2, 2026-10-05): NOT broad route-list admission for ntp.html, but a short-lived session minted when the hub's settings view mounts and verified per sensitive route in the SW. This bead builds and PROVES THE MECHANISM with an EMPTY allowlist. It admits NO route to the hub. 8v5l.3 adds routes one panel at a time, each an owner-approved, reviewed allowlist edit.

START: owner (Paul), 2026-10-12 22:05 BST. Evidence snapshot: origin/main 73ea41ba (v0.3.678); re-verify every line at claim. Work in your OWN worktree off origin/main (AGENTS.md).

Size M. Risk CRITICAL (authority boundary). A different-model SECURITY review is required before merge; the implementer never reviews its own work. Parallel with 8v5l.1; blocks 8v5l.3.

## The honest limit (write it into the code comment, THREAT_MODEL.md and the PR; do not oversell)

The hub document also renders untrusted content. Any script running inside ntp.html can call the mint route and then every route the allowlist admits. A session therefore NARROWS scope and lifetime and makes admission explicit, revocable and auditable. It does NOT recreate the browser-enforced boundary the exact-options iframe gives today. The only unforgeable input is `sender.documentId` (browser-attested). The token is not a secret that defends against script in the hub document, and no doc or comment may claim it is. That is why the allowlist starts empty and why credential routes stay out by default (decision bead chrome-agent-platform-l354r, question (a)).

## Verified seams

- Single choke point: the one dispatcher listener `extension/background/service-worker.js:13229` `chrome.runtime.onMessage.addListener(`. It builds `routeContext = { principal: "extension", documentId, senderUrl }` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:13245-13249`), upgrades to "owner-options" ONLY if `isExactOptionsSender(sender, chrome.runtime.id, optionsUrl)` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:13251`, the function's single call site; `extension/background/service-worker.js:13252` `principal: "owner-options"`), then calls `dispatchRoute(message.type, message, routeContext)` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:13291`).
- `dispatchRoute` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:6507`) deletes every `__*` body key and `userActivation` before the handler runs (`extension/background/service-worker.js:6514` `if (key.startsWith("__") || key === "userActivation") delete safeBody[key];`). A credential carried as `message.__settingsSession` is therefore invisible to handlers by construction and can only be read by the listener BEFORE dispatch.
- Precedent to reuse, not reinvent: `issueBridgeNonce` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:5699` `async function issueBridgeNonce(tabId, documentId) {`): a per-`documentId` nonce in a memory map mirrored to `chrome.storage.session` (survives SW restarts), bounded by `BRIDGE_NONCE_MAX`, oldest-first eviction, `crypto.randomUUID()`.
- `requireSettingsSender(context)` (`extension/background/routes/auth.js:10`) accepts ONLY `context.principal === "owner-options"`. 22 call sites: `extension/background/routes/mcp.js` 35/55/71; `extension/background/routes/provider.js` 25/119/171/181; `extension/background/routes/vault.js` 133/146/156/163/170/178/190; `extension/background/service-worker.js` 8024/10082/10118/10148/10181/10217/10452/11656. It must NOT be widened.
- Census: `SETTINGS_ONLY_DIRECT` has exactly 51 routes (`tests/sw-dispatch-authority-census.test.ts:46`; `docs/SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS.md` section 4.2); the registered population is 290 (`tests/sw-dispatch-authority-census.test.ts:466` `assertEquals(registered.size, 290,`). Layer 1/2/3 text in the census doc section 2 changes with this work. The census UNDERCOUNTS the real Settings-only surface: handlers that call `requireSettingsSender` yet are classified elsewhere include `alarms.permission-granted` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:8024`, listed read-only), `mcp.servers.get` (`extension/background/routes/mcp.js:35`, listed read-only) and `site-skills.set` (`extension/background/service-worker.js:11656`, listed OWNER_EXTENSION_FENCED). Do not read "51" as the whole set: enumerate the real one before you touch any category.
- Hub senders today: principal "extension" (`isOwnerPrincipal` accepts "extension" or "owner-options"). `ui:`-bound approvals can be resolved ONLY by "owner-options" (`extension/lib/owner-approval.js:934` `mayResolveApproval`), which is why no panel that needs that is hub-eligible.

## Recommended design (the claimant refines it with the reviewer; the INVARIANTS are not negotiable)

1. Pure module `extension/lib/settings-session.js`: `createSettingsSessions({ now, store, ttlMs, maxSessions })` returning `{ open({ documentId, scopes }), verify({ token, documentId, route }), close({ documentId }), sweep() }`. Injectable clock and store (no `chrome.*` inside) so it is unit-testable with a fake clock; the SW injects a store mirrored to `chrome.storage.session`, so a service-worker restart does not strand a live hub view.
2. Routes `settings.session.open` / `settings.session.close`. Open is REFUSED unless ALL hold: `sender.id === chrome.runtime.id`; `sender.url` is exactly `chrome.runtime.getURL("ntp/ntp.html")` (pin precisely whether the hub's own `#` fragments are accepted and reject every query); not a content script (`authorizeToolReport(...).kind !== "content-script"`, `extension/lib/pure.js:912`); `sender.frameId` null or 0 (a subframe of the hub, such as a sandboxed artifact frame, can never mint); non-empty `sender.documentId`; `documentLifecycle` null or "active". Requested `scopes` are INTERSECTED with the SW's static allowlist; an empty intersection mints nothing.
3. Verification happens in the listener, BEFORE `dispatchRoute`: read raw `message.__settingsSession`. The check is async (storage.session), so the dispatch becomes `verify(...).then((ctx) => dispatchRoute(...))`. A missing, malformed, expired, revoked, wrong-document or wrong-scope session leaves `principal: "extension"` untouched (fail CLOSED: no upgrade, a `securityEvent("blocked-action", ...)` entry that NEVER contains the token, nor does any receipt, log line or error text).
4. KEEP `principal: "extension"`. On success set only `routeContext.settingsSession = { documentId, scopes, expiresAt }`. Do NOT mint a new principal. Do NOT widen `requireSettingsSender`, `isExactOptionsSender`, `OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES`, `mayResolveApproval` or `isOwnerPrincipal`.
5. Sibling guard in `extension/background/routes/auth.js`: `requireSettingsSession(context, route)` passes only if `context.settingsSession` exists, is unexpired, `settingsSession.documentId === context.documentId` and `route` is within the session's scopes. A route admitted to hub sessions then calls a combined `requireSettingsSurface` (`principal === "owner-options"` OR `requireSettingsSession`). Migrating any real route is OUT OF SCOPE for this bead.
6. Static allowlist `SETTINGS_SESSION_ROUTES` (route -> [panel scopes]) STARTS EMPTY. A route may be added only by a commit that (i) names the panel, (ii) records Paul's approval for THAT route as a comment on the decision bead chrome-agent-platform-l354r, (iii) updates the census in the same commit (category row, counts, doc sections), (iv) adds a test proving the route is refused without a session. Mutants below prove (iii).
7. TTL default <= 15 minutes; explicit revoke on `settings.session.close` (the hub calls it on settings-view unmount); revoke when the owning tab/document goes away if that is cheap; a stale session must never outlive its document. Bound the table (`maxSessions`, oldest-first eviction) like the bridge nonce.

## Census and docs obligations (docs/SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS.md, AGENTS.md "SW dispatch authority")

- The two new routes must be CLASSIFIED, never left in "Unclassified Mutations" (section 4.9). Best fit: `OWNER_EXTENSION_FENCED` (section 4.5, `isOwnerPrincipal`) plus the extra hub-document sender predicate; if you create a new category, name it and add its count. Population 290 -> 292.
- Every "290" pin moves together: `extension/background/routes/ROUTE_MAP.md` (`**290**`), `THREAT_MODEL.md` (both the component-map pin and the T4 evidence line), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (`290-route population`), `docs/NATIVE-AGENT-POSITION-PLAN.md` (`290-route dispatch authority`), `docs/SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS.md` sections 1/2/3, and the census test (`tests/sw-dispatch-authority-census.test.ts:7`, `:430-458`, `:464-466`). Keep the test's own falsification drills working.
- Add a THREAT_MODEL.md row for the hub-session residual risk (the honest limit above).
- Opening a NEW non-dispatcher `chrome.runtime.onMessage` listener is NOT part of this design; `tests/onmessage-sender-guard.test.ts` must stay green unchanged.
- Known doc drift to reconcile while you are in the census (do not widen scope to fix it silently; file or fix it as its own commit): `extension/background/routes/ROUTE_MAP.md:19` says `mcp.servers.get` is open to "extension", `extension/background/routes/mcp.js:35` gates it with `requireSettingsSender`, and `tests/sw-dispatch-authority-census.test.ts:136` lists it read-only.

## Acceptance

1. Pure-module tests with a fake clock and fake store: open/verify/close, expiry edge, eviction, restore after a simulated SW restart, scope intersection, wrong document, wrong route, replay after close.
2. Listener-level tests with crafted senders (no real Chrome needed): hub top frame mints; hub SUBFRAME refused; content script refused; options page and side panel refused; wrong extension id refused; mint without `documentId` refused. Verify path: a valid session sets `settingsSession` but leaves `principal` "extension"; a session replayed from another `documentId`, an expired, a revoked and a wrong-scope session are refused; `message.__settingsSession` never reaches a handler.
3. Falsification drills, each run and recorded RED by the REVIEWER (not the author): (m1) verify without comparing `documentId`; (m2) skip the expiry check; (m3) accept a scope the session does not hold; (m4) allow minting from a subframe; (m5) allow minting from a content script; (m6) upgrade `principal` to "owner-options" on a valid session; (m7) put the token in a `securityEvent`, error text or response; (m8) remove the `__` scrub in `dispatchRoute`; (m9) add a route to `SETTINGS_SESSION_ROUTES` without a census entry. Each mutant must fail a named test.
4. These stay green WITHOUT edits: `tests/owner-approval-security.test.ts`, `tests/configure-deeplink.test.ts`, `tests/provider-gate.test.ts`, `tests/internal-sender-contract-audit.test.ts`, `tests/onmessage-sender-guard.test.ts`. The journeys that pin the current semantics keep passing: `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:8160` (`approval: NTP cannot programmatically resolve an owner approval`) and `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:8083` (`approval: primary NTP Settings iframe can deny an exact request`).
5. A test asserts `SETTINGS_SESSION_ROUTES` is EMPTY at merge, so a non-empty allowlist can only arrive as a conscious, separate, census-visible change.
6. Written security review by a different model family against docs/CONSTITUTION.md section 1 (sender-origin spoofing, credentials never in logs/receipts), with the threat-model addendum attached to the PR. No browser-visible change: the full suite and the Chrome journeys are green on the final commit.

## Must NOT change

`requireSettingsSender` semantics, `isExactOptionsSender` (`extension/lib/pure.js:888`), `OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES` (`extension/lib/pure.js:881`), `mayResolveApproval`, the categories of the 51 `SETTINGS_ONLY_DIRECT` routes (never move one to a weaker category), `PAGE_ALLOWED_ROUTES`, the principal vocabulary (no new principal), the `dispatchRoute` scrub, and every existing route's behaviour. Provider keys never appear in the bundle, logs or receipts.

Added SW settings-session mechanism (SETTINGS_SESSION_ROUTES empty allowlist, settings.session.open/close, pre-dispatch verification, census 290->292). Independent security review PASS (cade1c44, all 9 mutants m1-m9 verified RED->GREEN). title: [VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE-STAGE-3a] Settings panels as mountable modules + PANEL_REGISTRY (behaviour-neutral, no hub change)
description:
Related: Stage-3 umbrella chrome-agent-platform-8v5l (under the VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE feature chrome-agent-platform-lmq); siblings 8v5l.1 (3a modular panels), 8v5l.2 (3b SW settings session), 8v5l.3 (3c hub Settings view); owner decision chrome-agent-platform-l354r; bug candidate chrome-agent-platform-4pf8z.

## Intent

Stage 3a of VIEW-FRAME-COLLAPSE (lmq -> 8v5l -> 8v5l.1). Turn each Settings panel into a module with a `mount(root, ctx)` / `unmount()` contract and add a `PANEL_REGISTRY`, with ZERO behaviour change on the standalone options page. This bead touches NO hub code, NO service-worker code, NO `options.html` markup and NO `options.css`. It is the prerequisite for 8v5l.3: a panel can only render in a second host once it stops reaching for `document`, `window.top`, `location` and raw `chrome.runtime.sendMessage`.

START: owner (Paul), 2026-10-12 22:05 BST. Every line number below is on origin/main 73ea41ba (v0.3.678): re-verify with `git grep` / `git show` when you claim, and say so if main moved. Work in your OWN worktree off origin/main (AGENTS.md: `npm ci`, then `deno install` LAST, then `npm run build:production`).

Size XL. Risk High (the largest file in the product, 44 test files read it as text). Different-model review required (the implementer never reviews its own work). Parallel with 8v5l.2; blocks 8v5l.3.

## Why options.js cannot simply be imported by the hub

`extension/options/options.js` is 5,207 lines / 228 KB and boots the whole page at module scope:
- top-level awaits at `extension/options/options.js:4799` `await refreshStoragePermission();`, `extension/options/options.js:4805` `await readDeveloperFeaturesFlag();`, `extension/options/options.js:4812` `await navigationController.syncCurrent();`
- module-scope `extension/options/options.js:493` `registerWasmPreviewHost();`
- module state `extension/options/options.js:4437` `const renderedSections = new Set();` and `extension/options/options.js:288` `let developerFeaturesEnabled = false;`
- its own `extension/options/options.js:4656` `export const navigationController = createNavigationController({`, so importing it into the hub would install a SECOND navigate interceptor on the same window.

Host coupling counted on 73ea41ba (re-measure at claim): 45 `document.getElementById`, 12 `document.querySelector*`, 78 uses of the `$()` helper (`extension/options/options.js:237`), 35 `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` (including the `boundedSend`/`send` wrappers at `extension/options/options.js:242-248` and the `sendMessage:` adapter lambdas at `:911`, `:1812`, `:2514`), 6 `window.parent`/`window.top` uses (`:3`, `:783-784`, `:1825-1826`, `:4769`), 9 `location.*` uses (`:3`, `:784`, `:789`, `:933`, `:1826`, `:1830`, `:4133`, `:4711`), 5 timers, 4 `onChanged`/`onMessage` listeners, 1 `window.addEventListener("focus")` at `extension/options/options.js:4798`, 1 `subscribeDiagnosticsRevision` at `extension/options/options.js:4832`. Raw sends outside options.js that a hosted panel also reaches: `extension/lib/backup-restore.js` (3), `extension/lib/data-archive.js` (1), `extension/shared/components-core.js:1831` (1).

## Verified starting point

- There are 16 panels, not the "13" the umbrella text says: `SETTINGS_SECTIONS` `extension/lib/pure.js:830` (16 ids) = 12 default-visible + 4 developer-only (`DEVELOPER_SECTIONS` `extension/lib/pure.js:857`: tool-library, board-permissions, hooks, prompts). `tests/settings-section-navigation.test.ts:47` already asserts 16 panels. The real hash for Providers is `#providers` (`extension/options/options.html:166` `<section id="providers" class="panel active" data-active="true">`); the `#section-providers` named in the umbrella text exists nowhere.
- The dispatch seam is `async function renderSection(` `extension/options/options.js:4463`; `async function ensureSectionRendered(` `extension/options/options.js:4443` takes the render claim BEFORE rendering and RELEASES it if the renderer throws (the hy91 blank-Providers fix): that contract must survive the extraction.
- Existing precedent for a DI'd panel: `export function mountSkillsSection(` `extension/skills/skills-panel.js:156` already takes `{ send }`. `useSkill` (`extension/skills/skills-panel.js:128-140`) falls back to copy-to-clipboard when `window.parent === window`, so it needs a callback seam for the hub (8v5l.3).

| panel | dev-only | entry points in options.js | proposed host | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| providers | | `renderProviders` :999, `initProviderServerTools` :1728 | exact-document | `provider.get/set/clear-key/test` are `requireSettingsSender` |
| mcp-servers | | `renderMcpServers` :4313 | exact-document | `mcp.servers.set/test` |
| local-folders | | `renderLocalFolders` :515 | exact-document | `fs-grant.remove`/`fs-grant.write-file` settings-only |
| user-wasm | | `mountUserWasmPanel` (import :89, dispatch :4478) | exact-document (document-bound) | pathname-bound store client |
| tool-library | yes | `renderToolLibrary` :352 | exact-document (document-bound) | `tool.preview.run`, `tool.package.*` |
| skills | | `mountSkillsSection` (dispatch :4493) | hub-ok | 7 routes: `skill.list`, `skill.discover`, `command.list` read-only; `skill.import`, `skill.importBatch`, `skill.delete`, `command.delete` census-UNCLASSIFIED mutations; none Settings-only |
| agents | | `renderAgents` :1555, `renderEnroll` :1105, `hydrateAgentsHeavyLists` :4455 | exact-document | `ui:`-bound approvals resolve only from owner-options |
| browser | | `renderBrowser` :2280, `renderActionPolicy` :2409 | exact-document | `tools.policy.set`, `browser-control.*` |
| board-permissions | yes | `populateBoardDenyAgents` :5159 | exact-document (conservative) | audit in this bead |
| permissions | | `renderPermissions` :2474 | exact-document | `webmcp.consent.*`, `capability.revoke` via approvals |
| web-services | | `renderVaultPanel` :3619 | exact-document | 7 `vault.*` routes |
| hooks | yes | `renderHooks` :2787 | exact-document (conservative) | `hooks.deny` settings-only |
| prompts | yes | `renderPrompts` :4161 | exact-document (conservative, NOT yet audited) | `prompt.set/reset/keep/rotateAttestationKey` |
| usage | | `renderUsage` :2948 | audit; likely hub-ok | NOT yet audited |
| data | | `renderData` :3307, `renderMemoryExplorer` :3103 | exact-document | `owner.export/import.all`, `system.factoryReset`, `memory.purge*` |
| about | | `renderAbout` :5071 | hub-ok | read-only |

The `host` column is a CONSERVATIVE proposal, not a decision: it is data in the registry, with no consumer in this bead, and only `skills` and `about` start as `hub-ok`. Which panels may actually move is the owner's call (decision bead chrome-agent-platform-l354r, an 8v5l.3 blocker).

## Scope

1. `extension/options/panels/<id>.js` per panel (reuse `extension/skills/skills-panel.js` and `extension/options/user-wasm-panel.js` where they already exist), each exporting `mount(root, ctx)` that returns `{ unmount() }`. options.js stays the standalone HOST: it builds the `ctx`, keeps the boot sequence and the `renderSection` dispatch, and calls `mount` from `ensureSectionRendered`. The standalone esbuild entry does not change (`build.mjs:708`).
2. The `ctx` contract (suggested; pin whatever you choose in a test): `send(type, payload)` with exactly the semantics each call site has today (do NOT turn raw sends into `boundedSend`: that adds a 12 s timeout and is a behaviour change), `boundedSend`, root-scoped resolvers `ctx.byId(id)` / `ctx.$(sel)` that never reach outside `root`, `embedded` (replaces `IS_EMBEDDED_SETTINGS` `extension/options/options.js:3`; a module must never derive it from `window.top`, because in the hub `window.self === window.top`), `developerFeatures()` (replaces the module state at `:288`), `navigateSection(id, { replace })` (replaces the `location` writes), `callbacks` (`useSkill`, `goHome`, `returnToComposer`, `editNamedAgent`, replacing the `window.parent.postMessage` sites at `:784`, `:1826`, `:4769` and `skills-panel.js:136`), `signal` (aborts in-flight renders on unmount) and `registerCleanup(fn)`. Standalone defaults reproduce today's behaviour exactly, including the `"*"` target of `cap:go-home`.
3. `unmount()` removes every listener, timer and subscription `mount()` registered OUTSIDE `root` (inventory above: the focus listener, the 4 `onChanged`/`onMessage` listeners, the 5 timers, `subscribeDiagnosticsRevision`) and aborts pending renders. A second `mount()` after `unmount()` must produce the same DOM and the same SW calls as the first (the 80dd2753 / 57c50b0d teardown-on-remount lesson).
4. `PANEL_REGISTRY` (one module under `extension/lib/` or `extension/options/`, pure data): per panel `{ id, developerOnly, host: "hub-ok" | "exact-document", routes: [...every SW message type the panel can send...], rawSendSites: [...] }`. The route lists come from a recorded audit: static scan of literal types plus the runtime recorder used by the parity script below; map each route to its census category (`docs/SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS.md` section 4). This bead also AUDITS the three panels that no one has audited yet: usage, prompts, board-permissions.
5. Drift pin: registry ids == `SETTINGS_SECTIONS` ids == `DEVELOPER_SECTIONS` flags == `<section id>` / `a.nav-item[data-section]` in options.html (16 nav items). Adding a 17th panel anywhere without the others must fail a test.

## Acceptance

1. Behaviour-neutral, proven by a PARITY script (new, e.g. `scripts/settings-panel-parity.ts`): for every one of the 16 sections, load standalone options.html at the BASE commit and at HEAD in the same Chrome, mount the section, and compare (i) the normalized DOM of the section, (ii) the ordered list of SW message types sent during mount, (iii) the count of live listeners/timers after mount. Identical, or the diff is explained in the PR.
2. The existing journeys and KATs that drive Settings stay green UNCHANGED: `scripts/kat-settings-cleanliness.ts`, `scripts/kat-settings-multi-section.ts`, `scripts/kat-providers-tabs.ts`, `scripts/kat-attention-badge.ts`; `tests/settings-focus-and-diag-badge-716s13.test.ts`, `tests/provider-gate.test.ts`, `tests/security.test.ts`.
3. 44 test files read `extension/options/options.js` as text and 66 reference `options.html`. Source pins must FOLLOW the code to the module that now owns it (re-anchor each pin on the specific panel module, not on a concatenation of everything) and must never be weakened. Report the assertion count before and after: it must not drop. `tests/postmessage-wildcard-guard.test.ts` (`ALLOWED_WILDCARD_CHANNELS` for `cap:go-home` and `use-skill`) and `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:623` (`options.bundle.js does NOT include provider.js or durable-runs.js`) must stay green: a new module must not pull `extension/lib/provider.js` or `durable-runs.js` into the options bundle.
4. Registry pins: (i) every literal message type a panel module sends appears in its `routes` (mutant: add `send("provider.set")` to the Skills panel, RED); (ii) a `hub-ok` panel's `routes` must not intersect `SETTINGS_ONLY_DIRECT` (`tests/sw-dispatch-authority-census.test.ts:46`) nor the approval-resolution routes (mutant: mark Providers `hub-ok`, RED); (iii) the drift pin in Scope 5 (mutant: delete one nav item, RED).
5. Contract tests with a fake `ctx` and a detached DOM fixture: `mount` touches nothing outside `root`, never reads `window.top`/`location`, never calls `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` directly; `unmount` leaves zero residual listeners/timers (counting harness; mutant: skip one `removeListener`, RED).
6. `ensureSectionRendered` keeps the claim-before-render / release-on-throw contract (mutant: stop releasing on throw, the existing pin goes RED).
7. Full unit suite + Chrome journeys green on the final commit; `npm run build:production` size report recorded in the PR (options.bundle.js reference is 450_000, `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:35`).

## Must NOT change

`extension/options/options.html` markup and ids, `extension/options/options.css`, `OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES` (`extension/lib/pure.js:881`), `isExactOptionsSender`, `requireSettingsSender`, the selectors the factory-reset journey relies on (`a.nav-item[data-section="data"]`, `#factory-reset-btn`, `.cap-confirm-dialog .cap-confirm-accept`; see bead rghlv), `cap:*` channel names, `extension/ntp/ntp.js`, the service worker, and any user-visible behaviour (focus order, copy, timing). No emoji icons; untrusted data still renders with textContent.

## Commit ladder (per-panel commits, lowest risk first; land rung by rung, not as one XL diff)

registry + `ctx` + parity script first (no panel moved); then About, Usage, Prompts, MCP servers, Browser, Local folders, Permissions, Web services (vault), Data, Agents, Providers LAST (largest state surface). Every rung runs the parity script and the focused tests; rebase often: this file has 12 other open beads touching it (see below).

## Collisions (open beads that edit options.js/options.html; related links added, none block)

jt83l (Settings IA relocation; a fresh re-implementation of vc52/p43i, do it AFTER the panel modules exist or keep it small and land it first), ie3x1, rghlv (in_progress, qa: factory-reset journey selectors), s06h, qq6or, urdr4, lrd8, ome8i, 3p3e.12, kw84a, hiuce, osi7q. Land small Settings fixes fast; whoever lands second rebases onto the other.

## Review

A fresh different-model reviewer, falsification-focused ("would each test fail if the behaviour regressed?"), against docs/CONSTITUTION.md section 1 (no sender-origin spoofing, textContent not innerHTML), section 2 (focus management must not regress) and section 4 (memory: unmount leaves no listeners). The reviewer runs the mutants in Acceptance 4-6 and records each RED.

title: Directory to Settings opens options.html#section-agents, outside OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES: owner-only routes may be refused (needs browser repro)
description:
## Observed (static analysis plus executing the real pure function; NOT yet reproduced in a browser)

Two producers send the owner to the Settings document at the hash `#section-agents`:
- hub Directory view: `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5769` `onNavigateSettings: () => openView("options/options.html#section-agents", "Settings"),` (the iframe is booted at a URL that INCLUDES the hash: `openView` builds `frameUrl` from the whole `path`, and a reused frame gets `contentWindow.location.hash` set to the same value).
- standalone Directory page: `extension/directory/directory.js:92` `location.href = "../options/options.html#section-agents";`

options.js tolerates the alias (`extension/options/options.js:4598` `if (cleanId.startsWith("section-")) cleanId = cleanId.slice("section-".length);`), so the right section opens. But service-worker authority is URL-shaped: `isExactOptionsSender` (`extension/lib/pure.js:888`) accepts only the exact options URL or a hash in the closed set `OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES` (`extension/lib/pure.js:881`, 18 hashes), and `#section-agents` is not in it.

Executed the real function on origin/main 73ea41ba (node, placeholder extension id, sender = `{ id, url, documentId, origin }`):
`""` true; `#providers` true; `#agents` true; `#skills` true; `#section-agents` FALSE; `#section-providers` FALSE; `?embedded=1` FALSE; `#agent=named:x&edit=1` FALSE.

Nothing rewrites the URL on boot: `syncCurrent` (`extension/lib/navigation-controller.js:163`) passes the current hash through whenever `normalizeHash` resolves, and options.js's `normalizeHash` falls back to "providers" for anything unknown (`extension/options/options.js:4658`), so the document URL plausibly STAYS `#section-agents` until the owner clicks another nav item.

## Hypothesis to confirm or refute in a real browser (CDP, with screenshots)

While the Settings document URL is `.../options/options.html#section-agents` its principal is "extension", so every `requireSettingsSender` route is refused with `SettingsSurfaceRequiredError` ("provider credential routes are restricted to the Settings surface", `extension/background/routes/auth.js:15`). In the Agents section that includes the site-tool-consent area: `renderSiteToolConsents` sends `webmcp.consent.snapshot` (`extension/options/options.js:1399`, handler `extension/background/service-worker.js:10117`), plus `webmcp.audit.list`, `webmcp.consent.tool.set`, `webmcp.consent.site.reset` and `tools.policy.set`, all Settings-only. How it surfaces (an error row, an empty list, a misleading provider-key error) is part of the repro.

Repro: open the hub, Directory, the Settings action; then open the site-tool-consent controls in Agents; also click the standalone directory page's Settings link. Record `sender.url` and the resolved principal at the service worker (a temporary `securityEvent` or the existing log), the DOM, and a screenshot.

## Producer inventory (origin/main 73ea41ba; re-measure with `git grep -n -E 'options/options\.html|openOptionsPage' -- extension` at claim)

Only the two `#section-agents` producers and one dead href fall outside `OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES`; every other producer is inside the closed set or carries no hash:
- OUTSIDE the set: `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5769` `#section-agents`; `extension/directory/directory.js:92` `#section-agents`; `extension/shared/components-conversation.js:2564` `options/options.html#provider` (DEAD: it is only the `detail.href` of the `fix-settings` event, and the single listener `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5271` `document.addEventListener?.("fix-settings"` ignores it and opens `#providers` at `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5274`; no code reads `detail.href`).
- Inside the set or hashless: `extension/ntp/ntp.js:639` and `:5265` and `:5274` (`#providers`), `:4590` and `:6027` (no hash), `:5740` (`#skills`), `:6064` (`#background-agents`); `extension/shared/components-conversation.js:4672` `options/options.html#local-folders`; `extension/about/about.html:24` `#about`; `extension/privacy/privacy.html:65` `#data` and `:66` `#about`.
- `chrome.runtime.openOptionsPage()` callers carry no hash: `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5267`, `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js:433`, `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.js:599`.

## Fix direction (only if confirmed)

Canonicalize aliases at the SOURCE: both producers link to a hash that is in OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES (`#agents`), or options.js `replaceState`s to the canonical hash as soon as it resolves an alias. Do NOT add `#section-*` to OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES: that widens the exact-document authority set (`isExactOptionsSender` is deliberately a closed set). Pin it with a drift test that enumerates every in-repo producer of a Settings URL and asserts each satisfies `isExactOptionsSender`. Bead 8v5l.3's URL contract must subsume this: legacy aliases (`section-<id>`, `section=<id>`, `provider`, `background`, `background-agents`) resolve to the canonical product hash BEFORE any frame is loaded or any URL is committed. `docs/DESIGN.md:89` `#section-agents` documents these aliases as supported deep links (also `#section-skills` and `#section=data`); reconcile that sentence with the canonical form you pick.

## Why it matters

Same defect class as P0 pek9 (commit 98134e38: embedded Settings failed `isExactOptionsSender` because the committed URL carried a query, so every owner route refused with a misleading API-key error). If confirmed, it silently degrades the Directory -> Settings path and is a landmine for the Stage 3 URL contract.

title: Decide: Stage 3 Settings-in-hub hosting policy - which Settings panels may render in the hub document (8v5l)
description:
## Ask (answer in one line; reply "defaults" to accept every recommendation below)

Stage 3 (8v5l) moves Settings panels out of the exact options.html document (an iframe of the hub today) and into the hub document. Authority in this codebase is DOCUMENT-shaped, so where a panel renders decides which principal its calls carry. This bead records the owner choices that decide which panels may move, where the hub gets its markup, how the bundle budget is handled, and what Stage 4 can still retire. The decision itself changes no code; the children read the answers:
- 8v5l.1 modular panel renderers + `PANEL_REGISTRY` (starts now, needs no answer)
- 8v5l.2 service-worker settings-session authorization (starts now, needs no answer; its allowlist starts EMPTY)
- 8v5l.3 hub-hosted Settings view (BLOCKED by this bead: (d) and (e) shape its first real rung)

Origin: owner START of Stage 3, Paul, 2026-10-12 22:05 BST ("yep sounds good", replying to item 5 of the coordinator's 2026-10-12 report: "START Stage 3? Default yes, after I split it into 3a/3b/3c and fix the lmq edges, which are written up on lmq." - markdown emphasis dropped). Evidence snapshot: origin/main 73ea41ba (v0.3.678); line numbers re-verified by `git show` on that commit.

## Why this is an owner call and not an implementation detail

- Today the Settings authority chain is: `isExactOptionsSender` `extension/lib/pure.js:888` (exact options.html document, plus 18 product hashes) -> principal "owner-options" `extension/background/service-worker.js:13252` -> `requireSettingsSender` (22 call sites) and `mayResolveApproval` `extension/lib/owner-approval.js:934`. The hub (`ntp/ntp.html`) is principal "extension".
- The hub document also renders untrusted content (model output, artifacts, imported text). A script running in the hub can call everything the hub is admitted to, and can mint whatever session the SW mints for the hub (8v5l.2 states this limit in its threat-model addendum: a session NARROWS scope and lifetime, it does not recreate the iframe's browser-enforced boundary).
- Concrete stakes: `provider.test` merges the STORED API key into a request to a CALLER-SUPPLIED base URL. `extension/background/routes/provider.js:188` `baseURL: String(m?.baseURL ?? cur.baseURL ?? "")` and `extension/background/routes/provider.js:189` `apiKey: String(m?.apiKey ?? "") || (cur.provider === (m?.provider ?? cur.provider) ? (cur.apiKey ?? "") : "")`. Whoever can call that route can direct the stored key at an endpoint of their choosing; the only other fence is the host-permission request the page makes on a user gesture. That is why the credential panels are the default exception in (a).

## Questions (recommended default first)

(a) Credential and owner-flow panels: Providers (`provider.get/set/clear-key/test`), Web services (the 7 `vault.*` routes, `extension/background/routes/vault.js:133`..`:190`), MCP servers (`mcp.servers.set/test`, `extension/background/routes/mcp.js:55` and `:71`), Data (owner export/import, factory reset, memory purge).
   1. RECOMMENDED: stay exact-document. The hub Settings view shows them through the existing iframe path at `options/options.html#<section>` (NO query string: `isExactOptionsSender` rejects every query and unknown fragment, `extension/lib/pure.js:891-897`).
   2. Gesture-bound step-up inside the hub (a new owner-approval seam; own design + own security review).
   3. A tiny credential-entry iframe only.
   4. Read-only list in the hub (via `provider.summary`) with an "Edit in Settings" link.

(b) `user-wasm` and `tool-library` are bound to the options DOCUMENT: pathname-checked store client `extension/lib/user-wasm-store-client.js:3-8`, `verifyOwnerOptionsContext` `extension/lib/wasm-package-admission.js:47`, SW exact-document re-assertions. RECOMMENDED: keep exact-document; they cannot render in the hub without a redesign.

(c) Approval-bound panels (Agents, Permissions): `ui:`-bound approvals can be resolved only by principal "owner-options" (`mayResolveApproval`, `extension/lib/owner-approval.js:934`; `runOwnerApprovedMutation` `extension/lib/owner-approved-mutation.js:41`). RECOMMENDED: keep exact-document and do NOT relax `mayResolveApproval`.

(d) Hub markup source. RECOMMENDED: lazy `fetch` + `DOMParser` of options.html, importing only the sections the hub hosts, so options.html stays the single source of markup (66 tests reference it and 44 read options.js as text). Alternative: copy ~54 KB (`extension/options/options.html`, 730 lines) into ntp.html: two sources, drift risk.

(e) Bundle budget. The repo is internally inconsistent and a lazy Settings view runs into it: the Constitution says budgets are "MEASURED AND REPORTED, not enforced" (`docs/CONSTITUTION.md:163-164`, and `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:14-19` records OWNER DECISION 2026-10-05 "The limits make no sense anymore"), yet `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1064` hard-asserts ntp <= 500_000, `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1070` options <= 450_000, `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1079` aggregate emitted chunks <= `STORE_AGGREGATE_CHUNKS_BUDGET_BYTES` (750_000, `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:24`), and the store build THROWS on the aggregate (`build.mjs:899-901`). `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1087` also requires that the SOURCE of ntp.js never mention `components-settings.js` or `tool-library`.
   1. RECOMMENDED: build the Settings view as its OWN lazily-imported surface bundle (the `SURFACE_BUNDLES` pattern, `build.mjs:742-749`, like `directory.bundle.js` at `build.mjs:745`) with its own report-only reference in `STORE_BUNDLE_BUDGETS` (`scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:32`). Then ntp <= 500_000 and the 750_000 aggregate are untouched; ntp.js still must not name `tool-library`.
   2. A dynamic `import()` inside the existing splitting build (`build.mjs:713-714`): simplest, but the lazy chunk counts toward the 750_000 aggregate, so the budget has to be raised with a recorded, measured justification.
   3. Amend the Constitution to say what the tests enforce.
   Measure with `npm run build:production`: the local `extension/dist` is the developer target (unminified) and its sizes are not comparable.

(f) Stage 4 (p9it) says "Completely delete panelFrames = new Map(), panelFrameFor(), and iframe creation logic in ntp.js". Under (a)-(c) some panels keep an iframe, so that cannot be literally true. RECOMMENDED: shrink Stage 4 to "retire the iframe POOL for every hub-ok panel; keep ONE exact-document iframe path for the exact-document panels with its own tests", and reword p9it's acceptance. Alternative: keep Stage 4 as written and treat (a)-(c) as a future redesign that blocks it.

## What each answer unblocks

- (d) and (e) gate 8v5l.3 rung 2 (lazy bundle + container). They are the only answers 8v5l.3 needs in order to START, so this bead BLOCKS 8v5l.3 (8v5l.1 and 8v5l.2 are long enough that the answer will not be on the critical path).
- (a)-(c) decide which panels 8v5l.3 may flip beyond Skills/About/Usage, and which routes 8v5l.2's allowlist may ever contain.
- (f) rewrites p9it's acceptance text.

## Not decided here

Whether any Settings-only route may ever be admitted to a hub session. That is per ROUTE, owner-approved on this bead as a comment, and lands as a reviewed allowlist edit with the census change in the same commit (see 8v5l.2).

## Done when

Paul answers (letters or "defaults"); the answers are recorded as a comment here and copied into the "Decision gate" line of 8v5l.3 and the acceptance of p9it if (f) changes it; then close this bead. Until then a worker must not treat any of (a)-(f) as answered.
close_reason: Owner (Paul, 2026-10-14 09:40 BST) answered 're: 1 - a-f defaults.' — defaults (a)-(f) recorded on l354r, 8v5l.3, and p9it.

OWNER DECISION RECORDED — Paul Kinlan, 2026-10-14 09:40 BST:
"re: 1 - a-f defaults."

All six recommended defaults (a)–(f) are ACCEPTED and now govern `chrome-agent-platform-8v5l.3` and `chrome-agent-platform-p9it`:
- (a) Credential and owner-flow panels (Providers, Web services, MCP servers, Data): stay exact-document (`options/options.html#<section>`, NO query string).
- (b) Document-bound panels (`user-wasm`, `tool-library`): stay exact-document.

- (d) Hub markup source: lazy `fetch` + `DOMParser` of `options.html`, importing only the sections the hub hosts (`options.html` stays the single source of markup).
- (e) Bundle budget: build the Settings view as its OWN lazily-imported surface bundle (`SURFACE_BUNDLES` pattern in `build.mjs:742-749`, like `directory.bundle.js` at `build.mjs:745`) with its own report-only reference in `STORE_BUNDLE_BUDGETS` (`scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:32`), keeping `ntp <= 500_000` (`tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1064`) and the `750_000` aggregate (`tests/bundle-budget.test.ts:1079`) untouched.
- (f) Stage 4 (`chrome-agent-platform-p9it`): shrink Stage 4 to "retire the iframe POOL for every hub-ok panel; keep ONE exact-document iframe path for the exact-document panels with its own tests", and reword `p9it`'s acceptance accordingly.

title: Remove the Chrome Prompt API (Gemini Nano) provider and migrate saved 'prompt-api' configs to demo (owner decision)
description:
## OWNER DECISION RECORDED — 2026-10-14 09:40 BST (Paul Kinlan: "re: 2 - we don't need it chrome prompt api. Remove it.")

Option **(a) REMOVE the Chrome Prompt API (Gemini Nano) provider** is selected by the owner. This bead is now an actionable P2 implementation task (work in a dedicated git worktree off `origin/main` per `AGENTS.md`, with a different-model review and full gate before landing).

### Complete verified seam inventory on `origin/main` (`73ea41ba`, v0.3.678)

1. **Adapter & model resolution**
   - Delete `extension/lib/models/prompt-api-model.js` (`createPromptApiModel`, `isPromptApiAvailable`, `estimateTokens`).
   - `extension/lib/provider.js:9`, `:28-30`, `:150-160`: remove the `prompt-api` import and branch in `resolveModelFromConfig`.
   - `extension/lib/provider-catalog.js:8`, `:77-82`: remove the `{ id: "prompt-api", label: "Chrome Prompt API (Gemini nano, on-device)", ... }` preset from `PROVIDER_CHOICES`.
   - `extension/lib/provider-test.js:6`, `:15-17`, `:109-135`: remove the `prompt-api` branch and imports from `testConnection`.
2. **Internal callers that called `prompt-api` directly**
   - `extension/background/service-worker.js:9300-9315` (`named-agent.refine`): remove the `resolveModelFromConfig({ provider: "prompt-api", ... })` first-try branch; use the configured provider directly.
   - `extension/lib/threads.js:22`, `:238-264` (`generateThreadName`): remove the `isPromptApiAvailable()` / `createPromptApiModel()` branch so `generateThreadName` uses the deterministic first-line fallback (and `nameThreadAsync` upgrades via the configured provider as it already does).
3. **Migration of stored `"prompt-api"` configs (global + named agents)**
   - Any saved global provider config (`provider: "prompt-api"`) or named-agent provider override (`provider: "prompt-api"`) must migrate/normalize cleanly to `"demo"` (or clear the unsupported id) without throwing, and surface an honest one-sentence notice when loaded in Settings (`extension/lib/provider-visibility.js`, `extension/background/routes/provider.js:126`).
   - `extension/lib/provider-visibility.js:7`: update `INTERNAL_PROVIDER_IDS` (keep `"demo"`; handle legacy stored `"prompt-api"` via the migration shim).
   - `extension/lib/provider-gate.js:46-49`: remove `"prompt-api"` from `LOCAL_PROVIDER_IDS` (keep `"demo"`).
   - `extension/lib/first-run-onboarding.js:71`, `:81`: remove `"prompt-api"` (or normalize migrated configs to `"demo"` first).
   - `extension/lib/named-agents.js:149`: remove `"prompt-api"` from the allowed provider set (migrating stored agent configs with `provider: "prompt-api"`).
   - `extension/lib/error-report.js:121`, `extension/ntp/ntp.js:5230`, `extension/options/options.js:153-156`: remove `"prompt-api"` labels/comments.
4. **Pricing, privacy statement, and tests**
   - `extension/lib/model-prices.js:5`, `:22`, `:95-96`, `:223`, `:299-302` and `scripts/refresh-model-prices.mjs:30-36`, `:92`: remove `"prompt-api"` / `"chrome-prompt-api"` / `"gemini-nano-prompt-api"` entries (keep the cloud-catalogue filter `!id.includes("nano")` in `model-prices.js:302` and `tests/named-agents-provider.test.ts:284` so `"gemini-nano"` never leaks from the Gemini cloud models endpoint!).
   - `extension/lib/privacy-statement.js:107` and `tests/privacy-statement.test.ts:114`: update `"Ollama, LM Studio and Chrome's built-in model run on this computer."` to `"Ollama and LM Studio run on this computer."` (and update `docs/components.html:659` if touched).
   - Delete `tests/prompt-api.test.ts` and `tests/prompt-api-tokens.test.ts` (update `docs/SYSTEM-PROMPTS.md:283` reference).
   - Update `tests/hub-run-ux.test.ts:22-24`, `tests/provider-gate.test.ts:92`, `:651-665` (replace with a falsification test for the `"prompt-api"` -> `"demo"` migration), `tests/provider-public-list.test.ts:47`, `:98`, `:130`, `tests/refresh-model-prices.test.ts:63`, `tests/threads.test.ts:141`, and `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:946`, `:4470-4476`.
5. **Out of scope (MUST NOT remove)**

title: agent-worker abort must name the ACTIVE run (abort-refused / run_not_live): worker guard, route relay, 3 tests
description:
Origin: 2026-10-12 parked-branch triage (bead 3cdz): branch work-afiu-r7@87e820ec = three review-round commits r7/r8/r9 of bead afiu (5562ea48, 521f2d26, 87e820ec). afiu was closed 'VERIFIED DONE' but only r5/r6 landed; the four 'merge: work-afiu-r7' commits on main (4522951d, 1e1d03f7, 01c6aade, a187fa7a) carry only version/CHANGELOG files. Verified on origin/main f4ff9170.

DEFECT: the worker's abort is unconditional and acks the REQUESTED id - extension/workers/agent-worker.js:279 `activeRun?.controller?.abort(); postMessage({ type: "agent-worker:aborted", runId: msg?.runId ?? "" ...`. A stop-run for a stale or different run id aborts whatever is active and reports success for the wrong run. The route (extension/background/routes/agent-worker.js:406) only expects the aborted reply. mxu5 (0c3cd85d) added service-worker callers that unregister the run and THEN post stop-run by agentId+runId (extension/background/service-worker.js:1762), so only a worker-side exact-match guard can refuse.

DO
- Fresh worktree off origin/main; apply 5562ea48, 521f2d26, 87e820ec reconciling with mxu5's edits in the route and worker files.
- Worker: reply abort-refused (code run_not_live) unless msg.runId equals the ACTIVE run's id; route: relay that as ok:false; the active-abort ack stays.
- Tests: no live run -> refused; wrong live run -> refused (asserted synchronously) and the active run keeps running; active abort still acked; route refusal case. npm run test:file on tests/agent-worker-protocol.test.ts and tests/agent-worker-host.test.ts.
FALSIFICATION: restore the unconditional abort -> RED. Different-model review.
MUST NOT CHANGE: the active-run abort ack and the 120 s timeout path.
REFERENCE (kept parked until this lands, then delete): branch work-afiu-r7. Closed bead afiu.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
Work complete on fleet/qazo-sswv2 @ 6b86411a (release 0.3.689).

Summary of changes:
1. extension/workers/agent-worker.js: In agent-worker:abort, require an exact active-run match (activeRun && activeRun.runId === String(msg?.runId ?? "")). If no run is live or a different run is active, reply agent-worker:abort-refused (run_not_live). Only abort activeRun when runId matches.
2. extension/background/routes/agent-worker.js: In mode === "stop-run", add agent-worker:abort-refused to expectReply.types. If received, relay as ok: false with error code (code: "run_not_live").
3. tests/agent-worker-protocol.test.ts: Added unit tests driving the real worker:
   - no-live abort is refused with agent-worker:abort-refused (run_not_live) and never acked as aborted.
   - wrong-live abort is asserted synchronously while the run is live, confirming refusal and verifying the live run completes cleanly to ok: true.
   - active-run abort is acknowledged with agent-worker:aborted without refusal.
4. tests/agent-worker-host.test.ts: Added route unit test verifying worker abort-refusal reaches caller as ok: false, code: "run_not_live".

Verification:
- Focused unit tests:
  - tests/agent-worker-protocol.test.ts: 7/7 ok (828ms).
  - tests/agent-worker-host.test.ts: 14/14 ok (75ms).
- Falsification: Restoring unconditional abort fails tests/agent-worker-protocol.test.ts (AssertionError: an abort with no live run must be refused).
- Production build: npm run build:production clean, byte-identical, version bumped 0.3.688 -> 0.3.689.
- Static checks: check:changelog, check:about, check:vocabulary, check:reachability, check:i18n all pass clean.
- Independent Review: openai-codex/gpt-6-sol reviewed delta 3452538a..6b86411a: PASS.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Guard agent-worker abort to require an exact active-run match, replying with abort-refused (run_not_live) if no run is live or a different run is active. Relay refusal in agent-worker route and add synchronous protocol and host tests.
WHY: Fixes defect where agent-worker abort was unconditional and falsely confirmed stops for completed runs or aborted newer active runs on stale requested IDs.
EFFECT: An abort command naming a non-active run honestly reports refusal (run_not_live) rather than false stop confirmation, leaving active runs undisturbed.

    over the package returns nothing). Its own help documents no MCP switch: "pi config" opens a TUI, and the one
    env-controlled lever it advertises is PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR ("Config directory (default: ~/.pi/agent)"), whose name the
    source derives dynamically as `${APP_NAME}_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.
  * So the branch's "the supported switch that turns host/imported config off" is an unsupported claim, and I am NOT
    repeating it as fact anywhere. The value is unverifiable from this VM, and CAP does not pin the pi CLI version at all
    (it pins only the adapter), so the variable could exist in some other pi build - I cannot check that from here.
  * I also will not overclaim the alternative: I did NOT prove that pi's MCP config lives under PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR. The
    mcpServers hits my grep found were inside a vendored Google SDK, not in pi's own MCP loading path, so PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR
    is a plausible lever rather than a verified one.
WHAT IS VERIFIED, and it is the half that matters for this bead's falsification: the pinned adapter spawns the pi CLI
with `env: process.env` (read in its source map, via PiRpcProcess.spawn({cwd, sessionPath, piCommand}), where piCommand is
PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND). So an environment variable set on the adapter DOES reach pi - the wiring is real and testable, and the
value can be corrected in one place later if the correct switch is identified.
(2) PI_ACP_HARNESS vs CAP_ACP_HARNESS - DECISION: NO CHANGE, they are two different consumers and not a mismatch.
  * acp-bridge.ts:1116 sets PI_ACP_HARNESS inside the ADAPTER's own child env, in the same object as the PATH comment
    "because it spawns the harness CLI itself" - it is the bridge telling the adapter which harness it is running.
  * acp-native-host.ts:13,20 reads CAP_ACP_HARNESS as the NATIVE HOST's launch environment (Chrome launches that process),
    defaulting to "pi", and resolves its adapter at :54 with that value.
  So the native host already knows its harness through its own variable and needs nothing from the bridge. Site 2's
  isolation env can use its existing HARNESS, and no channel rename is required. Recorded because the boot instruction
  asked for the decision, not because it needs code.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX, stated so nobody is surprised: I will implement the composition and the wiring at BOTH sites, and
pin the wiring with the both-paths falsification the bead demands (a mutant removing it from either site goes RED). The
variable NAME and VALUE I wire will carry an explicit caveat in the code, the test and the doc saying pi's handling of it
is unverified against the installed pi and was unsubstantiated on the parked branch - so nobody reads the comment as a
proof of isolation that was never measured. If you would rather I wire PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR-style isolation, or hold the
value until the real switch is confirmed, say so and it is a one-place change in the composer.

title: heavy-gate-slot: announce 'waiting' only after a grace + fresh read (n772) and classify flock setup vs contention by status pair (o3rx)
description:
Origin: 2026-10-12 parked-branch triage (bead 3cdz). Two closed P2 beads, n772 and o3rx, were closed 2026-10-09 "already on main by content" for their PRE-REVISION premise (true: the default-reader path mismatch is fixed at scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts:105-107). A semantic check of the parked branches fix/n772-one-sidecar-path@0dae9c74 and fix/o3rx-flock-setup-vs-contention@f0959578 (f0959578 is also the second commit of fix/k9i3-clear-timers@011de744) found their real deliverables are NOT on origin/main f4ff9170.

MISSING ON MAIN (scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts, acquireHeavyGateSlot)
1. n772 - a FREE slot still announces "heavy-gate: <gate> waiting for the fleet-wide gate slot ... held by an unnamed holder (no announcement sidecar)" at the top of the first loop iteration (:283-289) although the acquisition completes in ~8 ms: a holder claim where there was no holder, so real contention is indistinguishable from an uncontended acquire in every gate log. Branch fix: announce only after a 200 ms grace with a FRESH holder read (so the real holder is named) and poll the read at 250 ms so the loop can reach that point within the bound. ANNOUNCE_WAIT_AFTER_MS appears nowhere on main.
2. o3rx - main's discriminator is still the stderr scan (:337, /cannot open lock file|Permission denied|No such file or directory/), so a silent non-handshake helper exit (a stub/wrapper flock exiting 0 or 70, or a signal) is blamed on a peer as "busy". Branch fix: classify by the (status, signal) pair - contention = quiet exit 1 or helper killed while waiting; everything else is SETUP with a 300-char bounded detail naming the status/signal (exitSignal, quietTimeout, killedWhileWaiting; none exist on main). o3rx's close holds only for the exit-66 'cannot open lock file' case.

TESTS MISSING (tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts): n772-a executing default-reader check (acquire the real default slot only if free, 300 ms bound, read via the DEFAULT reader; print an explicit INCONCLUSIVE rather than pass when another lane holds it); n772-b private-slot isolation (announcement beside its own slot, default bytes identical before/after); n772-c a free slot announces NO wait, a contested wait names the holder once; o3rx-a/b/c missing-sh exec failure, read-only lock dir (chmod 500), silent stub flock exit 0/70 must be SETUP, never "held by".

HOW
- Fresh worktree off origin/main. Re-implement from the branches as a DESIGN REFERENCE; do not rebase or push the foreign branches (hub ruling 2026-10-08: foreign branches are not the VM fleet's).
- Port n772 + o3rx together (disjoint source regions; both append tests at EOF). Union with main's existing k9i3 backstop-clear block (df14bba5) - do not drop it.
- Re-measure status.code for a SIGKILLed helper under the repo's Deno (the branch assumes null; Deno may report 128+signal). The drills need Linux flock.
- Reproduce the branch authors' mutants: M1 reintroduce the reported drift -> n772-a RED; M2 private slot resolving to the default path -> n772-b RED; M3 announce at the top of the first iteration -> n772-c RED; M4 read the whole deadline instead of polling -> n772-c RED.

MUST NOT CHANGE: exit-66 'cannot open lock file' behaviour, private-slot isolation, the slot bound semantics.
GATES: npm run test:file -- tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts, then the full gate; a different-model review.
REFERENCES (kept parked until this lands, then delete): fix/n772-one-sidecar-path, fix/o3rx-flock-setup-vs-contention, fix/k9i3-clear-timers. Closed beads n772, o3rx, k9i3.
