title: pi-subagents worktrees symlink node_modules to the primary, so build:production refuses cap-security-dependency-resolve and the printed fix (deno install) is the unsafe one
description:
Measured 2026-10-09 in a pi-subagents worktree at origin/main 7bf4524c7 (/home/exedev/worktrees/chrome-agent-platform/pi-worktree-...-s0-0), chrome-agent-platform-gafh port.

WHAT HAPPENED: `npm run build:production` refused immediately:

  Error: cap-security-dependency-resolve: AJV (/home/exedev/chrome-agent-platform/node_modules/.deno/ajv@8.20.0/node_modules/ajv/dist/runtime/uri.js) resolves fast-uri 3.1.7 at /home/exedev/chrome-agent-platform/node_modules/.deno/fast-uri@3.1.7/...; npm and Deno locks require fast-uri 3.1.7 at <worktree>/node_modules/.deno/fast-uri@3.1.7/...  Run `deno install --frozen-lockfile` in this worktree and retry.

CAUSE: the worktree's node_modules is a SYMLINK to the primary checkout's node_modules (`node_modules -> /home/exedev/chrome-agent-platform/node_modules`, created when the pi worktree was materialised), so every resolution reports the PRIMARY's path while scripts/bundle-budget.mjs compares it against the worktree's expected path and refuses. The guard is right; the setup is what is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS: the failure names neither the symlink nor the fix, and the message it does print ("run deno install --frozen-lockfile in this worktree") is the DANGEROUS one here — with node_modules symlinked to the primary, deno install writes into the shared primary store, which is exactly the cross-lane interference AGENTS.md forbids. A pi worker lane that needs a production build (any lane running a browser gate or npm test) hits this with no path forward it can trust.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKED, in the documented order (npm ci THEN deno install LAST, chrome-agent-platform-knu79): `rm -f node_modules` (rm -F, so it removes the symlink and not its target's contents) && `npm ci` && `deno install` && `npm run build:production`. After that the bundle-budget fast-uri assertion passed and dist.complete bound the exact HEAD.

ACCEPTANCE FOR DONE: either (a) the pi-subagents worktree materialiser stops symlinking node_modules (give each worktree its own real node_modules), or (b) bundle-budget.mjs DETECTS the symlinked-store case and refuses with a message that names the symlink and gives the safe recovery (`rm -f node_modules && npm ci && deno install`, never deno install alone against a symlinked store) — and the same for any guard that compares a resolved path against the worktree root. Falsification: a worktree with a symlinked node_modules runs npm run build:production to a named, actionable message rather than the current AJV/fast-uri line.

SEAMS: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:217 (refuse) + :263 (assertLiveFastUriResolution), scripts/lib/... (the worktree materialiser is outside this repo: pi-subagents), AGENTS.md "set it up before the first gate" ladder.

title: a harness loading ${ROOT}extension crashes with an opaque TypeError when extension/dist is absent - name the cause
description:
Measured 2026-10-09 (chrome-agent-platform-gafh port, pi worktree at origin/main 7bf4524c7).

WHAT HAPPENED: scripts/kat-sandbox-egress.ts was run in a worktree that had node_modules but NO extension/dist (generated by npm run build:production). It died on its FIRST browser step with:

  error: Uncaught (in promise) PageThrowError: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getURL')
    at <anonymous>:2:46
    at scripts/kat-sandbox-egress.ts:272:12

The message names neither the cause nor the file. The cause: extension/manifest.json:52 declares "background": {"service_worker": "dist/background/service-worker.js"}; with that file absent Chrome REFUSES to load the unpacked extension, so navigating to chrome-extension://<id>/options/options.html lands on an error page where chrome.runtime is undefined — and the first line of the eval (chrome.runtime.getURL(...)) throws. Nothing checks that the extension the harness is about to drive actually loaded, so an unbuilt tree reads as a mysterious page throw.

WHY IT MATTERS (the repo's own canon): a harness that cannot tell "the extension did not load" from "the sandbox misbehaved" is the same class as test-honesty mode 5 and the fixed-debugging-port rule — a verdict about a tree it never loaded. Here it was expensive rather than silent (the run aborted), but the same gap on a lenient path would report PASS having asserted nothing. It cost one wasted browser gate plus the first KAT attempt before the missing dist was identified.

ACCEPTANCE FOR DONE: a harness that launches with {extension} fails LOUDLY and NAMED before its first eval when the unpacked extension did not load. E.g. launchChrome (or a shared helper) asserts the extension's service-worker target exists (cdp.serviceWorker() already returns null when it does not), or that chrome.runtime is defined on the page it opened, and the error says "the extension at <path> did not load: <path>/dist/background/service-worker.js is missing — run npm run build:production" rather than a TypeError from inside the eval. Falsification: with extension/dist removed the harness fails with the named message (not the TypeError); with the build present it runs as before. Do NOT weaken it into a skip.

SEAMS: scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts (launchChrome, openCdp, CdpClient.serviceWorker at :1103), scripts/kat-sandbox-egress.ts:263 (its three launches), and every other harness whose EXT literal is `${ROOT}extension` (scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:14 and ~40 more).

comments.text:
Root Cause & Mechanism:
1. Codex CLI adapter returns JSON-RPC error frame { error: { code: -32000, message: 'Authentication required' } } and _auth/status_update notification { authStatus: { kind: 'none', label: 'Not logged in' } } because Codex CLI lacks an active OpenAI API key/session on this VM.

  * Log adapter auth status updates when not logged in: [acp-bridge] adapter auth status for harness "<harness>": <label>.
  * Log adapter process exit status and stderr detail unconditionally, even if client socket closed first.
- In cap-evidence/vl6c-browser-acceptance.ts:

WHY: When an ACP harness adapter encounters errors (such as unauthenticated Codex CLI), the bridge log was silent and acceptance reported 'ERROR undefined', hiding the failure reason.

title: Implement the append-only master-journal WAL under ONE write authority (dedicated workstream)
description: Split out of chrome-agent-platform-9epn.10 after j5yz scout+oracle analysis (plan /home/exedev/cap-evidence/j5yz-9epn10-plan.md): a SAFE append-only WAL is not a small patch - it needs one authority covering master CAS/receipt/re-enrollment, archive overflow, cutover/backup restore, and raw-file readers of journal.json. 9epn.10 now lands only the corrected measurement RED (cumulative journal.json bytes across 300 appends). This bead owns the implementation + crash-state cutover. Do not land a partial migration that can lose receipt/CAS/archive state.
design:
Design of record proposed by j5yz scout+architecture advisor (2026-10-09): /home/exedev/cap-evidence/j5yz-9epn10-plan.md; scout /home/exedev/cap-evidence/j5yz-9epn10-wal-scout.md; advisor /home/exedev/cap-evidence/j5yz-9epn10-wal-oracle.md. These are a plan, NOT a tested durability claim. 9epn.10 owns the baseline byte-amplification falsifier and must land first.

Safety boundary: the master journal WAL becomes ONE authoritative store, with no per-append journal.json mirror. Do not expose WAL writes while masterMemory().get/getStrict/has/snapshot/getVersion/keys, trusted set, compareAndRestore/Delete, delete/clear, journalAppendOnce, journalCommitCancellation, journalAppendWithReceipt, journalCompensateExecution, archived overflow, raw OPFS backup/restore, target registry and old-backup import still disagree about authority. Site/named/background journals remain legacy initially; skill-identity migration's raw journal JSON handling is background-scoped and must remain intact.

Cutover/recovery: under the existing master-directory write mutex, strict-read legacy journal.json and journal-archive.json and their existence/envelope versions; write+verify a bounded checkpoint, archive base and empty generation-stamped WAL; publish a durable cutover pointer LAST. Before the marker legacy is authoritative and an interruption retries migration; after it only the new generation is authoritative. Retain old files until verified cleanup. Never merge an interrupted half-migration with legacy data. Preserve tombstone authority and epoch reset across clear/delete/re-enrollment so stale WAL cannot resurrect rows.

Append/version: issue and persist a never-reused generation before a framed WAL transaction. One transaction must account for the new row AND any live-ring eviction/archive effect; a separately committed archive JSON write is not atomic. Close+verify before returning a version or receipt. A partial final frame must be quarantined/recorded before append repair; corrupt complete/interior frames or a sequence gap fail closed. Do not silently skip using run-log-wal.parseRecords (it tolerates bad rows). Replay on restart from a verified checkpoint/offset; bound the in-memory tail.

Receipts/CAS: preserve absent vs present-empty, 500-row eviction restoration, foreign later appends, same-value ABA refusal and generation-scoped refusal. Receipt needs WAL operation identity, epoch, exact write token and pre/eviction evidence; compensation may only follow proved append-only lineage and uses the ACTUAL new generation token, not current.version+1. Cancellation is a versioned operation on the same WAL authority. A failure during append/compaction/compensation cannot silently claim a row durable or lose acknowledged rows.

Compaction/archive/backup: write+verify a new checkpoint generation, publish pointer then retire only covered WAL; append archive overflow to immutable/appendable bounded segments rather than rewriting an ever-growing journal-archive array. Include checkpoint/WAL/archive in authority-aware export and import as a coherent snapshot; exercise old-backup import and new-profile backup→restore. Classify new leaves in archive-target-registry, and ensure purge/orphan cleanup deletes or invalidates every generation without losing tombstone protection. No cross-context single-writer assumption without Chrome/browser proof.

Ordered execution: (1) format/crash-state table + fault-injecting seek/keepExistingData/close/partial-write fake and legacy compatibility tests; (2) reader/cutover adapter with WAL writer disabled; (3) all master mutations + framed writer + receipt/CAS/cancellation; (4) archive/checkpoint compaction and raw-file integration; (5) actual Chrome restart/backup→restore and 120/500 seeded-scale performance, only then GROWTH_SOFT=false at ≤1.2×. Landing an intermediate boundary must not publish a partial WAL authority. Required falsifiers: crash at every cutover and append publication step, terminal torn tail and corrupt interior, restart, concurrent master append/setTrusted/CAS/delete/clear, ABA/re-enrollment, receipt absent/empty/500 eviction+foreign later, cancellation, backup/restore, archive rollover. Reuse 9epn.10 cumulative-bytes RED and zero-keys GREEN; the latter was already green on pre-change main and is not a RED proof.

title: Q23 hygiene: enrolled consent deny-matching is case-sensitive (re-registering a denied tool in different casing re-asks instead of honoring the sticky Deny)
description: Found by j5yz while hardening ckebt (not introduced by D2 or ckebt; pre-existing enrolled-path behaviour). The ENROLLED Q23 consent path matches tool names verbatim: site-tool-consent.js:244 snapshotFrom compares candidate.name === identity.name; :442-455 promotion merges by verbatim record.name; tools.js:480 folds an old Deny by exact name; SW :9736-9740 fresh candidate matches exact name then the consent snapshot. Effect: after a Deny for 'Foo', a page can re-register the same tool as 'foo' (or another casing) and be RE-ASKED — the existing exact-name Deny persists but is not applied to the case-variant. This is NOT an auto-approval bypass (the owner is prompted again, default remain deny), but it weakens Q23 'Deny sticky' for casing variants. FIX (when scoped): normalize the consent identity for deny MATCHING/remembrance in the enrolled path the same way ckebt already does for the ephemeral path (nameKey lowercase), WITHOUT changing approval semantics or requiring exact-name dispatch to relax (dispatch must still require the exact fresh declared name). Do not fold into the D2 preparatory landing or ckebt.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
Implemented and pushed on branch fleet/qazo-n6c31 @ 4e5bb968e72260fe83e36687c16e03b60a4a42bf (off origin/main @ 0d5ebc73c).

WHAT CHANGED:
- extension/lib/site-tool-consent.js:
  - Exported nameKey (lowercase normalization) to unify tool name normalization across enrolled and ephemeral paths.
  - Updated snapshotFrom to match Deny records case-insensitively using nameKey so re-registering a denied tool under different casing ('Foo' -> 'foo' or 'FOO') immediately resolves to 'denied' without re-prompting the owner.
  - Preserved strict identity matching for Allow (Allow does not relax to casing variants).
  - Updated setSiteToolConsent to replace existing records under the same normalized nameKey.
  - Updated promoteEphemeralSiteToolConsents to ensure any persisted Deny displaces run-local decisions across casing variants.
- extension/lib/tools.js:
  - Updated prepareEnrollmentPromotion to ensure old-generation sticky Deny records displace run-local decisions across casing variants during promotion.
- extension/lib/ephemeral-site-tool-consent.js:
  - Imported shared nameKey from site-tool-consent.js.
- tests/webmcp-autoapprove.test.ts:
  - Added test verifying enrolled consent Deny is sticky across lowercase, uppercase, and mixed-case re-registrations.
- tests/enrollment-promotion-transaction.test.ts:
  - Added test verifying old-generation Deny cannot be bypassed by promoting a differently-cased Allow.

VERIFICATION EVIDENCE:
- npm run test:file -- tests/webmcp-autoapprove.test.ts: 20/20 passed (717ms).

WHAT: Normalize Q23 enrolled consent Deny matching to be case-insensitive (using shared nameKey), while preserving exact-name dispatch and strict Allow semantics.
WHY: When an owner denied a tool, a site could re-register the same tool in different casing ('Foo' -> 'foo') and re-prompt the owner instead of honoring the sticky Deny.

title: check-reachability: re-export false-negative — a direct origin use credits sibling barrels (strictExports must stay non-default)
description: Follow-up to kf3h (landed with documented residual, strictExports non-default). Final review found: resolveCanonical() credits the origin correctly, but final classification treats reachedKeys.has(canonicalKey) as sufficient for EVERY barrel export resolving to that origin (scripts/check-reachability.mjs:600-608). So if a consumer imports and calls foo directly from c.js while a.js and b.js merely re-export foo with no consumers, the direct call marks c.js:foo reached and ALSO marks the unused a.js:foo and b.js:foo reached -> dead barrel exports hidden, and a valid retained entry on one is reported redundantly reachable. FIX: record the specific re-export nodes traversed by each used import; credit the origin and ONLY those intermediate nodes; add a fixture with a directly used origin + an unused sibling barrel. Do NOT enable --strict-exports until this is fixed.

title: vk1t trailing-slash override test mutates process-global CAP_DURABLE_ROOT in-process under deno test --parallel: ENOTEMPTY on its own cleanup and torn reads in unrelated tests
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing gate, commit c4d4633a, attempt 1, 2026-10-08 13:44)

`tests/chrome-profile-admission.test.ts:54` "vk1t: trailing-slash durable-root override still admits under the
normalized profile root" FAILED (6 ms) in its `finally` (line 66):

    Error: Directory not empty (os error 66): remove '/Users/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/vk1t-durable-override-fixture-34975-1791463427466'

It passed in 28 of the 29 retained full-run logs from the jjsz lane trees (26 distinct full runs, one red, about 4 percent).
The failing log is `/Users/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/jjsz-landing/gates/c4d4633a-attempt1-display-awake/test.log`, lines 8912-8921.
The test, `chrome-profile-dir.ts` and `durable-root.mjs` are not touched by the jjsz diff; the extension dist is byte-identical to origin/main.
The leftover fixture directory held an EMPTY `cap-chrome-profiles/`: a concurrent `chromeProfileDir()` caller created and later removed an entry
under `${base}/cap-chrome-profiles` between vk1t's directory traversal and its final rmdir.

## Mechanism (reproduced with scratch files, evidence: `/Users/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/jjsz-landing/vk1t-race/`)

Line 59 does `Deno.env.set("CAP_DURABLE_ROOT", `${base}/`)` in the shared parallel test process. `deno test --parallel` interleaves test
MODULES in ONE process; `tests/durable-root.test.ts:13-25` (bead 5rwd) records the same hazard and moved ITS env cases into a child process.
`durableRoot()` reads `process.env.CAP_DURABLE_ROOT` on every call, so any concurrent test that calls `durableRoot()`, `durableDir()` or
`chromeProfileDir()` while the override is set (2-14 ms in the retained logs, 32 and 83 ms outliers) resolves `${base}/` instead of the real root.

Scratch repro (deno 2.9.0, macOS arm64, `deno test --parallel --no-check` over two files, CAP_DURABLE_ROOT pre-set to a scratch root):
1. Env window widened to 400 ms plus an unrelated reader that never touches the env var: 1001 to 1120 of the reader's default
   `chromeProfileDir()` calls resolved UNDER the victim's fixture, 3 runs out of 3.
2. The unwidened vk1t body repeated 400 times against a flat-out reader: `Directory not empty (os error 66)` on 14, 15 and 19 of 400 iterations
   per run (3.5 to 4.8 percent). That is the exact message and failure point of the gate red.
3. The same hammer made the READER fail: `chromeProfileDir: fixture root must be a direct cap-chrome-profiles-* child of the durable root`
   57, 70 and 77 times per run. `chromeProfileDir` reads `durableRoot()` twice (line 60 default argument, line 72), and the env flipping between
   the two reads is a torn read. An INNOCENT test fails with a message that never mentions vk1t.

## Impact

- Reds the test itself in roughly 4 percent of full runs on this host (base rate on origin/main unmeasured).
- Can fail or silently misdirect any concurrent test that resolves the durable root; there are hundreds of such call sites (acp-*, agent-*, build-*,
  chrome-profile-location, the jjsz-* tests, ...). The jjsz lane adds about nine more readers, so it slightly widens the exposure, but it did not create it.
- Same class as MERGER-PLAYBOOK section 2 `m3a2` (process-global CAP_DURABLE_ROOT mutated in the shared parallel process), different mutator.
  The playbook names only `tests/durable-root.test.ts:69`, so under its rule this is a PRODUCT RED until the owner records a decision.
  (Companion: chrome-agent-platform-m9g43 recommends the playbook amendment.)

## Do

1. Move the override case into a CHILD process with its own environment, the 5rwd pattern in `tests/durable-root.test.ts:26-71`:
   `new Deno.Command(Deno.execPath(), { args: ["eval", script], clearEnv: true, env: { HOME, CAP_DURABLE_ROOT: `${base}/` } })`.
   The parent asserts only on what the child prints: the created path starts with `${base}/cap-chrome-profiles/` and is a directory. Keep the
   fixture cleanup in the parent, now race-free because nothing else can resolve `${base}/`.
2. Add a static pin: no `tests/*.test.ts` may set `CAP_DURABLE_ROOT` in the PARENT test process (`Deno.env.set("CAP_DURABLE_ROOT"` or
   `process.env.CAP_DURABLE_ROOT =`). Child-script strings and the machine-path-honesty detector fixtures are the allowlist. Mutation drill:
   re-introduce the in-process set, the pin must go RED.
3. Do NOT add a retry or swallow ENOTEMPTY in the test: that hides the misdirected readers (finding 3 above).

## Acceptance

- No test mutates `CAP_DURABLE_ROOT` inside the shared parallel process; the pin fails when one does.
- The scratch repro (`victim-loop.test.ts` + `reader-hammer.test.ts`, run against the FIXED test body) shows zero ENOTEMPTY and zero torn-read errors.
- `npm run test:file -- tests/chrome-profile-admission.test.ts` passes; `npm test` green.

## Must not change

- `chromeProfileDir()` admission semantics (cap, flock across processes, symlink refusal, trailing-slash normalization that this test pins).
- The 5rwd child-process cases in `tests/durable-root.test.ts`.

title: A sleeping macOS display makes every screenshot test fail (12 s, null screenshot) and reads as a product red
description:
OBSERVED (2026-10-08, chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing, commit 2247514c on one macOS arm64 host). A full gate went red twice in a row on exactly the same two real-browser tests, and both full runs started minutes apart:
- tests/g09i-sidebar-tab.test.ts:54  AssertionError "capture the collapsed rail before keyboard navigation"
- tests/w51r-create-click.test.ts:91 AssertionError "the open dialog needs screenshot evidence"
Both failed at 12 to 13 s. That is safeCaptureScreenshot (scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts, about line 1000) giving up: first attempt up to the caller's 6 s, a 1.5 s compositor wake, a fallback capped at 4 s, then it returns null and the test asserts on null. Nothing else failed in either run (5998 passed, 2 failed, 1 ignored; test:changed fell closed to the whole suite).

MECHANISM (measured, not guessed). `pmset -g log` shows "Display is turned off" at 12:36:14, 37 s after the first full run started; the console session was locked and both displays reported "Display Asleep: Yes" afterwards. Isolation A/B on the SAME tree, same host, minutes apart, each test alone (not under load, one-minute load 5.7 to 11):
  - displays asleep (console locked): g09i 3/3 FAIL, w51r 3/3 FAIL, 12 to 15 s each, same assertion messages as in the gate;
  - displays awake (`caffeinate -d -i -u` around the run; the console STILL locked): g09i 3/3 PASS, w51r 3/3 PASS, 3 to 4 s each.
So the display being asleep, not load and not the session lock, is what makes Page.captureScreenshot return nothing in headless=new Chrome for Testing on macOS. The control for the whole suite: a full gate on the same tree with the display held awake (`caffeinate -d -i -u`): `npm test` GREEN (6000 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; 20 serial + 637 parallel files; 104 s) and `test:build` GREEN; `test:changed` (the same whole suite on this diff) was red on ONE unrelated test (ntp-boot-staging, a 51 ms main-thread task) and green on both screenshot tests. Logs: the landing evidence bundle, red-gate-ab/display-state/.
This is a SECOND, SEPARATE cause. Every earlier real-browser red of that landing (ntp-boot-staging long task 51 to 72 ms, delegation Runtime.evaluate timeout, Target.getTargets deadline, bgagent-delete) happened with the display ON (pmset timeline in the bundle README), so this does not explain them and must not be used to explain them.

WHY IT MATTERS: the failure is silent and unnamed. A gate started on a laptop whose display has slept (an agent working while the owner is away, which is the normal mode of this repo) reads as a PRODUCT RED on two unrelated UI tests; docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md section 2 gives it no signature, so it either blocks a good landing or invites a mood-based waiver. Two such runs cost a landing cycle here.

DESIGN OPTIONS (pick one and state why; the first is the smallest):
 (a) scripts/run-tests.mjs (and the landing gate commands) hold a display-awake assertion on darwin for the phases that launch browsers: spawn `caffeinate -d -i -w <pid>` once per run and release it at exit; plus one line in docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md ("macOS: a sleeping display makes every screenshot test fail; the runner keeps it awake").
 (b) detect a sleeping display before the real-browser fan-out and REFUSE environmentally with the exit-75 verdict (scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts is the model) naming the display state and the number of tests it left unverified, so it can never read as green or as a product red.
 (c) both.
Whichever, a test must prove it: a fake darwin power-state seam (inject the `pmset -g` / `system_profiler` reader) so the wrap and the refusal are driven deterministically on Linux CI too.

ACCEPTANCE: a gate started with the display asleep either passes the screenshot tests or stops with a NAMED environmental refusal that counts the unverified tests; a mutant that removes the wrap (or the detector) is rejected by a named test, drilled with a byte-identical restore; no assertion in tests/g09i-sidebar-tab.test.ts or tests/w51r-create-click.test.ts is loosened (they must still fail when the screenshot really is null). Must NOT change: the screenshot helper's honest null on a real failure.

SEAMS: scripts/run-tests.mjs, scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts (safeCaptureScreenshot), scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts, scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts (the exit-75 verdict), docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md, docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md section 2 (see chrome-agent-platform-m9g43).
close_reason: LANDED on main as bbec9158 (release 0.3.693), merged fleet/j5yz-jkeuo@556a24d7, full gate PASS on tree 1ee90fed in 426s. Preserves the screenshot helper terminal failure CAUSE (stage, outcome and error text) instead of collapsing every path into a bare null, with the null contract unchanged, no assertion weakened, no timeout changed and no user-visible product change; the falsification leg was recorded and independently verified (base helper against the candidate test reds the diagnostics assertion, restored tree green 4/0). The macOS display-sleep workaround and the fail-closed display-session preflight were deliberately OUT of scope and are routed host-side per the hub, which confirmed no masking is acceptable in product tests - this change does not mask.

title: tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts is state dependent: red on a host whose beads tracker has not pulled, green on one that has
description:
OBSERVED (2026-10-08, chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing). tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts, the SOURCE-BOUND test (line ~91, assertion ~105 "expected at least one already-closed referenced bead in the last 30 commits"), is red on a host whose beads tracker has not pulled recently and green on one that has. Its window is `origin/main~30..origin/main`, so the beads it must find move with every landing. The oracle reads the committed .beads/issues.jsonl snapshot first and falls back to a live `bd show`; at fddeb1a2 the committed snapshot held 2 of the 24 beads those 30 commits reference (neither closed), so the answer comes from the live tracker.

MEASURED: pristine worktree at origin/main fddeb1a2, bd 1.3.0. Against a tracker of 1147 issues (not pulled): 22 of 22 referenced beads print "not found" and the test is red. After `bd dolt pull` (1215 issues): the same test is 4/4 green (SOURCE-BOUND about 6 s). `bd show a b c` with several ids works on this bd (found ids print, missing ids print "not found", exit 0), so the fallback itself is not broken; the dependence on tracker currency is the defect. The lane that found it first mis-diagnosed it as a broken fallback, took its own copy of the test, and retracted that later (see the jjsz landing record).

WHY IT MATTERS: a gate that goes red because a host has not pulled looks exactly like a product regression, and a fresh clone with no tracker (or a CI host) cannot be green at all. It also means the test proves nothing about the link tool on such a host, it only reports on the tracker.

DESIGN (choose one, state why): (a) pin the window to a fixed historic range that is present, with known closed beads, in every clone's committed snapshot, so the property is checked against history that never moves; or (b) keep the moving window but, when the tracker lacks the referenced beads, skip HONESTLY (an ignored test with a named reason, never a silent pass), and keep one fixed-fixture test that proves the closed/open classification in every environment. Whichever you pick, the classification (a referenced, closed bead is reported closed; a referenced open one is reported open; a bead with no landing reference is reported not landed) must still be proven by an assertion that fails if scripts/beads-landing-link.mjs stops classifying.

ACCEPTANCE: the test is green on a host whose tracker lacks the last 30 commits' beads AND still red under a mutant of scripts/beads-landing-link.mjs that reports everything as open (drill it, byte-identical restore). Must NOT change: the tool's behaviour or its CLI.

SEAMS: tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts, scripts/beads-landing-link.mjs, docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md section 3 step 10.

title: fleet-check run from a disposable pi-subagents worktree dies with rc 7 / zero output and caches a FALSE FAIL when the worktree is cleaned under the gate
description:
MEASURED 2026-10-08, three times: background 'worker' subagents dispatch fleet-check from their pi-subagents-managed worktree; when the worker finishes/times out, pi-subagents removes the worktree WHILE the gate is still queued/running. The gate then exits rc 7 (never 124/137/143) with a log containing only heavy-slot waits + 'gate started' and ZERO test output, and the classifier caches state FAIL. Observed: knu79 tree b9d43a71 (twice), 8ebqf tree df4dd956, 5xo59 tree 516500aa. A CLEAN re-run of knu79 from a PERSISTENT worktree PASSED 5599/0 + build 3/3, proving the reds were artifacts.

FIX OPTIONS (pick one, add a regression):
(a) subagent workers must run fleet-check from a PERSISTENT worktree (never the disposable pi-subagents worktree), or
(b) fleet-check snapshots/copies the tree before running so cleanup cannot kill it, or
(c) pi-subagents cleanup waits for any registered fleet-check/detached child before removing the worktree.
PLUS: the classifier must distinguish a gate whose worktree vanished (report KILLED/unknown, NOT FAIL) and must not cache a bogus FAIL. Recovery already used: rm ~/.fleet/checks/<tree>.{json,lock} then re-run from a persistent worktree.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan (fleet:chrome-agent-platform)
comments.text:
2026-10-08 10:40Z - HUB NOTE ON SEVERITY, because the title understates this and it blocks a reviewed change rather than merely wasting a slot.

The reported chain: a background worker dispatches fleet-check from its DISPOSABLE pi-subagents worktree; the worker exits; the worktree is cleaned underneath the running gate; the gate exits rc7 with zero test output; and - the part that matters most - a FALSE FAIL gets CACHED against that commit tree. Hit four times in one day (knu79 x2, 8ebqf, 5xo59), and a re-run of knu79 from a persistent worktree passed 5599/0.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN WASTED CPU: fleet-check verdicts are CACHED PER COMMIT TREE on the VM, and the cache is what a reviewer or merger is told to quote instead of re-running. So a bogus FAIL does not just cost one run - it becomes the recorded verdict for that tree, and the next person to ask about it is handed "this tree failed" with zero test output as the evidence. That is a poisoned result in the instrument the fleet uses to decide whether to land, which is a different class from a slow or wasted run. Corollary for whoever fixes it: the fix must include NOT CACHING a gate result that produced no test output, because a cache entry with no evidence is worse than a cache miss.

THE FOUR FIX OPTIONS, ranked by how much they remove rather than mitigate:
1. The gate holds its own worktree reference so cleanup cannot pull it out from under a running job - removes the race entirely.
2. Cleanup WAITS for a running gate on that tree, or the dispatcher pins a persistent worktree for gate runs - removes the race for the dispatch path.
3. Do not cache a verdict whose output is empty or whose exit code indicates the harness died (rc7 here) - limits the damage to the wasted run.
4. Snapshot the tree before running - protects the evidence.
Options 1 or 2 alone fix it; option 3 alone does not, but it should be added regardless, because it is the guard that turns any future variant of this into a wasted run rather than a poisoned verdict.

RAISED BY PAUL the same hour, independently: "workers producing 0 commits is absolutely insane and a failure. These are errors in the build and/or testing process." This bug is a concrete instance of exactly that, and the root cause is the fleet's tooling rather than the workers - worth noting in the writeup so the fix is aimed at the harness rather than at lane discipline.

title: build.mjs cap-ai-sdk-dedup fail-closes on an npm-flat node_modules and only says 'run deno install' (insufficient after npm ci overwrote the layout)
description:
REPRODUCED FROM PAUL, 2026-10-08, on his Mac (node v25.3.0) at main dfb4a054 (0.3.600) after 'git pull origin main' + 'npm run build':

  Error: cap-ai-sdk-dedup: no @modelcontextprotocol/sdk instance is bound to the extension's zod
  (/Users/paulkinlan/Code/chrome-agent-platform/node_modules/zod). The SDK must share one zod with
  lib/mcp-client.js and agent-do; run deno install and retry.
    at build.mjs:475

ROOT CAUSE (strong, not yet falsified on a Mac): build.mjs requires the DENO peer-context node_modules layout.
On this VM node_modules/zod is a SYMLINK into node_modules/.deno/zod@3.25.76/... and node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk
is a symlink into node_modules/.deno/@modelcontextprotocol+sdk@1.31.0/... , so the SDK's zod peer === realpath(node_modules/zod)
and the initial check passes. Paul's error printed CANON_ZOD_DIR as a REAL path (/Users/.../node_modules/zod, not a .deno path),
i.e. npm ci/npm install produced a FLAT npm layout: node_modules/zod is a real directory, no Deno peer context exists. The
fallback scans node_modules/.deno store entries for an SDK whose zod peer === that real dir; npm's real dir can never equal a
store entry's zod, so it throws. The message says 'run deno install', which is NOT sufficient while npm's real zod dir occupies
node_modules/zod — hence Paul's 'why am I STILL getting this'.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) Reproduce the broken state and confirm the fix: from a fresh clone, 'npm ci && deno install' (documented order in AGENTS.md:44)
    must build; and 'npm ci' run AFTER 'deno install' (which flattens node_modules) must be recoverable.
(2) Either make the build self-heal (re-run/repair the deno peer context or fall back to the npm-resolved SDK when it is the
    single zod peer) OR make the failure message name the EXACT remediation and ordering: remove node_modules, npm ci, THEN
    deno install LAST; note that re-running npm ci/install after deno install reintroduces the error, and that a stale
    node_modules/.deno store may need removing. Name the conflicting path and whether node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk
    exists / which zod it binds, so the next person is not guessing.
(3) Add a machine check or test that fails loudly when the layout is npm-flat (so this is caught in CI, not on Paul's Mac).
(4) Documentation: the requirement that deno install runs LAST must be explicit in AGENTS.md/README, not only implied.

EVIDENCE: Paul's transcript 2026-10-08; VM layout inspected (node_modules/zod -> .deno symlink). Related: chrome-agent-platform-63et
(why node_modules/.deno is load-bearing), bbz3s (stale .deno store), d0cbe614/3caea694 (layout-independence selection).

title: Stale .deno store survives a changed deno.lock: a developer build can still bundle the OLD fast-uri while both lockfiles say the new one
description: Follow-up from the lf9xe review (2026-10-08). The fix pins deno.lock to fast-uri@3.1.7 and that IS the authority for the shipped bytes, but deno.lock alone does NOT rewrite an existing .deno store: build.mjs:395-398 only auto-runs deno install when the SDK entry is MISSING, and the new security-dependency-drift gate (scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:276-283) is only reached on the STORE build path (build.mjs:770), not on a normal developer build. Consequence: on a checkout whose .deno still holds fast-uri@3.1.5, npm run build can bundle the OLD vulnerable copy while package-lock.json and deno.lock both declare 3.1.7 - and the merge gate (npm test -> the custody test) does NOT catch it, because that test compares the two LOCKFILES, not the resolved bundle. The merger verifies the built metafile for this landing, so the landing is safe; the hole is the next stale checkout. j5yz's assessment is that a one-line fix is not enough: merely checking for the presence of fast-uri@3.1.7 misses the case where AJV still resolves an old 3.1.5 symlink, and the current guard covers store builds but not DEBUG builds. DIRECTION: compare the LIVE AJV-RESOLVED fast-uri version/path against BOTH lockfiles before any build target, then auto-heal (run a frozen deno install) or FAIL CLOSED with a named error; add tests for the stale-store case and the mixed-version case. Owner: unassigned. Next action: pick up as its own bead after o75bp. Related: lf9xe (the pin), im9q8 (the lock-vs-shipped drift context).

title: Approval requests are still approvable when their bounded detail is absent - make the fail-closed decision live at the caller layer, not only the binder
description: Found by the verification review of the oagmf fix (2026-10-08, branch tip 6358ec97). The fix correctly rejects a content-script registration with more than 8 matches at the tool closures (browser-tools.js:2083 t12ScriptMatches, called before reaching Chrome) and independently at the service-worker approval route (service-worker.js:10263), so the nine-match attack is blocked. REMAINING GAP (P2, NOT a demonstrated bypass): when the detail binder returns undefined, extension/lib/owner-approval.js:812-836 still constructs an approvable request WITHOUT detail, and extension/shared/conversation.js:949-970 drops the invalid detail but retains the approval, so a generic card can still be approved. Today the upstream checks make that unreachable for the >8 case, which is why it is not exploitable - but the claim 'fail closed at every layer' is therefore not literally true, and if any future change relaxes the tool or route check, this fallback quietly becomes the bypass. ACTION: (a) make the approval request itself fail closed when a registration's bounded detail is absent or inconsistent, rather than falling back to a generic card; (b) test the CALLER (owner-approval / conversation normalisation), not only the binder, including the absent-detail and count-mismatch cases; (c) leave the existing tool and route checks in place - this is defence in depth, not a replacement. Owner: unassigned.

1. Caller-layer fail-closed in owner-approval.js (approvalCardDenial):
   - When action is in SCRIPT_REGISTRATION_APPROVAL_ACTIONS (or detail presents as script registration), if detail is absent, null, empty, has an invalid digest, has 0 matches, or exceeds/mismatches the 8-match cap, approvalCardDenial returns null immediately.
   - When approvalCardDenial returns null, the service-worker requireOwnerApproval caller rejects and cleans up the pending approval ({ ok: false, approvalDenied: true }), ensuring no generic fallback approval card can ever be published.
   - If an unrelated action presents script registration detail, approvalCardDenial returns null (fail-closed against forged/mismatched actions).

2. Caller-layer fail-closed in conversation.js (normalizePermissionRequirement):
   - In normalizePermissionRequirement, validates all approvals in req.approvals: any approval claiming a script registration action or detail MUST have matching action/detail and valid bounded detail from boundScriptRegistrationApprovalDetail, else normalizePermissionRequirement returns null.
   - approvalCardSpecFromRequest returns null when requirement normalization fails, completely preventing the creation of a generic card.

3. Testing:
   - Added caller-level test suite in tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts testing both approvalCardDenial and normalizePermissionRequirement across all 4 script registration actions (register/update user script, register/update content script) covering:
     • absent detail (undefined, null, {})
     • inconsistent detail (invalid digest, 0 matches)
     • count mismatch / overflow (>8 matches)
     • corrupted match arrays (non-string items)
     • foreign action mismatch (e.g. browser.close-foreign-tab with script detail)
     • valid detail (verifying correct detail preservation)
     • approvalCardSpecFromRequest returning null on invalid input.
   - All 92 tests in focused set pass (chrome-tools-t12 40/40, owner-approval-security 26/26, permission-approval-in-context 21/21, owner-approval-classification 1/1, security-doc-drift 4/4). Built clean with build:production.

title: security-doc-drift guard pins THREAT_MODEL citations to exact line numbers, so unrelated code landings force manual doc retargeting
description: Observed 2026-10-08 during the 3m3sn-fix union: the security-doc-drift guard landed with the docs-audit cluster (1998e731, bead 5x4iw) pins THREAT_MODEL.md citations to service-worker.js line numbers - e.g. chrome.runtime.onMessage.addListener at :12265 and the allowlist check 'near :12295'. That works and the guard did its job, but the design means EVERY code landing ahead of a cited line requires a manual doc retarget, and the failure mode is a red gate on a branch that never touched the doc. Options to consider: (a) keep line pins but make the guard's failure message print the new resolved line so the retarget is mechanical; (b) pin a stable ANCHOR instead of a line - e.g. assert the cited symbol/string still exists at or near the citation and derive the expected line from the code, so the doc can cite a symbol and the guard computes the line; (c) reduce the number of pinned lines to the smallest set that actually guards against drift. title: Pre-existing error swallowing in skill-resolve.js: fatal store read failures yield an empty skill set silently - decide whether to surface them
description: Found during the independent delta review of the 3m3sn fix (2026-10-08), and confirmed PRE-EXISTING on main, not introduced by that branch: extension/lib/skill-resolve.js swallows the failure of the stores it reads - 'await stores.getCustomSkills().catch(() => [])' (main line 47) and 'await stores.loadAllImported().catch(() => [])' (main line 52), plus a try/catch around file read at main line 62. Effect: a fatal store read failure (corrupt DB, permission error, quota) is indistinguishable from 'this skill does not exist' - the resolver quietly returns fewer skills and the agent runs WITHOUT a skill the user believes is installed. The 3m3sn branch added a memo wrapper around these calls (createMemoizedSkillStores) and removed top-level .catch(() => null) wrappers it had added, so it is a net improvement in propagation, but it does NOT close this: the deeper swallows are still on the path. QUESTION TO SETTLE (owner decision): when the skill store cannot be read, should the run (a) fail loudly with the store error, (b) continue but surface an owner-visible warning naming the skills that could not be loaded, or (c) stay silent as it is now? The current behaviour is (c) by accident rather than by decision, and there is NO test covering the failure path. Whatever is decided, add a test pinning it. Owner: unassigned.
close_reason: LANDED in 0d3e309c0 (0.3.602) per Paul's decision (a) fail loudly. Skill-store read failures now propagate (agent stops), the error names the store + cause/code, absence ([] resolves) stays non-fatal, and a test drives rejecting stores. Independent review PASS-WITH-NOTES; gate 5603/0 + build 3/3.

Default recommendation from coord if Paul has no preference: (b) — fail-open with a visible, named warning, because silently running the agent without a skill the user believes is installed is the actual harm; but do not implement before the call.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan (fleet:chrome-agent-platform)
comments.text:
2026-10-08 10:00Z - HUB FRAMING ON THIS DECISION, relayed to Paul who has it now.

The hub agrees that the silent option cannot stand, and the point worth adding is about option (b) specifically: a warning is only better than failing loudly IF THERE IS A SURFACE WHERE IT IS ACTUALLY SEEN. The finding is that the agent runs without a skill the user believes is installed - so a warning that lands somewhere nobody reads reproduces the original defect with extra steps, and the user still believes the skill is loaded. The question to settle alongside the choice is therefore: name the surface (extension UI, log the user inspects, status endpoint) and how it is noticed. If no such surface exists today, (a) is the right answer, because failing loudly is the only option that cannot mislead.

Two related notes so the decision does not get made in isolation:
1. A transient store fault is not the same failure as a persistent one. If you pick (b), consider naming whether the store is retried, and whether the warning clears when the store recovers - a warning that never clears trains the user to ignore the whole channel.
2. Whatever is chosen, the test should drive the FAILURE, not just the happy path: corrupt or permission-block the store in a fixture and assert the chosen behaviour observes it. A behaviour nobody has provoked in a test is a behaviour nobody has verified.

Recorded here as hub input; the decision is Paul's and the bead waits on him.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan (fleet:chrome-agent-platform)
comments.text:
2026-10-08 10:00Z - PAUL'S DECISION, verbatim: "fail when skill error." Option (a) confirmed - fail loudly with the store error. NOT (b) the visible warning, and NOT (c) silence. The hub relayed it as urgent because this bead was waiting on it and nothing was dispatched.

WHAT (a) REQUIRES:
- A fatal skill-store read failure (corrupt database, permission, quota) PROPAGATES instead of yielding an empty skill set, so the agent stops rather than running without a skill the user believes is installed.
- The surfaced error NAMES THE STORE AND THE CAUSE, not merely that skills failed to load. The point of failing loudly is diagnosability; an error that reports a failure without saying what or where reproduces the original defect in a louder costume.
- Do NOT collapse every store fault into a crash: a genuinely absent optional skill is a different event from a store that cannot be read. The finding was about UNREADABLE stores, and the fix must not convert a normal "no such skill" into a failure.

ACCEPTANCE CONDITION: the test must DRIVE THE FAILURE - corrupt or permission-block the store in a fixture and assert the behaviour observes it. A happy-path test verifies nothing about this change. This was already hub input on this bead; with the decision made, it is the condition on closing.

CONTEXT WORTH KEEPING: the coord's own recommendation was (b), the visible warning. The hub's added point was that (b) is only better than (a) if there is a surface where the warning is genuinely seen - a warning nobody reads is silence with extra steps. Paul chose fail-loud, which sidesteps that question entirely: it is the only option that cannot mislead, at the cost of stopping on a transient fault. If that cost becomes real (a store that flaps), the right follow-up is to make the store failure rarer or retried, NOT to weaken the failure visibility.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-coord
comments.text:
coord 2026-10-08 — PAUL DECISION (verbatim: 'fail when skill error'). OPTION (a): fail loudly with the store error. ACCEPTANCE (from Paul):
1. A fatal skill-store READ failure (corrupt DB, permission, quota) must PROPAGATE — the agent stops; it must NOT yield an empty/partial skill set that lets the run continue without a skill the user believes is installed.
2. The error must NAME THE STORE AND THE CAUSE (not just 'failed to load skills'); the next person must be able to act on it.

title: resolveSkillRefs serializes whole-store reads and is computed twice on the run-start path
description:
Source: nightly software-factory project-audit of origin/main@4e440af7 (2026-10-08, target chrome-agent-platform-factory).

resolveSkillRefs(task) (extension/background/service-worker.js:1042-1045) resolves each /skill:<id> ref one at a time in 'for (const id of ids)', and each resolveSkill(id) -> extension/lib/skill-resolve.js -> stores.loadAllImported() re-reads the FULL importedSkills index (plus legacy-row migration) and then readSkillFile for the body. K distinct refs pay K full index listings + K OPFS body reads, serialized. The same call is duplicated: line 4391 computes mergeRunSkills(agentSkills, await resolveSkillRefs(task)) and the journaled-skill branch recomputes await resolveSkillRefs(task) with the IDENTICAL task string (line 4398) — paid twice on the continuation/resume path the owner sees. Same serial pattern in resolveAgentSkills (line 1059) for up to 128 saved skill refs.

Next action (behaviour-preserving): (1) resolve ids concurrently in resolveSkillRefs with Promise.all (skillRefIds already dedupes; keep index order; keep per-id error tolerance by mapping resolveSkill(id).catch(()=>null)); (2) hoist the duplicate call at 4398 — resolve the task refs ONCE and reuse; (3) parallelize the journaled loop (journaledSkillIds capped at JOURNALED_SKILLS_CAP=24). Optional follow-up: memoize loadAllImported() per resolution so K refs share one index read. Acceptance: run-start makes one index read and no duplicate resolution, pinned by a test that counts loadAllImported invocations.

title: agent-composer suggestion listbox hand-rolls JS rect math instead of Popover API + CSS Anchor Positioning
description:
Source: nightly software-factory project-audit of origin/main@4e440af7 (2026-10-08, target chrome-agent-platform-factory).

<agent-composer> _showPopup() (extension/shared/components.js:8952-8991) measures .composer once with getBoundingClientRect() and writes absolute top/bottom/left/width/max-height inline styles, choosing flip direction via spaceBelow/spaceAbove. There is no scroll/resize listener, yet the composer ships in the thread view where .thread-body is the scroll container and <agent-composer> is position: sticky — so once the container scrolls or the window resizes, the listbox keeps open-time coordinates and detaches. The popup is position:absolute in a clipping context, not the top layer. The same file already positions the mic-device menu (:1357-1363), attach menu (:2020-2049) and diagnostics panel (:11560-11574) with anchor-name/position-anchor/position-area and exposes supportsAnchorPositioning(); only the composer palette still hand-rolls. The sibling <prompt-bar> popup (components.js:10136-10211, gallery-only) has the same hand-rolled .pop/.open pattern and should be fixed in the same change.

Next action: make the composer popup a popover=manual element tethered by CSS anchor positioning (anchor to .composer, position-area: block-end span-inline-end, position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, width: min(440px, anchor-size(width))), keep the combobox a11y contract (aria-expanded/controls/activedescendant, Escape/Tab) unchanged, and keep the existing getBoundingClientRect() branch ONLY as the supportsAnchorPositioning()===false fallback. Mirror on <prompt-bar>. Acceptance: listbox follows the anchor on scroll/resize without listeners, verified in a browser (1280px + narrow), and no selector churn for CDP journeys.

title: Model-authored user-script/content-script registration installs JS with no owner-visible digest approval
description:
Source: nightly software-factory project-audit of origin/main@4e440af7 (2026-10-08, target chrome-agent-platform-factory).

The model-callable tools register_user_script / update_user_script / register_content_script / update_content_script accept a caller-supplied js string up to 32 KiB and install it via chrome.userScripts.register (extension/lib/browser-tools.js:6345) and chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts (:6484), persisting across sessions. The grant path withScriptRegistrationGrant (:2128-2177) checks the userScripts/scripting permission, exact-origin host permission, browser-control grant (t12OriginsCovered), and run ownership — but there is NO approval bound to the bytes installed: the owner never sees a digest of the js being registered. INV-8's digest discipline already exists for other destructive actions; this surface lacks it. THREAT_MODEL.md has no S14/T19 invariant for it.

Note: prior bead chrome-agent-platform-jbsi (closed) named this same gap; the digest approval is verified still absent at HEAD.

Next action: declare the invariant in THREAT_MODEL.md (S14/T19) and add a falsification test that a registration under a model principal cannot persist without an approval bound to the script digest (and that the registered body is not silently truncated). Acceptance: registering a user/content script requires an owner-visible digest approval, and deleting the digest gate reddens a test.
close_reason: Closed

title: webmcp.diagnostics.get page route returns a global owner setting, not scoped to caller origin
description:
Source: nightly software-factory project-audit of origin/main@4e440af7 (2026-10-08, target chrome-agent-platform-factory).

webmcp.diagnostics.get is one of the eight PAGE_ALLOWED_ROUTES entries (extension/lib/pure.js:1287) and its handler takes no arguments and reads a single global preference: 'async webmcp.diagnostics.get() { return { enabled: await webmcpDiagnosticsEnabled() }; }' (extension/background/service-worker.js:9689-9691). Every other page-reachable route is origin-scoped by construction, but this one has no origin parameter, so any http(s) page on which the content script is injected (all_urls) can learn whether the owner globally enabled WebMCP diagnostics — a cross-origin state disclosure and a fingerprinting bit. LOW impact on its own, but it is the one entry in an otherwise route-by-route-defended allowlist whose state is global.

Next action: either drop webmcp.diagnostics.get from PAGE_ALLOWED_ROUTES (the isolated-world relay already receives what it needs via enrollment/bootstrap) or make the returned value origin-scoped and pin that the handler refuses a caller-supplied origin. Extend the sender-contract test that fixes PAGE_ALLOWED_ROUTES membership to assert the SEMANTICS of each entry, not just presence. Acceptance: no page can read a global owner preference through a page-reachable route, verified by a falsification test.

title: README.md:80 falsely states user-uploaded Wasm is 'storage only' while shipped code executes it
description:
Source: nightly software-factory project-audit of origin/main@4e440af7 (2026-10-08, target chrome-agent-platform-factory).

README.md:76-81 ('Your WebAssembly files') states uploads are 'storage only: uploads are not run or registered as callable tools.' That is false as shipped: extension/lib/tool-catalog.js:35-42 lists 'user-wasm' in TOOL_SOURCE_KINDS, adaptUserWasmTools projects owner store rows into descriptors, extension/offscreen/offscreen.js:64-66 registers registerUserWasmHost(), whose listener (extension/lib/user-wasm-host.js:43-72) executes cap:user-wasm-run in a fresh worker. The README's own link target contradicts it: docs/USER-WASM-STORAGE.md:4-6 says modules are 'adapted into the catalog ... and execute through wasm-execution-worker.js under a 15-second deadline and per-agent digest allowlists'.

Reconciliation bead 9zw7.3 fixed USER-WASM-STORAGE.md + tool-platform-architecture.md but missed README.md. Security consequence is reviewer-facing: a reader reasoning from the README concludes owner-uploaded Wasm is inert when it is an admitted execution lane.

Next action: rewrite README.md:76-81 to match USER-WASM-STORAGE.md:4-6 (uploads stored unvalidated; once allowlisted for an agent they execute via wasm-execution-worker.js as a user-wasm tool source), and add README.md to the docs drift-guard file set for the user-Wasm capability statement. Acceptance: README.md no longer claims storage-only and the capability statement is covered by a drift guard.

title: THREAT_MODEL.md and RISK-REGISTER.md omit/undercount the offscreen code-execution lanes
description:
Source: nightly software-factory project-audit of origin/main@4e440af7 (2026-10-08, target chrome-agent-platform-factory).

The threat model and risk register no longer describe the offscreen document's real code-execution surface. extension/offscreen/offscreen.js registers eleven-plus hosts (registerEmscriptenHost :53, registerWasmJobHost :58, registerUserWasmHost :66, registerSvgRasteriseHost :71, registerOnDeviceTextHost :76, plus ACP-model, agent-worker, python, wasm-stream, callexport, table-worker, clipboard) but:
- THREAT_MODEL.md names only one Wasm row (S6 'Python worker and Wasm modules' -> wasm-executor.js/python-network.js); the strings emscripten, user-wasm, wasi, rasterise, on-device-text, S14, T18, T19, INV-15 do not appear. Grep confirms none of these tokens are present in THREAT_MODEL.md.
- docs/RISK-REGISTER.md R12 (:96) and THREAT_MODEL.md:49 still state the document 'multiplexes five independent subsystems', understating the single-point-of-failure blast radius by more than half.

The lanes are defensively built (SW-only sender predicate extension/lib/pure.js:959-966; per-asset SHA-256/size re-verification + exact-key envelope rejection extension/lib/emscripten-host.js:1-33) and docs/SW-DISPATCH-AUTHORITY-CENSUS.md 6.2 does enumerate them — so this is a modelling gap, not a code defect. But THREAT_MODEL.md is the doc AGENTS.md tells every auditor to read FIRST; an auditor trusting it under-reports the attack surface and would not check the envelope exact-key checks or a new host added without isTrustedServiceWorkerSender.

Next action: fold the census 6.2 inventory into THREAT_MODEL.md — add component-map rows and surface rows (S6b/S6c/S6d) for user-Wasm, admitted-Emscripten, WASI-job, SVG-rasterise and on-device-text; a threat (T18) for envelope forgery/confusion; an invariant (INV-15) that every offscreen execution host accepts jobs only from the service worker; and note that manifest 'wasm-unsafe-eval' makes INV-4 not read as 'no code execution'. Re-measure R12's subsystem list from the register*Host() calls and add the reclaim-interrupts-every-lane blast-radius line. Acceptance: THREAT_MODEL.md + RISK-REGISTER.md name every host in offscreen.js and a cheap guard fails when a new register*Host() appears without the register entry being revisited.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
qazo — IMPLEMENTATION & REVIEW COMPLETE on fleet/qazo-9ud9e @ 07a5bd16.

Mechanism & Changes:
1. Frontier check tracking: Added continuous lastCompletedCheck and lastStartedCheck tracking in check() / updateFrontier(name). Before assertions run, lastStartedCheck starts on EXPECTED[0]. Each completed check updates lastCompletedCheck and advances lastStartedCheck to the next check in EXPECTED.
2. Abnormal exit summary (printAbnormalExitSummary): On any throw, unhandled rejection, uncaught error event, watchdog hang, or silent premature exit where missing downstream checks remain, prints a prominent boxed diagnostic banner naming:
   - reason (error message, protocol failure, or unhandled rejection)
   - last completed check
   - active frontier check (where execution halted)
   - unreached checks count
   - raw error stack/details without masking the original failure.
3. Snapshotted frontier before meta-assertions: Snapshot { lastCompletedCheck, lastStartedCheck } at the start of finally so the final meta-checks (FINAL_CHECK and order check) never overwrite the reported frontier.
4. Robust early-stop distinction: Added JourneyEarlyStopError sentinel class and isIntentionalEarlyStop() exact matching so only genuine matching stop targets exit cleanly; crashes prior to the stop target or substring matches proceed to full abnormal exit diagnosis.
5. Startup boundary: Extended main() try-block around fixture server startup and profile creation (homeCacheProfile now throws on invalid HOME instead of exiting unmonitored), guaranteeing early startup aborts report EXPECTED[0] as the frontier.
6. Bounded per-check watchdog: Arms a 90s unref timer (configurable via CAP_JOURNEY_WATCHDOG_MS) reset on every assertion to distinguish hangs from exits (exiting 124 with in-flight frontier).
7. Zero noise on passing runs: Normal PASS runs only output standard check passes and summary.

title: acp-service status can misreport the installed auth mode: launchd ProgramArguments parsing admits XML comment contamination
description:
Found by the third adversarial security review of the loopback opt-out (gpt-6-sol), 2026-10-07. NOT a security defect in the bridge - the bind and auth guards are correct - it is a STATUS-REPORT accuracy bug.

scripts/acp-service.mjs readInstalledServiceUnit extracts the raw <array> text and searches it for <string>--allow-anonymous-loopback</string> (:273-277). A valid XML comment INSIDE that array containing the flag (e.g. <!-- <string>--allow-anonymous-loopback</string> -->) is ignored by launchd but makes status report an authenticated installation as ANONYMOUS (:307-310). Conversely an XML-encoded flag string can be interpreted by the plist parser without matching that regex. The existing negative fixture places its comment OUTSIDE the array, so it covers neither case (tests/acp-loopback-optout.test.ts:410-441). The systemd side is already correct: inspection is restricted to the ExecStart line (:285-294).

FIX: parse the plist actual ProgramArguments STRING VALUES (excluding XML comments, decoding entities) and derive isAnonymous from those parsed values only; add an in-array negative fixture that must report token-required. Keep the systemd behaviour as is. Report the installed mode truthfully; if parsing cannot be made reliable, label the line as an assumption rather than claiming the installed mode.

title: waitForServiceWorker: the first Target.getTargets can wait out the whole 30 s per-call budget under the parallel phase (g09i-sidebar-tab, sandbox-egress-confinement red with 'Target.getTargets: deadline')
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing gate, 2026-10-07, macOS arm64, 14 cores, Chrome for Testing 149)

Two real-browser tests went red in full parallel-phase runs of the jjsz landing candidate `e2fa9a97` with the SAME error:

- `tests/g09i-sidebar-tab.test.ts` (in `npm test`)
- `tests/sandbox-egress-confinement.test.ts` (in `npm test`, and again in a scratch parallel-phase run of the same tree)

```
error: Error: Target.getTargets: deadline
    at scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:902     (the `send` wrapper built by the CDP connector)
    at async waitForServiceWorker (scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:968)
```

`sandbox-egress-confinement` reported `FAILED (31s)`: the wall is the 30 s default per-call budget (`opts.timeoutMs ?? 30000`, `withTimeout` at chrome-launch.ts ~1051). The failing call is the FIRST CDP call after the browser printed its DevTools endpoint, so the time was not spent in `waitForServiceWorker`'s own 250 ms retry loop (its separate 15 s deadline is never consulted): one `Target.getTargets` got no answer for 30 s, `send` threw, and nothing catches it. The same gate also failed `ntp-boot-staging` (one long task of 55-72 ms against a 50 ms ceiling) and `site-agent-delegation-attachments` ("CDP Runtime.evaluate timed out"); those two are `chrome-agent-platform-mujlt` and `chrome-agent-platform-tf48c`.

## What is and is not known

- The tests pass in isolation: 5 of 5 runs each of `ntp-boot-staging`, `site-agent-delegation-attachments`, `g09i-sidebar-tab` and `sandbox-egress-confinement` on the same tree (evidence bundle `red-gate-ab/`, `iso-reruns.sh`), at a host load of 5 to 13.
- The production delta between the last green gate (`177b3e1e`) and the red one contains no extension code (`extension/dist` is byte-identical apart from the marker) and no change to `scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts` or `scripts/lib/process-tree.ts`.
- An interleaved A/B of the parallel phase alone (three pairs, `177b3e1e` then `e2fa9a97` each time, 8 s apart; the order confound is stated in `docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md`) gave one real-browser red per side (`bgagent-delete` on the older tree, `ntp-boot-staging` on the newer) and no `Target.getTargets: deadline` at all in six runs. So the signature has been seen three times in two runs of the candidate tree (two in `npm test`, one in a scratch parallel-phase run) and never in the six A/B runs: its rate is NOT measured, and no mechanism is proven.
- A 30 s silence from a Chrome that has just accepted the WebSocket is not ordinary slowness. Candidate mechanisms (all unverified): the browser main thread starved while up to 14 browsers boot at once on 14 cores; a browser that is alive but stuck during start-up; a reply that never arrives on a connection that stays open. Nothing distinguishes them yet, because the failure prints neither the host load nor the number of Chrome processes alive at that moment. (A launch-lock wait is not a candidate: it happens inside `launchChrome`, before this call.)

## Why this needs its own bead

`docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md` section 2 names three environmental signatures; this is not one of them, so by the playbook it is a PRODUCT RED until someone proves a mechanism or the rule is amended (`chrome-agent-platform-m9g43`). A merge host then has two bad options: re-run until green (which hides it) or stall the queue.

## Acceptance

1. A failure of this kind prints, at failure time, the host load average and the count of Chrome-for-Testing processes alive (reuse `measureEvaluateTimeout` / `classifyEvaluateTimeout` in `scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts`), so the next occurrence is evidence rather than an anecdote.
2. `waitForServiceWorker` has a stated policy for a per-call timeout (retry until its own deadline, or fail with a message that names the budget and the load), pinned by a test that feeds it a `send` that stalls once. Do not just widen 30 s: say what the number is for.
3. The flake rate of the four named tests under the real parallel phase is measured on the same host, randomised order and load-gated starts, before and after whatever is changed.
4. If the answer is placement (the load-sensitive real-browser tests belong in the serial phase, or the parallel phase needs a browser-concurrency cap), that is a partition decision for the owner: record the numbers here and do not move it silently.

Must NOT change: no test is weakened or skipped to make a gate pass; `ntp-boot-staging`'s zero-long-tasks assertion stays as it is until the measurement says what a correct ceiling is.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
Implementation and verification complete on fleet/qazo-3nurz @ e99b5ea70:
- Stated per-call timeout policy in waitForServiceWorker: bounded by callTimeoutMs (default Math.min(5000, totalTimeoutMs), bounded by remaining overall budget).
- Transient stall recovery: transient Target.getTargets timeouts/stalls are caught and retried across polling attempts instead of aborting immediately or burning the 30s connection budget on call 1. Added .catch(() => {}) handler to avoid unhandled promise rejections on late completions.
- Terminal transport failures (e.g. cdp websocket closed) and non-timeout protocol errors fail fast immediately without retrying or misclassifying.
- Classified deadline timeout: when all attempts stall and exhaust the overall deadline, samples host load via measureEvaluateTimeout / classifyEvaluateTimeout and counts live Chrome-for-Testing processes via countLiveChromeProcesses(), logging evidence and throwing ServiceWorkerTargetTimeoutError ([loaded] vs [idle-never-settled]).

qs8v7 follow-up evidence for this test's failure class, from the union gate on tree e247af8f (~/.fleet/checks/e247af8fb64167eef2b628cceb8a8a825c67edd2.log).

WHAT HAPPENED: the run reported "712 files total, 0 skipped" and ONE failed test - this one ("3nurz: waitForServiceWorker returns null when Chrome is responsive but worker never registers"), under a genuinely loaded box. Its own output names the condition: "[waitForServiceWorker] Target.getTargets: deadline exceeded (120ms total budget, 30ms per-call budget, 3 attempts, 3 timed out) under loaded: live-chrome=7 load1=12.50 load5=8.20". The verdict layer then read it as product: "run-tests: parallel phase contains non-environmental failure(s) - preserving PRODUCT RED (exit 1)", so a full union gate (320s) burned and a good delta looked broken.

WHY IT IS ENVIRONMENTAL AND WHY THE RULE DID NOT CATCH IT: the m9g43 rule needs a named concurrent heavy job with overlap. The box had one (a Rust build; the quiet-window sampler saw it as "rustc"), and the failure carries the load numbers, but nothing connects the two: this test does not go through the quiet window, and the machine sample that the governor takes is not attached to the failure's classification. So the failure is classified from its own exception text alone, and a CDP deadline under a named load condition has no path to the ENVIRONMENT verdict.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT (design, not this bead): thread the run's machine sample into the real-browser failure classification, so a CDP-deadline class failure whose own log names load and a live heavy builder can be reported as an environmental refusal (exit 75 with the marker) instead of a product red - with the isolated-pass requirement kept. comments.text:
STATUS: IN_REVIEW on fleet/qazo-d9lv0 at commit 3725dcb2.

Root Cause & Mechanism:
1. Investigation:
   - Observed failure in union gate: tests/composer-command-disclosure.test.ts:143 "the built extension shows the command-insertion disclosure in the picker" (Actual "no [data-composer-input]" vs Expected null).
   - In tests/composer-command-disclosure.test.ts, after attaching to the newly created NTP target, the test relied on a fixed blind delay `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000))` before executing the in-page check.
   - Under heavy parallel machine load (union gate running 8 test suites across 2 vCPUs), 2000ms was insufficient for the custom element `<agent-composer id="composer">` to finish mounting and rendering its inner DOM (`[data-composer-input]`). When querySelector executed once with zero polling, `ta` was null, causing an immediate abort with `{ error: "no [data-composer-input]" }`.
   - Additionally, `ev()` had no retry loop for "Cannot find default execution context", which can race during document navigation/attach.
2. Fix:
   - In `ev()`, added a bounded retry loop (up to 10 attempts with 200ms backoff) on `Cannot find default execution context` errors.
   - Added bounded poll (up to 15s) for `document.readyState === "complete" && !!document.getElementById("composer")`.
   - Inside the page evaluation: replaced instantaneous query with bounded retry (up to 10s at 50ms intervals) for `#composer` and `[data-composer-input]`.
   - Replaced fixed 1500ms sleep after typing `/tabs` with active bounded polling (up to 10s at 50ms intervals) until the suggestion popup opens and populates with items and disclosure note.
   - Preserved fail-closed reporting with explicit error objects if deadlines expire.
   - Zero product changes, zero version/CHANGELOG changes.
3. Verification:
   - Ran tests/composer-command-disclosure.test.ts 5 times sequentially under Chrome for Testing: 5/5 passed (1s each, exit 0).

title: MERGER-PLAYBOOK section 2 has no honest rule for a load-induced red that matches none of the three named signatures
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing, 2026-10-07)

Two real-browser tests went red in ONE full parallel run on a commit whose diff provably cannot affect them
(`select-tests --list` selects neither, the diff is a 19-line unrelated test). Mechanism evidence: the
delegation KAT's `CDP Runtime.evaluate timed out` reproduces under controlled CPU starvation (see the sibling
beads); the ntp-boot-staging long task did not reproduce in 23 further navigations (one unexplained 6 ms
overshoot of a 50 ms wall-clock threshold).

docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md section 2 names exactly three environmental signatures (fnmr futex hang, m3a2 env race,
4vfj stale selector) and says a failure that does not match one with its isolation discriminator proven is a
PRODUCT RED and the branch must not land. That leaves a merge host no honest way to land past a DEMONSTRATED load
flake. The pressure then goes the wrong way: re-run until green (which hides the flake) or stall the queue.

## Proposal

Add a fourth classification, "load-induced timeout", that REQUIRES (1) a measured load reading at failure time
(the existing `measureEvaluateTimeout` / `classifyEvaluateTimeout` machinery in scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts),
(2) an isolation re-run of the same test on the same commit passing N/N, (3) the merger recording both in the
landing bead; a repeat on the same test within M landings reopens it as a product red.

## Acceptance

docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md section 2 amended; a script emits the classification from a measured reading (so it is
evidence, not an attestation); a test pins that a failure WITHOUT a loaded reading is still a product red.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing record, 2026-10-08. MERGER-PLAYBOOK section 2 ("only three named environmental signatures; everything else is a PRODUCT RED") gave this landing no honest way to handle two things it met on one macOS arm64 host. Evidence: the landing evidence bundle (cap-evidence/jjsz-landing: red-gate-ab/README.md, red-gate-ab/display-state/README.md, gates/*), and docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md (the red-gate paragraph).

1. A HOST-STATE red with a measured mechanism and a discriminator, which the rule has no row for: with the macOS display asleep, Page.captureScreenshot returns nothing in headless=new Chrome for Testing, so every test that asserts on a screenshot goes red (tests/g09i-sidebar-tab.test.ts:54, tests/w51r-create-click.test.ts:91; 12 s each). Discriminator: the same two tests alone, same tree, same host: displays asleep 6 of 6 FAIL (12 to 15 s); displays held awake (`caffeinate -d -i -u`, console still locked) 6 of 6 PASS (3 to 4 s); the pmset log shows the display turned off 37 s after the first red full run started. Two full runs were red on exactly these two tests and nothing else. See chrome-agent-platform-jkeuo. A control run on the same tree with the display held awake (`caffeinate -d -i -u`): `npm test` GREEN (6000 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored), `test:build` GREEN, `test:changed` red on the ntp test alone (51 ms) and green on both screenshot tests. Recommended amendment: a fourth kind of signature, "host-state red", with this as its first row, whose discriminator is the A/B above; and a line in the landing checklist that on macOS the gate runs under `caffeinate -d -i` (or the runner holds the assertion itself).

2. A load-dependent real-browser FAMILY whose cause is not shown: ntp-boot-staging (a main-thread task of 51 to 72 ms against a 50 ms ceiling), Target.getTargets / Runtime.evaluate per-call budgets (12 to 31 s), screenshot budgets. It appeared on every lane tree measured, in 6 of 18 phases that ran ntp on the later lane trees (e2fa9a97, 130524a9, 2247514c) against 1 of 7 on the earlier ones (177b3e1e, 86528c3f) (Fisher two-sided p about 0.63; not randomised, not load-matched, and there is NO clean-main control on this host: every compared tree already carried the lane's speed-ups). An isolated rerun passes 20 of 20; a CPU-starvation repro (14 and 28 busy loops, load to 205) reproduced the delegation timeout in 2 of 6 and never the ntp task (0 of 6), so "load" is not shown to be the mechanism of the ntp red. The playbook gives the rule nothing to say here, so the choice is "land past it silently" or "never land". Recommended amendment: (a) the landing record must carry the start-of-phase load1 of every red phase (the landing gate script now records uptime at the start and end of every step), (b) a failing real-browser test must be re-run in isolation N of N green AND a green full run on the exact landing tree must exist before landing, with every attempt disclosed, or (c) an owner-recorded waiver naming the tests; never a classification by mood or by load alone. (d) A fix for the family itself is tracked in chrome-agent-platform-mujlt (ntp attribution), chrome-agent-platform-tf48c (the delegation KAT does not use classifyEvaluateTimeout the way chrome-journeys.ts does) and chrome-agent-platform-3nurz (the Target.getTargets deadline).

title: site-agent-delegation-attachments KAT: fixed 10 s CDP evaluate budget with no load classification; fails reproducibly under CPU starvation
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing gate, commit 86528c3f)

`tests/site-agent-delegation-attachments.test.ts` -> `scripts/kat-site-delegation-attachments.ts:43` failed in a
full parallel run with "CDP Runtime.evaluate timed out" (a fixed 10 s per-command budget), 12 s total, with NOTHING
failing before it. It passed on 177b3e1e (4 s) and 5/5 in isolation on the tip (2-3 s).

## Mechanism (reproduced; evidence: /Users/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/jjsz-landing/flake/)

Controlled CPU starvation with self-bounded hogs on the tip:
- 28 hogs: ok, durations 7 s / 4 s / 2 s (it grows with load);
- 14 hogs (load average >= 176): run 1 ok, runs 2 AND 3 FAILED at 12 s with the identical
  `CDP Runtime.evaluate timed out` signature.
So the signature is reproducibly load-induced, not a product regression.

## The gap

The repo already has the sanctioned classifier: beads 9t1p/qk7p built `measureEvaluateTimeout` /
`classifyEvaluateTimeout` / `evaluateTimeoutReport` in `scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts` (a MEASURED load reading:
loaded -> environmental, exit 75; idle -> "idle-never-settled" = PRODUCT RED, the known cause being an unanswered
service-worker `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` round trip). `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` uses it. This KAT does not:
it has a fixed 10 s budget and a bare throw. History: 3ui7 and xch2 (both closed) show this KAT stalling and
reddening the parallel phase before.

## Do

Route the KAT's evaluate path through `classifyEvaluateTimeout` (or scale the budget from a measured pre-flight).

## Acceptance

A mutant that makes the page never answer (idle) is still a PRODUCT RED; a timeout measured under load is
reported as environmental with the reading, never as a silent pass; the KAT's passing path is unchanged.
