b562566b adds a raw `console.warn(...)` at extension/background/routes/enclave-proxy.js:247. The repo's rule ("no raw console.* calls in the shipped extension tree", tests/code-health.test.ts:299; the constitution's logging rule) FAILS, and the failure names exactly:
  -     "background/routes/enclave-proxy.js:247"
Evidence: `npm run test:file -- tests/code-health.test.ts` at b562566b → 1 failed / 4 passed. CONTROL at the primary checkout (4d3a86ec, which does NOT contain this commit), same command, same machine: code-health PASSES (35 passed / 6 failed in the batch below), and the other six reds (machine-path-honesty, durable-root, task-view-simplify, first-run-onboarding-composition, harness-registry ×2) fail THERE TOO — so those six are the pre-existing i76t set, and code-health is the SEVENTH, introduced by this commit. The gate note in the bead comment ("six pre-existing ... none touching this diff") was written before b562566b and is not true for it.
FIX (one line): log through the shipped logger — `import { capLog } from "../../lib/cap-log.js"; const log = capLog("enclave-proxy");` (the pattern extension/background/routes/agent-worker.js:18,64 already uses) and call log.warn with the same scrubbed detail. The scrub()-before-logging in this diff is right and should stay.

=== MEDIUM 2 — a successful Remove reports "Remove failed: unknown" in the danger colour ===
Driven in the panel: add REVIEW_REMOVE_KEY, click Remove → the row disappears (the delete LANDS) and the status line reads exactly `Remove failed: unknown`, styled `var(--danger,#b3261e)`. Cause: extension/lib/secret-vault.js:237 returns `{ keyId, deleted: true }` — no `ok` field — while the panel branches on `res?.ok` (extension/options/options.js:3494). `res.ok` is undefined → falsy → the failure line, with `res?.error` also undefined → "unknown".
WHY THE SUITE IS GREEN: tests/secret-vault.test.ts:274 asserts only that the row is gone, never the status line.
FIX: assert the route's success flag consistently (return `{ ok: true, keyId, deleted: true }` from the route, or branch the panel on `res?.deleted`), and add a test that the Remove status line reports success. (This is a user-visible falsehood on the exact surface this stage ships: a person retries a delete that already happened.)

=== MEDIUM 3 — the strict settings-safe code contract is bypassed by the THROWN refusals ===
The commit's claim is "{ok,status,code} only — NO error text, NO URL, NO raw envelope reaches the Settings DOM". Verified TRUE for the returned refusals (a real service rejection returns exactly {ok,status,code}; the panel line for a custom key reads `Connection failed (connection_failed).`; the raw secret never appears in html, text or ANY attribute — canary-driven). But the PRE-I/O refusals are `throw`s tagged with `e.code` (unknown_service, bad_method, target_refused, origin_not_approved, template_error, and substituteTemplates' nesting/missing-value throws in enclave-proxy.js), and service-worker.js:6491 wires `testConnection` straight to the raw proxy handler with no try/catch — so vault.js's whitelist is NEVER REACHED for them. The refusal arrives at the Settings page as a full classified envelope with TEXT:
  chrome.runtime.sendMessage({type:"vault.test", service:"no-such-service"}) →
  {ok:false, error:"vault.test: enclave proxy: unknown service \"no-such-service\" — A tool call failed…", errorCategory:"tool-failure", errorReason:"vault.test: enclave proxy: unknown service …", errorAction:"…", errorDetail:"tool: vault.test"}
Two consequences: (a) the stated guarantee is unimplemented for that family — and members of it embed a URL/origin in their message text (origin_not_approved names the resolved origin; target_refused embeds checkFetchTarget's error), so any future caller that renders the envelope's `error` leaks it. The panel's *sibling* lines DO render `res?.error` (options.js:3482 rotate, :3494 remove, :3555 save), which I demonstrated receiving an envelope's text for vault.set/vault.rotate (value-free today: the vault's messages echo a key id, never a value). (b) The whitelist is partly theatre: `auth_failed`, `timeout`, `secret_unavailable` are produced NOWHERE in the extension (grep: 0), `not_wired` only by vault.js, and the 5 thrown codes never arrive as returned codes. A REAL rejected Brave token (canary key, live request) reported `code=redirect_refused status=null` — never `auth_failed` — so "Test connection ... verify token validity" cannot say "your key was rejected".
FIX (small): map the thrown refusals to `{ok:false, code}` at the proxy boundary (or catch `e.code` in the vault route's testConnection wrapper) so the whitelist is the only path to the caller; make a 401/403 map to `auth_failed`; add a test that EVERY refusal path returns a code and no message text.
NOT REACHABLE TODAY, stated honestly: the URL-bearing refusals are not reachable from the shipped panel (it only tests the fixed brave-search or an unknown custom id), so no live URL leak exists — the mechanism is what fails the contract.

=== VERIFIED PASS (independent, driven) ===
• Browser, loaded extension, options.html#web-services: the panel is the active section, the nav item is current and reads "Web services", the renderer ran (not a static shell).
• SECRET-DOM CHECK (scope 2): a canary key added through the form never appears in documentElement.outerHTML, body.innerText, or ANY element attribute; the only form on screen is the tail mask (`…9876`); the value field is cleared after save; vault.status returns masked fields only (no value field, no canary).
• Password semantics: row input type=password with placeholder "leave blank to keep"; Show/Hide flips type and label both ways; a blank row input DISABLES the action and clicking it rotates nothing (the stored key is kept); the add form has its own working Show/Hide.
• Per-row controls: Show, Rotate, Remove, Test connection all present and driven; owner gating proven the other way — a NON-Settings page (ntp.html) is refused vault.status and receives no rows.
• Test connection UI: the status line is a whitelisted code, no text, no URL, no canary ("Connection failed (connection_failed)." for a custom key).
• Census couplings (scope 3): SETTINGS_SECTIONS and OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES both carry web-services (extension/lib/pure.js:841,884); options.html has the nav item (:126) and the section (:496); options.js ensureSectionRendered has the web-services branch (:4071); the i18n catalogue carries options_web_services in extension/_locales/en/messages.json:336 and extension/shared/i18n.js:135; the 16-section census assertions in tests/options-lazy-sections-9epn9.test.ts:66,77 are green.
• Suites: secret-vault 14 + enclave-proxy 8 = 22 pass; options-lazy-sections + settings-ia-716s4 + settings-section-navigation + owner-approval-security = 47 pass; npm run test:changed → 4997 passed / 7 failed, of which SIX are the pre-existing main-level set (control above).
• Build/budget (scope 4): npm run build:production OK; extension/dist/background/service-worker.js = 2,551,122 bytes against the 3,000,000 store budget (headroom 448,878) — under. (The bead's number, 2,550,751, differs by 371 bytes; both under, so I did not chase it.)

=== LIMITS OF THIS REVIEW ===
• Not driven: a non-English locale rendering of options_web_services; the Row's Remove flow after a page reload (state persistence across reload was not in scope).
• The 8/8 author evidence in ~/cap-evidence/jao15-panel was captured BEFORE b562566b: its test-connection line shows the OLD text ("Connection failed: enclave proxy: brave-search redirected — …"), i.e. it does not evidence the commit under review. My run re-drives that path at b562566b.
• Minor design observation, not a finding: the Add-form grid wraps loosely at 780px (the "API key" label sits beside a wide Key id field) and the row's four controls wrap 2+2; functional, mildly untidy.

VERDICT: NOT CLEARED. Three fixes (each ~one line: capLog; delete's ok flag/panel branch; thrown-refusal mapping + auth_failed), then a re-review that re-runs this driver and code-health. Bead stays in_progress; do not close or land b562566b as-is.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
LIVE TOOL WIRING REVIEW (branch jao1.6-enclave-ledger, commits 026a1f66 + ef531d47 + 2f63b051) — NOT CLEARED. Two findings (one HIGH boundary break, one MEDIUM gate), plus a large body of verified PASS. Reviewer: deepseek-flash (independent; author cap-glm-flash). Reviewed at HEAD 2f63b051 in a fresh worktree (npm ci + deno install + build:production; dist.complete binds 2f63b051, target store).

== FINDING 1 (HIGH) — scoped (hook) runs now receive brave_search, breaking the untrusted-event boundary ==
service-worker.js:2854 (added by these commits) computes the synthesized tools UNCONDITIONALLY:
    const enclaveTools = await enclaveServiceToolsForRun();
and :2893 spreads them into extraTools for EVERY run. Every neighbouring tool family in this same function is explicitly gated against scoped runs:
  • :2781 `browserToolset(scoped, …)` — scoped runs get the read-only browser set;
  • :2803 `liveManagementTools = scoped ? {} : managementToolset({…})`;
  • :2892 `workflowRunRoute: scoped ? null : …`;
  • MCP mount `if (approvalExecutionId && !scoped)`;
  • provider-server records `(providerServer && !scoped)` under the comment at :2367-2369: "SCOPED (hook) runs are driven by UNTRUSTED browser events — a paid provider-side tool must never be latchable from one".
Hook runs ARE scoped runs (:11934-11937 creates them with `scoped: true` and a task that says "The following is UNTRUSTED event data"). So a hook run can now send model-authored query text to https://api.search.brave.com through the proxy — a data-egress channel and quota spend from runs the file forbids exactly that for. brave_search is the only tool family in this function without a `scoped` clause.
FIX (one clause + one test): `const enclaveTools = scoped ? {} : await enclaveServiceToolsForRun();`, and a test asserting a scoped run's toolset contains no brave_search. This does not weaken the acceptance: agent.run (the owner-driven run) is not scoped.

== FINDING 2 (MEDIUM) — the "configured" half of the gate is INERT, and enclave.status disagrees with behaviour ==
The wiring passes `secretGate: (svc) => Boolean(svc.auth?.secretId)` (`:6534`) to synthesizeServiceTools, whose signature is `{ descriptors, proxyCall, vault }` — the key is silently ignored, so the gate does nothing and the comment above it ("A service without a configured key … is not offered") is false.
PROVED out-of-band (probe: ~/cap-evidence/jao15-wiring-review-deepseek/jao15-wiring-probe.ts, composing the SW's EXACT option object): with an EMPTY vault the toolset is `["brave_search"]`; with `secretGate: () => false` it is STILL `["brave_search"]`.
CONSEQUENCES: (a) the review scope's requirement "offered to agent.run on every turn when enabled + configured" is unmet — only "enabled" is honoured; (b) a run with no key gets a tool that can only fail, and it fails unhelpfully: buildRequest omits the auth header when the vault read is empty, the 401 returns as `{ok:false,status:401,body}`, and the tool throws "brave_search failed" AFTER a real network round trip; (c) `enclave.status` computes `exposed: enabled && configured` (`:6545`) — so the Settings surface reports exposed:false for an unconfigured service while the run is actually offered the tool. Status and behaviour disagree, which is the class this repo treats as a defect.
FIX: gate on the CONFIGURED set (filter descriptors in enclaveServiceToolsForRun() by the same masked projection enclaveStatusForSettings() already reads, or implement the option in synthesizeServiceTools), and derive `exposed` from that same function so the two cannot drift.

== FINDING 3 (LOW, process) — the slice ships with zero tests ==
The three commits touch only service-worker.js, options.html/js, check-reachability.mjs and .beads/issues.jsonl — no test file. Nothing in tests/ references extraTools, enclave.status, cap:enclave-enabled, or the toggle id. The existing tests/service-tools.test.ts composition (vault → enclave-proxy → synthesized tools) is the natural home; ONE assertion (empty vault ⇒ brave_search ABSENT) would have caught finding 2, and a scoped-run toolset assertion would catch finding 1. Also for the record: the first commit put `const enclaveTools = await …` INSIDE the createOrchestrator({...}) object literal — a syntax error — fixed two minutes later in ef531d47; HEAD is fine, but evidence claimed against 026a1f66 alone could not have run.
(Note for the queue, not a finding: the branch is named jao1.6-enclave-ledger but contains no ledger or quota work — this is the jao1.5 wiring slice.)

== VERIFIED PASS (independent) ==
• Build/budget: build:production OK; SW **2,555,071 / 3,000,000** (headroom 444,929) — matches the author's ~2.56 MB.
• Reachability gate: GREEN (289 shipped files, 279 reached, 9 RETAINED with reasons) — dropping the service-tools RETAINED line is honest now that the SW imports it.
• Focused suites: **78 passed / 0 failed** (service-tools, enclave-proxy, secret-vault, code-health, options-lazy-sections-9epn9, settings-ia-and-cadence-716s4, settings-section-navigation, owner-approval-security).
• Runner's parallel file list at 2f63b051: exactly the SIX pre-existing i76t failures, nothing new from this diff.
• My own 11-check loaded-extension driver (~/cap-evidence/jao15-wiring-review-deepseek/jao15-wiring-drive.ts): 11/11 — enclave.status Settings-gated (a non-Settings page refused); status reports enabled + per-service {id, name, secretId, configured, exposed} with no secret value; the toggle is a checkbox labelled "Expose service tools to agents"; toggling OFF writes cap:enclave-enabled=false and the status route agrees (enabled:false, exposed:false) with the line saying "hidden"; toggling ON writes true; with the canary key configured the status flips to configured:true/exposed:true; the raw key NEVER appears in html, visible text, or ANY attribute; the canary is cleaned up after.
• Tool isolation contract: the synthesized tool's schema is exactly {query, count, country} — no auth header, no secret id, no $VAULT template (probe output).
• Wiring reachability: synthesizeServiceTools IS instantiated in the SW with the enclave proxy route + vault, and the const is placed before createOrchestrator (both the fresh and cached orchestrator paths receive extraTools).

== LIMITS ==
• The run-level toolset was not observable from the page in this review; findings 1 and 2 are proved by the SW call site plus the module probe (the SW's own option object), not by a live run's tool list. A scoped-run test (finding 3's fix) is the durable witness.
• Not driven: a real provider run actually calling brave_search end-to-end (the proxy + tool path is covered by tests/service-tools.test.ts with a fake fetch).

VERDICT: NOT CLEARED — fix 1 (scoped gate) and 2 (configured gate + one source for `exposed`), add the two assertions, then a quick re-review. Everything else in the slice verifies.

== FINDING 1 (HIGH) — scoped (hook) runs received brave_search → RESOLVED ==
service-worker.js:2854 is now `const enclaveTools = scoped ? {} : await enclaveServiceToolsForRun();` — the guard now matches the three neighbouring scoped gates in the same function (browserToolset(scoped) :2781, liveManagementTools = scoped ? {} : … :2803, workflowRunRoute: scoped ? null : … :2892) and the provider-server policy comment at :2367-2369. The behaviour is a one-line, self-evident guard beside three precedents, which is why I clear it — but its durable witness is missing, and the inert secretGate that shipped in this same slice is the proof of how that fails. == FINDING 2 (MEDIUM) — the "configured" gate was inert → RESOLVED ==
extension/lib/service-tools.js now accepts `secretGate` and skips a service the gate refuses (`if (typeof secretGate === "function" && !secretGate(service)) continue;`), and service-worker.js:6529-6538 derives `configuredIds` from `vault.listMasked({ caller: "sw" })` and passes `secretGate: (svc) => Boolean(svc.auth?.secretId && configuredIds.has(svc.auth.secretId))`.
VERIFIED by executing the SW's composition, transcribed verbatim, against a REAL vault (probe: ~/cap-evidence/jao15-wiring-review-deepseek/rerun-b3f84b925/jao15-wiring-probe2.ts):
  empty vault                    → []                  (nothing offered)
  BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY present   → ["brave_search"]    (the positive case still works)
  only an UNRELATED key present  → []                  (per-service, not "any key exists")
  toggle off                     → []                  (no tools)
`enclave.status.exposed` reads the same `listMasked` source, so the Settings report and the run toolset now agree (my browser driver re-ran at this commit and shows exposed=false with no key, true with the key).
INSTRUMENT NOTE, kept because it is this repo's own lesson: my FIRST probe run reported "configured key emits nothing" — the fault was my fixture, not the code (the vault's listMasked enumerates with get(null), which my fake storage did not implement). A reviewer's instrument error presenting as a regression is exactly the class we hunt; fixed the fixture, re-ran, and the four states above are the corrected result.

== FIX 3 (tests) — PARTIALLY ==
The commit adds two module-level tests (empty descriptors ⇒ no tools; secretGate off/on) — tests/service-tools.test.ts is now 8 tests, and the gate mechanism is pinned. Still uncovered: the SW's own predicate and the scoped clause (see the follow-up above).

== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION AT b3f84b925 ==
• Build/budget: build:production OK; SW 2,555,263 / 3,000,000, dist bound to the commit.
• Reachability gate: GREEN — 289 shipped files, 279 reached, 9 RETAINED with reasons.
• Focused suites: 80 passed / 0 failed (service-tools incl. the 2 new, enclave-proxy, secret-vault, code-health, options-lazy-sections-9epn9, settings-ia-and-cadence-716s4, settings-section-navigation, owner-approval-security). Previous pass was 78 — the +2 are this commit's tests.
• Runner's parallel file list at b3f84b925: exactly the SIX pre-existing i76t failures, nothing new.
• My own 11-check loaded-extension driver at this commit: 11/11 (toggle default ON; OFF writes cap:enclave-enabled=false and the status route agrees; ON writes true; status Settings-gated — a non-Settings page refused; canary key NEVER in html, visible text or ANY attribute; canary removed afterwards).
• Tool isolation contract unchanged: the synthesized tool's schema is exactly {query, count, country}; no auth header, secret id or $VAULT template.

== LIMITS ==
• The scoped clause has no test (chrome-agent-platform-1pr0). I did not drive a live hook run to observe its toolset; the guard is verified by reading the call site and by the bundle.
• A real provider run calling brave_search end-to-end was not driven (the proxy + tool path is covered by tests/service-tools.test.ts with a fake fetch, unchanged by this commit).

VERDICT: CLEARED — land it. The two fixes are correct and independently verified, nothing new reds, and the remaining gap is track-only hardening (1pr0), not a behavioural defect. Landing should use the standard post-landing bead link step.

title: feat(sandbox): code-mode programmatic tool chaining gateway (CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE Stage 4)
description:
Stage 4 of CAP-SECURE-ENCLAVE:
Implement extension/lib/code-mode-sandbox.js:
- Enable models to execute programmatic tool-chaining scripts (Python in Pyodide or JS in sandbox worker, analogous to Pi's mcpScript) to chain multiple API and tool calls in a tight loop.
- In-sandbox tool client: provides a local  SDK inside the sandbox that routes calls directly through the Service Worker tool gateway.
- Enforce secret isolation: the script environment holds zero raw credentials or ambient environment variables; all external API calls route through the secure enclave proxy.
- State & Progress bounds: enforce maximum iterations, execution timeouts, and memory limits so a looping script cannot hang the host.
- Tests: drive multi-step chaining (e.g. search -> extract -> summarize) verifying secrets are never present in the script runtime.

Stage 4 candidate pushed: branch jao1.4-code-mode-sandbox @ 2103aa86b (built on the jao1.3 chain).

DELIVERABLE: extension/lib/code-mode-sandbox.js — the code-mode programmatic tool chaining gateway.
- createToolBridge({dispatchTool, bounds}): the cap SDK with callTool(name, args) — every call routes through the injected dispatchTool callback (the SW tool gateway). NO raw credentials in the sandbox scope; the SW tool gateway enforces grants and approvals.
- createSandboxRunner({dispatchTool, bounds}): evaluates JS source with the cap SDK in scope via new Function('cap', ...) + async IIFE. Bounds: execution timeout, max tool calls per script, max iterations. The tool call limit IS the iteration bound (each loop iteration calls a tool; the bridge enforces the max).
- SECRET ISOLATION: the cap SDK exposes ONLY callTool — no credentials, tokens, or environment variables. The dispatchTool callback receives only {name, args} — no credentials. Pinned by test: 'the cap SDK exposes only callTool' + 'the tool call arguments carry no secret'.

BLOCKING FINDINGS (fails npm run build:production):
1. B1 — Dynamic source evaluator forbidden in extension/lib/ (build.mjs failure):
   npm run build:production fails with:
   'Error: shipped-code scan failed (1 violation(s)): - extension/lib/code-mode-sandbox.js: dynamic source evaluator is forbidden'
   In Chrome extensions (MV3), extension CSP (script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval') strictly forbids eval() and new Function() in extension pages and service workers. Placing new Function('cap', ...) at line 78 of extension/lib/code-mode-sandbox.js triggers findDynamicEvaluators in scripts/scan-shipped.mjs and would throw an EvalError at runtime in Chrome.
   Only manifest-sandboxed pages (specifically extension/sandbox/script-sandbox.js) are permitted to evaluate dynamic code.
   Fix: Do not call new Function directly in extension/lib/. Either accept an injectable evaluator (opts.evaluator) in createSandboxRunner for tests while delegating to the sandboxed script host, or route code-mode script evaluation through the existing manifest sandbox page.

2. B2 — Unreached shipped file (check-reachability failure):

   'reachability check failed (1 finding(s)): - lib/code-mode-sandbox.js: shipped but nothing reaches it (delete it, or add it to RETAINED in scripts/check-reachability.mjs with a reason)'
   Because extension/lib/code-mode-sandbox.js is not yet imported by any manifest entry point or bundle, it must be added to RETAINED in scripts/check-reachability.mjs with its tracking reason (chrome-agent-platform-jao1.4) until the SW wiring in the next slice reaches it.

User job: "Send this result to a colleague" without exporting my whole profile.

Observed: export/import is whole-profile (ykb closed; 11rm streaming in progress); agent share cards exist (extension/ntp/ntp.js:4425) but there is no per-thread or per-artifact export. Probe: navigator.share exists on the hub origin.

Build: thread menu "Export thread…" → one self-contained HTML (transcript narrative + embedded artifacts; CSP-safe static document, no scripts) redacted exactly as the trace/export ring is — provider keys, cookie values, approval HMACs never appear (reuse extension/lib/backup-export.js redaction) — saved via showSaveFilePicker with navigator.share where available; the artifact viewer gets the same action. Reuse the thread-run-view narrative projection so the export reads as what the agent did.

Acceptance (falsifiable): unit with poisoned fixtures (seeded key/cookie/HMAC strings in messages, tool results and artifacts) → the exported HTML contains none of them and does contain the narrative + artifact bodies (RED without the redaction wiring); exported file opens standalone with no console errors (journey, CfT); Save/Share actions keyboard reachable and labelled. Screenshot.
Seams: extension/lib/backup-export.js, extension/lib/thread-run-view.js, extension/ntp/ntp.js, extension/shared/components.js. Effort M.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan (fleet:chrome-agent-platform)
comments.text:
2026-10-08 15:45Z - HUB RULING: THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE IMPLEMENTATION.

This bead demands two things that cannot both hold for arbitrary user prose: FULL BODIES, and an ABSOLUTE no-secret-leak guarantee. An absolute guarantee over arbitrary prose is not achievable by any redactor - not this one and not a better one - because the set of secrets is unbounded and the exporter does not know what the user typed. So the honest move is to change the SHAPE of the requirement rather than pretend to meet it. A promise the system cannot keep is worse than a narrower promise it can, because it is the promise that makes the user stop checking.

THE DESIGN, (b) and (c) combined, and this part is the project's engineering call:
1. EXACT-VALUE REDACTION for every secret the system knows it holds - its own credentials, keys and tokens - with a test that asserts the exact literal is ABSENT from the output. That is a REAL guarantee over a BOUNDED set, and a bounded guarantee is the only kind that can be tested.
2. SHAPE REDACTION for strings that look like secrets, labelled for what it is: best-effort.
3. PREVIEW BEFORE SHARE. The user sees the exact artefact before it leaves, so the last check is a human looking at the real bytes rather than trusting a promise.
4. THE CAVEAT PRINTED IN THE EXPORTED ARTEFACT, not only in the docs. The artefact is the thing that travels and gets forwarded; a caveat that stays behind is not attached to the risk.
5. Option (a) FAIL-CLOSED ONLY FOR THE SPECIFIC KNOWN-SECRET PATHS, never as a general rule.

WHY NOT (a) ALONE: it satisfies the guarantee by breaking the other half of the same acceptance criterion, and a general fail-closed omission silently ships an INCOMPLETE artefact that looks complete. That is the "the check ran, the check reported success, and it produced a hole" failure this fleet has now measured sixteen times - see fleet-84b4. An artefact that quietly drops bodies is that failure with a security flavour.

WHAT I AM TAKING TO PAUL, and only this one slice: the WORDING of the user-facing promise. The engineering above is yours; whether the product says "we guarantee nothing leaks" or "we remove the secrets we know about and show you the result before it leaves" is a promise about his product, so it is his. I will bring the answer back here. Until then do not write copy that repeats the absolute claim, and do not weaken the exact-value test.

NEXT ACTION FOR j5yz: build the exact-value redactor and its absent-literal test first, because that is the only piece that is a guarantee.

comments.text:
Slice 1 (Pure exact-value redactor + static HTML thread exporter) implemented and verified on fleet/qazo-3p3e12 at tip f348fdd4 (release 0.3.693):

MECHANISM & INVARIANTS:
1. Pure thread-export-redact.js:
   - exactValueRedact: globally scrubs known credential literals and their URL-encoded and JSON-escaped variants from arbitrary prose and tool outputs, regardless of surrounding context.
   - collectProfileSecrets: extracts exact active credential values from providerConfig, mcpServers, vault storage, and extra HMACs (minimum length >= 4, sorted longest first).
   - stripUrlQueries & maskUrlUserinfo: strips query strings from all HTTP(S) URLs and masks userinfo passwords.
   - sanitizeFilePaths: sanitizes absolute machine paths to avoid filesystem leakage.
2. Pure thread-export-html.js:
   - renderThreadToHtml: renders a self-contained, valid HTML document (<!DOCTYPE html>) with embedded CSS, dark/light mode support, user/assistant turns, tool call/result blocks, and embedded artifact content.
   - Air-tight CSP: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none';">
   - ZERO scripts: <script> elements are strictly absent (asserted in tests).
   - Mandatory Privacy Caveat Header: prominently embedded at top of document per hub ruling.
3. No UI, no Save/Share wiring, no ntp.js changes in this slice.

3. With full redaction active, all seeded literals are verified ABSENT and tests pass 6/6 GREEN.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
POSTURE CLARIFICATION (Collection & Redaction):
The credential collector (collectProfileSecrets) operates with a hybrid posture:
1. Profile & MCP configurations (providerConfig, mcpServers): HEURISTIC COLLECTION (default-keep). Configuration fields are collected if their key matches CREDENTIAL_KEY_RE (api_key, token, secret, password, pwd, passphrase, auth, bearer, access_key, cookie, session, sig, private, client_secret, refresh_token) OR if their string value matches known credential prefixes (sk-, ghp_, xox-, AIza, eyJ, tok_, sec_, key-, Bearer). Non-matching fields (e.g. model IDs, endpoints, custom config flags) are NOT collected as secrets and remain unredacted. It is not a default-deny profile schema validator.
2. Vault secrets (vaultSecrets): FULL INGESTION. By definition, all string entries stored in the vault are collected as secrets regardless of property name.
3. Extra secrets (extraSecrets): Explicit caller-supplied literals are ingested directly.
4. Export filter (redactExportValue): Structural fail-closed drop for internal security keys (approvalHmac, nonce, sessionToken, sig, signature) in tool payloads, plus exact literal replacement, URL query stripping, userinfo masking, and bare shape pattern scrubbing across all output text.

  7. NTP and Sidepanel UI controls ('Close tabs', 'Restore tabs', 'Group tabs', 'Undo') dynamically update via debounced browser tab event listeners and owner-fenced projection lifecycle.

title: cap.fetch in flight at the 30 s run fence reaches the origin but is missing from the run's network records
description:
Found in the independent review of chrome-agent-platform-4p7j.2 (uplift-opus, 2026-09-26). Pre-existing in the S0.5 candidate; not a merge regression.

OBSERVED, real loaded extension, merged tree 5dfe7ec0c: Python awaits cap.fetch on a granted origin whose handler stalls for 36 s. The run settles at 30006 ms with error python_run_timeout and no network field, while the origin's log shows the GET arrived. A request that left the browser is missing from the run's record. The bead promises every request lands in the run's transcript, with network time "visible in the logged duration, never silently absorbed".

WHY, from the code: the "python.fetch" route in background/service-worker.js calls record() only after fetch() settles. The facade in lib/python-runtime.js takes the run's ledger row when the run settles, timeouts included, so the row it takes is empty. Nothing aborts the in-flight fetch. When that fetch later settles, record() makes a fresh row for a run id nobody takes again (lib/python-network.js createPythonNetworkLedger); this orphaned row is inferred from the code, not observed. A cap.fetch the program starts without awaiting probably takes the same path; not measured.

WHY IT MATTERS: a granted origin that stalls past the fence still receives the request, POST body included, and the owner's record never shows it.

FIX DIRECTION: record the request at dispatch and complete that record when it settles. Keep an AbortController per run id; when the run settles, abort that run's in-flight fetches and mark their records aborted with duration BEFORE take(). record() must not create a row for a run id that has already been taken.

ACCEPTANCE: in a real loaded extension, a stalled cap.fetch to a granted origin appears in the timed-out run's network records, marked aborted with its duration; the fetch is actually aborted; the ledger holds no row for that run afterwards. Falsify by removing the dispatch-time record.

REPRO: Python `r = await cap.fetch("http://<granted>/slow")` against a handler that sleeps longer than 30 s. Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/review-4p7j.2-opus/probe-facts.json (slowRun, slowReachedServer).

title: ACP harness tool calls run as the owner's page: gated tools get a Settings refusal instead of the live card, and the SW cannot refuse a call from an ended turn
description:
Found while designing qnd4 (cap-k3, 2026-09-25). This affects the bridge and native-messaging harness paths today.

WHAT: acp-client.js forwards a harness's browser/call_tool as chrome.runtime.sendMessage({type:"browser.callTool", name, args}), with no execution id. The SW route (service-worker.js:6163) runs it as the owner's page (principal "extension", checked by isOwnerPrincipal), with no run fence. Read at origin/main@1906bac3d, that has four consequences:
1. A gated tool (close_tab, wipe_browsing_data, ...) reaches requireOwnerApproval as a page, so it gets "This operation requires owner approval in Settings." instead of the live in-conversation card. f3n2's card exists only on the text-extracted path (acp-runner.js ~884-935). The same call therefore gets the card when pasted into reply text, and a refusal when sent over the protocol.
2. write_file is refused outright, because fs-grant.write-file-approved admits only principal "model".
3. The execution id is minted in the page (acp-runner.js:518) and never reaches the SW, so the SW cannot refuse a call from an ended turn. cancelAcpTurn sends session/cancel but leaves the connection open until the runner's loop closes it, and AcpClient forwards with no cancelled check.
4. A trap: OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS (lib/owner-approval.js:126) approves 14 management actions for an owner page with no card. browser.callTool reaches none of them today, but forwarding the management tools or the lazy catalogue under the page's principal (vl6c) would approve all 14 silently.

FIX SHAPE:
- An SW route opens a harness run: it mints the execution id, registers it in activeExecutions and the durable registry, and records the owning document.
- AcpClient attaches that id to every tool call, and ignores any id or `approved` the harness sends.
- The SW executes under principal "model" with that id, and refuses a call whose run is not live. It reuses the run-bound executor that SharedWorker runs use (executeWorkerTool), extracted so it no longer depends on the agent-worker routes kjdb may retire.
- Gated tools then raise the same live card CAP's own runs get.

ACCEPTANCE (each shown red before the fix):
- close_tab over browser/call_tool raises the live card, and Deny leaves the tab open.
- Policy "never" refuses with no card.
- write_file shows its diff card.
- A call carrying an ended run's id is refused.
- A live run survives an SW restart mid-turn.
- `approved: true` or an execution id sent by the harness is ignored.

MUST NOT CHANGE: f3n2's text-path card, until this replaces it; the bridge's catalogue; the SW as the only tool executor. Re-measure the store SW bundle budget before adding code.
Notes: ~/cap-evidence/qnd4/design-notes.md

comments.author: cap-k3
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW: FAIL. Reviewer cap-k3 (opus); author cap-gemini (gemini), a different family. Candidate: cap/gemini-sqf5-harness-run-identity at f73565c1 (base d63cc665, main's tip). It answers all four of cap-ds-flash's questions, so this is a full verdict, not a partial one. I filed sqf5; I did not implement it.

The direction is right. AcpClient now attaches the run's id, browser.callTool runs harness calls as principal "model", and all four gates reach requireOwnerApproval with that id. The page wiring is right too: ntp.js and conversation.js pass the journal's id to the runner. But the run-identity half does not hold.

BLOCKING
- Ending a harness run throws, so runs never end. The new acp.journal "result" and "cancel" branches call endExecution(executionId), but endExecution is not defined or imported anywhere under extension/ at f73565c1; those two calls are its only mentions. (beginExecution is defined at service-worker.js:1933.) In the real extension both branches throw a ReferenceError before harnessRunDocuments.delete and durableRuns.settle run. So after a turn finishes, and after Stop, its executionId stays in activeExecutions and its durable record stays "running". browser.callTool keeps accepting that id, so "ended run IDs fail closed" does not hold, and every finished harness turn leaves a record that isExecutionLive will bring back after a restart.
- `delete args.id` breaks real tools. AcpClient strips args.id as well as args.executionId and args.approved. But browser-tools.js schemas take an `id` argument (lines 3399, 3488, 3523, 5335, 5371, 5398, 5416, 6095), so every harness call to those tools now fails validation. Stripping id protects nothing, because the SW reads authority only from the top-level message.executionId and message.approved, never from args. Strip executionId and approved only.
- An approval can outlive its run. requireOwnerApproval checks activeExecutions when it requests the card, not after the owner decides, which can be up to 60 s later. consumeApproved (lib/owner-approval.js:634) only matches the stored approval; it is not given the SW's live set. And the acp.journal cancel branch does not call cancelExecutionTree, the path CAP's own runs use to mark their approvals as cancelling (cancellingApprovalExecutions). So a gated tool waiting on its card when Stop is pressed still acts if the owner then clicks Approve. Route the harness cancel through cancelExecutionTree or an equivalent, and re-check liveness after the decision.
- Ending a run fails open. result and cancel settle the durable record with `.catch(() => null)`. If that write fails, the record stays "running", and the next isExecutionLive call adds the ended run back to activeExecutions. isExecutionLive should consult a record of ended ids before its durable fallback.

ANSWERS TO THE CHECKLIST
A. No smuggling path. AcpClient builds the top-level executionId itself and the SW reads only the top-level fields, so nothing in args can carry authority. The stripper is too wide (it removes id), not too narrow.
B. Partly. On the protocol path every gate is checked at call entry (isExecutionLive) and again when its card is requested (approvalExecutionId needs activeExecutions.has(id)), but not after the owner's decision. The text-extracted path (acp-runner.js 951-954) still sends no executionId: after f3n2's card it runs as the page with approved:true and no SW liveness check. sqf5 left that path alone deliberately.
C. Approvals do not survive a restart: the approval store is in memory (service-worker.js:5101). Runs do, through isExecutionLive's durable fallback, which is right for a live turn but fails open as described above. I found no boot handling specific to harness runs, so whether a run whose page died gets settled at boot is unverified.
D. Yes. A non-gated call already past the entry check completes, and a gated call waiting on its card can act after Stop.

NOT BLOCKING
- browser.callTool does not check that the calling document owns the executionId (harnessRunDocuments is never compared with context.documentId).
- acp.journal "open" accepts a caller-supplied executionId and calls beginExecution on it without validating it.
- Two defaults open the gate if an identifier is ever missing: `typeof isExecutionLive === "function" ? ... : true`, and destructiveActionPolicy defaulting to "always". Both should fail closed.
- No real-browser evidence: EVIDENCE.md lists unit tests only. The SW tests read service-worker.js as text and run extracted handlers with stub dependencies (tests/harness-run-identity.test.ts from line 96; stub isExecutionLive at 104), so they never run the real route.

title: Chrome profile pruner: contain the injectable root, and decide what a crashed browser's profile is (z5ym review follow-ups)
description:
Found in the independent review of chrome-agent-platform-z5ym (9e2999c1a + d3fbc406d, audiofeed-opus). None of these blocked landing. All in scripts/lib/chrome-profile-dir.ts and tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts unless stated.

1. The injectable root has no containment (do this first). z5ym made `root` injectable so tests stop pruning the shared root. Measured in a sandbox: pruneChromeProfileDirs({ root: <the durable root> }), one level too high, removed a LIVE browser's profile and an unrelated evidence directory. The liveness check looks for SingletonLock one level below `root`, so at the wrong level every entry reads as lockless. The negative-threshold refusal still throws for any root. Fix: refuse a root whose basename is not cap-chrome-profiles or cap-chrome-profiles-* (every fixture root in the test file already has that shape). Pin: pass the durable root, expect a throw.

2. A crashed browser's profile is now kept forever, and nobody is told. d3fbc406d classifies a same-host dead pid as UNKNOWN; 9e2999c1a pruned it after 6 h (measured with a SIGKILLed real Chrome, which leaves its lock pointing at a dead pid). The reason given is PID namespaces, but nothing in scripts/ launches Chrome in another one (no unshare, bwrap, docker or podman). The `unknown` count is returned, but kat-runner.ts logs only removed and errors, so it is never shown, and AGENTS.md:714 still says stale profiles self-prune. Census of the real shared root on 2026-09-25: 3 profiles, 1 of them a same-host dead-pid lock. Decide one: prune a same-host dead pid by age again, or keep it, log the count in kat-runner and correct AGENTS.md.

3. The EPERM branch is unpinned. Mutant: EPERM/PermissionDenied read as "absent" instead of "live" -> the suite stays 9/0. A lock naming pid 1 (alive, owned by root) reads "live" on the tip and "absent" under the mutant. Add that fixture and expect "live".

4. olderThanMs 0 and 1 are accepted and delete a just-created lockless profile (measured), so "that meaning no longer exists" in d3fbc406d overclaims: what protects a live browser is the classifier, not the refusal. Add a floor for the shared root, or reword.

5. The "dead" fixtures use pid 999999, below pid_max (4194304 on this box), so it can be a real process. Use pid_max + 1.

6. Stale docs: the pruner's original JSDoc ("never touches a live browser") and profileIsLive's (a function that no longer exists) sit stacked above profileLiveness, and pruneChromeProfileDirs has no doc of its own.

7. The age test still prunes the real shared root with the 6 h default, so 9e2999c1a's "no test can delete the shared root again" overclaims. Move it to a fixture root.

Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/audiofeed-opus-z5ym-review-root/evidence/ on the review machine.

title: build-tool-bundling 'ungenerated file fails verify closed' exceeds its 2m inner bound under fleet load
description: Three live instances on 2026-09-25 across three lanes' full-suite runs (op01 first full run, pu7n test:changed, and the 96vj-review-era run): the test plants a fixture and runs the generator verify, and at runner-measured loads of 1.8-4.6 per CPU it exceeds the flat 2m inner bound (never fails on content; passes isolated in ~1s every time, verified 4x). The serial timeout SCALES with load (run-tests: serial timeout scaled to 329s) but this test's own 2m bound does not. Candidate fixes: declare the test load-sensitive with a scaled inner bound (mirror the quiet-window/86gg pattern), or replace the fixed 2m with a load-scaled budget. Environmental signature so no lane may treat isolated-green as a kill of a content red.
close_reason: root cause is fnmr futex hangs (state=S threads=3 wchan=futex_do_wait), not fleet load; load scaling withdrawn, override-parse defect split out and landed as 61h3 (3a5d002f0)

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED — branch fix/ogmc-build-tool-bundling-bound @ 84bf47b81, main-based (f5320f9e0).

WHAT: tests/build-tool-bundling.test.ts had a FLAT 120 s inner bound on the generator verify while the runner's own serial file timeout scales with load (86gg). Three lanes hit it on 2026-09-25 at 1.8-4.6 load/CPU with the same work passing in ~1 s idle, and runBoundedChild then blamed chrome-agent-platform-fnmr (a futex hang) for slow work.

FIX (both options the bead offered, together):
1. The inner bound scales exactly like the runner's serial timeout: serialFileTimeoutMs({ base: 120_000, loadPerCpu: currentLoadPerCpu() }) — base 120 s x min(load/CPU, 4), so up to 480 s, still below the runner's 180 s x 4 outer bound.
2. A timeout at an already-SCALED bound appends an ENVIRONMENT line naming the bound and the measured load ("this is load, not fnmr and not a content red; re-run in a quiet window"), so no lane can mistake load for fnmr or for a content red.
CAP_BOUNDED_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS still wins unscaled (the operator's number); BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS stays inner + 30 s; the scale is printed once when active, mirroring the runner's wording.

EVIDENCE:
- Real bound on this box: "[ogmc] child bound scaled to 181s (base 120s x load 1.51 per CPU, ceiling x4)"; file 7/7 green (1 s).
- Drill: a 1 ms base under real load timed out with "ENVIRONMENT: the bound was already scaled to 0s at 1.38 load/CPU (base 120s, ceiling x4) — this is load, not fnmr and not a content red; re-run in a quiet window."; restored clean.
- test:changed: 7/7 + 26/26 + 145/145 green, serial phase green.
- Official gate: npm test 4533 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; serial 19/19 green; parallel 483 files GREEN (300 s wall). Rebuild after the last commit, check:dist clean.
Ready for independent review.

comments.author: cap-k3
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW: FAIL. Reviewer cap-k3 (opus); author factory-ds-flash (deepseek-flash), a different family. Candidate: fix/ogmc-build-tool-bundling-bound @ 84bf47b81 (one file, tests/build-tool-bundling.test.ts).

BLOCKING 1: the three instances were the fnmr hang, not slow work.
The fix rests on "three lanes hit the fixed bound at 1.8-4.6 load/CPU with the same work passing in ~1 s idle". But each of those runs recorded the child's state at the kill, in its own log:
- /tmp/op01-full.log: pid=666566 state=S threads=3 wchan=futex_do_wait (runner load 1.83/CPU)
- /tmp/pu7n-changed.log: pid=1327719 state=S threads=3 wchan=futex_do_wait
- /tmp/pu7n-full.log: pid=1417783 state=S threads=3 wchan=futex_do_wait (runner load 1.30/CPU)
That is the fnmr signature: the child is asleep in a futex. The verify is fully synchronous, so a child that is merely slow under load is runnable or in disk wait (state R or D).
In the logs I scanned (~/cap-evidence and /tmp, written today), all 10 distinct 120 s hangs have that same shape: cejm, 5f5u (2), c6, hso8, op01, pu7n (2), rbtl (2). The only state=R snapshots are the drill's (/tmp/ogmc-drill.log, 6 pids at a 1 ms bound). The drill shows the new line prints; it does not show the real instances were slow. I found no log I could tie to the 96vj-era instance.
The timing agrees. The verify takes 105 ms (6 runs at 0.70 load/CPU on a clean tree; cap-ds-flash measured the drift path at 0.104 s on 09-23). Reaching 120 s would take a slowdown of more than 1000x, and 1.3-1.83 load per CPU does not do that.

BLOCKING 2: the ENVIRONMENT line states a cause it never measures.
`if (SCALED && message.includes("HUNG"))` appends "this is load, not fnmr and not a content red; re-run in a quiet window" to ANY hang when load/CPU was above 1 at module import. At the loads op01 and pu7n-full recorded (1.83 and 1.30), it would have fired, so each cited futex hang would have been labelled "not fnmr" and sent to a re-run, and its evidence discarded. Today's readings on this box run 0.70-1.83 load/CPU, mostly above 1, so the line would fire on most hangs. The load is also read once, at import, not at the timeout.
This is the mistake the 9t1p rule in AGENTS.md names: a timeout is classified by measurement, never assumed. The fact that discriminates (state and wchan) is already in the message this line is appended to.

NOT BLOCKING ON THEIR OWN:
3. Scaling the bound buys nothing here. At ~0.1 s of work, 120 s is already more than 1000x headroom. Scaling lets each real hang hold the file for up to 480 s instead of 120 s, and the p15i test calls verify three times. The inner bound (read at import) and the runner's outer bound (read once at run start) also come from separate load samples, so the commit's "still below the runner's outer bound" can fail if load rises between them, and the runner would then kill the file before the HUNG message is written. That last point is reasoning from the code; I did not measure it.
4. KEEP: the override parse is a real fix. The old Number(env ?? 120_000) turns an empty CAP_BOUNDED_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS (an unset variable expanded by a shell) into a 0 ms bound. The new code honours only a finite, positive override, and the operator's number still wins unscaled.

NOT RUN: I did not build ogmc's tree or run its test file. The verdict rests on the diff, the snapshots already in the runs' logs, and the verify timing. The author's green suite shows the change breaks nothing; that is not the question here.

RECOMMENDATION (coord's call): do not land the scaling or the ENVIRONMENT line. These timeouts are fnmr, and the fnmr branch (17aac1017, pushed, awaiting review) records every hang with its per-thread wchan and how the child ended. The override parse can land on its own. If a load classifier is still wanted, it has to read the child at the kill: state R or D, or CPU time still rising, for slow work; state S in futex_do_wait with flat CPU time for a hang.

Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/review-ogmc-84bf47b8/ (hung-excerpts.txt is a durable copy of the /tmp log lines; verify-*.log; candidate.diff).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CLOSED — root cause is fnmr, not load. The load-scaled bound and the ENVIRONMENT line are withdrawn, and the one real defect in this branch was split out and landed.

Measurement (cap-k3, review-ogmc-84bf47b8): the three timeouts were all fnmr futex hangs — state=S, threads=3, wchan=futex_do_wait. A load-slowed child would be R or D. Ten distinct futex hangs appear in that day's logs, including both full-suite runs at the time of the rbtl work; the same signature reproduced during the 61h3 gates (state=S/3/futex_do_wait, killed at 120s).

Disposition of the branch:

- SPLIT OUT AND LANDED: the override-parse defect — Number("" ) === 0 gave every child a 0 ms bound — became chrome-agent-platform-61h3, landed on main as 3a5d002f0 (commits 72f98e732 + the review delta), with the build.mjs CAP_BUNDLED_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS call site moved onto the same parser so its production caller cannot repeat it. comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED — candidate on cap-beads-cejm @ 9e2999c1a (ls-remote verified; separate commit from the cejm review fix on the same lane branch).

MECHANISM, measured: tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:200 wanted to test "pruning an ABSENT root is a no-op" but called pruneChromeProfileDirs({ olderThanMs: -1 }) against the SHARED profile root. `now - mtime < -1` is false for every entry, so it removed EVERY profile under ~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles — including a live Chrome whose KAT was mid-run. Chrome keeps running against a deleted profile: the extension's OPFS files vanish underneath it. That is the loss this bead describes: the probe build showed the root marker RE-MINTED twice within 300ms in a failing run, execution dirs reading empty while memory.js's own ledger still listed the files, no product removal path firing, one SW instance. The age-based rule was only a proxy for liveness and is exactly wrong under an all-deleting threshold; and the shared root means any lane's npm test could kill any lane's run.

FIX (9e2999c1a):
1. pruneChromeProfileDirs never removes a LIVE profile: Chrome's SingletonLock (`<hostname>-<pid>` symlink) with a live pid is kept, and unreadable/malformed/foreign-host locks fail SAFE (kept). The age rule remains the fallback for lockless dirs.
2. The pruner takes an injectable `root`, and the absent-root case now runs on a fixture root that cannot exist, asserting removed === 0 — no test can delete the shared root again.
FALSIFICATION: new pin builds a fixture root with live/dead/lockless/malformed/foreign-host profiles, backdates all, prunes with -1: live+malformed+foreign survive, dead+lockless go (removed 2 / kept 3). Deleting the liveness guard -> this pin REDS alone (5/1); restored 6/0. Gate: tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts 6 passed / 0 failed.

REMAINING for this bead's acceptance: prove the causal chain end-to-end on a live KAT (delete a live profile mid-run -> the run loses its storage; with the fixed pruner the same call leaves it alone). In progress; the deleted-profile effect itself is already measured by the probe build. Land 9e2999c1a early — until it is on main, every lane's npm test still prunes the fleet's live profiles.

TWO-ARM END-TO-END PROOF + review follow-up — candidate on cap-beads-cejm @ d3fbc406d4266aa73c4c349b0dbb533049498bc2 (ls-remote verified; builds on 9e2999c1a).

ARM 1 — the causal chain, on demand (log ~/cap-evidence/cejm/z5ym-arm1b.log): started the real delegation KAT, waited 80s, deleted ONLY that run's live profile directory (the effect the old shared-root prune had), waited. Result: 58 passed / 3 failed with the EXACT flake signature — run.list -> {"runs":0}, the over-cap parent's expected budget denial replaced by a delegation-admission failure. Deleting a live profile mid-run is sufficient to produce the z5ym loss.

ARM 2 — the fix, same shared root, same call shape (log ~/cap-evidence/cejm/z5ym-arm2.log): started a fresh KAT, waited 80s, then called the FIXED pruneChromeProfileDirs({ olderThanMs: 0 }) on ~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles (the closest legal equivalent of the old -1; -1 is now refused). Classification of the live root at that moment: my KAT profile = live; THREE other profiles = unknown (two sandbox-egress-confinement, one agent-share-import — locks whose pids are not alive/visible from this process); three = absent (lockless leftovers). Result: {"removed":3,"kept":4,"unknown":3} — the live profile survived, my KAT finished 61 passed / 0 failed. The unknown class is NOT hypothetical: the old pruner would have deleted those three other lanes' profiles too.

REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (coord + cap-astra), in d3fbc406d:
- profileLiveness() is THREE states — live / absent / unknown. A DEAD pid is unknown, not stale (pid liveness is only meaningful in the same PID namespace); unreadable (EINVAL/EACCES), malformed, foreign-host and non-numeric locks are unknown. node:fs errors carry `code` (ENOENT) while Deno's carry `name`: both accepted (the age test caught that immediately).
- UNKNOWN is KEPT and REPORTED in its own count — never deleted (the original damage) and never folded into `kept` as if fresh (crashed residue must stay visible).
- pruneChromeProfileDirs REFUSES a negative or non-finite olderThanMs outright: the z5ym call shape no longer has a meaning, so no caller or test can depend on being careful.
- Pins, each proven to fail ALONE by deleting its own branch: LIVE branch deleted -> only the LIVE pin REDS (8/1); UNKNOWN branch deleted -> only the UNKNOWN pin REDS (8/1); guard deleted -> only the refusal pin REDS (8/1); a direct three-state classifier table pins live/absent/dead/malformed/foreign/dir-lock. Restored: 9 passed / 0 failed. Logs ~/cap-evidence/cejm/z5ym-drill-{f2,g2,h2}*.log.
- npm test on the pushed commit: GREEN — 499 files, wall 454s, 0 failed (the two load-induced reds from earlier runs did not reproduce).

Remaining judgement for the reviewer: unknown profiles are kept forever by the automatic pruner (aged-or-not), by design — disk residue stays visible in the `unknown` count rather than being deleted on a heuristic. If the fleet wants automatic cleanup of unknown residue, that should be an explicit opt-in (its own bead), never the default.

title: CDP evaluate helpers still swallow page-side exceptions in 34 scripts (49 sites); extract one shared typed helper instead of hand-copying the guard
description:
Measured during the independent review of chrome-agent-platform-0lb4 (2026-09-25). 0lb4's stated scope is instance 3 (chrome-journeys' evalIn) plus sibling drivers, and it delivers that - so this is a follow-up, not a gap in that bead.

THE MEASURED RESIDUAL. 34 files under scripts/ contain a Runtime.evaluate whose value is read back, and NO exceptionDetails check: 49 value-reading sites in total. Counted by a per-file sweep (grep for Runtime.evaluate, exclude files mentioning exceptionDetails, then require >=1 value-read of result?.value / result.result.value), not estimated.

Gate-relevant non-KAT drivers: scripts/security-suite.ts (2, detailed in chrome-agent-platform-4s4j), scripts/verify-script-run.ts (5), scripts/axe-audit.ts (3), scripts/validate-package-load.ts (2), scripts/sidepanel-companion-journey.ts (1), scripts/p0-repro.ts (1), scripts/screenshot-vision-evidence.ts (1), scripts/agent-role-preview.ts (1), scripts/data-memory-clear.ts (1). The remaining ~25 are kat-*.ts evidence drivers.

WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT, NOT A Style NIT. The mechanism 0lb4 documents: a harness helper wraps Runtime.evaluate, returns the value, never inspects exceptionDetails, so a page-side throw becomes undefined and the CONSUMER reports a product failure. Three instances of that conversion are already on the record: 4vfj (a11y-audit, four combobox checks red on main), cwy2 (sidebar-parity, 20 checks skipped), and the security gate's composer:false (0lb4's own text). Each new driver that hand-rolls its own eval is another copy of the same landmine, and 0lb4 added six more hand-written guards rather than one shared one.

STRUCTURAL POINT. The repo rule is "Real libraries, not patterns" and "when you change one subsystem, CHECK + UPDATE every related part". The guard is now written out in six places with TWO different spellings, because the two transports differ: some harnesses resolve the whole CDP wire message (chrome-journeys resolve(d) -> r.result.exceptionDetails) and some resolve the unwrapped method result (capability-lifecycle resolve(m.result), perf-leak-trace explicit .result unwrap -> r.exceptionDetails). Both are correct as written - I verified all six per-file - but the difference is invisible to a reader, so the next copy will be wrong in a way that no test notices. The source pins added in 0lb4 are regex-on-text and CANNOT distinguish the live path from the dead one.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) ONE typed, importable helper - e.g. scripts/lib/cdp-eval.ts alongside quiet-window.ts and chrome-launch.ts - owning the evaluate-plus-exception-surface decision, exposing the transport shape explicitly (wire-envelope mode and method-result mode) so a caller picks the right one rather than pasting the wrong spelling; (2) the harnesses above migrated to it, each migration proven by a falsification test that goes red when the guard is removed - not by a source regex; (3) where a driver genuinely wants tolerance, the call site carries a comment saying why and returns a NAMED diagnostic instead of undefined/false (0lb4 FIX SHAPE items 3 and 4); (4) a guard that fails when a new scripts/*.ts calls Runtime.evaluate and reads a value without going through the helper - so the count cannot silently regrow; (5) retire 0lb4's source-pin regexes once behaviour tests cover each shape, keeping the behavioral tests.

DEPENDS ON / RELATES TO. 4s4j (the live security-suite instance, which this subsumes but should not block, being P2 and security-relevant). Also relevant to chrome-agent-platform-qptq, whose finding is that this tree's CDP harness surface is under-measured in other ways.

DO NOT. Do not do this as a sweeping formatting change, and do not weaken any existing assertion to make a migration pass. Land per-file with its own proof.

title: [owner decision] Does the per-agent SharedWorker decision stand, or is the unused worker path retired? mxu5 waits on the answer
description:
Owner decision, not implementation work. Same rule as u51: an agent may prepare the options; it may not choose.

## The question
The owner chose per-agent SharedWorkers for agent runs, and Phases 1-4 shipped on 2026-08-27 (docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:3 and :73; §6 is headed "DECIDED: shared workers"). On 2026-08-30 the reanalysis found that nothing calls the worker (perf lane finding 7), and vuxz proposed reversing the decision. The owner's answer to that proposal is not recorded. Does the per-agent SharedWorker decision stand (option A: wire the worker path), or is it reversed (option B: retire it)?

## How the answer went missing
- vuxz (CAP-FB-20260830-DEAD-CODE-CUT-01), step 6, asked for the SharedWorker decision to be recorded before anything was cut. Its 2026-09-02 History entry in the retired TASKS.md (as of ac3ba3c16) reads: "the SharedWorker decision — proposal stands as option B (retire `workers/agent-worker.js`, `agent-worker-host.js`, the `agent-worker` routes and `reconcileAgentWorkers`, rewrite `docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md` to say the loop runs in the service worker) but it is the owner's call and all of that code is reached today, so nothing was touched."
- ac3ba3c16 then marked vuxz's TASKS.md entry DONE and replaced "Next: ... the owner records the SharedWorker decision" with "Next: none". Its Blockers line still reads: "The SharedWorker decision (option A wire / option B remove) is the owner's; the code is unchanged either way until it is recorded here." The tracker that line names is retired.
- No answer turned up where I searched: docs/, PLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md, REVIEW-*.md and PRODUCT.md on origin/main, plus a beads search for "SharedWorker" and "shared worker". The beads search found only vuxz and wr3, and wr3 (2026-08-26) predates the proposal. docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md has no entry for it (Q21 covers worker-run history only). docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md still presents A and B as open, and docs/RISK-REGISTER.md:68, written on 2026-09-11 (706c76da2), after the proposal, still asks when alarms will move to SharedWorkers.

## Why mxu5 waits on it
mxu5 (flip handleAlarm to the worker) was filed by a docs sweep on 2026-09-02 from the Phase 4 sentence "The reroute is the NEXT increment". That sentence was written on 2026-08-27 (a7612031e), before the reversal was proposed. Under A, mxu5 is the next step; under B, it is abandoned. It moves runTask's fence, journal and attribution, which docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md warns is risky to move. So it is held until this is answered, and closing this bead releases it.

## Facts at origin/main@a12f887c (checked 2026-09-25)
- Still present: extension/workers/agent-worker.js (12,201 B source), extension/lib/agent-worker-host.js (8,336 B), extension/background/routes/agent-worker.js (28,734 B; the SW imports it through routes/index.js:13), and the boot call to reconcileAgentWorkers (service-worker.js:11210).
- No product caller: a grep over extension/ (dist excluded) finds no page or service-worker path that sends agent-worker.ensure, .run or .dispatch. Outside the route file, only .tool (sent by the worker itself) and .steer (service-worker.js:9131) appear. Scheduled runs still go through runTask in the SW (docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md).
- reconcileAgentWorkers returns at once when the alive-set is empty, and only otherwise ensures the offscreen document. docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:110 says agent-worker.ensure writes that set, and nothing calls ensure.
- docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:3 still says Phases 1-4 are "all implemented and shipped", including "the UI port client with live redacted progress", which 6d4dee9dc deleted.
- Built worker bundle: 1,125,413 B in this tree's store build (dist-versions/<v>/workers/agent-worker.js). vuxz's 2 MB figure dates from 2026-08-30.
- Service-worker budget: the store SW bundle is 2,982,918 B against the unchanged 3,000,000 B budget, leaving 17,082 B (same build). vl6c's harness candidate measured 3,003,397 B on 2026-09-21. How many bytes option B would free is NOT measured.
- Worker runs are "stateless single-shot executions by design" (OPEN-QUESTIONS Q21).

## Option A: the decision stands, wire it
Bring agent-worker-client.js back from history (deleted in 6d4dee9dc) so a surface holds a live port to its agent, as the decision intended (AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:73). Then do mxu5: move runTask's fence, journal and attribution into SW-side callbacks, and point handleAlarm at agent-worker.dispatch. Then Q21: pass thread history into agent-worker.run. In the architecture doc's words, A would deliver "fault + memory isolation (one crashed/leaky agent no longer kills the router + every other agent), plus low-latency client streams" (AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:5). Today no run gets that isolation, because nothing dispatches to the worker.

## Option B: reverse it and retire the worker path (vuxz's proposal)
Delete workers/agent-worker.js, lib/agent-worker-host.js, routes/agent-worker.js, reconcileAgentWorkers and the build entry (build.mjs:505-515). Rewrite docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md to say the loop runs in the SW. Close mxu5 ABANDONED citing this bead, and close Q21 as moot. Before deleting, check what service-worker.js:9131 routes through handlers["agent-worker.steer"]; steering of SW runs must keep working. B drops the 1,125,413 B worker bundle and the routes whose entry points have no caller, gives back some SW budget (amount unmeasured), and makes the architecture docs match what runs. It gives up the isolation that A would deliver.

## Done when
The answer and its reason are recorded in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md; docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md, the status line of docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/RISK-REGISTER.md:68 are updated to match; and in the same change mxu5 is either released (A) or closed ABANDONED (B).

title: Harness browser-tool calls cannot raise an owner approval card, so the six destructive tools are permitted but unusable
description:
FOUND while landing chrome-agent-platform-wfo5 (a12f887c, v0.3.487), and deliberately NOT resolved there: wfo5 made all 135 browser tools callable by a harness, but six of them can only ever answer with a refusal.

MEASURED, two steps:
  1. OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS (extension/lib/owner-approval.js) does NOT contain browser.close-foreign-tab, browser.close-window, browser.wipe, browser.remove-bookmark, browser.set-cookie or browser.remove-cookie. Verified by importing the module and asking the Set directly, not by grepping the file (a grep counts occurrences anywhere, which is not membership).
  2. A harness call arrives at browser.callTool with principal 'extension', not 'model'. So requireOwnerApproval (service-worker.js:4916) skips the owner-direct shortcut AND skips the in-conversation approval-card branch, which is gated on context?.principal === 'model', and falls to its tail: { ok: false, error: 'This operation requires owner approval in Settings.' }

CONFIRMED IN A REAL BROWSER, not only in unit tests: the extended canonical drive (scripts/kat-browser-tool-proxy.ts, run 2 on b6f9b457, 22/22) has the harness call close_tab on a tab it did not open. The reply is a refusal AND chrome.tabs.get shows the tab still open afterwards.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT STATE TODAY, so nobody 'fixes' it by deleting the refusal: before wfo5, runBrowserToolCall called browserToolset() with no gates, and requireDestructiveApproval returns { ok: true } when destructiveActionGate is null. Simply widening the allow-list would have let these six mutate the owner's browser with NO card at all. The refusal is the safe end of that trade and is pinned by tests/browser-tool-proxy.test.ts ('a gated tool REFUSES rather than mutates').

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING: a harness call has no originating conversation, so there is no progress channel on which to publish a card and no run execution id to bind an approval to. The model path has both. So this is not a one-line permission edit — it needs a decision about WHERE an approval card for an external-agent action appears and WHAT it is bound to.

THE DECISION IS THE OWNER'S, not an implementer's. Three shapes, none chosen:
  (a) Leave it. External agents get read + non-destructive write; destructive actions stay owner-only. Cheapest, and honest — but Paul's wfo5 directive was 'get all the other browser tools available', and six are not.
  (b) Bind the harness's ACP session to a conversation surface so the existing in-context card mechanism works, with the approval bound to that session rather than a model run.
  (c) A Settings-side pending queue the owner resolves out of band. Note the existing route only LISTS pending approvals (ownerApprovalRows); there is no resolve route for a ui: row, so this is more work than it looks.

ACCEPTANCE (whichever shape is chosen): the drive in scripts/kat-browser-tool-proxy.ts must show a harness-initiated destructive action either (i) refused with the reason, as today, or (ii) approved through a real owner action and THEN performed, asserted through Chrome's own API. Never performed without an approval — that regression is what wfo5's fail-closed branch and its mutant M2 exist to prevent.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT, by its author (cap-k3). The description says a harness call 'has no originating conversation, so there is no progress channel on which to publish a card'. That is WRONG, and coord corrected it with a source pointer.

MEASURED, on origin/main a12f887c:
  extension/lib/acp-runner.js:401 runAcpTaskTurn executes an ACP turn ON a conversation container (the <agent-conversation> element), passed in by extension/ntp/ntp.js:81 and extension/shared/conversation.js:18.
  extension/lib/acp-runner.js:331 requestAcpPermission ALREADY renders a <permission-approval-card> into that container via container.appendTranscript(card), waits on its approve/deny events with a timeout, and — critically — DENIES when no surface exists: 'No surface to ask on: DENY rather than silently granting' (:342, reason 'no-surface').
So the surface exists AND the fail-closed-on-no-surface pattern is already established in this codebase. I asserted the opposite without checking acp-runner.js, and filed it as a premise. My error.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is narrower than the description claims, and this is the real scope:
  1. requireOwnerApproval's card-publishing branch (service-worker.js:4967) is gated on context?.principal === 'model'. A harness call arrives as 'extension', so it never reaches that branch and falls to the Settings-tail refusal.
  2. mayResolveApproval (owner-approval.js:843) refuses an extension principal for any row whose runId starts with 'ui:' — which is exactly what approvalExecutionId returns for an owner principal.
  3. PRECEDENT for the fix already exists: webmcp.use-tool carries a bespoke resolverDocumentId carve-out (service-worker.js:4941-4953) that binds a card to an originating document and lets an extension principal resolve exactly that row. The harness case is the same shape with a different action set.
  4. The six actions are ALREADY in DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS (owner-approval.js:65-70), so createPendingApproval accepts them — no change needed there.

Also correcting item (c) in the description: it says there is no route to resolve a ui: row, only to list them. There IS a resolve route ('approval.resolve', service-worker.js:~8488) — what blocks a ui: row is mayResolveApproval's rule, not a missing route.

COORD'S DESIGN DECISION (seq1619), recorded so it is not mistaken for the implementer's: shape (b). Card mounts in the active task conversation container where the task was entered, with Approve/Deny. Policy default stays 'ask' with 'never' as the strict opt-out; no third state for now. Coord asked for it to be flagged to Paul in the report rather than treated as settled — the bead's 'the decision is the owner's' line stands, and this is coord's sequencing call with Paul's confirmation still owed.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED AND PUSHED — `fix/4lc0-cas-rewriter-vs-readers` @ `ab684f65`. The bead's open question is answered, and the answer was a module-import side effect.

IDENTIFIED (it was NOT a spawn): `tests/tool-descriptions.test.ts` rewrites `extension/wasm/cas/`. It imports the generator for one constant:
  `import { AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS } from "../scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs";`
and **the import RUNS it** — the generator's work is at module top level (WASM_OUT rm/mkdir at :394-398, the loops at :230/:236/:247/:318, the write path at :482) and its `isMain` flag (:34) gates only the final `process.exit(0)`. So a *reader* of a constant regenerates 38 shipped files.
HOW IT WAS FOUND: the sweep the bead asked for — run each candidate ALONE and fingerprint the CAS dir by per-file mtime. It was one of 19 candidates, and the only one whose fingerprint moved (18 clean). Two candidates initially "failed" alone with no dist built; after `npm run build:production` the sweep was decisive.

THE FALSIFICATION PAIR (driving the partition's phases with a fingerprint watcher, `/tmp/4lc0-demo.sh`):
| | serial phase | CAS changed DURING parallel | samples seeing it |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (main's partition) | none | **yes** (`c5c28e…`→`9a7b5e…`) | **3** |
| post-fix | `tool-descriptions` | no | **0** |
Pre-fix, gzip-preview did not red in *my* window (the rewrite takes ~15 ms and gzip-preview's reads missed it) — which is exactly why the *mechanism* had to be made deterministic rather than chased run to run. The bead's own NotFound came from the same window.

FIX (two parts; either alone is insufficient):
1. `SERIAL_REASONS` names `tests/tool-descriptions.test.ts` with the measured reason — the established mechanism, ordering the rewriter before its readers.
2. The hazard scan learns the shape that let it join the parallel phase: `IMPORT_BUILD_RE` → class "imports build.mjs or the bundled-tool generator (module side effects)", equal to spawning one. Without this, a future importer joins the parallel phase silently: the guard is structurally blind to it.

ACCEPTANCE (the bead asked for 10 consecutive subset runs): **10/10 green**, 0 CAS changes during the parallel phase in every run, 0 NotFound, 0 FAILED, writer serial in every run.

MUTANTS: **M1** declaration removed → guard test **RED** ("build-artifact hazard(s) would run in the PARALLEL phase — add each to SERIAL_REASONS … or to EXEMPTIONS with a proof of parallel-safety"); **M2** declaration AND scan class removed (= main's state) → guard **GREEN**, i.e. blind — that is the blind spot the scan change closes.

GATES: `npm run test:changed` 150 passed / 0 failed; `npm test` serial phase **18 files** GREEN in 192 s (was 17), parallel phase **477 files** GREEN in 59 s (was 478), 4459 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. The phase counts moved exactly as intended: the rewriter left the parallel phase.

ROOT CAUSE LEFT STANDING: importing a generator should not rewrite the tree. Filed as **`chrome-agent-platform-i1i9`** (P3, discovered-from this bead) with the measurement and the reviewable shapes (work behind `isMain`, or constants moved to a pure module — explicitly NOT a 900-line mechanical indent). This bead's fix contains the hazard by ordering and detection; i1i9 removes it.

title: The journey gate's scripted cookie probe never starts its run (0 of 5 provider requests, phase 'no durable run record') — the named cause of the 132/370 abort
description:
FOUND BY the 9t1p measurement (the first correctly-classified run of the journey gate): the scripted cookie probe's run never enqueues, so the gate aborts at 132/370 on any box.

EVIDENCE (scratch/journey-measure-9t1p = current main + cap-9t1p-eval-timeout @ 5270deab; log /tmp/jm-journeys.log): exit 1 (product red, NOT 75) after `chrome journeys: 132/370 passed`, with the fixed runner's own report:
  journey failure: scripted probe "check which cookie tools exist": the scripted provider received 0 of 5 requests after 136s and the run reached phase no durable run record
and the box measured idle at the time: `quiet-window: box quiet after 6044 ms — load1=6.06 load/core=0.19 heavy-builders=5 active=0[esbuild]`.

WHY IT MATTERS: the run phase is "no durable run record" — the agent.run never enqueued, the provider was never called (0 of 5), and the probe waited its full 136 s before reporting. The NEXT awaited evaluate (an in-page chrome.runtime.sendMessage round trip, e.g. thread.list) then never settled, which is what surfaced as `cdp timeout: Runtime.evaluate (targetId=unavailable)` and was misread as fleet load. So the two defects are stacked: this one (the run not starting) is the cause; the unanswered round trip is the symptom; the misclassification was the third layer, now fixed.

REPRO: run `npm run test:chrome` on a tree carrying 5270deab with the box idle — the gate opens (it did: load/core 0.19), reaches ~132/370, and exits 1 with the probe report above. Previously the same run took 7m29s in a different tree and 8m here before this point, so it is not a timing race at this level; it is the run never starting.

ACCEPTANCE: the scripted cookie probe's run ENQUEUES. A durable run record exists for it, the provider receives the 5 requests it expects (search_tools ×4 + text), and the journey gate can pass the keyless/cookie block on an idle box. The check that fails today is the probe's own shortfall assertion, so a fix must make it pass WITHOUT weakening that assertion or the "no durable run record" phase reporting.

SCOPE NOTE: the probe, its task text and the block it belongs to are the keyless/cookie-tools work whose orbiting beads (gsyp, xqhz) closed — see chrome-agent-platform-35o1 and the owner-of-record bead 76qp.
