title: evalIn/evl swallow page-side exceptions: the shared CDP evaluate helper behind chrome-journeys (and a11y-audit before it) returns undefined for a throw, so a missing element reads as a product defect
description:
THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS, and the first two are what make this worth filing rather than noting.

The shape: a harness helper wraps Runtime.evaluate, returns the value, and never inspects exceptionDetails. A page-side throw therefore becomes undefined, the harness continues, and whatever assertion consumes the undefined reports a PRODUCT failure instead of an instrument failure.

INSTANCE 1 — FIXED (bead 4vfj, landed on main @ 5d51debf). scripts/a11y-audit.ts's local evl() did `return r?.result?.value`. Its own guard, `if (!t) throw new Error('no composer textarea')`, had been swallowed for the guard's whole life; four combobox checks then read ARIA attributes off a null element with ?. and reported {} — so a GATE inside test:all was red on main and the red looked like a broken WAI-ARIA contract. Repaired: evl surfaces the exception, the required elements throw, and the gate measures 40 passed / 0 failed (was 36 / 4).

INSTANCE 2 — FIXED (bead cwy2, on main @ 983706df). scripts/sidebar-parity.ts's evaluate() DID inspect exceptionDetails, but the probe itself read `.getBoundingClientRect()` off a null element, so the run died as an uncaught TypeError naming no selector and skipping all 20 checks. Repaired: a missing required control is a recorded, named check plus an abort that names the selector, and an aborted run still prints its summary.

INSTANCE 3 — OPEN, and it is the shared helper behind the strongest gate. scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:318-329:

    async function evalIn(cdp, session, expression) {
      const r = await withTimeout(cdp.send("Runtime.evaluate",
        { expression, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true }, session), 15000, "evalIn");
      return r?.result?.result?.value;
    }

No exceptionDetails. Every one of the suite's ~370 checks that reads the page through evalIn inherits the swallow. Also check the sibling helpers before fixing: boxOf (:367), clickSel (:394), typeInto (:445) all route through evalIn, and scripts/security-suite.ts's cdp.eval path plus its clickAt (:194-200, which does `.catch(() => null)`) are the same shape in a different file — clickAt turning a throw into `false` is precisely how the security gate's `composer:false` presented as a product state until the receipt was read.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST TIDINESS: tonight two gates inside test:all were red on main and in BOTH cases the red was a missing element reporting itself as a product defect — once through a swallowed exception, once through an exit-124 timeout that our own canon told lanes to read as environmental. The swallow is what converts an instrument defect into a product accusation, and a product accusation sends the next lane to debug working code.

FIX SHAPE:
1. evalIn inspects exceptionDetails and throws with the page-side description, exactly as the a11y-audit repair now does. One place, ~4 lines.
2. But it must NOT be done blind: surfacing throws across ~370 checks will convert every latent swallowed throw into a visible failure at once. That is the point, and it is also why the change needs a QUIET-WINDOW drive of the whole suite before it lands — the suite is 370 sequential CDP round-trips, its registry entry records 370/370 only in an uninterrupted quiet window, and a run under load produces a verdict that means nothing (bead eo4d.1). Budget for a red run that names a dozen latent instrument defects, and treat each as a finding rather than as a regression.
3. Where a caller genuinely wants tolerance, make it explicit at the call site (`.catch(() => null)` with a comment saying why), never implicit in the helper.
4. The same pass should give the two multi-slash sites' pattern a home: an absent required element returns a NAMED diagnostic in the payload ({error: "composer input not found: <selector>"}), which works even while the helper swallows, and is what chrome-agent-platform-4vfj's latest branch does at :2699 and :2736.

ACCEPTANCE: evalIn surfaces a page-side exception with the description; npm run test:chrome driven in a quiet window with the verdict reported by count (n/370) and any newly-surfaced failure listed by check name and classified as instrument or product; no check silently downgraded to keep the count.

NOT MEASURED: I have not run test:chrome under this change or any other tonight — the box was not quiet (38 heavy build processes against CAP_QUIET_MAX_COMPILERS=1; bead dnop says that count is inflated by name-only matches on parked esbuild services). Everything above about instances 1 and 2 is measured with transcripts; everything about instance 3's blast radius is read from source and labelled as such.

VERDICT: PASS on the code and its tests, with ONE LANDING CONDITION and two non-blocking findings. Full report sent to coord and cap-merger-gemini; this is the record copy. Every claim below was re-driven in an isolated worktree at /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/review-0lb4, not read from the candidate comment. Note the reviewer filed this bead, so it was reviewed against the acceptance written here rather than leniently.

VERIFIED CORRECT:
- evalIn inspects r?.result?.exceptionDetails and throws with exception?.description ?? text ?? "evaluate threw"; await main() became if (import.meta.main) await main() so the helper is importable without running the suite.
- ALL FIVE SIBLING GUARDS USE THE CORRECT PATH FOR THEIR OWN send SHAPE, checked individually because a wrong path is a silently dead guard: capability-lifecycle resolves m.result (:87) so r?.exceptionDetails is right; perf-leak-trace unwraps .result (:49) so r?.exceptionDetails is right; agent-provider-picker resolves the FULL message (req.resolve(m), :552) so r?.result?.exceptionDetails is right; read-page-host-grant-acceptance (:132) and tool-call-evidence (:117) call cdp.send directly which resolves {result}, so r?.result?.exceptionDetails is right. Copying one shape across all five would have produced dead guards that the source pin still passed.
- FALSIFICATION REPRODUCED BY THE REVIEWER: mutating the guard to `if (false && r?.result?.exceptionDetails)` gives 1 passed / 3 failed — source pin plus both behavioral exception tests red, with the clean-evaluation CONTROL staying green, so the mutant did not red the file by breaking everything. (A first mutant that deleted the whole block was killed only at TYPE level, which proves nothing about behavior; it was redone preserving types.)
- NO REGRESSION to the adjacent pin: the pre-existing tests/cdp-eval-page-exception-honesty.test.ts (bead mee3, guarding openCdp().eval()) is still 4/4 green alongside the new file's 4/4. The two filenames are confusably similar but cover different helpers — not duplication.
- GATES AT 5f650619, run by the reviewer: npm test exit 0 — serial phase 17 files GREEN 317s + parallel 479 GREEN 106s, 496 files total, zero failures, all four new tests verified BY NAME inside the suite; build:production rc=0; review worktree clean with the mutant fully reverted.

LANDING CONDITION — the acceptance-required drive has NOT happened and the reviewer could not perform it either. This bead's acceptance requires "test:chrome driven in a quiet window with the verdict reported by count (n/370) and any newly-surfaced failure listed by check name and classified as instrument or product". The candidate comment reports code, tests and falsification but no test:chrome run. The reviewer measured the box rather than forecasting an exit code: load/core 0.812 (1m) / 1.008 (5m) / 1.085 (15m) against the 0.35 threshold, 7 heavy builders — the gate would refuse. This matters because the bead's own premise is that ~370 checks read the page through this helper and it WARNED that surfacing throws "will convert every latent swallowed throw into a visible failure at once… budget for a red run that names a dozen latent instrument defects". That prediction is unmeasured, and test:chrome is a gate inside test:all. LAND ONLY AFTER a quiet-window drive reports n/370 and classifies each newly-surfaced failure as instrument or product; landing first is a legitimate desk call but should be made knowingly.

FINDING 1 (non-blocking, concrete cost): @ts-nocheck is NEW on scripts/chrome-journeys.ts — absent at d31158b0, present at 5f650619. Measured: deno check on that file went from 627 errors to exit 0. Presumably added so the new test could import evalIn without inheriting that baseline, which is understandable, but it permanently disables the DIFFERENTIAL instrument on the strongest gate's 9000-line harness — and that instrument caught a real defect on 2026-09-23 (a missing composerSend import, 2 fresh TS2304) that NO test caught. Alternative that keeps both: extract evalIn into scripts/lib/cdp-eval.ts (small, typed, importable) as the repo already does for quiet-window.ts and chrome-launch.ts, then drop @ts-nocheck. Not a blocker because deno check on this file was never a gate (AGENTS.md documents it as differential-only), but the loss is real.

FINDING 2 (non-blocking): the five siblings are covered by a SOURCE PIN only ("0lb4 source pins: chrome-journeys and sibling evaluate helpers inspect exceptionDetails"). A substring pin cannot distinguish r?.exceptionDetails from r?.result?.exceptionDetails — exactly the difference between a live guard and a dead one — and only chrome-journeys' evalIn has behavioral coverage via the mock CDP WebSocket. A future change to any sibling's send shape, or a guard copied between files, would silently produce a dead guard the pin still passes. Fix shape: one behavioral test per resolve shape (there are only three — m.result, m, and {result}), or an assertion tying each guard's path to its sender's shape.

No product code is touched: all six changed files are harnesses plus the new test.

title: chrome-journeys quiet-window gate can be held closed by fleet build concurrency alone — the two conditions fail independently
description:
Found taking the journey leg for chrome-agent-platform-muc. The gate refuses (exit 75, EX_TEMPFAIL) unless BOTH conditions hold, SUSTAINED 3x2s: load1/core <= 0.35 (CAP_QUIET_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE) AND heavy compilers <= 1 (CAP_QUIET_MAX_COMPILERS), where heavy = rustc/cargo/cc1/ld/esbuild/ninja/make/wasm-opt/magick/ffmpeg. It waits CAP_QUIET_WAIT_MS (10 min) then refuses with an ENVIRONMENT: line and CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL.

TWO MEASURED REFUSALS, TWO DIFFERENT MECHANISMS — this is the finding, not the count:
1. 23:07-ish run: load1=9.09 (0.28/core) AND heavy-builders=4[esbuild] — both conditions failed.
2. 23:07:48 → 23:17:50 run (waited 601,839 ms): load1=5.70 (load/core 0.178) — LOAD WAS SATISFIED FOR THE WHOLE WINDOW — and heavy-builders=4[esbuild] kept it closed on the second condition alone. CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL {"at":1790115470233,"load1":5.7,"load5":9.9,"load15":13.56,"cores":32,"loadPerCore":0.178125,"compilers":4,"compilerNames":["esbuild"],"measurable":true}.
A third lane reproduced the refusal independently on the same evening. Logs: /tmp/muc-journeys.log and /tmp/muc-journeys2.log (lane machine), ~/cap-evidence for the retained copies.

WHY IT MATTERS: the obstacle is FLEET BUILD CONCURRENCY, not the machine and not any one branch. Any lane's esbuild bundle rebuild (a production build takes ~10s, and several lanes build all evening) can hold the journey gate closed for its whole 10-minute window, so the gate can be un-takeable while the fleet is working even on an idle machine. The reviewer hit the same wall on an unrelated branch, so this blocks landing, not one candidate.

WHAT A LANE MUST NOT DO (recorded so it is not rediscovered as a 'fix'): never kill, renice or otherwise interfere with another lane's processes to manufacture a quiet window — a lane that kills a peer's build to unblock its own test trades a real result for a convenient one and the peer only sees a failed build. Also do not raise CAP_QUIET_MAX_COMPILERS in a lane: running the journey under four builders tests a machine nobody ships on, and a green produced under conditions the declaration says are invalid is the defect class this repo spent the day cataloguing from the other direction.

OPTIONS (a policy call for the owner, per coord 2026-09-22): (a) serialise the journey and KAT legs across the fleet through a declared slot instead of competing for an emergent one; (b) raise the compiler cap deliberately and accept what such a run measures; (c) accept that the gate cannot be taken during fleet activity and schedule it for a quiet window — which may mean this leg never runs while the fleet is busy, and that is a real answer. Until it is decided, lanes sit on the window with a bound.

ACCEPTANCE for closing this bead: one of the three options is chosen and recorded with its rationale, and the chosen mechanism is verifiable — e.g. a declared slot the journey leg can actually acquire while other lanes build, or a stated schedule, or a documented threshold change with what it now proves. Evidence of the fix working: a journey run that STARTS (no exit 75) while at least one other build is in progress, or a recorded decision that says plainly this gate only runs on an idle fleet.

Related: chrome-agent-platform-muc (the candidate waiting on this leg), chrome-agent-platform-mkax/canon (the three-verdict rule and the load-sensitivity contract).
close_reason: Landed on origin/main @ 61d2152a (v0.3.457). Quiet-window gate now counts actively compiling processes via CPU advance sampling rather than process names, preventing parked build daemons from keeping gates closed; includes dynamic compiler burner calibration. Full two-phase suite green (16 serial + 474 parallel = 490 files, 4425 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, wall 191s).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND WHILE HOLDING THE WINDOW — and it is not fleet build concurrency. The gate counts a PARKED esbuild SERVICE DAEMON as a build.

MEASURED (holding the window for muc, ~/cap-evidence/muc/journey-window.log, sampled every 60s): machines went fully idle — load1 1.79-2.70, load/core 0.056-0.084 — while heavy=3[esbuild] persisted for 17+ consecutive samples, so builders_ok stayed 0 and the gate could never open. A 10-second CPU sample proves the three processes are NOT compiling: their accumulated CPU time did not move at all (0:41, 1:05, 0:33 across multi-day lifetimes).

The three, with ages and owners:
- pid 3569751, age 1d14h48m, parent `node ./node_modules/.bin/vite --host --port 5173`
- pid 1285365, age 2d00h34m, parent `isocan serve --foreground`
- pid 1438531, age 3d02h53m, parent `vite --port 5174 --strictPort --host`
All three are `.../@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild --service=0.28.2 --ping` — the long-lived esbuild SERVICE that Vite keeps open for its dev server. None is in this lane's tree, none is building anything, and none will exit on its own.

WHY: scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts:214-217 reads /proc/<pid>/comm and matches HEAVY_PROCESS_NAMES (line 44-47) — a NAME-ONLY match. It cannot distinguish an active compiler from a parked service that happens to share the binary name. The file's own comment (line 42) states the intent: a heavy process is one that 'starves CDP'. A daemon with flat CPU starves nothing, yet it holds the gate closed forever. The rule already knows how to exclude things that do not starve the browser (browsers and test workers are excluded deliberately) — a parked esbuild service belongs in that class.

CONSEQUENCE (supersedes the framing in the description): this is NOT 'the fleet is building so the journey cannot run'. While any lane leaves a Vite/dev-server esbuild service running — and the ones measured had been up for ONE TO THREE DAYS — the journey gate is permanently un-takeable on an idle machine, and waiting cannot help. Two independent lanes' refusals and both of mine are explained by one mechanism. It also means the load condition was never the blocker in the last two refusals: load_ok held; builders_ok never did.

OPTION (d), now the cheapest and most honest fix, to sit beside the policy options already recorded: count ACTIVE compilation rather than process-name presence — e.g. only count a HEAVY_PROCESS_NAMES process whose /proc/<pid>/stat CPU time advanced since the previous sample, or exclude `--service`/`--ping` esbuild servers the way browsers and test workers are excluded. Either keeps the declaration's intent intact (a real build still blocks the gate) and removes a blocker that is not doing any work. A lane must NOT do this unilaterally: it changes what a load-sensitive verdict means, so it needs the same policy decision as the other three options, with a mutant proving a genuinely compiling process still holds the gate closed (otherwise the fix would let the journey run under a real build — the exact condition the declaration exists to exclude).

EVIDENCE: ~/cap-evidence/muc/journey-window.log (full 60s series with load and builder counts), /tmp/muc-journeys.log and /tmp/muc-journeys2.log (the two gate refusals, exit 75, with CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL payloads).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — candidate pushed: fix/dnop-quiet-window-active-builds @ a2226ccd05015f5c2b1a4461236d627c065ef331 (remote verified). NOT landed; landing needs a verdict from someone who is not me.

CHOICE, stated as coord required: ACTIVITY, not names. The threshold counts name-matched processes whose accumulated CPU (utime+stime) advanced since the previous sample, or which were never seen before (fail closed — a build already running when the gate starts must still block it). A pid whose /proc/<pid>/stat starttime changed is a different process and counts active for the same reason. I deliberately did NOT add an esbuild '--service/--ping' special case: the activity rule is more faithful to the file's own intent and covers every parked compiler (a parked tsc/make/magick watch), while a name exclusion would fix exactly one binary. Name matches stay as evidence and the environment line now reports both: 'heavy-builders=4 active=0[esbuild]'. A sample with no activity information (hand-built/older caller) falls back to the name match — an unknown is never read as quiet.

LIVE PROOF, on the real box with the three parked daemons still running:
1. the gate WAITED while a real compile was active: 'quiet-window: waiting for a quiet box (bound 600000 ms) — active heavy-builders 4 > 1 (named: esbuild; compiling: esbuild)';
2. then it OPENED: 'quiet-window: box quiet after 10068 ms — load1=4.06 load5=4.86 cores=32 load/core=0.13 heavy-builders=4 active=0[esbuild]'.
Before this change the same box could never emit that second line. #1 is also the mutant coord asked for, live: with four esbuild named matches present, the moment one was genuinely compiling the gate still refused.

MUTANTS, both directions:
- a genuinely compiling process still holds the gate shut — the end-to-end test that used to copy /bin/sleep to rustc/esbuild/cargo (name-only load, i.e. the defect's own shape) now runs REAL esbuild compiles back to back and asserts exit 75 + CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL with activeCompilers >= 1;
- a parked daemon does NOT — the same test file drives the REAL sampler twice and asserts this test's own compiling pid is active via CPU advance while this test's own /bin/sleep-named pids are not. Every assertion is scoped to pids the test created, so another lane's build can neither pass nor fail it (p15i);
- pure-rule tests: advancing CPU → active, flat → idle, unseen pid → active, reused pid → active; and the /proc/<pid>/stat parse survives a comm with spaces and parentheses (a misparse there is the same defect in the arithmetic).

GATES, phases named: npm test at this tip — 16 serial (build/artifact) + 472 parallel files, 488 total, 4412 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 205s (serial 164s, parallel 40s). The quiet-window file itself: 18 passed / 0 failed.

CARRIED FINDING from the same run (recorded here because it is the next blocker, not this bead): with the gate fixed, chrome-journeys STARTED and reached 132/370 before aborting on 'cdp evaluate exceeded the budget under fleet load' — the qk7p environmental class, at load/core 0.13. So the quiet-window condition is necessary but was NOT sufficient for a full 370-check run under fleet load: the box measured quiet by this gate's predicate and the CDP cliff still fired ~8 minutes in. That strengthens the case for option (a) (serialise journey/KAT legs across the fleet through a declared slot) rather than for more threshold tuning.

VERSION NOTE for the merger: the post-commit hook bumped this branch to 0.3.454 — the number the merger published for muc. Renumbering on landing is the merger's, per coord; flagging so it is not a surprise.

Related: chrome-agent-platform-muc (its journey leg is what exposed this), chrome-agent-platform-qk7p (the CDP budget verdict), chrome-agent-platform-mkax (the three-verdict contract).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
REVISE ADDRESSED — new candidate on the same branch: fix/dnop-quiet-window-active-builds @ 7efc78bd630889a93d3e149add181c68a514046d (remote verified; the previous tip a2226ccd is superseded). The sampler fix is untouched; only the two tests that prove it changed.

WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND IS ACCEPTED AS STATED: the mechanism was confirmed in source (activity not names, fail-closed on unseen processes, older callers falling back to the name count), and the two tests that PROVE it were measuring the machine as well as the code. A test whose result moves with the ambient daemon count or the box's compile speed is not portable, and the box is not part of the branch.

THE FIX, BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY TUNING:
- calibratedBurner(dir, targetMs) measures a real compile on THIS box and scales the synthetic input until ONE compile outlasts the window the test needs; startCalibratedCompiler starts exactly one such process. The old fixed ~35 MB input was ~1.7 s here — and short enough on a faster box that the compile had already exited before the second sample (sampler test) or that a quiet gap opened BETWEEN two compiles (journey-gate test). Both tests now ASSERT the calibration covered the window (compileMs >= targetMs), so a box too fast to be covered fails loudly naming that reason instead of flaking.
- The sampler test asserts only about the pid IT started (the parked half already did) and its name-match assertions are LOWER BOUNDS over what the test created, never an exact count of the box.
- The journey-gate test keeps ambient parked daemons deliberately — the property is that a genuinely COMPILING process holds the gate whatever else the box runs — and with a calibrated burner that no longer depends on the box's speed.
- Both tests carry comments explaining the calibration and the pid-scoping, because the obvious simplification reintroduces a test that only passes at home.

PORTABILITY EVIDENCE (two ambient conditions, same result; the inputs no longer include the ambient count):
- 10 parked esbuild-named + 6 rustc-named idle processes (fixtures this session started): 18 passed / 0 failed, 15 s.
- after removing them (4 ambient esbuild, 0 rustc): 18 passed / 0 failed, 15 s.
npm test at the tip, phases named: 16 serial (build/artifact) + 473 parallel files, 489 total, 4422 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 202s.

HONEST LIMIT OF THIS REPAIR, so a re-review can judge it: I could NOT reproduce the reviewer's failure on this box, even with ~10 parked daemons and a completed /proc walk (a temporary truncation diagnostic never fired). So the calibration targets the most plausible mechanism — box speed — rather than a reproduced trace. If the two tests still red on the reviewer's box, their exact failure output is the next input and I will take it as the mechanism evidence rather than guessing again.

ALSO FILED from this investigation: chrome-agent-platform-1io9 — a TRUNCATED /proc walk in the sampler reports zero builders (i.e. a quiet box), the same reading defect one level down. Out of scope here on purpose: that is a behaviour change to the sampler and needs its own review.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE, one sentence (coord, 2026-09-23, to go on the beads that own these tests): **the test assumed the fleet's own gate slot was free.** Two tests about contention, written without accounting for the contention the fleet creates by existing — one queued behind a real gate (its 7m29s duration was the tell: the gate it spawns takes the fleet-wide slot BEFORE it measures, so it waited behind another lane's journey gate until its own burners had exited, and the refusal then came from the box's load with activeCompilers 0), and the other held the real slot to prove a refusal while held, so a real gate made the TEST's own hold fail ("held by chrome-journeys (pid 3128320)").

This is the same defect as voicebox's suite failing under its own concurrency, in a different repository, found the same way: a test whose SUBJECT is contention must not create contention to test it — a private slot path removes the assumption in both cases. Fixed and verified in chrome-agent-platform-zeew (branch fix/zeew-hermetic-tests @ 2a302db2), with both mutants RED under conditions deliberately worse than the failing run (a live foreign holder on the real slot, load1 23.19).

title: Curated agent templates suggest BACKGROUND recipes as skills, so the create dialog can only check part of the suggestion list
description:
Found while repairing scripts/kat-agent-templates.ts (chrome-agent-platform-za08) on the loaded extension.

Observed, measured in a real browser (fresh profile, create dialog): AgentTemplates' 'chief-of-staff' entry suggests five skills — daily-summary, weekly-digest, tab-hygiene, link-collector, meeting-prep — and the dialog checks exactly TWO rows. The other three suggest nothing and are silently absent from the selection.

Mechanism (source, not inference): the skills section can only CHECK a suggested id whose row exists in the profile's skill catalog (lib/agent-skill-rows.js checkTemplate → lib/recipes.js templateSkillMatches over the rows built from skill.list). In extension/lib/recipes.js those three ids are mode: BACKGROUND, and background recipes are scheduled templates — they are not rows in skill.list (measured: skill.list returned 34 entries; tab-hygiene and link-collector matched, the other three have no row). Result: a curated template advertises suggestions the owner cannot select, and the create dialog shows '2 selected' where the template's own data says five.

Why it matters: the template's suggested skills are a product promise (a starting point the owner can accept or edit). Three fifths of it silently does nothing, which is the same shape as the day's other defects — the UI reports success for a thing that did not happen.

Acceptance for done: either (a) the curated templates' suggested skills reference ids that exist as selectable skills, or (b) the create dialog renders a suggested-but-unavailable skill honestly (shown as unavailable with the reason, never silently missing), or (c) the template data and the claim are reconciled deliberately and documented. Whichever is chosen, a check in scripts/kat-agent-templates.ts must fail if a curated template suggests an id with no selectable row — do NOT weaken the existing mechanism check, which today asserts exactly the suggestions whose row exists are checked.

Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/za08-run6.log (NOTE line prints suggested/checkable/checked); the fixture's NOTE on every run reports the three lists. Related: chrome-agent-platform-za08 (the fixture repair that exposed it), chrome-agent-platform-l0r (recipes→skills rename, the same recipes/skills split).
close_reason: Landed on origin/main as v0.3.471 at commit 97a4f4261bdc0f72e9cef2d650b925ac87259eca. Unavailable template skill suggestions disclosed in agent config dialog; countLabel single-sourced; kat-agent-templates 43/43 passed in real browser.

comments.text:
LANDED (per coord's ruling, implemented as a DISCLOSURE): feat/xiln-unavailable-suggestions @ 113902bddb4b6e8a1fb5f793aea485343637ef0c (remote verified), version 0.3.466. npm test at the tip: 16 serial + 476 parallel, 492 files, 4445 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 211 s; check:gallery green; worktree clean after the build.

WHAT: extension/lib/agent-skill-rows.js (the shared skills-section builder) now computes which of a template's suggested ids have NO row in this profile, with the SAME matcher the checkboxes use (templateSkillMatches — so the disclosure and the checks can never disagree about what exists), renders them into an optional unavailableHost ("Suggested by this template, not available in this profile: <ids>"), adds "· N suggested but unavailable" to the count copy, exposes unavailableSuggestions() as evidence, clears on uncheckTemplate, and establishes the host's hidden state itself rather than trusting the caller. The dialog (extension/ntp/ntp.js) mounts that host as a role="status" line under the skills list.

THE DATA PROBLEM IS NOT FIXED, and the bead says so in those words: the curated templates still name BACKGROUND recipes (daily-summary, weekly-digest, meeting-prep for chief-of-staff) that are not skills in the catalogue, so those suggestions still cannot be checked. Whether a template should suggest them at all is a data decision, unchanged here. Disclosure ≠ repair, and the two claims are kept apart.

TEST: tests/skill-catalog.test.ts (driving the real render path through the file's existing fake DOM) — two checkable skills + the chief-of-staff suggestion list → exactly two checked, the other three NAMED, count "3 suggested but unavailable"; an all-available template discloses nothing and adds no suffix; uncheckTemplate clears it. title: [bug] durable-root.test.ts mutates shared process env with /proc/cap-chp-impossible, racing dist-staleness-note in parallel suite
description: tests/durable-root.test.ts:69 sets CAP_DURABLE_ROOT=/proc/cap-chp-impossible as a process-global during its run. Because deno test --parallel runs test modules in a shared process, durableRoot() reads process.env live and causes racing tests (such as dist-staleness-note.test.ts) to fail with ENOENT: mkdir '/proc/cap-chp-impossible/...'. Reproducible ~1-in-3 running those two files in parallel. Isolate durable-root test env or restore cleanly with a lock/override.

title: test:changed fails closed to full suite for unimported scripts/** harnesses and unmapped bookkeeping JSON
description:
Root cause & measured behavior (reconciled across author measurements and independent review at 935ea3c2):

1. UNIMPORTED HARNESSES: Standalone harnesses under scripts/ (e.g. sidebar-parity.ts, a11y-audit.ts) are not imported by unit tests. Because scripts/select-tests.mjs uses static reverse-import reachability, unimported harness files trigger changedWithoutCoverage() fail-closed even though tree-inspecting guards (harness-registry, scripts-exit-codes, substring-pin-honesty, etc.) cover them. Directly imported harness libraries (like composer-target.ts) are covered.
2. UNMAPPED BOOKKEEPING JSON: The post-commit version hook bumps package.json, package-lock.json, and extension/manifest.json. These JSON files have no static importers in the reverse graph and are not covered by CONTENT_EXT_RE, triggering fail-closed on committed trees. (extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js is covered; the three JSON configs are not).
3. CONCURRENT TIP ADVANCE: changedFiles() compares against origin/main directly rather than the merge-base, so when origin/main advances, foreign landed files enter the working diff and contribute to fail-closed.

Acceptance:
1. Map unimported scripts/** harnesses to their inspecting guard suite (the dqc1 cross-cutting list) plus core instead of failing closed to 488 files.
2. Map version-only bookkeeping JSON diffs to the serial build/bootstrap/inventory suite.
3. Scope changedFiles() to merge-base so concurrent main landings do not pollute the changed set.
4. Fail-closed diagnostic message explicitly names which file/mechanism triggered the full suite fallback.

Those paths must resolve as covered (reachableTestFrom finds an importer, or CONTENT_EXT_RE/an earlier skip applies); I have not read which, and I am not going to assert a mechanism I did not verify twice.

WHAT BOTH MEASUREMENTS ACTUALLY AGREE ON:
- Mechanism 3 is the trigger, confirmed twice. Run 1 listed scripts/sidebar-parity.ts; run 2 listed scripts/a11y-audit.ts and NOTHING else. A harness under scripts/ is not imported by any unit test, so it can never be subset-covered, and scripts/** is what most lanes edit. Run 2 also proves the fix shape: scripts/lib/composer-target.ts, which a new test DOES import, was not listed — a harness lib with a test is subset-eligible.
- Mechanism 2 confirmed once, directly. Run 1 listed cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts, which was bead cgei's landing and not my edit (coord confirmed filing it). changedFiles() runs  against the WORKING TREE, so when the base is behind the tip another lane's files enter your changed set. That instability is worth its own look: either the classification depends on the base in a way nobody intends, or run 1's tree state (two commits of version bumps plus a rebuild) put those files in a state run 2 did not. Labelled a hypothesis, not a finding.

RESTATED ACCEPTANCE, narrowed to what is measured: a scripts/** change with a tree-inspecting guard that covers it (the dqc1 list: harness-registry, scripts-exit-codes, substring-pin-honesty, durable-root, quiet-window, chrome-profile-isolation, machine-path-honesty, test-partition-guard) should select those guards plus the always-on core rather than the whole suite; the changed set should be scoped to the merge-base so another lane's landing cannot force your fail-closed; and the fail-closed message must name WHICH mechanism fired, because today 'no reachable test' reads identically for a harness nobody inspects, a config file, and a foreign landing.   run 2 (4vfj, base d0f01545 = tip):             scripts/a11y-audit.ts ONLY

My retraction of mechanism 1 was correct as a retraction of the STRONG claim ('every commit guarantees fail-closed'), but my run-2-based statement that those paths 'must resolve as covered' was too strong in the other direction: they resolve as covered SOMETIMES. For a11y-audit, sidebar-parity and constrained-width-layout, every test that so much as mentions them contains ZERO Deno.Command/spawnSync/execFileSync. 1. scripts/lib/changed-file-mapping.mjs — classifies an uncovered file and names what covers it. Version-only detection PARSES BOTH SIDES and compares flattened key paths; it never greps for lines containing "version", which is the mo2f.3 trap (that filter passes a nested dependency bump exactly as cleanly as a project bump).
2. scripts/select-tests.mjs — maps the two provable classes, scopes the changed set to the MERGE-BASE, and every fail-closed run now NAMES the file and the mechanism. Tested against the REAL manifest — version-only bump maps (true); version bump + weakened CSP does NOT (false); version bump + added 'debugger' permission does NOT (false); nested dependency bump does NOT (false).

M2 revert merge-base scoping to the moving tip → 1 red, 'uses the merge-base when git resolves one'. Both restored green.

FOURTH TRIGGER, contributed by the exe.dev VM fleet (coord, 2026-10-05 02:41Z) — not filed as a duplicate, just recorded because it is structural rather than situational.

TRIGGER: `npm run test:changed` falls closed on ANY landing tree that carries a release FOLD. Measured on a staged landing (merge onto current main + manual version fold, because this VM has no git hooks): `node scripts/select-tests.mjs --list` prints
  select-tests: FAIL CLOSED — changed file(s) with no reachable test cannot be proved covered by a subset:
    extension/manifest.json
    package-lock.json
    package.json
  Running the FULL suite (npm test) instead.
Those three files are THE FOLD, not the feature under review: a version bump touches them and none has a reachable test, so the fallback is unconditional for any folded landing.
CONSEQUENCE: the bounded per-change subset is only obtainable on an UNFOLDED feature branch — which is where the same change's reviewer did get one (22 files, 163 passed / 0 failed). By the time a landing lane has folded, `test:changed` can never give the bounded answer, and on a box where the full suite cannot complete (see chrome-agent-platform-kj9s: 19 build/artifact files, 5/19 failed, 3396s wall, budgets of 180-300s against a 656s build) that means a landing can have no test:changed evidence at all.
SUGGESTED REMEDY for nco2's owner: treat the fold's files as covered-by-construction (the fold is mechanical and its own gates are sync:changelog / check:changelog / check:changelog-order / check:vocabulary) rather than letting an unreachable-test verdict on package.json force a full suite. Then `test:changed` stays a per-change gate at landing time instead of falling closed exactly when the change is about to ship.
RELATED, ALREADY RECORDED ELSEWHERE: triggers (1) genuinely unmapped files, (2) a branch merely behind main (base defaults to current origin/main), (3) main advancing DURING the gate so a freshly rebased branch goes stale mid-run. This adds (4) the fold.

- scripts/kat-agent-delegation.ts fails 1-in-2/3 runs on this box: runs 01, 04, 07, 09, 12, 15, 18 all failed with the reviewed error class ("settling registry CAS failed", "abort-attempt record CAS failed", "terminal registry CAS failed", later "run aborted" / "the parent run is no longer durably running").

Every removal path was instrumented and silent (store.delete/compareAndDelete on any handle, store.clear, removeTracked, purgeStoreDir, durableRunMemory.clear, forgetCachedState). One SW instance throughout (boot-attached console stream never breaks; one recover-start). The loss is broader than a record: later runs read run.list -> {runs:0} and delegation admission denies with "the parent run is no longer durably running".

WHAT THE CANDIDATE DOES (the failure MODE, not the loss): a lost CAS is treated as information, not a run failure. On a settling/terminal CAS loss, re-read the STORE (bypassing the cache) and accept another writer's terminal projection, retry at the fresh revision, or — when the record is ABSENT — RE-CREATE it from the run's own outbox projection. The live-run writers (heartbeat, toolSafety) get the same invariant gated on `active`, never overwriting a record another writer took out of the live phases; purges now retire the writer. A no-movement refusal still throws (the injected-fault pins are untouched).

- settling reconcile removed -> the VANISHES-settle pin REDS alone (69/1); restored 70/0.
- terminal reconcile removed -> the vanishes-AFTER-marker pin REDS alone (69/1); restored 70/0.
- heartbeat reconcile removed -> the heartbeat-survives-vanish pin REDS alone (70/1); restored 71/0.

WHAT IS NOT MET: "demonstrate repeated clean real-browser runs". Post-fix the KAT is 2 clean of 4 (runs 25-28; loads 47-75) vs 1 of 4 pre-fix in the same session — the record-level recovery works, but the underlying loss takes the INDEX too, so run.list and child admission still break. The loss itself is unattributed and filed as chrome-agent-platform-z5ym (discovered-from this bead), with the instrumentation evidence and the ruling-out above. The KAT continues to report a product-shaped failure for an environmental storage loss; classifying that in the harness is part of z5ym's acceptance, not smuggled into this candidate.

Both failures are environmental/owned elsewhere and neither touches durable-runs.

REVIEW ASK: the recovery semantics themselves — the recreate-on-absent branch, the `active` gate, and that a purged run can never be resurrected by its own heartbeat. Then decide whether the recovery lands with z5ym open (it removes a misleading failure mode and cannot fix the loss) or is held.

build:production all rc=0; every mutant restored, tree verified clean).

VERDICT: FAIL — one blocking finding (F1). It is a missing pin, not a wrong design: the recovery paths
this change adds are genuinely proven, and the refusal that keeps them safe is the one thing nothing
tests.

WHAT I VERIFIED AS TRUE AND STRONG (this is careful work, and the finding does not diminish it):
 - 71 passed / 0 failed on tests/durable-runs.test.ts, exactly as claimed.
 - The KAT is NOT in the diff at all (git diff --name-only has no scripts/kat-agent-delegation.ts), so
   "preserve all 61 behavioural assertions" holds by construction rather than by promise.
 - THEIR OWN FALSIFICATION CLAIM REPRODUCES. I disabled the vanished-record reconcile path
   (`return await writeRecord(value, null)` -> throw) and got **70 passed / 1 failed**, the failure in
   the cejm pins. So the three new pins (VANISHES-settle, vanishes-after-marker, heartbeat-survives-
   vanish) are real, executing, and able to fail. That is the standard, met.
 - The investigation is honest in a way that matters: the mechanism was established with instrumented
   runs and ALL DIAGNOSTICS REVERTED, and the comment states plainly "I am NOT claiming the KAT flake is
   fixed" and "ACCEPTANCE PARTIALLY MET". It correctly separates the failure MODE (what this change
   fixes) from the state LOSS (which it routes to chrome-agent-platform-z5ym rather than pretending to).
 - A no-movement refusal still throws, so an injected-fault pin cannot be satisfied by the new path.

F1 (BLOCKING) — THE OWNERSHIP REFUSAL IN writeRecordWhileActive IS UNPINNED; MUTANT SURVIVES THE WHOLE
FILE. scripts -> extension/lib/durable-runs.js:489-492:
      if (fresh.revision === expectedRevision || !stillLive(fresh)) throw new Error(label);
   with the comment "A record another writer took out of the live phases (terminal, paused, cancelled)
   must NEVER be overwritten by a liveness write: the run is over, so ownership is lost."
   I removed exactly that protection — mutant M3: `if (fresh.revision === expectedRevision) throw ...`,
   i.e. a still-live check that no longer exists, so a heartbeat or toolSafety write may overwrite a
   TERMINAL, PAUSED or CANCELLED record at a fresh revision — and the suite stayed **71 passed / 0
   failed**. Nothing in tests/ names retireWriter or the resurrect property in this context.
   Why this is not cosmetic: with the check gone, an in-flight liveness write on a run the owner just
   cancelled or that another writer settled can rewrite the record back toward a live phase. That is a
   cancelled-or-finished run reappearing as running, in the subsystem that gates delegation admission
   ("the parent run is no longer durably running") and approval state. It is also the *inverse* failure
   of z5ym's loss: z5ym makes records disappear; this makes one reappear. A refusal that no test can
   observe is a refusal that will be "simplified" away by the next lane that finds it inconvenient —
   which is precisely how this repo has already been burned five times (the Test-honesty canon).
   Related, same cause: M1 — neutering retireWriter (so a terminal/purged execution is never dropped
   from `active`) also gives **71 passed / 0 failed**. The comment asserts "a purge retires the writer
   so a purged run can never be resurrected by its own heartbeat"; that guarantee is equally unobserved.
   Note the asymmetry, because it is the useful part of this review: every POSITIVE path added here is
   pinned and falsifiable, and no NEGATIVE path is. Recovery code that is tested only for working is how
   an ownership rule silently disappears later.

MINIMUM TO CLEAR F1 (cheap, no design change):
 1. A pin per refusal branch: seed a record whose phase another writer moved to terminal/cancelled, then
    attempt a heartbeat and a toolSafety write on the stale revision, and assert the write is REFUSED
    with the label error and the record's phase/revision are UNCHANGED. Prove each by deleting the
    corresponding branch and showing that test red — the same drill I ran, which currently prints 71/0.
 2. A pin for the purge-retires-writer invariant: purge or terminalise, then have the run's own heartbeat
    attempt a write, and assert no record is re-created (this is the property the comment already
    claims, so the test is really a receipt for a claim already in the source).
 3. Both are unit-level against the fake/opfs harness already in this file — neither needs the browser,
    so neither inherits the box-load problem that blocks the rest of this bead's acceptance.

STILL OUTSTANDING AFTER F1 (the author says so himself; recording it so it is not read as resolved):
acceptance asks to reproduce or identify the failed CAS (mechanism characterised, root cause of the OPFS
state loss still open and routed to z5ym) and to demonstrate repeated clean REAL-BROWSER KAT runs without
retries masking failures. I did NOT run scripts/kat-agent-delegation.ts — on a box at load 1.5-2.8 per
core a flake-fix's "N clean runs" evidence is not obtainable and would be worth nothing if claimed, so
this bead's browser-side acceptance remains unmet by me and by the candidate. Explicitly: the change is a
mode-tolerance fix, so "the flake is fixed" must not be written on this bead until repeated real-browser
runs exist.

STATE: FAIL on F1, held for the author. The recovery design is sound and its tests are real — add the two
refusal pins and this is mergeable on the code side, with the browser acceptance tracked separately
against z5ym.

title: No test executes ntp.js: source-scanning suites miss real UI regressions
description:
Systemic gap found during 7zf0 triage and review: no test in this repository executes ntp.js directly in a test environment. Over 68 test files source-scan ntp.js with Deno.readTextFile or regex matchers (e.g. task-inline-edit-and-panel.test.ts, route-focus.test.ts, agent-deletion-navigate.test.ts).

Two concrete examples of the failure mode:
1. agent-deletion-navigate.test.ts tests navigation state by re-implementing an inline simulation of the router logic rather than executing ntp.js, so ntp.js can regress while the test stays green.
2. 7zf0 regression test: when extension/ntp/ntp.js was reverted to main, 3 of 4 tests in agent-header-rename-reload.test.ts still passed because the 'behavioral' tests executed an inline simulation instead of the actual script, leaving the regex source-pin as the only failing assertion.

Demonstration: tests reading text can verify presence of tokens, but cannot falsify runtime behavior, race conditions, event ordering, or DOM state transitions in ntp.js. ntp.js needs real browser-driven harness or headless page execution tests for its core state machines and route transitions.
close_reason: Closed

title: scripts/sidebar-parity.ts crashes on main: the hub composer selectors drifted (#task-input/#run-task) and a null probe skips all 20 checks
description:
MEASURED on unmodified origin/main @ a3e35928 (worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-sidebar-parity, npm ci + deno install + build:production done):

  npm run test:sidebar
  error: Uncaught (in promise) Error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')
      at <anonymous>:1:55   (scripts/sidebar-parity.ts:81 evaluate -> :156)
  exit=1, ZERO checks run, no SIDEBAR PARITY summary line.

The registry row still reads "18/2 at the re-inventory (two sidebar parity checks red); promote once green" (scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:85). That is stale: the harness does not reach its checks at all today, so the hub's Tasks/Agents sidebar parity (expanded / collapsed / RTL / dark geometry, hover + keyboard delete, New-task focus) has NO running browser coverage.

ROOT CAUSE (measured with a read-only CDP probe on the loaded hub, ntp.html):
  agent-composer textarea#task-input -> false
  document.querySelector('#task-input') -> false
  document.querySelector('#run-task')   -> false
  #composer [data-composer-input]       -> true
  #composer [data-composer-send]        -> true
  the textarea's real id is "composer-input"
The composer renders per-instance ids (`${this.id}-input` / `${this.id}-send`) and exposes the stable hooks data-composer-input / data-composer-send for exactly this purpose (extension/shared/components.js:7035). The same drift was measured independently by the astra lane in bead chrome-agent-platform-b5q4 for cap-evidence/model-edit-still-refused-journey.ts; scripts/chrome-journeys.ts already carries a compat fallback in boxOf() (#task-input -> [data-composer-input], #run-task -> [data-composer-send]). sidebar-parity.ts never got it.

SECOND DEFECT, same class (found after the selector repair): the run then aborted with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')" at the `thread.list` probe (`.then(r=>r.threads.length)`). The dispatcher answers a throwing handler with {ok:false,error,...} (service-worker.js onMessage catch), which has no `threads` key. Reading `.length` off that is an anonymous crash that names neither the route nor the error. Sibling harnesses already defend with `?.threads?.length ?? 0`.

WHY THIS IS A CLASS, NOT A ONE-OFF: an uncaught TypeError in a probe aborts the whole harness, so every later check silently never runs and the printed output names no selector. That is the probe-null family this repo has already paid for twice (bead 4a44 "probes measure null/0 - the parity checks have never passed in a real browser run"; bead rfca "Settings browser gates assert visibility, not rendered content"). A harness that cannot see its element must record a NAMED red and say how much of it never ran.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. npm run test:sidebar reaches its checks and prints its SIDEBAR PARITY summary on current main. No uncaught TypeError.
2. The composer probes use the component's stable hooks, scoped to the hub composer (#composer [data-composer-input] / [data-composer-send]) - not the per-instance ids, and not a bare document-wide [data-composer-input] (ntp.html has a second composer, #thread-composer).
3. A missing/zero-sized required control is a recorded, named check failure AND an abort that names the selector; a non-array thread.list reply names the raw reply.
4. An aborted run still prints the summary line with the abort counted as a failure (exit non-zero) - the reader always learns how much ran.
5. Any check that is red AFTER the instrument is repaired is reported honestly as a product finding (or filed as its own bead), not quietly deleted. The harness must not be weakened to go green.
6. scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:85 reason updated to the newly measured pass/fail count (docs never drift).

GATES: the harness run itself (transcript retained), npm run test:changed, npm test once before push, tests/scripts-exit-codes.test.ts + tests/harness-registry.test.ts still green (the script keeps a failure-derived Deno.exit and exactly one registry class).

FALSIFICATION: reverting the selector to #task-input must reproduce the crash; the new named check must go red when the composer hook is renamed.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main @ 983706df (v0.3.451). Migrated sidebar-parity to [data-composer-input]/[data-composer-send] hooks; 20 checks execute (19 pass / 1 fail owned by o1y1). Full two-phase suite green (16 serial + 471 parallel = 487 files, 4404 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, wall 226s).

title: The changelog jargon filter does not cover the internal words that actually leak
description:
Measured 2026-09-22 on branch cap/mcp-harness-tools.

JARGON_RE (extension/options/changelog-filter.js, mirrored in scripts/bump-version.mjs as FILTER_JARGON_RE) is:
  /journey|KAT|assertion|CDP|harness|worktree|lane|tracker|splice/i

A changelog entry reading 'correct my own capability claim — NO pinned adapter implements client-hosted MCP' PASSED that filter and was written to CHANGELOG.md. It is first person, internal, and states no consequence for a person reading a release note. The words that leaked — 'capability claim', 'pinned adapter', 'client-hosted', 'MCP' — are none of them in the alternation, so the filter was green on a sentence no user could act on.

This is the mechanism that is supposed to catch internal vocabulary reaching a user-facing changelog, and it passed a first-person internal sentence. It was caught by a human reading the note, not by the gate.

Acceptance: the filter (or a check over it) rejects first-person engineering prose and the leaked vocabulary above, with a test that FAILS on the exact sentence quoted here. A refusal must NAME the offending word — the same defect was filed earlier for the filter's failure to name its cause.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main as v0.3.481 at commit 8defd34ea26a742df7baa2965e7979593b239369. Leaked vocabulary (capability claim, pinned adapter, client-hosted) added to JARGON_RE; FIRST_PERSON_RE added; WebMCP/MCP preserved. title: check-reachability sees files with no importer, but not exported functions with no caller
description:
Measured 2026-09-22 on branch cap/mcp-harness-tools.

scripts/check-reachability.mjs failed the build on two shipped MODULES that no entry point imports:
  lib/harness-mcp-server.js: shipped but nothing reaches it (delete it, or add it to RETAINED with a reason)
  lib/harness-tool-provider.js: shipped but nothing reaches it
That is correct and it was right to fail.

But the same guard cannot see a FUNCTION that nothing calls inside a file that IS reached. scripts/acp-bridge.ts exported isBrowserLaunchingMcpServer with a full JSDoc block and 11 passing assertions in tests/acp-bridge-mcp-isolation.test.ts, and no caller anywhere in the repository. Its comment even claimed the load-bearing half was a symbol (capMcpServerEntry) that exists nowhere in the repo and had died with a deleted module, while a comment thirty lines below described a different and incompatible safety model. Two safety models attached to a function nobody calls, and the build was green.

Same shape as today's other findings: a check that reports on the class NEXT TO the one that matters. The file-level guard makes dead modules impossible and dead exported functions invisible.

Acceptance: either extend the reachability check to report exported symbols with no importer/caller (allowing a tested exemption list with reasons), or state in docs/TEST-COUPLING-INVENTORY.md that this class is uncovered and why. Prefer the first.

title: Two latent checks that cannot fail: a once-taken non-vacuity guard reused per width, and an absent label reading as un-clipped
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/l3ts-check-strength (ac0a62d4), in cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts. Both are the same "cannot fail" class as q264/qzae/cgei, stated as LATENT because the reviewer could identify the hole at the predicate level but could NOT reach it from the driver's current probes. Not fixed by that branch.

(1) THE NON-VACUITY GUARD IS TAKEN ONCE, AT ONE WIDTH, AND REUSED FOR ALL OF THEM.
  Line 422-430 computes panelHasButtons from panelResults["300"] ONLY:
    const panelHasButtons = !panelResults["300"].error && panelResults["300"].buttons.length > 0;
    check("side panel: the harness buttons rendered", panelHasButtons, ...);
    check("...guard...", panelHasButtons && panelResults["300"].containerVisible === true &&
      panelResults["300"].buttons.every((b) => b.w > 0 && b.h > 0), ...);
  That single boolean then gates the loop at line 480 (`if (panelHasButtons) { for
  const w of PANEL_WIDTHS) ... }`), while the checks INSIDE the loop iterate
  `r.buttons` unguarded, per width.

  CONSEQUENCE: a probe returning `buttons: []` at some width w yields THREE
  vacuous passes at that width - line 485 `.every(...)` on [], line 494
  `.every(...)` on [], line 497 `.every(...)` on [] - because the guard that would
  have caught it was taken at 300px and never re-taken at w. The guard reads as
  covering the loop; it does not.

  FIX SHAPE: take the guard PER WIDTH inside the loop, on `r.buttons.length > 0`,
  rather than once outside it.

(2) AN ABSENT LABEL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN UN-CLIPPED ONE.
  Line 351: const labelClipped = label ? getComputedStyle(label).clip !== "auto" : false;
  If `.hq-label` is missing entirely, labelClipped is false. The new collapsed-rule
  check (line 494) asserts `b.labelClipped === expectClipped` with expectClipped
  = (w < 320). At 400px expectClipped is false, so a MISSING LABEL SATISFIES IT.
  It fails CLOSED at 260/300px (expectClipped true, so a missing label is RED), so
  this is SINGLE-DIRECTION ONLY: the 400px direction is satisfied by absence, the
  collapsed directions are not.

  FIX SHAPE: carry a `hasLabel` boolean in the probe and require it, so absence is
  RED in both directions rather than green in one.

ACCEPTANCE: for (1) a probe with an empty button list goes RED at every width, not
only at 300px; for (2) a chip with no .hq-label goes RED at 400px as well as at
260px. Both proofs recorded, and each shown passing when the defect is present so
the check is not itself vacuous.

EVALUATION COMPLETE (cap-gemini, 2026-09-25).
BRANCH: cap/gemini-mx1g-zod-peer, COMMIT: ac260948d (pushed to origin).
EVIDENCE: cap-evidence/mx1g-zod-peer-parity/EVIDENCE.md.
TESTS: tests/mcp-zod-peer-parity.test.ts (7 tests, all green).

FINDINGS & RECOMMENDATION: RETAIN SEPARATE PEER CONTEXTS (DO NOT UNIFY).
1. Emitted Converter Size: Despite 78 files / 108.5 KB source in zod-to-json-schema, tree-shaking in the production service worker bundle limits its emitted preminify contribution to EXACTLY 2,460 bytes. Deduplication yields negligible byte savings.
2. Silent Conversion Failure on Zod 4: zod-to-json-schema@3.25.2 only parses Zod 3 AST (_def.typeName); passed a Zod 4 schema it fails silently and emits an empty schema ({ "$schema": "..." }) with 0 properties.
3. Downstream Error Formatting Incompatibility: Zod 4 omits issue.received and issue.type; CAP's validationIssueDetail in extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js relies on issue.received and degrades to 'must be string; received undefined' under Zod 4.
4. Mixed Shape Rejection: MCP SDK objectFromShape throws 'Mixed Zod versions detected in object shape.' when Zod 3 and Zod 4 are mixed.
5. Early v4-mini Constraint Drops: zod@3.25.76/v4-mini drops minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum/description checks, whereas Zod 3 preserves them.

All gates clean: test:file (7/7 passed), test:changed (500 files, 4509 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored).

REVIEW: PASS on the decision (RETAIN, do not unify). Mergeable as an evaluation PR. Independent pass:
qwen3.8-flash fresh session, diff-against-claims; author cap-gemini (gemini) => different family.
Evidence + repro: ~/cap-evidence/mx1g-review-qwen-20260925/VERDICT.md
Worktree ~/worktrees/cap-qwen-mx1g-review-20260925 (setup all green). Findings Q1-Q4 below; Q1 filed as
chrome-agent-platform-qptq, linked discovered-from this bead.

VERIFIED (why it passes):
 1. The 7 tests are REAL executing tests, not text pins. Ran them: 7 passed / 0 failed, 955 ms. They
    build actual z3/z4 schemas, call the real zodToJsonSchema and objectFromShape (asserting the mixed
    throw both directions), register tools on a real McpServer, and run a real esbuild build to read
    metafile.outputs[].inputs[].bytesInOutput. None of the five catalogued "green asserts nothing" modes
    are present - no substring pin, no import-for-call-site, no conditional death, no swallowed catch.
 2. The dual-peer premise is real in this tree, not assumed: node_modules/.deno/zod@3.25.76 AND
    zod@4.4.3 both present, zod@4.4.3 pinned 37x in deno.lock (no ambient/network fragility), and the
    SDK's own package.json declares peerDependencies.zod "^3.25 || ^4.0". I checked this specifically
    because comparing a real version against a hypothetical one would have been the worst possible way
    for this to be green.
 3. Claim 3 maps onto CAP's real code: lazy-tool-protocol.js:610 does read issue.received, and :601/:607
    read issue.type too - so the exposure is slightly BROADER than stated, in the direction supporting
    RETAIN.
 4. Authority respected: package.json/lock/manifest deltas are only the post-commit version bump. No
    dependency added, no extension/ or shared/ source touched.
 5. THE 909-LINE .beads/issues.jsonl CHURN IS BENIGN REGENERATION, NOT AN ACCIDENTAL STAGE (the question
    coord asked). File is tracked and refreshed by this repo's own pre-commit hook; the candidate export
    is strictly fresher than base (836 ids vs 835, ZERO dropped). Spot-checked against the live DB rather
    than trusted: f3n2 (absent from base) exists and is in_progress, and wfo5's new close_reason names
    a12f887c, which IS the current origin/main tip. It sweeps other lanes' current state into the diff but
    fabricates nothing and leaks nothing private. Not a REVISE-on-hygiene case.
 6. The byte figure is deterministic: 2460 across three consecutive runs (406/441/508 ms).

Q1 (new bead qptq) THE FRAMING MISSES THE ACTIONABLE HALF OF ITS OWN NUMBER. 2,460 bytes is not a cost of
   keeping two peers - it is dead weight that ships because CAP's CLIENT-only import drags the SDK's
   SERVER-side compat module into the service worker. Traced on the installed SDK:
     mcp-client.js:29 client/index.js -> shared/protocol.js:4 -> ../server/zod-json-schema-compat.js
       -> zod-to-json-schema (78 files, 2,460 emitted bytes)
   `git grep -n 'sdk/server' -- extension/ shared/` = NO HITS, and server/mcp.js is NOT in the bundle -
   this compat module is the one server subtree that leaks. So unification is not even the lever for these
   bytes; RETAIN stands, strengthened.

Q2 (recommend fixing pre-merge) A MEASUREMENT PROMOTED TO A PERMANENT EXACT-VALUE GATE.
   assertEquals(emittedBytes, 2460) pins an exact count of a transitive third-party subtree reached through
   the whole SW import graph. Not flaky, but per the coupling canon ("if a hit is a COUNT, assume your
   change moves it") any SDK bump reds a test whose message says "exactly 2460 bytes" and explains
   nothing, and the ycez Store-SW budget lane is an obvious tripwire. Either assert a bound (~<=2.6 KB)
   and keep 2,460 as a dated figure in EVIDENCE.md, or keep the exact assert and put the mechanism +
   re-anchor procedure in the failure message.

Q3 (recorded, not blocking) THE BEAD'S FOURTH GATE IS ARGUED, NOT DRIVEN. Acceptance named remote MCP
   journeys; EVIDENCE.md 3.3 supports that by reading mcp-client.js's imports, with no journey or KAT
   exercised. Not failing on it: the recommendation is change-nothing, so a thin gate 4 cannot ship a
   defect, and the conservative default is exactly what the bead prescribes when a gate is unproven. But
   the record should stop a later lane citing mx1g as JOURNEY evidence - here it was not even "it serves",
   it was "I read the imports".

Q4 (nits) (a) the BEAD COMMENT phrases claim 3 in present tense ("degrades to 'received undefined');
   nothing degrades today - production binds bare `import { z } from "zod"` -> 3.25.76. EVIDENCE.md gets
   it right ("If Zod 4 were unified here..."). Worth correcting on the bead so nobody files a bug that does
   not exist. (b) @ts-nocheck line 1 is defensible for a cross-major suite but carries no reason on the
   line; extension/lib/mcp-client.js:1 is the in-repo precedent that does. (c) the deep
   ../node_modules/.deno/... imports are FORCED, not sloppy - the SDK exports map exposes only './server',
   so objectFromShape/isZ4Schema/toJsonSchemaCompat are unreachable by bare specifier. I checked before
   raising it. One comment line saying so prevents a future hygiene pass tidying it into a broken import.

STATE: review PASSED; safe to land. Q2/Q4a are cheap and worth folding in, but do not gate on them.

comments.text:
chrome-agent-platform-5f5u: the A/B did NOT reproduce the stall, so the fix is scoped to what WAS observed — and an integration check caught it lying

THE A/B, RUN FIRST AS THE BEAD REQUIRED ("Reproduce controlled A/B before attributing"): same real
adapter (claude-agent-acp), two arms, 60 s prompt deadline, with a DELIBERATELY INVALID key so no
secret is read or needed (cap-evidence/5f5u/ab-drill.ts):
  A_no_key:       promptAnswered=false timedOut=true callbacks=3 60002ms
  B_invalid_key:  promptAnswered=false timedOut=true callbacks=3 60001ms
IT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE DIFFERENCE — both arms stalled identically, and BOTH reported
`apiType=native baseUrl=native`, so in this harness the key never became the auth source at all. The
attribution therefore stays OPEN on the bead, and nothing here claims to fix a stall.

SO THE FIX IS JUSTIFIED BY THE WARNING THAT WAS ACTUALLY CAPTURED, not by the unreproduced story. The
adapter's own stderr says an auth source "takes precedence over your claude.ai login". Two consequences
follow whatever the stall's cause turns out to be, and both are implemented:
  1. SCOPE the overriding source out of the ADAPTER CHILD env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY by default), never
     from the host, never from disk, reversible with CAP_ACP_KEEP_API_KEY=1 — the bead is explicit:
     "Preserve host settings/credentials; do not auto-delete user API keys." There is a test asserting
     the caller's environment object is NOT mutated, and one asserting the note never echoes a value.
  2. SURFACE the adapter's precedence warning as an actionable host-side line, because a precedence
     change visible only in a child's stderr is invisible in the surface the user watches.
Both spawn sites are covered: the WebSocket bridge (which spread the host env into the child) and the
native host (which passed NO env at all, so the adapter inherited everything).

AND THE INTEGRATION CHECK CAUGHT MY OWN FIX LYING. The bridge printed "CAP scopes it out of the adapter
child", while an adapter that prints its own environment reported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: PRESENT` — the
note claimed a mechanism that was not happening, and the unit tests were green because they tested the
helper, not the wiring. Cause, MEASURED rather than assumed: Deno MERGES `env` over the parent's
environment by default, so omitting a variable does not remove it. `clearEnv: true` is what scopes a
child, and that is now asserted by a test that spawns a real child twice — PRESENT with the default,
ABSENT with clearEnv — so deleting the line reds a test instead of shipping a false claim again.

title: Bind existing CAP tools to an in-browser harness with no bridge
description: Separate owner-required zero-server stage discovered in vl6c. Native ACP CLI adapters require a host process; browser tabs cannot spawn stdio CLIs or listen as HTTP servers. Provide a callable existing lazy catalogue binding for an in-browser harness, retaining SW run identity, durable ownership, live approvals and origin isolation. No transport server prerequisite. Acceptance: entirely browser-local harness executes existing CAP tool with browser network/server disabled and denied mutation remains denied.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: cap-k3
comments.text:
Claimed by cap-k3 (an opus lane) on 2026-09-25. Worktree ~/worktrees/cap-qnd4-inbrowser-harness, branch cap/qnd4-inbrowser-harness off origin/main@a12f887c. Setup green (npm ci, deno install, build:production). Store SW bundle: 2,982,918 B of the 3,000,000 B budget, so 17,082 B headroom.

First step: thicken this bead into an implementable design before writing code. As written it is too thin to implement from. The design must answer:
1. What the harness is. For example, an ACP agent running in a worker or offscreen document and speaking ACP JSON-RPC over a MessagePort instead of stdio.
2. What drives it with "browser network/server disabled": a deterministic scripted agent for the acceptance, the on-device Prompt API, or both. If "network disabled" means all network, a harness that needs a remote model cannot pass the acceptance; the design must say which reading applies.
3. Where it binds. Default: reuse the browser.callTool route that landed in 2amt/wfo5 (owner-principal fence, approval cards) instead of adding a second tool path. Still to check: what those commits actually enforce.
4. Overlap with vl6c (bridge catalogue exposure; its candidate is over the SW budget), f3n2 (harness approval cards), o65r and gab8 (native messaging). extension/lib/acp-runner.js:478 says "no bridge process", apparently about native messaging, which still needs an installed host; confirm the boundary.
5. Budget: new SW code must fit in 17,082 B, or live outside the SW bundle.
6. Falsification tests: a denied mutation stays denied; run identity and durable ownership survive a SW restart; a cross-origin call is refused; network-off is asserted by the test, not assumed.

comments.author: cap-k3
comments.text:
FINDINGS BEFORE HANDOFF (cap-k3). I was re-tasked to 4p7j on 2026-09-26, so I am releasing this claim. The design is not written into this bead yet. Everything I gathered is in ~/cap-evidence/qnd4/design-notes.md: facts with file:line at origin/main@1906bac3d, a draft direction, and the owner decisions.

The three findings that matter most:
1. Host the harness in a NEW manifest sandbox page, not in a Worker started from an extension page. A worker shares the extension's origin, and with it CAP's OPFS and IndexedDB. A sandbox page has an opaque origin and no chrome.*, and CAP's sandbox CSP has connect-src 'none'. Embed it with sandbox="allow-scripts" so it cannot open popups or submit forms.
2. The transport is already pluggable: AcpClient takes a transport, and AcpNativeTransport is the reference. An AcpPortTransport over a MessageChannel needs no protocol change.
3. Harness tool calls today run as the owner's page, with no SW run identity. Filed as chrome-agent-platform-sqf5. qnd4 should build on that fix, not route the in-browser harness through browser.callTool as it works today.

Open owner decisions (details in the notes): which harness ships; how a harness with no network reaches a model; Store policy for running harness code in the sandbox; and whether a turn must survive the page closing.

FIRST SLICE pushed: branch qnd4-port-transport @ 908f9cf97 (2 commits off origin/main 24d20fe0a). IN_PROGRESS — this is the transport slice of the cap-k3 design (~/cap-evidence/qnd4/design-notes.md), not the whole bead.

DELIVERED: extension/lib/acp-port.js — AcpPortTransport, the MessageChannel transport for an in-browser sandboxed harness, contract-mirroring AcpNativeTransport (connect/send(raw)/close/onMessage(raw)/onClose/closed) so the runner injects either without protocol change (k3's finding 2). Nonce handshake standing in for the native host's connect/disconnect signals, FAIL CLOSED: constructor refuses a missing/empty nonce; a wrong-nonce ack, a non-ack first message, or a handshake timeout each close the transport with a named error; a peer bye is a transport signal (onClose), never a consumer frame. Framing identical to native: stringify/parse at the boundary, port messages as objects.

Measured defects the tests caught in my first cut: an unauthenticated channel object could survive a rejected connect (now the CONSTRUCTOR throws — fail closed before any object exists).

Remaining on the bead (per the k3 design + owner decisions): the sandbox harness page (manifest sandbox entry), the options/runner wiring, GAP A (SW run identity for harness calls — sqf5 builds on it), GAP B verification, and the acceptance KAT (CDP network-off + gated-deny + origin-null assertions). comments.author: master-opus
comments.text:
REVIEW: FAIL — stays IN_REVIEW. Reviewer master-opus (opus); author cap-gemini (gemini), so the reviewer is from a different model family. Candidate 3ccd1f56. I reviewed the tree that would land: af411243 = origin/main 374f44b7 + 3ccd1f56. Only .beads/issues.jsonl conflicted (I kept main's export); service-worker.js merged automatically.

WHAT HOLDS (verified)
- The six core ACP files are byte-identical to 3cf1d93d, the candidate vb-extensions reviewed on 09-21 with a real codex roundtrip.
- Harness tool calls take the run-bound route cap-k3's 09-26 warning asked for, not browser.callTool: bridge MCP endpoint (per-connection bearer token, random path, requests with an Origin header refused, revoked on close) -> reverse RPC -> offscreen AcpClient tool handler -> AI SDK tool call -> agent-do. So they run with the same authority, approval cards and fencing as any CAP model, limited to the tools the run offers.
- The offscreen host accepts only the service worker (extension id, exact SW URL, no tab).
- Native harness permissions bind the run's executionId and Chrome's attested sender.documentId. They deny on timeout, cancel, no surface, or an ended run; auto-allow only with acp.permissions=auto.
- provider.permission-summary strips the bridge token.
- Build on the landing tree: exit 0, store SW 2,537,601 bytes (budget 3,000,000).
- 20 test files green via npm run test:file: the ten in EVIDENCE.md plus the existing ACP suite.
- The two loosened first-run assertions are legitimate. permission-summary gains a parameter here, and main's own SW calls attachmentContext(attachments, {...}), so main's exact-string assertion matches zero times on main.

BLOCKING
B1 — The bridge tells the harness the opposite of what it just mounted. scripts/acp-bridge.ts:813 applies applyBrowserToolDeclaration to every session's first session/prompt, whether or not toolsEnabled is set. Driving the real exported function, the first prompt block reads: "The browser exposes tools to you DIRECTLY over this connection (no MCP server, no HTTP endpoint). To call one, emit a JSON-RPC request as your next line". That is in the same session where the bridge has just added the CAP MCP endpoint. Nothing in this path reads that text: extractBrowserToolCalls runs only inside runAcpTaskTurn, which has no production caller after this change. A model that follows the instruction prints inert JSON into the chat instead of calling the tools. Fix: skip the declaration when toolsEnabled, or replace it with one line pointing at the CAP tools.

B2 — Pi and native-host harness runs stop working, and no owner decision is recorded. Every ACP turn now goes agent.run -> runTask -> acpRunConfig. That throws for pi and for acp.transport=native, and with transport unset it goes straight to the WebSocket bridge without trying the native host. Before this change, runAcpTaskTurn preferred the native host, and Pi worked as a chat harness; jjzm (e41f2cb9) kept that on purpose ("empty Pi sessions and other adapters pass through"). pi is still the default harness id (ntp.js:4384, acp-runner.js:358/379/499, acp-thread-journal.js:56). Fix, one of: keep a tool-less chat path for harnesses that can't take CAP tools; or get Paul's explicit OK to drop them, and stop offering them.

B3 — Acceptance isn't shown, and the doc this commit adds says not to merge. docs/ACP-HARNESS-TOOLS.md opens: "This branch is incomplete and must not be merged as a working integration... full-suite and real-harness/browser acceptance have not passed." The budget half is now stale. The acceptance half is still true: EVIDENCE.md lists focused tests and a build only. The 09-21 roundtrip drove codex from Deno through createAcpModel, not through the extension path this commit changes (agent.run -> offscreen proxy -> AcpClient), and the reviewer supplied its deny decision. Needed: one real drive — built extension in Chrome, bridge on a free port, Claude Code selected. "List my tabs" should run list_tabs and return the answer; close_tab should raise the approval card, and denying it should deliver the denial to the harness. Then update the doc to the true status.

GATE: the full npm test on the landing tree exited 1. The serial phase hit the known fnmr hang (build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs --verify), so the parallel phase never ran. This candidate didn't cause that, but there is still no full-suite run for it.

NON-BLOCKING
N1 — The legacy browser/call_tool handler in AcpClient is still live, and it is checked before the new tool handler. AcpClient now runs in the offscreen document, which the SW treats as the owner (principal "extension"), with no run fence. I found no live path to it, because standard adapters don't send that method. Still, a client with toolHandler set should refuse it.
N2 — The bridge forwards adapter-originated _cap/tools/* requests to CAP, so the "private" channel isn't enforced. Same authority as the MCP route, so not an escalation. Fix: drop adapter-to-CAP frames whose method starts with _cap/.
N3 — With parallel tool calls, all but one get "already processing a tool call".
N4 — Mid-turn steering and continuation messages never reach the harness. This isn't in the doc's list of limitations.
N5 — The runAcpTaskTurn import in ntp.js:89 is dead, and acp-browser-tool-loop.test.ts pins a loop with no production caller.
N6 — Each site worker forks its own harness connection, so N site workers start N harness processes per run.
