title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-RUNTIME-01] Emscripten module runtime with reviewed glue, closed linking and killable pthreads
description:
Intent: deliver a second managed-Wasm execution runtime for admitted Emscripten libraries without changing the existing WASI security boundary. Paul/coordinator direction is Option B's CAP-authored WASI image tool first (e5o8), then this runtime. Design/static evidence can proceed now. Extend this existing epic; it remains under qazo and is not a duplicate catalogue/import system.

Measured baseline: wasm-vips 0.0.18 core vips.wasm is 5,084,535 bytes, SHA256 7ca144fb2db374b456059ca3891b762e19f713f6d230747a9f97953ebeb9bbfb. Imports: env89 + wasi_snapshot_preview1 10 + GOT.func1 (100 entries, 98 functions; env89 includes memory). Imported shared memory has min=max=16,384 pages = fixed 1 GiB. Three side modules require env/GOT, shared memory, function tables and dylink.0; the full four-Wasm graph is 11,895,030 bytes. The 4,614,586-byte figure is the compressed npm tarball, not core Wasm. Shipped ES6 glue contains two new Function and two eval sites, and imported Emval bridges can reach globalThis/Module properties. No Wasm instance or package JS has been executed for this design.

Design: new closed schema-2 emscripten-module-v1 runtime under the existing bundled lane. Bind JS adapter/glue/bootstrap, all Wasm/side modules and operation schemas into one inventory-verified graph. Do NOT widen BUNDLED_ALLOWED_IMPORT_MODULES or relax schema-1 memory/import rules. Import authority is symbol+kind+type+implementation, not an env wildcard. Trusted bundled glue is part of CAP's TCB; owner-uploaded glue is excluded, and a worker alone does not sandbox arbitrary JS. No eval/new Function, CSP widening, executable URL loading, Blob-script or main-thread fallback. Remove or strictly confine ambient Emval/JS bridges; prefer a thin native wrapper over unrestricted bindings.

Reuse the current singleton offscreen host, SW-only sender checks, registry/CAS/WAL/revocation, sealed stream/artifact custody and durable run authority. New operation-specific adapter registry selects literal local factories; callers never submit Module hooks or code paths. Fresh workers/FS/heap per job; fail-closed intent/final audit, host-owned deadline/cancel, live authority recheck before output publication, no stale outputs after revoke/restart.

Stages: A0 compiler/no-eval ABI proof; A1 typed manifest/graph admission; A2 single-thread offscreen host and real dispatch; A3 file/output custody and durable lifecycle; A4 closed eager side-module linker; A5 killable pthread WorkerGroup and shared-memory classes; A6 rebuilt vips admission/integrated linking+pthreads; A7 individually measured catalogue rollout. Explicit blocks edges, not title numbers, establish order. First implementation stage is blocked by e5o8 per Option-B-first direction; simpler packages need not wait for high-memory vips.

Memory: retain WASI tiny/default/large = 32/128/256 MiB. Upstream vips cannot fit by changing INITIAL_MEMORY at runtime. A separate shared-fixed-1024 class remains unadmitted pending exact-build loaded Chrome allocation/workload/pressure/cancel evidence; smaller variants require new native builds/digests. CAP already has COOP same-origin + COEP credentialless: test actual offscreen/root/pthread isolation, not just manifest strings. All helper workers must be host-owned or independently proven to die with the parent.

No-eval linking is an explicit uncertainty: Emscripten 6.0.0 settings comments call RELOCATABLE/dlopen unavailable, while the pinned linker uses makeEval abort sites for embedded side-module JS. Build and execute fixtures to resolve the combined configuration. If needed dynamic linking fails, keep that stage blocked; a new static-link codec variant is not evidence that side linking works.

Evidence/design: /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/EMSCRIPTEN-RUNTIME-DESIGN.md; artifact pins, compile-only inspection, glue snippets and upstream source pins are beside it. CAP source baseline 35ad5264f1c8b3d7c261fb358a2dbf89d27e5741, clean worktree cap-astra-option-a-20260905. Design is a proposal, not admission or runtime success. Keep provenance/signature claims honest: current authority validates release inventory but signer verification is not implemented. Every native/package dependency and generated post-bundle code asset needs pinned provenance and recorded license notices; no private infrastructure snapshots in public evidence.
acceptance_criteria: All runtime children have independently reviewed, source-bound evidence; WASI regression tests remain unchanged/green; actual model and Settings calls execute admitted native operations and publish validated reusable artifacts; corruption, cross-origin/agent access, arbitrary JS/global reach, external code, side-module substitution, stale epoch, audit failure, cancellation and worker restart fail closed. Real pthread/side-module work and full group termination are proven for enabled profiles. Rebuilt vips is admitted only after no-eval/ambient-bridge/memory gates pass. Before coordinator push: production build, focused and changed tests, npm test once, loaded Chrome journeys through launchChrome with durable evidence. No main push/merge by worker.

comments.text:
STAGING PLAN (scoping only — no implementation, no code branches, no pushes). Prepared against origin/main 00ddcf76 (2026-10-05). Sources: this epic, the eight stage beads, the design doc, and a read-only pass over the current runtime surfaces.

## 0. RECONCILIATION — WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (measured, not assumed)
- All eight stages are ALREADY FILED as sub-beads with this epic as PARENT and with DEPENDS-ON edges already wired: ltkj.1 (ABI-01), .2 (ADMISSION-01), .3 (HOST-01), .4 (CUSTODY-01), .5 (LINK-01), .6 (THREADS-01), .7 (VIPS-01), .8 (ROLLOUT-01).
- Every stage bead already carries an explicit Acceptance paragraph (plus ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA sections) — e.g. .3 "loaded extension real native operation from both call paths returns expected values; wrong sender, malformed envelopes, stale graph, initialization/busy-loop timeout, duplicate results and unavailable-worker …", .5 "real loaded main+side computation and constructors, exact positive result, wrong digest/ABI/kind/tag/symbol/memory bound and FS-shadow injection all RED before execution", .7 "genuine model and Settings calls process known JPEG/PNG/WebP and each enabled side-codec fixture…".
- ltkj.1 (stage A0) is CLOSED: "Landed @ 245cfdbb (v0.3.297): A0 Emscripten record and verified sandboxed ABI landed; full npm test 416 files green; unblocks ltkj.2".
- The epic's blocker is CLEARED: e5o8 (Option-B CAP-authored WASI image tool) is CLOSED — "MERGED @ f0e79836 — option-B imageops shipped … 721KB, wasi-only imports, 18/2048 pages default tier, reproducible rustc 1.97.1 … Coordinator diff review PASS."
- Therefore: NO new stage beads are needed (the request to file them is already satisfied), and the next actionable stage is ltkj.2 (A1), not A0.

## 1. STAGED SLICES (id · stage · title · state · acceptance gist · ordering edge)
- ltkj.1 · A0 · Prove a pinned no-eval native ABI without ambient JS authority · MERGED 245cfdbb · landed proof: full npm test 416 files green · —
- ltkj.2 · A1 · Bind schema-2 runtime assets and typed imports to one admitted graph · OPEN · Settings-only validation action writing the EXISTING registry/WAL; source-pinned numeric positive on the REAL generated inventory + SW broker; default/release schema-2 candidates/assets empty; numeric-only full admission; image/link structural audits with runtime refusal deferred · dep ltkj.1 (done)
- ltkj.3 · A2 · Single-thread offscreen runtime + authenticated dispatch · OPEN · real native operation from BOTH call paths; wrong sender / malformed envelope / stale graph / init and busy-loop timeout / duplicate results / unavailable worker all refuse; shipped admission stays disabled until A3 gates pass · dep ltkj.2
- ltkj.4 · A3 · Job-scoped files, fail-closed audit, sealed output publication · OPEN · a real model call produces a file artifact used by a LATER task; concurrent/sequential agent-origin canaries cannot cross-read; cancellation/revocation held at real publication races · dep ltkj.3
- ltkj.5 · A4 · Fence eager side-module linking to the admitted graph · OPEN · real loaded main+side computation and constructors; wrong digest/ABI/kind/tag/symbol/memory-bound and FS-shadow injection all RED BEFORE execution; busy constructor terminates under host deadline · dep ltkj.2 (linking needs A1's graph, not A2's host)
- ltkj.6 · A5 · Own pthread worker groups + measure shared-memory classes · OPEN · (its own acceptance section; bead states it "can proceed alongside A4; combined side-link/thread acceptance belongs to A6") · dep ltkj.2
- ltkj.7 · A6 · Admit a confined source-rebuilt vips tool with verified codecs · OPEN · genuine model/Settings calls on known JPEG/PNG/WebP + each enabled side-codec fixture, dimensions/format/content verified independently; combined link+threads acceptance lives here · deps ltkj.5 + ltkj.6
- ltkj.8 · A7 · Roll out individually proven Emscripten catalogue packages · OPEN · advance only candidates backed by actual model tool call → validated result; missing version-specific work gets its own bead; hash_blake3 (uslb) is the existing call-export precedent · dep ltkj.7 (first candidate), then per-candidate beads

## 2. SECURITY-BOUNDARY ANALYSIS — WHAT "WASI UNCHANGED" MEANS HERE (file-anchored)
Today's boundary, as it actually is:
- The WASI host is ONE module: extension/lib/wasi-preview1-runtime.js — its import object is literally `imports: Object.freeze({ wasi_snapshot_preview1: wasi })`.
- The execution worker's import policy is a hard ALLOWLIST: extension/lib/wasm-execution-worker.js `imports: { allowed: ["wasi_snapshot_preview1"], disallowed: [] }`.
- The bundled lane's authority is extension/lib/wasm-package-authority.js (`LANES = ["bundled"]`, `wasi_snapshot_preview1` among the admitted import modules, schema-2 injected into the SW rather than imported — ycez).
- The store package boundary is scripts/store-target-policy.mjs (exact CSP equality, worker/Wasm allowlists, and now — in review on cap-beads-sapd — zero source maps + forbidden audit markers).

What the new runtime must do WITHOUT changing any of that:
- Its imports (measured on the vips baseline: env 89 + wasi_snapshot_preview1 10 + GOT.func 1 incl. memory; three side modules needing env/GOT, shared memory, function tables, dylink.0) are OUTSIDE today's allowlist. The approved shape is a NEW closed schema-2 graph with import authority expressed as symbol+kind+type+implementation — NOT widening `BUNDLED_ALLOWED_IMPORT_MODULES`, NOT relaxing schema-1 memory/import rules, NOT an env wildcard.
- No CSP change (no eval/new Function, no Blob-script, no executable URL loading, no main-thread fallback); the store policy's exact-equality CSP check is the gate that proves it.
- Trusted bundled glue is TCB; owner-uploaded glue stays excluded, and a worker alone is not a sandbox for arbitrary JS. Emval/JS bridges are removed or strictly confined; a thin native wrapper is preferred over unrestricted bindings.
- Reuse unchanged: the singleton offscreen host, SW-only sender checks, registry/CAS/WAL/revocation, sealed stream/artifact custody, durable run authority. Fresh worker/FS/heap per job; host-owned deadline/cancel; live authority recheck before publication; no stale outputs after revoke/restart.
- Memory tiers stay WASI tiny/default/large = 32/128/256 MiB. The vips 1 GiB shared-fixed class stays UNADMITTED pending exact-build loaded-Chrome allocation/workload/pressure/cancel evidence; smaller variants need new native builds/digests. COOP same-origin + COEP credentialless exist — test real offscreen/root/pthread isolation, not manifest strings.
- Provenance honesty: current authority validates release inventory; signer verification is NOT implemented. Keep that claim out of any stage's acceptance.

## 3. REBASE NOTE vs CURRENT MAIN
- Epic measback baseline was CAP source 35ad5264 (2026-09-05); current main is 00ddcf76 (2026-10-05). 22 commits touched the runtime's surfaces in between.
- Plan-affecting landings: 09c4a6c0 (ycez — the schema-2 surface is injected, decoder can never enter the SW; aligns with ltkj.2's contract), 4c36b26d (9epn.5 — store target policy + archive map realigned to the surface bundles; new assets must join BUNDLE_ARCHIVE_MAP/inventory), 1a50cf3e (4h2x — deny ambient sandbox connections/remote images in CSP) and 0dc06ffc (ovfm.1-2 — sandbox CSP blob), ca5457d5 (40an — multiple Wasm tables reported as reference-types; affects side-module/linker structural checks in A4), 5b128f12 (uslb — hash_blake3, the first call-export Wasm tool: the A7 rollout precedent), 5e623a52 (python runtime: the managed-runtime precedent), f0e79836 (e5o8 shipped — the epic's blocker), and bbd3d003 (sapd store map/audit-marker boundary — IN REVIEW, not landed: when it lands, every new store asset must ship zero .map files, no authored sourceMappingURL, and no audit markers).
- No rebase conflict is being caused by this plan: it adds no code. The note exists so each stage starts from 00ddcf76+ rather than the epic's 2026-09-05 baseline, and so A1's schema-2 work meets ycez's injection rule and A7's packaging meets 9epn.5's archive map.

## 4. RISK REGISTER + THE EXISTING REGRESSION GATE THAT CATCHES EACH
- R1 no-eval linking is unproven (Emscripten 6.0.0 comments call RELOCATABLE/dlopen unavailable while the pinned linker uses makeEval abort sites) → gate: ltkj.5's fixture acceptance + tests/emscripten-module-audit.test.ts + tests/emscripten-abi-evidence.test.ts. Keep A4 blocked if it fails; a static-link codec variant is NOT evidence that side linking works.
- R2 import-authority widening by accident → gate: tests/wasm-package-authority.test.ts + tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts (CAS bytes/inventory) + the store policy's import/allowlist checks.
- R3 CSP/eval creep → gates: tests/store-target-policy.test.ts (exact CSP equality), tests/sandbox-egress-confinement.test.ts, tests/emscripten-abi-evidence.test.ts, and the bundle-budget/self-contained-bundle checks.
- R4 store budget pressure (STORE budget machinery: tests/bundle-budget.test.ts; the 2,983,291 standing figure and its ~16.7 KB headroom are from ltkj.2's contract) → gate: tests/bundle-budget.test.ts on every stage that adds bytes.
- R5 1 GiB shared-memory class overreach → gate: ltkj.6's thread acceptance + tests/bundled-tools-job-lane-tier.test.ts (tier admission) — unadmitted class must refuse, not degrade silently.
- R6 ambient JS/Emval bridge leakage → gates: tests/emscripten-module-audit.test.ts (new Function/eval sites), tests/bundled-tools-binary-io.test.ts, tests/sandbox-egress-confinement.test.ts.
- R7 cross-task/agent data bleed through job files → gate: ltkj.4's concurrent/sequential origin-canary acceptance + tests/bundled-tools-live-execution.test.ts.
- R8 stale output after revoke/restart, or a helper worker outliving its parent → gates: ltkj.4's publication-race acceptance + tests/bundled-tools-job-lane-tier.test.ts + the durable/authority tests referenced by .3/.4.
- R9 provenance/licence claims outrunning the mechanism → gate: keep the epic's honesty clause; record pins + notices per dependency; no signer-verification claim.
Every gate above is an EXISTING repo test or a stage-bead acceptance already written — the plan adds no new gate machinery.

## 5. NEXT, IN ORDER
1. Start ltkj.2 (A1) — first unmerged stage, blocker cleared, and its contract is already corrected/endorsed (coordinator191/193).
2. ltkj.3 (A2) after .2 lands (its own rule: "starts only after .2 actually lands").
3. ltkj.4 (A3) after .3; ltkj.5 (A4) and ltkj.6 (A5) both after .2 — .6 may run alongside .5.
4. ltkj.7 (A6) needs .5 + .6; ltkj.8 (A7) per proven candidate, with hash_blake3 as the existing precedent.

## 6. WHAT THIS SCOPING DID NOT DO
No implementation, no code branch, no push. No bead was created because all eight stage beads already exist (evidence in section 0). The frozen custody/design docs were read only; nothing was edited.

INDEPENDENT READ-ONLY REVIEW (reviewer lane, 2026-10-06) — branch cap/gemini-2uhx-awasm-noble @ e38c416c, delta 3a5d002f..e38c416c, reviewed against main @ 61b8e4c9. No writes, no suite run (banned for this pass).

WHAT I INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (not taken from EVIDENCE.md)
1. Provenance is real. Tarball blob at packages/bundled/evidence/awasm-chacha/awasm-noble-0.1.4.tgz = 3,312,149 B, sha256 a78cc0db73a29bacb87ad8d8610130df4cc6c4f69f7a0f64ac433e9f3445da91, sha512-b64 LFkAq7Vn…vOg== (both match PIN). I decoded the atob blob out of its targets/wasm/chacha_poly1305.js: 43,461 B, sha256 e1acae9b…f11330 — byte-identical (cmp) to the shipped CAS blob.
2. Zero imports and 41/41 pages, measured: node WebAssembly.Module.imports() = [], exports include memory + encryptInit/encryptBlocks/decryptInit/decryptBlocks/tagFinish/aadBlocks/aadInit/…; memory.buffer = 2,686,976 B = 41 pages and grow(1) is refused → matches manifest initialPages/maxPages 41.
3. Inventory digests are honest: manifest sha256 = a992edde…b9541355 and sbom sha256 = cbc7a48e…39f2e51d37 exactly as bundled-inventory-data.js declares.
4. THE CRYPTO IS REAL, NOT FAKED. Harness layout matches the pinned tarball's own generated wrapper segments (counter@0, sigma@16 "expand 32-byte k", key@32, nonce@64, aadLen@80, dataLen@88, poly.tag@992, buffer@1008). Running the branch's executeCallexportRun against the shipped CAS bytes and comparing to OpenSSL: RFC 8439 §2.8.2 byte-exact — d31a8d34648e60db7b86afbc53ef7ec2…b4831d7b…586cec64b6116 ‖ tag 1ae10b594f09e26a7e902ecbd0600691 — plus exact matches for empty-pt, 64 B, 65 B, aad-17, aad-160, aad-65536/65537/200000 (chunk boundary), data-1 MiB, data-2 MiB; OpenSSL ciphertext decrypts through the harness. So AAD length encoding, padding and the tag are correct.
5. Fail-closed holds: 31 B key → key_length_invalid, 11 B nonce → nonce_length_invalid, mode "bogus" → invalid_mode, >2 MiB data → input_over_budget, tampered ct/AAD → invalid_tag.
6. No eval / new Function / Emval anywhere in the diff (git diff … -- '*.js' '*.mjs' | grep -c = 0); the module is driven by CAP-authored JS over the offscreen host with the unchanged isTrustedWasmStreamSender sender gate, and the manifest is re-validated per run against the immutable inventory digest. Shared memory is rejected by the authority (wasm-package-authority.js:456).

FINDINGS (file:line on the branch)
P1-1 DEAD PROVENANCE POINTER. extension/wasm/manifests/cap.bundled.chacha20.poly1305-1.0.0.manifest.json:1 declares "rebuildRef":"packages/bundled/awasm-chacha/build.sh" — that path does not exist in the branch tree (git ls-tree e38c416c -- packages/bundled/awasm-chacha = empty; the real script is packages/bundled/evidence/awasm-chacha/extract.mjs). Main already fixed exactly this class: scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs rebuildRefFor() (7rok) resolves extract.mjs, and tests/wasm-manifest-rebuild-ref.test.ts:37 fails any manifest whose rebuildRef names a missing file. That guard did not exist at the merge base, so test:changed could not have caught it. Fix: rebase onto main and REGENERATE (never hand-merge bundled-inventory-data.js) so rebuildRef becomes packages/bundled/evidence/awasm-chacha/extract.mjs; the manifest bytes and its digest, and the inventory digest rows, all change.
P1-2 NO KNOWN-ANSWER VECTOR. tests/callexport-admission.test.ts:150-183 (and :185, :227) only round-trip the harness against itself: encrypt→decrypt and tamper detection. A wrong sigma/offset/length layout that is self-consistent round-trips green. The repo's own precedent for this lane pins official vectors (tests/callexport-admission.test.ts:104-115, BLAKE3 test_vectors.json af1349b9…/6437b3ac…). Smallest fix: assert the RFC 8439 §2.8.2 vector above (key 80..9f, nonce 070000004041424344454647, aad 50515253c0c1c2c3c4c5c6c7) on encrypt output — it is already green on this tree per my run.
P1-3 SECRET KEY IS NOT COVERED BY THE REDACTION MODEL, AND IT REACHES THE PROVIDER BOUNDARY. The tool's argument name is `key` (a 44-char base64 32-byte AEAD secret). extension/lib/pure.js:959 SECRET_KEY_RE matches api_key/access_key/token/secret/… but NOT a bare `key`, and the generic-assignment pass in redactSecretText (pure.js ~1090) excludes bare `key` too. Measured in node: redactSecretText(JSON.stringify({toolId:"chacha20_poly1305",data:"aGk=",key:"<44 chars>",…})) → key returned UNCHANGED, and redactSecrets(obj) likewise; only cap-log's scrubLogValue masks it (24+ char run). Run-digest stores one line per tool result as redactSecretText(compactJson(args,160)) (extension/lib/run-digest.js:221) and run-digest.js:15-24 documents that digest is attached to the provider-bound continuation message — so a short encrypt call (args JSON ≈130 chars, `key` inside the 160-char cut) puts the key in plaintext into the model egress AND the persisted transcript. This is a design decision, not a mechanical edit: either declare per-tool secret argument names (row/descriptor `secretArgs: ["key"]`) honoured by run-digest + the transcript card, or extend the digest-path keyword class to a bare `key` (repo-wide over-redaction risk on unrelated "key" fields). INDEPENDENT READ-ONLY REVIEW (deepseek; cross-family vs the gemini author) — branch fleet/2uhx @ 9bb4a447, delta 61b8e4c9..9bb4a447 (single commit). No checkout, no build, no suite run; every claim below is from source, from the branch blobs, or from the two-line redaction probe noted in F1.

VERDICT: PASS-WITH-NOTES — 3 findings (1xP1, 2xP2).

=== FIX VERIFICATION (the 3 P1s from the failed pre-rebase review) ===

P1-1 rebuildRef — FIXED. extension/wasm/manifests/cap.bundled.chacha20.poly1305-1.0.0.manifest.json now declares build.rebuildRef = "packages/bundled/evidence/awasm-chacha/extract.mjs", that file ships in the branch, and scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs:42-50 (rebuildRefFor) can emit only that third candidate for lane "awasm-chacha" — so the value is generator output, not hand-written. REGENERATED, NOT HAND-MERGED: I hashed the blobs at 9bb4a447 and the digest chain closes — manifest sha256 180c0006c134408ff3d0e8dae65cdb809754bbf00c35679207e838641a02f880 / 1987 B, sbom cbc7a48ee1e77c4d755e7cdf7f3ff74bc076ddd7b53539e4593d1e39f2e51d37 / 1392 B, CAS wasm e1acae9b3ee3da01b2bd0574f906fede6f5219da4b9b43fd5c36ee16fbf11330 / 43461 B — all three match extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js (manifests + files entries) and the row's binary.sha256, and the manifest's own sbom.sha256 names that same sbom. tests/wasm-manifest-rebuild-ref.test.ts passes on content (rebuildRef names an existing file; its `declared >= 30` floor is untouched). Caveat: I could not run --verify (the launch tree is at base 61b8e4c9), so "regenerated" rests on the digest chain + the generator-only field, not on a byte-identical verify run.

P1-2 KAT — FIXED. tests/callexport-admission.test.ts:265-324 asserts the RFC 8439 §2.8.2 vector on ENCRYPT, byte-for-byte — ciphertext d31a8d34...6b6116 (asserted :311) and tag 1ae10b594f09e26a7e902ecbd0600691 (asserted :312), driven with the RFC's key 80..9f, nonce 070000004041424344454647 and AAD 50515253c0c1c2c3c4c5c6c7 — then decrypts those same bytes back to the RFC plaintext. Not a self round-trip.

P1-3 SECRET KEY REDACTION — PARTIAL. The mechanism is the right SHAPE and the global widening did NOT happen: SECRET_KEY_RE is byte-identical at 61b8e4c9 and 9bb4a447 (pure.js:959; `key` alone does not match), the new surface is targeted (KNOWN_TOOL_SECRET_ARGS pure.js:1151, redactToolArgs pure.js:1164), and the run-digest/continuation acceptance IS met: run-digest.js:216-217 redacts `shownArgs` before compactJson, `name = selected ?? tool` resolves to the real tool id (lazy-tool-protocol.js:1189/1219 `selectedTool: descriptor.name`), and tests/run-digest.test.ts:160-210 drives BOTH shapes (direct `tool:"chacha20_poly1305"` and `tool:"execute_tool", selected:"chacha20_poly1305"` with the nested `arguments` envelope) and asserts both the raw key's absence AND that "[REDACTED]" is present in renderTurn(0) and in attach()'s prompt. That test is non-vacuous — I measured both generic layers on that exact payload (node import of extension/lib/pure.js at 61b8e4c9, where those two functions are unchanged): redactSecrets and redactSecretText BOTH leave "AAECAwQFBgcICQoLDA0ODxAREhMUFRYXGBkaGxwdHh8=" intact, so without redactToolArgs the digest arg line would carry the key. tests/pure.test.ts:595-627 asserts SECRET_KEY_RE.test("key")===false plus the non-declared-tool no-op. BUT the SW-egress half does not work on the only path the provider can take — F1 below.

=== FINDINGS ===

F1 (P1) The SW-egress half of the P1-3 fix is a no-op for every real chacha call: the raw AEAD key is broadcast live, persisted in the journal and durable run log, and rendered by the activity explorer.
 - The provider is given ONLY the four lazy protocol tools (agent.js:1405 `const allTools = lazy.tools`, :1449 `tools: allTools`; lazy-tool-protocol.js:1861-1868 `execute_tool` inputSchema `{selectionRef, arguments}` — the contract tests/lazy-tool-protocol.test.ts:108-110 rely on), so every model-initiated chacha call arrives as `execute_tool` with args `{selectionRef, arguments:{key,...}}`.
 - agent.js:1594 emits the tool-call progress event as `{ toolName: e.toolName, toolArgs: e.args }` — the PROVIDER-FACING name, no `selectedTool` (that field only exists on the result event).
 - service-worker.js:3893 then does `redactDeep(redactToolArgs(event.toolName, event.toolArgs))` with toolName "execute_tool" → pure.js:1171-1173 finds no entry and returns args UNCHANGED (`if (secretSet.size === 0) return args;`). The nested-`arguments` recursion in redactToolArgs (:1186-1188) is only reached when a secret set exists, so the envelope never gets unwrapped.
 - The generic layer cannot rescue it (measured, see P1-3 above): SECRET_KEY_RE has no bare "key"; redactSecretText's generic assignment pass (pure.js:1105-1108) also omits bare "key".
 - Consequences, all from this one no-op: the live broadcast (service-worker.js:3891-3893); the per-agent journal row `journalJson(redactSecrets(event.toolArgs))` (:3964) and the durable run log (:3967) — a durable at-rest copy of the tool's key material; and the activity explorer, which renders that row's inputs through redactSecrets only, so the tree and its COPY button show the key (components.js:12694 `const safeValue = redactSecrets(parsed.value)`, :12704 `addBlock("inputs", e.args)`).
 - The fix's own claim is the standard here: the commit body says "per-tool secretArgs (\"key\") redaction in run-digest, tool card, and SW egress". Two of those three are incomplete on the reachable path (SW egress entirely — F1; the card until a result exists — F2).
 - Smallest fix: the selected tool is genuinely known only at the pre-tool seam — resolve it there (agent.js onPreToolUse has the selectionRef, and the protocol owns the selection registry) and put `selectedTool` on the tool-call progress event so the chokepoint can use `event.selectedTool ?? event.toolName`. A self-contained alternative that touches only pure.js: when the tool is a lazy protocol tool (`execute_tool`), redact a nested `arguments` object against the UNION of KNOWN_TOOL_SECRET_ARGS' names.
 - Honest severity note: the key is model-supplied in-context material, not an owner credential, and the explicitly stated acceptance (run-digest / provider-bound continuation) IS met. It is P1 because the named SW-egress surface is claimed fixed and is not, and the key persists in the journal/explorer.

F2 (P2) The live (still-running) tool card shows the key. components.js:5751 `rawToolName = lazyName || (name === "execute_tool" ? "" : (name || "tool"))`; lazyName comes from unwrapToolPayload(result|detail).selectedTool, which does not exist until the result lands, and conversation.js:496-503 hands the running card `name: callEff.name` ("execute_tool") with `args: callEff.args` = the already-unwrapped inner `{key,nonce,data,mode}`. So `redactToolArgs("", {key,...})` (components.js:5768) is a no-op and the expanded running card's "inputs" block (:5941) plus its copy button show the raw key until the result arrives. Landed and replayed cards are CORRECT (conversation.js:1571-1583 resolves eff.name/eff.args, so the table hits). Fix: fall back to the union of KNOWN_TOOL_SECRET_ARGS names when rawToolName is empty.

F3 (P2) Evidence/doc accuracy.
 - cap-evidence/2uhx-awasm-noble/EVIDENCE.md:52 still says "tests/callexport-admission.test.ts: 10 passed / 0 failed" — that was the pre-rebase file (e38c416c had 10 `Deno.test`s); the reviewed tip has 12. Lines 4-5 still name the pre-rebase branch/worktree (`cap/gemini-2uhx-awasm-noble` @ /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/...) and base 3a5d002f0; the tip is fleet/2uhx @ 9bb4a447 on 61b8e4c9. "noble vectors" is gone.)
 - Docs drift (no test guards it, so the suite stays green, but AGENTS.md "docs never drift" makes it a defect): README.md:71 ("38 bundled Wasm tools — 38 single-tool packages"), PLAN.md:14 ("141 generated files ... 38 packages"), PLAN.md:200, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:511 and :515 still say 38, while extension/lib/master-skill.js:66 was correctly updated to "39 on-device bundled Wasm tools".

=== P2 ITEMS VERIFIED OK ===
 - P2-1 pinned: tests/callexport-admission.test.ts:326-372 drives the validator's real error strings (shape/toolId/unexpected_keys/required_fields/mode/aad), the frozen valid result with default mode, and the SW envelope (CALLEXPORT_RUN_TYPE + `args: validatedArgs ?? {}`). Note the two SW assertions are source-text pins: they have live occurrences (so tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts stays green), but they would also pass with the line commented out — the SW dispatcher is not exported, so execution coverage is not achievable without extracting it.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
2026-09-05 DESIGN (cap-wasm-catalogue lane) — empirical blocker found, options below.

EVIDENCE (npm wasm-vips@0.0.18, tarball sha512-AJyCvxZj/3qceKNnh+YyEobu/IaJFoPN7x7SxyyHmYBS3kASMqJqxQEuN0ZHKQDWsCJ8armfx4Tq3uKrNc+nMA==, registry.npmjs.org/wasm-vips/-/wasm-vips-0.0.18.tgz):
- vips.wasm: 5,084,535 bytes (5.08MB, larger than the catalogue's ~4.6MB estimate). Imports: env x89 (Emscripten runtime) + wasi_snapshot_preview1 x10 (fd_close/fd_write/fd_read/fd_seek/fd_fdstat_get/random_get/clock_time_get/proc_exit/environ_get/environ_sizes_get) + GOT.func x1 (DYNAMIC LINKING). sha256 7ca144fb... (full pin at admission if pursued).
- vips-heif.wasm (3.48MB), vips-jxl.wasm (2.17MB), vips-resvg.wasm (1.16MB) are Emscripten SIDE MODULES (env x134-252 + GOT.mem/GOT.func) — the package needs a dynamic linker.
- vips.js glue references SharedArrayBuffer/pthread (6 sites) — threaded build.

BLOCKER: the bundled admission authority admits ONLY imports.allowed=[wasi_snapshot_preview1] (wasm-package-authority.js:37 BUNDLED_ALLOWED_IMPORT_MODULES) and the execution worker is a WASI preview1 runtime (wasm-execution-worker.js:22). wasm-vips's env x89 + GOT dynamic linking + pthread/SAB cannot pass the authority or run in that host. Admitting it as-is is INFEASIBLE without a new runtime class.

OPTIONS:
A. New 'emscripten-module' package/runtime class: execute the vips.js glue + side-module linking + pthread emulation inside the offscreen module worker. Large: a second wasm host architecture, new manifest semantics, COOP/COEP question for SAB. Its own epic, not this bead.
B. (RECOMMENDED) CAP-authored WASI image tool — the csvtool clean-room precedent (packages/bundled/evidence/csvtool): a small Rust CLI wrapper over the pure-Rust  crate compiled to wasm32-wasi: vips-class basics (info/resize/convert/re-encode jpeg/png/webp) via stdin→stdout. Fits the admission pipeline TODAY (deterministic cargo build, wasi imports only, memory32, reviewable evidence tree). Delivers Paul's actual need (image analysis/compression/resizing) inside the shipped trust model.
C. Route wasm-vips through the OWNER-SELECTED package path (bead tzc) instead of the bundled channel — the owner installs it explicitly; the bundled-reviewed-only policy stays untouched.

Awaiting coordinator/owner pick: A (new epic), B (recommended), or C.

comments.text:
# Docs audit — 2026-09-05 (lane cap-arch-docs, bead chrome-agent-platform-5zl6, umbrella 9zw7)

**Audited tree:** `origin/main@14e2a817` (2026-09-05). Claims were verified against the code at
the tip via `git show origin/main:<path>` — not against the local checkout (which sits 10 commits
behind at `75364f28`). Read-only analysis; no product or doc files were modified.

**Scope:** `README.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, `PLAN.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, root trackers, and `docs/*.md`
(incl. `docs/plans/`, `docs/admissions/` presence, `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`,
`extension/background/routes/ROUTE_MAP.md`). `docs/admissions/*` and `docs/plans/rust-lane/*`
per-lane records (42 + 59 tracked files) were spot-checked for presence only — they are declared
per-lane authorities for still-open candidate work, so their internal state is owned by those lanes.

Every finding cites file:line at `origin/main`. Severities: **H** = actively misleads a reader
about the current product/process; **M** = stale but recognizably dated; **L** = cosmetic.

---

## A. Retired trackers still presented as the live authority (H)

The 2026-09-02 owner directive (AGENTS.md, "Task tracking: beads only") retired TASKS.md,
TASKS-DONE.md, KNOWN-ISSUES.md and docs/UI-FIXES-TRACKER.md. Both retired root files now carry a
correct RETIRED banner (TASKS.md:1-9, KNOWN-ISSUES.md:1-5). But the docs that point at them were
never updated:

1. **README.md:243** — the document map declares TASKS.md "**Task state, and the only authority
   for it.** … The entry always wins over any summary of it." Directly contradicts the beads-only
   rule; a new reader is sent to a frozen file.
2. **README.md:246** — KNOWN-ISSUES.md described as "Gate state and the few open findings… A thin
   view over TASKS.md". Retired.
3. **README.md:247-248** — docs/UI-FIXES-TRACKER.md and TASKS-DONE.md listed as live map entries
   with no retirement note.
4. **PLAN.md:41** — "Task state lives in TASKS.md (the authority)".
5. **PLAN.md:48** — "TASKS.md is the task authority".
6. **PLAN.md:76** — "archived to TASKS-DONE.md, so TASKS.md holds only live work".
7. **PLAN.md:229** — "The authority is the **Open work queue** table in TASKS.md (39 open)."
   (39 open is doubly stale: the file is retired, and live state is `bd ready`.)
8. **docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md:3** — the whole file is a redirect to root KNOWN-ISSUES.md, i.e. a
   signpost to a retired file. Should point at beads.
9. **docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-ARCHIVE.md:5, 9, 60, 117, 135** — repeatedly tells readers live findings
   "live in TASKS.md" / to look up CAP-FB ids in TASKS.md. The archive itself may stay, but its
   pointers are dead ends.
10. **docs/AGENT-MODEL.md:81** (status section) — "Residual: … tracked in KNOWN-ISSUES."
11. **docs/UI-FIXES-TRACKER.md:28** — references TASKS.md as the evidence authority. (The tracker
    itself is a legacy view per AGENTS.md; keeping it as history is fine, pointing from it at
    another retired file is not.)

## B. Stale quantitative claims (H — several are in the README a newcomer reads first)

Ground truth measured at `origin/main@14e2a817`:

| Claim | Docs say | Code says | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser tool count | README.md:56 "**125 Chrome tools**"; README.md:107 "the browser-tool count is 126"; PLAN.md:31 "**126**"; PRODUCT.md:196-198 "flat list of 126" | **138** browser tools (+ 3 developer-only cookie tools), 50 management, 188 capability rows | tests/chrome-tool-capabilities.test.ts:60-72 (`CHROME_TOOL_CAPABILITY_TABLE.length === 188`, 138 chrome-api, 50 management, `CHROME_TOOL_CAPABILITY_BOUNDS {browserTools:138, managementTools:50, totalTools:188}`); extension/lib/browser-tools.js has 138 `tool({` definitions |
| Capability table size | PLAN.md:32-33 "dropped to 155 … regrown to 160"; docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md:35,44 "159 → 155", "167 → 166" | **188** | same test as above |
| Bundled Wasm tools | README.md:70 "**28 bundled Wasm tools**"; PLAN.md:170 "**28 bundled Wasm packages ship**" | **31** admitted (sed, awk, jq joined the 28) | packages/bundled/README.md:1-3 ("31-tool execution tranche") listing all 31 admitted descriptors |
| Lazy provider definitions | README.md:62-63 "every run receives **exactly two definitions**, `search_tools` and `execute_tool`" | **Three**: `search_tools`, `list_tools`, `execute_tool` | extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js:1464, 1478, 1491 (the three `tool({…})` definitions) |
| Unit tests | README.md:253 "**1779/0**"; PLAN.md:11 "**1779 pass / 0 fail**" | stale (2457 pass at the 2026-08-30 reanalysis; higher today) | REVIEW-2026-08-30.md; the number moves daily — the honest fix is to stop hardcoding it (see fix plan) |
| Chrome journeys | README.md:253 "**127/127**"; PLAN.md:12 "**127/127**" | stale (138/138 at 2026-08-30; current count differs) | REVIEW-2026-08-30.md |
| Chrome-lazy metadata counts | docs/tool-platform-architecture.md (§"Source-only Chrome lazy capability metadata") "the exact **nine** `browserToolset(false)` and **29** `managementToolset` names", "all 38 descriptors" | 138 + 50 | tests/chrome-tool-capabilities.test.ts:67-69 |

Note README.md is internally inconsistent (125 vs 126 in the same file) in addition to both being
stale.

## C. References to deleted surfaces/directories (M)

`extension/chat/` and `extension/memory/` no longer exist at tip (deleted; verified via
`git ls-tree origin/main extension/`). `extension/recipes/` is also gone (though
`extension/lib/recipes.js` still exists — the recipes→skills rename is an open P3, bead
chrome-agent-platform-l0r). Stale references:

12. **README.md:194** — the architecture tree lists `chat/` ("the conversation surface").
13. **PLAN.md:86** — "Landed and shipping" includes "NTP hub, side panel, **chat**, directory,
    **memory explorer**, options".
14. **PRODUCT.md:66-67** — "Twelve HTML surfaces ship; two of them — `chat/chat.html` and
    `memory/explorer.html` — are referenced by nothing at all and still ship to users." Both files
    were subsequently deleted (the "Subtract surfaces" action happened): **10** HTML files ship now
    (verified: artifact, artifacts, directory, ntp, offscreen, options, privacy, sandbox×2,
    sidepanel). The paragraph should record the deletion, not the dead weight.
15. **docs/CONSTITUTION.md** (§1 XSS bullet) — "chat/directory/memory render untrusted data with
    textContent/escaping" — two of the three named surfaces are gone.
16. **docs/UX-AUDIT-2026-08-28.md:73** — evidence row cites the `chat` surface (360px overflow).
    Point-in-time audit; acceptable as history, but any "still true" reading of it is broken.

## D. Stale status headers on design/plan docs (M)

17. **docs/tool-platform-architecture.md** — the worst offender for the architecture story:
    - Status line: "live bounded lazy-provider cutover is a **0.2.180 release candidate** … fresh
      browser acceptance plus independent release review remain pending." The cutover shipped long
      ago (tip is 0.3.229; PLAN.md describes the lazy provider as landed and shipping).
    - §"Live bounded lazy protocol": "bundled Wasm rows are **always projected as disabled
      catalog-only metadata. They receive no selection reference, validator, authorization
      callback, or provider dispatch closure**" — contradicted by
      extension/background/service-worker.js:1430 (`executableBundledToolRecords(…)` folded into
      every run's records with `closureGeneration: "task-execution-core"`) and by
      docs/UNIX-TOOLS-ADMISSION.md:5-9 ("available through the ordinary `search_tools` →
      `execute_tool` path"). packages/bundled/README.md:10 ("Model calls use the lazy selection
      authority and live run fence") agrees with the code. The doc is the odd one out.
    - Repeated "source-only / unreachable / no product file imports this" claims for the OPFS
      workspace, WASI execution host, and package authority slices — all three now have shipped
      execution paths (extension/lib/wasm-executor.js, wasm-offscreen-host.js, wasm-stream-*.js,
      opfs-tool-workspace.js consumed by the live pipeline).
    - §"Planned authority split" items 1-4 are described as future; all are landed.
18. **docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md** —
    - Header says "Phases 1–4 all implemented and shipped" but §6 still reads "Phase 2 — move the
      agent-do run loop into the worker (**NEXT**)" (and Phases 3/4 as forward-looking). Internal
      contradiction.
    - §7: "The `chrome.offscreen` API requires no manifest permission — confirmed by this
      codebase… works with `permissions: []` and no `offscreen` entry." The manifest at tip
      declares `offscreen` as one of the four **required** install permissions
      (extension/manifest.json `permissions: ["alarms","offscreen","sidePanel","storage"]`).
      Either the doc's claim was wrong or the posture changed; as written it misinforms.
19. **docs/AGENT-DELEGATION.md:2** — "Status: implemented (**candidate on branch
    `cap-agent-delegation`**)." Delegation is merged: extension/lib/agent-delegation.js and
    `delegate_to_agent` (extension/lib/chrome-tool-capabilities.js:205) are on main.
20. **docs/THREAD-LOADING-REDESIGN.md:3** — "Status: DESIGN, awaiting owner review. **Nothing
    here is implemented.**" The thread-open work landed (`0.2.314`/`0.2.317`, PLAN.md:152-156:
    per-execution ordered log index + cursor pagination).
21. **PLAN.md:189-192** — "Python via Pyodide … The remaining step is the Pyodide runtime
    **binary**, a blocked Emscripten build." Pyodide shipped: official 0.26.4 core admitted and

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Candidate ffc4b263 pushed to branch cap-beads-m6id (off main 27ec8926).
- Defect: a second permission request in the same run never rendered a card if the requirement had already been decided, causing subsequent requests to hang for 60s and expire.
- Fix: in extension/shared/conversation.js maybeRenderApproval:
  1. Denied requirement: immediately resolves subsequent request as denied (fast & honest failure, no 60s timeout).
  2. In-flight requirement (pending/granting): queues waiter behind active card (existing.requestIds) so owner's single decision settles both without duplicate cards.
  3. Settled requirement (granted/expired/cancelled): renders fresh card in the transcript for the new request.
- Falsification & verification: tests/in-flight-permission-cards.test.ts (3/3 GREEN):
  - Proved RED on unpatched code (denied second request hung until timeout; post-grant second request rendered no card).
  - Proved GREEN post-fix.
  - Concurrent same-requirement requests share 1 card and both settle on decision.
- Gates: npm run test:changed parallel phase GREEN (484 passed / 0 failed in 19s), store build PASS (2,998,720B <= 3,000,000 budget), all conversation/permission suites green.
- Ready for independent review.

title: Settings browser gates assert visibility, not rendered content — audit for the hy91 blind spot
description:
Discovered while fixing chrome-agent-platform-hy91. scripts/kat-settings-multi-section.ts opened Settings with no fragment and asserted only that #providers was the single VISIBLE panel. Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/logs/cap-dptw-gates/ (area suite logs).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
# bfbd — the agent board's three interlocked gates, measured (ds-flash-2, 2026-09-18)

Measurement-plus-options, as coordinated: nothing here changes policy. Every number below is from the current
tree, with the command that produced it. Synthetic board only (mock memory); no real board was touched.

## Commands
```
deno run -A cap-evidence/bfbd-gates-measure.ts fill     # shipped module, both regimes
deno run -A --v8-flags=--max-old-space-size=256 cap-evidence/bfbd-gates-measure.ts naive   # mutants
```
Harness: `bfbd-gates-measure.ts` (copied here). Raw: `bfbd-fill4.json`, `bfbd-naive2.log`, `bfbd-naive3.log`.

## The constants and the derived thresholds
| constant | value |
|---|---|
| `BOARD_MAX_LOG_BYTES` | 196,608 (192 KiB) |
| `BOARD_MAX_OPEN_JOBS` | 100 |
| `BOARD_MAX_SETTLED_JOBS` | 50 |
| `BOARD_MAX_MESSAGES` | 200 |
| `BOARD_MAX_DESCRIPTION` / `BOARD_MAX_RESULT` / `BOARD_MAX_MESSAGE_BODY` | 2,000 / 4,000 / 2,000 |
| memory store per-value cap the comments cite | 256 KiB (262,144) |
| derived: trim gate threshold | `192 KiB − 4 KiB − 2048` = **190,560** |
| derived: delivery reserve per open threaded job | `4,000 + 2048` = **6,048** |

## Where each gate actually fires (max-size posts)
| regime | accepted | refused with | bytes at refusal | log after settling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **threaded** (`posterThreadId` set → reserve applies) | **23** | `board-full` | **51,774** (26% of budget) | **151,019** |
| **unthreaded** | **86** | `board-full` | **193,071** | 193,071 |
| messages (`sendMessage`, 2 KB bodies) | 400 accepted, **never refused** | — | peak **195,121** | — |

Reading: the reserve is what makes the threaded path refuse at 26% of the budget — it is deliberately holding
~139 KB for the 23 open jobs' results, and after settling all 23 the log sits at 151 KB, under the budget.
The unthreaded path has no results to reserve for, so the byte gate binds near the budget. Messages are a
**drop** gate, not a refusal gate: 400 accepted, oldest trimmed, peak 195 KB.

## The bead's premise, corrected by measurement
The bead says *"naive Infinity removal → fill-until-refusal tests OOM"*. Reproduced, that is **not** what
happens, and the real mechanisms are more useful:

| naive change | what actually happens |
|---|---|
| `BOARD_MAX_LOG_BYTES = Infinity` (byte cap only) | the log **stabilises at 425,627 bytes** — the count caps still bound it — i.e. **1.62× the 256 KiB per-value cap the comments cite**, so the failure mode is a **store refusal, not an OOM** |
| all four caps → `Infinity` | **unbounded**: 22.9 MB of log by cycle 3,500 and RSS climbing 247 → 294 MB, still rising when the 300 s ceiling stopped it (bounded 256 MB heap) — this is the genuine run-away, and it needs the COUNT caps removed, not the byte cap |

The phase-2 evidence the bead points at is a different failure: `area1-suite.log` shows
`RangeError: Invalid typed array length: Infinity` from `tests/tool-exec-preview.test.ts:98`
(`new Uint8Array(EXECUTOR_BOUNDS.maxWasmBytes + 1)`) — an Infinity-into-typed-array crash in another tool's
bounds, not an OOM of the board.

## The wall itself — a boundary I am NOT inventing a number for
The board's comments justify 192 KiB with "the memory store's 256 KiB per-value cap (memory.js
`MAX_VALUE_BYTES`)". **That constant does not exist in the current tree** (`grep -rn MAX_VALUE_BYTES
extension/lib/memory.js` returns nothing; `memory.js` is an OPFS directory/store abstraction), and the board
writes through an **injected** store: `const writeLog = (key, events) => memory.setTrusted(key, events)`.
So whether a 425 KB log would be refused in production is **not determined by this measurement** — it depends
on the injected store (chrome.storage.local's 10 MB quota? OPFS? a SW-side cap?), and the only evidence the
wall bites is the r3 probe's `board-store-error` (89 posts, 18th settle dead) quoted in the code. The cheap
missing experiment is a browser KAT that writes a >256 KiB value through the SW's memory store and records
the refusal — offered, not assumed.

## Options, with what each costs and what it breaks
| option | what it costs | what it breaks / risks |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Keep the caps; add the archive key** (evict settled jobs to an archive keyed `board:job:<id>`, keep a pointer in the log; GC on a schedule) | a new store surface, an archive reader for the owner UI, and a GC policy | needs the **retention decision** (below); a viewer that ignores the pointer shows a job with no result |
| **B. Raise the byte budget toward the real wall** | one constant, once the wall is measured in production | if the wall is real, raising past it converts a clean `board-full` into `board-store-error`; if the wall is gone, this just moves memory pressure |
| **C. Move the log out of the per-value store (OPFS append-only + index)** | a new IO path, migration, and compaction on the file | the largest change; loses the single-value atomicity the current writes have |
| **D. Leave as is, document the caps as deliberate** | a doc edit | the P0 directive ("remove ALL self-imposed caps") stays unmet; nothing breaks |

## Recommendation, and the decisions Paul actually has to make
Recommendation: **A, preceded by the wall measurement.** The count caps plus the byte authority already keep
the shipped paths bounded and correct (max observed 195 KB); what the P0 directive wants is *unbounded
history*, and history that must not live in the log is exactly what an archive key is for. B alone is a
number to tune, not a design; C is defensible but is the biggest change for the smallest observable gain
today.

Two decisions, not one:
1. **Does the board need unbounded history at all?** ("remove all caps" may mean "no arbitrary small caps",
   in which case A is scope the fleet does not need and D is honest.)
2. **If yes: where does evicted history live and for how long?** An archive key with no retention policy
   grows without bound on the owner's disk instead of in the log — so the archive needs its own answer
   (keep forever, keep N days, keep until the canvas is deleted).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
# bfbd — the agent board's three interlocked gates, measured (ds-flash-2, 2026-09-18)

Measurement-plus-options, as coordinated: nothing here changes policy. Every number below is from the current
tree, with the command that produced it. Synthetic board only (mock memory); no real board was touched.

## Commands
```
deno run -A cap-evidence/bfbd-gates-measure.ts fill     # shipped module, both regimes
deno run -A --v8-flags=--max-old-space-size=256 cap-evidence/bfbd-gates-measure.ts naive   # mutants
```
Harness: `bfbd-gates-measure.ts` (copied here). Raw: `bfbd-fill4.json`, `bfbd-naive2.log`, `bfbd-naive3.log`.

## The constants and the derived thresholds
| constant | value |
|---|---|
| `BOARD_MAX_LOG_BYTES` | 196,608 (192 KiB) |
| `BOARD_MAX_OPEN_JOBS` | 100 |
| `BOARD_MAX_SETTLED_JOBS` | 50 |
| `BOARD_MAX_MESSAGES` | 200 |
| `BOARD_MAX_DESCRIPTION` / `BOARD_MAX_RESULT` / `BOARD_MAX_MESSAGE_BODY` | 2,000 / 4,000 / 2,000 |
| memory store per-value cap the comments cite | 256 KiB (262,144) |
| derived: trim gate threshold | `192 KiB − 4 KiB − 2048` = **190,560** |
| derived: delivery reserve per open threaded job | `4,000 + 2048` = **6,048** |

## Where each gate actually fires (max-size posts)
| regime | accepted | refused with | bytes at refusal | log after settling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **threaded** (`posterThreadId` set → reserve applies) | **23** | `board-full` | **51,774** (26% of budget) | **151,019** |
| **unthreaded** | **86** | `board-full` | **193,071** | 193,071 |
| messages (`sendMessage`, 2 KB bodies) | 400 accepted, **never refused** | — | peak **195,121** | — |

Reading: the reserve is what makes the threaded path refuse at 26% of the budget — it is deliberately holding
~139 KB for the 23 open jobs' results, and after settling all 23 the log sits at 151 KB, under the budget.
The unthreaded path has no results to reserve for, so the byte gate binds near the budget. Messages are a
**drop** gate, not a refusal gate: 400 accepted, oldest trimmed, peak 195 KB.

## The bead's premise, corrected by measurement
The bead says *"naive Infinity removal → fill-until-refusal tests OOM"*. Reproduced, that is **not** what
happens, and the real mechanisms are more useful:

| naive change | what actually happens |
|---|---|
| `BOARD_MAX_LOG_BYTES = Infinity` (byte cap only) | the log **stabilises at 425,627 bytes** — the count caps still bound it — i.e. **1.62× the 256 KiB per-value cap the comments cite**, so the failure mode is a **store refusal, not an OOM** |
| all four caps → `Infinity` | **unbounded**: 22.9 MB of log by cycle 3,500 and RSS climbing 247 → 294 MB, still rising when the 300 s ceiling stopped it (bounded 256 MB heap) — this is the genuine run-away, and it needs the COUNT caps removed, not the byte cap |

The phase-2 evidence the bead points at is a different failure: `area1-suite.log` shows
`RangeError: Invalid typed array length: Infinity` from `tests/tool-exec-preview.test.ts:98`
(`new Uint8Array(EXECUTOR_BOUNDS.maxWasmBytes + 1)`) — an Infinity-into-typed-array crash in another tool's
bounds, not an OOM of the board.

## The wall itself — MEASURED, and there is no 256 KiB per-value cap

The board justifies 192 KiB with "the memory store's 256 KiB per-value cap (memory.js `MAX_VALUE_BYTES`)".
That constant does not exist in the tree, and the board writes through an injected
`memory.setTrusted` — so the wall was measured rather than assumed, using the PRODUCTION store in a real
browser (`cap-evidence/bfbd-store-wall-kat.ts`, run below).

```
deno run -A cap-evidence/bfbd-store-wall-kat.ts <outDir>
```
It imports the shipped `lib/memory.js` into an extension page and writes through `masterMemory().setTrusted`
— the board's exact write function — with the board's key shape.

| value written | accepted? |
|---|---|
| 196,608 B (the board's own budget) | **yes** |
| 262,144 B (the cap the comments cite) | **yes — there is no refusal here** |
| 425,627 B (what the count caps alone allow) | **yes** |
| 1 MiB | **yes** |
| 5 MiB | **yes** |
| 20 MiB | **yes** |
| 100 MiB | **yes** |
| **400 MiB** | **yes** |

So: the store accepts 400 MiB through the board's own write path, and the "256 KiB per-value wall" the code
cites **does not exist**. All probe keys were removed afterwards.

**What this changes:** the board's caps are **not** keeping the log under a store wall — they are bounding
*operational cost*. The board folds the whole event list on every operation (`listJobs`/`foldJobEvents`) and
serializes the whole log on every write (`eventsBytes`), so the real constraint is **O(n) work per post and
per settle**, not storage. That is the number a decision should be made on, and it is why option A (archive
key) is the shape that actually reaches unbounded history without an O(n) fold over it.

## Options, with what each costs and what it breaks
| option | what it costs | what it breaks / risks |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Keep the caps; add the archive key** (evict settled jobs to an archive keyed `board:job:<id>`, keep a pointer in the log; GC on a schedule) | a new store surface, an archive reader for the owner UI, and a GC policy | needs the **retention decision** (below); a viewer that ignores the pointer shows a job with no result |
| **B. Raise the byte budget** | one constant — and it is **available**: the store accepted 400 MiB, so there is no wall to hit | buys only a constant factor, because the fold is O(n) per operation: a 10× bigger log is ~10× the work per post and per settle |
| **C. Move the log out of the per-value store (OPFS append-only + index)** | a new IO path, migration, and compaction on the file | the largest change; loses the single-value atomicity the current writes have |
| **D. Leave as is, document the caps as deliberate** | a doc edit | the P0 directive ("remove ALL self-imposed caps") stays unmet; nothing breaks |

## Recommendation, and the decisions Paul actually has to make
Recommendation: **A**, now with the wall question settled. The measurement removes the argument for keeping
192 KiB as a *store* requirement — it was never one — and replaces it with the honest one: the log is folded
in full on every operation, so its size is a *latency* bound. Unbounded history therefore wants to live
somewhere that is not folded (the archive key), not in a bigger log (B buys a constant factor at O(n) cost)
and not necessarily in a different substrate (C is the biggest change for a gain A already provides).

Two decisions, not one:
1. **Does the board need unbounded history at all?** ("remove all caps" may mean "no arbitrary small caps",
   in which case A is scope the fleet does not need and D is honest.)
2. **If yes: where does evicted history live and for how long?** An archive key with no retention policy
   grows without bound on the owner's disk instead of in the log — so the archive needs its own answer
   (keep forever, keep N days, keep until the canvas is deleted).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW (qwen3.8-flash, fresh session) of op01-code-diff-limit-split @ 4a1990b2c. Author glm
=> different family. Ref verified on the remote BEFORE setup (`git ls-remote origin | grep op01` ->
refs/heads/op01-code-diff-limit-split @ 4a1990b2cd6f8...), per the content-first standard; and confirmed
NOT an ancestor of origin/main, so this is a genuine candidate, not an already-landed change.
Worktree ~/worktrees/cap-qwen-op01-review-20260925; npm ci / deno install / build:production all rc=0;
every mutant restored and re-verified green (16/0) with no stray Infinity left in the file.

VERDICT: **PASS.** Both acceptance criteria verified by my own mutations rather than by reading the
diff, and both hold exactly.

1) VALUES UNCHANGED — mechanically checked, not eyeballed. I extracted every key from the old flat
   CODE_DIFF_LIMITS and from all three new blocks (DOC/RETENTION/VIEW) and compared as name/value pairs:
   before=12, after=12, **identical=12, changed=0, added=0, removed=0**. The split is purely structural.
   Consumption rewiring also checked, because that is where a split actually breaks rather than in the
   const block: no consumer anywhere in extension/, shared/, tests/ or scripts/ still references the old
   merged symbol; each new authority is genuinely used (DOC 11 refs / RETENTION 10 / VIEW 9 across 2-3
   files), so no authority is stranded-but-imported. The only remaining mentions of CODE_DIFF_LIMITS are
   an explanatory comment and a test that asserts the merged const is GONE
   (tests/code-diff-artifacts.test.ts:401) — an anti-reconvergence pin, which is the right instinct: it
   stops a later lane helpfully re-merging the blocks and silently reintroducing the OOM.
   extension/shared/diff-core.js is a one-line comment rename only, consistent with the new authority.

2) THE ACCEPTANCE DRILL — I ran BOTH directions, which is what proves it is a separation rather than a
   renaming. Baseline: 16 passed / 0 failed in 410 ms.
   A) LIFT THE VIEW CAPS ONLY (set all three CODE_DIFF_VIEW_LIMITS values to Infinity, retention
      untouched) -> **14 passed / 2 failed**, and the two failures are exactly the view-named tests:
        "unified and side-by-side views hash authoritative CAS, bound lines, neutralize controls, and
         keep binary metadata-only"
        "views refuse missing/mismatched CAS, invalid UTF-8 and total line budget"
      NO retention or doc test failed, and **there was no OOM and no hang** — the run completed in
      ~183 ms. That is precisely the acceptance: dptw's view-limit removal fails ONLY the view tests,
      retention stays green, nothing blows up. Before this split the same edit took the whole file down.
   B) LIFT THE RETENTION CAPS ONLY (view untouched) -> the retention test fails by name ("retention
      preflights missing/extra/digest/size and per-blob caps with zero partial writes") and then the
      process dies on a REAL HEAP OOM: "Reached heap Limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of
      memory", exit 133. So the memory-safety budget is still load-bearing and still announces itself
      catastrophically when violated — the split confines the danger, it does not disguise it. That is
      the correct asymmetry and the strongest evidence the authorities were split along the real seam
      rather than for tidiness.

   NOTE ON MY OWN METHOD, so nobody repeats it: my first pass at (A) wrapped the run in
   `ulimit -v 4000000` to catch an OOM, which produced a Trace/breakpoint trap that looked like the OOM
   I was testing for. It was my own harness — V8 reserves large virtual address space, so an
   address-space rlimit kills a healthy run. The real verdicts came from unbounded runs reading the
   actual failure text. If a future reviewer reports an OOM here, check whether they capped the process.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND op01: dptw is an epic about removing self-imposed size caps, and until this
split the safe path for any lane doing that work was to hit a heap OOM and conclude the caps were
load-bearing globally. Now a lane can lift view limits locally, see two named test failures, and leave
retention alone. That converts a trap into a legible boundary.

NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATION (no change requested): nothing pins direction (B). No test asserts that
violating the retention budget fails by name rather than OOMing the process — the preflight test covers
the semantics, and the OOM is only something I discovered by experiment. That is acceptable: it is hard
to assert on a heap exhaustion without deliberately inviting one, and the bead's premise already records
the measurement. Mentioning it only so the record shows it was considered, not missed.

STATE: **PASS, ready to land.** Values provably unchanged, both drill directions behave as claimed, no
stale consumers, and the anti-reconvergence pin is a nice touch. Base is behind main (merge-base
f6d8e48e5) — extension/lib/code-diff-artifacts.js and extension/shared/diff-core.js moved on main since
then, so rebase and re-run this one file before pushing; it is a 410 ms gate.

title: Full suite is not --parallel-safe: dist-marker order dependence (build-bootstrap must precede bundled-tool-packages)
description:
Discovered while measuring deno test --parallel behaviour for chrome-agent-platform-9hoc.

Observed: the full suite runs SERIAL by default (deno test runs modules one at a time; 8x4s probe = 33s serial vs 4s --parallel). --parallel would cut the 345s gate massively, but it is NOT safe today:
- tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts runs 'node build.mjs --target=store' and regenerates the dist.complete marker (target=store) in extension/dist-versions/
- tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts + tool-exec-preview.test.ts validate that marker with expectedTarget store
- Alphabetical serial order self-heals (build-bootstrap < bundled-tool-packages). Under --parallel the validator can run before/while the regenerator runs -> false reds (measured: bundled-tool-packages + tool-exec-preview + security-suite-custody FAIL under --parallel, all PASS serially).
- Reproduced deterministically: deno test -A --parallel on the 7-file hazard set fails; the same files serial pass.
- Also observed: after a developer build (marker target=developer), bundled-tool-packages.test.ts alone fails 'expected store, got developer' — marker state is ambient and order-dependent.

Acceptance: make --parallel safe for the full suite (order-independent dist marker custody — e.g. the marker validators tolerate/regenerate a store marker themselves, or dist-marker tests serialize) OR document --parallel as out of scope and keep the serial gate. Subset picker (9hoc) already runs subsets serial to match gate semantics exactly.
close_reason: Resolved by the two-phase runner landed at 72c5857e: the 7 dist/artifact-mutating files run serially, the other 327 with --parallel. Full-suite --parallel of every file remains unsafe by design; a guard test pinning serial-set membership is filed as a follow-up.

title: Agents never clean up the tabs/windows they open — encourage + support lifecycle cleanup (tool descriptions, skills, and a cleanup affordance)
description:
Owner feature request 2026-09-02: when an agent plans with tab-opening tools (tabs.open / new tab, new window, etc.), it never cleans up after itself — tabs stay open long after the task ends. The tab count grows across tasks and the owner closes them by hand.

GOAL: agents tidy up after themselves — without breaking the cases where leaving a tab open IS the point (e.g. 'open this article for me').

WORK:
1. AUDIT the lifecycle-bearing tools: tabs.open, window creation, tabs create/select, capture flows, any tool that creates persistent browser state. List each with what it leaves behind.
2. TOOL DESCRIPTIONS: each lifecycle tool's description gets explicit cleanup guidance for the model: state what it opens, that the agent should close what it no longer needs (tabs.close) when the task that motivated it is complete, and that leaving things open should be a deliberate choice told to the user ('left the docs tab open for you').
3. SKILL: a first-party cleanup skill (e.g. browser-tidy) the system prompt/skill promotion can surface: after finishing a task, review what you opened; close scratch tabs; report what you left open and why.
4. RUN-END HOOK (the real teeth): on task/run completion, the run summary includes the tabs/windows the run OPENED (they're already tracked in the tool catalog/usage), so cleanup is one obvious step — and consider an optional owner setting: 'auto-close tabs opened by a finished task (except ones the agent flagged as keepers)'. Default OFF (owner trust), surfaced in Settings.
5. Falsification tests: description guidance present on every lifecycle tool (a test that walks the lifecycle tool list and asserts each description mentions cleanup); the run-end summary lists opened tab ids; the auto-close setting (if implemented) closes exactly the run's tabs and nothing else.

Related: chrome-agent-platform-jb0a/kmpq/p45y are unrelated; this is behaviour-shaping + tooling, not a cap.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
OPTIONS PAPER — the product name (Q11), decision-ready. The surface is measured: 'Chrome Agent Platform' appears **84 times across 59 files** on main; the USER-FACING subset is small (manifest name:4, _locales/en/messages.json ×2, artifact/artifacts/options HTML titles, options About-brand div, and system-prompts.js:110 — the hub agent's own identity sentence); the rest is docs/comments. Repo/CLI/package identifiers (chrome-agent-platform) are internal and separable.

HARD CONSTRAINT: the Chrome Web Store rejects extension names using the 'Chrome' mark — so the DISPLAY name must drop 'Chrome' before WEBSTORE-RELEASE-01 regardless of taste. The deck should carry the same display name.

OPTIONS:
1. **'Agent Platform'** (drop 'Chrome' only) — smallest conceptual change; cost identical to any rename (~12-18 user-facing files + docs tail). Weakness: generic, store-search collisions, weak deck title.
2. **'Agent Hub' (or 'The Agent Hub')** — RECOMMENDED. It is already the product's own word: PRODUCT.md defines it as 'a new-tab agent hub that orchestrates the web', the UI's home IS the hub, and the system prompt says 'You are the … hub agent'. Zero new vocabulary to teach; the deck title writes itself ('Agent Hub — your agents, one new tab away'). Cost: the same mechanical rename + one sentence reword in system-prompts.js (a behavioral surface — pin/check the hub-agent copy tests after).
3. **A coined, ownable name** (Paul's taste; shortlist only as placeholders) — strongest for store search + trademark, highest taste-risk and longest decision time. Grounded candidates: 'Attendant' (the operator-desk framing the identity model already uses), 'Hivemind'-class names (collision-heavy — avoid).
4. **Defer** — keep the placeholder for the deck. Not recommended if the deck is imminent: the deck name would be the placeholder, and the Store rename debt grows.

RECOMMENDATION: **Option 2 ('Agent Hub')**, with the repo/CLI/package identifiers UNCHANGED (chrome-agent-platform stays as the internal name — decoupling display from identifiers is the cheap half), the docs tail (59 files) updated opportunistically, and the system-prompts.js identity sentence reviewed as the one behavioral surface (it is pinned by the hub-agent copy tests).

ADOPTION COST of the recommended option (measured): user-facing surface ≈ 10-14 files (manifest name, _locales ×2-3, HTML titles ×3-4, options About-brand, system-prompts identity line, README/PRODUCT/AGENTS headers); docs tail follows opportunistically; no package/repo/CLI renames required for the display decision.

comments.text:
Addressed all reviewer findings from deepseek/deepseek-flash review:

1. P0 (Gated on keyless demo model):
   - In dispatchScheduledWorkerTask, check getProviderConfig() and agent.provider; if provider !== 'demo', return null and fall back cleanly to SW runTask to preserve real model inference until worker model proxy (P3) is wired.

2. P1-1 (Fence enforcement & live run control):
   - liveRecord in runControl now includes isFencedOut: () => Boolean(fence?.signal?.aborted).
   - In agent-worker.tool, reject immediately with 'run_fenced_out' if live.isFencedOut().
   - On fence abort, immediately unregister live run control (runControl?.unregister(executionId)) before dispatching stop-run steer.

3. P1-2 (Per-agent memory journal append):
   - resolveJournalStore in service-worker.js handles agent:<id>, background:<name>, bare instanceId, and bare alarm names.
   - Workers relay journalTarget to agent-worker.progress, correctly routing tool events to named/background agent stores.

4. P1-3 (Canonical durable log normalizer):
   - In agent-worker.progress, normalize tool events via normalizeDurableLog, ensuring canonical tool, callId, and id properties for thread projection cards while preserving toolName.

5. P2 Findings addressed:
   - P2-1: Scheduled tasks with multimodal attachments fall back to SW runTask.
   - P2-2: Gated markScheduledDone on explicit scheduleName && scheduleToken.
   - P2-3: Added callId/nonce suffix to logKey in agent-worker.progress to prevent same-millisecond deduplication drops.
   - P2-4: Cleared 120s timeout timer in finally block.
   - P2-5: Settled admitted durable run with phase 'failed' if worker dispatch fails.
   - P2-6: Used 'default' agentId for unnamed background scheduled tasks to prevent alive-set bloat.
   - P2-7: Removed .catch(() => {}) on fallback markScheduledDone.
   - Lifecycle order fix: Called onRunSettled AFTER markScheduledDone in agent-worker.result so handleAlarm's finally block does not release the in-flight lock before the one-shot payload is consumed.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Reroutes scheduled agent alarm executions in extension/background/service-worker.js handleAlarm through agent-worker.dispatch to the per-agent SharedWorker host when developer features are enabled. WHY: Scheduled agent tasks previously bypassed the Phase 4 SharedWorker execution architecture and ran inline in the service worker because runTask's fence, journal, and attribution mechanisms had not yet been decomposed into SW-side callbacks.
EFFECT: Scheduled agent tasks now execute inside dedicated background workers under the Phase 4 architecture when developer features are enabled, reducing service worker load while preserving full durable attribution, run fencing, and memory journal integrity.

comments.text:
PLAN (bak-k3, 2026-09-26) — Merge built-in recipe-backed background agents into the named-agent store.

DESIGN: every built-in background skill becomes a SEEDED named-agent record (derived from backgroundSkills(), never persisted unless edited): { id: skill.id, name, role: '', skills: [skill], builtin: true, seeded: true, surfaceRef: 'background:<id>', memoryKey: 'recipe:<id>', defaultSchedule: { periodInMinutes } }. The surfaceRef/memoryKey overrides keep EXISTING attribution + OPFS memory + journals byte-identical — zero data loss; e5oe keeps the physical recipe: renames as future cleanup.

SLICES:
1. lib/agent-seeds.js (pure): seed derivation, seedOverlay (persisted wins), projectUnifiedAgents filter (a disabled seed is a template, never an agent row — preserves the current hub contract). + tests.
2. named-agents.js: listNamedAgents/getNamedAgent overlay seeds; mutation fns refuse seed ids ('built-in — duplicate to customize'); SW enrichAgentsWithSchedules sets live enabled on seeds. + tests.
3. Service worker: (a) agent: fire branch + runNamedAgentTask + named-agent.history honor record surfaceRef/memoryKey overrides; (b) background-agent.set on a BUILT-IN id delegates to applyAgentSchedule (mints agent:<id> with the skill prompt + period, hooks subscribe/unsubscribe unchanged, cancels legacy recipe:<id>) — custom duplicated skills keep the recipe: path; (c) background-agent.list dual-reads enabled from agent:<id> OR recipe:<id>; (d) startup re-key migration (extracted lib, mint-then-cancel: scheduleTask agent:<id> preserving at/task/period/owner, then await cancel recipe:<id>.marked — the alarm handler skips cancelling payloads, so no double-fire; failure leaves the recipe: task live for next-startup retry). + tests driving the real extracted module.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW: PASS, with non-blocking findings (uplift-opus, Claude Opus, 2026-09-29). Candidate bak-k3-wz6i @ e40ca99d8 (66ff6dd48 plus the committed KAT), author bak-k3 (k3, a different family).  Nothing merged.

GATES in a fresh detached worktree (npm ci, deno install, build:production, clean tree):
- npm test: serial phase 17/18. The one red is the known hang in tests/build-tool-bundling.test.ts "regen idempotence" ("HUNG: no exit within 120s ... futex_do_wait", chrome-agent-platform-fnmr); that file passes 7/0 in 1 s on its own. A red serial phase makes run-tests.mjs skip the parallel phase, so I ran that phase the way run-tests.mjs does (partition() from scripts/test-partition.mjs, deno test -A --config deno.runner.jsonc --parallel, CAP_TEST_RUNNER=1): 491 files, 4592 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, matching the author's count. Tree clean afterwards.
- scripts/kat-background-agent-store.ts, now committed and registered: 14/0 in a real loaded extension (Chrome for Testing). It reads through wireValue and derives ROOT with fileURLToPath, so the kwrx and e273 guards stay green.
- The new tests can fail. Three planted bugs each turn them red (baseline 44/0): a failed mint still cancels the legacy task -> "rekey: a mint failure leaves the legacy task LIVE"; create may shadow a seed -> "createNamedAgent refuses to shadow a built-in seed id"; a disabled seed becomes a row -> the isVisibleAgentRow test and the projection test.

WHAT HOLDS
- Seeds are derived; a persisted record wins the overlay; create, update and delete refuse seed ids before any approval gate or teardown.
- The memory directory: every path that runs a built-in writes backgroundAgentMemory("recipe:<id>") (the agent: fire branch, runNamedAgentTask, named-agent.history, the hook fire, background-agent.run), so its journal stays in one place.
- Attribution: a durable record's agentId is agentSurfaceRef, "background:<id>" for a scheduled fire on both the new and the legacy path, so the hub timeline label is unchanged.
- No wider paid-tool access: runTask turns a missing providerServerAgentId into null, and the legacy recipe fire passed null too.
- recoverOnBoot() is now called twice at module load; it memoises one promise (lib/scheduler.js), so that is harmless.
- The two edited tests (named-agents-provider, sched-attr) still pin their properties.

SHOULD FIX
1. "runs/journals/attribution are byte-identical" overstates it. The memory directory and attribution match; the run does not. A scheduled fire of a built-in now has runKind "agent" (was "scheduled"), scheduleName "agent:<id>" (was "recipe:<id>"), agentRole "" (was "background:<id>"), promptScope "agent:<id>" (was none, so an agent-scope prompt override now applies) and agentSkills [the skill]. The task text is still skill.prompt; if the orchestrator composes the whole skill from agentSkills, the Sorting Hat's instructions appear twice (not traced that far).
2. named-agent.grep reads namedAgentMemory(agent.instanceId || slug). It was not made override-aware like history, run and fire, so for a built-in it searches a directory the agent never writes.
3. One built-in now has three runners that compose differently: the scheduled fire (agent branch, agent-scope prompt, skills), the hook fire (agentRole "recipe:<id>", no prompt scope, no skills) and background-agent.run (agentRole "background:<id>"). An agent-scope prompt override reaches only the scheduled fires.
4. A persisted agent created before this build whose slug equals a built-in id (an owner agent named "Auto group by domain", say) wins the overlay; the new create guard only stops new ones. Enabling the built-in then schedules agent:<id>, which fires as the OWNER's agent (their role, skills and memory) running the Sorting Hat prompt, and the startup re-key re-mints agent:<id> from the legacy payload over the owner's own schedule (scheduleTask replaces by name). Narrow, but silent. Check for a persisted record at the seed id in the set branch and the re-key; skip and log the conflict.
5. The fire, run and history paths honor memoryKey/surfaceRef on ANY record. Only seedRecordForSkill sets them today and the write paths build explicit fields, but agentsMap reads cap:namedAgents raw, so a restored or hand-edited store could point one agent at another's memory. Honor them only when agent.seeded === true.
6. The re-key mints agent:<id> unconditionally. After a cancel-after-mint failure (documented and tested: both stay live until the next boot), an owner edit to agent:<id> in between is overwritten by the next boot's re-key.
7. The KAT stops at enable, row and disable; nothing fires a run. The identity claims rest on code reading (which supports them for directory and attribution) and source pins. A KAT leg that fires one run and asserts the durable record's agentId and journal directory would close that, as the plan's own acceptance asked.
Nits: a past-due legacy `at` falls forward a full period (tested as intended), so a missed catch-up run is dropped and "exact next-fire" holds only when the next fire is in the future; if recoverOnBoot() rejects, the chained re-key waits for the next worker start.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DECISION RESOLVED: Tabular Artifact Promotion (docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #16)

DECISION:
Adopt single-body artifact storage and formally defer grouped chunked promotion.

RATIONALE:
1. Architectural Consistency:
   • Under owner directive dptw (2026-09-03), ASSET_BOUNDS.maxContentBytes was set to Infinity in extension/lib/artifacts.js.
   • Artifacts are stored whole as single-body documents rather than clipped or partitioned into chunks, aligning with the platform's unbounded data architecture.

2. Complexity & Risk Avoidance:
   • Grouped chunked promotion requires atomic cross-chunk reservations, ref-counting, and distributed orphan collection across digest-keyed fragments.
   • Single-body storage cleanly avoids this failure surface without compromising data fidelity.

3. Status:
   • Resolved in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q16 (commit 33eb9121 / u51).
   • Single-body storage retained; chunked promotion deferred.

3. Status:
