title: durable-root free-disk reserve measures $HOME instead of the durable root when the parent dir is missing (scripts/lib/durable-root.mjs:114)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-yc91a delta 21977174..5b9f3bf7 (5b9f3bf7 = c81f0b4a rebased + 1 commit, 10 files, +189/-44) on branch fleet/yc91a.

DEFECT: the new iqt8f byte bound (commit 5b9f3bf7, scripts/lib/durable-root.mjs:113-121) chooses its statfs anchor as `existsSync(parent) ? parent : homedir()`. When the immediate parent does not exist yet, free space is measured on HOMEs filesystem rather than on the filesystem that will receive the directory, so the reserve can miss the disk it exists to protect (fail-open: target fs full, $HOME has room -> creation allowed) or refuse a creation that is perfectly safe (fail-closed: $HOME full, target fs empty). The correct anchor is the nearest EXISTING ancestor of `dir` (which is durableRoot() itself for the common single-part call `durableDir("acp-cwd-<ts>")` before the root exists).

Repro (proven; run from a worktree at 5b9f3bf7):
  $ CAP_DURABLE_ROOT=/home/exedev/rev-yc91a-repro/rootB CAP_DURABLE_DIR_MIN_FREE_BYTES=999999999999999 node -e "import(\"/abs/path/scripts/lib/durable-root.mjs\").then(m=>{try{m.durableDir(\"missing-parent\",\"child\")}catch(e){console.log(e.message)}})"
  THROW: CAP_DURABLE_DIR_MIN_FREE_BYTES exceeded: /home/exedev has 1943162880 bytes free (reserve 999999999999999, requested /home/exedev/rev-yc91a-repro/rootB/missing-parent/child)
  ...the anchor named in the message is $HOME, not rootB.
  Control, same env, parent present (the correct path): anchor is the durable root ->
  THROW: CAP_DURABLE_DIR_MIN_FREE_BYTES exceeded: /home/exedev/rev-yc91a-repro/rootB has 1487155200 bytes free (...)
  Pre-fix control: the base module (21977174:scripts/lib/durable-root.mjs) has no reserve at all and creates both dirs without error.

REACHABILITY, measured: this VM has exactly one real filesystem (/ ext4; every other mount is tmpfs/selinuxfs), so with CAP_DURABLE_ROOT on / or under $HOME the wrong anchor is harmless TODAY - do not read this as a live incident. It becomes real wherever CAP_DURABLE_ROOT is on a second volume (the module own error text and AGENTS.md:840 both tell operators to point CAP_DURABLE_ROOT at a disk-backed directory, and this release note advertises the reserve as the disk bound), or for any `durableDir(a,b)` whose `a` does not exist yet. Filed P3 on that basis: latent, zero reachability on the fleet VM.

Evidence: probe script /home/exedev/rev-yc91a-repro/probe.mjs (cases B2/B3), tip module copy /home/exedev/rev-yc91a-repro/tip.mjs. Reviewed delta behaviours reproduced in the same session: entry-cap validation (abc/0/-1 -> named error), 5GiB reserve -> named error, reserve=0 -> allowed, nested missing parent -> wrong anchor, 2-entry cap -> third dir refused; tests/durable-root.test.ts 11/11 and tests/acp-service-harness-default.test.ts 10/10 pass at 5b9f3bf7 (private CAP_DURABLE_ROOT).

Fix owner: chrome-agent-platform-yc91a (branch fleet/yc91a author; muse-msp/muse-wonder-full-1.0).

title: New runner module re-declares the environmental-verdict constants and a second Chrome resolver instead of the single sources; its run-tests.mjs import is unused (scripts/lib/browser-prerequisite.mjs:17-18,65-95; scripts/run-tests.mjs:33)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-jy7aj delta e2bbb8bc..20e4e5ed (20e4e5ed = fleet/qazo-jy7aj tip).

WHAT IS DUPLICATED
1. The environmental verdict: scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts:740/757 defines ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT = 75 and ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER = "CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL" as the repo's canonical values (pinned by tests/quiet-window.test.ts:349-352). scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts:12 and scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts:35 import them, and browser-refusal.ts's own header states the point: the verdict and its wording should "exist in ONE place" so the two cannot drift. The new scripts/lib/browser-prerequisite.mjs:17-18 declares its OWN copies of the same two constants.
2. A second Chrome resolver: browser-prerequisite.mjs:65-95 re-implements the puppeteer-cache glob, the version parsing, the subpath list and the newest-executable selection that scripts/lib/chrome-for-testing.ts already owns ("Resolution order, ONE place, every consumer", chrome-launch.ts:157-166).

WHY IT MATTERS (measured, not argued): nothing pins the new copies. scripts/run-tests.mjs:33 imports ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT and never uses it (the refusal path uses prereq.refusal.exit), and the runner still compares the literal 75 at :233 and :242 — so the runner's own environmental verdict is now defined in three places: quiet-window.ts, browser-prerequisite.mjs, and a bare literal. The new test tests/browser-prerequisite.test.ts imports ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT/MARKER from the module under test and asserts them against that same module, so a drift between it and quiet-window.ts is caught by nothing.

The .mjs copies are not gratuitous: run-tests.mjs is executed by node (`test: node scripts/run-tests.mjs`) and cannot import the .ts modules, so some Node-visible form is needed. The finding is that the form chosen adds a second source and leaves the third one (the literal) in place.

FIX SHAPE (owner decides): one Node-visible home for the two constants (a small .mjs constants module, or a static guard test asserting the .mjs copy equals quiet-window.ts's values and the runner's refusal path uses it instead of 75), and drop the unused import at run-tests.mjs:33. For the resolver, either delegate to a Node-visible single source or add a test that pins browser-prerequisite.mjs's precedence answers to chrome-launch.ts's for the same injected inputs, so the preflight's opinion and the launch's opinion cannot diverge silently.

EVIDENCE: grep/line references above, read on the reviewed tip 20e4e5ed. No behaviour was exercised beyond the jy7aj verdict's reproductions.
FIX OWNER: chrome-agent-platform-qazo (author of fleet/qazo-jy7aj).

title: Bounded document readers have no total inflated-byte bound: a 32 KiB .xlsx expands to 31 MiB (~968x) inside the 256 KiB transport cap (extension/lib/python-documents-bundle.js:176,200,249)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-x7n6o delta e2bbb8bc..3f8cd276 (tip 3f8cd276, tree 896e3de0), branch fleet/j5yz-3p3e11.
Repro: python3 /home/exedev/cap-evidence/rev-x7n6o-20261016/repro_all.py /tmp/rev-doc-bundle.js   (F3 section)
Observed: an .xlsx whose worksheets each hold one 10 MiB inlineStr cell compresses to 32509 bytes and declares 31457552 bytes of member inflate (968x); load_workbook parses all 3 sheets successfully in 0.19s (CPython) and hands executeReadSpreadsheet 10485260-byte cell strings. MAX_ZIP_MEMBER_BYTES caps only EACH member (:176, checks at :200 and :249) and the JS side caps only the base64 transport string at 256 KiB (MAX_DOCUMENT_TRANSPORT_BYTES); nothing bounds the SUM. c1c0 has no inflate cap at all, and a streaming zip is not bounded by the transport cap.
Expected: a total inflated-byte (or member-count x member-size) admission bound that fails closed with document_incomplete, so the documented 256 KiB transport cap is a real bound on parse work. As written the documented cap reads lower than the work it permits.
Impact: a small hostile or merely pathological attachment can force hundreds of MiB of transient XML/ElementTree work (transport-cap-sized payload ~ 190 KiB zip -> ~600x). In the offscreen Pyodide worker that is a stall/OOM risk for the whole document tool; it degrades to an explicit failure if the WASM heap rejects the allocation, not to data loss. Sandbox contains it to the worker, hence P3 rather than P2.
Evidence: /home/exedev/cap-evidence/rev-x7n6o-20261016/repro_all.py (F3), repro_inflate3.py. Measured on review tip a89f61af9cc0b4b257c9d0c6aa3a3244499579639fb7d5de968813eb2f664978.

title: Enclave proxy: distinguish an unauthorised redirect from other refused redirects (future enhancement)
description: Filed on the hub decision for fpb0 (option b, deferred as a future product enhancement rather than done now). The refused-redirect path matches res.type === opaqueredirect, and an opaqueredirect carries status 0 and NO headers by construction, so the proxy cannot see a 401 or 403 there and an unauthorised redirect is indistinguishable from any other refused redirect. Delivering a real rejected-token state therefore requires changing proxy behaviour, which is security-relevant and is why fpb0 took the narrow option instead (drop the unproduced auth_failed and timeout codes from the declared set). If Paul wants the distinction, this bead is the place: it needs a mechanism that infers or preserves authorisation failure across the refused-redirect boundary without weakening the refusal itself - for example a probe or a marker that does not require reading the opaque response. Evidence and mechanism context on fpb0: auth_failed has no producer, timeout likewise unproduced, connection_failed comes from enclave-proxy.js:433/438 plus a fallback, redirect_refused from :451/456, and provider-test.js:31 returns an off-contract auth for 401/403 that the vault would degrade to connection_failed.

title: CAP's ledger cannot satisfy the fleet's GATE-COVERAGE-MANIFEST contract, so the strongest producer form is unavailable to the fast gate
description:
Found while activating the fast gate (chrome-agent-platform-dj2yd), by reading fleet-check's declared contract fields instead of guessing them, then having the verifier reject my first attempt.

WHAT HAPPENED: I declared CHECK_FAST_MANIFEST_RE='^fast-gate: manifest: ' - CAP's own ledger line. fleet-check accepted the declaration but its producer verifier then refused to certify the run: state UNKNOWN, reason 'final line is not a well-formed declared manifest with graph and numeric failed outcome'. A green run (tip 0463ac4f, cmd 'npm run gate:fast', rc 0, 390 passed / 0 failed) therefore recorded UNKNOWN instead of PASS.

WHY: the fleet's manifest contract is a different wire format from CAP's ledger. ~/fleet/remote/producer-verdict.py requires the COMPLETE FINAL LINE to match the declaration and to parse as space-separated key=value fields with graph=<decision> and failed=<numeric> - the GATE-COVERAGE-MANIFEST shape. CAP's scripts/lib/gate-manifest.mjs emits 'fast-gate: manifest: {json}' mid-log, followed by the runner's own summary lines, so it can never be the final line and never carries graph=/failed= in that form.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE (dj2yd): the CAP conf now declares CHECK_FAST_PASS_RE='^select-tests: parallel phase GREEN' instead, keeping CHECK_FAST_COVERAGE_REQUIRED=1 so the coverage the extractor reads out of CAP's manifest is still mandatory. Verified as a falsifier would want: the regex matches the real green gate log (verifier: state PASS, producer_line 'select-tests: parallel phase GREEN in 22s') and matches ZERO real red gate logs (two logged red runs: state UNKNOWN, 'no declared producer PASS line in final gate attempt'). Note the obvious-looking alternative is unusable: the passed-count line has ANSI escapes inside it ([32mok[0m | N passed | 0 failed), so no ^ok regex ever matches the raw bytes.

OPTIONS (owner's call, nothing taken unilaterally): (a) make CAP's ledger ALSO emit a fleet-shaped final line (graph= + numeric failed=) when the fast gate runs, and switch the conf to the manifest form; (b) get the fleet verifier to accept CAP's JSON manifest form; (c) leave it - the PASS-line contract plus required coverage is honest, just weaker (it certifies 'the phase went green', not 'the producer's own structured receipt says graph=... failed=0'). (a) looks cheapest and keeps CAP's rich disclosure.
Triage to coord.

title: [fleet] the subagent harness silently falls back to another model when a provider 401s, so a lane can cite a review as family X when family Y ran it
description:
Found while landing chrome-agent-platform-bverr, after coord noted that openai-codex/gpt-6-sol is 401-dead fleet-wide tonight (hub measured all twelve VMs and pinned mergers to deepseek for it).

WHAT HAPPENED
- I dispatched two reviewer subagents asking for openai-codex/gpt-6-sol (:high). Both runs COMPLETED normally and returned detailed verdicts - no error was surfaced to me - so I recorded both as gpt-6-sol reviews.
- The run events tell a different story: run 6578eeb9 (bverr) names "model":"gemini-3.8-flash" 152 times with 401 and fallback entries in the same file, and run 75354a0b (iwu1z) names "model":"gemini-3.8-flash" 120 times with 17 401 entries. The assistant turns in the bverr run's session file record model gemini-3.8-flash only. Both reviews were really executed by antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash, and both made real tool calls (bverr's: 30 bash, 5 read, 2 grep), so the evidence in them is genuine - the ATTRIBUTION was wrong, not the work.

WHY IT MATTERS (near miss)
- The fleet's rule is that a different model FAMILY reviews every change. A silent fallback can land the reviewer on the implementer's own family: a deepseek implementer whose reviewer falls back to deepseek would satisfy every visible check while violating the rule, and nothing in the lane's record would show it. Here it landed on gemini-3.8-flash, which is a different family from the deepseek implementer, so the independence held by luck rather than by design.
- It also means two 'independent' verdicts can be one model twice: both of my reviews were gemini-3.8-flash.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT (owner's call; nothing taken unilaterally)
(a) harness: fail loudly instead of substituting, or (b) record the EFFECTIVE model in the run status/events where a lane can read it without parsing session transcripts, or (c) at minimum surface a fallback notice in the child's returned result. Process stopgap until then: a lane must verify the effective model (async run events/session) before citing a review as an independent-family verdict, and should name the model that actually ran.
Triage to coord/hub.

title: [fleet] the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl export moves during a run whenever a lane writes to its bead, so the gate witness can STALE on bookkeeping
description:
Found while landing chrome-agent-platform-bverr (the STALE-witness fix). SECOND independent cause of the same witness failure, and unlike bverr it is not CAP code.

EVIDENCE
- `git ls-files --error-unmatch .beads/issues.jsonl` -> TRACKED, in every worktree. The beads docs describe this file as a passive export, but git tracks it, and `bd comment` / `bd dolt push` rewrite it in place.
- Measured in ~/worktrees/chrome-agent-platform-imp-0eq00-idem: right after a `bd comment ... ; bd dolt push`, `stat -c '%n %z' .beads/issues.jsonl` read 2026-10-14 23:42:18.560Z.
- The fleet witness digests `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 stat -c '%n %s %z'` (nsec ctime + size, no content) over every tracked file at gate start and end. So a bookkeeping write inside that window moves a tracked file's ctime and the record reads STALE with reason "the worktree's CONTENT changed during the run without a commit", with git status CLEAN and the code under test untouched.
- Near miss, same minute: my bverr fast gate (asked 23:42:25Z, PASS, 372 passed) had that file written at 23:42:18Z - 7s before the start snapshot. Land it inside the run and the gate STALEs over a bead comment.

IMPACT
Any lane that comments on or pushes its bead while its own gate is running can red its own record, in any project that uses this gate shape with these beads settings. It is timing-dependent, so it reads as a flake and wastes a whole gate (measured cost of one wasted full gate: ~350s).

OPTIONS, none of which I took unilaterally (owner/policy decision)
(a) repo: stop tracking .beads/issues.jsonl (it is documented as a passive export) - touches tracking only, no code;
(b) process: no bd writes in a worktree while its gate is running - cheap but a coin flip without a lock;
(c) fleet-side: the witness ignores that path - hub-owned tooling, same shape as the bverr twin 6v1bf.
Triage to coord/hub.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/fleet-check-stale-paths.test.sh — chrome-agent-platform-4kyqm: A STALE VERDICT MUST NAME THE WRITER.
#
# THE DEFECT (measured 2026-10-14): a full union gate ran 351s and was recorded STALE because a tracked file
# changed while the suites ran. The record said "the worktree's CONTENT changed during the run without a
# commit" and stopped there, so the writer (the .beads export and the docs/diff-core.bundle.js sync are the
# known in-run writers) had to be guessed, and finding out costs another whole gate.
#
# THE FIX: on a STALE verdict the record carries .stale_paths - the git status --porcelain lines for TRACKED
# files, bounded, paths only. This test is built to the DEFECT, not to the fix: each arm's command must prove
# it actually changed the tree (its marker must appear in the log) before the assertion is read, so an arm that
# silently did nothing is reported as a skip rather than a pass.
#
# SELF-CONTAINED: its own heavy queue and slots so it can never queue behind a real gate; its own HOME; FLEET_LANE
# is a fixture so no notification can reach a real lane. CHECK_OVERRIDE points it at any fleet-check under test.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/fleet-4kyqm.XXXXXX)
cleanup() { rm -rf "$ROOT"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

PASS=0; FAIL=0
pass() { echo "  ok   $1"; PASS=$((PASS + 1)); }
fail() { echo "  FAIL $1: $2"; FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); }
skip() { echo "  SKIP $1: $2"; }

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)

# A LANE ENVIRONMENT EXPORTS FLEET_CHECK_CONF (the machine-wide per-project conf), which takes precedence over
# the fixture's $HOME/.fleet/check.conf and makes every arm here run the REAL project gates. The upstream
# stability test does not do this because it is run outside a lane; this one must be safe inside one.
unset FLEET_CHECK_CONF
CHECK="${CHECK_OVERRIDE:-$HERE/bin/fleet-check}"
export FLEET_HEAVY_DIR="$ROOT/heavy"; mkdir -p "$FLEET_HEAVY_DIR"
export FLEET_HEAVY_SLOTS=2
export FLEET_LANE="4kyqm-test"

# No network from a fixture: the notification POST must not reach a real lane, and must not be the reason an
# arm is slow. Unset FLEET_CHECK_TEST_HOLD (below), this forwards nothing.
mkdir -p "$ROOT/bin"
cat > "$ROOT/bin/curl" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 0
STUB
chmod +x "$ROOT/bin/curl"
export PATH="$ROOT/bin:$PATH"

# run_arm NAME EXPECTED_STATE CHECK_FAST_CMD EXPECTED_PATH_MAX MARKER
# Builds a clean repo with TWO tracked files, runs a fast gate whose command touches the tree, and prints the
# verdict. EXPECTED_PATH_MAX bounds the captured lines (CAP_STALE_PATHS_MAX).
run_arm() {
  local name="$1" expected="$2" cmd="$3" path_max="$4" marker="$5"
  local T R rec state
  T=$(mktemp -d "$ROOT/arm.XXXXXX"); R="$T/repo"
  git init -q -b main "$R"
  git -C "$R" config user.email test@example.com
  git -C "$R" config user.name "stale paths test"
  printf 'original' > "$R/input"
  printf 'original' > "$R/other"
  git -C "$R" add input other
  git -C "$R" commit -q -m init

  export HOME="$T/home"
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.fleet"
  {
    echo "CHECK_FAST_CMD='$cmd'"
    echo "CHECK_FAST_TIMEOUT=90"
  } > "$HOME/.fleet/check.conf"
  [ -n "$path_max" ] && export CAP_STALE_PATHS_MAX="$path_max" || unset CAP_STALE_PATHS_MAX

  ( cd "$R" && bash "$CHECK" --fast ) > "$T/out" 2>&1 || true

  rec=""
  for _ in $(seq 1 450); do
    rec=$(ls "$HOME"/.fleet/checks/*.fast.json 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
    if [ -n "$rec" ]; then
      state=$(jq -r '.state // "?"' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
      [ "$state" != "RUNNING" ] && break
    fi
    sleep 0.2
  done
  if [ -z "$rec" ] || [ -z "${state:-}" ]; then
    skip "$name" "PREMISE NOT MET: no record produced (the gate may not have run)"
    return 0
  fi
  state=$(jq -r '.state // "?"' "$rec")

  # THE PRECONDITION IS ASSERTED BEFORE THE CONSEQUENCE: a command that changed nothing proves nothing, and a
  # test that can pass because the job never ran is the defect this family of beads exists to remove. The
  # evidence is the TREE, not the output: the marker is accepted from stdout or the gate's own log, and
  # failing that the worktree itself must still carry the modification the command made. (Where a runner
  # routes its child's stdout is a property of fleet-check's logging, not of this fix, so the assertion must
  # not depend on it.)
  local status_line; status_line=$(git -C "$R" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no | tr '\n' ' ')
  if [ "$name" != "clean-run" ] && [ -z "$status_line" ] \
     && ! grep -q "$marker" "$T/out" "$HOME"/.fleet/checks/*.fast.log 2>/dev/null; then
    skip "$name" "PREMISE NOT MET: nothing in the worktree changed and the marker never appeared"
    return 0
  fi

  if [ "$state" = "$expected" ]; then
    pass "$name: verdict recorded $expected (worktree=[${status_line% }])"
  else
    fail "$name: expected $expected" "state=$state reason=$(jq -r '.state_reason // ""' "$rec" | cut -c1-120)"
  fi

  local paths
  paths=$(jq -rc '.stale_paths // empty' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ "$expected" = STALE ]; then
    if [ -n "$paths" ]; then
      pass "$name: the record names the tracked path(s) that changed: $paths"
    else
      fail "$name: a STALE record must name the writer" "no .stale_paths in $(basename "$rec")"
    fi
    # PATHS, NEVER CONTENTS: the fixture's content marker must not leak into the record. Asserted only when
    # there IS a capture: "an empty capture contains no contents" is vacuous, and a vacuous pass is how a
    # missing feature reads as covered.
    if [ -n "$paths" ]; then
      if printf '%s' "$paths" | grep -q "$marker"; then
        fail "$name: the capture leaked file CONTENT" "$paths"
      else
        pass "$name: capture carries paths only, no file contents"
      fi
    fi
  elif jq -e 'has("stale_paths")' "$rec" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "$name: a non-STALE record must not carry .stale_paths" "$paths"
  else
    pass "$name: no capture on a healthy run, so its presence is itself evidence of invalidation"
  fi
  RUN_ARM_DIR="$R"
}

# Arm 1: the measured 2026-10-14 case - a TRACKED file mutated mid-run with no commit. The record must name it.
run_arm mutate-no-commit STALE 'printf corrupt > input; echo gate-observed-$(cat input)' '' gate-observed-corrupt
if [ -n "${RUN_ARM_DIR:-}" ]; then
  captured=$(jq -rc '.stale_paths // []' "$(ls "$HOME"/.fleet/checks/*.fast.json | head -1)" 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')
  case "$captured" in
    *input*) pass "mutate-no-commit: the named path is the file the command mutated (input)" ;;
    *)       fail "mutate-no-commit: the record did not name 'input'" "$captured" ;;
  esac
fi

# Arm 2: UNTRACKED files are explicitly NOT witnessed, so naming one would misdescribe the witness. The
# capture must stay silent about them while still naming the tracked file that did change.
run_arm untracked-not-named STALE 'printf corrupt > input; printf scratch > untracked-scratch; echo gate-observed-$(cat input)' '' gate-observed-corrupt
if [ -n "${RUN_ARM_DIR:-}" ]; then
  captured=$(jq -rc '.stale_paths // []' "$(ls "$HOME"/.fleet/checks/*.fast.json | head -1)" 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')
  case "$captured" in
    *untracked-scratch*) fail "untracked-not-named: an untracked file was named" "$captured" ;;
    *input*)             pass "untracked-not-named: tracked file named, untracked file not named" ;;
    *)                   fail "untracked-not-named: the tracked file was not named" "$captured" ;;
  esac
fi

# Arm 3: BOUNDED. Two tracked files change and CAP_STALE_PATHS_MAX=1: one line plus a disclosed count, so a
# pathological run cannot make the record unbounded and a clipped capture can never look complete.
run_arm bounded STALE 'printf corrupt > input; printf corrupt > other; echo gate-observed-$(cat input)' 1 gate-observed-corrupt
if [ -n "${RUN_ARM_DIR:-}" ]; then
  rec3=$(ls "$HOME"/.fleet/checks/*.fast.json | head -1)
  len3=$(jq -r '.stale_paths | length' "$rec3" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [ "$len3" = "2" ] && jq -re '.stale_paths[] | select(test("more tracked path"))' "$rec3" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    pass "bounded: 1 named path + a disclosed clipped count (no silent truncation)"
  else
    fail "bounded: expected 1 line + a truncation disclosure" "len=$len3 lines=$(jq -rc '.stale_paths // []' "$rec3")"
  fi
fi

# Arm 4 (CONTROL): nothing touches the tree - must stay PASS and must carry no capture, or the field degrades
# into decoration that every record has and no reader can trust.
run_arm clean-run PASS 'echo gate work done' '' 'gate work done'

echo ""
echo "$PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
```

title: ADR: gates build-if-needed via dist.complete validation; every tier emits a fail-closed coverage ledger
description:
Context: production build (~95s) is paid once per tier per change (FAST prefix + merger FULL prefix, ~/.fleet/check-chrome-agent-platform.conf); FAST PASS median 153s local cache (n=190), FULL PASS median 437s (n=99). scripts/dist-complete.mjs already binds exact commit+source bytes+outputs, and tests/build-smoke.test.ts already reuses build.mjs exit-0 record, so artifact freshness is provable without rebuilding. 146 cached PASS records have coverage ABSENT and sampled present-coverage shows suites:[] with unmapped non-empty, so cached green is not yet producer-truthful.
Decision: (1) FAST tier builds only when selection consumes dist or build inputs changed, else records explicit build omission; when build is needed, validate-or-build against dist.complete, never re-stamp. FULL keeps validate-or-build; commit binding is NOT weakened to tree-only. (2) Every gate record carries producer coverage ledger {suites executed, omitted+reason, unmapped, build disposition}; unmapped/absent-ledger never reads PASS. Producer ships before any strict consumer rejection.
Consequences: expected FAST saving ~95s on non-dist changes (falsifier <60s on 3 real changes = revert); FULL union saving expected near zero and claimed only if merger measures it on >=5 NEW union trees. test:build internal builds exempt (they are the subject). test:heavy/test:chrome absence from FULL command becomes an explicit ledger omission, not implied coverage.
Alternatives considered: unconditional build (status quo, costs ~190s/change lifecycle); tree-only marker reuse across commits (rejected: version-bump hook mutates source bytes per commit; byte-determinism unproven); consumer-first strictness (rejected: would refuse 134 existing FAST PASS records before producer can emit truth). Full design on chrome-agent-platform-0eq00 architect comment 2026-10-14.

title: beads pre-commit hook re-stages .beads/issues.jsonl on every commit, causing gated-tree != pushed-tree churn
description:
P3 tooling (owner: chrome-agent-platform-merger; architect pass if a redesign is wanted). Observed during the chrome-agent-platform-5ui2q landing on 2026-10-11.

PROBLEM: the beads pre-commit hook installed in the shared git dir (chrome-agent-platform/.git/hooks/pre-commit -> 'bd hooks run pre-commit') re-exports and STAGES .beads/issues.jsonl on every commit. So a commit that is meant to change only the message or a single file silently sweeps in the whole passive export.

IMPACT: the merger full gate is cached BY TREE. The landing sequence is: merge fleet/<x> (creating the gated merge commit), run fleet-check, then amend the message with the gate record. The amend re-sweeps the export, so the pushed tree no longer equals the gated tree and 'fleet-check --status <pushed-sha>' finds no cache. On 5ui2q this produced three SHAs:
  15919e65f  amend -> tree ffc96205 (gated tree 3d0a4f52 + .beads delta)
  0c71cde4b  first restore attempt, re-swept by the same hook -> tree 113e2b2a (its message is therefore WRONG)
  4f5324283  corrective commit made with 'git commit --no-verify' -> tree 3d0a4f52 EXACTLY; 'fleet-check --status 4f5324283' => PASS

WORKAROUND USED (no force push): 'git checkout <gated-sha> -- .beads/issues.jsonl' then 'git commit --no-verify'. Verification: 'git diff --name-only <gated> HEAD | grep -v ^\.beads/' must be empty and 'fleet-check --status <sha>' must return the cached PASS.

CANDIDATE FIXES: (a) merger-side discipline - never 'git add -A', and make the amended landing commit with --no-verify after pinning .beads to the gated content; (b) stop tracking .beads/issues.jsonl at all (it is a passive export; Dolt sync uses refs/dolt/data) or gitignore it; (c) make the hook export-only, not 'git add'; (d) make the check cache key on the product tree rather than the whole tree. (b)/(c)/(d) are architect-level choices.

EVIDENCE: gated tree 3d0a4f520053937c0209bff779e342e368fd335c (gate log /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/3d0a4f52....log, PASS 6245/0/2 + build 3/3, 404s); final origin/main 4f5324283b8daeadd06c15318e7258e8cd41af63 with tree 3d0a4f52.

title: 5ui2q review-finding: the new journey test models CDP failures from assumption, not the wire — a dropped transport never rejects synchronously and a closed target is -32602, not -32000 (tests/journey-focus-fail-closed.test.ts:653-656)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-5ui2q delta a2c3d9b9d..c4eaf18ea (tip c4eaf18ea) branch fleet/qazo-5ui2q.
P3, report-only and NON-BLOCKING: the branch does fail closed (see the review verdict on 5ui2q); this is
test-shape / evidence precision only, verified by deepseek/deepseek-flash.

DEFECT
The scenarios in tests/journey-focus-fail-closed.test.ts:653-656 model CDP failure shapes the real client
never produces, so the test's "fails closed immediately ... root cause preserved" claim is stronger than
the wire behaviour it stands for.

1. The "dead transport" scenario (:655, err = "Target.activateTarget: WebSocket connection closed.") is a
   SYNCHRONOUS throw from the mock `send`. The real Cdp.send (scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:317-330) cannot
   reject synchronously for a dead transport: once the socket is CLOSED, ws.send() (:328) returns normally,
   the entry stays in `pending`, and only the 15s timer (:323-326) rejects, with message
   `cdp timeout: Target.activateTarget (requestId=<n>, targetId=..., sessionId=...)`. ws.onclose
   (:228-233) only pushes to fatalEvents; it never rejects `pending`. So on a dead transport the journey
   fails closed after UP TO 15 SECONDS with a TIMEOUT attribution, not immediately with the transport error.
   Nothing in the test exercises the real 15s path.

2. The "-32000" in the commit body and in the bead comment does not reproduce on this build; a genuinely
   closed target returns -32602.

REPRO (measured 2026-10-11 on this VM, /usr/bin/chromium --headless=new, reviewer lane rev-5ui2q; scripts
kept at /tmp/rev-5ui2q-transport.ts and /tmp/rev-5ui2q-closedtarget.ts, both bounded and self-cleaning)
A. dead transport — start chromium with --remote-debugging-port, open the debugger WebSocket, SIGKILL
   chromium, then run Cdp.send()'s exact shape:
     ws.readyState after chrome death: 3 (CLOSED)
     ws.send() returned synchronously with NO throw -> promise stays pending until the 15s timer
     REJECTED: cdp timeout: Target.activateTarget (requestId=1)
B. closed target — PUT /json/new, Target.closeTarget it, then Target.activateTarget:
     CLOSED TARGET REJECTED: cdp error 2 (-32602): No target with given id found
   (a never-existed target id gives the same -32602 on this build.)

WHY THIS IS ONLY P3
The product behaviour under review is correct in both cases: the promise rejects, the awaited call throws,
and the journey fails closed before the #home click and composer input (confirmed by the mutant RED run in
the review). Only the modelled error shape, the fail-closed latency and the attribution differ, and the
test asserts none of them. It is not a correctness or landing blocker.

SUGGESTED FIX
Model the client's real rejections rather than an invented one — add a scenario rejecting with
`cdp timeout: Target.activateTarget (requestId=1, targetId=..., sessionId=...)` (and/or
`cdp error 2 (-32602): No target with given id found`) — and either measure or drop the "-32000" from the
commit body/bead prose.

Fix owner: chrome-agent-platform-qazo (branch author)

title: Imported commands require exact-body owner adoption before becoming task instructions
description:
Context: On origin/main@4d4d75512 imported commands are stored with a static `<run-token>` untrusted fence, but /command picker and NTP starter chip copy that same string into the owner-message composer; service-worker task admission and ACP treat it as the user task, while the protected policy names a different random token generated at orchestrator assembly. The existing P2 review-finding chrome-agent-platform-3io3p owns implementation; imported SKILLS have a separate model-time re-fence.

Decision (proposed; coord approval required): Keep imported commands untrusted as stored remote data, but classify the exact reviewed body as owner-authored instruction only after an explicit owner preview/gesture bound to its command id, source and SHA-256 content digest. At insertion/send reject unknown provenance, changed or malformed legacy fences, missing approval and stale bodies; render the approved body as readable plaintext task, not a misleading placeholder or a model-visible untrusted fence. Approval is NOT import/selection/send by itself and never bypasses CAP's protected prompt, tool grants or destructive-action approvals. If adoption UI is not ready, disable automatic imported-command insertion with an honest review-required status. Do not expose the real random run token in UI/logs; keep per-assembly token fencing for truly untrusted skill/tool material.

Consequences: Preserves legitimate imported-command workflows after deliberate owner trust, but requires preview, source/digest tracking, a safe legacy migration, all picker/starter/Use routes and task admission tests. Reimport/revoke invalidates approval; owner-pasted arbitrary text is still owner-authored and cannot be reliably taint-tracked. Rationale/callsites/test falsifiers and ~one lane-day estimate are on chrome-agent-platform-3io3p. Alternative considered: per-assembly re-fence commands in the task: fixes token mismatch but labels their instructions DATA and silently breaks the command function; automatic trust at import/pick: keeps function but preserves the injection vector; bare native ACP dispatch: drops the CAP envelope (rejected by decision chrome-agent-platform-6yfm).
notes:
2026-10-12: owner policy choice RECEIVED (Paul: exact-body owner adoption bound to id+source+SHA-256, with imported-command insertion disabled behind a review-required status meanwhile). Next action: independent architectural acceptance by a different-model reviewer against the 3io3p falsifiers, recorded as ACCEPT/CHANGES in a comment; then coord releases qazo's HOLD on 3io3p. This bead is the ADR, not the implementation - close it when the acceptance is recorded.

title: ACP exit diagnostic undercounts by one when a newline directly follows an ESC inside an unterminated OSC (scripts/acp-bridge.ts:461)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-cploc delta b0b0ac28e..3be4d46d2 (tip 3be4d46d2), branch fleet/qazo-cploc. P3 diagnostic-honesty follow-up; non-blocking (does not block landing).

Repro (deno run, tip 3be4d46d2):
  const s = new StderrSanitizer(); const out = [];
  s.processChunk("\u001b]0;abc\u001b\ndef", l => out.push(l));
  s.flush(l => out.push(l));
  -> s.droppedLinesCount === 1, but two suppressed lines ("0;abc" and "def") were dropped.
  Control "\u001b]0;abc\ndef" (no ESC) -> droppedLinesCount === 2.
  Also "\u001b]0;abc\u001b" + "\ndef" split across a chunk boundary -> 1.

Observed: the inOscEsc fallthrough at scripts/acp-bridge.ts:461 marks any char that is not '\\', ']' or ESC - including "\n" - as line content (hasOscLineContent = true) and does not increment droppedLinesCount. A newline that immediately follows a lone ESC inside an unterminated OSC is therefore never counted, and the exit diagnostic under-reports the suppressed line count by one.

Expected: a newline inside an unterminated OSC counts as a dropped line regardless of whether the preceding char was an ESC, i.e. the inOscEsc branch should route "\n" through the same accounting as the inOsc newline path at scripts/acp-bridge.ts:475-479.

Evidence: scripts/acp-bridge.ts:442-462 vs :475-479; probe output /tmp/rev-cploc-probe2.ts ("ESC then newline then text" count=1, control count=2).
Fix owner: chrome-agent-platform-qazo (branch fleet/qazo-cploc).
close_reason: Closed

title: [review-finding] rbd84: recorded root cause contradicts the failure evidence it quotes, and no test in the delta falsifies the new readiness/bringToFront gates
description:
Independent review finding (deepseek/deepseek-flash) of chrome-agent-platform-rbd84, delta b257fd925..8d7b3f7ef (branch fleet/qazo-rbd84).

SEVERITY: P3 (record accuracy + fix provability; the delta itself is PASS on the behaviour I could reproduce).

1) The hand-off's mechanism #4 says the click happened before ntp.bundle.js installed the #new-agent listeners. The quoted failure cannot show that:
  grep -h -o 'state did not arrive in 12000ms.\{0,130\}' /home/exedev/.fleet/spool/delivered/*.json | head -2
  -> {'ready':true,'buttonDisplay':'flex','open':false,'nativeOpen':false,'status':'','clicks':0}
  'clicks' is incremented by a DOCUMENT-LEVEL capture listener the harness installs itself (tests/w51r-create-click.test.ts:96), so clicks:0 means the real mouse event never reached #new-agent at all - a click that lands on a handler-less element still increments it. A listener-installation defect would read clicks:1, open:false.
  The pre-click precondition already required document.readyState === 'complete' (base test line 76), and ntp.html loads the bundle as a deferred type="module" (extension/ntp/ntp.html:2330), so module evaluation - including the top-level #new-agent listener at extension/ntp/ntp.js:5664 - has completed before ready:true is observable.
  Distinction confirmed by mutation: with openQuickCreateAgent() removed from the real handler in extension/dist/ntp.bundle.js the harness reports {"clicks":1,"open":false} after 60000ms (/tmp/rev-rbd84-mutation.log), i.e. event delivered, dialog not opened.

2) The author's planted falsifier ('removing clickVisibleCreateAgent dispatch') re-tests pre-existing harness behaviour; nothing in the delta falsifies the two NEW gates (Page.bringToFront, waitForAppReady({timeoutMs:readyTimeoutMs})). I could not reproduce the RED either: the base version of the test passed 2/2 in 1s at loadavg1=4.61 on the same box (/tmp/rev-rbd84-base-underload.log), and the tip passed 2/2 in 2s (evidence /home/exedev/cap-evidence/w51r-create-click/1791656600891-1413482/wide-open.png shows the real Create dialog). So the fix is plausible (its two named mechanisms are exactly the remaining candidates for clicks:0: background-tab input routing and stale geometry from a pre-hydration layout shift) but unproven; no observed evidence shows the delta removes the flake.

3) Related but distinct signature, same test, retained in the merger's logs: /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/8b54ef1a65b674afd6ffe311f8d7b6ebb63e45e8.log (tree 8b54ef1a, sha 8225390a9, 2026-10-08) shows 'w51r state did not arrive in 10000ms: {ready:true,buttonDisplay:null,...,clicks:0}' - the PRE-CLICK ready wait, button never rendered. Neither bringToFront nor the hydration gate addresses that (only the scaled bound does). Whoever owns the follow-up should decide whether the bead's single 'w51r timeout' covers both signatures.

Expected: the hand-off states a mechanism the observed state supports (or marks it unproven), at least one falsifier exercises the new gates, and the two failure signatures are either shown to share a cause or tracked separately.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
Implementation completed on branch fleet/qazo-cploc @ 3be4d46d2 (base b0b0ac28e):

Problem & Root Cause Analysis:
1. In scripts/acp-bridge.ts:470-475, StderrSanitizer incremented droppedLinesCount exclusively when a newline character (\n) was encountered inside an unterminated OSC sequence.
2. If an adapter child process emitted an unterminated OSC payload without a trailing newline (e.g. \u001b]0;SECRET_PAYLOAD) or with trailing characters after a newline (e.g. \u001b]0;a\nTAIL) before EOF/exit, the unclosed final line fragment was suppressed fail-closed, but droppedLinesCount remained 0 (or undercounted by 1).
3. On process exit, createAcpServer checked (sanitizer.droppedLinesCount > 0 || sanitizer.unterminatedOscSeen) and formatted the diagnostic as:
   `stderr suppressed after unterminated OSC (${sanitizer.droppedLinesCount} line${sanitizer.droppedLinesCount === 1 ? "" : "s"} dropped)`
   When droppedLinesCount was 0, this printed the self-contradictory string:
   'stderr suppressed after unterminated OSC (0 lines dropped)' despite suppressing payload bytes.

Mechanism:
1. In scripts/acp-bridge.ts:
   • Added private boolean hasOscLineContent to StderrSanitizer to track when characters have arrived on the current line within an unterminated OSC.
   • Set hasOscLineContent = true upon entering an OSC (\u009d or \x1b]) and for each character received on that line inside the OSC.
   • On \n inside OSC, increment droppedLinesCount and reset hasOscLineContent = false (the completed line is accounted for).
   • In flush(), if an unterminated OSC was active (this.inOsc === true) and hasOscLineContent === true, increment droppedLinesCount and clear hasOscLineContent so unclosed trailing line fragments are counted.
   • In createAcpServer exit diagnostics, format non-zero dropped line count as 'stderr suppressed after unterminated OSC (N lines dropped)', falling back to 'stderr suppressed after unterminated OSC' without claiming '0 lines dropped'.
2. Verification:
   • Focused unit tests: verified 0 newlines counts 1 line dropped, 1 newline with trailing text counts 2 lines dropped, and chunk splits maintain accurate counts. Clean terminated OSC with \x07/ST resets count to 0 and permits subsequent lines.
   • Focused integration test: mock adapter emitting unterminated OSC without trailing newline before exit verifies exit log and WebSocket close reason report '(1 line dropped)' with zero canary leaks.
   • All 16 tests in tests/acp-bridge-adapter-logging.test.ts passed in 2s.
   • Planted mutation falsifier confirmed RED on unpatched base.
3. Holding heavy build / fast gate while merger full gate runs in heavy slot (pid 1691469). Tip frozen @ 3be4d46d2.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: In scripts/acp-bridge.ts, track line content within unterminated OSC sequences and increment droppedLinesCount on flush() for unclosed trailing lines, and prevent formatting '(0 lines dropped)'. Add unit and integration assertions in tests/acp-bridge-adapter-logging.test.ts.
WHY: Unterminated OSC payloads without trailing newlines were suppressed fail-closed but reported '(0 lines dropped)', misinforming operators about suppressed output.
EFFECT: Accurately reflects all suppressed lines and trailing fragments in ACP bridge exit diagnostics and WebSocket close reasons without leaking payloads or weakening fail-closed sanitization.

  // S3

Observed: out == []  — the canonical Node crash shape is swallowed, because the allowlist is
anchored at ^ERROR/^FATAL/... and "Uncaught Error:", "    at ..." and "Failed to spawn ..." match none
of the patterns.
  // S4
  s.processChunk("\u001b]0;broken-title");
  s.processChunk("\nserver listening on 127.0.0.1:7788\nturn rejected: policy\ndone\n");
Observed: out == []  — after one malformed OSC the bridge still relays nothing but allowlisted lines
for the rest of the child's life, and the exit path still reports the diagnostic as "no stderr" when
no allowlisted line happened to appear.

Secondary (same theme, C1 encoding): an OSC started with C1 \u009d discards previously recovered
candidates unconditionally (scripts/acp-bridge.ts:500-508 via resetOsc), while the 7-bit ESC ] path
flushes them (scripts/acp-bridge.ts:505-518, 443-470) — the same logical event has two behaviours,

call, coordinate with the P2 on payload replay in chrome-agent-platform-vpo4n so the fix does not
widen the leak): (a) add unanchored crash anchors ("Uncaught Error", "Error:", "error:", a leading
whitespace+at stack-frame) to the candidate test; or (b) keep the allowlist narrow but make the
suppression visible — say "stderr suppressed after unterminated OSC (N lines dropped)" instead of
"no stderr" in the exit diagnostic, so the operator is told diagnostics were withheld rather than
told there were none.

title: StderrSanitizer swallows the entire remaining stderr after an unterminated OSC, so the exit diagnostic reports 'no stderr' (scripts/acp-bridge.ts:390-460)
description:
Reviewed chrome-agent-platform-d3feo delta 6276f45be..70fd8dced (tip 70fd8dced), branch fleet/qazo-d3feo. This is a diagnostic regression introduced BY this delta (pre-fix the raw line reached the log; post-fix it is dropped).

WHAT: the streaming sanitizer enters inOsc on ESC ] (or C1 OSC \u009d) and discards every following character — including newlines and the line buffer — until a terminator (BEL, ESC \, C1 ST) arrives. An adapter that emits an unterminated OSC therefore loses ALL subsequent stderr, not just the OSC payload. flush() emits nothing because lineBuffer stayed empty.

Repro (deno test, worktree at tip 70fd8dced):
  const s = new StderrSanitizer(); const out = [];
  s.processChunk("\u001b]0;partial-title", l => out.push(l));
  s.processChunk("\nERROR: real adapter failure, exit 17\n", l => out.push(l));
  s.flush(l => out.push(l));
Observed: out == []  (the real failure line never reaches onLine, so lastStderr stays "" and the exit path logs 'no stderr' and closes with an uninformative reason).
Expected: only the OSC payload is dropped; "\nERROR: real adapter failure, exit 17" is relayed as [adapter-stderr] and kept in the exit diagnostic.
Secondary effect: an unterminated OSC also suppresses any later 5f5u auth-precedence warning, so the host-side actionableAuthWarning never fires even though the child printed it.
Impact: operator visibility only (diagnostics, not the protocol frame or the turn result) and it needs a broken/hostile adapter, so P3 — but it defeats the exit-diagnostic purpose this branch added (there is a test "acp-bridge captures exit diagnostics even when stderr lacks a trailing newline").
FIX DIRECTION (smallest): treat a newline with no terminator seen as an implicit OSC abort (relay the line, drop the payload), or cap OSC swallowing at the next newline / a bounded byte budget, and add a case pinning "\u001b]0;x" + "\nREAL LINE\n" -> REAL LINE is emitted.
Evidence: /tmp/rev-d3feo-hunt.test.ts case H2 (fails on tip 70fd8dced); scripts/acp-bridge.ts:390-460 (inOsc branch), :1058-1080 (stderrDrained/onLine).
Fix owner: chrome-agent-platform-qazo (branch fleet/qazo-d3feo). Follow-up polish; does not block landing.

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
Completed implementation and independent review pass on branch fleet/qazo-l5rup @ a59b0d1b7.

Mechanism:
- In scripts/acp-bridge.ts (StderrSanitizer):
  1. Suppress continuation collection and diagnostic emission once inOscDiscardOnly is latched, checking cumulative byte count (>4096 bytes) after every character and escape sequence.
  2. Latch discard-only state and clear candidate diagnostics when a ninth candidate diagnostic arrives, whether terminated by a newline or unterminated at EOF / 7-bit boundary.
  3. Ensure flush() and flushUnterminatedOsc() check !inOscDiscardOnly so overrun payloads without a terminator or trailing newline are never emitted.
  4. On a C1 OSC start (\u009d), discard any previous unclosed OSC candidate diagnostics unconditionally.
  5. Handle 7-bit OSC start (ESC ]) inside inOscEsc so a new 7-bit OSC sequence flushes preceding diagnostic candidates rather than swallowing them as payload.
  6. Ensure pre-OSC lineBuffer text is always flushed at EOF before resetting unclosed OSC state.
- In tests/acp-bridge-adapter-logging.test.ts:
  Added unit and integration assertions for byte/candidate limit latching through EOF, C1 and 7-bit OSC boundaries, pre-OSC text preservation, and adapter crash diagnostic recovery (11/11 tests pass in 2s; 7/7 tests pass in tests/acp-child-env.test.ts in 175ms).

Independent review (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol, run ae55cc29-ea16-4e5f-9b5a-5508898966bf):
VERDICT: PASS-with-notes
'Correct: The discard-only latch suppresses candidate output at EOF after either limit. The cumulative limit is checked after each continuation character or newline, and a ninth candidate at EOF clears the earlier candidates. Tests cover these cases. C1 OSC resets and discards pending candidates; a new 7-bit OSC recovers preceding candidates. Pre-OSC text and unterminated diagnostics are preserved. The diff is focused on this behavior, its tests, and release bookkeeping. Findings: No issues found.'

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: In scripts/acp-bridge.ts, StderrSanitizer recovers stderr error diagnostics when an adapter emits an unterminated OSC escape sequence before failing, while enforcing strict discard-only latching upon byte (>4096) or candidate (>=8) limit overruns and discarding unverified payloads across C1 boundaries.
WHY: Unterminated OSC sequences previously caused the sanitizer to swallow all subsequent stderr lines through EOF, resulting in uninformative 'no stderr' exit diagnostics and obscuring actual adapter crash causes.
EFFECT: Operators and diagnostic exit logs retain true crash diagnostics (e.g. fatal errors, auth precedence warnings) even if preceded by malformed or unterminated OSC sequences, without leaking unverified terminal control payloads.

title: pew31 review: probe-timer timeout is classified as a real CDP evaluate timeout, so a hung SW can exit 75 'environmental' on a loaded box (app-readiness.ts:186 + chrome-journeys.ts:9118/9353)
description:
Review-finding (chrome-agent-platform-rev-pew31, model family deepseek; author was Gemini 3.8 Flash) on the fix delta fa339ed47..50d3c7735 (tip 50d3c7735) for chrome-agent-platform-pew31.

CONCERN / PROVENANCE: the per-probe timer's rejection is now shaped as
  `cdp timeout: Runtime.evaluate (probe evaluation timed out after <N>ms for <surface>)`
(scripts/lib/app-readiness.ts:186). That string matches isCdpEvaluateTimeout() (scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts:752, /cdp timeout: Runtime\.evaluate/), so at the classification layer our own readiness-probe bound (default probeTimeoutMs=2000) is indistinguishable from a real CDP Runtime.evaluate budget timeout (15000ms, chrome-journeys.ts:311-315).

CONSEQUENCE in the real journey caller: chrome-journeys.ts:9118-9129 sees isCdpEvaluateTimeout=true, sets evaluateTimeoutVerdict = await measureEvaluateTimeout(), and the finally block (chrome-journeys.ts:9353-9356) exits via evaluateTimeoutReport(): when the box measures "loaded" that is ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT (75, "re-run, not a defect"). Before this delta the same hung evaluate surfaced as "app never became ready" -> product red (exit 1). Net: a genuine product defect (service worker never answers Runtime.evaluate) can now be read as an environmental refusal whenever the box happens to be loaded, attributed to a 2s probe bound rather than the 15s CDP budget. The only marker separating the two is the human-readable parenthetical; nothing automated distinguishes them.

Known trade-off: the founding finding explicitly permitted "propagate/classify that rejection", and 9t1p's idle-box branch (idle -> product red) still applies when the box measures quiet. Filed so coord can judge whether the probe bound should participate in the CDP-timeout/environmental class at all.

REPRO (no browser needed; bounded):

  const { waitForAppReady } = await import("file:///home/exedev/worktrees/rev-pew31-tip/scripts/lib/app-readiness.ts");
  const { isCdpEvaluateTimeout } = await import("file:///home/exedev/worktrees/rev-pew31-tip/scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts");
  const evaluate = (_e: string) => new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error("cdp timeout: Runtime.evaluate (requestId=99)")), 250));
  let caught: any = null;
  try { await waitForAppReady(evaluate as any, { timeoutMs: 700, probeTimeoutMs: 100, pollIntervalMs: 20, surfaceName: "NTP main" }); } catch (e) { caught = e; }
  console.log(String(caught?.message), isCdpEvaluateTimeout(String(caught?.message)));
  TS

OBSERVED (base fa339ed47, same input): "app never became ready for NTP main within 700ms (last probe: ...)" false

description:

title: mxu5 review: post-dispatch admission failure (restore fence / quota) orphans the worker run — no stop-run steer, run executes untracked (extension/background/service-worker.js:1685-1745)
description:

On failure the code does 'runControl?.unregister?.(executionId); return admissionFailure' with NO stop-run steer and no settle. handleAlarm then sees a truthy workerDispatched and does NOT fall back to runTask (:2019-2040), and because admissionFailure.ok is false it also calls markScheduledDone (:2069).

The host post happens first; only afterwards is the restore-fence admission rejected, and no 'agent-worker.steer {mode:stop-run}' is sent.

(unregister happens first, so tools fail run_not_live — but the run still runs its model loop); its terminal result logs 'cannot settle an unknown execution'.
EXPECTED: check admission before the worker can start, or on post-dispatch admission failure steer stop-run (and/or settle) before returning.
EVIDENCE: service-worker.js:1685-1745; durable-quota.js:29-50.

title: zqgn3 guard: extPath.endsWith('extension') heuristic is redundant and over-broad (latent false positive for third-party extensions)
description:
REVIEW FINDING (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, independent review of chrome-agent-platform-zqgn3 @ 207d480d4, delta a562fb73b..207d480d4).

LOCATION: scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts, assertExtensionBuilt(), the dist-directory check condition:
  if (manifestText.includes("dist/") || extPath.replace(/[\/\\]$/, "").endsWith("extension")) { ... }

ISSUE (P3, report-only): the second disjunct `.endsWith("extension")` is redundant for this repo AND over-broad.

- Redundant: the repo manifest always declares background.service_worker "dist/background/service-worker.js", so `manifestText.includes("dist/")` is already true for `${ROOT}extension` and every variant/copy harness in the repo (buildVariant, copyTree, copyDir all preserve the manifest). The `endsWith("extension")` clause adds no coverage for any current call site.

- Over-broad: a FUTURE harness that loads a third-party unpacked extension whose directory basename ends with the substring "extension" (e.g. "my-extension", "test-extension") and which uses a flat structure WITHOUT a dist/ subdirectory would be rejected with "dist is missing — extension/dist not built - run npm run build:production" even though the extension is perfectly loadable. The guard's contract (per the launcher docstring "Two ways to call it ... the launcher builds the standard headless argv") is not repo-extension-only, so the heuristic can false-positive on a legitimate non-repo extension.

EVIDENCE: verified by reading the diff (git diff a562fb73b..207d480d4 -- scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts); `grep` of all scripts/*.ts launchChrome call sites shows every current extension path is ${ROOT}extension or a full-tree copy/variant that includes dist/, so nothing trips it today. `manifestText.includes("dist/")` alone is the principled check.

SUGGESTED FIX: drop the `|| extPath.endsWith("extension")` disjunct (keep `manifestText.includes("dist/")`), or narrow it to an exact basename === "extension" + only when the path is inside the repo tree. Re-run `npm run test:file -- tests/extension-dist-guard.test.ts` (the repo-extension tests still pass because the manifest references dist/).

RELATED (minor, note-only): the "directory does not exist" error message ("launchChrome: the extension at <path> does not exist — extension/dist not built - run npm run build:production") appends the "extension/dist not built - run npm run build:production" suffix even when the WHOLE directory is missing (not just dist); for a wrong-path case "run npm run build:production" is not the fix. The leading "does not exist" clause is correct and sufficient; consider dropping the canned suffix from that one branch.

title: Gate 8 discarded-stream promotion sub-case is vacuous w.r.t. discard (seal before discard)
description:
Review finding on chrome-agent-platform-78s (fleet/78s-port, mb=aebfcc136..tip=c7ddd007e).

tests/tool-platform-abuse-gates.test.ts, "abuse gate 8" discarded-stream sub-case:

  const discardedStream = await createWasmStreamOutput({ owner, storage }); // UNSEALED
  await discardWasmStream({ ref: discardedStream, owner, storage });
  await assertRejects(async () => promoteWasmStreamToArtifact(discardedStream, { owner, storage, force: true }), Error);

The stream is never sealed before discard, so the assertRejects(..., Error) is satisfied by the UNSEALED check (validateSealedWasmStream -> fail("wasm_stream_authority"), wasm-stream-files.js:207) even if discardWasmStream were a complete no-op. The test therefore does NOT actually pin the "discarded stream cannot be promoted" property — a discard regression would go green.

Fix: seal the stream (write stdout + sealWasmStreamOutput) BEFORE discardWasmStream, so a no-op discard leaves a sealed+owned stream that promoteWasmStreamToArtifact(force:true) would SUCCEED on, turning the assertion red.

Severity: P3 (test-quality / non-vacuity). Not a product correctness or security hole — the underlying discard-then-promote behavior does fail closed in the real code (streamDirectory throws on the missing directory).

Evidence: wasm-stream-files.js:202-209 (validateSealedWasmStream sealed/owner checks), :319-331 (discardWasmStream removes directory), tool-stream-platform.js:180-187 (promoteWasmStreamToArtifact -> validateSealedWasmStream).

title: Proposal: Consolidate 29 test entry points in package.json to 4 standard scripts
description:
Rationale: There are 29 `test:*` scripts in `package.json` (e.g., `test:kat`, `test:ui`, `test:sidebar`). This creates tooling drift where agents use different sub-commands instead of standard tools.
Cost: ~0.5 lane-days. Consolidate into `test` (full), `test:changed` (fast), `test:build`, and `test:heavy`. Remove the rest or move them to a dedicated test runner config.
Risk if we do nothing: Confusion, unmaintained entry points that agents waste time trying to use.
Who: implementer lane.

title: ADR: Tier tests into Fast, Full, and Heavy to bound gate cost (fleet-r4nb)
description:
Context: The project runs the full suite (15+ min) for every change, bottlenecking merges. Main gained ~31 test files which increased the cost (fleet-r4nb).
Decision: Define three tiers: Fast (`test:changed`, for dev iteration), Full (`test`, for normal merges, skipping heavy fixtures), and Heavy (`test:heavy`, for WASM/browser journeys that take minutes). The fleet gate will run Fast and only run Full/Heavy selectively.
Consequences: Gate time is proportional to blast radius. Merger throughput increases.
Alternatives considered: Retrying flaky tests or throwing more hardware, which doesn't scale as the file count grows.

title: build.mjs:160 sequential readFile+sha256 loop in the package-store exemption walk
description:
Source: nightly software-factory project-audit 2026-10-09 (origin/main@7bf4524c7). Evidence: /home/exedev/agents/findings/chrome-agent-platform-factory-delta.md (rule `sequential-await-waterfall`, fingerprint 5cac7210).

[LOW] build.mjs:160 — each matching extension/wasm/**/*.js inventory row awaits readFile() then hashes the bytes before the next row is touched, serializing the build's package-store exemption walk across all rows. The reads are independent local files, so this is a real (small) latency waterfall in build-time tooling — not the shipped runtime path.

Remediation: resolve the reads and hashes concurrently with Promise.all; the exemption Set is order-independent.

title: backup-export.js:204 sequential-await waterfall: awaits each OPFS open between entry bodies
description:

[LOW] extension/lib/backup-export.js:204 — the export generator awaits each OPFS open between entry bodies (depth-1 lookahead), serializing independent OPFS opens instead of issuing them concurrently. Remediation: open independent entries concurrently (bounded Promise.all) so the export is not serialized on per-entry OPFS open latency.

[LOW · routed critical] extension/lib/script-host.js:66 — the sandboxed-script fetch keeps a direct, unbrokered fallback that skips the run-scoped policy when chrome.runtime is absent (e.g. a non-extension context), so a sandboxed script can perform a direct fetch bypassing the brokered/approval-gated fetch path that the extension otherwise enforces. Remediation: remove or confine the direct-fetch fallback so the sandboxed script has no network path other than the brokered fetch; if the fallback must exist for a test/hosted context, keep it off the shipped run-scoped path.

title: scheduler boot recovery is fire-and-forget: schedule.cancelOrphans can observe pre-migration recipe:* ids during the one-time recipe->skill rekey
description: Pre-existing, non-blocking, self-healing. scheduler.js:1212-1237 memoizes one bootRecoveryPromise and awaits clearStaleInflight -> migrateSkillIdentities -> reconcileScheduledTasks; the SW launches it fire-and-forget on module eval (SW:12887) with no dispatch barrier, so the owner route schedule.cancelOrphans can run before the one-time recipe->skill rekey (skill-identity-migration.js, guarded by cap:migration:skillIdentityV1) resolves. The route recognizes BOTH recipe:* and skill:* (SW:10773-10800) and builds its known set from both, so pre-migration names are valid input, not auto-deleted; and a concurrent rekey between list and cancel makes cancellation confirm absence/failure and report failed rather than falsely claiming cancellation. Impact: a sweep may report failures and need the next sweep; no data loss, no false cancellation. NOT introduced by 3p3e.3 (no scheduler.js / skill-identity-migration.js diff) and raised as P2 report-only in the d8f4f3f78 review; the 3p3e.3 orphan test change is a legitimate determinism fix (awaits the same memoized recoverOnBoot() promise before seeding), not a mask. Possible fix if ever prioritised: add a boot-recovery barrier before route dispatch, or have cancelOrphans await the migration promise.

title: D2 residual: pending enrollment promotions escape the scripting-Disable sweep and self-complete on a later boot
description: Follow-up from 3p3e.3 D2 review (P2-6). Pending promotions are excluded from listOrigins(), so the scripting-Disable sweep never tombstones or abandons them; a later boot's reconcileEnrollmentPromotionsOnBoot can then complete the promotion without an owner gesture in that session. No authority exists while scripting is disabled (pending is non-authorizing) and completion requires re-enabling scripting, so this is hygiene, not a bypass — but Disable is not total. Fix: fold pending rows into the sweep (abandon or mark retryable cleanup) so the owner's Disable gesture is complete.

title: beads-landing-link captures a trailing full stop in the bead id, and --comment exits 0 when a bd comment fails
description:
OBSERVED (2026-10-08, landing of chrome-agent-platform-jjsz @ c4d4633a):
`node scripts/beads-landing-link.mjs <range> --comment <sha> --bundle <path>` listed
`chrome-agent-platform-t5o2i.` (WITH a trailing full stop) as a referenced bead, and its own
`bd comment` for that ref failed with
  Error: resolving chrome-agent-platform-t5o2i.: no issue found matching "chrome-agent-platform-t5o2i."
The other four refs (jjsz x12, 80yqb, mwj7v, qo3u8) were commented fine. The script exits 0 either
way, so the failure is only visible by reading the last line it prints per bead; a lane that does not
read that output believes every referenced bead was linked.

CAUSE: scripts/beads-landing-link.mjs extractBeadRefs() builds the pattern
  <prefix>([a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*)
so the id class admits '.' and '-' ANYWHERE after the first character, including as the final
character. A bead id written at the end of a sentence ("... see chrome-agent-platform-t5o2i.") is
captured with its full stop. A trailing '-' (a dash used as punctuation) would be captured the same way.
The commit that exposed it: 02f83394 (body ends a sentence with the bead id).

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. extractBeadRefs strips trailing '.' and '-' characters from the captured id (an id never ends in
    either), while keeping interior dots (hierarchical child ids such as `<prefix>abc.1` must still
    resolve) and still lower-casing.
 2. `--comment` exits NON-ZERO (and prints which beads failed) when any `bd comment` call fails, so a
    landing record cannot silently miss a bead. Today it always exits 0.
 3. tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts gains: (a) a unit case with an id followed by '.', ',' and ')' in
    a subject and a body, expecting the bare id; (b) a case with an interior dot id keeping its dot;
    (c) a --comment case with a stub `bd` that fails for one id, expecting a non-zero exit.
    Each must FAIL when the fix is reverted (byte-identical restore drill).
 4. docs/MERGER-PLAYBOOK.md section 3 step 10 is NOT changed by this bead (owner's file); if the
    playbook text says "run it and you are linked", note the exit-code change on the landing bead.

DOES NOT CHANGE: the report mode output format, --verify, the DEFAULT_PREFIX, the `--json` shape.

SEAMS: scripts/beads-landing-link.mjs (extractBeadRefs, main), tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts.
Note that tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts was made fast in the jjsz lane (8 s -> 32 ms); keep it fast.

FOUND BY: the jjsz coordinator while closing the landing record. Worked around by hand: a manual
`bd comment chrome-agent-platform-t5o2i ...` (noted on that bead).

title: build.mjs: knu79's two deno-install self-heal calls are unbounded execFileSync (the fnmr hang class)
description:
OBSERVED (2026-10-08, found by the chrome-agent-platform-jjsz build reviewer reading merge 3 of the landing). build.mjs:423 and build.mjs:432 (the knu79 deno-store self-heal, origin/main 00381f49) run `execFileSync("deno", ["install", "--frozen-lockfile"], { cwd: ROOT, stdio: "inherit" })` with NO timeout and NO process-group bound. The same file's header (build.mjs:93-95, chrome-agent-platform-fnmr) records that an unbounded execFileSync wedged a worktree's build for 3h37m, and runBoundedChild (scripts/lib/bounded-child.mjs:173, imported at build.mjs:26) exists for exactly this: it names the hang, samples wchan and takes the group down. A `deno install` that blocks on the network (a stalled registry or npm fetch) or on a lock reads as a hung build with no output naming the cause.

WHY IT MATTERS: the self-heal runs on the path a fresh worktree takes (no node_modules/.deno store), i.e. the first build of every new worktree, which is the most common first action of every agent on this fleet. A hang there blocks the whole merge queue's first gate with nothing in the log. It is also the only remaining unbounded child in build.mjs's resolution path (the generator call at :96 is bounded).

NOT A LANE REGRESSION: this is origin/main code (knu79), not the jjsz lane's. Filed as discovered-from jjsz because the review of the landing found it; the lane did not touch these lines (merge 3 took main's bytes).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Both calls go through runBoundedChild (or an equivalent bound) with a timeout from boundedChildTimeoutMs, stdio kept inherit so the install progress still shows, and a timeout names `deno install --frozen-lockfile` as the stalled step.
- A test pins it: the two call sites are read as text (the pattern tests/build-parallel-discipline.test.ts uses) and a mutant that puts back a bare execFileSync("deno", ["install" ...]) goes red; a behavioural test with a fake `deno` that never exits proves the bound fires and the error names the command (the pattern in tests/bounded-child.test.ts).
- docs/TEST-COUPLING-INVENTORY.md names the new pin.

MUST NOT CHANGE: the one-time self-heal behaviour when the store is missing or incomplete (pinned by tests/build-sdk-dedup.test.ts, which knu79 extended in 00381f49), and the fail-loud message at build.mjs:436.

title: jjsz review residue: injection-pin survivors (a-f), leader-exit sweep second bound, bbz3s pin strength
description:
OBSERVED: findings the review rounds of the chrome-agent-platform-jjsz landing named and that were NOT closed there (each is small and contrived, or pre-existing; none blocks the landing). One bead so none is lost; split it when picking one up. The reviewers were same-family and read-only: the falsifications below are REASONED from the pin code (round 6), not run, unless marked drilled.

1. tests/jjsz-lifeline-runner-exit.test.ts, the pin of scripts/security-injection.ts. Mutants that still pass, each keeping the reap statement verbatim and the one counted write `proc = l.proc`:
 (a) a SECOND top-level try/finally, or a second `kill()`, is invisible: the pins read the first one (round-4 build review 3c).
 (b) bare-kill forms the rule does not read: `x.proc.kill(...)`, `proc["kill"]()` (computed, so the dotted path is null), `process.kill(proc.pid, ...)`, an aliased `Deno.kill`, `new Deno.Command("kill", ...)` (round-4 3e, round-6 security review).
 (c) a member write on the launch result before the store: `l.proc = null`, `Object.assign(l, {proc: null})`, `const l = {...(await launchChrome(...)), proc: null}`, and the toothless `l.proc = wrap(l.proc)`. Lifeline state is a WeakMap keyed by the ChildProcess (scripts/lib/process-tree.ts, `lifelineState`), so a wrapper or copy gets killed but its `settled` is never found and the helper never waits for the sweep.
 (d) reachability and position of the one write: `if (never) proc = l.proc;`, or the store moved after `waitForServiceWorker`. The rule counts writes; it does not require the write to be a direct statement of boot().
 (e) `kill = async () => {}` after the declaration: function bindings are writable and the pin reads the intact `function kill`.
 (f) the finalizer: a profile removal that is not literally `Deno.remove(` (`Deno.removeSync`, an `rm` alias, a `rm -rf` Command) ahead of `await kill()`, or a removal in the `catch` (which runs before the finally).
 FIX: the structural fix is chrome-agent-platform-80yqb (launchChrome waits for an in-flight sweep, so no call-site pin is needed and a fifth runner is covered). Until then close (a)-(f) in the pin: collect every function named kill and every top-level try, match member access by property name, and require the store to be a direct statement of boot().
 ALREADY CLOSED in the landing, do not re-file: the alias-then-null mutant, plain/compound (`||=` `??=` `+=`)/destructuring writes, `++`/`--` and for-in/of heads that assign the name, a return or throw ahead of the reap, and a clause-by-clause mutant for the operator, the right-hand side and the reaped argument.

2. scripts/lib/process-tree.ts around lines 460 and 470 (the leader-exit sweep): after the 5 s bound times out, `await attempt(() => watcher.status)` and `await closing` have no second bound, so a watcher stuck in uninterruptible I/O would hang the runner. Same exposure as disarmBody and exotic; new only in that four runners now wait for the sweep where before they did not (round-5 security review, finding 5). Fix: race the two awaits against a short second timer and log honestly.

3. tests/security-dependency-resolution.test.ts (the bbz3s pin), pre-existing on main: the pin never anchors the bundle fan-out, `plugin < builds` is near-vacuous (TDZ), it does not prove the AJV/fast-uri check is unconditional, and the first-occurrence text could match a comment. The stronger anchor is `] = await settleAll([` (round-4 build review, 4). The landing's anchor swap from `await Promise.all([` to `await settleAll([` is faithful; this is about the pin's strength, not that swap.

4. tests/beads-landing-link.test.ts: state dependence of main's own test, tracked in its own bead.

ACCEPTANCE (per item): a mutant that re-introduces the shape is rejected by a named test, drilled with a byte-identical restore; no existing assertion loosened. Must NOT change: the helper's behaviour, the journeys' bare final kill (carved out in scripts/lib/reap-leader.ts).

comments.text:
UPDATE (2026-10-08, jjsz landing rounds 5-7; reviewers are same-family and read-only; falsifications are REASONED from the pin code unless marked drilled).

CLOSED in C10 (drilled: each goes RED on its own row, byte-identical restore; bundle coordinator-drills/round7-c10):
- object-rest `({ ...proc } = x)`: a form-table row (drill D18).
- the guard test of `if (proc)` (round 7): mutant = a dead guard that keeps the right argument, `if (ws === undefined) await reapLeaderAndSettle(proc)` (D19).
- the Await test of `awaitedCall`, shared by all four pins (round 7): mutant = `void` instead of `await`; a form table for awaitedCall pins it directly and also isolates its callee, CallExpression and statement-type clauses (D20-D23). The order check's own use of it has a row (a voided kill between the boots, D24).

STILL OPEN (all Low; each is a contrived edit, none is a known regression):
- S1 a late or dead store of `proc = l.proc`: the write count, operator and right-hand side are right but the position is not (a store after boot() returns, or in an unreachable branch).
- S3 `kill = async () => {}` (a rebinding of the function name), or a second top-level `kill` / try that the pin's `find` ignores.
- S4 a `return` or `throw` ahead of the finalizer's awaited `kill()`: the finally still reads `await kill()` and never reaches it.
- S5 bare-kill spellings the dotted-name rule does not read: `l.proc.kill(...)`, `proc.kill.call(proc, ...)`, `Deno["kill"](...)`, `globalThis.Deno.kill(...)`, `process.kill(pid, ...)`. A property-name rule (any call whose callee ends in `.kill`) would subsume `l.proc.kill` and the existing `proc.kill` rule.
- Judged benign by the round-7 reviewer (no soundness effect): the `!s.alternate` and Block-branch parts of the guard test (an if/else shape), the `>1` side of the reap count, bare `await proc.status` (the old-shape rows also hold `proc.kill`), and `removeAt < 0` failing closed.

CORRECTION (disclosed): C9's commit title says "every clause of the injection pin has a mutant". Round 7 showed two clauses it did not cover (the guard test and the Await test); C10 covers them. The honest claim is "each clause the reviews named has a mutant that only it rejects", never "no clause is left".

comments.text:
UPDATE (2026-10-08 13:3x, jjsz landing, security review round 8 on C10 10ae42ff: PASS, no HIGH/MED; same-family read-only reviewer, nothing executed; verbatim report in the evidence bundle, review-round8/security-reviewer-round8-report.md).

CORRECTIONS to the survivor list above (the reviewer found three over-listed, the safe direction; each was re-read against scripts/security-injection.ts and injectionViolations in tests/jjsz-lifeline-runner-exit.test.ts before this comment):
- S3, "a second top-level `kill`": a second `function kill` is a SyntaxError in a module, so it cannot exist. The real first-match survivor is a SECOND top-level try/finally (the pin's `program.body.find(... TryStatement && finalizer)` reads only the first). A rebinding `kill = async () => {}` stays listed.
- S4, "a `return` or `throw` ahead of the finalizer's awaited `kill()`": the finalizer is at the top level of the module, where `return` is a SyntaxError. Only a `throw` or a `Deno.exit(...)` can precede it.
- "a profile removal that is not a literal `Deno.remove(`": that is fail-closed (a finalizer with no literal `Deno.remove(` is rejected, "update this pin"). The survivor is the reverse: a literal `Deno.remove(` call that is NOT the profile removal satisfies the order rule by itself (removeAt is the first statement with any `Deno.remove` call).
docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md is corrected to the same wording in C11.

RECOMMENDED FIRST (reviewer: "worth more than a t5o2i line"): close S1, the late store. `proc = l.proc` is at scripts/security-injection.ts:98, and the pin counts writes anywhere in the program, ignoring position. Moving the store below the `onopen` wait or the service-worker wait stays green; a boot failure there leaves `proc` null, so the finally's `kill()` reaps nothing and a Chrome plus its watcher leak (`descendant-residue`). Closure: require `proc = l.proc` to be statement [1] of `boot()` (right after `const l = await launchChrome(...)`), plus one mutant that moves it down. The same idiom closes S4's throw case: require the finalizer's first statement to be `await kill()`. Not done in the jjsz landing (the class is open and disclosed; no known regression).

INFO from the same round: D23's first form (an optional chain on `statement.expression`) is an EQUIVALENT mutant (no non-ExpressionStatement carries an AwaitExpression `.expression`), so it survived by design; the statement-type clause is isolated by crash only (14 TypeErrors when removed). Two rows of the awaitedCall table (`kill();` and `await kill;`) are over-determined (two clauses reject each); harmless spec rows. The suite and journey "drop the await" rows are bare calls, which the CallExpression-type clause rejects too; the Await clause is covered through the shared helper (all sites read through `awaitedCall`). Still unisolated and benign: `!s.alternate`, the Block-consequent branch, the `reaps.length > 1` side, a bare `await proc.status`, `removeAt < 0` (fail-closed). `plainCall` (used once) has no table, all its clauses fail closed.

title: Journey watchdog starts at main() entry, before the browser exists - decide whether it should start after the CDP connect
description: Follow-up from the 9ud9e fix (2026-10-08). qazo had an UNCOMMITTED edit that moved 'resetWatchdog()' from the top of main() to just after 'cdp = new Cdp(ws)', on the theory that the 90s per-check watchdog should not be consuming its budget during browser/CDP startup. j5yz deliberately left it out of the fix branch because the two behaviours are a real trade-off and not part of the union-gate regression: (A) watchdog at main() entry: any pre-browser phase (profile setup, browser launch, websocket open, long admission waits) counts against the 90s budget, so a slow box can trip the watchdog before a single check has run - the harness would report a watchdog hang that is really environment slowness; (B) watchdog after the CDP connect: the launch phase is unguarded, so a genuine hang during launch produces no named frontier and relies on the outer fleet-gate bound (which is a kill, not a diagnosis). ACTION: decide which phase should be covered and by what - e.g. keep the per-check 90s watchdog post-connect, and give the pre-connect phase its own separate bound with its own named failure message, so neither phase is silent and neither is misattributed. Evidence to gather first: how long the pre-connect phase actually takes on a quiet box vs under load, from the RUN: lines and existing journey logs in ~/cap-evidence. This is a diagnosis-quality bead, not a product defect. Owner: unassigned.
