title: Supply-chain inventory drift: package-lock.json says fast-uri 3.1.7 / MCP SDK 1.31.0 but the SHIPPED bundle carries 3.1.5 / 1.30.0 (deno npm resolution)
description: Found while settling the fast-uri reachability question (see the live-advisory bead). The npm lockfile resolves @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.31.0 and fast-uri 3.1.7, but the built bundle actually ships node_modules/.deno/@modelcontextprotocol+sdk@1.30.0 and node_modules/.deno/fast-uri@3.1.5 - the deno-managed npm resolution path picks different versions than npm lock. Consequence: advisory matching against the lockfile version can be WRONG in either direction (a fixed version in the lock may not be the shipped version, and vice versa), which undermines every dependency advisory verdict we take. ACTION: (a) decide which resolution is authoritative for shipped bytes and make the other agree, or add a build-time assertion that the versions in the bundle match the lockfile for security-relevant packages; (b) until then, match advisories against the .deno resolution for shipped code. Related: the akt29 build dedup work, which already touches the two-store (.deno vs npm-hoisted) layout. Owner: unassigned.

title: package-lock.json forwarded entry declares 0.3.5 but pins the 0.2.0 tarball
description:

title: Harness readiness: journey/KAT scripts interact before NTP hydration, so clicks silently no-op
description: Recurring gap found twice independently in one day. (1) idx0: cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts crashed at HEAD on a fresh run because it never polled for DOM/module readiness - fixed by promoting it to a kat with an explicit readiness guard (landed 4c0122e4). (2) 2026-10-07 j5yz .4 diagnostic on tree 4e60cc4d: the Create click fired before the NTP module had installed its dialog listener, so the dialog never opened and the run exited 1 with ZERO samples - a false INCONCLUSIVE that cost a whole bounded Chrome run. No extension source is at fault in either case; the pattern is that harnesses assume the page is interactive as soon as it is navigable. Proposed: one shared readiness primitive (poll for a named app-ready signal/frame before the first interaction, with a bounded wait and a NAMED failure state when it times out) used by scripts/chrome-journeys.ts and the kat harnesses, so a pre-hydration interaction is reported as 'app never became ready', not as an unexplained exit 1. Related: the P3 journey-primitive refactor bead. Owner: unassigned; do not start while j5yz/qazo are on the current reds - it is a follow-up.

The writer's gate and the call site are pinned: `tests/build-once-record.test.ts` executes the gate, and `tests/build-parallel-discipline.test.ts` rule B pins the single call and its exact arguments. Nothing pins what is CAPTURED. A wrong key field (the commit alone, or a digest of the wrong thing) or `stdout: ""` leaves every test green, and `tests/build-smoke.test.ts` asserts only exit code 0 on the reused record.

The reader (`tests/fixtures/build-once.mjs`) revalidates against the live `dist.complete` marker, so a wrong key cannot make a missing build look current. A wrong or empty `stdout` silently weakens what `build-smoke` and `store-doc-denial` then assert on.

## Acceptance

A test that runs a real (or injected) store build in a scratch tree and asserts (1) the written record's file name equals `<commit>-<source digest>` computed independently of `build.mjs`, and (2) its `stdout` equals the build's own captured output (non-empty, containing the `build:` progress lines). RED when the key uses the wrong field or `stdout` is blank (byte-identical-restore mutation drill, one mutant per field).

## Must NOT change

The record format (`{ code, stdout, at }`) and `writeBuildOnceRecord`'s internal gate.

title: cleanupSteps (copied into 7 test files) swallows cleanup failures: a leak cannot redden a passing test
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-3 build review, finding 4; the helper was added by the jjsz timing/cleanup worker)

Seven test files each carry a copy of a `cleanupSteps` helper that runs every teardown step and swallows each failure, so one failing step does not skip the rest:
tests/jjsz-lifeline-leader-exit.test.ts, tests/jjsz-lifeline-match.test.ts, tests/jjsz-lifeline-process-table.test.ts, tests/jjsz-macos-build-lock.test.ts, tests/jjsz-macos-custody-lock-verdicts.test.ts, tests/process-tree-cleanup.test.ts, tests/security-suite-lock-probe.test.ts (`scripts/agent-provider-picker.ts` has an older, separate use of the name).

It never rethrows. A teardown that FAILED (a process still alive, a directory that cannot be removed) therefore cannot redden a passing test, which is the leak these tests exist to catch.

## Proposed fix

Run every step as now, remember the FIRST failure, and rethrow it afterwards ONLY when no error is already propagating, so it never masks the test's own failure. One shared module instead of seven copies.

## Acceptance

A test of the shared helper: a failing step is rethrown after the others ran; with an error already propagating the original error wins; RED when the rethrow is removed (mutation drill). Each caller's behaviour is otherwise unchanged and no existing assertion is weakened.

title: Pin the Pyodide two-phase staging in build.mjs: no test names the verify-all-before-copy order
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-3 build review, finding 2)

`build.mjs` stages the admitted Pyodide runtime in two phases (build.mjs ~L784-808): a `settleAll` over the sha256 admission checks, then a `settleAll` over the copies. A drifted byte therefore fails the build closed with NOTHING copied, instead of leaving its already-verified siblings in STAGE. `docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md` 6.1 used to describe every rule in that section as pinned by a test that goes red; this one is not. A search of `tests/` finds no test that names the phase order or either admission error string (`pyodide runtime admission mismatch`, `has no admission hash`), so collapsing the two phases into one verify-and-copy pass per file (the pre-jjsz shape) would keep every gate green. The jjsz landing changed this block from a sequential loop to the two phases, so the behaviour it relies on is new and unpinned.

## Why it matters

The order is a fail-closed property of the build: a failed admission must not leave half of the runtime in STAGE. The later `dist.complete` and `scan-shipped` gates cover the final bytes, so this is defence in depth, not the only guard; exploiting the verify-to-copy window needs write access to the repository.

## Acceptance

- A test drives the staging with a runtime tree in which exactly ONE admitted file's bytes differ from `wasm-tools/python/MANIFEST.json` (a scratch copy or an injected root; never the committed files) and asserts BOTH: the build fails with the admission-mismatch error naming that file, AND no file of the runtime exists under `STAGE/wasm-tools/python` afterwards.
- It is RED when the two phases are collapsed into one pass (verify then copy per file), proven by a byte-identical-restore mutation drill. A second mutant adds a copy BEFORE the verify phase (a fresh instance, per the rule-pin canon in AGENTS.md "Test honesty").
- Optionally an AST pin in `tests/build-parallel-discipline.test.ts` that the verify `settleAll` is awaited before the copy `settleAll` starts.

## Seams

`build.mjs` (Pyodide block), `scripts/lib/build-concurrency.mjs` (`settleAll`), `tests/build-parallel-discipline.test.ts`, `wasm-tools/python/MANIFEST.json`.

## Must NOT change

The sha256 admission itself, the manifest format, the seven pinned files, `settleAll`'s rethrow-in-declaration-order semantics.

title: Rule-level pin for lifeline-aware leader kills: the jjsz reap pins are per-site, ~30 scripts still bare-kill a launched leader
description:
## What was observed

The jjsz crash lifeline (`attachProcessLifeline`, `scripts/lib/process-tree.ts`) makes a launched browser's process
group die with its launcher. A watcher shell lingers for about 110 ms AFTER the leader exits (`kill -TERM; sleep 0.1;
kill -KILL; pkill -f <profile>`). A caller that kills ONLY the leader (`proc.kill(...)` then `await proc.status`) and then
exits, or relaunches a browser on the same profile, therefore races that watcher:

- exit under the security custody supervisor: the supervisor takes a final `observeDescendants` sample after the runner
  exits and then judges `liveObservedResidue`, so a still-alive watcher reads as `descendant-residue` (exit 70);
- relaunch on the same profile: the watcher's profile `pkill` can kill the SECOND browser.

The jjsz round-2 security review (N1/N2) proved both. The fix is `reapLeaderAndSettle`
(`scripts/lib/reap-leader.ts`: kill the leader, await its exit, then await the lifeline's `settled` promise), and it is
applied at the three sites that need it: `scripts/security-suite.ts`, `scripts/page-actions-journey.ts`,
`scripts/keyless-first-result.ts`.

## The gap

The pins for that are PER SITE (an AST check of each of those three files, with in-file mutant checks), not a RULE.
`grep -n "proc.kill(" scripts/*.ts` still finds about 30 other bare leader kills (for example
`emscripten-abi-loaded.ts`, `perf-gallery-previews.ts`, `perf-seeded-scale.ts`, `read-page-host-grant-acceptance.ts`,
`screenshot-vision-evidence.ts`, `webmcp-acceptance.ts`). None is judged by the custody supervisor and none relaunches on
the same profile TODAY, which is why they were left alone. A NEW script that copies one of them, or an existing one that
gains a relaunch, would reintroduce the race with no gate going red. AGENTS.md "Test honesty": a pin on a RULE needs a
second mutant that adds a FRESH instance of the forbidden shape; a per-site pin cannot see one.

## Design direction

1. Decide the rule precisely before pinning it: "a script that holds a `launchChrome` handle and later either (a) exits
   under `scripts/security-suite-supervisor.mjs` custody or (b) calls `launchChrome` again with the same profile must not
   kill the leader with a bare `proc.kill` + `await proc.status`; it goes through `reapLeaderAndSettle` or
   `teardownChrome`". Scripts that never relaunch and are not custody-judged stay free to use a bare kill.
2. Enforce it with an AST scan over `scripts/*.ts` (esbuild strips types, acorn parses: both already used by
   `tests/jjsz-lifeline-runner-exit.test.ts`), with an explicit, justified allow-list for the ~30 non-judged scripts so a
   new entry has to be argued for.
3. Pin the scan with a fresh-instance mutant: add a new script that holds a launch handle, bare-kills it and relaunches on
   the same profile, and assert the scan goes red; plus a mutant that REMOVES one of the three existing
   `reapLeaderAndSettle` calls.

## Acceptance

- A test that goes red when a script outside the allow-list bare-kills a launched leader and then relaunches or exits
  under custody, and stays green on the current tree.
- The allow-list entries each carry a one-line reason.
- No change to `reapLeaderAndSettle` semantics.

## Must not change

`scripts/lib/process-tree.ts` lifeline semantics, `scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs` judgement, and the hash-pinned
`tests/fixtures/security-suite-fake-runner.mjs` (the supervisor self-test fixture; do not add scenarios).

Context: `docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md` section 6.4 (crash lifeline), bead chrome-agent-platform-80yqb (the sweep has no
generation check, which this rule mitigates but does not replace), `tests/jjsz-lifeline-runner-exit.test.ts` header.

title: Measure the version-dir GC grace: the default went 2000 -> 50 ms with no measured basis
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz; round-2 reviews, build N10(c) and security N6; Info)

jjsz cut the default version-directory GC grace in build.mjs from a fixed 2000 ms to 50 ms
(`resolveGcGraceMs`; `CAP_BUILD_GC_GRACE_MS=2000` restores it). The grace exists so a process that resolved the OLD
dist version just before a rebuild published the new one can finish reading it before the old tree is removed. The
2 s was a guess and so is 50 ms: the trade bought ~2 s per build (build:production 8.5 s -> ~5 s) but no test can
observe an old-tree reader window, so the safety margin is now an assumption.

## Do

Measure it: a stress harness with readers that resolve the previous version, read N files slowly, while a rebuild
publishes and GCs; find the smallest grace with zero failed reads on this host and one loaded host; set the default
from the measurement (with headroom) and document the number's basis in docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md 6.1.

## Acceptance

A recorded measurement (script + result) justifying the default, or the default restored to a measured value; a test
that a reader started before publish still reads a complete old tree for the grace period.

title: build-lock steals when kill(pid,0) says alive but ps says gone: re-check kill(0) and treat a persisting contradiction as alive
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-2 security review, build-lock residual; Low)

`holderIsDead` (scripts/lib/build-lock.mjs): after `kill(holder.pid, 0)` SUCCEEDED (the process answers), a probe
verdict of `{ok:false, reason:"gone"}` is read as proof of death and the lock is stolen. On macOS "gone" is
`ps` exit 1 with EMPTY stdout and EMPTY stderr; on Linux it is /proc ENOENT. Those are exactly right for a process
that died between the two probes (the race the comment describes), but a `ps` that exits 1 silently for any OTHER
reason (not observed; not excluded) would read a LIVE build's lock as stealable, and two concurrent builds corrupt
dist.

## Do

When kill(0) said alive and the probe says "gone", RE-RUN `kill(holder.pid, 0)`: ESRCH now means it really died
(steal); success again is a persisting contradiction and must be treated as ALIVE (refuse to steal, keep polling).
Update the existing seam test that models the race with a single always-alive kill so it models [alive, ESRCH].

## Acceptance

A test with a kill seam that answers alive twice and a probe that says gone refuses to steal (RED when the re-check
is reverted); the real-death race ([alive, ESRCH]) still steals; the Linux /proc behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

title: killProcessTree's teardown pkill/pgrep uses the raw unescaped, unanchored treeMatch while the lifeline sweep escapes and anchors it (pre-existing)
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-2 security review, finding N4; Low; PRE-EXISTING on main)

`killProcessTree`'s teardown path (scripts/lib/process-tree.ts, the pkill/pgrep it runs for `treeMatch`) uses the
caller's `treeMatch` RAW: not regex-escaped and not end-anchored. The lifeline sweep, by contrast, uses
`lifelineMatchPattern` (every ERE metacharacter escaped, `( |$)` anchor, so `user-data-dir=/x/p1` no longer matches
`/x/p10`). A profile path with '.' or a prefix relationship to another live profile can therefore over-match on the
teardown path exactly as the sweep used to before its F4 fix. main has the same behaviour, so this is not a
regression of the jjsz landing.

## Do

Route the teardown pkill/pgrep patterns through `lifelineMatchPattern` (or a shared `profileMatchPattern`), keeping
the empty-pattern refusal and the "-" leading-character refusal.

## Acceptance

A test with two live stand-in processes whose command lines are `.../p1 ` and `.../p10 ` proves a teardown for p1
does not signal p10; RED when the escaping/anchoring is reverted. No change to the teardown's verdict semantics.

title: Lifeline watcher signals the bare leader pid as well as its group and arms with no verified group (security review N3)
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-2 security review, finding N3; Low)

`scripts/lib/process-tree.ts` LIFELINE_SCRIPT signals with `kill -TERM -"$CAP_LIFELINE_TARGET" "$CAP_LIFELINE_TARGET"`
(and the same with -KILL). The second operand is the BARE leader pid. When the group is known to be the leader's
own setsid group the bare operand adds nothing (the leader is a member of group -T) but it also signals WHATEVER
process holds that pid if the group no longer exists and the pid was recycled to a non-leader. Separately the
watcher arms even when `group` is undefined (`target = group ?? proc.pid`) or the leader is already gone, so the
signal path runs after a leader that was never isolated.

This is the pid-reuse class of lsk1p (empty group + pid reuse), made slightly wider by the bare operand. It needs
the pid space to wrap inside the sweep window, so it is Low; it is a ONE-LINE script change plus an arming rule.

## Do

1. Drop the bare operand when the group is verified (`kill -TERM -"$T"` only).
2. Arm the signal path only when `isolatedProcessGroup` recorded the leader (the caller passes `group`); with no
   verified group, arm only the profile pkill (or refuse and warn, as for treeMatch).

## Acceptance

Tests that are RED when each is reverted: a stand-in non-leader process holding the target pid is NOT signalled
by the sweep; an unverified group does not reach the group-signal path. The real-Chrome reaping numbers
(7 SIGSTOPped helpers reaped in ~62 ms) are unchanged. Related: lsk1p, 6tau8, 80yqb.

title: npm run test:security cannot run on macOS: Deno fstatSync(9) on an inherited fd is EBADF (main refuses identically)
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz, 2026-10-07, macOS 15 arm64, Deno 2.9.0)

`npm run test:security` exits 2 within 1 s: the receipt shows `result: FAIL, exit: 2`, and the runner log says
`SECURITY-SUITE REFUSED: canonical inherited lock fd is missing. Run via npm run test:security only.`
Pristine origin/main refuses identically on macOS (its `verifyInheritedCanonicalLock` is /proc-only, and macOS has
no /proc). The jjsz branch added a no-/proc branch (`fstatSync(fd)` dev/ino compare + a `flock -n -E` probe) that
works in Node (the supervisor, which verifies fd 9 and passes), but CANNOT work in the Deno runner: Deno's
`node:fs` fd namespace is not the OS fd table. Measured: `bash -c 'exec 9>x.lock; deno eval "fstatSync(9)"'`
throws EBADF while `node -e` fstat succeeds on the same inherited descriptor; `ls -l /dev/fd/9` shows the lock file.
So the real security gate has never been runnable on macOS, and the new branch is exercised only through its
injected-seam unit tests.

## Do

On no-/proc platforms stat `/dev/fd/<fd>` (macOS fdesc stat == fstat of that descriptor) in BOTH runtimes instead
of `fstatSync(fd)`; keep the dev/ino compare and the flock probe. Seam it (`statPath("/dev/fd/9")`) so the
jjsz-macos-custody-lock-verdicts tests cover the real call.

## Acceptance

`npm run test:security` runs end to end on macOS (or the refusal is a documented, deliberate platform gate with
a distinct message). This also unlocks the REAL measurement of the lifeline residue judgement (the supervisor's
final liveObservedResidue sample vs a lingering lifeline watcher; see reap-leader.ts), which at landing time was
proved only by a deterministic fixture under the real custody functions, not by the real flow.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: Correction to the "Do" section above, measured afterwards (macOS 15 arm64, Deno 2.9.0): `statSync("/dev/fd/9")` is NOT equivalent to fstat on macOS. It reports devfs's device (dev 703529602, not the lock file's 16777229) with the lock file's inode, and `stat("/dev/fd/N")` also succeeds for a descriptor that is not open in the process (Deno holds its own low-numbered fds). The form that works: open the descriptor write-only and fstat the HANDLE, `Deno.openSync("/dev/fd/9", {write: true}).statSync()` (Node: `fs.openSync("/dev/fd/9", "a")` + `fs.fstatSync(fd)`), which returned the lock file's dev and ino exactly (equal: true). The open must be write-only because the supervisor opens the lock with `exec 9>` (O_WRONLY) and macOS refuses an `/dev/fd` re-open that asks for more access than the original. Fail closed when the open throws (not inherited) and when dev/ino differ.

title: Lifeline sweep has no generation check: its profile pkill can kill a later Chrome launched on the same profile inside the sweep window
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-2 security review, finding N6; and N2)

The crash-safe lifeline's leader-exit sweep (`sweepBody` in `scripts/lib/process-tree.ts`) ends with
`pkill -9 -f 'user-data-dir=<profile>( |$)'` and runs for >= ~110 ms after the leader exits. It has NO generation
check: a browser launched on the SAME profile inside that window is killed. Landing mitigation:
`reapLeaderAndSettle` (scripts/lib/reap-leader.ts) awaits the sweep at the three call sites that exit or
relaunch right after killing a leader (security-suite.ts finally, page-actions-journey.ts,
keyless-first-result.ts). The residual is any OTHER caller that relaunches on one profile without awaiting
`lifelineState(proc).settled`, and any cross-process relaunch (a handle-less teardown has no key).

## Proposed fix (remove the class, not the instances)

Match on something unique to the launch, not the profile path: pass a per-launch marker in Chrome's args (e.g.
`--cap-launch-id=<uuid>`) and have the lifeline's pkill pattern use THAT; or record the leader's start time at
attach and make the watcher refuse to pkill when a live process with the profile pattern started later.

## Acceptance

A test that relaunches on the same profile while a slowed sweep is in flight keeps the second browser alive and
still reaps the first browser's helpers; it is RED when the marker/start-time guard is reverted.
Related: lsk1p (group pid reuse), 4o93n (other lifeline edge cases).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Round-3 security review (finding 1, MEDIUM, BLOCK) plus a real-Chrome measurement by the coordinator: `scripts/security-injection.ts` is a FOURTH site, and the first scan that said "no other script relaunches on the same profile" was wrong.

What happened: `kill()` was a bare `proc.kill("SIGKILL"); await proc.status`, and `boot()` opens a SECOND Chrome on the same profile right after it (the first `await kill()`, then the second `boot()`). The lifeline's leader-exit sweep (new in the jjsz work: `main`'s lifeline is disarmed when the leader exits, so `main` never sweeps) ends with `pkill -9 -f 'user-data-dir=<profile>( |$)'` at least 100 ms later. That pattern matches the second browser's command line and kills it during start-up.

Measured (Chrome for Testing 149, macOS arm64, trees built, an empty `CAP_CHROME_SLOT_DIR` per run, 3 runs each; the oracle is "the second boot reached the checks", i.e. the log contains `permissions held (seeded)`; the script's own pass/fail is NOT the oracle because its checks fail on macOS on `main` too, Chrome for Testing drops the seeded Preferences grants):
- unfixed jjsz tip e2fa9a97: second boot reached 0/3. Every run died in the second `boot()` launch (scripts/security-injection.ts:154 via :96): two "launchChrome: Chrome never printed a DevTools endpoint" after 2 to 5 s, one EPERM from killProcessTree.
- origin/main 1d818d09: 3/3.
- fixed (`kill()` awaits `reapLeaderAndSettle(proc)`): 3/3. Stray Chrome for Testing processes after every batch: 0.
Evidence: /Users/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/jjsz-landing/real-chrome-injection/ (RESULT.txt, run logs, the script).

Fixed per-site in the landing (call-site, order and bare-kill pins plus a declaration-count binding rule in tests/jjsz-lifeline-runner-exit.test.ts). The CLASS is still open: the guard is per-site and any caller that relaunches on one profile without awaiting the sweep reproduces it. The round-3 widened scan found no further site (same-profile bare-kill relaunchers); `perf-seeded-scale`, `read-page-host-grant-acceptance` and `screenshot-vision-evidence` end with a bare kill and are harmless.

Structural fix (what this bead should do): make `launchChrome` itself await an in-flight sweep on its own profile (a registry keyed by the profile path holding `lifelineState(proc).settled`), so no caller has to remember; or the per-launch marker in the proposed fix above. Acceptance gains: a launcher that kills a leader and immediately relaunches on the same profile, WITHOUT calling `reapLeaderAndSettle`, keeps the second browser alive; RED when the registry wait is removed.

title: Lifeline watcher is not isolated until its wrapper calls setsid(): a parent process-group kill inside that window takes the watcher with it
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz, found by worker W2 while making the crash test deterministic)

The lifeline watcher is isolated by its own wrapper: `setsidSpawnSpec` runs `/usr/bin/perl -MPOSIX -e 'POSIX::setsid() ...; exec ...'` on macOS (or `/usr/bin/setsid` on Linux), and that `setsid()` runs a few milliseconds AFTER `Deno.Command.spawn()` returns. Until then the watcher still shares the PARENT's process group. A SIGKILL of the parent's whole GROUP inside that window (a test runner killing its process group, the shape the crash test simulates) kills the watcher together with its parent, and nothing reaps the browser. W2's probe: killing the parent's group immediately after attach orphaned the target in 7 of 20 runs; once the watcher's own group was visible, 20 of 20 were reaped. A kill of the parent ALONE, or of its group after the window, is covered.

Real exposure is small: `launchChrome` keeps running for at least the browser's start-up after attaching. The guarantee is stated in scripts/lib/process-tree.ts (`attachProcessLifeline` doc) and tests/process-tree-cleanup.test.ts waits for isolation before it kills the group.

## Intent
The crash guarantee should hold from the instant `attachProcessLifeline` returns, not a few milliseconds later.

## Design options
1. Make attach wait for `processGroup(watcher.pid).group === watcher.pid` before returning. That makes `attachProcessLifeline` asynchronous, so `launchChrome` (already async) awaits it; every other caller must accommodate. Bound the wait (about 500 ms) and warn once if it elapses, as for a failed spawn.
2. Have the watcher's parent-side stdin pipe be the only coupling and put the isolation in the spawn itself (a double-fork helper that returns only after `setsid` completed).

## Acceptance
A test that kills the parent's whole group IMMEDIATELY after attach (no wait for isolation) and still sees the group reaped; RED when the wait is removed. Measured with the real-Chrome harness as well.

title: Lifeline watcher signals its group by number with no leader-identity re-check (empty group plus pid reuse can hit another lane's tree)
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz: round-1 security review finding 7, and worker W2's F6, documented but not implemented)

The lifeline watcher (`LIFELINE_SCRIPT` in scripts/lib/process-tree.ts) signals the browser's group by NUMBER: `kill -TERM -"$T" "$T"; sleep 0.1; kill -KILL -"$T" "$T"`, with no re-check that the process leading that group is still the leader the lifeline was attached to. A LIVE group is always the right one (the kernel does not reuse a PGID while any member lives). The hole is an EMPTY group whose pid has been recycled: all of (1) this process's event loop is wedged so the leader is reaped before the sweep runs, (2) every member is gone so the pid is free, (3) that pid is handed to a NEW process that leads a group of its own (another lane's setsid child), and (4) this process is then SIGKILLed inside that window. The watcher then signals the unrelated group, and the bare trailing `"$T"` signals the pid itself.

jjsz's leader-exit sweep shrinks (1)-(3) to the event-loop latency plus the watcher's shell start-up (milliseconds), but it also means this signal path now runs after EVERY leader exit, not only at parent death. Blast radius if it ever fires wrongly is a different lane's process tree.

## Design
Record the leader's start time at attach (`isolatedProcessGroup` already stores `startTicks` in `leaderStartTicks`), pass it to the watcher in a third env var (`CAP_LIFELINE_START`), and have the watcher compare before signalling: Linux `/proc/$T/stat` field 22; macOS `/bin/ps -o lstart= -p $T` under `LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC` (the same pinned environment build-lock uses). Skip the group signal when a process with pid `$T` EXISTS with a DIFFERENT start; a leader that is simply absent still means "the old group, or nothing", so the signal still goes out.

## Acceptance / falsification
- A test that stands up a process with the recorded pid but a different start (inject the reader) and asserts the watcher does NOT signal; restoring the unconditional signal turns it RED.
- The real-Chrome scenarios still pass: launcher-kill, leader-kill, leader-kill-wedged all REAPED in about 60 ms (harness: /tmp/jjsz-probe/w2/real-chrome-w2.ts, archived in the jjsz evidence bundle).
- Must NOT change: disarm ordering (shell SIGKILLed before stdin closes), the one-shot sweep, group validation.

title: Bound and environment-pin the remaining gate probes: custody ps env, flock probe timeout, quiet-window ps timeout
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz, W1 residuals)

jjsz hardened build-lock and the quiet-window sampler: `ps` runs under a cleared environment with `LC_ALL=C` and `TZ=UTC`, and build-lock bounds it with a 5 s timeout. Custody's `ps` got a 5 s SIGKILL timeout too (`makePsRun`, scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:139-146). Three reads were left unhardened:

1. `scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs`: the `ps` calls are bounded but still run under the INHERITED environment (no `LC_ALL=C`, no `TZ=UTC`), so a non-C locale or a different TZ changes the `lstart` text. Identity comparison within one run is consistent, but a value recorded under one launch environment and read under another can mismatch.
2. `probeCanonicalLockHeld` (custody ~:238-250): its default runner (`run = (file, args) => execFileAsync(file, args)`, ~:240) has NO timeout, so a wedged `flock` hangs the custody chain.
3. `scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts:358` `defaultRunPs`: the environment is pinned but there is NO timeout, so a wedged `ps` blocks the quiet-window verdict indefinitely (the per-file window in scripts/test-partition.mjs is the only backstop).

## Intent
Every external probe in the gate path is bounded and environment-pinned, so a wedged tool becomes a typed, classified failure rather than a hang.

## Design
Reuse the `PS_ENV` + timeout pattern from scripts/lib/build-lock.mjs. A timeout must classify as UNREADABLE (fail closed), never as gone/clean: on timeout throw the existing typed `ProcessUnreadableError` (custody) or return `measurable:false` (quiet-window).

## Acceptance
- Seam tests that an exec which never resolves (or throws ETIMEDOUT) yields the unverified / not-measurable verdict, and RED when the timeout is removed.
- No change to verdicts on the happy path.

title: Decide the macOS fail-closed trade-offs jjsz introduced: retry before exit 70, and the one-time build-lock start-format transition
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz, deliberate fail-closed behaviour that needs an owner decision)

jjsz made two macOS paths fail CLOSED where they used to fail open. Both are documented in docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md 6.4 but have operator-visible consequences nobody has signed off:

1. **A TRANSIENT `ps` failure at the final residue check exits 70 on macOS** (the custody chain's "cannot confirm cleanup" verdict). A one-off `ps` hiccup now fails a security-suite run that would previously have passed. The check does not retry.
2. **One-time build-lock transition.** A live build-lock owner recorded BEFORE the upgrade holds a `start` string in the inherited-locale text; the new reader computes the canonical C-locale text, so the first comparison reads "different process" and the lock is stealable once. After the upgrade the recorded value is canonical and stable. Separately, a persistently broken `ps` now makes lock ACQUISITION refuse (bounded, about 24 s) rather than steal.

## Decision needed
(a) Add a bounded retry (for example 3 tries, 100 ms apart) around the final residue-check `ps` read before declaring unverified, or keep exit 70 as a strict verdict.
(b) For the transition: treat a recorded `start` that does not match the canonical form as UNKNOWN (alive) rather than different, which removes the one-time steal; or accept it as negligible (a build in flight during a repo upgrade of the build scripts themselves).

## Acceptance
Whatever is chosen has a seam test that is RED when reverted; the doc text in CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md 6.4 is updated in the same change.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Decision recorded by the jjsz landing (F5, from worker W2's review of the crash lifeline): when `attachProcessLifeline` cannot start its watcher (no /usr/bin/perl, EAGAIN on fork), `launchChrome` writes ONE line to stderr ("NOT protected") and the launch continues, with the pre-jjsz crash exposure. Chosen over refusing the launch because refusing would hard-fail every acceptance script on a host with a missing perl or a transient fork failure, for a protection that only matters if the launcher is later killed. The cost: such a run has no crash protection and the only signal is that one stderr line.

Open for the owner: flip to fail-closed (refuse the launch) if a silent unprotected run is judged worse than a hard failure. Pinned by tests/jjsz-lifeline-leader-exit.test.ts "a watcher that cannot start says so ONCE ... and returns a no-op (jjsz F5)"; that test would have to change with the policy. Documented in docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md section 6.4.

title: serial-build-once key binds the indexed source only: key the record on the dist.complete hash too
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-1 review, build/perf lane)

On a successful store build, `build.mjs` (~L307, ~L1024) writes `<durable root>/serial-build-once/<commit>-<source-digest>.json`. The reader, `storeBuildOnce` in `tests/fixtures/build-once.mjs` (~L31, ~L59), trusts a record only while the live `dist.complete` validates against the current tree AND the key equals the record's. That is sound today: a stale record cannot make a broken or missing build look current, because the reader revalidates against the real marker.

The key, however, binds only the git-indexed source, not the build that was run. Two builds of the same source that differ in anything outside the index (an environment variable that changes output, a different `CAP_BUILD_*` setting, a local patch that is untracked) share one record, and a record from one is accepted for the other whenever the live marker validates.

## Intent
Make the key describe the build, not only its input, so the record cannot be reused across builds that are allowed to differ.

## Design
Key on the live `dist.complete` content hash (it already binds HEAD, every indexed source byte and the generated bundles) in addition to commit + source digest. The reader computes it from the marker it is already validating, so no extra read of the tree is needed.

## Acceptance
- A test that two builds producing different marker hashes from the same source and commit write and read different records. Reverting to the old key must turn it RED.
- The existing tests/build-parallel-discipline.test.ts rule B (single writer, after the last fatal step, gated by shouldRecordBuild) stays green.
- Document the change in docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md 6.2.

title: Re-measure and tighten the serial per-file windows in test-partition (850 s / 550 s predate the parallel build)
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz)

`scripts/test-partition.mjs:122-123` gives two serial files very wide per-file windows: `tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts` 850_000 ms ("278s measured (contended) x 3.1") and `tests/build-debug-mode.test.ts` 550_000 ms ("173s measured (contended) x 3.2"). Those measurements pre-date jjsz's parallel build (a warm store build went from about 8.5 s to about 4.5 s on one Apple-silicon workstation; the full build gate from minutes to 31-36 s). A hang in either file is now detected up to ~14 minutes late, and that window is the only backstop when a file blocks.

## Intent
Windows should be the measured time on the CURRENT code times a margin, so a block is detected in minutes and the number is honest about where and when it was measured.

## Acceptance
- Re-measure both files on the merge host (Linux fleet host) AND on the Mac with `npm run test:file`, under the same contention the serial phase sees (run once alone, once with the parallel phase running).
- Set each window to roughly 3x the contended measurement; update the comment with the host, date and numbers.
- tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts and tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts stay green; no test is loosened.
- Must NOT tighten so far that a loaded merge host flakes: leave at least 2x headroom over the worst contended run observed.

title: macOS boot fence in build-lock is inert: machineBootId is the constant unknown-boot
description:
## Observed (pre-existing, found while reading scripts/lib/build-lock.mjs for chrome-agent-platform-jjsz)

`machineBootId()` (scripts/lib/build-lock.mjs:44) returns the constant `"unknown-boot"` on macOS because there is no /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id. The boot fence therefore never fires on macOS: a lock file left by a build from BEFORE a reboot can have its pid reused by a different process after the reboot, and the fence that exists to catch exactly that is inert.

## Intent
Give macOS a real boot identity so the fence works.

## Design
`sysctl -n kern.boottime` prints `{ sec = 1759800000, usec = 0 } Tue Oct  7 ...`; take the `sec` field (locale-independent, monotonic per boot). Run it with the same hardened environment build-lock uses for `ps` (`LC_ALL=C`, `TZ=UTC`, cleared env, 5 s timeout) through the existing exec seam, and fall back to `"unknown-boot"` only when the read fails (the fence stays inert rather than throwing).

## Acceptance
- A seam test with canned `sysctl` output: a different `sec` value makes an otherwise-identical lock stale; an identical one keeps it live.
- A test that a failed `sysctl` read degrades to the old constant and does not throw.
- Linux unchanged (still reads /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id).

title: macOS custody proofs are weaker than Linux: sid is fabricated as pgid; canonical-lock proof does not prove fd 9 itself holds the lock; flock is PATH-resolved
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz, W1 + security review, 2026-10-07)

Two macOS custody proofs are weaker than their Linux counterparts, by construction. jjsz documented both in code; this bead decides whether to strengthen them.

1. **`sid` is fabricated as `pgid`.** `ps` cannot report a session id, so a macOS identity carries `sid: pgid` (scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:5, :103, and the `sid === pid` note at ~:440). The `sid === pid` clause of the "is this the launched leader" check is therefore implied by `pgid === pid` on macOS and proves nothing. A portable signal exists and was measured on this Mac: `ps -o stat=` includes `s` for a session leader (`Ss` = setsid'd, `S` = setpgid-only, `S+` = a plain child). Wiring it would make the macOS check really distinguish a setsid'd launch from a setpgid-only one.
2. **The inherited canonical-lock proof is "the file behind fd 9 is the lock file (same dev/ino) AND somebody holds it", not "fd 9 itself holds it".** `verifyInheritedCanonicalLock` (custody ~:274) on macOS uses `flock -n -E 97 <lockfile> true`: a "cannot take it" verdict proves the lock is held by someone, not by the inherited descriptor. `flock` is resolved through PATH (same as scripts/security-suite-supervisor.sh:16), so a PATH shim could answer. The Linux branch reads /proc/locks and proves the exact holder.

## Intent
Decide, per item, whether to strengthen or to keep and keep documented. Do not weaken either.

## Options
1. `s`-flag: add `stat` to the `ps -o` column list in `parsePsIdentityLine`, derive `sid` = pid when `s` is present and the process is its own group leader, else null; adjust the leader check to require the flag. Seam-test with canned `ps` rows (`Ss`, `S`, `S+`).
2. Lock: resolve `flock` to an absolute path once (`/opt/homebrew/bin/flock`, `/usr/local/bin/flock`, `/usr/bin/flock`) and refuse a binary that does not answer `--version` like util-linux or discoteq; or hold-test through the inherited descriptor itself (`flock -n 9` in a child that inherits fd 9: flock is per open-file-description, so a duplicate shares it) provided the probe cannot change the lock state.

## Acceptance
Each option that is taken has a seam test that is RED when the strengthening is reverted. Linux /proc behaviour unchanged.

title: Admit hash-wasm sha3-384/sha3-512/keccak-256 variants (shared 4,018-byte binary vs the 1:1 CAS-to-manifest invariant)
description: Filed 2026-10-07 during 3wei. hash_sha3_256, hash_sha3_384, hash_sha3_512 and hash_keccak_256 all resolve to the IDENTICAL 4,018-byte binary (sha256 4b3e3ab7...), differing only by the ABI initParam (bits) and finalParam (padding byte). scripts/package-archive.mjs:538 (buildBundledWasmManifestMap) throws 'duplicate bundled Wasm manifest mapping' when two manifests claim the same CAS path, and tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts:409 pins that as a hostile duplicate-identity rejection; :125 pins cas.length === manifests.length. Under the current model, 3 of those 4 variants cannot be admitted. 3wei therefore admits ONLY hash_sha3_256 and defers the rest. RESOLVE BY one of: (a) a deliberate, reviewed extension of the store model to allow N manifests per CAS blob while keeping duplicate-manifest-IDENTITY rejection (must be security-reviewed — this is an identity boundary); (b) a distinct upstream/variant binary per algorithm (e.g. a parameterised CAP-authored build) with its own provenance; (c) a single multi-variant tool contract. Do NOT loosen the invariant casually.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
PRIOR ART for options (b)/(c) - recorded 2026-10-12 from the parked branch origin/cap-beads-3wei@19ebe9997ce6 (parked-branch triage, bead 3cdz). Read-only reference: that branch never landed (3wei was closed through the 14 hash-wasm call-export tools instead, 9fe653fb) and it is the ONLY ref that contains a4ae5c4c / 19ebe999, so it stays parked until Paul decides whether to keep it.

WHAT IT IS: a CAP-authored Rust WASI tool, ONE manifest, ONE CAS blob, six algorithms behind a single tool contract. That satisfies the 1:1 CAS-to-manifest invariant WITHOUT loosening it (this bead's option (c)), at a size cost.

CONTRACT (packages/bundled/evidence/hasher/src/main.rs, 75 lines)
  hasher --algo sha256|sha512|sha3-256|sha3-512|blake2b|blake3
  stdin = the source bytes; stdout = lowercase hex digest + "\n"; errors -> stderr "hasher: <msg>", exit 2
  refused: unknown flag, missing --algo value, extra arguments, unknown algo. No network, no env, no threads.
  Pinned crates (default-features=false): sha2 =0.10.9, sha3 =0.10.8, blake2 =0.10.6, blake3 =1.8.2, hex =0.4.3
  Release profile: opt-level 2, lto, codegen-units 1, strip, panic=abort.

ARTIFACT (as committed on the branch)
  hasher.wasm 97,135 B, sha256 c5f0f9b744f1c5c5620ccf48bfa894c932c2f5ebb0105d7d8cadfa1df5de7d3b; build-a == build-b (Cargo.lock-pinned, byte-reproducible).
  Imports wasi_snapshot_preview1 only; memory initialPages 17 / maxPages 2048 (default tier); replayClass read-only; capabilities compute+crypto; licence MIT AND Apache-2.0; CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM.
  Compare: this bead's hash-wasm variants share ONE 4,018-byte binary. The CAP-authored build is ~24x larger because it carries all six algorithms.

KNOWN-ANSWER VECTORS (tests/hasher-admission.test.ts, 214 lines; input "hello"): sha3-512 = 75d527c368f2efe848ecf6b073a36767800805e9eef2b1857d5f984f036eb6df891d75f72d9b154518c1cd58835286d1da9a38deba3de98b5a53e5ed78a84976. I recomputed sha3-512, sha3-256 and blake2b of "hello" with Python hashlib on 2026-10-12 and all three match the test's expected values. The test also pins the RFC 4634 sha256("abc") vector, build-a == build-b reproducibility, and the manifest's tier/replay/capability declarations.

DO NOT merge or rebase the branch: its tip (19ebe999) commits an UNRESOLVED merge conflict in extension/lib/bundled-tool-packages.data.js (markers at :945 <<<<<<< HEAD, :974 =======, :1005 >>>>>>> a4ae5c4c - verified on the tip), carries 183 cargo target/ files (~20 MB) and is ~1600 commits behind main. Use it as a design reference only; the source is small enough to re-create on a fresh worktree off origin/main with the KAT test as the spec (and a fresh security review of the identity boundary, as this bead already requires).

Note for the decision: option (c) trades binary size for keeping the invariant intact; options (a)/(b) keep the tiny shared binary and need the store-model change or a parameterised build. This comment does not choose.

description:

The test suites and the self-contained instruments were plumbed on that branch (fleet/merger-jsjy); these five were NOT, and the reason is not difficulty but verifiability.
  THE FIVE: cap-evidence/acp-browser-acceptance.ts (creates the bridge at 3210 and already seeds acp.endpoint + acp.token for its LAN case, so its LOCAL case needs the same treatment), cap-evidence/acp-settings-browser-acceptance.ts (creates the bridge at TEST_PORT and drives the real Settings page, which reads acp.endpoint/acp.token), cap-evidence/acp-journal-acceptance.ts (bridge at 3210, extension uses the DEFAULT endpoint), cap-evidence/vl6c-browser-acceptance.ts (bridge at PORT, seeds acp.endpoint in extension storage at ~line 142), cap-evidence/acp-multiharness-probe.ts (drives an AcpClient against a bridge it does not itself create).

Routing the secret through them is not just a URL edit — the extension has to be given the token too (acp.token in kv/storage, or an endpoint that already carries ?token=), and that is a per-instrument decision about which surface each one is exercising. They can only be verified by running the journey, which needs a browser-capable box and a built extension, so a blind patch would be an unverifiable change to evidence instruments — the same trap as landing a gate no one can run.
  ACCEPTANCE: for each, the bridge it creates requires the secret it seeds into the extension (or the endpoint it configures carries ?token=), the journey runs to its own success marker on a browser-capable box, and the run's log shows the authenticated path rather than a bypass. If any instrument is obsolete, retire it explicitly rather than leaving it broken.

title: ACP bridge residual: a local process that binds 127.0.0.1:3210 BEFORE the bridge harvests the persisted token from the extension's upgrade, and can then impersonate the harness indefinitely
description:
RAISED BY THE CROSS-FAMILY REVIEW of chrome-agent-platform-jsjy (gemini-3.8-flash, weaponisation line, 2026-10-06) and deliberately NOT fixed in that change — recorded as a scope boundary, not overlooked.
  THE RESIDUAL: the bridge speaks plain ws:// on loopback and the extension presents its shared secret in the UPGRADE QUERY STRING (acpEndpointWithToken -> /acp?token=<secret>). Nothing authenticates the SERVER to the client, so an unprivileged local attacker who binds 127.0.0.1:3210 first is simply 'the bridge' as far as the extension can tell, and the extension will hand over the secret. jsjy's change makes that secret PERSISTENT (generated once, stored at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cap-acp/bridge-token, mode 0600, reused across restarts) rather than ephemeral per start, so a token harvested once stays valid — the review is right that this AMPLIFIES the pre-existing race rather than creating it.
  WHY IT IS NOT FIXED AT THE SAME TIME: jsjy's acceptance was the DEFAULT-AUTH gap (no authentication at all on loopback). Closing this one requires authenticating the server to the client, which is a different mechanism — TLS/wss with a pinned certificate, a per-run secret (which reintroduces the setup friction jsjy removed), or delivering the secret out of band via the native-messaging transport (chrome-agent-platform-o65r, explicitly out of scope for jsjy). Choosing among those is a design decision with an operator-workflow cost, not a one-line hardening.
  RELATED: the same review noted two further local-attacker avenues that are inherent and lower value: --token on the command line is visible in ps/proc cmdline (the default path uses the file, not the flag), and 0600 is unenforceable on a filesystem without POSIX permissions (e.g. a FAT/NTFS mount), which is why the bridge also refuses non-loopback binds by client policy.
  ACCEPTANCE: decide and implement one server-authenticating mechanism (wss + pinned cert, per-run token, or native transport), OR document explicitly that the loopback bind is trusted against local processes and cite the threat model. Either way T13/THREAT_MODEL should carry the residual, since jsjy's landing note records it only in the bead.

title: the wfxe postMessage wildcard guard reports line numbers from the COMMENT-STRIPPED source, so its violation messages point at a line that does not exist
description:

Measured: the cap:go-home site in extension/options/options.js is reported as options.js:4599; its real line is 4614 (grep -n postMessage extension/options/options.js), i.e. 15 comment lines above it were removed. The drift grows with the file's comment volume, so in the big files it is large.

NOT yi5q (that bead is about DYNAMIC origin||"*" fallbacks the literal matcher never sees).

title: [tooling] the widened repo-walk detector does not scan tests/helpers, so a repo-walking guard can hide in a helper — which is exactly the shape a faithful -static split encourages
description: FOUND by qazo while landing chrome-agent-platform-ygxk (2026-10-06), and it is the reason it declined to split that file. THE GAP: p1lp widened the detector to match KNOWN SOURCE ROOTS by definition rather than any uppercase identifier, which closed the kz27 over-match AND the two escaping guards. But the detector scans TEST FILES; it does not scan tests/helpers. So a repo walk moved into a shared helper is invisible to the audit — and the fleet's own split pattern POINTS THAT WAY: when a mixed file is split into a -static half, the shared machinery has to live somewhere, and tests/helpers/ is the natural home. That means the next faithful split can silently reopen the hole p1lp just closed, which is the same failure mode as the original kz27 blind spot (a guard everyone believes is always-on but is not). EVIDENCE: qazo measured the alternative rather than asserting it — sharing the machinery between halves requires a tests/helpers/ module, which would put the repo walk outside the scanned roots. ACCEPTANCE: either extend the detector to scan tests/helpers (and any other shared test-support root) for the same KNOWN SOURCE ROOTS shape, or add an explicit assertion that no repo walk exists outside the scanned roots so a helper-based walk fails closed; and prove it with a REAL-TREE falsification — place a repo-walking helper under tests/helpers behind an always-on-ish guard and show the audit FAILS CLOSED (names it and refuses to pass), then remove it and show green. Related: p1lp (landed 090151e7) for the detector's current shape, and uvo3 for the two owed -static splits that will face this decision.

(3) BOTH HALVES OF THE OVER-MATCH PIN ARE ACCEPTANCE, not one: a repo-walking helper is NAMED, and a helper that walks ONLY its own fixture directory is NOT admitted — the second half is what stops the scan being widened until it admits every fixture reader, which is how quiet-window entered ALWAYS_ON and tripled every subset gate. Also accepted: my honest substitution note, so if the real tree has no repo-walking helper I say so and use the substituted fixture rather than claiming a real-tree pass that did not happen — my plan is stronger than a substitution (a real helper file created under tests/helpers, asserted to be NAMED, then removed in a finally) and I will state which of the two the evidence actually is. SEQUENCING: uvo3 after afpl, sequentially, same ALWAYS_ON list — and uvo3 is precisely the bead that will CREATE helpers of this shape when it extracts the two -static halves, which is why afpl has to land first.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW (different family from the author) — fleet/qazo-afpl @ 6f885424, reviewed in a
clean reviewer worktree at exactly that sha (git status --porcelain empty before and after; every
temporary patch reverted with git checkout --; no browser launched).

VERDICT: REJECT — 2 x P1, 2 x P2. Not fixable by re-gating; the full gate is not what is missing.

====================================================================================
ANSWERS TO THE FOUR VERIFICATION POINTS
====================================================================================

(1) DOES THE DETECTOR ACTUALLY SCAN tests/helpers? YES — the scan is sound; the CLASSIFIER it feeds
is not. Roots scanned, named from the code: sharedSupportFiles() at
tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts:215-296 walks EVERY subdirectory of tests/ (so
tests/helpers/, tests/support/, tests/utils/ are covered generically rather than by name — better
than hardcoding), excluding only fixtures/, node_modules and dotfiles (:244, :276), with symlink
confinement (:230) and loop prevention (:231); PLUS the non-test .ts/.js/.mjs modules directly under
tests/. Measured on the real tree via deno eval: 6 files today (tests/00-use-npm-test_test.ts,
fake-idb.js, fake-locks.js, test-hooks.js, package-extension-freshness-driver.mjs,
wasm-fixture-builder.mjs). tests/helpers/ does not exist at HEAD, so the count is 6 + whatever I
planted. Fail-closed half verified real-tree: a non-test can be exempted by NEITHER route (:185 and
:189 both gate on `isTest &&`), and when I added a flagged helper to SOURCE_INSPECTING_GUARDS the
audit STILL named it AND :440 red separately. That half is correct and well built.

(2) REAL-TREE FALSIFICATION — reproduced independently, both directions, and it is where P1-1 comes
from. Planted 5 helper spellings under tests/helpers/ + 2 depth-1 controls under tests/:
  FAILED | 9 passed | 1 failed — message named tests/helpers/zz-a-upper-root-join.ts,
  zz-d-imported-root.ts, zz-e-author-scratch-shape.ts with actionable guidance.
  rm -rf tests/helpers -> ok | 10 passed | 0 failed (797ms).
  Residue verified absent by BOTH rg --hidden --no-ignore and python os.walk (p4tf); git status empty.
  2 of the 5 spellings were NOT named -> Finding 1.
The SHIPPED falsification at :458-475 is a scratch-tree SUBSTITUTE (durableDir("scratch")), not the
real tree. The substitution is a defensible engineering choice (p15i: never write untracked files
into the tracked tree) and its finally-cleanup leaves no residue (verified: nothing under
~/cap-evidence/scratch/). But the acceptance said REAL-TREE, and the promised "I will state which of
the two the evidence actually is" is recorded nowhere — the bead's last comment is the 10:57 gate log
and there is no author report comment at all.

(3) NO OVERREACH — CLEAN. The diff touches NO p1lp classifier regex (grepped the diff for all seven
names: zero +/- hits). Every removed line is accounted for: the import widening;
/readDirSync\(\s*join\(\s*ROOT\b/ (a genuine over-match — it fired on join(ROOT, "tests",
"fixtures"), the author's own negative case at :492; the TOP-LEVEL case join(ROOT, "tests") is still
caught by JOIN_ENDS_AT_TOP_LEVEL, proven by shape A being named); the name list at :177 (widened by
readdirSync/opendir/opendirSync, not narrowed); the two `isTest &&` guards (a TIGHTENING for the new
inputs, a no-op for the old ones); the non-recursive enumeration; the old message. No unrelated tree
is scanned: all 14 measured entries were under tests/. Symlink escape and symlink loop both refused
in a scratch tree (enumerateTestFiles -> [], sharedSupportFiles -> []), so readdirSync(recursive)
does not follow symlinks and :230 holds. kz27/fgik over-match stays closed: the p1lp DOM-walk
negative at :410 passes, and my proposed fix below keeps all five over-match negatives unmatched.

(4) EXISTING ASSERTIONS + deno check — CLEAN. deno check --config deno.runner.jsonc on the changed
file: exit 0. Guard file 10/10. Cross-cutting watchers a subset gate cannot see (AGENTS.md coupling
rule 4) run together: test-partition-guard, substring-pin-honesty, machine-path-honesty,
durable-root, file-url-root-guard, harness-registry = 61 passed / 0 failed in 9s. Blast radius is one
file: nothing imports it (only other tracked reference is the name string at
scripts/select-tests.mjs:73).

====================================================================================
FINDINGS
====================================================================================

--- FINDING 1 (P1, acceptance-critical) ---
The source-root CLASSIFIER is anchored to depth 1, so the natural spelling for a tests/helpers/
module escapes the root this bead exists to cover.

WHERE: tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts:127-128
  const REPO_ROOT_URL = /new URL\(\s*["']\.\.\/?["']/;
  const TOP_LEVEL_URL = new RegExp(`new URL\\(\\s*["']\\.\\.?\\/(?:${TOP_LEVEL_DIRS})\\/?["']`);
consumed by denotesSourceRoot (:135-142) and identifierIsSourceRoot (:143-150) from :215.
REPO_ROOT_URL admits only ".." and "../"; TOP_LEVEL_URL admits only "../<topdir>". A file two levels
deep derives the repo root as "../../" and extension/ as "../../extension/" — neither matches.

EVIDENCE (real tree, my worktree, HEAD 6f885424). IDENTICAL code, only the ../ count differs:
  tests/zz-b1-same-shape-depth1.ts              new URL("../")           + Deno.readDir(root) -> NAMED
  tests/helpers/zz-b-lower-dotdot-url.ts        new URL("../../")        + Deno.readDir(root) -> NOT NAMED
  tests/helpers/nested/deep/zz-b3-depth4.ts     same                     -> NOT NAMED
  tests/zz-c1-same-shape-depth1.ts              walk(new URL("../extension/"))  -> NAMED
  tests/helpers/zz-c-walk-dotdot-subdir-url.ts  walk(new URL("../../extension/")) -> NOT NAMED
The scan is NOT the problem: my instrumentation showed sharedSupportFiles() DID read
tests/helpers/nested/deep/zz-b3-depth4.ts (321 bytes) — the file is read, the walk is in it, and the
classifier says no. "../../" is this repo's own depth-2 idiom (scripts/lib/chrome-profile-dir.ts:78,
scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:279) and it is the ONLY correct way for a tests/helpers/ module to
name the repo root. So the property this same file pins at :404-413 ("a walk over a LOWERCASE alias
of a source root must be flagged when it is unlisted") is FALSE for every file the diff newly scans.
That is p1lp's UNDER-MATCH verbatim, relocated into the new root — and the bead's WHY is exactly
"the next faithful split can silently reopen the hole p1lp just closed". uvo3 will do precisely
that: scripts/select-tests.mjs:181-199 names tests/wasm-package-authority.test.ts and the
heavy-gate-slot file as the two mixed files owed a -static split, and their shared machinery lands
at depth 2.

WHY THE SHIPPED PIN DID NOT SEE IT: :458-475 plants `const ROOT = "/repo"` — an identifier matching
KNOWN_SOURCE_ROOTS (:114) by NAME, plus join(ROOT, "tests") matching JOIN_ENDS_AT_TOP_LEVEL. That is
the single most detectable spelling and it is not a repo root at all. It proves the plumbing
(helpers reach the classifier and get named), not the property (a realistic helper repo-walk is
caught). Canon: "a pin on today's instance" and "every replacement pin ships with the mutant the old
pin missed".

SMALLEST FIX (validated by me, 10/10 cases, no over-match regression) — make :127-128 depth-agnostic:
  const REPO_ROOT_URL = /new URL\(\s*["']\.\.(?:\/\.\.)*\/?["']/;
  const TOP_LEVEL_URL = new RegExp(`new URL\\(\\s*["']\\.\\.(?:\\/\\.\\.)*\\/(?:${TOP_LEVEL_DIRS})\\/?["']`);
Still NOT matched after the fix (fgik sub-root over-match stays closed): new URL("./fixtures/"),
new URL("./"), new URL("../.cache/"), new URL("../../out/"), new URL("../../extension/wasm/").
Then add the depth-2 lowercase-alias spelling as a SECOND planted helper in the :458 falsification,
and prove the new pin has teeth by showing it fails at :127-128 unreformed.

--- FINDING 2 (P1) ---
A support module has NO exemption path at all, so a PROSE-ONLY false positive is a permanent red
whose guidance is unactionable — the exact outcome coord's refinement (1) forbade.

WHERE: :185 and :189 (`isTest &&` on both exemption routes) + :440-451 (the new assertion forbidding
a non-test in either list) + the bare-name SCANNER_PATTERNS at :70-95, applied to support modules at
:342. Contributing cause: 6f885424 removed stripComments, so prose is now matched in the one surface
that cannot be exempted.

EVIDENCE (real tree). Planted tests/helpers/zz-prose-min.ts — three lines, NO walk of any kind:
  // Shared helper. Deliberately does NOT shell out to git ls-files; it reads the
  // two files it is given.
  export function add(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; }
-> FAILED | 9 passed | 1 failed, naming it, with "Move the walk into the test file that needs it".
There is no walk. I then added it to SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS with a full reason + bead id: the audit STILL
named it (:189 requires isTest) AND :440 red with "SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS entry ... must be a test file".
Both exits closed; the only resolution is rewording a comment.

THE TRIGGER TEXT ALREADY EXISTS IN THE TREE — this is not hypothetical:
  tests/postmessage-wildcard-guard.test.ts:12 — "it looks for SCAN_DIRS/filesUnder(/git ls-files in a
    test file that is not..." — green today ONLY because it is listed at
    scripts/select-tests.mjs:74, and :185 skips it before any pattern runs.
  scripts/lib/source-materialization.mjs:4 — "`git ls-files` alone is the TRACKED set." — green today
    only because it is outside tests/.
A faithful -static split moves shared machinery AND its explanatory comments into tests/helpers/.
Either comment landing there reds permanently, on a bead whose whole point is to give the next
splitter a red they CAN act on.

SMALLEST FIX: keep the no-exit policy for the DEFINITION-BASED signal (walkOrReadRoots, :176-179) and
stop applying the three prose-matchable name patterns (/SCAN_(?:DIRS|ROOTS|TREES)/i,
/git\s+ls-files/i, /GUARD_ROOTS/) to non-test support modules at :342 — a helper that genuinely walks
a source root is already caught by walkOrReadRoots, as shapes A/D/E proved. Add a pin: a support
module whose only match is inside a comment is NOT flagged.

--- FINDING 3 (P2, report-only) ---
"no repo walk exists outside the scanned roots" is asserted NOWHERE, and a live in-tree example sits
outside. The design recorded on the bead says the classifier enforces that property; it does not —
the classifier only reads tests/**. scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:263 does Deno.readDirSync(SCRIPTS)
where SCRIPTS = fileURLToPath(new URL("../", import.meta.url)) (:259) — a KNOWN_SOURCE_ROOT walk in
shared test-support machinery, imported by tests/harness-registry.test.ts:19, which asserts on
harnessFiles() at :26 while containing no walk itself. Safe today ONLY because that test happens to
be listed at scripts/select-tests.mjs:71; nothing fails if the next such helper is consumed by an
UNLISTED test. That is the acceptance's option 2, genuinely absent. Fix: either extend
sharedSupportFiles() to the shared support roots under scripts/lib/ that tests import, or state the
gap in the docstring at :200-213 and file a bead — but do not record it as covered.

--- FINDING 4 (P2) ---
enumerateTestFiles (:329-332) omits the node_modules exclusion sharedSupportFiles applies at :244 and
:276; it filters only "/fixtures/" and "fixtures/". A future tests/**/node_modules would have its
.test.ts files demanded in SOURCE_INSPECTING_GUARDS. One line: && !f.includes("/node_modules/").

====================================================================================
IS ACCEPTANCE MET WITHOUT THE FULL GATE?
====================================================================================
NO — and the missing full gate is NOT the reason. The gate history as recorded is honest: the
parallel phase was green (246/0) before a reaper kill caused by the then-unfixed Chromium orphan
leak, which per the canon is an ENVIRONMENTAL verdict — INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass and never a
product red. On gate evidence alone this diff would be mergeable: it is confined to one test file,
carries no product code and no list edit, nothing imports it, and I ran the whole class of
cross-cutting watcher that AGENTS.md coupling rule 4 says a subset gate cannot see (61/61 green).
What blocks it is Finding 1: the acceptance's real-tree falsification does NOT fail closed for the
natural helper spelling, and the shipped pin structurally cannot see that. Re-run npm test after
Findings 1 and 2 are fixed (AGENTS.md still requires it before push; extension/dist is not built in
this reviewer worktree, so I could not have produced a meaningful full-gate verdict here regardless).

Per instruction I did NOT fix any of this on the branch. All planted files removed, both temporary
scripts/select-tests.mjs patches reverted, HEAD still 6f885424, git status --porcelain empty, and no
browser was launched by this review (0 chrome processes reference this worktree).
