ROUND 7 DELTA RE-REVIEW (reviewer, independent) — fleet/qazo-afpl @ 9d01f01a, delta from the rejected c0a3645d.

VERDICT: REJECT — narrow. NEW-3 (P2) CLOSED and independently proven. But THREE blocking findings:
the N1 pin for NEW-2 is VACUOUS (mutant survives), the :556 finally->try tidy RE-OPENED the NEW-1 pin
(the exact P1 regression mutant now survives AND a green suite deleted a staged foreign file), and the
HUB REQUIREMENT guard does not exist anywhere in the repo.

DELTA BOUNDARY (measured, not assumed)
  c0a3645d is NOT an ancestor of HEAD (the branch was rebased onto 51feb4a9). c0a3645d and 937fc50b carry
  the same subject, and `git diff c0a3645d 937fc50b -- tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts` is
  EMPTY, so 937fc50b IS the reviewed c0a3645d content on the new base. The review delta is therefore
  `git diff 937fc50b 9d01f01a` = ONE file, tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts, +66/-8.
  Whole-branch delta `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) HEAD --stat` (base 51feb4a9) = the same
  ONE file, +455/-16. fleet/qazo-afpl == origin/fleet/qazo-afpl == HEAD == 9d01f01a.
  Pristine guard sha256 before/after every experiment: cde428c72d2c02d99009b8fc846dbf537e50ccd42c9c78546aacdd1a5771cf6b.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. NEW-3 (P2) — CLOSED. The reconciliation is at module scope and is load-bearing.

CODE (tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts)
  :35-40   export const AFPL_REAL_TREE_RESIDUE = [ the exact 4 paths ]  — zz-afpl-depth2-walk.ts,
           zz-afpl-prose-only.ts, zz-afpl-fixture-read.ts, zz-afpl-preexisting-sibling.ts.
           Exact paths only: no directory removal, no prefix/shape match (p15i satisfied).
  :42-51   export function reconcileAfplRealTreeResidue(): void  — Deno.removeSync per path, try/catch.
  :53      reconcileAfplRealTreeResidue();  <- MODULE-EVALUATION CALL, above the FIRST Deno.test (:55).
  :55-75   Deno.test("afpl: SIGKILL residue is reconciled before the audit scans the tree") — declared
           ABOVE the audit (:391); plants the 4 paths (:61-63), calls the reconciler (:64), asserts
           existsSync === false per path (:65-67). Also mkdir/rmdir tests/helpers only if it created it.
  :520     the old :476-479 in-test block is GONE, replaced by a call to the same function.
  Deno evaluates the whole module (including :53) before ANY test body runs, so the sweep precedes :391
  unconditionally — not merely by declaration order.

INDEPENDENT PROOF — A/B, using the REAL fixture signature (not a placeholder). Planted in the real tree:
  tests/helpers/zz-afpl-depth2-walk.ts = `const root = new URL("../../", import.meta.url);` +
  `export function census() { for (const f of Deno.readDirSync(root)) void f; }`, plus the other 3.

  (a) PRISTINE HEAD, residue planted, FULL FILE RUN:
      => 12 passed | 0 failed, exit 0. "qcfc: self-checking audit ... ok (186ms)" GREEN IN THE SAME RUN.
      This is the exact reproduction that was RED at c0a3645d (10 passed | 1 failed, at :359).
  (b) PRISTINE HEAD, residue planted, `deno test --filter "self-checking audit"` (only the audit runs, so
      no test body can sweep or clobber):
      => ok | 1 passed | 0 failed | 11 filtered out, exit 0. The module-scope call swept it at import.
  (c) MUTANT M-A — delete ONLY the `reconcileAfplRealTreeResidue();` call at :53, same residue, same
      --filter:
      => FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed | 11 filtered out, exit 1
      => AssertionError at tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts:401 (mutated-file line; the
         audit's own assertEquals is at pristine :402-406)
         [Diff] - [ "tests/helpers/zz-afpl-depth2-walk.ts", ] / + []
      (b) GREEN vs (c) RED is a single-line A/B: the module-scope placement IS the cause. The green is
      NOT attributable to a side effect of another test. This is the observation my round-6 reproduction
      could not make, because at c0a3645d the sweep only happened as a side effect of the fixture test.
  (d) MUTANT M-B — neuter the reconciler body to a no-op, residue planted, full file run:
      => "afpl: SIGKILL residue is reconciled before the audit scans the tree ... FAILED"
      => AssertionError: residue tests/helpers/zz-afpl-depth2-walk.ts must be reconciled
         [Diff] - true / + false   at :60 in the mutated file (pristine :66, inside the :65-67 loop)
      The new :55 test HAS TEETH — it is not a name-only or text-only pin (canon mode 1).
  After every run: `git status --porcelain` empty, tests/helpers removed, guard sha256 unchanged.

P2 NOTE (non-blocking) on the :55 test's payload. It writes the literal "// residue\n" at :62, which
  is NOT a scanner signature. Measured consequence: under M-B the audit at :391 stayed GREEN even though
  the 4 residue files were still on disk, because :55 had already overwritten my real fixture content with
  a non-scanner payload before :391 ran. So :55 proves the RECONCILER MECHANISM but does not itself
  reproduce the END-TO-END symptom (real fixture content reaching the classifier). Evidence (a)-(c) above
  used the real signature and do prove the end-to-end property, so NEW-3 is closed on its own merits.
  Smallest improvement: have :62 write the actual fixture bodies — at minimum the depth-2 walker's
  `new URL("../../", import.meta.url)` + `Deno.readDirSync(root)` — so a future ordering regression reddens
  the audit as well as :55, and the test reproduces the symptom it is named for.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. FINDING F1 (P1, BLOCKING) — the :556 finally->try tidy RE-OPENED the NEW-1 pin.
##    The exact P1 regression mutant now SURVIVES, and a green suite deleted a staged foreign file.

The tidy itself was applied as asked:
  :585-588  owned-file cleanup moved to the END of the try block
  :589-590  const siblingSurvived = existsSync(siblingFile); assertEquals(..., true, "NEW-1: ...")
  :591-601  finally is now assertion-free: idempotent sweep of [...testFiles, siblingFile] + the
            non-recursive rmdir guarded by if (!helpersDirPreexisted)
So N2's masking concern is addressed. BUT the assertion at :590 now executes BEFORE the finally at :591,
so it can no longer observe anything the cleanup in the finally does — which is precisely where the
destructive act lived in the original NEW-1 bug.

MUTANT M-N2b — reintroduce the exact pre-fix regression as the first statement of the finally:
  `try { await Deno.remove(realHelpersDir, { recursive: true }); } catch {}`
  => 12 passed | 0 failed, exit 0. **THE MUTANT SURVIVES.**
  At c0a3645d this SAME mutant was KILLED (round-6 record: "afpl: REAL-TREE falsification ... FAILED
  (10 passed | 1 failed, exit 1) ... NEW-1: pre-existing sibling in tests/helpers must NOT be removed").
  This delta therefore REDUCED test strength. It violates falsification gate 1 in AGENTS.md ("a changed
  test must be proven able to fail ... revert the product fix, show the assertion go RED"): the assertion
  was moved and never re-proven, and it no longer goes red.

PROVEN DESTRUCTIVE, NOT A NO-OP MUTANT (the decisive evidence). I planted a genuinely FOREIGN file in the
shared dir and STAGED it, simulating another lane's landed helper:
  tests/helpers/zz-review-foreign-victim.ts   git status "A "
  sha256 554d98a5db0b08d4c40e98c265bd106ca039e55689cc765d115c573247dade25
Ran the file under M-N2b:
  => ok | 12 passed | 0 failed, exit 0     (a GREEN suite)
  => tests/helpers/zz-review-foreign-victim.ts: *** DELETED *** ; git status now "AD" (in index, gone on
     disk); tests/helpers directory GONE entirely.
That is the original NEW-1 P1 reproduced verbatim — destruction of another session's staged work by a
passing test, which AGENTS.md forbids outright and which p15i names ("a check attributes only what its own
run created") — and at 9d01f01a NOTHING IN THE SUITE NOTICES. The product cleanup at HEAD is still
correct; what is broken is the pin that is supposed to keep it correct, so the next refactor can silently
re-land the wipe.

EXACT CORRECTION (empirically validated by me, then reverted — file byte-identical to HEAD afterwards).
Move the survival assertion to AFTER the try/finally block, and stop listing siblingFile among the finally's
owned removals so the canary is genuinely foreign to the cleanup:
  :593   for (const f of [...testFiles, siblingFile]) {  ->  for (const f of testFiles) {
  :589-590  delete from inside the try
  after :601 (the finally's closing brace), still inside the test body:
      assertEquals(existsSync(siblingFile), true,
        "NEW-1: pre-existing sibling in tests/helpers must NOT be removed by test cleanup");
      try { await Deno.remove(siblingFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
JS semantics give BOTH properties at once: if the try body throws, the finally runs and the exception
propagates, so the post-finally assertion never executes (N2's no-masking preserved); if the try body
succeeds, the assertion runs after ALL cleanup and observes the finally (NEW-1's bite restored).
VALIDATION I RAN on this shape:
  (i)   correction + M-N2b mutant => RED, 11 passed | 1 failed, exit 1, AssertionError
        "NEW-1: pre-existing sibling in tests/helpers must NOT be removed by test cleanup" (at :603 of my corrected
        variant, i.e. immediately after the finally).
        The mutant is KILLED by the intended assertion and message.
  (ii)  correction alone => GREEN, 12 passed | 0 failed, exit 0, and my foreign STAGED file SURVIVED
        byte-identical (sha256 554d98a5... unchanged).
  (iii) correction + MUTANT M-N2c (a simulated DETECTOR regression: the planted depth-2 walker's content
        replaced with a non-scanner body so F1 fails) => the reported error is the DETECTOR one,
        "REAL-TREE: a depth-2 repo-walking helper must be SCANNED and NAMED: []", NOT the sibling one.
        So the correction does not reintroduce canon mode 4 (red by the wrong mechanism).
If the author prefers to keep the assertion inside the try, the alternative is a SECOND canary file that is
not in any removal list, asserted after the finally — but then it must also be added to
AFPL_REAL_TREE_RESIDUE (:35) so a SIGKILL on the failure path is swept by :53.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. FINDING F2 (P1, BLOCKING) — N1 / the NEW-2 pin is VACUOUS. The mutant STILL survives.

The pin added at :711-723 does not exercise the clause it was written to protect.
  :712   const nmTopDir    = join(scratch, "tests", "node_modules");
  :713   const nmNestedDir = join(scratch, "tests", "helpers", "node_modules");
  :718   const enumeratedWithNm = enumerateTestFiles(scratch).map((e) => e.rel);
  :719-723 assertEquals(enumeratedWithNm.some((f) => f.includes("node_modules")), false, ...)
`enumerateTestFiles(testsDir)` treats its argument AS the tests dir (:382 readdirSync(testsDir,
{recursive:true}), :385 rel = `tests/${f}`). So with testsDir = scratch, the two planted files are reported
as `tests/node_modules/zz-nm.test.ts` and `tests/helpers/node_modules/zz-nm-nested.test.ts` — BOTH contain
`/node_modules/` and are excluded by the PRE-EXISTING `!f.includes("/node_modules/")` clause. Neither path
can ever reach `!f.startsWith("node_modules/")` at :384, which is the ONLY clause NEW-2 added. The pin is
one directory level too deep. My round-6 N1 note specified `<scratch>/node_modules/zz-nm.test.ts` and
`<scratch>/helpers/node_modules/zz-nm-nested.test.ts`; the implementation added an extra `tests/` level.

MUTANT M-N1 — delete ` && !f.startsWith("node_modules/")` from :384 (the identical mutant that survived at
c0a3645d):
  => 12 passed | 0 failed, exit 0. **THE MUTANT STILL SURVIVES.** N1 is NOT closed.

DIRECT PROBE (imported the real enumerateTestFiles from the module; scratch tree under
durableDir("scratch"), per the durable-root rule). Four paths planted:
  (A) <scratch>/node_modules/zz-TRUE-top.test.ts              <- the TRUE top-level shape
  (B) <scratch>/tests/node_modules/zz-nm.test.ts              <- what the pin plants as "top-level"
  (C) <scratch>/tests/helpers/node_modules/zz-nm-nested.test.ts <- what the pin plants as "nested"
  (D) <scratch>/zz-sanity.test.ts                             <- must be returned (non-vacuity)
  UNDER MUTANT M-N1:  returned = ["tests/zz-sanity.test.ts","tests/node_modules/zz-TRUE-top.test.ts"]
      (A) TRUE top-level returned? **true**  <- the NEW-2 bug, re-introduced, and NOTHING catches it
      (B) returned? false   (C) returned? false   (D) returned? true
      i.e. the pin's two paths stay excluded via the OLD clause, so :719-723 still passes with the bug live.
  UNDER PRISTINE HEAD: returned = ["tests/zz-sanity.test.ts"]
      (A) returned? **false**  <- the clause IS load-bearing in the product; it is simply unpinned.

EXACT CORRECTION (smallest): root the fixtures at `scratch` itself, not at `scratch/tests`.
  :712   const nmTopDir    = join(scratch, "node_modules");
  :713   const nmNestedDir = join(scratch, "helpers", "node_modules");
Then (A) yields readdir rel `node_modules/zz-nm.test.ts` with NO leading slash, which ONLY
`startsWith("node_modules/")` excludes — my probe above is the acceptance: the pin must go RED under M-N1.
Keep a non-vacuity companion (a file that MUST be returned) so the assertion cannot pass on an empty
enumeration; (D) in my probe serves that role and :635/:640 already cover the nested-test direction.
Optionally assert the two paths separately rather than via `.some(f => f.includes("node_modules"))`, so a
future failure names WHICH shape leaked.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. FINDING F3 (P1, BLOCKING) — the HUB REQUIREMENT guard DOES NOT EXIST.

Requirement as given: a guard that NO test can recursively remove SHARED paths AT ALL (not merely a
corrected path), narrow enough not to trip per-run scratch makeTempDir; it must bite — a recursive
Deno.remove targeting tests/helpers/ must RED.

ABSENT, verified exhaustively (bead p4tf method — rg --hidden --no-ignore PLUS a python os.walk over every
.ts/.mjs/.js in the tree, excluding .git/node_modules/dist/.cache):
  - `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) HEAD --stat` = ONE file
    (tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts). No new guard file, no touched second file.
  - All 12 Deno.test declarations in that file, enumerated by line: :55, :77, :84, :93, :391, :409, :429,
    :443, :470, :493, :511, :607. NONE is a recursive-removal guard.
  - `rg -n --hidden --no-ignore -i "recursively remove|SHARED_PATH|shared path"` over tests/ and scripts/
    => ZERO hits.
  - `rg -n --hidden --no-ignore 'Deno\.test\("' tests/ | rg -i "recursiv|shared (dir|path|tree)|wipe|destroy"`
    => only unrelated hits (redactSecrets "recursively", searchFsGrantFiles "recursively matches names",
    "preserved" assertions). No guard of this class exists anywhere in the repo.
  - The ONLY `{ recursive: true }` REMOVAL in the whole guard file is :731, on the per-run
    `Deno.makeTempDir({ dir: durableDir("scratch"), prefix: "cap-afpl-census-" })` — correct and not the
    shared tree.
So there is nothing to bite: a recursive `Deno.remove` aimed at tests/helpers/ in ANY test file would be
flagged by NO guard. F1 above shows the hazard is live rather than hypothetical — I made a green suite
delete a staged foreign file and remove the shared directory, and the only thing that noticed was my own
out-of-band `git status`.

EXACT CORRECTION (shape, narrow enough not to trip scratch): add a source-inspecting guard (this file is
already the right home — it has the enumerateTestFiles/sharedSupportFiles machinery and is ALWAYS_ON) that
reads each enumerated test file's SOURCE and fails on a recursive removal whose target is a SHARED path.
  - Detect: /Deno\.remove(?:Sync)?\s*\([^)]*\{\s*recursive\s*:\s*true/ AND node:fs /rmSync?\s*\([^)]*recursive/.
  - Constrain the TARGET, not the call: flag only when the removed expression resolves to a repo-shared
    root — a `join(ROOT, ...)` / `${ROOT}...` / `new URL("../"...)`-derived path, or a literal
    tests/helpers|tests/support|tests/utils|scripts|extension path. Do NOT flag a removal of a binding
    assigned from `Deno.makeTempDir(` / `makeTempDir({ dir: durableDir(` — that is the per-run scratch
    exemption, and :731 plus the ~30 existing `Deno.remove(scratch, { recursive: true })` cleanups in
    tests/ (test-partition-guard, tokei-shim-admission, serial-phase-*, store-target-policy, tar-stream,
    bounded-child, scan-shipped, ...) must stay green.
  - Ship it with the mutant that proves it: add `Deno.remove(join(ROOT, "tests", "helpers"),
    { recursive: true })` to any test file and show the guard REDS, then remove it and show green. Also
    ship the negative mutant (a makeTempDir scratch recursive removal) and show it stays GREEN, or the
    guard is untested in the direction that will produce false reds for every other lane.
  - Register any NEW test file in SOURCE_INSPECTING_GUARDS (scripts/select-tests.mjs), or the :391 audit
    will red it for scanning tests/** without being ALWAYS_ON.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. NO-REGRESSION CHECKS — ALL CLEAN (no re-opened findings)

  - NO SIGNATURE SKIP in the classifier or the scanner (the thing my round-6 correction forbade).
    Programmatic body scan of findUnclassifiedSourceScanners (:108-267) and sharedSupportFiles (:268-352)
    for /zz-afpl|AFPL_REAL_TREE_RESIDUE|reconcile|signature/i => NONE in either body. The reconciliation
    lives only at :35-53 and in the two afpl tests.
  - SCRATCH-TREE PROOF INTACT and green in every run: :635 "a repo-walking helper must be SCANNED and
    NAMED — this is the coverage proof, not a skip" and :640 "a depth-2 lowercase-alias repo-walking helper
    must be SCANNED and NAMED". The scratch test deliberately names tests/helpers/zz-afpl-depth2-walk.ts
    inside a scratch root and still passes, so the fix did not buy NEW-3 by teaching the classifier to
    skip its own fixtures.
  - CLASSIFIER + sharedSupportFiles BYTE-IDENTICAL to the rejected-then-cleared c0a3645d: `git diff -U0
    c0a3645d HEAD -- tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts` has exactly 4 hunks (@@ -31, @@ -474,
    @@ -540, @@ -663); a range check over those hunks confirms NO hunk intersects :108-267 or :268-352.
    REPO_ROOT_URL / TOP_LEVEL_URL / KNOWN_SOURCE_ROOTS / the isTest-vs-support-module matchesScanner split
    are untouched.
  - F1 / F2 / F3 UNTOUCHED and green at baseline and after every experiment: F1 (:562 depth-2 walker
    NAMED), F2 (:575 prose helper NOT flagged), the fixture-reader over-match half (:582), F3 (:429 the
    real repo-walking guard flagged when unlisted), plus p1lp symmetry (:443). The delta removes no
    assertion. F1/F2/F3 are NOT re-opened. (My M-N2c mutant deliberately broke F1 and F1 reddened with its
    own message, which additionally confirms F1 still has teeth.)
  - `deno check tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts scripts/select-tests.mjs
    tests/real-browser-teardown.test.ts` => clean, exit 0.
  - FOCUSED GATES on pristine 9d01f01a (no full gate, per instruction):
      source-inspecting-tests-guard + select-tests + select-tests-always-on + select-tests-r3 +
      select-tests-residue + real-browser-teardown  => 37 passed | 0 failed, exit 0
      test-partition-guard + substring-pin-honesty  => 25 passed | 0 failed, exit 0
    NOT run (out of scope): npm test / full serial phase / Chrome journeys.
  - HYGIENE: no browser was launched by any run in this review; `pgrep -f "chromium|chrome"` empty
    afterwards. Every mutant reverted via `git checkout --`; guard file sha256 verified
    cde428c72d2c02d99009b8fc846dbf537e50ccd42c9c78546aacdd1a5771cf6b (byte-identical to HEAD);
    `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` EMPTY; tests/helpers ABSENT; the reviewer-planted
    foreign staged file removed with `git rm --cached` + `rm`. Tree left pristine at 9d01f01a.
  - CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged and still acceptable (round-6 N3): the "pre-existing sibling" is a file the
    test itself plants (:529), so it is a proxy for "cleanup does not wipe the directory" rather than a
    genuinely foreign file. F1's correction is the moment to make it honest — either rename the message or
    (better) plant a canary the cleanup does not own, as my validated correction in section 2 does.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SUMMARY FOR THE AUTHOR — three edits, all in tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts:
  F1 (P1) move the NEW-1 survival assertion to AFTER the try/finally and drop siblingFile from the
          finally's owned list (:589-590, :593). Validated: kills M-N2b, stays green alone, does not mask
          a detector failure.
  F2 (P1) re-root the NEW-2 pin's fixtures at `scratch`, not `scratch/tests` (:712-713). Validated: the
          true top-level shape is returned under M-N1 and excluded at HEAD, so the pin will then bite.
  F3 (P1) add the shared-path recursive-removal guard, with the makeTempDir/durableDir scratch exemption
          and both mutants (positive + negative).
  P2    optionally make :62 plant the real fixture signatures so :55 reproduces the symptom end-to-end.
NEW-3 needs no further work. Do NOT touch the classifier, sharedSupportFiles, or the scratch-tree proof.

ROUND 7 ADDENDUM (reviewer) — THE REVIEW TARGET MOVED MID-REVIEW. My verdict above is against 9d01f01a.
Read this before acting on it.

WHAT HAPPENED (measured, read-only git)
  At the start of this review: fleet/qazo-afpl == origin/fleet/qazo-afpl == HEAD == 9d01f01a.
  At the end of this review:      fleet/qazo-afpl == origin/fleet/qazo-afpl == 755589e3.
  9d01f01a is NO LONGER AN ANCESTOR of the branch tip (git merge-base --is-ancestor 9d01f01a 755589e3 => NO).
  The branch was rewritten and then advanced:
    e5847a2b  17:47:28  same subject+timestamp as my target 9d01f01a -> 9d01f01a rewritten as e5847a2b
    755589e3  18:12:09  "guard(fs): forbid recursive removal of shared repository directories by tests"

DO MY FINDINGS STILL APPLY? Yes for F1 and F2 — proven by hunk-range analysis, not by assumption.
  `git diff -U0 9d01f01a 755589e3 -- tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts` has EXACTLY TWO hunks:
    @@ -519,3 +518,0 @@   deletes the now-redundant in-test `reconcileAfplRealTreeResidue();` call
                          (my round-6 correction explicitly offered this: ":476-479 can be deleted (it
                          becomes redundant)"). BENIGN — the module-scope call at :53 still sweeps before
                          every test, which is what my M-A mutant proved load-bearing. NEW-3 stays CLOSED.
    @@ -733,0 +731,122 @@ appends 122 lines at the END of the file (the new F3 guard).
  NEITHER hunk intersects F1 (:585-601, the sibling assertion + finally) or F2 (:711-723, the NEW-2 pin).
  A programmatic range check over both hunks confirms it. So the code I mutated is byte-identical at
  755589e3 and BOTH MUTANTS STILL SURVIVE THERE, shifted by -3 lines:
    F1 (P1) sibling assertion at ~:586-587, finally at ~:588-598 — M-N2b (recursive wipe in the finally)
            still green, and it still deletes a foreign staged file from tests/helpers while reporting
            12 passed | 0 failed. The validated correction in section 2 applies unchanged.
    F2 (P1) the NEW-2 pin at ~:708-720 — still rooted at `join(scratch, "tests", "node_modules")`
            (:712-713 at 9d01f01a), so M-N1 (deleting `&& !f.startsWith("node_modules/")`) still survives.
            The validated correction in section 3 applies unchanged.
  I did NOT re-run the mutants at 755589e3; the hunk-range proof makes the re-run unnecessary for F1/F2,
  and re-running against a moving target is how a review ends up certifying a tree nobody ships.

F3 (P1, the HUB REQUIREMENT) — APPEARS ADDRESSED at 755589e3, BUT **UNVERIFIED BY ME**. NOT WITHDRAWN.
  755589e3 appends `findRecursiveRemovalsOfSharedPaths()` plus two Deno.test blocks: the guard
  ("afpl: no test in tests/ recursively removes shared repository directories (e.g. tests/helpers)") and a
  falsification drill with 4 bad samples and 3 scratch/temp negatives. That is the right SHAPE and it is
  the item my section 4 found absent at 9d01f01a. What I have NOT done, because it was not my assigned
  target and needs its own pass:
    1. Prove it BITES on the real tree (the parent's stated acceptance: "a recursive Deno.remove targeting
       tests/helpers/ must RED"). The 4 bad samples are SYNTHETIC strings fed straight to the function —
       that proves the parser, not the detector against tests/** as it actually ships. Canon: this is the
       F3-shaped gap the file itself already documents for the repo-walk detector ("a real file proves the
       DETECTOR against the tree we actually ship"). A real-tree drill is owed.
    2. Sweep the false-positive direction across the whole suite. `SCRATCH_OR_TEMP_PATTERN` includes the
       bare tokens `parent`, `profile`, `victim`, `outDir`, `downloads`, `STAGE`, and
       `SHARED_PATH_PATTERN` matches bare `tests` and bare `scripts` — so a variable named e.g. `parent`
       or `profile` exempts a removal, and a removal of anything whose text contains "tests"/"scripts"
       is flagged. Whether that over-/under-matches the ~480 existing test files is UNMEASURED. Note
       `tests/worktree-audit.test.ts:27` does `Deno.remove(`${parent}/${entry.name}`, { recursive: true })`
       — it survives only because `parent` happens to be in the exemption list, which is an exemption by
       VARIABLE NAME, not by ownership. That is fragile in exactly the way p1lp's canon warns about
       ("The identifier's SHAPE carries no information; its DEFINITION does").
    3. Check the template-literal stripper (`code.replace(/`[\s\S]*?`/g, m => m.includes(";") ? '""' : m)`)
       for the failure mode the repo already retired once — round 3 removed a "corrupting stripComments"
       for this reason (commit 8454ffa4). A non-greedy backtick pair spanning two unrelated literals can
       blank real code.
    4. Confirm `npm test` is green with the guard added (it inspects every test file, so it can red the
       whole suite on a pre-existing pattern in another lane's file) and that no new file needs
       SOURCE_INSPECTING_GUARDS registration.

byte-identically; F3 has a candidate that needs the four verifications above. Recommend the parent
re-dispatch a fresh delta review with TARGET 755589e3 (not 9d01f01a, which is no longer on the branch) —
and pin the target for the duration, since this branch has now been rewritten twice under review
(c0a3645d -> 937fc50b rebase, then 9d01f01a -> e5847a2b rewrite), which is how findings get lost.

DELTA RE-REVIEW — fleet/review-afpl4 @ 078af6d0 (parent 755589e3)
Reviewer: independent (fresh session, different model). Read-only + mutants, all restored.
Focused gate only: `npm run test:file -- tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts`. No full gate, no browser launched.
Worktree verified pristine at end (`git diff --exit-code 078af6d0` clean, no untracked files, `tests/helpers/` absent, no stray chrome).

VERDICT: REJECT — the three carried P1s are all genuinely CLOSED with independent mutant evidence, but this same delta introduces two new P1s. One of them silently blinds the very guard F3 asked me to verify, and it is the retired "corrupting stripComments" class (8454ffa4) returning in a new shape while the delta's own comment claims that class is closed.

============================================================
PART 1 — THE THREE CARRIED P1s: ALL CLOSED
============================================================

Baseline: 15 passed / 0 failed. `deno check --config deno.runner.jsonc tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts` clean.
No test deleted or skipped: Deno.test count at merge-base 51feb4a9 = 8, at HEAD = 15; a name-set diff is purely additive (7 new, 0 removed). `rg -n 'Deno\.test\.(skip|ignore|only)|\{\s*(skip|ignore|only)\s*:'` on the file: no matches. Branch footprint is one file (666+/16-).

--- F1 CLOSED (survival assertion could not observe cleanup) ---
Fix as claimed and verified: assertions moved AFTER the try/finally (:600-609); `siblingFile` removed from the finally's owned list (:590).

MUTANT M-F1 (independently reproduced). Inserted as the finally's FIRST statement at :589:
    try { await Deno.remove(realHelpersDir, { recursive: true }); } catch { /* ignore */ }
Result: 13 passed / 2 FAILED. The mutant DIES on the sibling message, at :601:
    error: AssertionError: NEW-1: pre-existing sibling in tests/helpers must survive cleanup byte-identically
It is independently killed a second time by the F3 guard at :870:
    Deno.remove(realHelpersDir, { recursive: true }) denotes shared path: "realHelpersDir join(ROOT, "tests", "helpers")"
  (note: that kill resolves the NAME `realHelpersDir` through its DECLARATION — direct evidence the exemption is definition-based, since `realHelpersDir` was deliberately removed from SHARED_PATH_PATTERN in this delta).
The mutant is genuinely destructive: it deleted the whole `tests/helpers/` directory including a planted STAGED foreign file (git status went `A ` -> `AD`).

STAGED FOREIGN FILE SURVIVAL (corrected code). Planted `tests/helpers/zz-foreign-staged-lane.ts` (134 bytes), `git add`ed, sha256 314abeeb72e903c9d18b0d21b1d273f69edf7e3a64e41e2073e0744e600d8cb7.
  - corrected code: 15 passed / 0 failed, `sha256sum -c` -> OK, byte-identical; 0 afpl fixture residue; `tests/helpers/` itself preserved (helpersDirPreexisted=true path).
  - under M-F1: file destroyed. So the pin discriminates exactly the property it claims.

NO MASKING (detector regression). Flipped the F1 expectation at :564 (`named.includes(...depth2-walk.ts)` true -> false). Result: 14 passed / 1 FAILED, and the ONLY error is the detector's:
    AssertionError: Values are not equal: REAL-TREE: a depth-2 repo-walking helper must be SCANNED and NAMED: ["tests/helpers/zz-afpl-depth2-walk.ts"]
The sibling message does NOT appear — the post-try assertion cannot mask a detector red, because the exception propagates past it. Verified.
Corollary observed: on a detector red the sibling leaks (`tests/helpers/zz-afpl-preexisting-sibling.ts` left on disk), and the NEXT run's module-scope `reconcileAfplRealTreeResidue()` sweeps it — confirmed empirically (leaked after the red run, gone after the following green run). Bounded and self-healing; see P2-c.

--- F2 CLOSED (NEW-2 pin was vacuous) ---
Fix as claimed: fixtures re-rooted to `join(scratch,"node_modules")` and `join(scratch,"helpers","node_modules")` (:720-721) + a must-be-returned companion (:727-730).

MUTANT M-F2. Deleted the `&& !f.startsWith("node_modules/")` clause from enumerateTestFiles (:390; that clause was added earlier in 20b572d8, so it is the clause the re-rooted fixture now actually exercises). Result: FAILED with
    enumerateTestFiles must exclude top-level and nested node_modules: ["tests/helpers/zz-nested.test.ts","tests/node_modules/zz-nm.test.ts"]
The enumerated rel is now `tests/node_modules/zz-nm.test.ts` (from readdirSync rel `node_modules/zz-nm.test.ts`), which ONLY the startsWith clause excludes — the pre-existing `includes("/node_modules/")` cannot match it. The pin is non-vacuous.

DIRECT PROBE against the corrected `enumerateTestFiles` (imported from the real module, run under a durable scratch root):
    <scratch>/node_modules/zz-top.test.ts              -> NOT returned
    <scratch>/helpers/node_modules/zz-nested-nm.test.ts -> NOT returned
    <scratch>/helpers/zz-real.test.ts                   -> returned
    ENUMERATED: ["tests/helpers/zz-real.test.ts"]
So `<scratch>/node_modules/zz-top.test.ts` is NOT returned, as required.

COMPANION ANTI-VACUITY. Mutated `IS_TEST_RE.test(f)` -> `!IS_TEST_RE.test(f)` (enumerate nothing): 12 passed / 3 FAILED, including the test carrying the companion (:615). The companion cannot be satisfied by an empty enumeration.

--- F3 CLOSED (shared-path guard: bites, definition-based, no false positives) ---
GUARD BITES on a real recursive remove of tests/helpers/. Planted a live, never-executed
    const victim = join(ROOT, "tests", "helpers"); await Deno.remove(victim, { recursive: true });
into a fresh `tests/zz-afpl-reviewer-control.test.ts`, then ran ONLY the guard file (the plant never executes):
    FAILED — tests/zz-afpl-reviewer-control.test.ts: Deno.remove(victim, { recursive: true }) denotes shared path: "victim join(ROOT, "tests", "helpers") join(Deno.cwd())"
The alias `victim` is resolved through its declaration. Control removed afterwards.

NOT VACUOUS: the guard scans 603 test files; raw removal-call sites 219, visible after masking 204; `recursive: true` occurrences in the masked corpus 230; violations 0 — and the control above proves the same corpus REDs when a real violation is present.

DOES NOT TRIP per-run scratch makeTempDirs: 0 violations across the whole tree, which includes this file's own live `await Deno.remove(scratch, { recursive: true })` (:743) where `scratch = await Deno.makeTempDir({ dir: durableDir("scratch"), prefix: "cap-afpl-census-" })`. Drills zz-good1/2/3 + zz-good-alias pass. Note zz-good2 was tightened in this delta from `join(durableDir("test"),"dir")` to `await Deno.makeTempDir({dir:durableDir("test")})` — a real narrowing, not a loosening.

GENUINELY DEFINITION-BASED, NOT NAME-BASED. MUTANT M-F3-NAME: re-introduced the retired SCRATCH_OR_TEMP_PATTERN as a bare-target-name exemption (`if (/\b(?:makeTempDir|...|scratch|...|profile|...|parent|victim|extractDir)\b/.test(target)) continue;`) after `resolve(target)`. Result: 13 passed / 2 FAILED, killed by two independent assertions:
    AssertionError: a shared path must be flagged regardless of the alias name in tests/zz-bad-alias.test.ts
    AssertionError: live removal must be caught; fixture-body call must be ignored
So a name-based exemption is now mechanically forbidden. The opposite direction is pinned by zz-good-alias (`const realHelpersDir = await Deno.makeTempDir()` -> NOT flagged), and by the M-F1 kill above where the same name `realHelpersDir` IS flagged when its declaration is `join(ROOT,"tests","helpers")`. Same name, opposite verdicts, decided by definition. This satisfies the p1lp canon (shape vs definition).

EXEMPTION IS NARROW — targeted probe against the extracted detector (8/9 as expected):
    const d = join(durableDir("cap"), "tests", "helpers"); Deno.remove(d,{recursive:true})            -> FLAGGED (durableDir alone does NOT make a path per-run)
    join(ROOT,"tests","helpers",Deno.makeTempDirSync())                                              -> FLAGGED (a nested temp leaf does not launder a shared root)
    Deno.remove("tests/helpers",{recursive:true})                                                    -> FLAGGED
    join(ROOT,"scripts")                                                                             -> FLAGGED
    await Deno.makeTempDir() then join(d,"tests","helpers")                                          -> admitted (correct: under a temp root)
    non-recursive Deno.remove(join(ROOT,"tests","helpers"))                                          -> admitted (correct: args.length<2)
    makeTempDir({dir:durableDir("scratch")}) then recursive remove                                   -> admitted (correct)

CLASSIFIER UNTOUCHED. `git diff 755589e3 078af6d0` filtered for findUnclassifiedSourceScanners / sharedSupportFiles / formatUnclassifiedScannersMessage / SCAN_DIRS / GUARD_ROOTS / SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS / realpathSync yields exactly one hit, and it is inside a fixture BODY STRING (fixtureBodies[1]), not a change to the classifier. Earlier-round F1/F2/F3 assertions are all still present and passing at HEAD (:566 depth-2 walk NAMED, :579 prose-only NOT flagged, :586 fixture-walker NOT admitted, :643/:648/:668/:683 scratch-tree counterparts, :72 residue reconciled).

--- P2 (:55 writes ACTUAL fixture bodies) ADDRESSED ---
`"// residue\n"` replaced by four real bodies (:61-67). They are classifier-relevant, not filler: [0] is a depth-2 `new URL("../../", import.meta.url)` repo walk (would be NAMED if reconciliation failed), [1] is prose mentioning SCAN_DIRS/git ls-files (must NOT be flagged), [2] walks only `join(ROOT,"tests","fixtures")`, [3] is byte-identical to the NEW-1 `siblingBody` at :532. So a reconciliation failure now double-fails (the direct assert at :72 plus the audit). Verified the four bodies align 1:1 with AFPL_REAL_TREE_RESIDUE.

============================================================
PART 2 — NEW FINDINGS INTRODUCED BY 078af6d0
============================================================

FINDING N1 — P1 — `maskGuardFixtureBodies` is not regex-literal aware; it corrupts real test files and silently blinds the F3 guard to them.
Location: tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts:749-779 (the new function), consumed at :864 (`code: maskGuardFixtureBodies(f.code)`).
The function is a single-pass tokenizer over comments and string literals, but it has NO regex-literal state. A `/` that ends a regex, or a quote inside a regex character class, desynchronizes it; from that point backtick/quote pairing is inverted and live code is masked to spaces.

Evidence, repo-wide differential probe over all 603 enumerated test files (raw removal-call sites vs masked):
    removal-call sites raw=219 masked=204  dropped=15 added=0 newlineMismatch=0
13 of the 15 drops are legitimate `code:` fixture bodies. TWO ARE LIVE CODE, in tests/evidence-durable.test.ts:
    DROP evidence-durable.test.ts:97  :: Deno.removeSync(required);
    DROP evidence-durable.test.ts:107 :: Deno.removeSync(tmp, { recursive: true });
Trigger: tests/evidence-durable.test.ts:64 — `text.matchAll(/\/tmp\/[^\s"')]*|\/home\/[^\s"')]+/g)` — the character class contains `"` and `'`. Line :57 (`/\/tmp\/|\/home\//`) additionally ends in a literal `//`, which the scanner reads as a line comment.
Measured blast radius: backtick parity raw=8 -> masked=2; masked output is blank from line 65 to EOF (110). 35 live-looking lines fully erased, including BOTH live removal calls and the whole second `Deno.test`.
Second victim: tests/package-scripts-exist.test.ts (trigger :27, `cmd.matchAll(/(?:^|[\s&|;(])((?:\.\/)?scripts\/[^\s&|;)"']+)/g)` — same `"`/`'`-in-character-class shape, plus `.replace(/^\.\//, "")` at :28). 35 live-looking lines erased from :51 to EOF.
Census: 2 of 603 files corrupted, ~46 and ~60 lines of live code respectively rendered invisible to the guard.

REGRESSION ATTRIBUTION (diff-caused, not pre-existing). Ran the PARENT's masking (`code.replace(/`[\s\S]*?`/g, m => m.includes(";") ? '""' : m)`, i.e. 755589e3) over the same file:
    OLD(parent)    : line97="Deno.removeSync(required);"  line107="Deno.removeSync(tmp, { recursive: true });"  Deno.remove* count=2  backticks=8
    NEW(078af6d0)  : line97=""                            line107=""                                            Deno.remove* count=0  backticks=2
The parent preserved both live calls; this delta erased them.

DECISIVE FALSIFICATION — the blindness hides a REAL violation, not just a parse difference. Appended to tests/evidence-durable.test.ts (after the line-64 trigger), as a never-called function so it cannot execute:
    async function afplReviewerBlindSpotProbe() {
      const victim = join(ROOT, "tests", "helpers");
      await Deno.remove(victim, { recursive: true });
    }
  -> guard test GREEN, 15 passed / 0 failed. A live recursive removal of tests/helpers in tests/ is invisible.
Identical code in a fresh file with no regex literal (`tests/zz-afpl-reviewer-control.test.ts`) -> guard RED, naming the file and the resolved shared path (quoted in Part 1). Both probes removed; worktree restored and verified.
So the detector logic is sound and the masking is the sole cause of the miss.

Why P1 and not P2: today's verdict happens to be unchanged (neither corrupted half contains a shared-path removal, so 0 violations either way), but the guard's coverage claim — "no test in tests/ recursively removes shared repository directories" — is now FALSE for two real test files, it fails OPEN, and it is silent. That is the exact defect class 8454ffa4 retired, and the delta's own comment at :862-863 asserts it is closed ("A backtick in a comment must not consume subsequent live calls (the old stripComments failure)"). It closes the backtick-in-a-comment variant and is defeated by a `//` or a quote inside a REGEX literal, which corrupts parity by the same mechanism. Any future shared-path removal added to the second half of either file ships unguarded.

SMALLEST FIX (preferred — eliminates the class rather than patching one shape): stop rewriting the source. Compute the byte ranges of `code:` fixture literals and have `findRecursiveRemovalsOfSharedPaths` SKIP a match whose `m.index` falls inside one, passing the ORIGINAL code through untouched. Nothing is ever masked, so no tokenizer desync can hide a live call; the `code:`-fixture exemption is preserved exactly.
ALTERNATIVE (keeps the current shape): add a regex-literal state to the scanner at :762 — when a `/` appears where a regex can start (previous significant char in `(,=:[!&|?{};+-*%~^` or absent, or after return/typeof/case/in/of/new/delete/void/do/else/yield/await/match/matchAll/replace/test), consume to the unescaped closing `/` honouring `[...]` classes, then the flags, and emit the literal verbatim.
REQUIRED ACCEPTANCE FOR EITHER FIX (the drill that would have caught this):
  1. A fixture file whose source contains a regex literal with BOTH a `//` tail and a quote inside a character class, placed BEFORE a live `Deno.remove(join(ROOT,"tests","helpers"),{recursive:true})`; assert the guard still flags it.
  2. The repo-wide differential as a permanent test: for every file in tests/, the removal-call sites in the processed corpus must equal the raw sites minus those inside `code:` literals (my probe is at ~/cap-evidence/afpl-review/mask-probe.ts and corruption-census.ts, ready to lift). Today it reports dropped=15 with 2 illegitimate; it must report 0 illegitimate.

FINDING N2 — P1 — the `!helpersDirPreexisted` cleanup branch is dead by construction; every green run leaves an empty `tests/helpers/` behind.
Location: tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts:593-598 (the finally's rmdir) vs :532-533 (sibling written) and :600-609 (sibling removed only AFTER the finally).
Mechanism: the test writes `siblingFile` into `realHelpersDir` at :533. The finally at :590-592 removes only `testFiles`, so `siblingFile` is still inside when :596 runs `await Deno.remove(realHelpersDir)` — a NON-recursive rmdir, which fails ENOTEMPTY and is swallowed by `catch { /* ignore */ }` at :597. `siblingFile` is removed afterwards at :609, leaving an empty directory that nothing removes.
Measured, from a tree where tests/helpers did NOT exist: removed tests/helpers, ran the file -> 15 passed / 0 failed -> `tests/helpers` exists again with 0 entries. Reproduced a second time on the final confirmation run (LEFTOVER). Because the directory then pre-exists, `helpersDirPreexisted` is true on every subsequent run, so it is never cleaned at all — it becomes permanent worktree residue.
REGRESSION ATTRIBUTION: same experiment against the PARENT (loaded 755589e3's version of the file, tests/helpers removed first): 14 passed / 0 failed, and afterwards `tests/helpers` does NOT exist — the parent cleaned it up, because `siblingFile` was in the finally's owned list and the rmdir could succeed. This delta broke it. Restored HEAD afterwards and re-verified by sha256.
Impact: git-invisible (git does not track empty dirs, so `git status` stays clean), no guard false-reds today. But it is a residue leak in a bead whose entire subject is SIGKILL/residue hygiene, it silently defeats the "preserve existing helpers dir" logic 20b572d8 added, and it makes a whole cleanup branch unreachable — a silent degradation, which this repo's canon treats as the defect, not the cosmetic outcome.
SMALLEST FIX (keeps F1's property — the survival assertion must still observe the cleanup): wrap the post-finally block so the sibling removal and the deferred rmdir are themselves finally-protected:
    try {
      assert(existsSync(siblingFile), "NEW-1: ... byte-identically");
      assertEquals(await Deno.readTextFile(siblingFile), siblingBody, "NEW-1: ... byte-identically");
    } finally {
      await Deno.remove(siblingFile).catch(() => {});
      if (!helpersDirPreexisted) await Deno.remove(realHelpersDir).catch(() => {});
    }
  and delete the now-unreachable rmdir at :593-598. Reasoned against all three paths: green -> sibling then empty dir removed, no residue; M-F1 mutant -> `assert(existsSync(siblingFile))` still REDs with the sibling message (the inner finally only runs after it); detector red -> outer exception still propagates unmaked. Re-run M-F1 and the detector-regression mutant after applying, plus the clean-tree experiment above (tests/helpers must NOT exist after a green run).

FINDING N3 — P2 (report only) — the definition resolver follows DECLARATIONS only, so a re-binding evades it.
Location: :828-838, `new RegExp("\\b(?:const|let|var)\\s+${id}\\s*=\\s*([^;]+);", "g")` over `code.slice(0, m.index)`, `.at(-1)`.
Probe: `let x = await Deno.makeTempDir();\nx = join(ROOT, "tests", "helpers");\nawait Deno.remove(x, { recursive: true });` -> NOT flagged (the last `let` declaration is still the makeTempDir, so isolatedRoot=true). 1 of 9 narrowness probes mismatched, this one.
Not a regression (the parent's single `defMatch` had the same limit, and was name-based on top of it), and no test in the tree does this. Smallest fix if wanted: also match bare assignments `(?:^|[;{}\n])\s*${id}\s*=\s*([^;]+);` in the same slice and take the last of either form.

FINDING N4 — P2 (report only) — the :61-67 fixture bodies are a second literal copy of the REAL-TREE fixtures and can drift.
fixtureBodies[0] omits the leading `// Real depth-2 helper walking repo root via ../../` comment that :538-542 writes; [1] is entirely different prose from :546-550; [2] uses `return Deno.readDirSync(...)` where :554-557 uses a `for` loop; only [3] is byte-identical to :532. Nothing couples the two sets, and `fixtureBodies[index]` is not length-checked against AFPL_REAL_TREE_RESIDUE (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is not set in deno.runner.jsonc, so `deno check` will not catch a 5th residue path — it would throw an opaque runtime error instead). Smallest fix: export one `AFPL_FIXTURE_BODIES: Record<string,string>` keyed by the residue rel path, have both the :55 test and the NEW-1 test read from it, and assert `Object.keys(AFPL_FIXTURE_BODIES).sort()` equals `AFPL_REAL_TREE_RESIDUE.slice().sort()`.

FINDING N5 — P2 (report only) — on a detector red the sibling leaks into the tracked tree until this module next evaluates.
Observed: after the detector-regression mutant run, `tests/helpers/` held `zz-afpl-preexisting-sibling.ts` alongside the foreign file. It IS swept by the module-scope `reconcileAfplRealTreeResidue()` (:54) on the next run — verified — and the content is prose-only so no concurrent scanner flags it. Bounded and self-healing, so report-only; N2's fix does not change it. If you want it airtight, add the created-directory case to reconciliation, or plant the sibling under a per-run scratch helpers dir and only use the real tree for the detector half.

============================================================
PART 3 — HYGIENE / REPRO
============================================================
Every mutant was restored from a sha256-pinned pristine copy (b9e600a30c2cc63dba2bb056f57fbf4a037b01c94add7ddf447080db8c24d524) and re-verified after each run; `git diff --exit-code 078af6d0` is clean and `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` is empty. My planted foreign file was staged and then unstaged+removed; the leftover `tests/helpers/` was rmdir'd. No browser was launched by any command in this review (all runs were the in-memory guard file), and `pgrep -f chrome|chromium` is empty. No other fleet/* branch or main was touched; work was done in the reviewer worktree only.
Probe scripts and the pristine copies are kept durably at ~/cap-evidence/afpl-review/ (guard-extract.ts, mask-probe.ts, corruption-census.ts, locate-corrupt.ts, first-div.ts, old-vs-new-mask.ts, narrow-probe.ts, enumerate-probe.test.ts, show-masked.ts, extent.ts, pristine-guard.test.ts, evidence-durable.pristine.ts, foreign.sha256, pristine.sha256).
Absence checks used `rg`/`grep -rn` over the working tree, per p4tf.

BOTTOM LINE: F1, F2, F3 and the P2 are all genuinely closed — the mutant kills are real, the messages are the right ones, there is no masking, and the definition-based exemption is pinned in both directions. Do not lose that work. But N1 makes the F3 guard silently blind to two real test files (proven by planting a live violation the guard could not see), and N2 leaks residue in a residue-hygiene bead and makes a cleanup branch unreachable. Both are new in 078af6d0 and both are fixable in a few lines. Fix N1 + N2 with the drills above and this should pass.

title: [tooling] the mcp-zod-peer-parity pin measures a NON-SHIPPED graph while its name reads as the shipped figure, and cannot build in a fresh worktree (no diff-core redirect, needs a pre-built extension/dist)
description: Found by j5yz while measuring chrome-agent-platform-qptq on the landed tree (2026-10-06), using the REAL build's .build/bundle-report.json as the reference. TWO DEFECTS IN THE SAME INSTRUMENT. (1) MEASUREMENT HONESTY: the pin builds the service worker with plugins:[browserDependencies] only, omitting build.mjs's capAiSdkDedup, so it measures a graph the product does not ship. The consequence is concrete and was nearly recorded as a product fact: the pin's configuration yields TWO peer-context copies of the zod-to-json-schema converter and 354 bytes across 6 files, while the REAL plugin set dedups the SDK to one canonical instance (174,037 bytes, no _1) and ships exactly ONE copy — 177 bytes across 3 files. qptq's 'two copies may be a dedup candidate' reframe was therefore FALSE for the shipped bundle and true only of the pin's graph, and it had to be corrected on the 3337 landing note after the fact. A pin whose NAME reads as the shipped figure must not measure a non-shipped graph: either build it with the real plugin set, or rename it so its scope is unmistakable and state the delta in its own comment. (2) WORKTREE FRAGILITY: the pin requires a pre-built extension/dist to build at all (there is no diff-core redirect), so it fails in a fresh worktree — a test that cannot run in a clean checkout will either be skipped by the next lane or, worse, be reported as a product failure. ACCEPTANCE: (i) the pin either uses the real plugin set (and its numbers then match the shipped bundle, provable against .build/bundle-report.json) or carries a name and a comment that state plainly that it measures a pin-local graph and why; (ii) it builds in a fresh worktree without a pre-existing extension/dist, or says explicitly and loudly that dist must be pre-built; (iii) prove (i) with a falsification: change the plugin set so the converter graph changes, and show the pin's own numbers move — a pin whose number cannot move is measuring nothing. NOTE: this is the same family as the night's other attribution defects (a count without a name; a verdict that cannot say which file failed), so it is filed rather than folded into qptq, which is a product question about 177 bytes.

title: [security] the wfxe postMessage recurrence guard fingerprints only the first 60 normalized characters, so a payload can grow a secret or an action past the prefix and still pass
description: Source: software-factory nightly project-audit 2026-10-06 (vuln-triage finding 6 of 25, medium). deadline (tests/fixtures/security-suite-fake-runner.mjs:114), while the supervisor's first sample + ACK takes

("escape-unconfirmed") before the supervisor could observe the escape, and the red then read as a custody
failure. Case B reds the ACK-consumed assertion, case A reds `code === 70` (97 won, and the residue override at
supervisor.mjs:386 masks which happened). The quiet-window/exit-75 route was evaluated and REJECTED with
evidence: nothing routes exit 75 as non-red for a test file, it applies to Chrome-launching gate scripts only,
and at 4-5x the 0.35/core threshold it would replace an 8-14% random red with a near-permanent refusal.

THE FIX: DECLARE the window instead of racing it.
 - fixture: CAP_SECURITY_TEST_ACK_DEADLINE_MS, defaulting to the old 1500 ms, bounded 1..60000 with a loud
   named refusal for an invalid value, and the DECLARED value + the escape child's pid recorded in the state
   file, so a test can assert the process honoured the number it was given.
 - test: the two escape cases DECLARE their numbers (budget 10 s, ack deadline 12 s, freeze 400 ms) and assert
   the CONTRACT as numbers - freeze < budget < ack deadline, with the budget ~3.6x above the worst measured ACK
   latency - plus the recorded declaration. They no longer race a literal only the fixture knew.
 - scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs: the TEST-ONLY self-test budget ceiling 5 s -> 20 s so that declaration is
   possible; the lower bound and the refusal of an absurd value are unchanged.
 - NEW deterministic backstop test: run the fixture DIRECTLY (no supervisor, so the ACK can never list the
   child) with a 1 ms declared window and require the loud refusal BY NAME. This is what keeps the refusal path
   pinned now that it no longer fires in the positive cases.
 - COUPLED RE-PIN, both places, as the coupling inventory demands: EXPECTED_FIXTURE_HASH (supervisor.mjs) and
   HASH_PINS (tests/file-url-root-guard.test.ts) both move to the fixture's new sha256.

FALSIFICATION, four drills, each requiring a NAMED assertion to go RED (all reverted, tree clean):
 1. supervisor never ACKs (ackSample no-op) -> case B REDS: "the supervisor's ACK must be consumed for this
    run's child (state events: [...])". VALID KILL, and it is now DETERMINISTIC where before it red ~8%.
 2. residue no longer forces exit 70 -> case A REDS on its code-70 assertion. VALID KILL.
 3. the fixture records a window it was NOT given -> REDS "the fixture must record the DECLARED window it was
    given". FIRST ATTEMPT WAS INCONCLUSIVE, and the reason is worth recording: editing the fixture changes its
    bytes, so the supervisor refused the runner on the HASH PIN and the run died with "supervisor emitted no
    result marker" - a mutant killed by an artifact check is inconclusive, not a kill (the house rule). Re-run
    WITH the pin re-added in the same patch: VALID KILL on the named assertion.
 4. the deadline branch deleted -> the new backstop test REDS "a window the ACK can never meet must produce the
    fixture's loud refusal". VALID KILL.
EVIDENCE: 12/12 runs of the whole file green at loadavg 2.3 (logs /tmp/j5yz-2zqd-r1..12.log); the ALWAYS-ON
reproduction (the bead's own measurement was 209 passed / 2 failed at loadavg 9.47) is running now through a
gate, and I will report the custody count under the load it actually saw.

NAMED RESIDUALS, not hidden:
 - supervisor.mjs:156 `attestDeadline = Date.now() + 2_000` is a SECOND hard-coded, non-injectable clock on the
   same path (the scout measured that most of the 2800 ms ACK latency was pre-freeze startup/attestation), so
   under heavier load it can fire first and produce a DIFFERENT red of the same family (exit 2, "PGID/SID
   attestation failed: child did not settle"). If the always-on run shows it, it is fixed in this change;

title: chrome-test-contract's launch-scanner regex has two structural blind spots: nested parens truncate the arg block, and a stray backtick can swallow a real call
description:
Found by the antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash review of chrome-agent-platform-qepn (PASS with notes, 2026-10-06).
  1. The predicate /launchChrome\s*\(\s*\{([^)]*)\}\s*\)/gs cannot tolerate a nested ')' inside the argument object: launchChrome({ profile: getDir("x"), args: [] }) does not match at all, so a REAL launch written that way is invisible to the guard (false negative). Pre-existing, not introduced by qepn; qepn's stripStrings made it more likely to matter because string args no longer supply stray parens. Fix: extract the balanced brace block (e.g. \{((?:[^{}]|\{[^{}]*\})*)\}) or parse with an AST.
  2. stripStrings' template-literal pattern /`(?:\\[\s\S]|[^\\`])*`/g spans newlines. A stray/unpaired backtick (e.g. a regex literal like /[`]/) would consume everything up to the next backtick, hiding any real call in between. No such literal exists in tests/ today; fix by handling regex literals before string stripping or requiring same-line pairing.
  ACCEPTANCE: a real launchChrome({ profile: getDir("x"), args: [] }) in any tests/ file reds the guard; a stray backtick line cannot hide a following real call.

title: [tooling] move build-behaviour test coverage out of every lane's npm test into a dedicated explicitly-budgeted gate
description:
Option D from the chrome-agent-platform-kj9s analysis (j5yz, 2026-10-06), filed as a follow-up decision rather than folded into kj9s. THE QUESTION: npm test currently pays for the build-behaviour coverage (13 production builds across four serial files) on EVERY lane's run, which is why the serial phase's red count varies with load and every landing gate is unreliable. comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
**p1lp — progress: detector widened with SYMMETRY (definition-based source roots), escapes adjudicated, real-tree falsification added.** Branch `fleet/qazo-p1lp`, tip `90644b05`, base `c06d6e00`.

**WHY A NAME LIST WAS NOT ENOUGH.** The kz27 pattern `/walk\(\s*[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*\b/` failed in both directions, and a wider name list cannot fix either:
- UNDER-MATCH: it demanded an uppercase identifier, so `tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts`'s `await walk(root)` — where `const root = new URL("../extension/", import.meta.url)` — escaped the audit entirely. That is the original failure mode in a different spelling.
- OVER-MATCH: it matched ANY uppercase identifier, which is how a 23s esbuild-spawning file entered the always-on set and tripled every subset gate (chrome-agent-platform-fgik).
- The reason a list cannot work: `walk(root)` is also how tests traverse a **DOM tree** (`tests/agent-permissions-panel.test.ts` passes an Element). The identifier's SHAPE carries no information; its DEFINITION does.

**THE RULE.** A walk/read counts as a scanner only when the thing being walked is a repo source root, established two ways: (1) a KNOWN source-root constant (`ROOT|EXT|EXTENSION_DIR|TESTS|TESTS_DIR|SCRIPTS|SCRIPTS_DIR|ROOT_DIR|GUARD_ROOTS`), or (2) an identifier **this file** defines from a source-root path (`new URL("..")`/`new URL("../extension/")`, a quoted `extension|scripts|tests|lib|packages/` segment, or an RHS mentioning `ROOT`). The literal kz27 patterns for ROOT-rooted template reads are kept, so nothing regressed. Deliberately NOT a bare word match: `const root = document.querySelector("#tests")` must not look like a source root.

**BOTH NAMED ESCAPES ADJUDICATED, in writing.**
- `tests/chrome-test-contract.test.ts` and `tests/code-health.test.ts` were ALREADY promoted into `SOURCE_INSPECTING_GUARDS` by the F3 delta review; I verified that rather than assuming it, and the widening does not disturb them.
- The widening's NEW catches, all adjudicated IN because each asserts a cross-cutting invariant over tracked source with NO spawn and no browser (host-independent and cheap — the qepn/3bv7/j3o1 lesson): **`tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts`** (the bead's named lowercase-alias case: `const root = new URL("../extension/", import.meta.url)` then `await walk(root)`), **`tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts`** (`const TESTS = \`${ROOT}tests/\``, walks the test sources), and **`tests/chrome-lock-fixture-scope.test.ts`** (`const TESTS_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL("./", import.meta.url))`, walks the test directory).

**MY OWN OVER-MATCH, CAUGHT BY A PRE-GATE PROBE RATHER THAN BY THE GATE.** Before running anything I mirrored the new rule over the real `tests/` tree with a dependency-free script, because every file the audit newly flags fails it closed and I did not want to spend a gate cycle discovering them. The first version flagged **five** files, and inspection showed two were not the audit's shape at all: `tests/tool-descriptions.test.ts` walks `extension/wasm/cas/` and `tests/tool-platform-foundation.test.ts` walks `extension/wasm/manifests` — **sub-roots**, i.e. data/fixture reads, exactly the over-match class that put a 23s file into the always-on set. So the rule now requires a walk rooted at the repo tree or a **TOP-LEVEL** source dir, with the dir name ending the path segment: `new URL("../extension/", …)` matches, `new URL("../extension/wasm/cas/", …)` does not, and a computed path (`${ROOT}${root}`) does not. Result: 3 new adjudications, no sub-root false positives, and the audit's unclassified list is empty. Two bugs in my own boundary handling were caught the same way (the first refused `../extension/` because the delimiter preceding the dir name is `/`).

**REAL-TREE FALSIFICATION, both directions, against files this repo ships** (the synthetic fixtures prove the parser; these prove the classifier): `tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts` unlisted -> must be flagged (the lowercase-alias MET case that used to escape), and `tests/agent-permissions-panel.test.ts` -> must NOT be flagged (the MISSED case — its `walk(root)` walks a DOM node, and admitting it is the over-match that cost 23s a gate).

**RESIDUAL DETECTION LIMITS, stated rather than implied away.** This detector is textual and single-file, and these are the shapes it still cannot see:
1. A **ROOT-rooted read of a non-source path** still matches — `Deno.readDir(`${ROOT}node_modules/@esbuild`)` in `tests/quiet-window.test.ts` — so that exclusion **remains necessary** and is not an oversight. Distinguishing "reads node_modules" from "walks tracked source" needs the target path, which no pattern here has. I replaced the stale "NOTE FOR p1lp" in its reason with that finding.
2. An identifier imported from **another module** (`import { EXTENSION_DIR } from ...`) is not linked back to its definition, so a walk over it is missed unless its name is in the known set.
3. A source root passed as a **parameter** (rather than defined by a `const`) is missed.
4. **Aliases/indirection** are missed: `const r = root; walk(r)`, `roots.forEach(walk)`, or a walk reached through a helper defined elsewhere.
5. It is textual, so a **string or comment** containing a matching shape can false-positive.

**RESULTS SO FAR.** `tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts` **8 passed / 0 failed** (the audit itself plus the new real-tree symmetry test); `tests/select-tests-always-on.test.ts` **7/0**; `tests/chrome-lock-fixture-scope.test.ts` **2/0 (118ms)**.

**ONE PRE-EXISTING RED, ADJUDICATED, NOT MINE:** `tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts` fails `guard: the attributed population and its documented exclusions` ("build-artifact pins are skipped by owner ruling; a change here means dist is being judged"). I checked it the same way as the earlier adjudications — with MAIN's versions of both files this branch changes, swapped in — and it fails identically, so it is a main-side red and not caused here. It is also the file this change newly promotes, which is worth coord's attention as a separate item: the promotion is not what breaks it.

**A PRECONDITION I FOUND AND WROTE DOWN WHERE IT BELONGS.** Promoting `tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts` exposed that it imports a built bundle (`extension/dist/shared/diff-core.bundle.js` via `extension/lib/artifacts.js`), so it cannot run standalone on a worktree that has never built — it fails type-checking, not on an assertion. That is a pre-existing property of the file, and it is safe in the gate flow because the serial phase builds before the parallel phase runs the always-on set (visible in the ia4z gate log). The entry now says so, because a bare promotion would have looked unconditional.

The reviewer (`antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash`, different family) returned FAIL with three P1s and two P2s. All five were real defects of mine, not disagreements, and they are fixed in `834ac6e1`:

**p1lp — the repo-walk detector now matches source roots by DEFINITION, both named escapes are adjudicated, and the falsification is real-tree** — IN_REVIEW

Branch `fleet/qazo-p1lp`, tip **`dcd5cac0`**, base **`c06d6e00`**. 4 files: `scripts/select-tests.mjs`, `tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts`, new `tests/chrome-tools-t12-static.test.ts`, and `tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts` (the split-out half).

**WHY A NAME LIST COULD NOT WORK.** The kz27 pattern `/walk\(\s*[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*\b/` failed in both directions, and widening the list would have failed both ways too: it demanded an UPPERCASE identifier, so `tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts`'s `await walk(root)` — `const root = new URL("../extension/", import.meta.url)` — escaped entirely, while it also matched ANY uppercase identifier, which is how a 23s esbuild-spawning file entered the always-on set and tripled every subset gate (chrome-agent-platform-fgik). The reason is that `walk(root)` is ALSO how a dozen tests traverse a **DOM tree** (`tests/agent-permissions-panel.test.ts` passes an Element): the identifier's SHAPE carries no information, its DEFINITION does.

**THE RULE.** A walk/read counts as a scanner when the thing being walked is the repo root or a **top-level** source dir, established by an explicitly enumerated set of shapes: a known source-root constant, a relative URL to the repo root or a top-level dir, a `join(...)` ending at a top-level-dir literal **whose receiver is itself a source root**, or a template ending at one. Sub-roots (`extension/wasm/cas`, `extension/wasm/manifests`, `scripts/git-hooks`, a probe dir inside `extension/`) are deliberately NOT matched — that class is the over-match that cost a gate. The original ROOT-rooted literal patterns are kept, so nothing regressed.

**ADJUDICATED WITH WRITTEN REASONS** (`SOURCE_INSPECTING_GUARDS` + `SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS`; the exclusion list is policed — each entry needs a real reason and an owning bead):
- **IN:** `tests/chrome-tools-t12-static.test.ts` (the split-out lease-guard invariant), `tests/unbundled-page-census.test.ts` (all five of its tests are the census), `tests/composer-selector-migration.test.ts` (found by the delta reviewer, not by me: `SCAN_ROOTS` over `scripts|capevidence|tests`, walks computed paths — the pattern family `SCAN_(DIRS|ROOTS|TREES)` now matches its name too), `tests/chrome-lock-fixture-scope.test.ts`.
- **OUT, with reasons:** `tests/wasm-package-authority.test.ts` (16 tests, one walker) and `tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts` (15 tests, one walker, and it SPAWNS to hold the slot so it is not host-independent) — the split is owed, because promoting a mixed file for one static invariant is the mistake the split pattern exists to avoid; and `tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts`, held out **while it is RED on current main** (adjudicated by running it with main's copies of this bead's files), because an always-on guard that fails would redden every subset gate. The two named escapes from the bead (`chrome-test-contract`, `code-health`) were already promoted by the F3 review — I verified that rather than assuming it.

**EVIDENCE.**
- Audit at this tip: `tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts` **8 passed / 0 failed**, unclassified list **empty**, 30 entries.
- **End-to-end falsification:** dropping a promoted guard from the list makes the audit **FAIL CLOSED naming the file**; restoring returns green. The real-tree symmetry test also pins both directions against shipped files: `tests/chrome-tools-t12-static.test.ts` must be flagged when unlisted (the lowercase-alias case that used to escape) and `tests/agent-permissions-panel.test.ts` must NOT be (its `walk(root)` walks DOM nodes).
- Split verified faithful: the source file lost only that test (**24 → 23, verified 23/0**), the split file is **1/0 (176ms)** and needs **no dist build** (it reads raw `.js` and skips `dist/` — corrected after the delta review).
- **Gate run on this tip** (`qazo-p1lp-gate3`, `test:changed`, dist pre-built): `CHANGED_RC=1` with **one named failure — `tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts` → `86gg: the SAME slow file is killed by the flat bound and survives the scaled one`, which is chrome-agent-platform-cihz**, the filed wall-clock flake (measured by me at **3/5 on this tip, 1/4 with main's `serial-phase.mjs`**, so it flakes without this change). Because a serial file failed, the run fail-closed and skipped 539 parallel files — **except the always-on guard set, which ran regardless and passed 223 passed / 0 failed**, including all four files adjudicated IN here. No failure among this branch's own files.
- No build leg is needed: this change touches `scripts/` and `tests/` only, not the extension build.

**REVIEW HISTORY.** `reviewer` (`antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash`, different family) returned **FAIL / BLOCK** on the first revision with three P1s (a single-dot `REPO_ROOT_URL` that made the tests-dir rule dead code; a `walk` extractor that demanded an immediate `)` and so missed `walk(root, opts)`/`walk(abs, rel)`; a declaration capture that stopped at the first newline and so missed formatted multi-line definitions) and two P2s (inline-expression arguments missed; promoting a mixed 24-test file whole). All five fixed in `834ac6e1`. The **delta review then returned PASS, merge verdict "OK with notes"**, confirming every one as genuinely fixed and adding four more notes (an optional slash after an interpolation; a `join` receiver over-match; **my own comment was wrong** about the split file needing dist; and the `composer-selector-migration` evasion) — all fixed in `dcd5cac0`.

**RESIDUAL LIMITS, stated rather than implied away:** a walk whose target is **computed** (`${ROOT}${root}`), an identifier **imported from another module**, a root passed as a **parameter**, and aliases/indirection are still missed. The shape whitelist is explicitly enumerated, so an unanticipated construction is missed rather than mis-flagged — the safe direction — and that is why it exists instead of a looser path match that produced false positives in both of my earlier attempts.

title: [tooling] extract the browser-free static scan from tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts into its own always-on guard
description:
Follow-on from the chrome-agent-platform-kz27 review (F1, 2026-10-06), filed so real guard COVERAGE is restored rather than quietly lost. CURRENT STATE: chrome-profile-location.test.ts is held out of ALWAYS_ON by a DECLARED SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS entry (reason + chrome-agent-platform-hlgr), because it unconditionally launches a real Chromium (four await launchChrome calls, no skip guard; docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md:13) and putting the whole file in ALWAYS_ON would make a working browser a prerequisite for every subset gate on every VM. THE COST OF THAT EXCLUSION, which this bead exists to remove: the file ALSO contains a BROWSER-FREE static source scan (scanScriptProfileSites) that inspects scripts for profile-path sites. That scan is a genuine cross-cutting guard of the same class as file-url-root-guard, and while the whole file is excluded it does not run in subset gates at all — so kz27 fixes the blind spot for three guards while knowingly dropping this one from subset coverage. The reviewer's preferred fix was the SPLIT; the exclusion was adopted to land the class fix tonight, and the split is tracked here.
ACCEPTANCE: scanScriptProfileSites (or its equivalent) lives in its own always-on guard file with NO browser dependency, is added to SOURCE_INSPECTING_GUARDS/ALWAYS_ON, and the live-browser race test stays out of ALWAYS_ON running only in the full suite. The SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS entry for chrome-profile-location.test.ts is then removed (never left alongside the split, which would be a contradiction the new audit case would reject). PROOF REQUIRED: the extracted guard RUNS in a subset gate (quote the selection line), and it goes RED when a profile-path site is reintroduced. Note the new audit case in select-tests.mjs already rejects an exclusion that exists on disk without a substantive reason, without a bead, or while also being in ALWAYS_ON — so the end state must be internally consistent.
close_reason: DONE 2026-10-06 — SATISFIED BY THE SPLIT, which is the merger's ledger note and it is correct: this bead existed to restore the browser-free static scan's always-on coverage after chrome-profile-location was held out by a declared exclusion during kz27. The revision at 41f7a028 implemented the SPLIT instead, so the static scan now lives in tests/chrome-profile-static.test.ts and IS always-on — verified independently by coord: 2 passed / 0 failed in 205ms with NO browser — and SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS now covers only the browser-dependent remainder, justified by docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md §2.3 and naming hlgr. The goal is met by a better route than this bead proposed (extraction rather than a parallel guard), so it is closed rather than left as a duplicate of landed work. Nothing remains: the coverage this bead asked for is in ALWAYS_ON and runs on every subset gate.

title: [tooling] the serial-phase failure notices go to stderr, so any log that captures only stdout shows the summary WITHOUT the failing-file names
description:
Found by chrome-agent-platform-merger during 0iln's full build gate, 2026-10-06, and it nearly cost the attribution dsoq was written to provide. WHAT HAPPENED: the gate log carried the runner's STDOUT lines but NONE of its STDERR lines. The merger PROVED the code emits them by running a hang fixture at a 2s bound and showing the 'TIMED OUT' notice, the 'FAILED' line carrying its durable per-file log path, and the FAILING SERIAL FILE(S) block all appear under a plain 2>&1. So the notices exist and are emitted; the log lost the stderr half. WHAT SAVED IT (and this is the point): dsoq's DURABLE PER-FILE LOGS were what made the failing files nameable at all, which turns that design choice from a nicety into demonstrated necessity.
FIX: emit the FAILING SERIAL FILE(S) block and the per-file TIMED OUT/FAILED lines on STDOUT as well as stderr (or unconditionally via the same sink as the summary), so any consumer that captures stdout alone still receives the attribution. Keep stderr emission too, because a human running the command reads it there.
ACCEPTANCE: a test that captures ONLY stdout from a run with a deliberately failing serial file still contains the failing file's name and exit code; and the same for a per-file timeout kill. Related: a separate FLEET-tooling gap (the gate wake/template) is reported to the hub, not here — and the wake template announcing any 124 as 'KILLED by the bound' is the sibling defect, since a single serial file timing out also yields 124.
close_reason: DONE — landed c06d6e00 (merge --no-ff of the reviewed 3e0c2292 onto b2a10894; parents b2a10894 + 3e0c2292) and COORD-VERIFIED on merged main: scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs and the new tests/serial-phase-stdout-attribution.test.ts are byte-identical to the reviewed tip (serial-phase.mjs re-checked against current main after the 3337 merge began and still identical). WHAT LANDED: the serial runner now emits its immediate per-file failure notice AND the named failing-file block on STDOUT as well as STDERR, so a stdout-capturing consumer or a mid-phase kill can no longer produce a count without a name; the durable per-file log remains the belt. The gate proof was live rather than unit-only (hang-probe notices on both streams, named block beneath) and both review P2s were fixed and PROVEN by single-site reverts. Two follow-ons were filed rather than folded in to keep this tight: chrome-agent-platform-weff (the same stderr-only defect at scripts/run-tests.mjs:53 and scripts/select-tests.mjs:381) and chrome-agent-platform-cihz (the pre-existing 86gg wall-clock flake, which fails 3/5 at this tip and 1/4 with main's serial-phase.mjs swapped in). Also recorded on this bead: the lane's own gate caught a defect class in the lane's own change — a helper inserted between a function's JSDoc @param block and the function made runSerialFiles lose its types, which only an in-process test could see because the spawned-driver test never passes options through the type checker.

comments.text: LIVE RECURRENCE 2026-10-06 — this is no longer theoretical and it has now happened after dsoq landed. qazo's o2t3 gate: test:changed was KILLED at its 1800s bound (exit 124), but BEFORE the kill the serial phase reported 'serial phase (6 build/artifact files) FAILED (1/6 failed) in 919s' — A COUNT WITH NO NAME — and the per-file durable log was NOT found in ~/cap-evidence/serial-phase-logs for that run's window, so the lane could not say whether the failure was its own. That is precisely the defect dsoq exists to fix, observed in production after dsoq shipped. TWO CANDIDATE MECHANISMS and they need different fixes: (a) the FAILING SERIAL FILE(S) block prints to STDERR and the gate log drops stderr, so the block existed and was thrown away — which is THIS bead, and would make the fix here sufficient; or (b) the phase was killed before the block printed, in which case the count came from somewhere that still does not carry the names and this bead's acceptance must ALSO cover the killed-phase case (emit each file's outcome as it completes, not only in a summary block at the end). NOTE the pid-suffixed log name: j5yz's chrome-agent-platform-grj9 added process.pid to the durable stamp, so a window search using the OLD naming will miss the log even when it exists — rule that out before concluding the log is missing. ASK SENT TO QAZO: report which stream the block uses and whether the pid-suffixed log exists.
