comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-coord
comments.text:
COORD CORRECTION 2026-10-06 — MY TWO-MECHANISM FRAMING WAS WRONG IN ONE HALF, and the author of dsoq has the better analysis because it wrote the code. CORRECTION: I wrote that 'a summary block at the end is structurally the wrong place and each file's outcome must be emitted as it completes' — but dsoq ALREADY emits a PER-FILE line the moment each file finishes ('run-tests: serial file <f> FAILED (exit <code>[, TIMED OUT]) in <secs>s — captured output: <log>'), and that path was proven live with a hang fixture at a 2s bound. So for a phase KILLED mid-run, the per-file lines for everything already failed had ALREADY been printed; the timing was never the problem. THE REAL SINGLE CAUSE: the per-file failure line AND the FAILING SERIAL FILE(S) block both go to STDERR (console.error) while the phase HEADERS go to STDOUT (console.log) — which is exactly why the o2t3 log carries headers and no name, and why jfbn's landing gate lost the same half. Mechanisms (a) and (b) are therefore ONE mechanism: attribution emitted on a stream the consumer discards.
ACCEPTANCE, COLLAPSED TO ONE SMALL FIX (author's proposal, adopted): EMIT THE ATTRIBUTION ON STDOUT AS WELL — both the per-file failure line and the summary block — keeping stderr for humans. That survives any stdout-capturing consumer AND any mid-phase kill, without adding an end-of-phase mechanism that a kill can delete. The per-file durable log remains the second copy (belt), and note j5yz's grj9 added process.pid to that stamp, so a window-name search using the OLD naming misses a log that exists — qazo is checking that rather than concluding the log is absent. ACCEPTANCE TEST: capture ONLY stdout from a run with a deliberately failing serial file AND from a run KILLED mid-phase, and require the failing file's name and exit code in each; and keep a case proving stderr still carries the human copy.

comments.text: COORD 2026-10-06 — ONE HALF IS NOW CONCLUSIVELY DEMONSTRATED, WITH STREAM EVIDENCE. qazo's o2t3 run separates the two mechanisms precisely, and (a) is proven: there is NO stderr capture or redirect anywhere in the chain (no console.error assignment and no process.stderr use in select-tests.mjs, lib/serial-phase.mjs or run-tests.mjs; select-tests spawns run-tests with stdio 'inherit'), YET the run's log is 717 bytes containing the STDOUT lines (six 'serial file X' banners plus the phase summary) and ZERO of the stderr-only lines — 0 TIMED OUT, 0 'serial file ... FAILED', 0 'FAILING SERIAL FILE(S):'. The banners (serial-phase.mjs:183) and the summary (:211) are console.log; the per-file attribution (:201) and the timeout notice (:114) are console.error. So in ONE file stdout survived and stderr did not: that is exactly this bead's class, demonstrated in production with the stream mapping named line by line. CRUCIALLY the per-file FAILED lines print BEFORE the summary, so they cannot have been 'not yet reached' — for the per-file attribution the answer is (a) stderr loss, conclusively, and the one-small-fix acceptance stands unchanged. For the summary BLOCK (which prints after the summary, :211 then :216) this log cannot separate (a) from a mid-gap kill, and it does not need to: emitting attribution on stdout covers both. ALSO CORRECTED ON THIS BEAD: my earlier note suggesting grj9's pid-suffixed naming might have hidden the log was WRONG — qazo's run stamp is the plain form because that run predates grj9's landing, and the failure logs existed all along; its first search was wrong (an ls -lat column filter that matched nothing, read as emptiness). That is the same failure mode as my own verification-script bug tonight: an empty result from a broken query reads as evidence unless you check the query.

WHY THIS BEAD IS WORTH P3-ELEVATED ATTENTION: its defect has cost the fleet twice in one night. The serial phase prints its per-file failure attribution and the FAILING SERIAL FILE(S) block to STDERR while the phase headers and the summary go to STDOUT, so a stdout-capturing consumer gets a COUNT WITH NO NAME. Instance 1: the 0iln landing gate reported 'serial phase (19 build/artifact files) FAILED (1/19 failed) in 471s' with no name, and coord had to identify the file from the durable per-file belt (tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts, killed by its own scaled 202.5s bound). title: [tooling] a browser-dependent guard must fail with an explicitly ENVIRONMENTAL reason when no browser exists — never a silent ignore
description:
Follow-on from the chrome-agent-platform-kz27 decision (2026-10-06), filed so it is not lost. CONTEXT: tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts unconditionally launches a real Chromium — FOUR calls at :136/:146/:155/:213 and ZERO skip/ignore guards — and docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md:13 says so outright. kz27's widened scanner detector correctly classifies it as a repo-tree-walking guard, but adding it to ALWAYS_ON would make a WORKING BROWSER A PREREQUISITE FOR EVERY SUBSET GATE ON EVERY FLEET VM, turning an environment difference into a red gate on the heterogeneous VMs. So it is currently EXCLUDED by a DECLARED exclusion (SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS in scripts/select-tests.mjs, with a reason AND this bead id) rather than silently omitted — which is strictly better than the status quo, because an exclusion now has to be written down and justified.
REQUIREMENT: when a browser-dependent guard runs on a host with NO resolvable browser, it must refuse with an explicitly ENVIRONMENTAL reason, reported as a DISTINCT environmental outcome WITH A VISIBLE COUNT. The repo already has the convention: CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL / exit 75, which the journey gates use on high-load hosts.
HARD CONSTRAINT — IT MUST NOT BECOME A SILENT IGNORE: an ignore with no count reads as a pass, which is exactly the vacuous-green trap this fleet already paid for (chrome-agent-platform-fyvc closed that for the RPC census; chrome-agent-platform-dsvq closed it for six suites). An environmental refusal must be visible, counted, and distinguishable from both a product failure and a pass.
ACCEPTANCE: (1) a no-browser run names the environmental reason and counts the refusals; (2) a regression test drives the no-browser path (binary/PATH forced absent) and asserts the named environmental outcome AND the count, and would go RED if the refusal degraded to an ignore or to a generic failure; (3) once the fleet standardises on browsers, the SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS entry for tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts is removed and the guard joins ALWAYS_ON — say in the report which fleet state the change assumes.
close_reason: DONE — landed eb59da7e (merge of 167f76a9 + 091c4a1d; the reviewed tip 091c4a1d) and verified by coord: main carries scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts plus tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts and tests/chrome-profile-location-environment.test.ts. WHAT LANDED: a browser-dependent guard now refuses ENVIRONMENTALLY when no browser exists — NAMED AND COUNTED, not silently ignored — which is the contract this bead existed to establish, and which unblocked afpl and uvo3 by satisfying their recorded dependency edges. REVIEW HISTORY worth keeping because it is the loop working: the cross-family reviewer PASSED with notes and found TWO P1s the author had missed, both fixed before landing — (1) the refusal sat in test 3 of 8, so exit 75 ABORTED the file five STATIC tests on a browserless host; the browser test now declines to assert and a new FINAL test emits the refusal so every static test runs first; (2) resolveChromiumBinaryReport trusted a CAP_CHROMIUM override without checking the path exists, so a missing override resolved as success, the refusal never fired, and the launch died ENOENT — an environment difference surfacing as a product-shaped red, the exact class this bead removes; qazo defended it in its own layer and did NOT edit another lane file. A P2 was also fixed: the process path was untested, so a degradation to exit 0 would have passed; a subprocess test now drives refuseWithoutBrowser and asserts exit 75, the marker, and that it never returns. PROMOTION POSITION (acceptance item 3), recorded: the file stays OUT of ALWAYS_ON — promoting it would end every subset gate at exit 75 on a browserless host for a guard this change did not ask for — and main own exclusion reason already names chrome-agent-platform-hlgr, so no reason edit was needed; promotion is one line once browser availability is uniform (coord 2026-10-06 sweep: six of eight VMs have one, this VM included). SUPERSEDED RUNS to ignore, recorded as the author reported them: gate2 ran against a worktree the author had switched (its error, reported at the time) and gate3 was bound-killed; the authoritative run is the tip 30e16566 gate, BUILD_RC=0 with CHANGED_RC=1 whose single red was PRE-EXISTING ON MAIN (tests/site-agent-delegation-attachments.test.ts, now filed as chrome-agent-platform-3ui7 and coord-reproduced at 6 passed / 1 failed on merged main). **Owed to another owner, not fixed here:** the `resolveChromiumBinaryReport` override-existence gap in `scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts` (j5yz).

---
**REVIEW VERDICT VERBATIM:**
VERDICT: PASS
## Review
### Correct (with evidence)
- **Distinct environmental verdict** (`scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts:25-43`): Missing browser resolution emits `ENVIRONMENT: no resolvable browser — refusing ...`, the machine-readable marker `CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL`, a JSON payload (`reason`, `refused`, `tests`, `tried`), and exits with `ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT = 75` (`scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts:535`), matching the repo's convention used in `scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts:123` and `scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts:646`.
- **Honest resolver contract** (`scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:149-167`): Using `resolveChromiumBinaryReport` rather than `resolveChromiumBinary` is strictly necessary. `resolveChromiumBinary` unconditionally falls back to returning the string `"/usr/bin/chromium"` without checking whether the binary exists on disk (`scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:144`), which would report a resolved binary on a browserless box, bypass refusal, and crash during spawn with a product failure (exit 1).
- **Preserved `CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md §2.3` and subset gates** (`scripts/select-tests.mjs:194-199`): Retaining `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` in `SCANNER_EXCLUSIONS` rather than promoting it to `ALWAYS_ON` is sound. As documented in `docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md §2.3`, subset gates promise not to launch browsers unless browser-related files change. Promoting it would cause every subset gate (`npm run test:changed`) across browserless hosts (2 of 8 fleet VMs) to abort at exit 75 for unrelated changes. The browser-free static scan was already split into `tests/chrome-profile-static.test.ts:1-12` and is in `ALWAYS_ON`.
- **Zero test registry/scanner violations**: `scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts` introduces no filesystem writes or tmpfs calls (`tests/durable-root.test.ts`), contains no scanner or hazard patterns (`tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts`, `tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts`), and `tests/select-tests-always-on.test.ts` passes cleanly against the retained exclusion.
---
### Findings (file:line)
- **P1: Static unit tests in `chrome-profile-location.test.ts` aborted mid-file by exit 75**
  - **Location**: `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:106` (calling `refuseWithoutBrowser`) vs `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:169-370`
  - **Evidence**: `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` contains 8 tests. Test 3 (`"9t1b: a REAL browser holds its profile while the whole tree is copied"`, line 91) calls `refuseWithoutBrowser()`, invoking `Deno.exit(75)`. Tests 4 through 8 (lines 169, 199, 238, 309, 335) test static profile helper invariants (`pruneChromeProfileDirs` age pruning, 3-state lock classifier, root containment, live profile protection, and unknown lock retention). None require a browser, but none of them execute on a browserless host because `Deno.exit(75)` terminates the process at test 3.
  - **Smallest fix**: Reorder the tests so the live-browser race test runs last in `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` (after all static helper tests have run), or isolate the browser race into its own dedicated test file.
- **P1: `CAP_CHROMIUM` override without existence verification produces product failure instead of environmental refusal**
  - **Location**: `scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:156-160`
  - **Evidence**: `resolveChromiumBinaryReport` checks `const override = envGet("CAP_CHROMIUM"); if (typeof override === "string" && override.trim()) return { binary: override, tried };`. If an operator or script sets `CAP_CHROMIUM=/missing/path`, `binary` is non-null. `browserRefusal` sees `report.binary !== null` (`scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts:23`) and returns `null` (no refusal). `launchChrome` then attempts to spawn the non-existent binary and throws an unhandled ENOENT error, exiting 1 (product red) instead of 75.
  - **Smallest fix**: In `resolveChromiumBinaryReport`, gate the `override` return on `exists(override)`, appending `(missing on this box)` and falling through if absent.
- **P2: Process-level execution of `refuseWithoutBrowser` is untested**
  - **Location**: `tests/chrome-profile-location-environment.test.ts:15-18` vs `scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts:46-52`
  - **Evidence**: `tests/chrome-profile-location-environment.test.ts` only imports and exercises `browserRefusal(...)`. It never imports or calls `refuseWithoutBrowser(...)`, nor does it execute `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` in a subprocess. If `refuseWithoutBrowser` were changed to call `Deno.exit(0)` or if line 106 in `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` were removed, `tests/chrome-profile-location-environment.test.ts` would still pass 3/3 green.
  - **Smallest fix**: Add a subprocess regression test (mirroring `tests/quiet-window.test.ts:584`) that executes a minimal harness calling `refuseWithoutBrowser` and asserts process exit code 75 and stdout marker presence.
- **P2: Duplicated comment block in guard test**
  - **Location**: `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:92-97` and `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts:98-103`
  - **Evidence**: The 3-line sentence `"// chrome-agent-platform-hlgr: this file's ONE browser-dependent test. On a host with no resolvable browser it must refuse ENVIRONMENTALLY..."` is duplicated back-to-back inside the test header.
  - **Smallest fix**: Deduplicate lines 92–103 into a single comment block.
---
### Specific Judgments
#### 1. Distinguishability and file-level exit 75
The refusal is distinguishable from a pass (`exit 0`) and a product failure (`exit 1`):
- Exit code 75 (`ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT`) is non-zero and non-one.
- The human log line starts with `ENVIRONMENT:`.
- The machine log line starts with `CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL` with JSON payload.
No automated runner checking `code === 0` will read it as green.
However, **exit 75 is a blunt instrument for a test file**:
The file's other tests are **NOT already run**. Tests 1 and 2 (lines 52 and 71) run before test 3, but tests 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 (lines 169–370) are static helper tests that run after test 3. Calling `Deno.exit(75)` inside test 3 aborts the process, preventing tests 4–8 from executing. Furthermore, in `npm test` (`scripts/run-tests.mjs:45`), `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` runs in the parallel phase with ~300 other files; an unhandled `Deno.exit(75)` within Deno's parallel test runner aborts the entire parallel test runner process.
#### 2. Count honesty and meaningfulness
Counting browser-dependent tests (`refused: 1`) is the honest unit for unverified browser functionality, avoiding inflating the failure to an entire suite or file. The payload `{ reason: "no-resolvable-browser", refused: 1, tests: [...], tried: [...] }` provides actionable diagnostic steps.
*Caveat*: While the count honestly reflects that only 1 browser test was intended to be refused, in practice 5 additional static tests in that file are also terminated by the process exit without being included in the refused count.
#### 3. Absence forcing and degradation resilience
- In `tests/chrome-profile-location-environment.test.ts`, `browserRefusal` genuinely rejects degradations: returning `null` fails `assert(refusal !== null)`, returning `exit: 0` or `exit: 1` fails `assertEquals(refusal!.exit, 75)`, and omitting the count fails lines 48–49.
- *Blind spots*: Because `tests/chrome-profile-location-environment.test.ts` only unit-tests `browserRefusal` and never calls `refuseWithoutBrowser` or spawns `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts`:
  1. A degradation where `refuseWithoutBrowser` calls `Deno.exit(0)` or `Deno.exit(1)` would still pass the test suite.
  2. A regression deleting line 106 of `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` would pass the test suite.
  3. Setting `CAP_CHROMIUM=/nonexistent` causes a product red (exit 1) rather than a refusal because `resolveChromiumBinaryReport` does not check existence on `CAP_CHROMIUM`.
- *Hook legitimacy*: Relying on `exists: () => false` is legitimate for testing absence because on a VM where `/usr/bin/chromium` physically exists, `resolveChromiumBinaryReport` checks the hardcoded path `/usr/bin/chromium` directly rather than checking `PATH`.
#### 4. `resolveChromiumBinaryReport` vs `resolveChromiumBinary`
Using `resolveChromiumBinaryReport` is correct and necessary. `resolveChromiumBinary` unconditionally returns a non-null string (`"/usr/bin/chromium"`) without verifying filesystem existence (`scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts:144`). If the guard had used `resolveChromiumBinary`, `report.binary` would never be null on a browserless box, spurious refusals would be impossible, and the test would have crashed with an unhandled ENOENT spawn error (product red).
#### 5. Defensibility of not promoting to `ALWAYS_ON`
The decision NOT to promote `tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts` to `ALWAYS_ON` is completely defensible.
Promoting it would cause every single `npm run test:changed` subset gate on browserless VMs (2 of 8 fleet VMs) to terminate at exit 75, blocking all developer/agent workflows on those VMs regardless of what files were edited. On browser-equipped VMs, it would force a full repository copy under a live browser on every subset gate, violating `docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md §2.3`. Cross-cutting static coverage was already preserved via `tests/chrome-profile-static.test.ts`. This satisfies acceptance criterion (3), correctly assuming the fleet state from the 2026-10-06 sweep (6 of 8 VMs have a browser).
#### 6. Wiring and unstated limits
`scripts/lib/browser-refusal.ts` is cleanly scoped:
- It does not perform temporary filesystem operations, complying with `tests/durable-root.test.ts`.
- It does not define an executable harness in `scripts/`, so it is correctly omitted from `scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts`.
- It does not contain repository scan patterns, complying with `tests/source-inspecting-tests-guard.test.ts`.
- `scripts/select-tests.mjs` was restored to main's version in commit `5da2c0c1`, keeping `tests/select-tests-always-on.test.ts` fully green (7/7 passed).
---
### Merge verdict
**OK with notes** (VERDICT: PASS).
The implementation satisfies all three acceptance criteria of bead `chrome-agent-platform-hlgr` without breaking the test suite or violating contracts. The P1 items (static tests aborted after line 106, unchecked `CAP_CHROMIUM` existence) and P2 items (duplicate comments, lack of subprocess execution test) should be addressed in follow-up beads.

title: [perf] artifacts previews: BATCH the asset.get round-trips instead of overlapping them — the single-threaded SW/OPFS path is the measured bottleneck
description: From qazo's chrome-agent-platform-0iln measurement (2026-10-06, tip d9ffafbf), and the more valuable half of what that work learned. EVIDENCE: with an 8-wide bounded pool the throughput stayed ~74-84ms/read in BOTH the serial baseline and the pooled fixed arm, while per-read latency inflated 5.4x (84 -> 463ms) under pool contention. So the await CHAIN was never the throughput bottleneck — the single-threaded service-worker/OPFS read path is. Consequence: overlapping reads buys bounded latency-hiding but not throughput, and it slightly regressed first-visible-preview (588ms fixed vs 495ms baseline). THE HIGHER-VALUE DIRECTION IS CUTTING ROUND-TRIPS: one batched asset.get (or a multi-id read) for up to MAX_PREVIEWS = 24 previews instead of up to 24 separate chrome.runtime -> SW -> OPFS round-trips. ACCEPTANCE: measure a batched read path against the pooled and serial arms using the scale-invariant readWindowShareOfSum metric AND a true readsSum denominator (the 0iln lesson: never derive a counterfactual from a p50 measured under contention), n>1 with interleaved arms; show either a throughput win or a first-visible-preview win. If neither materialises, say so and close this as measured-not-worth-it. Do NOT claim a speed win from concurrency alone.
close_reason: measured-not-worth-it: batched path regresses first-visible preview (64ms vs 34ms serial / 36ms pool-8) and ties serial on throughput (7.3ms/read); single-threaded SW/OPFS serialization dominates

comments.author: chrome-agent-platform-qazo
comments.text:
EMPIRICAL MEASUREMENT & CLOSURE DISPOSITION: measured-not-worth-it

Conducted interleaved multi-arm benchmark (n=3 rounds, counterbalanced execution, 30 seeded artifacts, 24 preview cards) across all five arms: serial (concurrency 1), pool-2, pool-4, pool-8, and batched (multi-id asset.get with 4-then-20 chunking).

Summary table (medians and means across n=3 interleaved rounds):
- serial:
  * firstPreviewMedianMs: 34ms (mean 36ms)
  * readsWindowMedianMs: 174ms (mean 182ms)
  * readsSumMeanMs: 173ms
  * shareOfSumMean: 1.052
  * throughputMedianMs: 7.3ms / read
  * totalMedianMs: 199ms
- pool-2:
  * firstPreviewMedianMs: 50ms (mean 59ms)
  * readsWindowMedianMs: 156ms (mean 222ms)
  * readsSumMeanMs: 428ms
  * shareOfSumMean: 0.521
  * throughputMedianMs: 6.5ms / read
  * totalMedianMs: 177ms
- pool-4:
  * firstPreviewMedianMs: 36ms (mean 47ms)
  * readsWindowMedianMs: 152ms (mean 178ms)
  * readsSumMeanMs: 673ms
  * shareOfSumMean: 0.265
  * throughputMedianMs: 6.3ms / read
  * totalMedianMs: 165ms
- pool-8:
  * firstPreviewMedianMs: 36ms (mean 42ms)
  * readsWindowMedianMs: 164ms (mean 166ms)
  * readsSumMeanMs: 1178ms
  * shareOfSumMean: 0.141
  * throughputMedianMs: 6.8ms / read
  * totalMedianMs: 190ms
- batched:
  * firstPreviewMedianMs: 64ms (mean 61ms)
  * readsWindowMedianMs: 176ms (mean 204ms)
  * readsSumMeanMs: 202ms
  * shareOfSumMean: 1.007
  * throughputMedianMs: 7.3ms / read
  * totalMedianMs: 200ms

Analysis & Findings:
1. Batched path:
   - First-visible-preview regresses significantly: 64ms median / 61ms mean vs serial 34ms and pool-8 36ms (worst of all 5 arms). Because card 0 must wait for the initial chunk (even bounded to 4) to be read and returned across IPC, time-to-first-preview is delayed.
   - Throughput: 7.3ms / read ties serial (7.3ms / read) and is slower than pool-4 (6.3ms / read) and pool-8 (6.8ms / read).
   - Total wall-clock: 200ms is the slowest of all arms.
   - Mechanism: Collapsing 24 round-trips into 2 round-trips confirms the 0iln diagnostic — IPC and await chains are not the primary bottleneck; the single-threaded OPFS/SW serialization dominates.
2. Concurrency tuning:
   - pool-4 reduces contention sum by ~43% compared to pool-8 (673ms vs 1178ms) and achieves the best median total wall-clock (165ms) while matching pool-8's 36ms first-preview median. However, within-arm variance across runs (100-200ms) dominates the ~10-25ms between-arm difference, and no configuration decisively beats pool-8 on user-perceived first preview.
3. Disposition:
   - Acceptance criteria explicitly mandates: 'If neither materialises, say so and close this as measured-not-worth-it.'
   - Independent review (qwen3.8-max) verified this negative result: batched path is not worth enabling, and shipping it as dead code or changing defaults is unwarranted.
   - Branch fleet/qazo-bofg reset cleanly to origin/main (b2659a0c).

title: [tooling] serial-phase reporting hardening from the dsoq review: spawn-error reason omitted, and the durable log stamp can collide across worktrees
description:
Two P2 findings from the antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash review of dsoq (2026-10-06), verified against the source but deliberately NOT applied at landing so the landed bytes stay identical to the reviewed revision.
(1) scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs:155 builds the captured failure text from result.stdout + result.stderr ONLY. When spawnSync fails at the OS level (ENOENT if the Deno binary is missing, EACCES, or ENOBUFS when maxBuffer is exceeded) the failure is correctly attributed to the file with code 1, but the REASON lives in result.error and never reaches the FAILING SERIAL FILE(S) block or the log. Smallest fix: include result.error.stack/result.error in text when present.
(2) scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs:151,163 uses a millisecond-resolution stamp with no process.pid for the durable per-file log, and serialLogDir() is shared under durableRoot() in $HOME/cap-evidence across all worktrees. Two runs on different worktrees that fail the same serial file in the same millisecond write the same path and overwrite each other, losing exactly the evidence this bead exists to preserve. Smallest fix: add process.pid to the stamp (the new test already namespaces with Deno.pid).
ACCEPTANCE: both fixes landed with a regression test for each; for (1) a test asserting a forced spawn error's reason appears in the captured output; for (2) a test asserting two runs with different pids produce different log paths.

title: [security] dynamic wildcard postMessage fallbacks (origin || "*") are outside the wfxe recurrence guard
description: Found by the antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash reviewer as a P2 design note during the wfxe review (2026-10-05), and filed rather than lost. tests/postmessage-wildcard-guard.test.ts matches only LITERAL wildcard arguments (WILDCARD_RE = /^["'\`]\*["'\`]$/), so dynamic fallbacks are not covered: extension/lib/preference-bridge.js:285 uses 'origin || "*"' and :183 uses 'expectedOrigin || "*"'. If either origin/expectedOrigin can be falsy at that point, the message is broadcast to ANY origin — the same hazard class the wfxe guard exists to prevent. NOT a defect in wfxe (its stated scope was static unexamined wildcards) and non-blocking. title: Contribute the merge closing block (assert-then-act, 4-branch fail-closed, distinct exit codes) as a tracked script
description:
CONTRIBUTE THE MERGE CLOSING BLOCK AS A TRACKED SCRIPT — four copies of one implementation now exist across the fleet and four copies diverge.

WHAT IT IS: the atomic assert-then-act block the merger lanes run as the last step of a landing. Dry-run the REAL target to a FILE with the status captured UNPIPED, decide on the captured output, and let that decision GATE the push — no unasserted action, nothing between the assertion and the act.

BRANCH ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: '[rejected]' is tested FIRST, because a refusal output still contains sha lines and can satisfy a positive update-row match incidentally. A rejection is the only branch that must win over every other match.

FOUR BRANCHES, FAIL-CLOSED, WITH A DISTINCT EXIT PER BRANCH so a caller cannot mistake "nothing to land" for success:
  0 OK                — update row present, no '[rejected]', and the published sha IS this HEAD -> push (or WOULD PUSH under a stub)
  2 NOTHING_TO_LAND   — 'Everything up-to-date'; run the throwaway write-path probe; DO NOT PUSH. This is NOT a pass.
  3 REFUSED           — '[rejected]'; DO NOT PUSH -> fetch + re-merge + RE-GATE the merged tree, never a blind retry
  4 UNKNOWN           — matched no branch; DO NOT PUSH (a git wording change, a locale, or a truncated capture must not fall through to a push)
  5 MISMATCH          — the dry run would publish a different commit than HEAD; DO NOT PUSH
The last branch being 'else: push' is the difference between a gate and an unconditional push wearing a gate's clothes.

THE CORRECTION THIS SCRIPT CARRIES, MEASURED: the fleet's settled update-row regex ('^ *[0-9a-f]{4,}\.\.[0-9a-f]{4,} +HEAD -> ') does NOT match the form git prints when the source is an explicit 40-character sha — which is this fleet's OWN push discipline. Measured on the j5yz landing: with SRC=<sha> the row is "c8b33a2e..3c39696c  3c39696c1f2edd7d2c733585e9be2070e164904c -> main" with NO HEAD token, so the HEAD-anchored regex classifies a legitimate landing as UNKNOWN. Fail-closed, so it is safe rather than dangerous, but it BLOCKS. The portable regex is '^ *[0-9a-f]{7,}\.\.[0-9a-f]{7,} +[^ ]+ -> '. INDEXING, also measured: the value to compare against HEAD is the one AFTER '..' (the local/new side); the value BEFORE it is the REMOTE's current value. A lane implementing "the first value is the local side" would refuse every valid push.

REHEARSAL REQUIREMENT, INCLUDING THE MUTATION STUB AND A CONTROL: rehearse with the push stubbed and report WHICH BRANCHES WERE REAL rather than "four green branches". Current evidence from this lane (2026-10-05): all four were produced by REAL git output, not synthesis — REFUSED from pushing an ancestor of main ('! [rejected] ... (non-fast-forward)', rc=1); NOTHING_TO_LAND from HEAD == main plus a real negotiation row from the throwaway; OK from a real fast-forward update row against an existing ref; UNKNOWN from a real '* [new branch]'. MISMATCH remains UNEXERCISED and is therefore relied on WITHOUT evidence. Controls after every rehearsal: main and the probed branch unmoved, probe refs created = 0. The UNKNOWN branch is additionally proven in PRODUCTION, because it fired for real on the j5yz landing and refused the push before the regex was fixed.

SCOPE / SEQUENCING: do this AFTER the current [hold:no-new-work] lifts. Filed as a bead rather than started, per the hub's instruction not to add work during the hold.

title: [security] DNS-rebinding residual in fetch-policy is host-string-only and absent from RISK-REGISTER
description:

title: [bug] Six secondary surface bundles declare a budget but are in neither the reporting table nor dist.complete
description:
Found by the VM-fleet reviewer (gemini-3.8-flash) during the chrome-agent-platform-74pb review (2026-10-05, tip 35d52544), and explicitly NOT introduced by that change — the reviewer traced it to 9epn.5.

Consequences:
1. The build's budget loop iterates STORE_BUNDLE_BUDGETS, so these six are never size-reported at all — not even as "<= reference".
2. `extension/dist/dist.complete` records sizes + sha256 for the six primary outputs only, so these six have no recorded size and no pinned hash in the marker.
3. Under the 2026-10-05 owner decision (sizes are MEASURED AND REPORTED, not enforced), "measured by nothing" is the worst state: they can neither fail a build nor be observed to grow.

NOTE the asymmetry the reviewer confirmed: the six PRIMARY bundles in STORE_BUNDLE_BUDGETS are pinned 1:1 against DIST_COMPLETE_OUTPUTS by tests/bundle-budget.test.ts, so none can silently drop out; the secondary six have no such pin.

ACCEPTANCE: decide which of the two is intended — (a) bring the six into the reporting set (STORE_BUNDLE_BUDGETS/ BUDGET_REPORTED_BUNDLES and, where they are shipped artifacts, DIST_COMPLETE_OUTPUTS), or (b) remove their unused `budget:` properties so the tree does not claim a measurement it does not take; and add the test that keeps the two sets in sync (the same shape as the existing "every generated bundle has a reference" pin) so no future bundle can land in the gap. State which was chosen and why.

title: [bug] h638-open-trace refuses its own live-open precondition: a send during an in-flight run is queued, not a new execution
description:
FOUND WHILE FIXING chrome-agent-platform-sxbz (the stale h638-open-trace driver).

The driver could not run at all before the fix (system Chromium ignores --load-extension; the four composer constants were retired ids). It now runs end to end — it launches the extension, builds a real task with history ("built a real task with history: {bubbles:6}"), reads durable executions, and sends the live turn — and then REFUSES, honestly, at its own running-open gate:

  newest execution at click time: {"id":"exec:9d6b540d-…","phase":"terminal"}
    (same id as the last settled one — the send was queued into the in-flight run)
  REFUSING to report a running-open number: the newest execution is "terminal"

WHY THAT HAPPENS: the driver assumes its live send (@demo-slow @demo-stream) STARTS A NEW execution, so that "newest execution" becomes the in-flight one and the open can be timed against it. But a send during an in-flight run is QUEUED INTO that run (thread-continuation semantics), so no new execution appears and the precondition never becomes true. The test it needs cannot be constructed the way it is written.

DECISION NEEDED (h638 metric owner): either
(a) measure the CONTINUATION — the open of a thread whose only in-flight work is a queued follow-up is exactly the owner's case ("a task he has been using that is CURRENTLY running"), so the driver should assert the queued-into state instead of a fresh execution id; or
(b) wait for a genuinely fresh run (send after the previous one reaches terminal) and accept that this measures a different scenario — which is what its own control run already does.

Not fixed here: choosing between those two is a measurement-semantics call, and sxbz's scope was to make the driver runnable (it is) with recorded reasoning. The refusal is now the driver's honest output instead of a silent wrong number.

title: [bug] Killed builds leave untracked .dist-stage-* residue that poisons npm run test:changed
description:
Found by the VM-fleet lane qazo (2026-10-04 23:13Z) while recovering from a killed build; reported with evidence, out of scope for its own increment.

DEFECT: an interrupted or killed build leaves untracked, NON-gitignored residue in the worktree — `extension/.dist-stage-<pid>-<timestamp>/` (two observed: 19 and 12 files) and `.build.lock.d/owner.json`. `scripts/select-tests.mjs` (the `npm run test:changed` entry point) collects candidates with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, so it sees that residue as changed-file-with-no-reachable-test and prints FAIL CLOSED:

  select-tests: FAIL CLOSED — changed file(s) with no reachable test cannot be proved covered by a subset:
    extension/.dist-stage-70457-1791155350084/...
  Running the FULL suite (npm test) instead.

CONSEQUENCE: any killed/interrupted build POISONS `test:changed` for that worktree until a human deletes the residue by hand. On a 2-vCPU VM where an interrupted build is normal (see the parallel-bound and detached-run findings), that converts a 30-second per-change gate into a full-suite run that cannot finish here. No cleanup path removes the files on the next run, and they are not ignored.

EVIDENCE (from the lane, at origin/main b90c3c74 after a clean rebase):
- `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists the .dist-stage directories.
- With the residue removed (both owning pids confirmed dead), `node scripts/select-tests.mjs --list` selects 22 files and no longer prints FULL_SUITE.
- The residue was created by two killed builds; `.build.lock.d/owner.json` names the owning pid.

PROPOSED FIX (owner's choice): (a) add `extension/.dist-stage-*/` and `.build.lock.d/` to .gitignore so untracked-residue collection ignores them; and/or (b) have build.mjs remove its own stage directory on exit (including on SIGTERM/SIGKILL paths, best-effort via a trailing cleanup hook), so the next run is not affected. A reviewer should demand a test that simulates a stale residue directory and asserts `test:changed` still selects a subset rather than failing closed.

RELATED, DO NOT CONFLATE: chrome-agent-platform-nco2 (the fail-closed design itself). This bead is the residue trigger; nco2 is the fallback behaviour.

comments.text:
FIXED — cap-beads-nz2r @ e783f5f4 (origin/main fa409e57 + this bead; dev tooling, no bump). Pushed. Worktree ~/worktrees/cap-nz2r.

VERIFY-FIRST, before any edit: planted the residue a killed build leaves (extension/.dist-stage-<pid>-<ts>/chunk.js + .build.lock.d/owner.json) in a fresh worktree and got the bead's exact signature — 'select-tests: FAIL CLOSED — changed file(s) with no reachable test cannot be proved covered by a subset: extension/.dist-stage-99999-…/chunk.js' → 'Running the FULL suite (npm test) instead.' → FULL_SUITE. (git ls-files --others --exclude-standard lists the stage files; the lock file is dropped by the selector's existing dot-prefix rule, which is why the stage dir is the poisoning one.)

TWO LAYERS, because either alone can be defeated:
1. .gitignore: the residue FAMILY git never reports as untracked — extension/.dist-stage-*, .dist-link-*, .dist-prev-*, .build.lock*, .lock-stage-*, .lock-quarantine-*, .owner.tmp-* (the family scripts/evidence-runner.sh already censuses).
2. scripts/select-tests.mjs: new exported isBuildResidue() drops the family from the candidate list structurally, so a stale/bypassed .gitignore cannot poison the gate either.

PINS: tests/select-tests.test.ts — 'nz2r: build scratch is never a changed source file (predicate + ignore rules)': the predicate accepts the whole family and rejects real sources, and 'git check-ignore -q' proves each pattern holds. NEW tests/select-tests-residue.test.ts (SERIAL, with its reason in SERIAL_REASONS — the partition guard accepted it and lists it as a serial hazard): plants a stage dir + lock at the real paths, runs the REAL selector before/with the residue, asserts the residue never appears in the selection and changes nothing about it, then sweeps its own probe and asserts it is gone. It compares the two runs rather than asserting 'not FULL_SUITE' because a worktree with its own uncovered changes may fail closed for those — what must never happen is residue ADDING a failure.

FALSIFIED: mutant A (gitignore removed, predicate kept) — the ignore pin REDS ('…chunk.js must be gitignored (git check-ignore exited 1)') while the residue end-to-end test still PASSES: measured evidence that the predicate alone holds the gate. Mutant B (gitignore + predicate removed = main's behaviour, residue on disk) — BOTH red, the residue test with 'the stage residue leaked into the selection'. Restored: 16 passed / 0 failed across select-tests + select-tests-residue + test-partition-guard.

DELIBERATE NON-CHANGE: build.mjs gets no signal handler. A SIGKILLed process cannot run one; the next successful build already sweeps every stale .dist-stage-*/.dist-link-* (build.mjs:951-963) and a stale lock self-heals by owner-pid liveness (build.mjs:279-293) — so the lasting damage was the gate, which these two layers close. Residue-on-disk-at-kill-time would be a follow-up needing a real behavioural test, not an untested handler.

GATES: npm run test:changed GREEN exit 0 — 23 files [2 serial hazards incl. the new residue test, 21 parallel], serial phase GREEN 2s; both new tests green inside it, with the verify-first residue still on disk and invisible. The probe residue was then deleted; the worktree is clean.

RELATED, NOT CONFLATED: chrome-agent-platform-nco2 (the fail-closed design itself) is untouched.

title: A rejected session/new still clears activeSessionId and the command list
description:
Found while fixing chrome-agent-platform-tliw (a refused session/load kept a phantom session active — fixed on cap-beads-tliw @ 3c07161e). The same 'a rejected request must not leave state behind' principle is NOT yet applied to session/new, and the difference is deliberate-but-undecided rather than obviously right.

MEASURED (extension/lib/acp-client.js newSession, ~186-192):

    this._resetCommands();          // wipes availableCommands, commandsReceived, pendingCommands
    this.activeSessionId = null;    // de-targets in-flight updates from the OLD session
    const result = await this.request('session/new', …);
    … this.activeSessionId = sessionId;

A REFUSED session/new therefore (a) drops an existing live session (leaves the client unattached) and (b) wipes the old session's advertised command list — the caller's session continues to exist on the agent side, but this client no longer reports it. The e2e test cannot see this: in tests/acp-end-to-end.test.ts the client has no prior session, so 'null afterwards' is indistinguishable from 'the prior session was dropped'.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH tliw: for loadSession the failure mode is WRONG (a live-looking id for a session the server never acknowledged, and the notification filter at :541/:545 keeps routing it), so rollback to the previous value is unambiguously correct. For session/new the failure state (not attached) is SAFE but arguably still a mutation-on-failure; restoring the prior session + its commands is a semantics decision: should a failed re-attach leave the old session usable (rollback), or should a refused re-attach mean 'you are detached' (current)? Also, restoring commands needs a snapshot of three fields (_resetCommands), so the shape of the fix follows the ruling.

DONE WHEN: the contract is decided and pinned — either (a) pre-reset values are captured and restored on rejection (with the in-flight de-targeting preserved), plus a test that a refused session/new keeps the prior session and its commands, or (b) the current detach semantics are documented at the call site and pinned by a test that says so on purpose, so nobody 'fixes' it silently later.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main @ 2ffbe342 (v0.3.569). Restores activeSessionId and command list on rejected session/new and malformed response. Focused tests 16/0 green.

title: Settings offers Revoke on All HTTP/HTTPS sites, which come from content_scripts matches and cannot be revoked
description:
Found while screenshotting Settings > Permissions during the independent review of chrome-agent-platform-4p7j.2 (uplift-opus, 2026-09-26). Not part of 4p7j.2's diff: this is main's "Chrome site access" group (chrome-agent-platform-4dg, 4dg.1).

OBSERVED on a stock install (merged tree 5dfe7ec0c; the same code is on main): the group lists "All sites" as "Granted at install" with no Revoke, and "All HTTP sites" and "All HTTPS sites" each with a Revoke button and the text "Revoke asks Chrome to take it back." Screenshot: ~/cap-evidence/review-4p7j.2-opus/settings-permissions-merged.png.

WHY: extension/manifest.json declares host_permissions ["<all_urls>"] and content_scripts matches ["http://*/*", "https://*/*"]. The group reads chrome.permissions.getAll(), which also returns the content-script patterns. siteAccessState (extension/lib/site-access.js) is given only host_permissions as the declared set, so the two content-script patterns land in the revocable list.

CONSEQUENCE (inferred; the click was not driven): content-script patterns are required permissions and chrome.permissions.remove refuses to remove required permissions, so Revoke on either row should only ever fail ("Could not revoke site access to ...").

FIX DIRECTION: include content_scripts[].matches in the declared (fixed) set passed to siteAccessState, beside host_permissions.

ACCEPTANCE: in a real loaded extension the two rows show the install state with no Revoke; an origin granted at runtime still shows a Revoke that works; a unit test pins the classification.

title: cap.fetch POSTs send Origin: chrome-extension://<id> to granted origins
description:
Found in the independent review of chrome-agent-platform-4p7j.2 (uplift-opus, 2026-09-26). Pre-existing in the S0.5 candidate; not a merge regression.

OBSERVED, real loaded extension, merged tree 5dfe7ec0c, with the granted origin logging request headers: a GET through cap.fetch carries no Origin, Referer or Cookie. A POST carries Origin: chrome-extension://<extension id>, over both http and https. Referer and Cookie are never sent. The bead's confused-deputy defaults say to strip "the implied Origin/Referer"; that holds for Referer but not for Origin on POST.

WHY: Origin is a forbidden request header, so fetch() in the service worker cannot drop it. sanitizeRequestHeaders removes only headers the caller set.

IMPACT: low. No credentials travel, but every granted origin learns the extension's id. cap.py's docstring calls requests ANONYMOUS; the Settings help text and the privacy statement's python-fetch line mention only cookies and logins.

FIX DIRECTION: either strip Origin on the proxy's own requests with a declarativeNetRequest session rule (check first that DNR applies to this extension's service-worker fetches), or say in all three owner-facing texts that the extension's identity is sent.

ACCEPTANCE: either a POST through cap.fetch reaches a granted origin with no Origin header, asserted in a real loaded extension, or the three texts name the exposure.

EVIDENCE: ~/cap-evidence/review-4p7j.2-opus/probe-facts.json ("seen").

title: discoverable-tabs-tools: the stale-signal assertion is vacuous — the LRU cap drops the stale entry, so the staleness filter is unpinned
description:
FOUND by the imod bounded mutation census (2026-09-26), entry discovery-stale. NOT fixed there by policy.

OBSERVED: tests/discoverable-tabs-tools.test.ts ('known-WebMCP registry is LRU-bounded and drops stale/zero signals') stays GREEN under a mutant that removes the staleness filter from pruneWebmcpRegistry (extension/lib/webmcp-detection-registry.js: 'now - lastSeen > WEBMCP_REGISTRY_STALE_MS ||' deleted). Control exit 0, mutant exit 0.

WHY IT IS VACUOUS: the test's stale document rides in a WEBMCP_REGISTRY_MAX+5 corpus, and pruneWebmcpRegistry ends with out.sort(...).slice(0, WEBMCP_REGISTRY_MAX). The stale entry has the OLDEST lastSeen, so it is dropped by the LRU CAP in both arms — the assertion entries.some(origin === 'https://stale.example') === false can only fail if the cap drops it, never because of the staleness filter. title: Six harnesses put Chrome's --user-data-dir inside the repo through ${OUT}, which the 9t1b launch-site scan cannot see
description:
Found during the z5ym review (audiofeed-opus). kat-agent-board.ts, kat-composer-slash-commands.ts, kat-fingerprint-surface.ts, kat-settings-cleanliness.ts, kat-task-lifecycle.ts and p0-repro.ts default OUT to `${ROOT}.cache/<name>` and launch Chrome with `--user-data-dir=${OUT}/profile...`. ROOT was checked as the repo root in kat-agent-board, kat-task-lifecycle and p0-repro; the other three follow the same pattern. So by default their live profiles sit inside the working tree, which is what 9t1b exists to prevent (a whole-tree copy races a running browser). The scan in tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts ("no Chrome profile in scripts/ lives inside the repository") flags only values containing ${ROOT}, ROOT}, import.meta.url, ./ or ../, so the OUT indirection passes.
Fix: use chromeProfileDir() at those six sites, and make the scan refuse --user-data-dir built from anything but chromeProfileDir() (or resolve a variable's default). Acceptance: the scan fails on today's six sites before the fix and passes after.

title: a teardown-only generator wedge fails a build whose work already completed — decide what a caller may accept (fnmr follow-on)
description:
FOUND WHILE REVIEWING chrome-agent-platform-fnmr @ 17aac1017, by reproduction rather than
argument. Two live occurrences of the futex hang were recorded on this box 8 minutes apart, and the
record the fnmr fix writes distinguishes them — but nothing decides what a CALLER should do about the
second kind. That decision is Paul's or coord's, not a lane's, so it is filed rather than assumed.

THE TWO SHAPES, both recorded by the new durable record
chrome-agent-platform-fnmr's hang is a shutdown wedge; fnmr's own history already says the pozs
mitigation (explicit process.exit(0), scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs:927-928) did not stop
it, and it did not stop these. From ~/cap-evidence/bounded-child-hangs/hangs.jsonl:

  22:05:01  endedBy=SIGKILL report=none
            stdoutTail="VERIFY OK: 141 generated files byte-identical to the committed tree
                        ⏎ OK: 38 packages, 111 shipped files, 38 manifest identities"
            -> the child FINISHED its work, printed both summary lines, and then wedged exiting.

  22:13:46  endedBy=SIGKILL report=none  stdoutTail="" (empty)
            -> no output at all: hung before finishing, or before flushing. Not the same case.

Same label, same snapshot shape (threads=3, all futex_do_wait), opposite conclusions about whether
the work is trustworthy.

WHY IT NEEDS A DECISION AND NOT A FIX FROM ME
build.mjs runs the generator as `--verify` and treats a non-zero/throwing child as a build failure.
So a shutdown-only wedge, where every generated byte has already been verified and reported, still
fails whatever test happened to be driving the build. Both of my full-suite runs on that tip went red
in the serial phase for exactly this reason: tests/build-tool-bundling.test.ts:92 (p15i reconciliation)
FAILED at 2m2s with a recorded hang, and in the 22:05 case the hang had already printed VERIFY OK —
the build's actual work was complete and correct.

That is not an argument that the child should be ignored. Accepting a killed child is safe for the
first shape and wrong for the second, and the difference is observable only from captured stdout —
which is why bounded-child.mjs now records stdoutTail at all: its own comment says the field exists to
answer "did the child finish its WORK and then fail to exit (a teardown-only hang, which a caller
could accept), or did it hang mid-work (which it cannot)?" The field is written; no caller reads it.

THE QUESTION
  1. Is a teardown-only generator wedge (stdoutTail carries the VERIFY OK and OK: lines, exit was
     forced) something build.mjs should ACCEPT after reaping the group, or always FAIL?
  2. If accept: on what evidence — exact stdout suffix match, or a completion marker the child writes
     as its last act so the decision does not rest on parsing human text?
  3. If always fail: then fnmr's serial-phase consequence stands (any test that spawns --verify can
     go red on a healthy build), and the honest move is to stop the serial files spawning it
     concurrently, or give those files a bigger bound — a different bead, decided knowingly.

Acceptance for whichever way it lands
  - A case per shape: a child that prints completion then hangs must be handled by the chosen rule,
    and a child that hangs with no output must not be mistaken for it. Both must be shown to fail
    before the rule exists, the way fnmr's own review demanded.
  - fnmr's root cause stays separate and unaddressed here on purpose; this bead is about what to do
    with the survivor, not about stopping the wedge.

CONTEXT: chrome-agent-platform-i8qn already owns automating the named-HUNG assertion. This is not
that: i8qn is about proving the error is named, this is about what a caller does once it is.

title: Provider picker test comment says lm-studio has no Settings card, but options.js:217 declares one
description:

WHAT IS WRONG
In tests/provider-public-list.test.ts, the test "provider options: the settings picker source never offers an internal provider" explains why it checks only one direction (lines 65-67 on origin/main): "(The inverse is deliberately not asserted — lm-studio is public but needs no picker card to stay valid.)"

The comment tells the next reader that lm-studio's card is optional. (b) If a public provider with no Settings card is meant to be allowed, keep the one-way check and rewrite the comment without the false example.

The comment states only true facts. For (a), a mutant that deletes the lm-studio card from options.js turns the test red, shown before landing.

SEAMS
tests/provider-public-list.test.ts (the test above); extension/options/options.js (PROVIDERS); extension/lib/provider-visibility.js (publicProviderChoices).

title: webmcp-detect-auth's negative control tests the shape guard, not the snapshot signature — a deleted HMAC check leaves the suite green
description:
Found while reviewing chrome-agent-platform-jy4e (the fixed-100ms-sleep flake). Out of jy4e's scope —
its acceptance says the negative control stays unchanged, and it is — but the control is weaker than
its name suggests, and that predates the flake fix.

WHAT THE TEST DOES TODAY
tests/webmcp-detect-auth.test.ts posts one forged snapshot:
  { __cap_webmcp_detect: 1, type: "snapshot", toolCount: 99 }
before the bootstrap has delivered a nonce. The relay's guard
(extension/content/webmcp-detect-relay.js:47-53) rejects it, but on which clause matters: it has no
`seq`, so `!Number.isInteger(data.seq)` refuses it on SHAPE. The authentication clause
(`data.tag !== await sign(...)`) is never the reason for this payload.

MEASURED — the authentication guard is not covered
Delete the signature check from the relay (`data.tag !== await sign(...)` → `false`) and run the
file: 4 passed / 0 failed, exit 0. A content script that relays any snapshot whose shape parses,
regardless of who signed it, keeps the suite green. Reverted after measuring.

THE GAP IS REAL AND THE FILL IS ONE POSTMESSAGE
Add a second forgery AFTER the genuine relay has landed — i.e. once the relay holds a nonce — with a
well-formed but unsigned payload (`seq: 7, toolCount: 99, tag: "guessed"`), then assert no toolCount 99
in `detections`. Measured both ways on the review worktree:
  product code UNMUTATED + this assertion          → 4 passed / 0 failed (sound; no false alarm)
  signature check removed + this assertion         → FAILED "LATE FORGERY RELAYED" (3 passed / 1 failed)
So it discriminates the regression the current control cannot see, and it does not fail on correct
code.

WHY IT MATTERS, stated without inflation
This is the passive-detection feed the SW uses to learn a page exposes tools. The nonce-only path is
covered (a page that posts before bootstrap is refused on shape); what is untested is the claim that
a page cannot get a snapshot relayed once the relay is authenticated — the case the HMAC tag exists
for. One assertion closes it. Severity is a test-strength gap, not a live product defect: the guard is
in the shipped source and I did not attempt to bypass it in a browser.

Acceptance: the planted unsigned snapshot is refused with the signature check present and accepted
when it is removed; the existing assertions are unchanged; the file stays green in the parallel phase.
Reviewer for the author's work should be a different family than the author's.

title: are enrolled site agents inside the four-surfaces invariant? the picker renders them, the other three project them away
description:
MEASURED-AS-FAR-AS-IT-GOES while working chrome-agent-platform-h97m. Raised there because h97m's
(a)/(b) framing treats the picker's surplus rows as an acp question, and the code says it is not only
acp. This bead asks the general question before a scenario answers it with a red.

THE OBSERVATION
Three surfaces project agents through projectUnifiedAgents(named, enabledBackground)
(extension/options/options.js:2076-2080, extension/ntp/ntp.js:1240 and :1174, the projection itself
at extension/lib/named-agents.js:1123). The side panel's picker instead renders every group the
registry returns (extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.html:189 <agent-picker callable-only> →
extension/shared/components.js:9385 _visibleGroups → filterGroups at
extension/shared/agent-registry.js:93, which takes callableOnly/excludeRef/excludeId/query and no
kind filter at all).

The registry returns FOUR groups (extension/background/service-worker.js:7795-7838): named,
background, site, acp. isCallable passes named and site unconditionally
(extension/shared/agent-registry.js:83 — "enrolled Site Agents are always callable"). So the moment a
profile has an enrolled site agent, the picker carries a row the other three surfaces will not count,
which is structurally the same divergence h97m is about, from a different kind.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY THIS IS NOT A CLAIM ABOUT A FAILURE
I did not observe it. No current journey enrols a site agent and then compares the four surfaces, so
there is no red to point at and no number to quote. It is an inference from the two lines above, and
it is written here as a question, not as a defect. acp's +3 IS measured (constant across fresh,
one-recipe, disabled-again, and 2/2/2-vs-5 in the scheduled scenario); site's contribution is not.

THE QUESTION FOR h97m's DECISION
Are enrolled site agents inside the four-surfaces invariant, or outside it like the harnesses are
proposed to be? Answering "in" means the hub and Settings must list them. Answering "out" means the
projection has to be a filter over kinds and not merely a call over two lists — because the picker
today has no kind filter to apply.

Acceptance
  1. A scenario that enrols a site agent and then measures all four surfaces in the same run, with
     the numbers printed. That converts this from inference to measurement, in whichever direction it
     goes.
  2. The answer recorded in docs where the invariant lives, naming site explicitly. h97m's own
     acceptance already asks for the chosen rule to be written down; this is the same document.
  3. If the answer is "out", the picker needs a real kind filter — not a site-specific special case
     bolted next to the acp one, which is how this ends up as three bugs wearing a coat.

title: a wall-clock assertion inside the timeout guard itself flakes under fleet load: tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts:80 sleeps 3.5s against a 6s scaled bound and runs in the parallel phase
description:
Found on the first full-suite run of chrome-agent-platform-i1i9's candidate (cap/qwen-i1i9-pure-import
@ 3635c992f), where it was the only red: 4506 passed / 1 failed. The second full run of the same tree
was green (4507 / 0). Nothing in that diff reaches this file's code path — its only load change is one
test file moving from the serial phase into the parallel phase.

THE TEST
  tests/serial-phase-timeout.test.ts:80
  "86gg: the SAME slow file is killed by the flat bound and survives the scaled one"

It writes a fixture that sleeps 3.5 s, asserts a 2 s flat bound KILLS it, then asserts a 6 s scaled
bound (`serialFileTimeoutMs({ base: 2_000, loadPerCpu: 3 })`) lets it finish. Both halves are
wall-clock assertions; the second has 2.5 s of headroom and runs in the PARALLEL phase.

MEASURED
- red run: machine load average 74 (1 min) at the time of the failure, 482 parallel files in flight.
- same file alone, on the same tree, minutes later: PASS in 7 s (6 passed / 0 failed).
- second full `npm test` on the same tree: PASS, suite green.
So it is intermittent and load-correlated, not a product defect in the timeout machinery — the
mechanism it tests (scaled bounds) worked; the 3.5 s fixture just did not finish inside 6 s of a
box running 74 runnable threads.

WHY IT IS STILL A DEFECT
The repo already holds the rule for this: a suite must not depend on ambient state it does not
create, and wall-clock queueing assertions are exactly what the 32-worker parallel phase makes
flaky — which is the stated reason tests/chrome-slot-semaphore-honesty.test.ts is declared SERIAL.
This file makes the same shape of assertion and is NOT declared. A flake in a timeout test is the
worst place to have one: the next lane reads a red in the timeout guard and re-runs, or worse,
believes a scaled-bound regression is real when it is the box.

FIX DIRECTION (pick one, do not invent a third that keeps the clock)
- Declare it SERIAL with the reason "wall-clock bounds assertions (3.5 s fixture vs 2 s / 6 s
  bounds) race the parallel phase", matching chrome-slot-semaphore-honesty's precedent. Costs one
  serial file; buys determinism.
- Or remove the dependency on wall time: the flat-bound kill and the scaled-bound survival are both
  properties of `serialFileTimeoutMs` and the runner's kill path. The arithmetic can be pinned
  without a sleeping child, and the kill path can be pinned with a fixture that HANGS (already done
  by the test above this one, which is not flaky) rather than one that merely takes 3.5 s.
- Whichever: do not widen the bound. Widening makes the test pass and keeps the flake, just rarer.

NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH: chrome-agent-platform-cejm (Delegation KAT intermittently failing on a
settling registry CAS error) — that is a race in product state, this is a clock assertion against
an unloaded box. Also not chrome-agent-platform-2bli (the suite's own parallel load making the
quiet-window sample refuse) — same family of cause, different mechanism, and that one already has
an owner.

title: webmcp-realsite-probe: the site half no longer reproduces — beads.gascity.com registers zero tools under the shim, so the probe's invoke/diagnostics steps cannot run
description:
FOUND during chrome-agent-platform-9uho (2026-09-25, uiflash), filed by coord's ruling. NOT a blocker for 9uho, and NOT a product claim: the probe's diagnostics half is fixed and driven on branch `verify/9uho-diagnostics-gate` @ e7623b29ac; this is the OTHER half of the same probe run.

WHAT IS OBSERVED (origin/main 27cf212d7, `deno run -A scripts/webmcp-realsite-probe.ts`, same result before and after the 9uho fix):
  FAIL: the site's REAL registration ran under the shim (search_docs present page-side) — null
  FAIL: hub: clicked Discover this page via a real click — undefined
  probe diagnostics: {"detectHook":"function(randomized)","pageToolCount":0,"offers":"{\"ok\":true,\"offers\":[],\"needScripting\":false,\"candidateTabs\":1}","pickerRows":[]}
  FAIL: the production invoke path reaches the site's REAL handler — {"ok":false,"error":"origin https://beads.gascity.com is not enrolled"}
  probe-evidence.json: siteRegisteredTools: [], pageConsole: [], invokeResult: {ok:false, error: "... is not enrolled"}

RULED OUT, so the next reader does not redo it: the site is REACHABLE (HTTP 200 in 0.45s at the time of filing); the extension loads and the service worker is present; the modelContext shim IS installed (the probe prints PASS "real site loaded with (shimmed) document.modelContext present"); and the diagnostics gate that gates the page-side console capture is now ON (9uho fix). The failure is that the SITE's own registration never runs: zero registered tools, an empty hub picker (`offers: []`, `pickerRows: []`), no page console output at all.

TWO CANDIDATE CAUSES, both cheap to distinguish (this is the whole next step):
  (a) THE SITE CHANGED. beads.gascity.com is Mintlify; the probe's premise is that it registers tools only when a native API already exists. Its current bundle may no longer register at all, may have moved to `navigator.modelContext` rather than `document.modelContext`, or may gate on another member of the surface. The static HTML carries no `modelContext`/`registerTool` string (weak evidence — the app is JS-driven), and `detectHook: "function(randomized)"` shows SOMETHING did look for the API.
  (b) THE SHIM'S SURFACE IS NO LONGER FAITHFUL. The shim is "webmcp-tools-shaped" from the era of ajcc; if Mintlify's registration now expects a different shape (registerTool signature, provides/description fields, an inventory read-back such as `getTools()` semantics, or an event), registration silently no-ops in exactly this way.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE: capture the site's own bundle/console at document_start and answer (a) vs (b) with a page-side probe (the probe already has the CDP plumbing; a scriptParsed+source scan for modelContext/registerTool, or an instrumentation shim that logs which member was touched, settles it). Then either repair the probe's shim/site assumption and re-run to a green invoke (the probe's original purpose: show a failed invoke carrying its honest cause), or, if the site genuinely no longer registers, retire the site half — the probe's header already says it fails honestly when the site is unreachable or changed, and a diagnosis artifact with a dead premise is worse than one with a named one.

RELATED: chrome-agent-platform-9uho (the diagnostics half, fixed: the probe opened `options.html` with no hash, the `#agents` panel was hidden, the toggle's rect was 0x0, and the click went to (0,0)); chrome-agent-platform-ajcc (the probe's original defect); chrome-agent-platform-0lb4 (a CDP evaluate helper that turns a page-side throw into an unexplained value — the same FAILURE MODE, not the same helper; the probe has its own local evalIn).

title: Service worker ships the SDK's SERVER-side zod->JSON-schema path (~2.4KB) reached only through the client import chain
description:
MEASURED during the independent review of chrome-agent-platform-mx1g (2026-09-25), while verifying that review's 2,460-byte figure.

OBSERVATION: extension/background/service-worker.js emits 2,460 preminify bytes from zod-to-json-schema (78 files reached), and also emits @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/server/zod-compat.js and server/zod-json-schema-compat.js. CAP never imports the SDK server API: `git grep -n "sdk/server" -- extension/ shared/` returns nothing. The shipped code path is client-only (extension/lib/mcp-client.js:29-33 -> client/index.js, client/streamableHttp.js, client/sse.js).

CHAIN (verified against the installed SDK 1.30.0): client/index.js -> ../shared/protocol.js (shared/protocol.js:4 imports ../server/zod-json-schema-compat.js) -> zod-json-schema-compat.js -> zod-to-json-schema. A server-side compat module, and its converter dependency, are dragged into the service worker by an SDK-internal edge leaving the one module CAP actually uses. server/mcp.js is NOT in the bundle, so this is the single server subtree that leaks.

WHY IT MATTERS: mx1g's byte figure is real, but it is not a cost of keeping two peer contexts - it is dead weight in the shipped bundle. The project has an active Store service-worker budget line (chrome-agent-platform-ycez), so ~2.4KB of unreachable converter deserves either removal or an explicit protected-by-reason record.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) confirm the chain still holds on the current SDK - a later release may split the compat import lazily; (2) then either (a) cut it, e.g. an esbuild alias/stub for server/zod-json-schema-compat.js in the browser build IF nothing on the client path calls parseWithCompat/getMethodLiteral at runtime, proven by a build-level test that fails if a live client call is stubbed, or (b) record in docs/RISK-REGISTER.md and the bundle budget that the 2,460 bytes is intentional-unavoidable, naming the SDK edge as the reason; (3) either way, re-anchor tests/mcp-zod-peer-parity.test.ts's exact-byte assertion in the same change and make its failure message say why the number can move.

DO NOT weaken mx1g's parity tests as part of this - they are the evidence that the peers must stay separate. Verify any stub against real client journeys, not a 200.
close_reason: CLOSED AS OPTION (b): RECORD, NOT CUT (coord's call 2026-10-06; the cut stays described below for anyone who takes it later, with its own bead and its own verification). THE RECORD: the SHIPPED SW carries ONE converter copy - 177 bytes across 3 files (zod-to-json-schema Options.js 83 + index.js 0 + parsers/string.js 94) - reached by exactly one chain: SW -> extension/lib/mcp-client.js -> @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/index.js -> shared/protocol.js -> server/zod-json-schema-compat.js -> zod-to-json-schema/dist/esm/index.js. So it is reachable (NOT unreachable dead weight) but NEVER CALLED: the converter's only user is toJsonSchemaCompat, whose only callers are in server/mcp.js (which the SW graph does not contain), and protocol.js imports only parseWithCompat + getMethodLiteral, neither of which touches the converter. It ships anyway because zod-to-json-schema's package.json declares NO sideEffects field, so esbuild cannot drop the compat module's unused top-level import. CORRECTED FIGURES (recorded, and the 3337 landing note is amended): 2,460 bytes / 78 files was the audit's configuration (no carrier fix, no SDK dedup); 354 bytes / 6 files is the mcp pin's configuration (carrier fix, no SDK dedup - the pin omits build.mjs's capAiSdkDedup); 177 bytes / 3 files / ONE copy is the shipped bundle (carrier fix + SDK dedup). The two-peer-context-copies reframe is therefore FALSE for the shipped bundle - it is a property of the pin's graph, and the SDK instance is already deduped. WHY NOT CUT (recorded rationale): 177 bytes is ~0.007% of an SW that just gained ~2.3 KB of headroom from chrome-agent-platform-3337; the root fix is UPSTREAM (zod-to-json-schema should declare sideEffects:false); and the available local cut (mark the package side-effect-free on resolve so esbuild drops the unused import - behaviour cannot change because nothing in the SW graph calls it) touches the SHARED bundle config and would demand byte-identity + per-bundle + full serial-phase re-verification. The instrument defects found while measuring this were filed separately as chrome-agent-platform-bvj5 (the pin measures a non-shipped graph while its name reads as the shipped figure; and it cannot build without a pre-built extension/dist). Measurement method: the REAL build's .build/bundle-report.json (build.mjs's SW metafile), walked for forward reachability and import edges - not a scratch build. Coord is flagging the cut-or-record call upstream so Paul can overrule.

title: quiet-window's permissive-launch phase reds when the sample is UNMEASURABLE (permissive thresholds cannot rescue a truncated /proc scan) — 2bli's sibling
description:
FOUND while gating `chrome-agent-platform-4lc0` revise 4 (unrelated to it), and it is a SIBLING of `2bli` with the same root cause but a different assertion — so `2bli`'s fix does not cover it.

THE CHECK: `mkax: the launcher refuses to START the browser when the box is not quiet` (tests/quiet-window.test.ts:424).

MECHANISM, and it is a design interplay rather than a plain flake: the test has two phases. Phase 1 stages an impossible threshold and expects a refusal — that passed. Phase 2 passes an **impossibly permissive** spec (`maxLoadPerCore: 1e9, maxCompilers: 1e9, maxWaitMs: 2000`) and expects the launcher to **LAUNCH**. But permissive thresholds cannot rescue an **UNMEASURABLE** sample: under the parallel phase's own churn the /proc walk truncated (*"proc scan truncated after 796 entries in 401 ms (budget 4096 entries / 400 ms)"*), 1io9's fail-closed refusal fired, and `launchChrome` threw **uncaught** at tests/quiet-window.test.ts:454 — so the test reddened for a reason that says nothing about the tree.

EVIDENCE: it passes alone in **390 ms** (load1 25.33); `2bli` fixed the *sample* test in the same file by scoping a deliberate scan budget, and this test needs the same treatment for its phase-2 launch expectation. Recorded beside the 4lc0 candidate rather than attributed to it.

ACCEPTANCE: phase 2 either takes a deliberate scan budget for the duration of its permissive-launch assertion (the operator remedy the refusal message names), or treats an unmeasurable sample as INCONCLUSIVE-with-cause rather than a red. The property must be preserved: phase 1's refusal (an impossible threshold does refuse) and phase 2's `quietWaitMs < 2000` must both still mean what they say, and the "browser was NEVER started" assertion must stay.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
chrome-agent-platform-r2ai: a truncated /proc walk is retried with room, and still refuses if that fails

THE DEFECT (filed by this lane, reproduced twice more since): quiet-window's permissive-launch phase
reddened when the sample was UNMEASURABLE. Permissive thresholds cannot rescue a truncated /proc
walk — an unmeasurable box is a refusal by 1io9's contract, deliberately — and the suite's OWN
parallel churn is enough to trip the 400 ms budget (measured repeatedly: "proc scan truncated after
796 entries in 406 ms (budget 4096 entries / 400 ms)"). Two tests asserted a measurable box:
`mkax: the launcher refuses to START the browser when the box is not quiet` (its phase 2 passes an
impossibly permissive spec and expects a LAUNCH) and the sibling fixed earlier in 2bli.

FIX, library-side, with the safety property intact:
  * `readLoadSample` is now a wrapper over `readLoadSampleOnce(prev, budget)`. When the first walk
    truncates it retries ONCE with 4x the budget — still bounded — because a truncated walk is not a
    property of the box when the suite's own load trips a 400 ms budget;
  * if the retry truncates too, the sample is STILL unmeasurable and the error now names both
    attempts, so a reader knows the budgets were exhausted rather than just the first;
  * the evidence field `retriedAfterTruncation` says when the retry is what produced the sample.
  * the test's permissive phase now treats an unmeasurable refusal as INCONCLUSIVE-with-cause (the
    retry makes it rare; when it happens the test says so instead of reddening), and every other
    refusal still reds.

blocking, and not in jy4e's scope.

2. The timeout names the condition. With the relay dropped entirely (the SW's webmcp.detected never

The remaining exposure is that the test now waits instead of asserting a fixed interval has elapsed.

title: The suite's own parallel load makes the quiet-window sample refuse, so mkax's measurability assertion reds for an unrelated change
description:
FOUND while validating an unrelated change (`chrome-agent-platform-w6wo`, the emscripten probe leftover): `npm test` reddened in the parallel phase on a check with no connection to that change.

THE CHECK: `mkax: a real sample from this box is finite, bounded and evidence-shaped` — tests/quiet-window.test.ts:410, asserting `readLoadSample().measurable === true`.

THE FAILURE, verbatim: `this box is measurable: proc scan truncated after 912 entries in 404 ms (budget 4096 entries / 400 ms) — the builder count is INCOMPLETE, so this sample is NOT a quiet verdict; raise CAP_QUIET_MAX_PROC_SCAN(_MS) deliberately if this box really has that many processes (chrome-agent-platform-1io9)`.

WHY IT REDS, and this is the awkward part: the refusal is CORRECT — 1io9 made a truncated /proc walk a refusal rather than a quiet box, and the parallel phase (478 test files, each spawning children) is itself enough process churn to exceed the 400 ms scan budget. So the suite's OWN load makes the box unmeasurable, and a test that asserts measurability reds for a reason that says nothing about the tree. Measured: the same check passes alone in 54 ms with load1 = 63.93 and 1092 /proc entries — i.e. it is process churn *during the parallel phase*, not steady load, that trips the budget.

ACCEPTANCE (pick the one that keeps the property honest):
1. The check states the property it actually tests — that a sample CAN be taken here — by giving itself a deliberate scan budget (e.g. CAP_QUIET_MAX_PROC_SCAN_MS raised for this test only, which the refusal message itself suggests), so the assertion is about sampleability and not about the budget constant; OR
2. it treats a scan-budget refusal as an explicit INCONCLUSIVE-with-cause (a line naming the refusal, the budget, and that the box was unmeasurable under self-inflicted load) rather than a red — the same shape the fleet already uses for environmental refusals.

MUST STAY RED: a *genuinely* unmeasurable box (a scan that fails for a real reason, e.g. an unreadable /proc) must still not report measurable: true — the refusal path itself is the 1io9 property and must keep its tests.

NOT THIS BEAD: the quiet-window design or 1io9's refusal — both are correct. This is about a load-sensitive assertion owned by neither.
close_reason: Work already on origin/main: resolved in commit 8d624f197c34b3f55a2024767c293b81a6b58b3a (chrome-agent-platform-r2ai); scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts retries /proc scan with 4x budget under test churn citing 2bli, and tests/quiet-window.test.ts handles unmeasurable sample as INCONCLUSIVE and pins CAP_QUIET_MAX_PROC_SCAN_MS.

title: [bug] Hub agent header: a named-agent.list correction that lands before openAgentSurface's history await is overwritten by the stale name
description:
FOUND while building the 32yz execution coverage. NOT reproduced in a real browser — filed as an ordering QUESTION with its measurement, not as a confirmed product defect, and deliberately not asserted in tests/ntp-agent-route-execution.test.ts.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (Deno, house DOM + chrome stub, real extension/ntp/ntp.js executed):
openAgentSurface has TWO writers of the agent header.
  • :2714-2723 — the named-agent.list callback: if a.name differs from threadTitle.textContent it corrects BOTH the header and history.state.
  • :2752-2758 — after 'const history = await loadAgentSurfaceHistory(kind, id)', the function unconditionally assigns 'threadTitle.textContent = name || \"Agent\"', where 'name' is the value the CALLER passed in.
When the list reply arrives BEFORE that await settles, the callback's correction is applied and then OVERWRITTEN by the stale caller-supplied name. Measured with a microtask-speed stub reply: TITLE ended \"ZZZ Stale History Name\" while history.state.name was \"ZZZ Fresh Persisted Name\" — the two surfaces DISAGREED, header stale, history fresh. With a 40 ms reply the correction survives and both read fresh.

WHY THIS MIGHT NOT BE REAL, stated plainly: a microtask-speed sendMessage reply is a stub artefact. But 'impossible in a browser' is a claim I have NOT verified, and the ordering is not obviously unreachable: named-agent.list is issued FIRST (:2714) while the history read is issued later (:2752), so the list winning the race is plausible. Both are IPC.

WHY IT MAY BE UNREACHABLE ANYWAY: the divergence only matters when named-agent.get and named-agent.list DISAGREE about the name. In the product's own flow both read the same store, so a disagreement needs a stale cache or an in-flight rename landing between the two reads.

ACCEPTANCE (whichever way it resolves):
1. DECIDE by measurement, not by reading: drive ntp.html in a real loaded extension, rename a named agent so get and list can disagree, and observe whether the header can end stale while history.state is fresh. tests/agent-header-rename-reload.test.ts already has the browser harness and the rename flow to extend.
2. If reachable: the post-await assignment must not clobber a NEWER correction — e.g. skip the assignment when the header already holds a name the list resolved for this same agent id, or have the callback record the resolved name and have :2758 prefer it.
3. If unreachable: record WHY (the measured ordering that makes it impossible) and close. Do not 'fix' an ordering that cannot occur.
4. Either way the guard belongs in tests/ntp-agent-route-execution.test.ts, which already isolates the two paths and carries a listDelayMs knob for exactly this.

NOT A REGRESSION IN 32yz'S WORK: 32yz's tests pass on main and kill three mutants; this is a question its harness surfaced, held separately so a green suite does not imply the question was answered.
