comments.text:
CANDIDATE: branch cap/7zf0-agent-header @ 471e444f7c80728e451bcb1d9fcdb9a30c2018a2.
Triage & fix: triaged visible name mismatch after rename & reload in real147 AFTER 04.
Root cause: openAgentSurface only navigated route if location.hash !== hash (not on name changes), keeping stale name in history.state. On reload, applyNtpHashRoute trusted meta.name from history.state without fetching named-agent.get for named agents, and openAgentSurface's asynchronous named-agent.list callback updated only conversation identity but never threadTitle.
Fix:
1. openAgentSurface synchronizes history.state via navigateNtpRoute when name changes on the same hash.
2. openAgentSurface named-agent.list callback updates threadTitle.textContent and history.state when a.name differs.
3. applyNtpHashRoute resolves named-agent.get for named agents, preferring live persisted name over stale meta.name.
4. revalidateOpenAgent updates history.state when found.name changes.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW (deepseek-v4-flash; the author was antigravity/gemini, so a different family). Branch cap/7zf0-agent-header @ 471e444f.

VERDICT: PASS on behaviour and land-ability. The fix is correct and I DROVE it. The branch's regression test does not falsify behaviour and must be replaced before this bead is closed.

WHAT I DROVE (real headless Chrome, the shipped bundle, my own worktree, TWO builds):
Sequence: seed a named agent -> set a history entry carrying the OLD name (the precondition the real UI produces when opening an agent from the hub) -> reload -> rename via named-agent.update -> reload -> read #thread-title.
- MAIN (fix absent): header = "ZZZ Original Name" while the registry already held "ZZZ Renamed Name"  => THE REPORTED DEFECT, REPRODUCED.
- BRANCH (fix applied): header = "ZZZ Renamed Name", history.state.name = "ZZZ Renamed Name"  => FIXED.
- Control in BOTH runs: named-agent.get returned the NEW name, so the stale header is the UI defect, not a failed write.
- History interleaving: history.length 2 -> 2 across rename+reload (no growth; back/forward intact), and forward restored the FRESH name.
Same drive against two builds produced different results, which is the evidence the builds really were different code.

THE CENTRAL FINDING (blocks the bead's acceptance, not the merge): the author reported "reverted-fix RED -> restored GREEN". I reverted ONLY extension/ntp/ntp.js to main and re-ran the new test: 3 passed | 1 failed. The only responding test is the source pin. The three tests named "behavioral" re-implement the logic INLINE and assert on their own re-implementation; they never touch ntp.js and CANNOT fail on a regression. So the RED is a text-presence red, not a behaviour red. The bead requires "a regression that fails on old behavior and passes after real Save/reload" - not satisfied. The handoff also carries no evidence path and no pre-fix state.
Systemic context: NO test in this repo EXECUTES extension/ntp/ntp.js - 68+ files source-scan it via Deno.readTextFile, and the closest sibling (agent-deletion-navigate.test.ts) has the identical source-pin + inline-simulation shape. The branch follows the house pattern; the house pattern is the defect. The driven sequence above is the missing regression.

- revalidateOpenAgent's doc comment still reads "A rename just updates the title" while the fix now also navigates there - comment/code divergence.
- applyCurrentHashRoute inlines openAgentChat's named-agent.get -> openAgentSurface body instead of calling it; the same sequence now exists twice and can drift.
- The background-kind half of the fix is untested (0 background assertions in the new test). Its stale-name precondition looks unreachable via the routes (background agents derive from recipes; background-agent.set only enables/disables), so I did not drive it.
- PRE-EXISTING, not this branch: applyCurrentHashRoute passes { pushHistory: false } to openAgentSurface / openBackgroundAgentChat / openThread / openView, whose signatures do not accept it. Harmless today only because navigateNtpRoute replaces inside an agent view.

GATES: 488 files matches the author's report. My full npm test exited 1 on tests/build-tool-bundling.test.ts:136 - "build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs --verify HUNG: no exit within 120s (wchan=futex_do_wait)". ENVIRONMENTAL, named and proven: the same file passes in isolation in 219ms (7 passed | 0 failed), this branch touches nothing in that pipeline, and bead chrome-agent-platform-fnmr already tracks this exact futex hang. Not a product red. title: The quiet-window harness pins are satisfied by their own import bindings — re-anchor the refusal handler they name
description:
Carved out of chrome-agent-platform-wzez (CLOSED, census delivered and independently verified) as the
audit's actionable tail. Coord assignment 2026-09-07 21:59Z: "take the 3 DEFEATABLE quiet-window
re-anchors as your bead (small, closes the class)". Owner: qwen (01a07d6e). Sequenced AFTER
chrome-agent-platform-c9y8's verdict — this bead touches tests/quiet-window.test.ts only, so there is
no file overlap with c9y8, but the guard extension is what makes these three pins visible to the
committed guard, so landing order matters for the story even if not for the merge.

THE FINDING (census row, mutation-confirmed as mutant W2). Three source-text pins in
tests/quiet-window.test.ts, inside the loop at :327 that walks the harnesses declaring themselves
load-sensitive:

    const src = Deno.readTextFileSync(`${ROOT}scripts/${file}`);
    assert(src.includes("QuietWindowRefusedError"),      `${file} must handle the refusal`);        // :328
    assert(src.includes("ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT"),   `${file} must exit with the environmental code`); // :329
    assert(src.includes("ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER"), `${file} must print the marker line`);     // :330

The loop currently has exactly ONE member: `declared` is
`Object.entries(HARNESSES).filter(([, e]) => e.loadSensitive !== undefined)` over
scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts, and only `"chrome-journeys.ts"` declares loadSensitive (verified by
hand at 4c89bd9d — harness-registry.ts:65 is the single occurrence). So all three pins judge
scripts/chrome-journeys.ts, where each token occurs exactly TWICE: once as an import binding at
:34-36 and once in live code at :136-139.

That makes all three DEFEATABLE on the census ladder: live > 0 and shadow > 0, so deleting the live
construct leaves the import behind and the pin stays green.

PROVEN, NOT INFERRED (mutant W2, house discipline, restored + re-hashed + empty git status):
delete the five-line refusal handler at scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:136-140 —

    if (e instanceof QuietWindowRefusedError) {
      console.error(e.message);
      console.error(`${ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER} ${JSON.stringify(e.sample)}`);
      Deno.exit(ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT);
    }

leaving `throw e;` and the three imports. Each token drops from 2 occurrences to 1 (import only).
`deno check --no-lock scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` reports 625 errors both at baseline and with the
mutant, i.e. no new syntax or type error (esbuild is unusable in this environment — rc=1 at baseline
too — recorded rather than hidden). Result: tests/quiet-window.test.ts went 13/0 -> 12 passed / 1
FAILED.

THE IMPORTANT HALF: the kill came from :347 "mkax: the REAL journey gate refuses with exit 75 under
artificial load" — an EXECUTING gate that runs the real harness under artificial load and asserts the
environmental exit code. The test that HOLDS the three substring pins, "mkax: load-sensitive harnesses
DECLARE themselves, and the declaration is honoured in source", PASSED with the handler deleted. So the
property is NOT a live hole, and this bead is hygiene, not firefighting: three pins that name a safety
property (an environmental refusal must reach a THIRD exit code with a greppable marker, never be
re-read as a product red) cannot see the deletion of the construct they name, and are backstopped only
by a slower, load-dependent, Chrome-launching gate.

Lesson recorded on wzez and worth repeating here: DEFEATABLE means "a shadow can satisfy this pin",
NOT "this feature is deletable". Only a whole-suite mutant separates those, which is why this bead
exists at P3 and not P2.

WHAT TO DO. Re-anchor the three pins on the CONSTRUCT, parsed rather than grepped, following the shape
ecke landed for bundled-inventory-data (816aae8e) and uodl landed for recordServerToolUsage /
buildTemplateSelect:

1. Pin the handler SHAPE, not the three words: the refusal must be caught by type, must print the
   marker, and must exit with the environmental code — e.g. a single anchored regex over the catch
   body covering `instanceof QuietWindowRefusedError` … `ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER` …
   `Deno.exit(ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT)`, or three assertions each anchored on its own construct
   (the instanceof test, the marker print statement, the exit call) rather than on the bare identifier.
2. KEEP IT GENERIC. The assertion runs once per member of `declared`, and a second harness can declare
   itself load-sensitive at any time, so the anchor must describe the required shape (catch the typed
   refusal, print the marker, exit with the code) and must not hardcode chrome-journeys.ts's
   surrounding lines. A pin that only matches today's single member is a pin that silently stops
   covering the next one.
3. Decide explicitly whether the three bare-word pins stay as provenance (the ecke/template-cards
   precedent) or are replaced. If they stay, they stay DEFEATABLE by construction and the committed
   guard will not flag them (live > 0), so say which it is in a comment rather than leaving both nets
   ambiguous.
4. Note for whoever implements: regex literals carrying a backtick or a quote are safe here — the
   guard tokenises regex literals properly (that was the audit's defect #5, and 222 regexes across 21
   target files depend on it).

ACCEPTANCE.
* Mutant W2 RE-RUN and killed BY THE PINS: with the five-line handler deleted, the test that holds
  them — "mkax: load-sensitive harnesses DECLARE themselves, and the declaration is honoured in
  source" — must FAIL, not merely the executing exit-75 gate at :347. Name the killing assertion and
  its message in the report, per house discipline.
* The restored tree must go green again (13/0), with the pristine hash of scripts/chrome-journeys.ts
  re-verified (4f8c205f2e1862d67c1c57799e58e9e3ed38fc9f33dc373865038f4d2aec1272 at 4c89bd9d) and an
  empty `git status --porcelain`.
* Generality proven, not asserted: a second mutant that adds a FAKE harness member declaring
  loadSensitive without the handler shape must be caught by the re-anchored pin, or the pin must be
  documented as single-member-only with the reason. Otherwise the re-anchor is a pin on today's file

mutation-results.json (both mutants, full discipline record), census-attribution.json rows for

  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)/                                                  -> "must catch the refusal BY TYPE — an import binding is not a handler"
  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)[\s\S]{0,400}?ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER/        -> "must print the greppable marker from inside the refusal handler"

No Chrome run from a spaced checkout has been performed; this is a source-level portability finding, not an observed browser gate RED or execution escape. title: Census the 203 unattributed source-text substring pins — population count, not fixes
description:
Follow-up carved out of chrome-agent-platform-uodl, which is complete and landed. SCOPE IS A CENSUS, NOT A FIX CAMPAIGN. The uodl audit attributed 654 source-text .includes(X) pins to a target file and adjudicated them; 203 further source-like .includes calls were NOT attributed and are absent from every number the audit reported. They reach their variable through a helper function, a destructured return, or an interpolation the scanner declines to guess. This is the audit's honest boundary and the largest remaining coverage hole: the true population is bigger than 654, so any claim of the form 'the repo has N weak substring pins' is currently unbounded from below.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD. uodl's acceptance forbade mass-rewriting the corpus, and its findings were proven by mutation one at a time. Extending attribution is a different kind of work: it is measurement, and it must not become a rewrite. Splitting it keeps that boundary explicit.

WHAT TO DO.
1. Extend attribution in cap-evidence/uodl/scan-substring-pins.py to cover helper-wrapped reads (a function that returns Deno.readTextFile(...) whose result is then .includes()'d), destructured returns, and the remaining interpolation forms. Attribute only what can be resolved WITHOUT GUESSING; keep declining anything ambiguous and keep counting it.
2. Re-run and report the census: how many of the 203 become attributed, how many remain unresolvable, and the classification breakdown of the newly attributed set under the existing LIVE-vs-SHADOW ladder.
3. Adjudicate any new VACUOUS rows by INTENT before calling them defects (cap-evidence/uodl/analyze-vacuous.py and its REVIEWED table are the worked example). A shadow-only occurrence count is an OBSERVATION, not a verdict: a pin can be about the shadow on purpose, e.g. a keep-in-sync pointer, and an import-only pin whose sibling asserts the call site is covered.
4. Mutation-confirm only rows that survive intent adjudication. House discipline: pristine snapshot, one targeted edit per mutant, restore plus re-hash plus empty git status after each, node --check on .js targets, stage 1 the pin's own file, stage 2 the full npm test for every survivor.

CRITICAL TRAPS, all paid for already on uodl.
- The mask MUST tokenise regex literals. 222 regexes across 21 target files carry a quote or backtick in a character class and a naive span scan reads them as string delimiters; that corrupted 75% of pins before it was fixed. Use cap-evidence/uodl/jstoken.py (33 unit tests) or the port already committed in tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts.
- Mask the TEST file too, or the scanner matches pins quoted inside comments that document a previous fix.
- An export DECLARATION is live, not an import shadow. Only a bare import or a re-export shadows.
- A thrown error's message is LIVE (error codes, fixture payloads, refusals). Only console.* narration is a shadow.
- tests/security-suite-custody.test.ts flocks the machine-global /tmp/cap-serialized-chrome-acceptance.lock on a 20s self-timed budget, so a concurrent lane running Chrome KATs can red it for everyone. Its failure is NOT a kill. Run stage 2 for a survivor with no Chrome-launching stage 1 before it.
- The committed guard tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts fails when a source-text .includes(X) pin has no live occurrence of X. Any newly attributed pin that is genuinely vacuous will trip it, so the census and the guard must stay consistent: either the pin is re-anchored, or it goes on the guard's allowlist with an adjudicated reason.

ACCEPTANCE. A written census: how many of the 203 are now attributed, how many remain unresolvable and why, the classification breakdown of the newly attributed set, and an intent adjudication for every new VACUOUS row. Mutation confirmation for any row that survives adjudication. NO mass rewrite — the guard and the allowlist are the durable mechanism, not bulk edits. State the residual unresolvable population plainly rather than silently dropping it.

Carved out of chrome-agent-platform-uodl (complete, commit 991bf5e2 on cap-launch-sweep-r2, gates green, handed to merger). Reusable tooling and evidence in cap-evidence/uodl: jstoken.py (the tokeniser — regex literals, newline-bounded quotes, ${} interp) with test-jstoken.py + test-scan-extract.py both ALL PASS; scan-substring-pins.py (scanner, defects #1-#11 fixed); analyze-vacuous.py (intent adjudication with a REVIEWED verdict table); mutate-uodl.py / prove-kills.py / prove-u2.py / custody-flake-check.py (mutation harnesses with restore+re-hash+clean-tree discipline); INVENTORY.md (1341-line severity-ranked findings) plus findings-pre-fix/ and post-fix/ snapshots. The committed guard is tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts, allowlist keyed testFile::target::token so line drift cannot break it. INTENT ADJUDICATION of every non-SOUND row (acceptance item 3): 1 DEFECT CANDIDATE
(bundled-tool-packages:317 `bundled-inventory-data`, IMPORT-ONLY — the message claims "the preview

-> scripts/chrome-journeys.ts, import shadow at :34-36 + live refusal handler at :136-139); 3

context) {`, `lockMarker: "CAP_CHROME_GATE_ACQUIRED",`); 4 unclassifiable-without-a-build (pins on
GENERATED output extension/dist/background/service-worker.js — a class of its own, since in a bundle
comments/imports are build decisions); 1 statically unclassifiable (a backtick token containing
${value}).

MUTATION CONFIRMATION (acceptance item 4), house discipline, both restored + re-hashed + empty git
status, worktrees removed:
* W1 (the IMPORT-ONLY row) = LIVE HOLE. Delete the single line `inventory: BUNDLED_INVENTORY,` at
  service-worker.js:6667; node --check OK; stage 1 the pin's own test PASSES (2/0 filtered run);
  stage 2 npm test rc=0 3999 passed / 0 failed — BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pristine baseline (3999/0,
  424 files, 115s vs 113s). Third instance of the uodl class and the first found in the unattributed
  population, i.e. invisible to the 654-pin audit by construction. Filed as
  chrome-agent-platform-ecke (P2, deps discovered-from:wzez) with the re-anchor recipe and the
  dist.complete-staleness trap (21/2 in the unfiltered file run is NOT a kill: the full suite's serial
  build phase re-indexes the mutated source first).
* W2 (the 3 DEFEATABLE rows) = KILLED at stage 1, so the property is NOT a hole. Delete the 5-line
  refusal handler at scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:136-140 leaving the imports: each token drops 2 -> 1
  occurrence (import only); deno check 625 errors at baseline AND mutant (no new error; esbuild is
  unusable here — rc=1 at baseline too, recorded not hidden); tests/quiet-window.test.ts -> 12 passed
  / 1 FAILED, killed by :347 "mkax: the REAL journey gate refuses with exit 75 under artificial load"
  (an EXECUTING gate), while the test holding the three pins PASSED. Stage 2 not required. Restored
  tree re-runs 13/0. Lesson recorded: DEFEATABLE means "a shadow can satisfy this pin", NOT "this
  feature is deletable" — only stage 2 separates those.

CORRECTIONS TO uodl'S LANDED NUMBERS (measured, with 0 unexplained residue). TOKEN_ABSENT 21 is
ENTIRELY scanner artifact: 10 INTERPOLATED (backtick tokens containing ${...} — the asserted string is
computed and can never occur verbatim; defect #14) + 11 QUOTED_ESCAPED (the token carries the test
file's \\n / \\" escapes while the target spells a real newline/quote; the unescaped token occurs in
all 11 targets; defect #13). Re-classified with escapes resolved: 10 SOUND + 1 WEAK-STRING, no new
hole. So P6 in INVENTORY.md is not a repo state, the ladder's real classified population is 644
(654 - 10 unclassifiable), and 11 rows were mis-filed out of the ladder. Base conflation
(`new URL(rel, import.meta.url)` is test-dir-relative, uodl resolved everything repo-relative) has
measured ZERO effect on the 654 — none of them is reached through a bare-literal new URL — but it
produced 9 false targets (tests/extension/...) inside the census before I fixed it. Defect #12
(pre-existing, cosmetic): summary.json's top-25 per_file_flagged sorted on count alone, so ties at
count 3 fell in PYTHONHASHSEED order and two runs of uodl's own scanner on one tree gave two

TOOL CHANGE PROVEN ADDITIVE before any census number was trusted: the modified scanner re-run at
uodl's own head 7f903962 reproduces every landed field (420 files, 654 pins, 104 absence, 203
unattributed, 11 unreadable, 199 flagged, 51/4/9 safety, classifications, vacuous_by_kind,
occurrence_labels) and all 654 + 104 + 199 rows identical by (file, line, token, classification,

PROSE-INTENDED reason or the guard goes red on day one). NOT done here: wzez is a census and forbids

title: Audit the repo's source-text substring pins — an includes() assertion is satisfied by a comment or an import, and two proven instances let a dropped ?toolautosubmit and a removed withTimeout bound survive the full suite
description:
A proven-weak pin pattern, found by the caller mutation sweep (er6x) and worth
auditing repo-wide because it is cheap to detect and silently defeats the guard
it claims to hold.

THE PATTERN: a test reads a source file and asserts
`sourceText.includes("<token>")`. That assertion is satisfied by ANY occurrence
of the token in the file — including a COMMENT describing the behaviour and an
IMPORT that is never used at the relevant call site.

TWO PROVEN INSTANCES, both in tests/kat-bistro-finalizer.test.ts against
scripts/kat-webmcp-bistro.ts, both surviving a FULL `npm test` run:

1. `assert(scriptText.includes("?toolautosubmit"), "KAT must append
   ?toolautosubmit")`. Mutant U1 removed `?toolautosubmit` from `URL_BISTRO`, so
   the demo no longer auto-submits its tool step — the entire reason the harness
   exists. The pin still passed, because the file's HEADER COMMENT says "Bounded
   execution with ?toolautosubmit, CDP interception, and clean process
   lifecycle". A comment about a guarantee satisfied the guarantee's pin.
2. `assert(scriptText.includes("withTimeout"), "KAT must bound execution with
   withTimeout")`. Mutant U16 removed the `withTimeout(...)` wrapper from the
   success invocation, leaving it UNBOUNDED. The pin still passed, because the
   import line and the teardown field both contain the word. A bound that no
   longer existed was reported as present.

Both are now killed by anchored pins (er6x): match the DECLARATION or the CALL
SITE and parse it — `const URL_BISTRO = "..."` then `new URL(...).searchParams
.has("toolautosubmit")`, and `const strRes = await withTimeout(...)` with the
numeric bound captured and range-checked.

SCALE, measured on ea037b90 — NOT a claim that all of these are vulnerable:
1119 `.includes(` assertions across the test files that read a source file, the
largest concentrations being tests/components.test.ts (74),
tests/conversation-status-ui.test.ts (68), tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts
(56), tests/durable-runs.test.ts (50), tests/kat-bistro-finalizer.test.ts (43).
Most are legitimate: many assert on HTML or generated content where the token
genuinely cannot appear in a comment, and many are checking that user-facing copy
exists. The vulnerable class is narrow and mechanically detectable.

THE AUDIT, which is the point of this bead. For every source-text `.includes(X)`
pin, resolve the target file and check whether X ALSO occurs inside a comment or
an import line of that file. Where it does, the pin can be satisfied without the
guarded code existing at all, and it must be re-anchored to a declaration or call
site. That is a static analysis over the test corpus — no browser, no mutation
runs needed to produce the candidate list. Then confirm the interesting hits the
cheap way: mutate the guarded construct, run the pin, and see whether it notices.
er6x's driver (cap-evidence/bistro-caller-sweep/caller-sweep.py +
kill-verify-caller.py) is a working template for that confirm step.

ACCEPTANCE.
  * A written inventory: every source-text substring pin whose token also appears
    in a comment or import of its target file, with the file, the line, the
    token, and where else it occurs.
  * A severity ranking — pins on SAFETY or HONESTY guards (exit codes, receipt
    announcement, error capture, bounds, path sanitization, evidence location)
    outrank pins on copy or layout, because a silently defeated safety guard is
    how a false GREEN ships.
  * Re-anchored replacements for the safety-critical hits, each proven by
    mutation: the mutant the old pin missed must now be killed.
  * A lintable rule or a scanner test so the pattern does not come back — e.g. a
    committed guard that fails when a source-text `.includes(X)` pin has X
    occurring in a comment of the target file. Note the repo already has static
    tree-scanning guards of exactly this shape (tests/durable-root.test.ts,
    tests/harness-debug-port.test.ts), so the mechanism is established.
  * Do not mass-rewrite the 1119. Fix the vulnerable class; leave the rest alone.

Related: er6x (the caller pins this was found by), 2b6a (the finalizer sweep; its
own lesson was "a test NAME is not coverage" — two committed tests named for
guards their injected seams did not actually exercise). This bead is the third
instance of the same underlying theme: the shape of a pin is not the same thing
as what it proves.
acceptance_criteria: A written inventory of every source-text substring pin whose token also occurs in a comment or import of its target file, with file/line/token/other-occurrence. A severity ranking with safety and honesty guards (exit codes, receipt announcement, error capture, bounds, path sanitization, evidence location) above copy and layout. Re-anchored replacements for the safety-critical hits, each proven by mutation. A committed scanner guard so the pattern cannot return. Do NOT mass-rewrite the 1119 includes() assertions — fix only the vulnerable class.
notes:
uodl audit — split-before-mutation done, 3 real false greens found, 2 were LIVE HOLES. Commit 991bf5e2 on cap-launch-sweep-r2 (worktree), gates green, NOT pushed, awaiting independent review.

SEVEN MORE SCANNER DEFECTS (#5-#11), each found by reading what the scanner PRODUCED. #5 is dominant: the mask never tokenised REGEX LITERALS. 222 regexes across 21 target files carry a quote/backtick in a character class (main-world.js:372 /https?:\/\/[^\s"'<>)]+/gi), and each opened a bogus string span. In main-world.js the cascade ran 372->447 and labelled 'function describePageError(...) {' at :420 as a STRING. 489 of 654 pins (75%) live in files with a provably corrupted mask, so the whole P1-P7 ranking was built on sand. Fixed with jstoken.py: real tokeniser (regex-vs-division by previous significant token, quotes stop at a raw newline, ${} interiors are expressions), 33 unit tests.
#6 every export line counted as an import shadow, but 'export async function f()' IS the construct (3 false VACUOUS in the P1 safety list). #7 message extraction matched only "tok", "msg", not the dominant assert(x.includes("tok"), "msg"), so it returned empty and blinded the whole intent analysis. #8 thrown-Error messages counted as shadows: wrong for error CODES (throw new Error("result_stage_write_no_progress")), for fixture payloads (webmcp-errors.html throws the credential it tests), and for refusals (build.mjs) — 6 false VACUOUS; narrowed shadow to console.* narration only. #9 SAFETY_WORDS contains \.\. and every relative import specifier contains ../, so all 7 import pins were ranked SAFETY on a module path. #10 bound names read from the pin's token, so a multi-line import's tail (} from "x") has no braces and webmcp-lazyauth:197 was filed UNCOVERED though the next line pins the call site. #11 BOTH implementations scanned raw test-file text, so the committed guard matched pins inside its own documentation — a re-anchor comment quoting the old assertion. A guard that fires on prose explaining a removed pin gets disabled.

CORRECTION TO THE PRIORITY CALL. The handoff named the SECRET-REDACTION guard (webmcp-honest-errors:31/:33) as highest-value first target. It is NOT a defect. api[_-]?key|token|secret|password occurs in the regex literal it guards -> LIVE -> SOUND. describePageError is a function declaration -> LIVE -> SOUND. redactSecretText is comment-only BUT its own message says 'the port declares its source of truth (keep-in-sync pointer)' — the pin is about the prose on purpose, and the redaction is pinned by the sibling assert(MAIN.includes("function redactBridgeText(")) which is live. Going straight to mutation would have re-anchored three sound pins. P1 went 34 -> 7 -> THREE real after intent adjudication.

TWO LIVE HOLES, proven by mutation against the FULL suite (not weak pins — unpinned features):
* U-E1: delete 'await recordServerToolUsage(billing);' from service-worker.js -> npm test 3977 passed / 0 failed. The provider-server usage record could be removed ENTIRELY and nothing in the repo noticed. provider-server-tools.test.ts:507 pinned the word ESTIMATE, which occurs in that file exactly once, in the comment at :4077.
* U-I1: make the buildTemplateSelect binding dead in ntp.js, import left in place -> also survived the full suite. This is the U16 shape.
* U-U1p (the bead's own U1) survives kat-bistro-finalizer.test.ts 27/0 and is killed by er6x's anchored pin at kat-bistro-caller.test.ts:46 — two-sided proof that the anchored replacement works and the leftover net did not.

THE security-suite-custody DEATHS WERE NOT KILLS. U-U1p and U-I1 each reported one unexpected full-suite failure, the same test, which PASSED under U-E1 and is green in the pristine at-rest baseline. Mechanism read out of the test's own header rather than assumed: its supervisor takes an exclusive flock on the MACHINE-GLOBAL /tmp/cap-serialized-chrome-acceptance.lock and its child's 20s budget counts its own time, so another lane holding the lock starves it. U-U1p's stage 1 ran two Chrome-launching KATs immediately before stage 2; U-E1's stage 1 launched no Chrome. Measured (custody-flake-check.py): 5/5 green at rest, 2/2 green under each mutant in isolation. Does not reproduce -> load-induced -> U-I1 SURVIVED the full suite and is a second live hole.

FIXES, each proven by re-running the identical mutant: U-E1 killed by the anchored call-site pin at provider-server-tools.test.ts:514; U-I1 killed at template-cards.test.ts:59; the kat-bistro replacement is an ABSENCE pin (the flag is owned by er6x's anchored pin) and new mutant U-U2 duplicates the URL into the script to prove the replacement has teeth — killed. estimatedUsd is pinned on its DECLARATION not the bare word, because that word also occurs in a usage.js header comment and a bare-word pin would be defeatable by it.

GUARD: tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts fails when a source-text .includes(X) pin has no live occurrence of X. Carries its own tokeniser because a naive comment-stripper inherits #5 and would cry wolf on sound pins until disabled. Allowlist keyed testFile::target::token with an adjudicated reason per entry; stale entries are reported so a fix cannot hide behind them. TEETH PROVEN: a probe pin appended to vocabulary.test.ts reddened it naming tests/vocabulary.test.ts:347 with the shadow evidence; removed, green. Runs ~235ms.

GATES: npm run test:changed rc=0; npm test rc=0 (3980 passed / 0 failed, 421 files); changelog 9/0; check:changelog in sync. title: Three equivalent mutants in the KAT finalizer record redundant or dead code — recorded so they are not mistaken for unpinned guards
description:
Three of the 47 mutants in the guard-by-guard sweep of
scripts/lib/kat-finalizer.ts survived the committed suite AND survived a
19-input divergence probe against pristine — they change no observable
behaviour on any input tried. They are recorded here as code hygiene, explicitly
NOT as coverage gaps: no test is missing, because there is nothing for a test to
pin. They are filed so that nobody later "fixes" them, mistakes them for
unpinned guards, or removes the redundancy without knowing it is redundancy.

B2 — `resultData.state = "RED"` inside the kat.log-write catch is a DEAD
  ASSIGNMENT. The payload is built afterwards as
  `JSON.stringify({ ...resultData, state: finalGreen ? "GREEN" : "RED" })`, so
  the spread always overwrites `state` with the value derived from finalGreen.
  The line can never reach the receipt. The adjacent `finalGreen = false` in the
  same catch IS load-bearing and IS pinned (mutant B1 was killed).

H1 — `finalGreen = false` inside the PUBLISH-failure catch is redundant. That
  catch ends with `exit(1)` and then an explicit
  `return { state: "RED", exitCode: 1, ... receiptPath: null }`, so finalGreen
  is never read again on that path. The explicit return is what makes a returned
  exit seam unable to yield GREEN, and it is pinned (mutants H2/H3/H4/H5 were
  all killed).

A2 — `!poisonDetected` in the isGreen conjunction is redundant TODAY because
  teardownChromeAndProfile sets poisonDetected = true and calls
  recordCleanupError("poison_slot_detected") in the same branch, so a poisoned
  slot always also makes cleanupError non-null and `!cleanupError` already
  forces RED. This one is DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than dead code, and it is
  worth a deliberate decision: if the coupling between the poison flag and
  recordCleanupError is ever broken, poison detection silently stops forcing
  RED and nothing in the suite would notice (mutant A2 survived both the suite
  and the probe). The cheap fix is a regression that pins poisonDetected
  INDEPENDENTLY of cleanupError — which requires a teardown seam that reports a
  poison detection without a cleanup error, i.e. pinning the coupling itself.

None of the three is a defect. All three are recorded so the sweep's
classification is complete and auditable: 47 mutants = 29 killed by a committed
assertion + 15 genuine coverage gaps (sibling bead) + 3 equivalent mutants
(this bead).
acceptance_criteria: No code change required for B2/H1 (dead/redundant assignments, both provably unobservable). A2 needs a deliberate decision: either keep the poison/cleanupError coupling and pin it with a regression that would fail if the coupling broke, or drop the now-redundant !poisonDetected term knowingly. Record the decision on this bead.

title: A failed receipt publication leaves kat.log on disk still claiming GREEN, contradicting the finalizer's own report-order comment
description:
scripts/lib/kat-finalizer.ts carries a report-order invariant comment that the
landed code does not implement. The comment says:

  // Report-order invariant (coordinator 2026-09-06): no failure may leave an
  // authoritative GREEN result.json. kat.log is written FIRST — a log-write
  // error folds into the final RED result; result.json is written LAST; if
  // the result write fails there is NO valid result (exit 1) and the
  // misleading kat.log is removed best-effort. Teardown has ALWAYS completed
  // by this point.

The publish-failure catch removes only the staged temp:

  try { await removeReportFile(tmpPath); } catch { /* best effort */ }

Nothing removes kat.log. So after a FAILED publication the evidence directory
holds a kat.log that says the run was GREEN, beside a result.json that either
does not exist or belongs to an earlier run.

PROVEN on the real Deno filesystem with EVERY filesystem seam at its production
default (cap-evidence/finalizer-sweep/probe-katlog-residue.ts, output in
probe-katlog-residue.log). The publication is made to fail without touching
permissions: result.json is a NON-EMPTY DIRECTORY, so the atomic rename rejects
with a real OS error. Observed:

  reportError  : "Is a directory (os error 21): rename '<tmp>' -> '<outDir>/result.json'"
  state        : RED            exitCode: 1        receiptPath: null
  exit seam    : called with 1
  dir listing  : ["kat.log", "result.json"]
  kat.log      : "PASS: bistro_loaded\nPASS: order_submitted\nRESULT: 2/2; GREEN\n"
  staged temp  : removed (no .tmp left behind)
  error log    : "FATAL: Failed to publish the KAT result: Is a directory (os error 21): rename '[path]' -> '[path]'"

So the finalizer's own behaviour is CORRECT and fail-closed — RED, exit 1, no
receipt attributable to the run, no orphan temp, and the paths in the log are
masked. The defect is the surviving non-authoritative artifact plus a comment
that claims it is cleaned up.

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH kat.log IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE. The receipt-authority
rule is that a path is authoritative only via a non-null receiptPath, and the
caller only prints `KAT receipt:` on that. That holds here. But kat.log is the
human-readable artifact a person or a log-scraping script reads next to the
receipt, and it asserts `RESULT: 2/2; GREEN` for a run that published nothing.
A stale prior result.json in a reused outDir makes it worse: the directory then
reads as a clean GREEN run with a GREEN log and a GREEN receipt, none of which
belong to this invocation.

ACCEPTANCE — this needs an owner decision, so it is filed rather than fixed:
either (a) remove kat.log best-effort in the publish-failure catch, making the
code match the comment, and pin that with a regression that asserts the
directory holds no GREEN-claiming kat.log after a failed publication; or (b)
correct the comment to state that kat.log is deliberately retained as
non-authoritative diagnostic residue, and pin THAT instead so the choice is
explicit. Either way the comment and the code must agree, and whichever
behaviour is chosen must be pinned by a test. Do not leave the contradiction.

No Chrome involved. Found while reading the module for the guard-by-guard
mutation sweep (see the sibling bead for that sweep); it is a reading + real-FS
finding, not a mutation survivor.
acceptance_criteria: The comment and the code must agree, and whichever behaviour is chosen must be pinned by a regression: either remove kat.log best-effort in the publish-failure catch and assert no GREEN-claiming kat.log survives a failed publication, or correct the comment to state that kat.log is deliberately retained as non-authoritative diagnostic residue and pin that. Real-Deno-FS proof already exists (result.json as a non-empty directory makes the atomic rename reject with os error 21 while every filesystem seam stays at its production default).

title: Chrome KAT profiles live inside the repo .cache, so any whole-tree copy races a live browser
description:
Found while de-serializing the Chrome gates (chrome-agent-platform-uzik).

Observed: tests/cdp-client.test.ts:301 copied the whole worktree with `cp -a <repo>/. <scratch>/.` to build a failing-build fixture. During a full `npm test` the copy failed:

  cp: cannot stat '/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-beads-uzik//./.cache/kat-bgagent-delete-1788697263982/Default/DIPS-journal': No such file or directory

The `.cache/` directory (gitignored, ~62 MB) holds live Chrome profile dirs created by ~25 KAT harnesses as `${ROOT}.cache/kat-<name>-${STAMP}`. Chrome creates and unlinks journal/lock files inside a profile while it runs, so a whole-tree copy taken during a live KAT fails on a file that vanished mid-copy. Under the old machine-wide lock this was unlikely to overlap; with bounded-concurrency slots (uzik) it is reachable, and it reads as a defect in whatever test happens to be copying the tree.

Interim fix landed in uzik: that test now copies with `rsync -a --exclude '/.cache/'` (the child never needs gitignored scratch).

Real fix / acceptance: browser profiles should not live inside the repository at all. Move the `${ROOT}.cache/kat-*` profile convention to the durable root (`durableDir()` from scripts/lib/durable-root.mjs) or a per-run temp dir, so no build, copy, package, or archive of the repo can ever include a live Chrome profile. Acceptance: (1) no `--user-data-dir` under `${ROOT}.cache` remains in scripts/ (extend tests/chrome-profile-isolation.test.ts to assert the profile root is outside the repo); (2) a whole-tree `cp -a` of the repo during a live KAT run succeeds; (3) full suite green.
close_reason: Chrome profiles moved out of repo to ~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles/ via chromeProfileDir, landed @ 9c1900f8

A whole-tree cp -a during a live browser run succeeds — driven for real in-suite: launch Chrome with the extension and a chromeProfileDir profile, confirm the profile is live (entries present), then run the exact failing command cp -a <repo>/. <dst>/. and assert exit 0. Also asserts the tree holds no Chrome profile SIGNATURE (Default/, SingletonLock, Local State, GrShaderCache) at depth 1 or 2.
3. Full suite green: npm test 3898/0 (serial 99/0 + parallel 3799/0, 397 files, 89 s); npm run test:changed fell closed to the full suite; build clean; check:vocabulary OK.

REAL KAT EVIDENCE: deno run -A scripts/kat-runner.ts --only=narrow-toggle → exit 0, 20 passed / 0 failed in 7 s, profile at ~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles/kat-narrow-toggle-153446-1788701655274-f2b3. The runner's new pruneChromeProfileDirs() call ran without touching it.

FALSIFICATION (4 guards reverted individually, each RED, all restored byte-identical): one KAT's profile moved back inside the repo → static guard RED (4P/1F); helper pointed back into the repo → 2P/3F (helper guarantees + live-copy signature check); uniqueness dropped (fixed suffix) → 4P/1F; prune ignoring age → 4P/1F (a fresh profile must survive). SCOPE BOUNDARY (deliberate, stated in the commit): KAT EVIDENCE dirs (screenshots, verdicts) still live under .cache/. Overlap risk is low: this branch touches 33 KAT harness bodies + kat-runner (one added prune call + import), while uzik touches kat-runner's runOne and chrome-launch; mkax touches chrome-launch/chrome-journeys/registry. kat-runner is the only shared file — uzik rewrites runOne's flock wrapper, this adds a prune call above the KAT loop; both belong.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
STATE: IN_REVIEW. Candidate: cap/qwen-vga1-drop-evidence at a99f79df1, based on origin/main
146897291 and 4 commits behind the current tip (f6d8e48e5) — merge forward; the CHANGELOG/version
files will collide the usual way and the post-commit hook re-bumps.

THE ONE CHECK THE BEAD ASKED FOR, RUN NOT ASSUMED
The condition was "IF legibility P0 landed". chrome-agent-platform-wal
(CAP-FB-20260827-TOOL-CALL-LEGIBILITY-01) is closed `DONE — origin/main@d5620af9`, and
`git merge-base --is-ancestor d5620af9 origin/main` passes, with that commit's own subject naming
the merge ("tool cards show the tool's own result, never the protocol envelope"). So the check is
YES and the harness is history. Git keeps the script.

WHAT MOVED (4 paths + 1 export, -763 lines)
- scripts/tool-call-evidence.ts deleted.
- scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts: its row removed.
- tests/composer-selector-migration.test.ts: its INVENTORY row removed.
- docs/CLEANUP-ANALYSIS.md: C10 marked removed with the landing evidence and the reason the ledger
  row had to move with it.
- .beads/issues.jsonl: the pre-commit hook's passive export.

WHY THREE SITES AND NOT ONE, AND THE PROOF EACH OF THEM HAS TEETH
The removal is only safe if the two registries and the file move together, and both registries
enforce that in the direction that catches a half-job:
- tests/harness-registry.test.ts fails on "registry entries whose file no longer exists". Proved: I
  put the row back with the file still deleted → 10 passed / 1 failed, naming tool-call-evidence.ts.
  Reverted → 11 passed / 0 failed.
- tests/composer-selector-migration.test.ts is a ratchet whose prune assertion demands deletion of
  a row for a file that no longer names a retired id. Proved: row restored → 2 passed / 1 failed,
  printing exactly that. Reverted → 3 passed / 0 failed.
Both mutants were applied to the committed tree from a saved copy and reverted; `git status` clean
after each. So the gate would have caught me if I had deleted only the script.

DOC HEADER, ONE EXTRA STEP
The same file's header asserted the harness registry held "99 entries". It held 109 when I measured
it and 108 after this removal, so the number had already rotted by ten. I replaced the count with a
pointer to the test that measures it in both directions, and left the reason in the line, because
ady6's own correction is the precedent: a count in prose is a pin that rots, and this one had been
rotting for three weeks with nobody failing on it.

GATES (all on the committed tree, after `npm run build:production` following the last commit)
- npm test: serial phase (18 build/artifact files) GREEN in 438s, then parallel phase (481 files)
  GREEN in 83s — 4504 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, 499 files total, wall 521s. Zero test-result
  FAILED lines in the log (checked: the 12 matches for "FAILED" are all inside test NAMES, each
  ending ok).
- npm run check:vocabulary: OK, 17 surfaces, one name per concept.
- npm run check:dist: clean at HEAD after the rebuild.
- Machine load through the run was 59–83, and the runner scaled the serial timeout to ~353s
  (base 180s x load 1.96/CPU, ceiling x4). It finished under that without an environmental refusal,
  so this is a real green, not a widened bound.

NOT CLAIMED
I did not run the browser journey gate: this change removes a manual-class evidence harness and
touches no product code, no page, and no route. Nothing in it is observable in the extension. If the
reviewer wants the journey number anyway it is a quiet-window `npm run test:chrome`, and the box has
not been quiet all evening.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
VERDICT (a) — STALE PROBE SEAM, NOT A SETTINGS REGRESSION. Fixed, driven, branch `verify/9uho-diagnostics-gate` @ **e7623b29ac3801704447c3292eb07e7eda908f68** (uiflash / deepseek-flash, 2026-09-25).

REPRODUCED FIRST on current origin/main 27cf212d7: `deno run -A scripts/webmcp-realsite-probe.ts` → `FAIL: diagnostics gate enabled — null`, exactly as filed.

THE MECHANISM, measured rather than inferred (three instrumented runs):
1. THE ROUTE. The toggle lives in `<section id="agents" class="panel">` (extension/options/options.html:150). The probe opened `options.html` with NO hash, so that panel is hidden: the element exists, `renderWebmcpStatus` has run, and its rect is **{w:0,h:0}** (measured). The probe's click helper accepted `{x:0,y:0}` as a valid box and dispatched the real mouse click at the viewport's top-left corner — onto the page header. Nothing flipped; the 8s poll returned null; the probe blamed the product. The acceptance harness opens `options.html#agents` for the same check and passes (test-artifacts/webmcp-acceptance-manifest.json, 2026-08-30).
2. THE CONTROL. A real click at the HOST's centre (`getElementById("webmcp-diagnostics")`) left the host's `checked` false; the clickable box is the shadow button (`?.shadowRoot?.querySelector("button")`).
3. THE PRODUCT IS HEALTHY, driven in the same session: `webmcp.diagnostics.set {enabled:true}` → `.get` returns `{enabled:true}`. So the toggle, the message route and the gate all work; only the probe's approach to them was wrong.

THE FIX (scripts/webmcp-realsite-probe.ts only, +41/−6): open `options.html#agents`; click the shadow button; assert the FLIP before polling the gate, so "the click missed" and "the gate did not enable" are two named failures instead of one anonymous null; and `clickSelector` now REFUSES a zero-area rect instead of clicking at (0,0) — a helper that clicks nowhere and reports nothing is how this survived three weeks.

DRIVEN AFTER: `PASS: Settings: clicked the Diagnostics toggle via a real click` · `PASS: Settings: the real click flipped the Diagnostics toggle` · `PASS: diagnostics gate enabled`. The probe's remaining failures are unchanged from before the fix and are upstream of enrollment — the real site did not register `search_docs` under the shim in these runs, which is the probe's own documented network/site dependency, not this bead. UNTESTED BY THE SUITE: `npm run test:changed` fails closed on this file ("no reachable test → running the FULL suite"); the full `npm test` is NOT yet run because the box is at load ~92 with three other lanes' suites in flight (fleet rule: one full suite at a time) — coord asked, and the landing gate can run it on the merged tree. Everything else is green: `deno check` clean, dist rebuilt and current after the commit.

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260830-PRIVACY-STATEMENT-01] One screen that says what the extension sends and stores, and a factory-reset journey
- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 security lane, findings 9 and 17. Nothing in the product tells the owner what leaves the machine (provider calls, skill imports, the model-driven fetch) or that the provider key sits unencrypted in the profile, and the full factory reset has no browser-driven proof.
- Updated: 2026-08-30 14:30 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P3
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `fc2255be`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: A one-screen "What this extension sends and stores" page is reachable from Settings and states outbound destinations, stored data classes (including that the provider key is stored unencrypted in the profile), the host-access posture, and how to wipe; a `factory-reset` journey seeds every storage class, runs the reset from the Settings button and asserts `enumerateStorageTargets()` is empty afterwards.
  - Context: no telemetry or analytics endpoint exists (security lane grep of every literal host). Outbound today: provider APIs (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.deepseek.com, a user-supplied OpenAI-compatible base URL), `extension/lib/skill-import.js` (api.github.com / raw.githubusercontent.com on an explicit import), the model-driven `cap:fetch` (RUN-SCRIPT-FETCH-APPROVAL-01 gates it), the dormant Pyodide CDN (BUNDLE-BUDGET-01 removes or pins it). Stored: `chrome.storage.local` (`providerConfig` including the key — `extension/lib/provider.js` `kvGet/kvSet("providerConfig")`; enrollment, grants, hooks, threads, usage, scheduled tasks), OPFS (per-origin memory, durable runs, artifacts/scripts), `chrome.storage.session` (bridge nonces), IndexedDB (fs grants), Cache. Wipe: Settings → Data & memory per-store Clear (`scripts/data-memory-clear.ts` acceptance) and the factory reset — `extension/lib/factory-reset.js` `FACTORY_RESET_STORAGE_CLASSES` (14), `enumerateStorageTargets` (27), `executeFactoryReset` (104), wired to `#factory-reset-btn` in `extension/options/options.js:2495-2600` with a destructive confirm at 2588. Gap: the reset has unit coverage only — `grep -n factory scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` → nothing. Key hygiene positives to state: write-only Settings input, redacted reads, diagnostics scrubber, storage-hook key-names-only. What must NOT change: the reset semantics; the statement must be generated from the same lists the code uses where possible (e.g. render `FACTORY_RESET_STORAGE_CLASSES` labels rather than a hand-typed copy) so it cannot drift.
  - Reproduce today: (1) build; Settings has no privacy/data statement page (grep `options.html` for "sends" / "stores" → nothing); (2) `grep -n "factory" scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` → no journey.
  - Files: `extension/options/options.html` (a "Privacy" row under About linking to `privacy.html`, or a section rendered from data — prefer a separate small page `extension/privacy/privacy.html` + `privacy.js` so it can be linked from the Web Store listing too), `extension/privacy/privacy.js` (renders three lists: outbound — from a `OUTBOUND_HOSTS` constant exported by `extension/lib/provider.js` plus skill-import and cap:fetch entries with their gating state; stored — from `FACTORY_RESET_STORAGE_CLASSES`; wipe — links to Data & memory and the reset), `extension/lib/provider.js` (export `OUTBOUND_HOSTS` from the provider presets), `extension/manifest.json` (nothing — the page is an extension page, not web-accessible), `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` (the factory-reset journey), `docs/PERMISSIONS.md` or the README's host-access section (link the page). Do NOT move keys to `chrome.storage.session` in this entry (optional follow-up; record the owner's decision).
  - Steps: (1) Factory-reset journey first: seed a provider config (demo, no real key), one thread, one artifact, one fs grant fixture (the KAT's OPFS handle), a hook deny, then click `#factory-reset-btn` with a genuine gesture, confirm, and assert `enumerateStorageTargets()` (call through a test-seam route or by reading each class from the page) returns empty and the first-run guide is back. (2) `OUTBOUND_HOSTS` export + the page with the three lists (textContent), one sentence each: "Sent: your messages and the page text you share go to the model provider you chose (host). Nothing else leaves this device unless you import a skill or approve a fetch." (3) The host-access sentence comes from HOST-ACCESS-STORY-01's decision (install-granted `<all_urls>` vs optional) — render it from a single constant that entry owns. (4) Link from Settings → About and from the README. (5) a11y pass on the page.
  - Out of scope: changing key storage; the host-access decision itself (HOST-ACCESS-STORY-01); gating `cap:fetch` (RUN-SCRIPT-FETCH-APPROVAL-01) and cookie tools (COOKIE-TOOLS-CUT-01) — the page states whatever their current state is, read from code where possible.
- Review: pending
- Gates: the falsification gates apply
  - Unit: extend the factory-reset tests (`grep -l factory-reset tests/`) with "the privacy page's stored-data list equals FACTORY_RESET_STORAGE_CLASSES labels" and "OUTBOUND_HOSTS lists every literal provider host in provider.js" (static scan of `provider.js` for `https://` literals vs the export). Falsification: add a new host literal to `provider.js` without exporting it, expect RED, add it, GREEN.
  - Browser: `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` — "factory reset: after seeding every storage class, the Settings reset empties enumerateStorageTargets and restores first run" (screenshot `settings-factory-reset-after.png` showing the first-run guide) and "privacy page renders the three lists and the host-access sentence" (screenshot `privacy-page.png`); `deno run -A scripts/a11y-audit.ts` extended to the privacy page.
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green (2457 / 138 at `fc2255be`; re-count).
  - Constraints: no keys in the page, logs or screenshots (seed the demo provider only); textContent; the page is not web-accessible; a11y — headings and lists, one `<h1>`; the reset journey uses a genuine gesture (`requireGenuineGesture` on the confirm).
- Blockers: Depends on CAP-FB-20260830-HOST-ACCESS-STORY-01 (must land first — the page states the host-access posture)
- Next: write the factory-reset journey (independent of the blocker) and land it; draft the page once the host-access decision is recorded.
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep=CAP-FB-20260830-PRIVACY-STATEMENT-01`

  - 2026-08-30 11:00 UTC — verified: no telemetry or analytics endpoint exists; the full factory reset has no Chrome journey in `test:all`.
  - 2026-08-30 14:30 UTC — rewritten in the detailed hand-off format (owner directive); `factory-reset.js` exports (14, 27, 104), the Settings wiring (`options.js:2495-2600`) and the absence of a journey re-verified.

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260829-PROVIDER-SET-NO-BASEURL-01] Saving a preset provider without a base URL yields a config that can never run
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — the one real observation left from the withdrawn `CAP-FB-20260829-SILENT-PROVIDER-RUN-01`
- Updated: 2026-08-29 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Priority: P3
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `84991bdd`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: saving a provider that HAS a known preset base URL (`anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini`, `deepseek`) without supplying one stores that preset rather than an empty string, so the permission preflight can derive a real origin; the BYO-endpoint provider, which has no preset, still requires one and says so
- Review: falsification — the assertion must go red against the current route, which stores `baseURL: ""`
- Gates: unit suite; the provider journeys
- Blockers: —
- Next: default `baseURL` from the provider descriptor in the `provider.set` route when the chosen provider has one
- Recover: `git grep -n "provider.set" -- extension/background/routes/provider.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — measured. `provider.set` with `{ provider: "anthropic", apiKey, model }` and no `baseURL` stores `baseURL: ""`, even though `extension/lib/provider.js` carries `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` as that provider's preset. The permission preflight then derives no origin and the run fails with *"provider permission preflight failed closed: configured provider origin is invalid"* — which blames the origin rather than the missing default. Supplying the base URL explicitly produces the correct message instead (*"the configured provider's exact origin is not granted"*). Low priority because the Settings UI fills the preset, so this is reachable mainly by the route; but a config that can never run should not be storable when the product already knows the right value.

title: Pin the Emscripten graph auditor's dependency-edge prefix-id ordering with a test (dependency_invalid from ordering is untested)
description:
Intent: pin the graph auditor's dependency-edge ordering with a test, so a change to its sort key cannot silently diverge from the manifest validator's literal (from,name) tuple order. Found 2026-10-12 while closing chrome-agent-platform-0mld as superseded.

OBSERVED on fetched origin/main f4ff91702cff: extension/lib/emscripten-manifest.js:123 compares literal (from,name) tuples and tests/emscripten-manifest.test.ts:38 pins that (canonical `main` then `main-side` accepted, reversed and duplicate -> manifest_order). The graph auditor extension/lib/emscripten-module-audit.js:371-372 instead builds `key = \`${edge.from}\0${edge.name}\`` and refuses `key <= previous` with `dependency_invalid`. For valid ids the two orders agree (NUL sorts below every id character, so a prefix id sorts first, exactly as the tuple compare does), but no test pins the auditor's prefix-id order: `dependency_invalid` from ordering is untested.

WHAT TO DO: add a test beside the existing audit tests that feeds the auditor the same edges as tests/emscripten-manifest.test.ts:38 (`main`/`z.wasm`, `main-side`/`a.wasm`) in canonical order (accepted), reversed (dependency_invalid) and duplicated (dependency_invalid). Prove the test can fail by temporarily swapping the key join for the old slash join (`${from}/${name}`, where '-' (45) sorts before '/' (47)) and watching the canonical case go red.

ACCEPTANCE: new RED-then-GREEN test; no production change expected; existing emscripten audit and manifest tests unchanged. MUST NOT CHANGE: the NUL-joined key or the manifest comparator.

title: security-suite.ts calls openCdp before the try whose finally reaps the browser: a connect failure skips the reap
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-3 security review, INFO; pre-existing shape)

`scripts/security-suite.ts` ~L254-256 calls `launchChrome(...)` and then `await openCdp(chrome.wsUrl)` BEFORE the `try {` whose `finally` reaps the browser (`reapLeaderAndSettle(chrome.proc)`). If `openCdp` throws (the DevTools WebSocket does not connect), the `finally` is never entered and the launched browser is left to the lifeline, which only fires when the runner process exits.

## Why it was not changed in the jjsz landing

The security suite cannot run on macOS (`chrome-agent-platform-8bp69`) and Linux is unverified (`chrome-agent-platform-mwj7v`), so an edit to its control flow could not be exercised on the only host available. The lifeline limits the damage (the browser is reaped when the runner exits), so this is a leak window, not an orphan.

## Acceptance

Move `openCdp` inside the `try` (or wrap it so a failure tears the browser down through `reapLeaderAndSettle`), on a host that can run the suite; keep the existing call-site pins in `tests/jjsz-lifeline-runner-exit.test.ts` green and extend them so a regression that moves `openCdp` back out of the `try` is RED.

comments.text:
Landing record (round-3 build review, INFO): at the merge with `origin/main` the conflicting `tests/tar-stream.test.ts` was resolved take-ours, which DROPPED main's looser form: `LC_ALL`/`LANG=en_US.UTF-8` on EVERY OS, stderr appended to the listing, and the listing NFC-normalised on every OS. Neither form was run on Linux (`chrome-agent-platform-mwj7v`). "Loosened on purpose" in this bead is therefore accurate for the darwin NFC accommodation only; the Linux arm is a different trade, not a loosening. If the merge host is a C-locale container and the test goes red, the one-line remedy is to export a UTF-8 locale that exists on that image for the `tar` call (`C.UTF-8` is the usual one), on Linux as well; that choice belongs to the merger with a Linux host in front of them.

title: boundedCommandSpec: a non-finite seconds silently produces an unbounded probe (perl alarm reads NaN as 0)
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz round-2 security review, finding N5; Info)

`boundedCommandSpec(seconds, ...)` in scripts/lib/process-tree.ts builds `String(Math.max(1, Math.ceil(seconds)))`.
`NaN` gives "NaN" and `Infinity` gives "Infinity"; perl's `alarm` reads a non-numeric string as 0, i.e. NO alarm,
so a caller-supplied non-finite bound silently produces an UNBOUNDED probe: the exact hang the helper exists to
prevent. Today every caller passes the constant PS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, so there is no live exposure; the exported
`runBoundedProbe(command, args, seconds)` accepts an arbitrary number.

## Do

`if (!Number.isFinite(seconds)) throw new RangeError(...)` (refuse, do not default: an unbounded probe is worse than
an error), or clamp to the default bound; pick one and test it.

## Acceptance

`boundedCommandSpec(NaN|Infinity|-Infinity, ...)` refuses (or clamps, as decided); RED when the guard is reverted;
the finite cases (0.2 -> 1, 5 -> 5) are unchanged.

title: Lifeline edge cases to decide on: unreportable pkill rejection after parent death, handle-less teardown cannot serialise with a sweep, cross-process pkill race
description:
## Observed (chrome-agent-platform-jjsz, worker W2 notes (c), (d), (e); all documented in docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md 6.4)

Lifeline edge cases that were found and deliberately NOT fixed. Each fails closed or needs a second failure; decide whether any deserves work:

- **(c)** A `pkill` pattern rejection (exit 2) cannot be REPORTED when the parent is already dead: the watcher exits 3 and nobody is listening. The group kill still ran.
- **(d)** `teardownChrome(null, profile)` (no process handle) cannot serialise with an in-flight leader-exit sweep, in this process or in another one: the serialising state lives on the `Deno.ChildProcess` (a `WeakMap` keyed by it), and a handle-less teardown has no key. The sweep's `pkill -f` can then SIGKILL that teardown's own `pkill`/`pgrep` (`pkill exited 137`), which fails closed (the teardown throws).
- **(e)** A concurrent `pkill`/`pgrep` of the SAME profile run by ANOTHER process can be SIGKILLed by the watcher's sweep. Fails closed; the same class existed before jjsz for any two cleanup paths racing on one profile.

## Acceptance
Either a note on this bead that none needs a change (with the reasoning), or a fix with a test that is RED when reverted. No change to the reaping behaviour measured on real Chrome.

title: 68 test files derive their root with new URL(...).pathname, so a checkout path containing a space or non-ASCII character silently points the tests at a path that is not there
description:
WHAT: 68 test files use `new URL("..", import.meta.url).pathname` (or a sibling-relative variant) instead of `fileURLToPath(...)`. For a checkout root whose path contains a space or non-ASCII character, `.pathname` returns the PERCENT-ENCODED form, so the derived root is not the tree on disk.

MEASURED (durable probe, /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/nwhc probe/):
  new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname        -> ".../nwhc%20probe/cap%20checkout/"  (percent-encoded)
  fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url))  -> ".../nwhc probe/cap checkout/"        (the real path)
Production code in this repo already uses fileURLToPath; the defect is test-only portability. It was found by the xrh4 review at tests/package-extension-freshness-driver.mjs:422, but that driver has since been restructured and no longer contains the pattern (chrome-agent-platform-nwhc closed on that evidence) — this bead is the remaining 68 files.

WHY IT MATTERS: on such a checkout the affected tests fail as 'file not found'/setup errors rather than reaching their real assertion, which is the silent-wrong-root shape this fleet has been fixing all day (54k5, h8rb): a path-derived root that is not the tree under test. Count as of 2026-09-18: 68 files under tests/.

FIX DIRECTION (one change, owner's call because it touches every lane's files): mechanical sweep to fileURLToPath(new URL("..", import.meta.url)) (covering the sibling-file variants too), plus a source-scan guard test in the style of tests/durable-root.test.ts and tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts so the pattern cannot return — the guard can only land WITH the sweep, since on its own it would red the suite across 68 files.

ACCEPTANCE: a source-scan control proves no test file derives a filesystem root through a URL pathname; the suite is green on this checkout; and a spaced-root control demonstrates the corrected derivation reaches the real directory (the probe above is that control).

title: Two agent-composer instances render the same id="task-input", so the document carries duplicate ids
description:
WHAT: extension/shared/components.js's agent-composer renders a fixed id="task-input" (and #run-task) for every instance. The NTP page has TWO instances in one document — the hub composer (#composer) and the thread composer (#thread-composer) — so the live DOM carries two elements with id=task-input. document.getElementById('task-input') silently resolves to the hub one whichever composer the user is looking at, and any id-based label/aria association can bind to the wrong instance.

REPRO: open the NTP hub, send one task (the view switches to the thread view), then evaluate in the page: [...document.querySelectorAll('#task-input')].length === 2 while both composers are in the document.

WHY IT MATTERS: the repo's own drivers already had to work around it (cap-evidence/acp-browser-acceptance.ts scopes its queries to the composer element; the comment at components.js:7057 says the ids are kept for CDP journeys). It also bit an independent review this morning: the owner-gate acceptance legs typed into the hub input while the thread view was showing, because the id-based lookup silently matched the other composer — the legs then verified nothing.

FIX DIRECTION: one id per document — render the input without an id and expose a data attribute (e.g. data-composer-input) plus a class, or derive a per-instance id. Keep the CDP journey contract working (tests/chrome-journeys.ts and several scripts address #task-input directly); that contract change is why this is filed rather than patched in passing.

ACCEPTANCE: two composers in one document produce no duplicate ids, and the journey/driver selectors that address a composer's input still work (updated in the same change).

Versions must stay CONTIGUOUS as well as descending - tests/changelog.test.ts enforces contiguity, so a deliberate gap is itself a gate failure - and the number a branch can take is therefore decided by LANDING ORDER, not by what it happened to carry when it was written.

chrome-agent-platform: raw 'deno test tests/' sweeps are refused by design (2026-09-04, bead 037b): deno.jsonc excludes tests/*.test.ts so only tests/00-use-npm-test_test.ts loads and fails with the runner commands. Runners pass --config deno.runner.jsonc (nodeModulesDir manual keeps npm resolution; lock false stops deno.lock rewrites). Deno.exit and top-level throws inside a test module do NOT stop a sweep (the runner records them and continues). A raw single-file 'deno test tests/x.test.ts' says 'No test modules found'; use npm run test:file -- tests/x.test.ts.

Detector/guard work rule (4lc0 six rounds, cap-astra + cap-ds-flash, 2026-09-24): every round's blocker was a shape the then-current rule's PROSE claimed to handle, so (1) pin limits as assertions that the bad case is NOT detected, never as comments; (2) before trusting a green from any new instrument, prove it can fail — the load-marker writes a file on evaluation, and a CAS fingerprint must be shown to move on a real generator run first; (3) an instrument comparing two identical error strings produces confident green from a blind check (seen twice: marker-path mix-up, require() in ESM); (4) prefer a rule that cannot be shaped around (name-is-hazard, fail closed) plus explicit exemptions falsified at load level, over a taxonomy of syntaxes; (5) prose about a deleted rule is worse than no prose — delete it with the code.

Label hygiene (found by the merger 2026-10-15): a landed bead kept merge-queue and kept nudging the watchdog, because Dolt unions label arrays when a lane pushes a pre-landing snapshot. Before adding or removing ANY label on an already-landed bead, run bd dolt pull first; otherwise a stale snapshot resurrects merged:false labels. Removal is not enough on its own - the snapshot that carries the old array wins, so the pull is the fix.
